teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: zero complaints cannot identify zero objections
teachingExamples.text: Suppose that, among 100 fictional users, only 20 can actually use a complaint channel; the other 80 cannot because of access restrictions stipulated for this teaching example. We now observe 0 complaints. State A stipulates that nobody objects; state B stipulates that the 80 unable to use the channel object, while the 20 able to use it do not. Both states produce 0 complaints, so this record cannot distinguish “nobody objects” from “objections exist but were not recorded.” These are not real survey data, nor is it claimed that all silent people actually oppose something.
teachingExamples.assumptions: 100/20/80 are all stipulated numbers; the two states produce the same record by definition; no actual complaint rate is assumed.
teachingExamples.boundary: Safer and more accessible conditions for expression may improve observation, but do not justify requiring everyone to disclose private experiences.

counterexamples.text: Constructed conditional counterexample: leaving a trial means losing the only essential service available. Even if nobody leaves, zero exits cannot directly establish that everyone is voluntarily satisfied.
counterexamples.effect: Limits inferences from constrained behavior to consent, absence of objection, or absence of loss, and limits treating technical rollback as complete recovery.

counterexamples.text: Constructed conditional counterexample: complaints are accepted only in person during working hours. The absence of complaints from people unable to attend does not establish that they have no objections.
counterexamples.effect: Limits inferences from constrained behavior to consent, absence of objection, or absence of loss, and limits treating technical rollback as complete recovery.

counterexamples.text: Constructed conditional counterexample: a system restores its old configuration, but sensitive material has already been seen by unauthorized people. Rolling back the technical state cannot undo information exposure that has occurred.
counterexamples.effect: Limits inferences from constrained behavior to consent, absence of objection, or absence of loss, and limits treating technical rollback as complete recovery.

questionAnswers.question: If nobody exits, can we declare that everyone consents?
questionAnswers.answer: No automatic declaration is warranted. First check whether exit is actually accessible, its price to be paid, and relationships of dependence; nor may one make the reverse declaration that everyone objects.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 159.

questionAnswers.question: To make responsibility traceable, may we require disclosure of all unrelated personal experiences?
questionAnswers.answer: That does not follow. Disclosure should be limited to what the current judgment and protection require, taking privacy and the costs of expression into account.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 157 and §1.5.2.

questionAnswers.question: If an analyst's model predicts more accurately than the person concerned, may the analyst authorize something on that person's behalf?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Evidential support and decision-making authority must be established separately.
questionAnswers.basis: Final sentence of Chinese source line 159.

questionAnswers.question: Does observing zero complaints in the mathematical example establish that the 80 people actually have objections?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Both states A and B can produce the record. The conclusion is non-identification, not selection of B as reality.
questionAnswers.basis: The two-state teaching construction in this section.

1.8.title: 1.8 Entering analysis through an event
1.8.lead: First separate the event, records, and inferences, then develop the analysis along channels and clocks that are actually supported; analysis need not automatically become prediction or action.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 161–172, heading “1.8 Entering analysis through an event”; assembly anchor /theory/part-01#section-1-8. Brief quotation translated from Chinese: “An explanation just thought up cannot be entered directly as a fact” (line 169). This section turns the preceding four types of task into a conditional route for event analysis, leading into actors, circles, projection, and bounded choice in Parts Nine through Twelve. [T-18]

The first step distinguishes three objects: what happened in reality, material that was recorded and obtained, and judgments the analyst forms from that material. For example, a work-stoppage notice is a piece of material; whether it is authentic, whether the plan was carried out, and when the actual stoppage occurred require separate judgments. Even an unverified notice may affect expectations by being believed, but that does not automatically make its contents factual. The time of occurrence, the time a record was obtained, and the time it was adopted in a model may also differ. Late-arriving evidence can revise today's understanding of the past; it cannot become information that was known at that earlier time. [T-18; T-event]

“Freezing the information cutoff” first means stating which materials available by what date the current version uses, retaining disputes, different sources, and unknowns, so that the starting point is not quietly altered after the outcome appears. Freezing does not mean never updating. New evidence can produce a new version with a timestamp and a correction relationship, rechecking only conclusions it actually affects; old judgments must not be combined with new material to create a prediction that appears to have known the outcome all along. [T-event; T-snapshot]

A multi-circle representation is a tool to use as needed, not a requirement to build an enormous circle map for every minor event. When it is needed, identify who is acting, the circle in which the problem mainly occurs, and which adjacent circles affect the answer through actual relationships. Actor states are developed in Part Nine, and joint objects and relations among circles in Part Ten; a name or shared location does not automatically establish an effective circle. Candidate objects still need explicit boundaries, relations, and tasks. [T-18; T-circles]

The second step treats material conditions and experience–meaning conditions proportionately. The former include time, tools, income, or accessible transportation; the latter include expectations, trust, shame, commitments, or value conflicts. Lack of money may cause pressure, but cannot be recorded as a negative attitude without supporting material; more resources do not necessarily resolve humiliation or value conflict. A cross-channel explanation should state which material change, through which experiential or action mechanism, changed which outcome. If the current task needs only technical quantities, do not require collection of unrelated private experiences; if discussing autonomy or life opportunities, aggregate resources cannot replace the experiences of the people concerned. [T-18; T-dual]

The third step separates clocks. Emotional changes over hours, changes in relationships after several rounds of interaction, organizational adjustments over weeks or quarters, institutional changes through longer procedures, and changes in capabilities and identity over years are examples for recognizing clocks, not a universal, precise timetable. A person's softened attitude on one day does not establish that long-term trust has recovered; approval of a budget does not establish that supplies are in place. Specify the update trigger, delay, maintenance conditions, and expiry conditions for each variable. [T-18; T-clock]

An event's direct effects apply only to variables actually reached by its channels and satisfying the conditions for the effect. Other variables may change through autonomous dynamics, endogenous accumulation, recovery, or expiry; those changes must be included according to declared and supported rules. Not being directly reached by this event does not imply necessarily remaining unchanged in reality. Conversely, advancing a narrative to “the next day” cannot refresh resources, rules, identities, and relationships simultaneously. Without a reliable basis for updating, retain the last observation together with its time and uncertainty, and mark it unknown when necessary. [T-18; T-clock]

When the task requires path projection, the frozen snapshot is the starting point and the event is the input; each subsequent segment should list direct effects, returning feedback, cross-circle effects, and the support for each. Feedback requires a return channel and subsequent change; hearing about consequences cannot be treated as effective feedback. Nor does drawing a line between circles establish that propagation occurred. Record subsequent states by unfolding them over time and preserving their grounds, rather than making the same node both its own cause and its own effect within a single projection. [T-path; T-feedback]

Branching does not mean arbitrarily writing several endings. Separate paths where the available material allows different facts, mechanism conditions, thresholds, actor choices, or external disturbances to change what follows, and give early signals, contrary signals, and stopping conditions for each branch. Compare only where comparison is supported; do not force probabilities or rankings without grounds. An observed signal need not uniquely establish a mechanism either: explain its discriminatory power. [T-18; T-branch]

A residual means that the current representation has not explained a difference. It may arise from an omitted condition, a measurement method, a mistaken mechanism, or another candidate; it is not evidence that a new variable already exists. Propose multiple distinguishable candidates and choose a minimal test that can change the current answer and has suitable risk and cost. Minimal does not mean the smallest possible sample, but necessity for the key branch point; authority to observe, privacy, and protection still require independent grounds. [T-branch; T-identify]

Historical material can show why information versions matter. NASA's 1999 Phase I investigation report on the Mars Climate Orbiter distinguishes the recorded loss of signal, the units problem discovered afterward, and revised estimates, and explicitly gives a cutoff date for some observations. Here it serves as a structural example from a published investigation. We do not claim that the analyst directly obtained raw telemetry, or present a retrospective explanation as an advance prediction. [R-MCO]

Finally, separate tasks by use. If the purpose is understanding alone, the work can end with a supported explanation and explicit unresolved points. Publishing a future judgment requires registering the target, horizon, simple baseline, and evaluation arrangements before the outcome, rather than selecting successful cases afterward. Comparing real actions requires placing action, delay, probing, exit, and inaction on a common comparison baseline, and specifying authorization, impact ceilings, stopping, and remedy. An analytical recommendation can be formed first; permission for actual execution must be established separately. Explanation, predictive quality, and the justification of action each carry their own evidential responsibilities. [T-18; T-purpose]

The strongest objection is: with insufficient material, would all this branching leave analysis permanently stalled? The answer is to retain only distinctions that change the answer to the current question or the comparison of options. If the currently compatible states yield the same answer to the question, a qualified conclusion can be given without recovering every latent variable. Conversely, when the key answers genuinely differ, a fluent narrative must not conceal non-identification. The standard for simplification is task sufficiency, not more variables or a smoother story. [T-identify]
argumentSteps: Starting point: events, material, and inferences have different statuses; the time material is obtained is not the time the event occurred.
Representation: fix the question, information cutoff, and disputes; select actors and circles as needed, and separately record relevant material and experience–meaning conditions.

Mechanism connection: let only direct effects supported by actual channels update the corresponding variables; independent dynamics proceed under their own declared rules, and expired evidence does not refresh automatically.
Projection conclusion: branches must depend on conditions, clocks, and mechanisms, and provide signals and stopping conditions; paths that cannot be compared remain unresolved.
Responsibility for candidates: residuals can only prompt candidates and discriminating tests; naming or diagramming them cannot confer factual status.

Use boundary: explanation may end there; foresight adds pre-outcome registration and baseline evaluation; real actions add common comparison, authorization, and protection. None establishes the others by proxy.
Evidential ceiling: the NASA report supports the stated distinctions in the historical investigation; the teaching numbers verify only the declared update rules, not universal real-world dynamics.

distinctions.leftText: A change in reality requiring its corresponding evidence.
distinctions.rightText: When which material was obtained; this may be later than the event.

distinctions.leftText: A change reached by this event through a channel.
distinctions.rightText: Endogenous dynamics, recovery, or expiry change according to independent rules.

distinctions.leftText: Preserves the version at the time and the limits of its information.
distinctions.rightText: Reality and subsequent understanding can still update; versions must be marked.

distinctions.leftText: A possible explanation awaiting discrimination and verification.
distinctions.rightText: Requires additional supporting material and the corresponding object contract.

distinctions.leftText: Answers the task of understanding and identifies unresolved points.
distinctions.rightText: Specific actions separately require authorization and protection.

boundaries: Constructed conditional counterexample: receiving a notice that “staff will be added next week” leads someone to raise today's service capacity. The plan has not been implemented; the channels of staff arrival and deployment are missing, so this update is unwarranted.

Constructed conditional counterexample: an event does not reach inventory, and someone asserts that inventory stays constant throughout the week. If known daily consumption continues, autonomous dynamics still change it.

Constructed conditional counterexample: after one apology, relational trust, organizational rules, and long-term identity are all changed to “improved.” Without separately supported mechanisms and clocks, this is merely narrative synchronization.

Constructed conditional counterexample: observing lateness leads someone to enter “lack of responsibility.” Competing candidates such as transport constraints, caregiving conflicts, and recording errors have not been distinguished; a label cannot complete identification.

Proportionate treatment of both channels does not mean collecting private experiences for every technical task; likewise, a local judgment for which technical quantities suffice does not automatically cover judgments of human dignity or autonomy.

Retrospective conclusions in the NASA report cannot directly count as information known at the time; an explicit observation cutoff in one passage cannot substitute for the occurrence dates of all facts in the report.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: record event updates and autonomous clocks separately
teachingExamples.text: A fictional warehouse holds 5 items at time t, and the event is a verified delivery of 3 items; it is separately specified that 1 item is actually used in the first hour, with no other inflows or outflows. Receiving the delivery first gives 5+3=8 items; advancing through that hour then gives 8−1=7 items. Knowing that resources changed does not automatically support a change in a service provider's emotions or in rules. If an observation for another field has expired and there is no basis for updating it, mark it as awaiting checking or unknown, rather than copying an old value as a new measurement.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All quantities are artificially specified; receipt precedes use during that hour; use of 1 item is a given actual process, not merely an upper capacity bound; there are no losses or other inflows or outflows.
teachingExamples.boundary: 7 items follows only under these assumptions. It is not real warehouse data, and experience cannot be inferred from the inventory value.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: retain two conditional paths for the same absence record
teachingExamples.text: A fictional service point records only that someone missed an appointment. Candidate path A is that transport made attendance impossible; candidate path B is that the person regarded the service approach as disrespectful. Both may also coexist. First check the accuracy of the appointment and attendance records, then, where permitted and safe, ask what accessibility arrangements or communication approach are needed, without requiring disclosure of unrelated experiences. Evidence of a transport shutdown supports part of A but does not automatically exclude B; if the person declines to answer, retain the unknown. Stopping conditions include exceeding permitted uses, increasing inappropriate disclosure pressure, or already having enough to answer the current question.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The people, event, and two paths are entirely constructed for teaching; no actual service provider or user was observed.
teachingExamples.boundary: This story must not be used to establish any absent person's actual motives; the proposed questioning was neither implemented nor tested for effectiveness.

questionAnswers.question: Credible material about yesterday's work stoppage arrives only today. Which date should be entered as the time of occurrence?
questionAnswers.answer: The work stoppage occurred yesterday; today is when the evidence was obtained, and the judgment about the past may be revised today. Yesterday's information set as it stood then must not be rewritten.

questionAnswers.question: If no new event reaches a variable, must it remain unchanged?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. There may be declared and supported autonomous dynamics, accumulation, or expiry; if even the update rule is unclear, the unknown must not be written as a constant.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source, line 167, and §10.7.

questionAnswers.question: Why is inventory 7 rather than 8 after the first hour in the numerical example?
questionAnswers.answer: The delivery's direct change is +3, with actual use of 1 item during that hour also assumed; first 8, then 7, belonging respectively to the event and clock advancement.
questionAnswers.basis: This section's mathematical construction.

questionAnswers.question: If a technical indicator suffices to answer whether a machine is overloaded, must the operator's private feelings also be elicited?
questionAnswers.answer: Unrelated experience need not be forcibly collected; but if the question changes to autonomy or dignity at work, the original indicator cannot replace those materials.

questionAnswers.question: If a model cannot explain a difference, may “hidden resistance” immediately be added as a fact?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It is at most one candidate, requiring comparison with other candidates and a discriminating test that preserves protections.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source, line 169, and §11.8.

questionAnswers.question: Must an action plan be provided after completing an event explanation?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A task seeking understanding may end with a grounded explanation and explicit unresolved issues; if its use escalates, the additional responsibilities of foresight or action must then be met.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source, line 171.

1.9.title: 1.9 Limits of Capability
1.9.lead: Capability requires support from continuing comparisons on applicable tasks, not from a large model, a long account, or fully completed contracts.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 173–178, heading ‘1.9 Limits of Capability’; assembly anchor /theory/part-01#section-1-9. Short quotation: ‘reality cannot be reproduced in full in a text’ (translated from Chinese, line 175). This section first acknowledges the limits of models and materials, then separately specifies what explanation, foresight, and choice must preserve, focusing on constraints against overstating capability. [T-19]

The five limitations are distinct. ‘Variables not yet observed’ means relevant conditions may not have entered the records; ‘mechanisms not yet understood’ means that even with records, how conditions produce consequences may remain unknown; ‘unavailable materials’ may be constrained by technology, resources, law, privacy, or another person's justified refusal; ‘subjects' choices’ means subsequent developments cannot be treated merely as the continuation of passive variables; ‘unforeseen events’ may change existing paths. Each limitation must be specified, not grouped indiscriminately as random noise or assumed solvable by increasing model size. [T-19；T-identify；T-privacy]

Written contracts make objects, windows, sources, mechanisms, boundaries, and responsibilities examinable. Stating ‘a key field is unknown’ is more reliable than silently guessing a value, but the contract itself produces no observations, discovers no mechanisms, and obtains no consent. A fully completed checklist may simply be filled with guesses; complete documentation and sufficient facts are different judgments. Equally, domain evidence that does not use this format does not thereby become invalid and should still be judged by its actual materials and tests. [T-19；T-domain]

Limited knowledge does not mean knowing nothing. If different states all yield the same answer to the current question, that grounded local conclusion can be retained; if the representation is sufficient only for direction, restrict the conclusion to direction, but if even direction is unidentified, say it is unknown. We must not reject all calculations because a model is incomplete, nor claim complete prediction of an entire object from a local success. [T-identify；T-forecast]

For explanation, retaining residuals acknowledges which changes the current model does not explain. Residuals may suggest measurement error, omitted conditions, an inapplicable mechanism, or problems with object partitioning; they do not automatically establish any particular new explanation. Competing candidates and discriminating observations may be proposed, but contrary materials must not all be renamed ‘deep mechanisms’ supporting the theory. The more an explanation accommodates everything without any possible failure case, the more its testability needs examination. [T-19；T-residual]

For foresight, retaining a simple baseline prevents a complex model from declaring its own victory. Compare it with task-appropriate simple methods and existing domain methods using the same target, horizon, information cutoff, and evaluation rules; separate the contributions of added information, computation, and structural assumptions. The baseline must not be a deliberately useless method, nor replaced after results by a weaker baseline to manufacture improvement. Greater task complexity does not make the baseline less important. [T-baseline]

Retaining outcomes at resolution means recording successes, failures, missing labels, unresolved results, and scope changes under the original rules. Before results, register an assessable target and horizon; afterward, check the outcome without feeding it back into the starting point or retaining only successful cases. A single-case score may validly be calculated, but it is not long-term calibration; one incorrect prediction also does not automatically overturn a method with established long-term support. Continuing comparisons should identify stable domains of application, failure conditions, and when downgrading or retirement is appropriate. [T-19；T-forecast]

For choice, retain both inaction and the different positions that bear the consequences. Under inaction, other processes still advance, potentially producing harm and responsibility; inaction is not costless. A positive aggregate benefit from an action also must not erase severe burdens on a minority, basic protections, or exit conditions. Choice may produce a clear recommendation under disclosed value premises, but model accuracy must not be exchanged for decision-making authority, and a single overall score must not resolve every value conflict on behalf of qualified subjects. [T-choice]

The real-world source is the 2022 NHC guidance-model paper cited in §1.1, but this section adds an observation about evaluation limits: for updated models, the authors distinguish in-sample improvement, comparison over one season, and insufficient independent samples, rather than declaring a gain robust merely because the model was updated. This illustrates the paper's cautious evaluation practice, not empirical evidence of the Xikari framework's capability. [R-NHC]

Framework size, number of terms, and account length indicate at most the effort put into expression and modeling; they do not directly measure accuracy, calibration, explanatory effectiveness, or net practical benefit. A longer analysis may indeed expose conditions and disagreements, but must show what additional testable content it contributes; a shorter analysis is not automatically better either. Judgment rests on evidential gains, costs, and boundaries within the specific task, not length itself. [T-19；T-baseline]

The strongest objection asks whether requiring continuing comparison prohibits all foresight on new questions without historical samples. It does not. Mechanistic conditions, exploratory paths, and the status of unproven capability can be retained, explicitly identifying conclusions that are only candidates, scenarios, or grounded limited directions; probabilities must not be invented merely to provide an answer. Suitable out-of-sample or prospective tests for a new question may be designed separately, but completing a design does not count as proving capability. [T-forecast]
argumentSteps: Premise: available records, understanding of mechanisms, and subsequent conditions are limited; real-world states are not fully determined by text.
Inferential connection: a more complete contract may expose unknowns and dependencies, but document structure cannot establish factual truth or future stability.
Responsibility of explanation: retain unexplained residuals and competing candidates, allow supported local conclusions, and do not eliminate counterexamples through theoretical vocabulary.
Responsibility of foresight: fix targets, horizons, baselines, and evaluation before results; afterward, check on the same basis and continue comparisons across subsequent tasks.
Responsibility of choice: retain the actual path of inaction and every cost-bearing position, while separately checking value premises, permissions, and protections.
Conclusion: grounded judgments and constructive options may be proposed now, but additional foresight capability cannot certify itself through complexity or the quantity of narrative.

Evidential ceiling: four teaching scores establish only arithmetic differences in that artificial sample; the NHC paper's limited evaluation conclusions do not transfer into certification of this framework.

caseNotes.title: Historical methodological example: an updated version still requires evaluation on independent cases
caseNotes.text: Discussing the 2020 version of T-CLIPER, DeMaria et al.'s 2022 paper distinguishes tests dependent on development data from the 2020 season comparison: the new version improved at most forecast horizons, but that season's sample was insufficient to show statistical significance, and evaluation on independent cases from more years was still needed. The additional observation concerns evaluation limits, rather than repeating §1.1's account of the model's purpose. [R-NHC]

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: four scores are not determined by length
teachingExamples.text: Suppose four fictional parcel-arrival counts share the same horizon, with true labels set for teaching at 10, 12, 8, and 10 items. A simple baseline predicts 10 items all four times; a complex model predicts 12 all four times. Evaluate using a pre-specified mean absolute error: baseline errors are 0, 2, 2, and 0 items, averaging (0+2+2+0)/4=1 item; complex-model errors are 2, 0, 4, and 2 items, averaging (2+0+4+2)/4=2 items. The complex model's exact hit on the second occasion still does not make it better overall across the four occasions.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All numbers are artificially constructed; predictions are fixed before each label appears; targets, time windows, available-information cutoffs, and evaluation rules are the same; labels are complete, and no response regime changes the target.
teachingExamples.boundary: Establishes only the arithmetic comparison in this construction. It is not an out-of-sample capability study and cannot establish the long-term relative merits or statistical significance of real-world methods.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: aggregates must not erase cost-bearing positions
teachingExamples.text: Assume for demonstration that an additive benefit score is accepted: 9 people each gain 1 point and 1 person loses 8, giving a total of 9−8=1. A positive total can coexist with a concentrated burden on one person. Implementation still requires examining whether scores are truly comparable, basic protection, consent, and authorization; this example does not authorize trading others’ losses for aggregate growth.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The people and scores are artificial assumptions; additivity is only a mathematical assumption used to distinguish totals from distributions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Real dignity, rights, and harms may not be commensurable; this total must not be used to make any actual policy decision.

questionAnswers.question: Does filling every field in a contract make the factual judgment sufficiently supported?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. Observations, assumptions, candidates, and unknowns must still be distinguished, and the material checked for support of the answer.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 175 and §11.3.1.

questionAnswers.question: If the complex model scores one exact hit in the four teaching examples, does it have a smaller mean error?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Its mean absolute error is 2 tasks, compared with the baseline’s 1; one successful instance must not be cherry-picked.
questionAnswers.basis: The explicit calculation in this section.

questionAnswers.question: If outcome labels have not been obtained, may 0 be entered to mean the event did not occur?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A missing label does not mean the event did not occur and cannot be scored as 0 under the same rule.

questionAnswers.question: If an updated model performs better at most forecast horizons in one season, but the sample is too small for significance, has a stable gain been established?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Report the comparison and uncertainty accurately and continue independent evaluation; nor may one claim that no difference has been proved.
questionAnswers.basis: R-NHC, updated-version comparison on page 2151, and this section’s boundaries.

questionAnswers.question: Must all local conclusions be withdrawn because a model is incomplete?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. If compatible states give the same answer to the current question, a limited conclusion can be retained; only the part whose key answers differ needs to be limited.

questionAnswers.question: Should inaction enter the comparison because it is necessarily safest?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It too has changes, harms, and responsibilities; retaining it serves comparison of actual alternative paths.

1.10.title: 1.10 A Common Grammar and Multiple Paths to Understanding
1.10.lead: Choose methods from the specific differences; common terminology helps check reasons without monopolizing the names of learning, meaning, love, and local help.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 179–190, headed “1.10 A Common Grammar and Multiple Paths to Understanding”; page anchor /theory/part-01#section-1-10. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “These paths have no fixed order of value” (line 183). This section avoids two forms of closure: choosing one grand cause before explaining all material, and letting the framework’s technical names decide whether everyday experience has value. [T-110]

Starting from a concrete puzzle means first identifying the difference to explain. Why one rule produces different results at different positions requires checking implementation, accessible resources, and positional conditions. Why a genuine improvement leaves long-term circumstances unchanged requires separating the local target, window, and other continuing constraints. Why lived experience does not enter an indicator requires examining the observation definition and omissions, rather than declaring experience invalid. These questions can connect but are not identical; materials and methods must follow the difference being asked about. [T-110; T-position]

Structure, psychology, interests, culture, and technology are possible explanatory entry points, not final causes granted priority by their names. Saying “it is all institutions,” “all mindset,” or “all technology” still does not explain who changed what, through which channel, under which conditions. Sound analysis puts competing explanations against material. When a technical mechanism is sufficient, technology may provide the main explanation without an unsupported psychological story. [T-110; T-practice]

Shared practice makes the process of action visible, including actual working rules, collaboration sequences, and exception handling. The circumstances of those bearing burdens reveal who spends time, what the body bears, whether refusal is possible, and resource limits. Intertemporal relations bring recurring rules, allocations, and carrier succession into explanation. The three paths may complement one another or receive different weight because a task needs only one; they establish no fixed value order placing practice below institutions, individuals below collectives, or the long term above the local. [T-110; T-practice; T-carry]

The source’s examples of equipment failure, local care, and public rules show that explanatory scope and value scope can differ. A failure may be explained mainly by a technical mechanism without personifying the equipment. An act of care can have value even without changing a collective state. Public rules may affect strangers, so face-to-face experience alone cannot establish all their consequences. Each claim still needs corresponding material; the general explanation cannot directly establish that a real arrangement has succeeded. [T-110]

“Knowledge and meaning do not hold only when they change a collective state” preserves room for ordinary understanding. Acquiring a skill, understanding history, appreciating a work, completing a game, or receiving comfort can be described through task performance, interpretation of the work, the person’s expression, or other appropriate material, without first proving organizational change. This does not declare that any self-report establishes all facts; it rejects using a narrow collective-mechanism criterion to cancel other appropriate evidence. [T-110; T-learning]

CM-LEARNING specifically addresses feedback-mediated learning: an effective return produces a retainable update, later rounds actually use it, and judgment rests on a predefined task comparison and the corresponding causal basis. Ordinary learning can also be supported by domain evidence. Failure to acquire this formal mechanism status cannot become “nothing was learned.” Conversely, learning a skill in the ordinary sense does not automatically certify that feedback mechanism, cross-context transfer, or net improvement. Completion with support and independent transfer after support is removed must also be judged separately. [T-learning]

HV03 addresses the orientation anchor interface: meaning material can first be retained; claiming that it becomes an effective anchor for a specified resource, action, or coordination outcome requires corresponding support. It is not the sole criterion of “meaningful.” HV11 addresses bounded human undertaking arrangements, separating action, cost, direction, voluntariness, and consequences. It is not a definition or detector of love or a personality ranking. High cost does not necessarily prove love or free consent, and easy companionship is not valueless because it lacks a high cost. [T-HV03; T-HV11]

When ordinary words enter formal judgments, state the meaning used. For example, “this learning helped” may mean only that someone mastered a task; it cannot silently become “CM-LEARNING has causal support.” “This repair made things a little easier for me” may be the person’s name for a local remedy; it cannot silently become complete recovery of the relationship, institution, and long-term life. Clear meanings enable dialogue among knowledge traditions rather than requiring everyone to learn terminology before they may speak. [T-110]

Everyday “small repair” should retain three things: who names it that way, what actually changed, and which losses continue. Reconnecting or adjusting a living arrangement may genuinely help, but the analyst cannot declare recovery on the person’s behalf. Ordinary help does not require pre-registration to exist. If the framework’s formal repair criteria are used, disclose target identity K* or function F* before outcomes, then check attainment. Attainment does not mean a return to the historical original or improvement in value; target justification, decision authority, and implementation authority remain separate inquiries. [T-110; T-repair]

Historical material makes this boundary concrete. In Part I, Chapter IV of The Story of My Life, Helen Keller recalls linking finger-spelling to water at the pump and describes changes in her desire to learn and emotions. This recollection permits discussion of how she understood that learning experience without first naming it collective-state change. It does not independently identify every learning mechanism or allow an outsider to measure her or her teacher’s love from a single narrative. [R-Keller]

A complete analysis connects the question, evidence, main explanation, strongest objection, judgment, and limits, and tells readers what new material would change the judgment. The strongest objection is not an obviously mistaken opinion inserted casually; it is the strongest competing condition for the main explanation. Even while other questions remain unresolved, an independently supported local answer can be given. Unsupported parts remain unknown rather than having their gaps hidden by fluent prose. [T-110; T-identify]

The strongest objection asks whether retaining multiple paths makes every explanation equally correct. It does not. No fixed value order does not mean no evidential differences: materials can still exclude an explanation, and a local target can still receive a clear answer. The common grammar makes objects, meanings, evidence, and boundaries mutually checkable. Understanding can end here; eligibility for foresight, high-impact adoption, and real-world action require additional responsibilities and do not follow automatically from understanding’s value. [T-110; T-purpose]
argumentSteps: Premise: the same phenomenon can include practices, burden-bearing positions, and intertemporal relations, but the current question need not develop all three equally.

Methodological connection: first identify the difference to explain, then compare technical, psychological, structural, and other mechanisms using relevant material, without allowing causal labels to prove themselves.

Semantic connection: ordinary learning, meaning, and love serve different purposes from specialized mechanisms/interfaces; retain their respective evidential requirements rather than inferring the nonexistence of ordinary experience from an unmet narrow contract.

Repair boundary: everyday help and naming can be described through appropriate materials; formal repair separately checks targets declared before outcomes and responsibility, without erasing ongoing loss through local improvement.
Conclusion: the common grammar makes arguments checkable but is not the only entry to value and knowledge; independently grounded local conclusions and understanding as an endpoint remain possible.

Testing the objection: multiple paths must not become “everything is right”; specify the strongest competing explanation, counterevidence, and material that would change the judgment, and add the corresponding responsibilities when widening the use.

distinctions.rightText: A specific feedback-mediated mechanism requiring checks of retention, use, task comparison, and related conditions.

distinctions.rightText: Its interface effect on a specified outcome requires separate support.

distinctions.leftText: Their definition cannot be monopolized by one interface in this framework.

distinctions.leftText: Retains who names it, the local change, and continuing loss.

distinctions.leftText: Compares different observational positions and mechanisms according to the question.
distinctions.rightText: Does not permit unsupported explanations to be treated as equal to supported ones.

boundaries: Source boundary: local care can have value of its own and public rules can affect strangers; no fixed value ranking is assigned by individual/collective or local/long-term categories.

Constructed conditional counterexample: someone repeatedly solves a newly learned type of chess problem while organizational institutions remain unchanged. This cannot negate the corresponding task learning, nor can it directly establish cross-domain transfer.

Constructed conditional counterexample: preparing one meal for a caregiver genuinely helps, but if reminders, shopping, scheduling, and overnight standby remain with them, it cannot establish that the entire burden has been taken up by someone else.

Constructed conditional counterexample: repairing a desk lamp restores its reading function while the shade remains damaged. If the target is only illumination, that local target can be checked; it cannot be renamed full restoration to the historical original.

Absence of a predeclared formal repair target does not cancel ordinary help. But one must not pick an easily attained target after the outcome and falsely claim success against an originally registered formal repair target.

A memoir is the person’s retrospective expression, with narrative selection and memory limitations; it is not a contemporaneous independent experiment, and one person’s experience cannot represent everyone.

caseNotes.text: In Part I, Chapter IV of The Story of My Life (1903), Keller recalls Sullivan spelling water into one hand while she felt flowing water with the other; she describes the connection between word and thing and subsequent changes in curiosity and emotion. This brings personal experience into understanding while retaining the boundaries of recollection as a genre. [R-Keller]

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: the scope of care assistance cannot quietly expand
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional situation, A originally cooks, reminds someone to take medication, arranges appointments, and remains on overnight standby. B cooks two meals this week, and A says “things are a little easier.” The given material supports help with executing two meals and preserves A’s expressed experience. If scheduling, reminders, and standby remain with A, it does not establish that all care has been taken up or the long-term burden has disappeared. Whether B acts voluntarily and can refuse also requires independent material.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All people and arrangements are teaching assumptions; A’s statement is a condition within the construction, not a real interview.
teachingExamples.boundary: No real family division of labor is presumed, and the degree of help does not automatically become an unlimited duty or formal HV11 eligibility.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a lamp’s functional target and its historical original
teachingExamples.text: A fictional repair discloses functional target F* before the outcome: after replacing the switch, the lamp continuously provides the predefined illumination under a specified power supply during a 10-minute inspection window; the shade’s appearance is excluded. If inspection materials support this target, the function target was attained within that window. The appearance cannot also be declared restored, nor can 10 minutes be extrapolated to long-term reliability. If “it still lights briefly” is adopted only at the end, it does not satisfy the original formal target’s test.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A conditional construction explaining a target contract, not electrical-repair guidance or an actual experiment; the inspection window and conditions are artificial assumptions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Attainment is limited to the declared window and function; actual repair authority, safety, and target justification require separate checks.

questionAnswers.question: If the mainly technical evidence for an equipment failure is already sufficient, must a psychological cause be added?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Methods follow questions and materials; causal labels have no fixed priority, and an unsupported psychological narrative adds no explanation.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 181–183.

questionAnswers.question: Without a CM-LEARNING instance, can one say a person acquired a skill?
questionAnswers.answer: Ordinary learning can be stated on appropriate domain evidence; the formal feedback-mediated mechanism, transfer, and net effects are judged separately.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 185 and §6.3.

questionAnswers.question: If A calls an act of help a small repair, may the analyst directly declare A’s life restored?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Retain A's own naming, the actual change, and the continuing loss; complete recovery is a broader claim still requiring proof.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 187.

questionAnswers.question: Does meeting the lamp’s functional target prove that its shade is restored, that it is reliable long term, and that the repairer necessarily had authority?
questionAnswers.answer: Neither automatically establishes the other. Target scope, time window, and authority must each be established.

questionAnswers.question: If multiple paths to understanding have no fixed value order, does that mean no judgments can be made?
questionAnswers.answer: No. One may compare evidence, exclude explanations, and give a clear local judgment while also disclosing the strongest objection and conditions for revising the judgment.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 175 and 189.

questionAnswers.question: What can Keller’s recollection support, and what can it not support?
questionAnswers.answer: It can support an account of how she narrates learning and meaning in that memoir. Alone, it cannot identify every mechanism, prove the framework, or measure love.
questionAnswers.basis: The status and boundaries of R-Keller material.

figures.caption: An author-made diagram of multiple paths. The columns imply no ranking of value and do not require all three paths to receive equal depth in every question.

figures.alt: Ordinary learning, meaning, concern, and small acts of help may each be discussed using appropriate material. CM-LEARNING, HV03, HV11, and formal repair address only their respective bounded questions.

1.10.diagramBrief: Figure 1 places three paths of understanding alongside one another without making a hierarchy of value. Figure 2 lists the different questions concerning ordinary experience and specialized judgments, showing that failure to meet a narrow contract does not cancel experience. HV03 and similar terms are not drawn as comprehensive definitions of meaning or love.

1.11.title: 1.11 Conditions for connecting judgments
1.11.lead: An established earlier judgment can enter the next stage only with its conditions attached. Locate the break before deciding whether to add information, revise a rule, or change an arrangement.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 191–200, heading “1.11 Conditions for connecting judgments”; assembled anchor /theory/part-01#section-1-11. A short quotation translated from Chinese reads, “Revision should address the actual point of failure” (Chinese source line 195). This section grounds structural explanation in conditions for connecting judgments, rejecting both automatic promotion of local success and withdrawal of every local result because the entire chain is incomplete. [T-111]

The first connection concerns information representation. An aggregate may suffice to answer a question about totals while losing distinctions needed to answer a distributional question. Check which answer the question requires, rather than asking only whether data have been reduced. The factorization q=g∘π gives a positive condition: source state x is represented as y through π; if every source state corresponding to the same y gives the same answer to q, q can be answered using y alone, without first reconstructing all of x. Satisfaction of this condition for one question does not automatically extend to another question or intervention. [T-F1]

The public proof is short. If q=g∘π already holds, π(x)=π(x′) necessarily gives q(x)=g(π(x))=g(π(x′))=q(x′). Conversely, if q is constant among states with the same representation, choose, for any actually reachable y, an x such that π(x)=y and define g(y)=q(x). Because all x corresponding to the same y give the same answer, this definition is independent of the choice, and q=g∘π. The proof is limited to the given domain, representation, and target. It does not guarantee that g is easy to compute, that material is available in time, or that implementation is possible or adoption authorized. [T-F1]

The second connection concerns causal effects. Two positive average causal edges in the same population may still be carried by subgroups that do not connect: one group carries the first stage's change in the mediator, while another carries the mediator's effect on the outcome. The two average edges therefore cannot simply be multiplied into a whole-chain effect. Evidence is needed concerning common response ranges, correspondence within cases, states, timing, capacity, cancellation, and parallel paths. A bounded total effect already identified by a qualified study may be retained. This section does not require knowing every microscopic mechanism before acknowledging any effect. [T-chain]

The third connection concerns joint implementation. Two independently feasible plans may both occupy the same staff member during the same period. Placing the plans together does not create a second unit of capacity. Concurrent implementation requires adequate concurrent resources and compatible dependencies and deadlines. Additional future capacity or an authorized extension may create a new plan; neither rewrites a task that missed its original deadline as completed. [T-joint]

The fourth connection runs from authorization to outcomes. Lawful authorization only permits something within the corresponding conditions. It does not prove that notice arrived, those concerned understood, resources were ready, action occurred, or effects took hold. A safety window requires checking the entire connection through detection, verification, issuance, reach, understanding, resource mobilization, and onset of effect. Completion of one earlier node does not establish that everyone at the end is protected. Conversely, an action's occurrence does not establish that it originally had authority. [T-purpose；T-time]

Connections can fail in at least seven kinds of location. If representation lacks a necessary distinction, add the smallest task-relevant distinction. If identification is insufficient, seek material distinguishing compatible explanations. If clocks or delays do not fit, adjust sequence or windows, or reopen comparison. If capacity is insufficient, change resources or the task combination. If a rule is wrong, correct it. If material exists but cannot be obtained in time, change access or decision arrangements. If authority is absent, seek appropriate authorization or stop the real action. These failures may coexist, but cannot all be called “complexity,” still less treated as problems solvable merely by adding variables. [T-111；T-F1；T-joint]

“Inputs, outputs, conditions, and failure modes” are not a form-filling ritual: they tell the next step what the previous step actually delivered. If the earlier step supports only a total, the next cannot assume knowledge of the distribution. If it yields only a candidate mechanism, the next cannot treat it as established reality. If it provides only a theoretically computable answer, timely access or implementation resources may still be missing. Revision should affect precisely the conclusions dependent on that break; earlier results with independent grounds remain. [T-111；T-missing]

Conditionality also enables affirmative conclusions. A representation sufficient for the task can answer it; a bounded total effect supported by qualified domain evidence can be reported; when assistance forms part of the task, expression or function achieved under that assistance can be a real accomplishment. Asking instead about independent performance without assistance requires separate evidence. One cannot retrospectively dismiss the assisted accomplishment, nor directly treat it as independent recovery. [T-111；T-learning]

Willett and colleagues' 2023 study used a brain–computer interface in one participant to decode attempted speech into text and evaluated it in real time using sentences excluded from training. There is describable task performance under assistance, while the authors explicitly state that this is not yet a complete clinically usable system and requires validation in more participants. This historical study illustrates retaining both bounded accomplishments and further limitations. This lesson offers no treatment advice and does not recast the demonstration as recovery of unassisted speech. [R-BCI]

Connections must be checked again when the question, operation, object, or window changes. Moving from totals to distribution changes the target; from natural change to intervention changes the operation; from the training population to unseen people changes the object; from availability today to persistence over years changes the window. This does not overturn the original conclusion every time: it asks whether the original evidence covers the new claim and identifies unresolved points where it does not. [T-111；T-F1；T-learning]

Finally, five kinds of work assist one another without substantiating one another by substitution: common grammar organizes questions; formal contracts delimit valid inferences; domain evidence supports empirical conclusions; normative reasons constrain choices; engineering implementation makes the method run. Demonstrating that a procedure runs does not establish factual correctness; factual correctness does not establish justified choice; a correct normative purpose does not establish an effective action. A shorter professional method should be allowed when sufficient. More complex representations must explain which necessary distinctions they preserve and the measurement, privacy, computational, and maintenance costs they add. [T-111；T-baseline]

The strongest objection is whether adding conditions to every edge drags practice into endless checking. The response is to locate the critical connections for the current objective and consequences, retain professional conclusions that are already sufficient, and not demand irrelevant detail. Only gaps that would change the task's answer or the feasibility of action block the corresponding connection. Continuing to refine an explanation despite a known failure of deadline or authority usually does not repair the actual break. [T-111；T-identify]
argumentSteps: Premise: different tasks require different information, local effects may come from different objects, and joint actions share time, capacity, and authority.

Representational inference: all states with the same representation give the same target answer if and only if a decoder using only that representation exists. The proof is limited to the given model.
Causal inference: local average effects do not supply the joint response distribution and cannot unconditionally compose a whole chain. Independently supported total effects may still be retained.
Implementation inference: separate feasibility meets each plan's own constraints; joint implementation must also satisfy shared capacity, dependencies, and deadlines.

Revision conclusion: locate the actual break, then add the corresponding distinctions, change rules, adjust windows/resources, or check authority. One kind of repair cannot substitute for every missing condition.
Positive conclusion: task sufficiency, bounded effects, and assisted function can all be established according to evidence. A change in task or use adds its corresponding responsibilities.
Overall boundary: grammar, form, empirical evidence, norms, and engineering each bear distinct responsibilities; none alone confers eligibility on the others.

distinctions.leftText: The existing representation can already answer the sum.
distinctions.rightText: Position or distributional distinctions must also be retained.

distinctions.leftText: Each local average effect has corresponding support.
distinctions.rightText: Earlier and later effects must connect in objects, states, clocks, and other relevant respects.

distinctions.leftText: Each plan independently meets resource constraints.
distinctions.rightText: Implementing them together additionally requires checking shared capacity and dependencies.

distinctions.leftText: Permits implementation under specified conditions.
distinctions.rightText: Reach, execution, and outcomes require separate factual evidence.

distinctions.leftText: Support may be a constituent condition of the task itself.
distinctions.rightText: The target changes and requires separate testing.

boundaries: Explicit elaboration of the original text's formal counterexample: two equally weighted subgroups each carry only one stage; each edge's average effect is 1/2, but the whole chain's effect is 0. See the teaching equations.

Author-constructed conditional counterexample: two tasks each require 1 hour and must be completed within the same 1-hour window, using the sole shared worker. Separately, 1≤1 holds; jointly, 2≤1 does not.
Author-constructed conditional counterexample: an approved notice remains in the sending queue and has not reached the target population. Approval does not establish that protection arrived.

Author-constructed conditional counterexample: a report contains complete components, but the user sums the wrong columns. The failure is in the calculation rule; collecting more components alone will not correct it.

Existence of a function factorization establishes only informational sufficiency for the given question. Implementation may still fail if the algorithm cannot finish before the deadline, or access or authority is absent.

Restricting multiplication of edge effects does not revoke a bounded total effect already supported by a qualified comparison. Nor is assisted function categorically denied because performance without assistance still fails.
Assisted task performance in the BCI study does not equal curing disease, unassisted natural speech, or general clinical usability. Discussion is limited to the historical conditions of that paper.
questions: With only a total of 10, can one determine whether A has at least 5 items?
Why need two average causal edges of 1/2 not produce a whole-chain effect of 1/4?
If two projects each require 1 person-hour and only 1 person-hour is available this period, can both be promised together?
If the calculation rule is wrong, will increased measurement precision automatically fix it?
If someone successfully expresses themselves with an assistive device but cannot do so after it is removed, does that cancel the original accomplishment?
If engineering software runs successfully, may one declare empirical validity and authorization for adoption?

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: the same total can answer a totals question, but not necessarily a distributional question
teachingExamples.text: Let the artificial state domain be X={(4,6),(6,4),(7,3)}, where the two numbers count items at positions A and B, and let π(a,b)=a+b. All three states give 10. For target q总=a+b, g(y)=y recovers the answer. For target q阈=“Does A have at least 5 items?”, the answers are no, yes, yes. The same representation 10 cannot decode simultaneously to no and yes, so the total alone is insufficient. Adding a binary field r=“Does A have at least 5 items?” makes the representation (total,r) sufficient for that threshold target, while still leaving (6,4) and (7,3) indistinguishable.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All three states and item counts are artificially defined, without measurement error. The target is a distributional threshold, not actual welfare or fairness.
teachingExamples.boundary: The proof concerns only the given domain and target. Whether the component material and fields are available in reality requires separate investigation; this does not automatically permit collection.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a reproducible model of the original text's two equally weighted subgroups
teachingExamples.text: Let G be 0 or 1, each with weight one half, and let event A be 0 or 1. Define mediator M=(1−G)A and outcome Y=G·M, with no other causal channel. In the G=0 group, A changes M from 0 to 1, but M does not affect Y. In the G=1 group, A does not change M, but intervening to change M from 0 to 1 changes Y from 0 to 1. Thus the average effect of A on M is (1+0)/2=1/2, and the average intervention effect of M on Y is (0+1)/2=1/2. Following the original mechanism gives Y=G(1−G)A=0 in both groups. The whole-chain effect of A on Y through M is therefore 0, not (1/2)×(1/2)=1/4.
teachingExamples.assumptions: This is an explicit binary mathematical implementation of the original counterexample in §11.6. G is fixed and exogenous, the groups have equal weight, the equations are fully specified, and intervention on the mediator replaces the M equation. It is not an actual study.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not establish that all real mediation effects are noncomposable. It only rejects unconditional multiplication without common response conditions.

counterexamples.text: Explicit elaboration of the original text's formal counterexample: two equally weighted subgroups each carry only one stage; each edge's average effect is 1/2, but the whole chain's effect is 0. See the teaching equations.
counterexamples.effect: Two average edge effects do not provide joint responses and cannot be multiplied unconditionally.

counterexamples.text: Author-constructed conditional counterexample: two tasks each require 1 hour and must be completed within the same 1-hour window, using the sole shared worker. Separately, 1≤1 holds; jointly, 2≤1 does not.
counterexamples.effect: Distinguish breaks in capacity, arrival, and rules to prevent local completion from masquerading as overall feasibility.

counterexamples.text: Author-constructed conditional counterexample: an approved notice remains in the sending queue and has not reached the target population. Approval does not establish that protection arrived.
counterexamples.effect: Distinguish breaks in capacity, arrival, and rules to prevent local completion from masquerading as overall feasibility.

counterexamples.text: Author-constructed conditional counterexample: a report contains complete components, but the user sums the wrong columns. The failure is in the calculation rule; collecting more components alone will not correct it.
counterexamples.effect: Distinguish breaks in capacity, arrival, and rules to prevent local completion from masquerading as overall feasibility.

questionAnswers.question: With only a total of 10, can one determine whether A has at least 5 items?
questionAnswers.answer: Not in this example: (4,6) and (6,4) have the same total but different answers. Adding a threshold field answers this target without distinguishing every state.
questionAnswers.basis: F1 and this section's three-state construction.

questionAnswers.question: Why need two average causal edges of 1/2 not produce a whole-chain effect of 1/4?
questionAnswers.answer: Earlier and later responses may occur in different subgroups. In this model G(1−G)=0, so no single group completes both stages.
questionAnswers.basis: §11.6 and the explicit equations.

questionAnswers.question: If two projects each require 1 person-hour and only 1 person-hour is available this period, can both be promised together?
questionAnswers.answer: Both cannot be completed within the given common deadline: joint demand 2 exceeds capacity 1. Changing the deadline or adding capacity creates a new plan requiring its own grounds and authority.

questionAnswers.question: If the calculation rule is wrong, will increased measurement precision automatically fix it?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The incorrect rule must be corrected. Insufficient data and an incorrect rule are different breaks.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 195.

questionAnswers.question: If someone successfully expresses themselves with an assistive device but cannot do so after it is removed, does that cancel the original accomplishment?
questionAnswers.answer: If the target originally allowed that support, the accomplishment remains; it does not establish independent recovery without support.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 197 and §6.3.

questionAnswers.question: If engineering software runs successfully, may one declare empirical validity and authorization for adoption?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Execution, empirical support, normative reasons, and authority require separate judgments.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 199.

1.12.title: 1.12 Theoretical Structure and Burdens of Argument
1.12.lead: First identify the burden of argument a statement bears, then ask how it is established; the number of identifiers cannot replace proof, real-world evidence or effectiveness in use.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 201–212, titled “1.12 Theoretical Structure and Burdens of Argument”; assembly anchor /theory/part-01#section-1-12. Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “theoretical strength is not accumulated by counting” (line 205). This section concludes the reading guide: the book organizes different work involving definitions, method, formal analysis, empirical inquiry, norms and procedures, rather than assembling one deductive chain that derives everything from a few axioms of nature. [T-112]

Definitions first specify what is being discussed, such as the return and subsequent change required for “effective feedback.” A definition can standardize terminology but cannot make a particular real feedback event happen automatically. Method constraints specify how to distinguish observation, reports, assumptions, simulations and proofs, how to limit transfer and retain counterexamples. They constrain analysts' inferences; they do not by themselves become laws the world necessarily follows. Both are starting points for organizing judgments, not empirical certification. [T-roles; T-method]

Conditional formal propositions are established by proof within explicit models. If assumptions about the state domain, mapping, target and operations hold, bounded relations can follow; mapping actual objects into those variables still requires independent evidence. Particular assertions in empirical question families and mechanism propositions need support or refutation from real-world materials and are not exempt from testing because they are written as formulas. Normative reasons state what is protected and why a choice is made; operational procedures arrange adoption, authorization, execution and correction. Correct facts do not automatically create these qualifications. [T-roles; T-form]

G1–G4 are entry points for four kinds of empirical question. G1 asks what a candidate grouping adds in a specified comparison. G2 asks about the effects of a specified channel and limits in measured dimensions. G3 asks whether stated historical variables add relevant information or causal explanation beyond the given current representation. G4 asks about representational closure and conditions for object/intervention conversion. These are not four universally established laws of nature: particular conclusions must bind their objects, targets, windows, comparison designs and failure modes. [T-G]

Whether a particular effect exists and whether current evidence is sufficient for formal support eligibility are different questions. Lack of registration, insufficient material or failure to pass an instance check does not directly mean the real effect is absent. Conversely, being able to formulate a question theoretically does not mean the instance is already true. Existing domain research may support its own bounded conclusions and must not be discarded solely because it does not use this framework's format. [T-roles; T-domain]

C1–C12 are not twelve facts of the same type. They govern how limited results can be used and how additional conditions can be combined. For example, C1 registers appropriately supported object/boundary judgments; C3 separates feedback, carrier learning and historical-increment learning; C8 has its own conditions for variation, differential retention and reproduction patterns; C12 bridges normative procedures rather than stating empirical causation. Listing several G names does not establish a C mechanism, and not every C must be derived from all G instances. [T-C]

F1–F6 are formal relations with specified objects and proofs, addressing task recovery; closure of dynamics and admissible interventions; common actions under information constraints; task preservation through successive conversions; error propagation under approximate closure; and task families and dynamic refinement. Their names serve here only as precise guideposts to argument; specific premises and proofs remain in §§4.18–4.19 and Appendix C. The F in F1 does not share a numbering scheme with the repair-function target F* or other local functions F; identical letters must not be conflated. [T-form; T-index]

The three numbering schemes therefore serve different purposes: G locates empirical questions, C supports bounded use or combination of results, and F helps check derivations within a given model. Adding 4, 12 and 6 yields 22 numbered positions, not 22 independent bodies of evidence, and does not prove the theory stronger than a shorter framework. Repeated numbering of the same materials or multiple explanations of the same example do not create additional independent observations. [T-112; T-method]

The source's first example distinguishes historical formation from conditional residuals. Practice can change current skills, which then affect later performance. If current skills sufficiently represent the effects relevant to the task, knowing the complete practice history may not further improve prediction. This “absence of additional information” does not cancel practice's formative effects or existing learning. If skill measurement is coarse, history may still add information; if an increment appears, distinguish improved current representation, predictive association and causal historical grounds rather than calling all of them irreversible destiny. [T-112; T-history; T-learning]

The second example distinguishes totals from local overload. Equal total demand and capacity can correctly answer whether totals are equal while one position's demand exceeds its own capacity and another remains idle. Whether resources can be reallocated, tasks are of the same type and the same window applies determines whether totals answer local questions. Identifying a distributional gap does not overturn the total calculation. The current task determines which distinction to add, and an instantaneous shortfall alone must not be presented as evidence that cumulative damage has already occurred. [T-112; T-load; T-F1]

The common method distinguishes what can be established, what cannot be carried forward by inference and what needs supplementation. Retain local conclusions about skills or totals that existing evidence supports. Precisely locate unresolved matters when material is missing for historical increments beyond the current representation or local overload. This avoids both absorbing every domain phenomenon into the same strong conclusion and declaring that nothing can be known whenever a limit appears. [T-112; T-missing]

The framework itself must also face comparisons capable of changing conclusions. A proposition fitting the materials does not establish that its classification is simplest; support for one instance does not establish the mechanism in every object; a logically rigorous manuscript does not establish that readers or tools perform better by using it. Instance effects, prevalence of applicability in an object population and the framework's net benefit in use are three distinct empirical targets, each requiring its own sampling, targets, controls and extrapolation scope. [T-evaluation]

Comparisons with professional and streamlined methods must give each side the same necessary materials, task and input cutoff, without removing protections to manufacture a faster comparator. Evaluate consequential misjudgments, valid answers, retention of unknowns, time and burdens separately: are fewer errors merely the result of refusing many questions? Do more answers include unsupported assertions? Does greater speed shift verification work to readers? Does greater breadth increase disclosure risks or maintenance costs? Without explicit normative weights, these different dimensions must not be forced into a single victory score. [T-112; T-evaluation; T-retire]

A comparison design that this task can propose but has not carried out would first select materials with explicit tasks and verifiable answer boundaries, fixing the cutoff, budget, permitted tools and protections. It would use the full framework method, a sufficiently strong domain method and a streamlined method as actual comparators; independently evaluate them under preset rules for error severity, valid answers and improper refusal; and record total time, disclosure and maintenance work. Where appropriate and authorized, random assignment or balanced ordering could reduce differences in tasks and practice. All of this is research design, not evidence of effects already obtained; there are no human-participant or reader-trial results. [T-evaluation; T-retire]

The strongest objection is whether the framework becomes a loose checklist if its parts are not unified into axioms. What matters is not a single deductive origin but explicit connections, checkable responsibilities at each layer and whether using it is more useful than sufficient alternatives. This response identifies what must be tested; it does not guarantee the framework will win. If alternatives consistently perform better on the relevant tasks, downgrading, retirement and handover should be allowed. Without a comparison, one must not instead claim equivalence or uselessness has been proven. [T-112; T-retire]
argumentSteps: Premise: definitions, formal proofs, empirical tests, normative reasons and operational procedures have different conditions of establishment.
Inferential connection: completing one responsibility does not automatically complete others; numbering can organize questions but produces no additional facts.

Historical example: current skills can carry the effects of past practice; zero historical increment after conditioning on a sufficient current representation is compatible with past formative effects.
Total-quantity example: an aggregate representation can suffice for totals while merging states with different answers about local overload; add distinctions according to the task.
Conclusion: retain established limited results, reject connections that overstep representation, evidence, norms or permissions, and locate unresolved matters in their specific dependencies.

Framework self-check: compare local propositional support, rates of applicability and net benefit in use separately; comparators must retain the same necessary materials and protections and report multidimensional costs.

Current judgment: this task explains theoretical roles and provides reproducible constructions; it has no comparative data on actual adoption and must not claim the framework improves real-world performance.

boundaries: Constructed conditional counterexample: treating “feedback's definition includes subsequent change” as “having a complaints mailbox means the institution has already changed.” A definition does not generate that empirical fact.

Constructed conditional counterexample: one G2 instance supports a channel, followed by the claim that all channels in all domains work. The object, window and channel have been extended beyond their boundaries.

Constructed conditional counterexample: current skill fully determines task performance within a model, and adding practice history does not improve prediction, so practice is declared never to have had an effect. This mistakes conditional increment for historical formation.

Constructed conditional counterexample: equal total demand and capacity across two positions is used to declare that neither is overloaded. Distribution and reallocation conditions have not been checked.

Constructed conditional counterexample: a streamlined method omits all privacy and verification requirements, runs faster and is declared superior to the full method. The compared tasks and protection conditions are no longer the same.

Formal constructions do not establish real learning or overload mechanisms. This task has not experimentally evaluated the framework's net benefit in use and has no grounds to claim uselessness or equivalence either.
