teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: history operates through current skills while additional historical information can still be zero
teachingExamples.text: Let the artificial binary variable H indicate whether stipulated practice was completed, current skill S=H, and later task score Y=10S. This is a specified teaching mechanism, not observational data. Within the model, changing H from 0 to 1 changes Y from 0 to 10 through S. But once S is known, Y is uniquely determined, and additional records of H cannot distinguish Y further. Thus “history adds no predictive information conditional on S” and “practice affects performance through S within the model” can both be true.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The equations, causal direction and sufficient skill measurement are entirely stipulated; there are no unmeasured conditions or random errors, and no actual training was performed.
teachingExamples.boundary: This model is not described as having passed a real-world G3 test and does not establish learning mechanisms in real people. The conclusion may change if real skill measurement is insufficient.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: equal totals do not identify local overload
teachingExamples.text: In the same hour, A and B each have capacity for 4 tasks, and tasks cannot move between them within this window. Demand is (4,4) in state one and (8,0) in state two. Both have total demand of 8 tasks and total capacity of 8. No position exceeds capacity in state one; in state two, A's demand exceeds its own capacity by 4 tasks while B is idle. The total 8 alone cannot determine “whether any position's demand exceeds capacity.”
teachingExamples.assumptions: Tasks are quantities of the same work type; the window and capacity of each position are fully specified. There is no task transfer, substitute personnel or postponement. All numbers are teaching constructions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Only demand–capacity relations within the same window are calculated; no real harm, malicious allocation, cumulative overload mechanism or value conclusion is presumed.

questionAnswers.question: Does a large number of D, G, C, F and other identifiers mean that the theory has more evidence?
questionAnswers.answer: No. They organize different burdens of argument; adding identifiers creates no independent materials or proofs.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 203–205, §2.2 and Appendix B.

questionAnswers.question: If G3 shows no additional information, can learning in general be denied?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Current skills may already carry the effects of relevant practice; learning in general and conditional historical increments require separate evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 207 and §§4.5, 6.3.

questionAnswers.question: In the teaching example, what is Y when S=1? Can knowing H add to this answer within the model?
questionAnswers.answer: Y=10; since S uniquely determines Y, additional H cannot further distinguish this target answer.
questionAnswers.basis: The explicit equations in this section, limited to the construction.

questionAnswers.question: If two positions have total demand and total capacity of 8, why can local overload still occur?
questionAnswers.answer: With different allocations and no transfer, (8,0) puts A 4 above its own capacity; the total does not preserve that distinction.
questionAnswers.basis: This section's capacity construction within a common window.

questionAnswers.question: If a manuscript has passed rigorous structural checks, may readers be said to have benefited?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Structural correspondence differs from actual performance in use and requires an actual comparison; an unperformed reader trial must not be described as proven effectiveness.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 209 and §4.17.4.

questionAnswers.question: If the framework group has verification and protections but the streamlined group does not, can the comparison fairly establish which is faster and better?
questionAnswers.answer: Insufficient. Retain the same necessary materials and protection requirements, and examine whether work is shifted and how errors and refusals change.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 209 and §16.24.

questionAnswers.question: Without data on net gains, is the correct conclusion that the framework is useless?
questionAnswers.answer: No. At present one can state only intended uses and verified local results; superiority, equivalence and uselessness each require corresponding grounds.

figures.alt: Definitions clarify meanings; method checks materials and inference; formal propositions are proved within models; empirical assertions face testing against data; normative procedures constrain choice and action. G, C and F each serve as different guideposts.
figures.caption: A diagram of burdens of argument created by the explanatory author; parallel boxes are not an axiomatic derivation chain, and the theory is not scored by their number.

figures.alt: In the artificial skill example, H leads to S and S to Y; once S is known, H adds no information about Y. Loads (4,4) and (8,0) for two positions have the same total but different local overload.
figures.caption: Two mathematical teaching constructions, with stipulated numbers and causal equations; neither establishes real-world mechanisms or the framework's effects in use.

1.12.diagramBrief: Figure 1 places five kinds of responsibility side by side—definitions, methods, formal arguments, empirical claims, and norms/procedures—and separately marks the navigational functions of G/C/F, avoiding a single deductive ladder of natural axioms. Figure 2 uses two examples to distinguish historical formation from conditional increments, and aggregate tasks from local tasks. The figures are currently static. Any future switching control would change only the explicitly stated skill-measurement or distribution conditions, without generating real-world data.

applicability.reason: This unit explains the argumentative roles and self-evaluation responsibilities in the current text and develops its two types of formal/conditional example. It does not claim that a real-world mechanism or benefits from adopting this framework have been established. The relevant evidence consists of the manuscript and public derivations; unrelated historical stories do not substitute for effectiveness comparisons that the framework has not yet conducted.

openQuestions: No comparative data on the framework's actual net benefits of use against sufficient professional or simplified methods were obtained for this question. Superiority or equivalence therefore cannot be concluded.
The proposed evaluation design has not been carried out. Any future study involving actual readers would require appropriate authorization, protections, and materials from actual participation.

intro-02-part.title: Part 2 Boundaries and Methods
intro-02-part.lead: Whether something may enter discussion, what kind of support it can receive, and whether action may be based on it are three different questions. Part 2 first defines the theory's scope of use, then explains what evidence each kind of conclusion requires.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source, lines 213–220; original anchor part_2. Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Belonging to the broadly conceived empirical structural world means only that a contract can in principle be established.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the original research extract available for download preserves the historical manuscript.

Broadly conceived concerns the variety of objects: natural processes, technology, ecology, human action, and institutions may all be candidates. Empirical narrows admission: comparable materials must exist, and the object, states, relations or transitions, interfaces, time, scale, and identity must be made clear. This does not claim that a single mechanism already explains all these domains, still less prove that the world necessarily has a common purpose.

The human structured world is one class of these objects. Discussing people requires additional roles, culture, norms, and authorization. Human purposes must not be assigned to wind, water, algorithms, or ecological processes. Equally, the fact that an object concerns people does not make factual judgments inherently carry authority to act on them. Part 1's general outline is recast here as working boundaries; the later H, N, and O respectively take up domain adaptation, value premises, and operational procedures.

Each application must state its current contract anew: what the object is, which scale profile SP represents, which period T covers, and on what basis K identifies the earlier and later object as the same. Then specify environment, region, data window, extrapolation unit, and exclusions. The broad overall object domain does not replace this narrow contract. Modeling a queue in one window, for example, does not explain every queue or permit directly transplanting its treatment into another institutional setting.

Purely metaphysical propositions may be discussed as philosophical questions, but without comparable materials and empirical fields they cannot borrow this book's evidential levels for empirical judgments. This restriction concerns the status of the conclusion; it does not declare the question meaningless. Conversely, empirical fields merely allow a testable question to be posed. Specific support must still be established through subsequent instances.

distinctions.leftText: Which kinds of object may in principle be studied.
distinctions.rightText: The objects, time, scale, environment, and exclusions actually studied on this occasion.

distinctions.leftText: Explains how it forms, operates, undergoes conversion, or dissolves.
distinctions.rightText: Claims that it pursues a goal; this requires support from its object type and materials.

boundaries: A system without empirical fields cannot receive the standing of an empirical conclusion; nor does naming an observable object automatically confer formal G support.
Narrowing the scope of application generally corrects extrapolation; it does not withdraw all supported local facts.
Selection in natural processes, outputs of technical systems, and human intentions must not be equated merely because the same word for choice or selection appears.
questions: A conclusion comes from one term at one school. A researcher says, “Schools all belong to the human structured world, so it applies to every school.” What is missing?
If a mathematical model explains the outcome of resource allocation, has it already answered what distribution would be justified?
argumentSteps: Premise: empirical judgments require comparable materials and clear referents; otherwise, different observations cannot establish what is being compared.
Connection: a broad object domain cannot eliminate differences in environment, time, and measurement, so the overall scope must be narrowed to the current contract on each occasion.
Conclusion: structural explanation may be conducted across many kinds of object, but each conclusion holds only within a scope supported by materials and bridges.

Responsibility: description and explanation rest on materials and inference. Who should be protected and who may act additionally require disclosed normative premises and authorization; they cannot be inferred from the object's being open to study.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a scope contract for one conveyor belt
teachingExamples.text: Suppose the study covers only one conveyor segment during a factory's day shift. B is its entrance and exit, X its belt speed and number of queued items, R the arrival and departure rules, I the upstream and downstream interfaces, and T one shift. SP is a nine-axis profile: abbreviated here, A aggregation level is this equipment segment, X spatial extent runs from the specified entrance to exit, T time span is one shift, and R resolution is the registered sampling protocol for belt speed and the queue. K requires the equipment and interfaces to retain specified relations. The five axes not developed—O organization, C causation, I influence, N network, and J jurisdiction and authorization—are omitted only in this teaching example. A complete application must still register each axis's status, with reasons where genuinely inapplicable. SP must not be reduced to resolution alone. The example specifies which process segment is being asked about. If the product or interfaces change on the night shift, the old contract does not automatically cover it.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All equipment and periods are illustrative; no actual observational data are included.
teachingExamples.boundary: The example only shows what the fields are for. It neither establishes explanatory gain from this grouping nor authorizes changes to production.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: naming all things that go badly as a system without common states, a window, or comparable materials.
counterexamples.effect: A name cannot produce a testable empirical object. It may remain a narrative question, but must not be assigned a level of empirical support.

questionAnswers.question: A conclusion comes from one term at one school. A researcher says, “Schools all belong to the human structured world, so it applies to every school.” What is missing?
questionAnswers.answer: What is missing is a basis for bridging and extrapolation across objects, periods, and environments. Membership in one overall object domain merely permits study; it does not guarantee the same mechanism or effect.

questionAnswers.question: If a mathematical model explains the outcome of resource allocation, has it already answered what distribution would be justified?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The model may explain the results of given rules. Justification requires explicit value premises, benefits and risks, the decision-maker, and authorization procedures.

2.1.title: 2.1 Two-Stage Object Admission
2.1.lead: First state the question clearly, then test it. Registering a candidate is like specifying the address of a research question; formal support depends on comparisons and results agreed beforehand. These two steps must not be reversed.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source, lines 221–232; original anchor section-2-1. Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Complete fields establish only that the question has been made clear.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the original research extract available for download preserves the historical manuscript.

In D0, S*=〈B,X,R,I,T,SP,K〉lists, in order, boundaries, state variables, relations or transition constraints, interfaces, time window, scale profile, and identity criterion. The asterisk reminds readers that it is a candidate. Completing every field does not establish an optimal boundary, relative independence of the object, or the existence of a mechanism. Exploration remains possible when essential fields are missing, but the contract must not be falsely presented as clear.

The second stage governs only claims seeking formal G1–G4 instance support and strong empirical C and CM claims that depend on such support. G1 asks about grouping gain, G2 about specified channels, G3 about historical conditional increments relative to the current representation, and G4 about representational closure and conversion. G3 in particular does not ask the general question of whether history ever influenced the present. Researchers must select the corresponding question rather than use one class of results to endorse another.

Before viewing the results, freeze an immutable version with an auditable timestamp: N0, a unique subtype, the single success criterion permitted for that subtype, controls and models, sample and extrapolation units, indicators, positive thresholds, decision and null-conclusion rules, and falsification and suspension conditions. Multiple targets or models also require freezing the primary target or aggregation rule, model selection or ensembling, and multiple-comparison rules. Freezing is intended not to make the world obey a form, but to prevent moving the question and success threshold after seeing the results.

A confirmatory or replication instance gains eligibility for the corresponding positive support only after completing and passing checks under its advance contract. A falsification instance supports only the falsification or null judgment originally registered. Exploration, drafts, deviations after evidence, and undisclosed deviations must not enter C branches requiring formal support through a formal-support edge. Deviations may be honestly recorded and a new proposal made, but the exploratory history must not be erased.

Retain at least four statuses: registered candidate; not positively supported; the null model is supported; and grouping gain receives limited positive support. Failure to pass the positive rule may reflect a small effect, inadequate measurement, insufficient sample size, or an unsuitable model; it does not automatically mean absence. Supporting equivalence or sufficiency within a specified tolerance additionally requires advance null-conclusion rules and statistical power or sensitivity, with the corresponding criteria met. §2.1.1 preserves what was already grounded in earlier research; §2.1.2 prevents formal proof from being treated as real-world samples.

v2 expressly limits the second-stage result to grouping gain. Registering an object, supporting object facts with reliable material, and obtaining G1 support for grouping gain within a task are three different things. A reliable membership record may support facts about a team and its members, without showing that grouping by this team predicts outcomes better than a matched ungrouped N0.

For example, an institution established by law cannot have its legal standing or membership denied merely because it has never undergone G1 testing. Conversely, accurate prediction from statistical grouping does not establish a unified will. Settle specific standing under constitutive conditions, predictive advantage under G1, and causal effects through the relevant channels separately.

distinctions.leftText: The question about the object can be described.
distinctions.rightText: A specific empirical question frozen beforehand receives limited support.

distinctions.leftText: The positive rule was not passed; the issue may remain unresolved.
distinctions.rightText: Meaningful departures have been excluded under the prespecified null rule.

distinctions.leftTitle: Truth or falsity of an empirical effect
distinctions.leftText: Whether the difference being asked about exists in the world.
distinctions.rightText: Whether the current information and research procedure suffice to provide the specified support under this framework.

boundaries: This procedure is not a universal truth check for all domain knowledge, historical records, and ordinary understanding. Existing research must not be invalidated wholesale for lacking G contracts.

An arbitrarily drawn threshold does not become scientific by being a threshold. Measurement validity, sample selection, competing explanations, and extrapolation conditions still require separate support.
Repeatedly adjusting a model on the same data does not turn it into independent confirmation. Retain its exploratory status before designing a genuinely new test.
questions: A set of results fails to reach the positive threshold, but no equivalence tolerance was preregistered. Should its status be recorded as the null model is established?
After registering a complete D0, may one immediately state that the system has objective independent standing?
If the same information has already helped select a model, does subsequently locking the file count as freezing before results?
argumentSteps: First premise: analysts may initially choose boundaries and representations, but the choice itself is not evidence that the choice has empirical standing.

Second premise: if comparison methods, thresholds, or models change with results already seen, a positive result may arise from retrospective selection and cannot be interpreted under the original contract.
Connection: first define a candidate through D0, then fix the testing contract for the requested G subtype before the evidence, making both the question and the decision procedure reviewable.
Conclusion: eligibility attaches to specific instances satisfying the contract, not to blank templates or to every completely filled-out candidate.

Responsibility for null judgments: not rejecting N0 is not equivalent to supporting N0 in a prespecified sense. Equivalence/sufficiency, tolerance, and identification sensitivity must each satisfy their requirements.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: registering a queue does not prove that grouping is useful
teachingExamples.text: Suppose researchers want to know whether grouping service requests by interface predicts waiting time more accurately than not grouping them. First register B, X, R, I, T, SP, and K; then fix the baseline, error measure, minimum improvement, and evaluation rules before an independent evaluation window. If grouping is changed after evaluation results are seen, the resulting pattern may be a new candidate, but must not masquerade as confirmation frozen beforehand. No study has been carried out here, and no numerical improvement has been invented.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The comparison concerns G1-style grouping gain, not the effect of a causal intervention. Actual information is required to form a formal instance.
teachingExamples.boundary: This is a teaching example of the procedure. It does not claim to have passed G1 or infer improved service quality from a complete candidate.

counterexamples.text: Teaching conditional counterexample: after only two very noisy measurements fail to reach a positive threshold, someone announces that the effect is zero.
counterexamples.effect: Without an advance null rule and sensitivity, the result is at most not positively supported. Failure with a small sample does not automatically exclude meaningful differences.

counterexamples.text: Teaching conditional counterexample: a researcher uses the same evaluation results to choose one of the ten best groupings, then describes it as the “sole preregistered model.”
counterexamples.effect: This violates freezing before evidence. Its honest status is exploration with a record of deviations, not confirmatory support.

questionAnswers.question: A set of results fails to reach the positive threshold, but no equivalence tolerance was preregistered. Should its status be recorded as the null model is established?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It may be recorded as not positively supported or unresolved; a zero conclusion requires additional rules and sufficient sensitivity.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: After registering a complete D0, may one immediately state that the system has objective independent standing?
questionAnswers.answer: No. D0 fixes only what the candidate refers to; relative independence, grouping gain, and other empirical claims require corresponding comparisons and evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If the same information has already helped select a model, does subsequently locking the file count as freezing before results?
questionAnswers.answer: Not for material already used to select the model. Disclose exposure to the material and its exploratory use, and freeze a new contract when suitable new confirmatory material is used.

2.1.1.title: 2.1.1 Domain evidence and eligibility as a formal instance
2.1.1.lead: Earlier research can be valuable while lacking eligibility as a formal instance of this framework. Preserve what it originally established; if stronger standing is sought, add a genuinely new test.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 233–240; source anchor section-2-1-1; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “does not lose its originally supported content because it has not yet been converted into a G-instance.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

This section prevents two opposite misuses. One rewrites past exploration or historical reconstruction as preregistered confirmation. The other discards all locatable historical material and research conclusions because today's forms did not exist then. The source permits retaining descriptions, explanations, or bounded causal conclusions actually supported by the research design, while prohibiting fabrication of a pre-outcome contract.

“Existing finding → source of a new question/model → new contract → test with new material” is a viable continuation. Independent material, a later time window, or appropriate replication may offer a new evaluation opportunity, but independence must be explained: one cannot tune a model using all the data and then relabel part of it as a previously unseen validation set. A later window still requires checking changes in objects and measurements.

If no feasible new test exists, state the existing domain conclusions and relations awaiting testing, rather than forcing them into a G-instance. Formal proof, textual interpretation, and normative argument can also contribute, using their respective grounds: axioms and derivations, versions and context, and value premises and reasons. They supply one another with questions and constraints, without impersonating real mechanisms or authorization.

This section uses Snow's case solely to examine the coexistence of historical material and current eligibility. The field investigation, interviews, and limitations in the 1855 text are historical evidence open to criticism; they do not lose their content because a contemporary G contract is absent. Nor have we used them to reconstruct a nonexistent pre-outcome timestamp.

distinctions.leftText: Supports bounded conclusions under the original research design.
distinctions.rightText: The standing of a specific instance obtained under this framework's pre-evidence contract.

distinctions.leftText: Can propose different models and questions.
distinctions.rightText: Disguises a retrospective finding as a pre-outcome commitment, changing the status of the material.

distinctions.leftText: Another algorithm may reveal implementation problems.
distinctions.rightText: Its evaluation has not already been used by the same model-selection process; its provenance and dependencies must still be stated.

boundaries: Snow's material on water exposure and the effect of removing the pump handle concern two different causal questions. Support for the former does not mean the latter has been separately identified.
Historical evidence need not become a G-instance to be discussed; likewise, being “historically famous” does not exempt a particular causal narrative from criticism.

This lesson did not recheck the original death registers or obtain individual-level data. The case relies on relevant passages in Snow's original work, rather than repeating a historical epidemiological study.

caseNotes.title: Broad Street, London, 1854: preserve the evidence and the differences between questions
caseNotes.text: In the second edition of 1855, Snow reported consulting death registers and investigating drinking-water habits; he presented the circumstances to the parish on September 7, 1854, and the pump handle was removed the next day. The original also states that incidence had already fallen substantially before use of the well water ceased, so it could not establish whether the water still had a disease-causing effect at that time. Here we preserve the distinction between “what the investigation reported” and “whether the net intervention effect was identified.”
caseNotes.sourceLabel: John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 1855, 2nd ed.
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed pages 39–41 and 51–52; the passages The Cholera near Golden Square and The Pump-well in Broad Street
caseNotes.boundary: This is the author's historical account of his investigation at the time, not this lesson's revalidation of every cause of the disease. The material can support a bounded exposure explanation; temporal sequence alone cannot estimate the effect of removing the handle, nor constitute a modern G preregistration.

argumentSteps: Premise: the way existing material was produced is already historical; its pre-event or post-event status cannot be retrospectively changed today.
Connection: evaluating the scope of evidence and evaluating eligibility under a particular framework are separate questions, so they can be recorded separately without canceling each other.
Conclusion one: preserve domain content actually supported by the design while stating that it has not automatically obtained positive support as a G-instance.

Conclusion two: if new eligibility is sought, first freeze a new question and evaluate it with suitable new material; if no feasible new test exists, retain the domain conclusion and its pending-test status.

Responsibilities: sources supply historical facts and research design; the present explanation supplies the mapping and the inference ceiling. Normative claims and authorization have separate grounds.

counterexamples.text: Snow himself noted that incidence had already fallen markedly before use of the well water ceased, and stated that it was impossible to determine whether active disease-causing matter remained in the well when it was closed.
counterexamples.effect: This limits the narrative that “removing the handle caused the entire decline,” but does not also invalidate his investigation of water exposure.

questionAnswers.question: Can an investigation from 1855 without a G-instance record still serve as material for the historical question of water exposure?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes, according to its investigative design, account, and limitations; do not fabricate a G preregistration for that time or automatically award formal support under this framework.

questionAnswers.question: If a researcher cannot obtain any new material, must earlier findings be rejected?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Retain originally supported domain conclusions and explain that the new formal eligibility has not been established.

questionAnswers.question: Can “the fall in incidence after removal of the pump handle” be taken directly as the net effect of removing it?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A counterfactual comparison is needed, addressing competing explanations such as the decline having already begun, population departure, and limitations of the material.

2.1.2.title: 2.1.2 Connecting formal conclusions with empirical instances
2.1.2.lead: Mathematics can rigorously answer “does this hold under these assumptions?” Real-world application must also answer “does this object satisfy these assumptions?” One answer may be determinate while the other remains unresolved.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 241–246; source anchor section-2-1-2; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “the number of computations does not increase independent empirical support either.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

A formal proposition first fixes the state domain, mapping, target, permitted operations, and logical premises. A proof explains how the conclusion follows from those premises; exhaustive checking over a finite domain checks every declared case; numerical checking must additionally specify precision, boundaries, and implementation error. These three can cross-check errors, but computation does not generate new real-world samples.

Connection to reality must be established item by item: what observable quantities the model variables correspond to; whether measurement and representation preserve distinctions needed for the target; which premises already have supporting material; whether error and the applicable range are acceptable; and what counterexample would overturn the mapping. The F layer in source §4.18–§4.19 particularly stresses that static recovery, dynamic closure, and intervention transferability are different propositions.

A formal counterexample suffices to refute the unconditional inference it targets. For instance, “an aggregate can always recover each component” fails with a single explicit mathematical counterexample; no factory or hospital experiment is needed first. But the counterexample does not show that every real-world aggregate is useless. If the target becomes the total, the same representation may be entirely sufficient.

Real-world adoption carries six independent responsibilities: formal feasibility; existence of an algorithm; computability within budget; timely availability of material; correct actual execution; and authority to adopt it. Passing one step does not imply passing the next. Knowing a decision rule exists may leave it both impossible to compute in time and impossible to supply with timely inputs; even computability and executability do not automatically confer authority to act upon people.

distinctions.leftText: The inference is valid within the declared axioms and semantics.
distinctions.rightText: Sufficient material supports the variable mapping and premises for the target object.

distinctions.leftText: Covers every state of this particular finite model.
distinctions.rightText: Material from the world, with issues of sampling, measurement, and dependence.

distinctions.leftText: There is a rule for obtaining an answer.
distinctions.rightText: Computational budget, material, implementation, and permission are separately satisfied.

boundaries: The mathematical counterexample already refutes “any aggregate can recover any detail,” but does not refute sufficiency when the target is the total.
Allowing additional information, such as x₂, changes the permitted operations and representation contract; the new recoverability cannot be counted as success under the old contract.

Exhaustive checking over a finite domain must list the complete domain; randomly sampling many states is still not proof over an infinite domain. Numerical near-zero does not automatically mean exact zero.
questions: Does running the same four-state exhaustive check one million times add one million independent pieces of empirical support?
In the counterexample above, can x₁ be recovered if additional access to x₂ is allowed?
If a rule has been proved to exist, can one thereby declare that it can automatically go live the next day?
argumentSteps: Mathematical premises: state domain X={0,1}²; representation π(x₁,x₂)=x₁+x₂; target q(x₁,x₂)=x₁; the recovery function g may read only π.
Take x=(0,1) and x′=(1,0). Then π(x)=π(x′)=1, whereas q(x)=0 and q(x′)=1.

If a g correct for every state existed, g(1) would have to equal both 0 and 1, a contradiction. Thus, on this complete state domain and under this representation, no single-valued function exactly recovers q.
If the target changes to qΣ=x₁+x₂, then gΣ(z)=z gives exact recovery. The conclusion is target-relative; it does not say all aggregation fails.

Real-world responsibility: interpreting x₁ and x₂ as real quantities requires separate support for the state domain, measurement, input availability, and permitted operations; the four-state proof supplies neither real-world occurrence frequencies nor intervention effects.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: the same sum, two different first components
teachingExamples.text: The four states are (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), and (1,1); their π values are 0, 1, 1, and 2, and their q values are 0, 0, 1, and 1, respectively. The target is not constant within the group π=1, so reading only the sum cannot recover the first component. If the target becomes the sum, every representation value directly supplies the answer. This is exact integer computation over a complete finite domain.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The domain contains only these four states; the recovery function is single-valued and reads only π, without identity labels or additional measurements.
teachingExamples.boundary: This is an example of mathematical recoverability, not an estimate of real-world effects, human types, or statistical error; it cannot establish that a real system happens to satisfy the model.

counterexamples.text: Mathematical boundary: q=x₁ is not recoverable on the original four-state domain; if the admissible domain shrinks to {(0,0),(1,1)}, each value of the same π corresponds to only one state.
counterexamples.effect: Restricting the admissible domain changes the premises and therefore recoverability; failure on the original domain cannot be generalized to every restricted domain.

questionAnswers.question: Does running the same four-state exhaustive check one million times add one million independent pieces of empirical support?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It may help reveal implementation errors, but it still checks the same model and produces no new real-world observations.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: In the counterexample above, can x₁ be recovered if additional access to x₂ is allowed?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes: x₁=π−x₂. But this expands the input conditions; it does not overturn the original impossibility of recovery when “only π may be read.”

questionAnswers.question: If a rule has been proved to exist, can one thereby declare that it can automatically go live the next day?
questionAnswers.answer: No. An algorithm, budget, timely material, correct implementation, and permission to adopt it still each need support.

2.2.title: 2.2 Roles of propositions and responsibilities of argument
2.2.lead: A sentence such as “this system works, so it should be used” mixes at least object definition, an effect judgment, a value choice, and permission to act. Break the sentence apart first to know what each part requires as support.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 247–272; source anchor section-2-2; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “The numbering organizes responsibilities of argument; it does not mean that all categories have the same truth conditions.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

D answers “what does this word refer to here?” Specifying meanings for “structure” or “repair” supports consistent judgment but does not establish that the corresponding object exists in the world or has been repaired. G answers specific empirical questions: which object, which comparison, and whether a difference under which conditions exceeds a threshold. G1–G4 are families of questions; instances carry particular factual assertions. A fact may be true despite insufficient current support, and a procedurally complete inquiry may still reach a wrong conclusion through a mistaken model. Formal eligibility cannot define the world.

E constrains how much is known: measurement blind spots, competing explanations, residuals, and conditions for cross-scale transfer must be retained. N makes value choices explicit: what to protect and what to restrict. These have different responsibilities; acknowledging epistemic limits does not automatically establish a value, and choosing to protect someone does not automatically establish every description of their circumstances. O organizes freezing, auditing, normative registration, authorization, option comparison, bounded execution, review, stopping, withdrawal, and remedy into procedures. It constrains how one may proceed without replacing factual grounds.

H is especially easy to misread. It is a marker for adaptation to the human domain, not a sixth kind of truth wholly exclusive of definitions, empirical claims, and norms. H1, H4, and H5 are empirical hypotheses requiring case-specific evidence; H2 is an operational typology; H3 classifies institutional write-back; H6 is a normative boundary. Sharing the H label does not make them all a priori axioms of human nature, still less make human meaning and institutional rules the roots of all natural processes.

F consists of conditional formal propositions established by proof under explicit state domains, mappings, targets, operation sets, and mathematical premises. Mathematical counterexamples can defeat universal inferences that exceed their premises; whether reality satisfies those premises still requires evidence. F1–F5 in source §4.18 and the task families and dynamic refinements in §4.19 respectively show boundaries for recovery, dynamics, intervention, composition, and approximation; their uses cannot be treated as identical merely because they are all formulas.

C does not add another class of facts about the world alongside D and G; it supplies contracts for how results are registered and under which mechanism conditions they are used, with C12 providing the bridge to normative procedures. Common method constraints are not additional laws of the world either. Adding more numbered labels to a conclusion increases its locatability, not its independent evidence.

The minimal bridge to action contains six items: a descriptive or explanatory conclusion, explicit normative premises, current evidence, lawful authorization, an action ceiling, and stopping or withdrawal conditions. If any is missing, the relevant real-world intervention should stop. Description, candidate generation, evidence gathering, inaction, or proposals for reversible probes may continue; proposing an option does not itself authorize its implementation. These are necessary review items, not a guarantee that listing them automatically satisfies every domain's legal, professional, or safety requirements.

distinctions.leftText: An object fits a classification by definition.
distinctions.rightText: The object and corresponding relations are supported by material, not generated by definition.

distinctions.leftText: Indicates which kinds of additional contracts apply to human objects.
distinctions.rightText: Further determine whether it is empirical, classificatory, procedural, or normative.

distinctions.leftText: Constrain how existing grounds may be used.
distinctions.rightText: Requires independent materials and cannot increase merely through numbering.

distinctions.leftText: Describes what may happen and why.
distinctions.rightText: Qualification to take a specified action toward a target; it does not follow from depth of understanding.

boundaries: A valid proof does not establish that a measurement mapping is true; passing a procedural check does not establish the existence of a substantive causal relation.
The action bridge is a minimal set of necessary conditions, not a complete administrative, medical, or legal permit; this lesson performs no real-world diagnosis or disposition.
Value premises may be criticized and revised, but renaming them ‘objective mechanisms’ must not exempt them from public justification.
questions: ‘H6 is a normative boundary, so H1 also needs no empirical materials.’ Why does this inference fail?
Does a formally supported instance define whether an effect is factually true or false?
If stopping conditions are missing but an option is considered highly beneficial, does the bridge permit immediate implementation?
argumentSteps: Premise: definitional conventions, empirical assertions, mathematical consequences, and value commitments have different conditions for validity; a uniform label of ‘proven’ must not replace them.
Decomposition: separate a compound statement into identifiable clauses and specify each clause's object and role; for H, also state whether it is empirical, operational, classificatory, or normative.

Connection: definitions require semantic consistency; empirical claims require designs and materials; formal claims require premises and proofs; norms require values and reasons; action additionally requires permissions and stopping mechanisms. Satisfying one does not complete the rest.

Conclusion: moving from ‘the explanation is credible’ to ‘action may be taken’ requires completing the action bridge; a missing component blocks only dispositions that depend on it, without automatically withdrawing independently established facts or proofs.

Evidential responsibility: the framework's own D, C, or methodological descriptions must not serve as object facts; procedural compliance or normative justification must not be presented as proof of a causal mechanism.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: separating ‘accurate, therefore mandatory’
teachingExamples.text: Consider: ‘We define a tool with prediction error below e as accurate; tool A meets this criterion on a specified test set; therefore everyone should be compelled to use it, and its developers have the right to deploy it directly.’ The first sentence is a D-style semantic convention; the second is an empirical assertion whose test design and scope require checking; the ‘should be compelled’ in the third requires N-style value reasons, while deployment qualification requires authorization and O procedures. Neither follows from the error result. A proof of an algorithmic error bound would instead be an F-style conditional conclusion, and whether reality meets its assumptions would still need checking.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The tool, threshold e, and tests are hypothetical; they do not represent a real product or completed experiment.
teachingExamples.boundary: Used only to distinguish argumentative responsibilities; it does not establish any tool's reliability, justification, or permission for deployment.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: stipulating that ‘every operation called repair is beneficial’, then using an operation's registration as repair to prove that it is beneficial.
counterexamples.effect: This inserts a normative conclusion into a definition and then supports it circularly; pre-specified goals, observed results, and value assessments should be separated.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: someone predicts a team's reactions most accurately and therefore claims permission to reassign its members.
counterexamples.effect: Epistemic advantage does not generate authorization; stop at explanation or a proposal rather than cross the permission boundary.

questionAnswers.question: ‘H6 is a normative boundary, so H1 also needs no empirical materials.’ Why does this inference fail?
questionAnswers.answer: H marks domain adaptation, not one uniform logical type. H1 is an empirical hypothesis requiring case-specific evidence; H6's normative status must not be transferred to it.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does a formally supported instance define whether an effect is factually true or false?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Instances and procedures govern how much support we may give; whether an effect exists in the world is the question they seek to answer, not something registration creates.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If stopping conditions are missing but an option is considered highly beneficial, does the bridge permit immediate implementation?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The relevant disposition should be suspended; options may be completed, a reversible probe proposed, or inaction retained. A judgment of benefit also requires its own evidence and normative reasons.

2.3.title: 2.3 Four Types of Dependency Must Be Kept Separate
2.3.lead: ‘It is needed’ may mean that a conclusion cannot be inferred without it, cannot be published, applies only to a domain, or constrains action. Draw these four meanings separately, or procedures will be mistaken for causes and norms for evidence.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 273–285; source anchor section-2-3; short quotation: ‘Only hard inferential premises enter the acyclic root–conclusion graph’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

inferential_requires denotes a hard inferential premise: without it, the stated conclusion cannot be obtained in this disclosed argument. For example, inferring ‘all states with the same representation have the same target value, so a target-recovery function exists’ requires the premise that target values are constant across states sharing a representation. It may enter the directed acyclic root–conclusion graph, with direction consistently understood as running from a premise to the conclusion that depends on it.

protocol_requires denotes a method check: evidence, causal, analogy, source, or domain-classification contracts specify how this judgment must be recorded, examined, and published. A missing check removes the corresponding publication qualification, but the check is not an additional empirical cause in the world. Freezing beforehand provides a fixed basis for evaluation under the original question, while actual execution and deviations still need checking; a frozen document does not cause the physical effect.

specializes denotes specialization: restricting a general proposition to a domain, object, or subtype requires listing additional conditions and scope. It does not automatically establish the existence of the domain's object, nor turn classificatory clauses into supporting materials. applies_to records which subjects, actions, or propositions a norm or procedure constrains; a privacy rule applying to a record does not, in reverse, establish the truth of the facts claimed in that record.

The original table labels the four relations respectively ‘yes, no, no, no’ for entry into the inferential acyclic graph. This does not make the latter three unimportant; it requires separate graphs or layers to preserve their different meanings. A publication process may include cycles of review, return, and resubmission; this is procedural structure. Procedural cycles must not be misread as empirical-inference cycles merely to fit everything into a single DAG.

A case may involve multiple relations simultaneously, each of which should be recorded separately. A factual claim might inferentially use comparison data, face a freezing requirement for publication, be restricted to a subtype in scope, and be normatively constrained in action. It must not be represented by a single untyped ‘dependency’ edge. If a protocol check fails, first remove the corresponding publication or support qualification; if a hard premise fails, the inferred conclusion depending on it loses that basis. The two failures affect different things.

distinctions.leftText: Without this premise, this argument fails.
distinctions.rightText: If the procedure is unmet, the claim must not be published at that level; this does not directly change what is true or false in the world.

distinctions.leftText: Adds scope and conditions.
distinctions.rightText: Materials support specific relations in the specialized object; these two functions are not interchangeable.

distinctions.leftText: Specifies who or what must be constrained.
distinctions.rightText: Determines whether a particular description is supported; being protected does not mean the description is established.

boundaries: The acyclic-graph restriction concerns argumentative dependencies; it prohibits neither feedback in real systems nor review cycles in operational procedures.
A method check must not be deleted because it is absent from the inferential DAG: it still determines whether the corresponding conclusion may be published and used with a particular status.

If a condition initially treated as procedural is also written into a mathematical proposition's premises, separately register its formal role in that proposition and its role as a publication check; the two uses of the same wording must not silently collapse into one edge.
questions: How should a valid mathematical derivation under given premises be recorded when the source contract is unmet?
What edge is mistaken in ‘privacy rules apply to this interview, therefore everything the interviewee says is true’?
May a rule specialized to human organizations be inferred backward through a specializes edge into a law of all natural systems?
argumentSteps: Premise: different ‘dependencies’ pose different counterfactual questions: does removing it break the inference, disqualify publication, change scope, or make action impermissible?
Classification: answer those questions for each edge and retain its relation type. A node may participate in several relation types, but sharing a name must not merge the meanings of its edges.

Connection: hard inferential premises enter the root–conclusion DAG only where the validity of the conclusion is what is being explained. Methodological, specialization, and applicability relations are stored separately.

Conclusion: layered graphs prevent inferring real mechanisms from publication requirements or real facts from normative applicability; they also identify which inferred conclusion should be suspended when a premise is compromised.
Responsibility: registering a type is not itself proof; every hard premise still requires the corresponding derivation or materials, and method checks must be assessed against the actual contract.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one conclusion about a recovery function and four relations
teachingExamples.text: Proposition P: if π(x)=π(x′) always implies q(x)=q(x′), then g can be defined on the image of π such that q=g∘π. Set g(z) to the q value of any preimage; the constancy premise ensures that choosing a different preimage does not change the result, making it a hard inferential premise. Requiring disclosure of the state domain and checking records is a method check; restricting X to a finite set is a specialization; an institution's rule prohibiting use of g for unauthorized dispositions toward people is normative applicability. The latter three must not be treated as evidence establishing q's constancy.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Discusses only a teaching setting involving sets, mappings, and a stipulated norm; it does not claim that any institution actually adopted the rule.
teachingExamples.boundary: The formal example supplies no real-world measurement sufficiency; publishing checking records also creates neither data nor authorization.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: ‘Publication requires ethical review, therefore ethical review is an empirical cause of the effect observed in the experiment.’
counterexamples.effect: This misreads protocol_requires or applies_to as a causal mechanism. Procedures may constrain research behavior, but this permission relation does not itself establish the target physical or social effect.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: a procedural graph contains ‘failed review → revision → renewed review’, and this is used to declare the entire argument invalid through circularity.
counterexamples.effect: A procedural cycle is not an inferential cycle. Check the hard-premise DAG separately for cycles; the same judgment must not be applied indiscriminately across graph layers.

questionAnswers.question: How should a valid mathematical derivation under given premises be recorded when the source contract is unmet?
questionAnswers.answer: Retain the formal derivation's conditional validity. Missing sources may block the real-world mapping or publication qualification, but that alone must not be used to declare the mathematical derivation false.

questionAnswers.question: What edge is mistaken in ‘privacy rules apply to this interview, therefore everything the interviewee says is true’?
questionAnswers.answer: applies_to supplies only protections and constraints on use; it must not serve in reverse as factual evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: May a rule specialized to human organizations be inferred backward through a specializes edge into a law of all natural systems?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Specialization narrows scope and adds conditions; it must not be reversed to expand a claim into a universal assertion about the world.

2.3.1.title: 2.3.1 Layered Responsibilities of the Common Method Kernel
2.3.1.lead: Two theoretical texts may share requirements for careful recording and inference, but must not stamp one another as true. What is aligned is each layer's responsibilities and conditions, not names or numbers.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 286–300; source anchor section-2-3-1; short quotation: ‘Neither serves as an authoritative source or a second piece of empirical evidence for the other’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

This section addresses the limits of interoperability between this framework and World Model: methodological responsibilities may be shared, while each text retains its own objects, arguments, and operational form. ‘May be shared’ does not mean correspondence has been verified across all versions. The current materials provide the current Xikari text, but not a full, identifiable version of World Model; this lesson therefore explains the declaration in this passage without claiming to have verified the other text.

The first layer in the original table, ‘definitions’, fixes assessable meanings for objects and terms; it can help the two texts establish what they are discussing, but does not prove that those objects exist in reality. The second layer, ‘common method constraints’, governs representations, the status of materials, and inference—for example, not treating simulations as observations or method checks as empirical causes. Shared adherence to these constraints creates no new natural or social law.

The third layer, F, answers what necessarily follows under mathematical premises. A proof's validity depends on its domain, mapping, target, operations, and assumptions; the same theorem name appearing in two texts does not eliminate the need to align premises and check proofs. The fourth layer, G, organizes specific empirical questions; actual support comes from instances with objects, comparisons, failure modes, and materials. Two texts retelling the same study do not constitute two independent observations.

The fifth layer, C, asks what existing grounds permit to be registered and used. It depends on relevant results, additional mechanistic conditions, and application windows; a rule's presence in the common kernel must not fill a missing mechanistic connection. The sixth layer, governance invariants, constrains publication, evaluation, suspension, and action; these limit the use of power and are not additional causes of changes in the research object.

D, G, and C numbers support stable references; the common kernel's Chinese numbering supports alignment across texts. Neither replaces a contract. Actual checking requires comparing complete meanings, premises, evidential statuses, targets, and failure rules side by side: record differences where the same name has different conditions, while differently named clauses with corresponding conditions may also admit a grounded mapping.

This section continues 2.2's argumentative roles and 2.3's dependency layers, preventing the circular move ‘I said it in another text too, so it has more support’. A common method may clarify interoperability; whether the framework is more useful for a class of real tasks remains a separate question requiring a comparison design and materials.

distinctions.leftText: How both texts record and use grounds.
distinctions.rightText: Empirical or formal claims about real-world regularities, requiring the corresponding proofs or materials.

distinctions.leftText: Makes contracts easier to locate.
distinctions.rightText: Meaning, premises, application window, evidence, and failure rules; numbering cannot replace them.

distinctions.leftText: May derive from shared definitions or the same materials.
distinctions.rightTitle: Two independent sources of empirical support
distinctions.rightText: Require genuinely distinct materials or designs relevant to the claim; they must not be counted by document number.

distinctions.leftText: Proposes checking responsibilities and possible ways of connecting.
distinctions.rightText: Actual versions, mappings, operations, and testing materials are all available for checking.

boundaries: No identifiable version of the other text has been provided, so full terminological equivalence, full-text consistency, or an already shared operational kernel must not be claimed.

The six layers are not an evidential ladder that automatically upgrades from low to high. A definition does not become an empirical fact by passing through a methodological layer, and the governance layer is no better than empirical materials at establishing causation.
A failed correspondence between texts should restrict that particular connection; a mere difference in names should not invalidate all independently supported conclusions in the other text.
questions: If two texts use the same Chinese number, may their clauses be merged directly?
Does jointly adopting ‘simulation must not be written back as observation’ increase a simulation's empirical truth?
Without the other text, what can this section complete, and what can it not complete?
argumentSteps: Premise: the two texts each have their own object domains, operating forms, and arguments; repeated names do not imply identical premises and semantics.
Connection one: comparing definitions, methods, F, G, C, and governance layer by layer distinguishes semantic compatibility, formal instances, empirical support, and limits on power.
Connection two: reusing the same source adds no independent material, so agreement across texts cannot be totaled as double empirical support.

Conclusion: shared methodological responsibilities can constitute interoperability requirements; whether particular texts satisfy the correspondence must be checked item by item after the correct versions are obtained.

Responsibility and present limit: the current Xikari source supports this section’s description of its interface; it cannot by itself establish the actual content of World Model or that interoperability has operated successfully.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: identically named “closure” must be aligned condition by condition
teachingExamples.text: Suppose Text A’s “closure” requires only recovery of the current target q from representation π, while Text B’s “closure” additionally requires the representation to update on its own after every admissible action. The names match, but B adds dynamic and action conditions. Alignment should record “A requires static recovery; B has additional dynamic requirements,” rather than treating them interchangeably. Conversely, two different names may admit a formal mapping only when premises, domains, and conclusions are equivalent item by item.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A and B are two texts constructed for teaching; they do not describe the actual content of World Model.
teachingExamples.boundary: The example illustrates an alignment method, not actual correspondence between books or any framework’s empirical effectiveness.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: two lectures cite the same study and then report “two independent studies support this.”
counterexamples.effect: Repeated retelling adds no original material; record the shared source and each interpretation without increasing the count of independent support.

counterexamples.text: Without obtaining the specified version of World Model, treating Xikari’s statement about shared methods as evidence of complete agreement between both texts.
counterexamples.effect: Actual correspondence to the other text remains unchecked; Xikari’s own account can presently be explained, but the other text’s content cannot be supplied on its behalf.

questionAnswers.question: If two texts use the same Chinese number, may their clauses be merged directly?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Complete definitions, premises, object domains, failure conditions, and operational meanings must be checked; identifiers are only location tools.

questionAnswers.answer: No. The requirement instead limits the status in which material can be used; actual support still needs external observation and bridging.

2.4.title: 2.4 Causal Protocol
2.4.lead: Seeing change after an action does not yet answer how much change the action caused. Conversely, a comparison answering the total-effect question may not identify every intermediate link.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 301–306; source anchor section-2-4; short quotation translated from Chinese: “limited identification of the effect, with the specific mechanism unresolved.” The current source appears in the corresponding section on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

A causal contract first specifies the treatment version and outcome. “Discontinuing a water source” differs from “issuing advice”; onset on a given day differs from death on that day; a local population differs from all city residents. Next fix the object, population, window, scale, and effect target. Without them, two studies calling something “effective” may answer entirely different questions.

Why the comparison identifies the target is central to a causal claim. A common input may affect treatment and outcome; self-selection makes recipients different at baseline; attrition changes the observed sample; measurement changes alter records; outcomes may influence treatment in reverse; one unit’s treatment may affect others. Address relevant issues individually rather than mechanically adding controls regardless of the task.

Identifying a total effect and identifying a specified structural channel carry different burdens. A claim that A affects Y through M needs the corresponding temporal order and mechanism chain, plus blocking, replacement, or natural variation meeting identification conditions that distinguish alternative explanations. Cross-level claims also check D3/E5 bridging. A design identifying only a total effect should not be forced to exhaust every microscopic process first; neither may the total effect fill in an untested mediator.

Evaluate causal strength, mechanism resolution, and extrapolation scope separately. A credible comparison within a bounded window does not establish a fine-grained account of every channel or transfer to every population. The reverse caution also matters: two mechanisms may offset, so a near-zero net total effect does not mean each mechanism is zero.

The next section, 2.4.1, distinguishes estimands such as “receiving an opportunity,” “accepting an intervention,” and “institutional expansion.” Section 2.4.2 uses an exact counterexample to show why accurate estimates of two average link effects still do not establish a composed whole-chain effect.

distinctions.leftText: A occurs before Y, satisfying one part of the required causal ordering.
distinctions.rightText: Can exclude or control the relevant competing explanations and support the specified counterfactual comparison.

distinctions.leftText: The combined change in the terminal outcome following a treatment change.
distinctions.rightText: Which channel produces change and under which common conditions.

distinctions.leftText: Answers a question within a population, window, and set of assumptions.
distinctions.rightText: Continued validity for new objects and scales requires additional grounds.

boundaries: Snow’s table contains separate columns for fatal cases arranged by onset date and counts by death date, not all infections or all cases of onset. Their denominators and event clocks must not be mixed.

Snow’s account of decline before discontinuation limits simple before-and-after attribution; it does not prove that removing the pump handle had no effect. Without a comparable counterfactual, a zero effect is not automatically identified either.
Retain the limited total-effect conclusion when a mechanism remains unidentified; when the total effect is not significant, retain independently grounded knowledge of local processes as well.
questions: A randomized comparison supports a treatment’s total effect but measures no mediator. May the total effect be reported?
If the total effect is near zero, may one write “all channels are absent”?
What can the decline in onset before handle removal establish in Snow’s case?

caseLinks.title: Broad Street: separate exposure evidence from the net effect of removing the handle

caseNotes.title: Broad Street: separate exposure evidence from the net effect of removing the handle
caseNotes.text: Snow’s Table I for the 1854 Broad Street epidemic arranges fatal cases separately by onset date and death date: fatal-case onsets numbered 143 on September 1 and 28 on September 7; the pump handle was removed on September 8. The original also notes population departure and decline before discontinuation. This section adds the event-clock and counterfactual distinction: these records do not allow low values after removal to independently establish removal’s net effect.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Snow, second edition, 1855, Table I and the author’s discussion
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed page 49, Table I; post-table discussion on pages 50–52; page 40 records the September 7 meeting and handle removal the following day
caseNotes.boundary: The table includes cases with unknown onset dates and counts only eventually fatal cases. This guide estimates neither all infections nor a reconstructed control group and does not infer a zero effect of handle removal.

argumentSteps: Premise: causal questions include a counterfactual comparison of treatment and outcome; seeing only the realized path does not directly reveal the outcome on the path not taken.

Connection: a credible design must explain why comparable groups, periods, or variation represent the target counterfactual and address confounding, selection, interference, and measurement issues relevant to that design.
Conclusion: report a bounded total effect under the identification conditions; a specified mechanism also requires channel-discriminating evidence, and extrapolation requires additional bridging.
Reverse check: a zero total effect may arise from offsetting paths; local paths may also exist without connecting in the same object and window.
Evidential responsibility: historical documents support their actual observations and comparisons; narrative coherence does not automatically supply a net-effect estimate.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: two paths exactly offset
teachingExamples.text: Let a∈{0,1}. One path adds a to the outcome and another subtracts a, giving terminal y(a)=a−a=0. Each constructed path varies with a, but y(1)−y(0)=0. This shows that the unconditional inference “zero net effect → no mechanisms exist” is invalid.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Both terms are additive components with the same units, object, and window, and the functions are fully given.
teachingExamples.boundary: Offsetting is stipulated, not estimated in a real system; changing units or adding interactions requires recalculation.

counterexamples.text: Snow’s Table I records 143 fatal-case onsets on September 1 and 28 on September 7; the pump handle was removed only on September 8. The author also acknowledges a substantial decline before discontinuation.
counterexamples.effect: A decline already underway cannot all be attributed to later handle removal; neither does this establish that removal’s net effect must be zero.

questionAnswers.question: A randomized comparison supports a treatment’s total effect but measures no mediator. May the total effect be reported?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes, within the design assumptions and scope, explicitly leaving the specific mechanism unresolved; a mediator chain must not be fabricated.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If the total effect is near zero, may one write “all channels are absent”?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Paths can offset, and measurement or precision may also be insufficient; examine the claimed channels separately.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What can the decline in onset before handle removal establish in Snow’s case?
questionAnswers.answer: It challenges the simple narrative attributing the entire decline to later handle removal; it does not itself identify removal’s net effect.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

2.4.1.title: 2.4.1 Estimands and Mechanism Responsibilities
2.4.1.lead: Ask “what exactly changed?” before discussing effects. A lottery offering an opportunity, a person choosing uptake, and full institutional expansion involve different counterfactuals and cannot share one undifferentiated “treatment effect” label.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 307–314; source anchor section-2-4-1; short quotation translated from Chinese: “Giving someone an opportunity, that person actually accepting an intervention, and expansion of the entire institution are different treatments.” The current source appears in this page’s corresponding section; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

Let Z denote receiving an opportunity, D actual uptake, and Y the outcome. Comparing randomized Z can identify the effect of offering the opportunity under the corresponding design conditions; directly comparing D=1 with D=0 may mix in self-selection. Even if Z changes D, additional conditions such as an exclusion restriction are needed to interpret the opportunity effect as a particular local effect of receiving treatment. When an additional assumption fails, withdraw the interpretation depending on it, without automatically withdrawing a still-credible randomized opportunity comparison.

The population average, the local average for a specified complier group, and each individual’s outcome answer different questions. A local effect may apply only to those whose uptake changes because the opportunity changes. It cannot directly generalize to never-takers, always-takers, all individuals, or full institutional expansion. Expansion may also change supply, congestion, interaction, and resource allocation, making the treatment version different.

More controls are not necessarily better. If the target is the total effect A→M→Y, holding M fixed changes the question. Controlling a variable jointly affected by A and other causes can also open an association that was previously absent. First specify variables’ positions in the generating process rather than adding every correlated variable to a regression. Even a larger sample does not remove indistinguishability produced by the design.

Failure of point identification does not require pretending to know everything or nothing. Retain bounds, sets of possible directions, exclusions by necessary conditions, or specific process knowledge supported by assumptions and material, and list the unanswered targets. Partial identification must actually follow from the corresponding constraints; assigning an arbitrary interval does not make it rigorous.

The source closes with common event substitutions: agreement text, verification, execution, and everyday use are not the same thing. An announcement, public understanding, arrival, border handling, and full clearance likewise cannot have one node stand for the entire chain. Each changed treatment or outcome definition requires rechecking its event, time, object, and dependency route.

distinctions.leftText: Can be compared through random assignment.
distinctions.rightText: Affected by eligibility, choice, and execution; not necessarily random.

distinctions.leftText: Average change for a specified group of compliers.
distinctions.rightText: Needs a different target and identification basis; it cannot be read directly from a local average.

distinctions.leftText: The target quantity cannot be uniquely determined.
distinctions.rightText: A stronger claim; bounds, directions, or process constraints may remain.

boundaries: “Most people did not take up the opportunity” does not mean random assignment necessarily failed; distinguish the opportunity effect from the uptake effect.

This guide offers no current medical, insurance, or policy advice. The Oregon facts are limited to the historical design checkable in the official abstract; it uses no health statistics or individual conclusions from an unread full text.
Controlling another variable may change the target or introduce bias; more observations improve some estimation precision but do not automatically repair identification.
