caseLinks.title: Oregon’s 2008 lottery: selection offered an opportunity to apply

caseNotes.title: Oregon’s 2008 lottery: selection offered an opportunity to apply
caseNotes.text: The official abstract of the 2011 NBER working paper states that in 2008 a group of uninsured low-income Oregon adults obtained the opportunity to apply for Medicaid through a lottery. The design itself distinguishes winning an opportunity from actually becoming insured; the former cannot be renamed universal receipt of an identical intervention.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Finkelstein et al., The Oregon Health Insurance Experiment: Evidence from the First Year
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Finkelstein et al., NBER Working Paper 17190, July 2011; first two sentences of the official page’s abstract (official text returned by search)
caseNotes.boundary: The official abstract was obtained; direct full-text/PDF requests currently returned 403, and no full-text reading is claimed. Only the lottery and application-opportunity design facts are used, not a finding that all IV conditions, individual effects, or institutional-expansion effects hold.

argumentSteps: Target definition: let ITT_Y=E[Y|Z=1]−E[Y|Z=0], the mean difference grouped by opportunity Z; the design must explain randomization, outcome comparability, attrition, and related conditions.

Additional conditions: if Z is randomized, actually changes D, affects Y only through D, has no defiers, and satisfies consistency and the corresponding no-interference conditions, then in the binary case ITT_Y／(E[D|Z=1]−E[D|Z=0]) can be interpreted as the local average effect for compliers.

Limitation: failure of conditions such as the exclusion restriction or monotonicity undermines this interpretation as a local effect of receipt. It does not automatically establish that the effect of the opportunity assigned by randomized Z is also absent.

Change of use: moving from a local effect of receipt to population-wide expansion, manipulation of a particular mediator, or individual prediction requires the corresponding additional assumptions and material; changing the title is insufficient.

Evidential responsibility: in this lesson the historical Oregon example supports only the design distinction that “randomly offering an opportunity to apply does not randomly guarantee enrollment.” The formula is a teaching explanation under explicit assumptions, not a substitute for all identification checks in the paper.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: one ratio, two layers of assumptions
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a randomly assigned opportunity increases the average outcome by 2 units and increases the receipt rate by 0.25, and additionally suppose the binary IV conditions above hold. The local average effect for compliers is then 2÷0.25=8 units. If the opportunity also directly affects Y, the numerator includes a path that does not run through D, so 8 loses that interpretation. If random assignment of the opportunity, measurement, and other relevant conditions still hold, 2 can still represent the opportunity effect.
teachingExamples.assumptions: 2 and 0.25 are purely teaching assumptions, not observed values from the Oregon paper. Units and the time window are fixed.
teachingExamples.boundary: This calculation cannot establish the exclusion restriction or monotonicity in reality, nor assign 8 to every individual.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: controlling a common outcome can create an association
teachingExamples.text: Let A and U be independent binary variables taking 0 and 1, and define S=A+U and Y=U. A does not affect Y in the population. Restricting the sample to S=1 leaves only (A,U)=(1,0) and (0,1), so those with A=1 have Y=0 and those with A=0 have Y=1: a negative association appears. Controlling the common outcome S changes the sample structure.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Independent, equally probable binary variables and deterministic functions are explicitly constructed assumptions.
teachingExamples.boundary: This counterexample rejects only “more controls necessarily mean greater reliability.” It does not imply that all controls are bad and is not an empirical estimate.

counterexamples.text: Teaching conditional counterexample: issuing an invitation itself provides additional consultation, affecting the outcome even when the main intervention is not received.
counterexamples.effect: The exclusion restriction is undermined. One cannot simply use the invitation as an instrument and divide the entire outcome difference by the receipt difference. The overall effect of randomized invitation can still be studied independently.

counterexamples.text: Teaching conditional counterexample: service capacity becomes insufficient after system expansion, although it was sufficient in the original small trial.
counterexamples.effect: The treatment and shared conditions have changed; the local trial effect cannot be generalized directly to full expansion without a bridge.

questionAnswers.question: If an invitation has a direct effect beyond encouraging uptake, must all results of the randomized invitation comparison be withdrawn?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. First withdraw the interpretation as an “effect of receipt” that depends on the exclusion restriction. If invitation randomization, measurement, and other design conditions remain credible, the opportunity effect may be retained.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does analyzing only eventual recipients automatically preserve comparability of the original randomized groups?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Receipt is a post-assignment choice; selecting recipients may destroy comparability.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why cannot “an agreement exists” directly fill the field “everyday execution succeeded”?
questionAnswers.answer: Text, verification, implementation, and actual use are distinct events. Subsequent nodes and their connections each require evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

2.4.2.title: 2.4.2 Local effects, joint responses, and the whole chain
2.4.2.lead: Two average effects can both be real and still produce no effect when connected: people changed by the first stage may be precisely those who do not respond to the second. Joint responses in the same objects are crucial.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 315–322; original anchor section-2-4-2. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “The 1/4 obtained by multiplying the two edge averages is not the whole-chain effect.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

Serial composition must preserve more than two averages. Does the first stage's output match the actual version of the second stage's input? Can the same objects and sequence be matched? Do the stages share a support range? Who responds to both? What is the terminal outcome? These joint conditions determine whether the chain connects. Different studies may indeed be incompatible, but even within the same population, losing the joint structure can still produce error.

The original gives a complete finite counterexample. s=0 and s=1 each have weight one half; treatment a and mediator m are binary; m(a)=a(1−s), y(a,m)=sm. Treatment changes the mediator for those with s=0, but they do not respond to the mediator. Those with s=1 respond to the mediator, but treatment does not change their mediator. The two stages' effects occur in different people.

The local average A→M is therefore 1/2, and the average M→Y under external assignment of M is also 1/2. Under the actual composition m(a), each type's terminal outcome is always 0, making the whole-chain effect 0. The product of averages, 1/4, differs from the average product of individual responses, 0. The given functions refute unconditional multiplication; they do not estimate the effect of any actual mechanism.

“Complete” is relative to a target, window, and dependency route. Identifying a bounded total effect need not require knowledge of every microscopic link. Manipulating a mediator, transferring across domains, or allocating responsibility requires the connections on which that use depends. Shared resources, counteracting paths, and feedback can change the composite outcome. Evidence for each node separately cannot be recast as an established whole chain within the same case.

distinctions.leftText: The effect of each stage averaged separately across the population.
distinctions.rightText: The terminal difference arising from actual sequential connection within the same object.

distinctions.leftText: Each local fact has corresponding grounds.
distinctions.rightText: Versions, identities, timing, and joint responses are compatible in this case.

distinctions.leftText: Covers the connections on which the current use actually depends.
distinctions.rightText: This is not required to identify every bounded total effect.

boundaries: This counterexample is calculated exactly from the original text's specified functions. It cannot establish that all real mediation analyses are invalid, nor negate a total effect identified through another qualified design.

Multiplication may hold if both stage responses are constant across people, or if sufficient structural conditions make the desired whole-chain quantity exactly equal the product of means. These are additional conditions, not consequences of the two means themselves.
Changing the treatment version, permitted mediator manipulation, or terminal target requires rewriting the calculation. Equal numerical values do not mean equal contracts.
questions: Why does “the same population” still not guarantee that the two stage averages can be multiplied?
Is the second stage's 1/2 in this example an average outcome observed under actual m(a)?
Must finding this kind of composition problem revoke a bounded total effect from an independent randomized trial?
argumentSteps: Premise: P(s=0)=P(s=1)=1/2; m(a)=a(1−s), y(a,m)=sm; change a from 0 to 1.
First stage: Δm=m(1)−m(0)=1−s, equal to 1 when s=0 and 0 when s=1, so E[Δm]=1/2.
Second stage: hold a fixed and externally set m from 0 to 1. Then Δ_my=y(a,1)−y(a,0)=s, with mean E[Δ_my]=1/2.
Whole chain: y(a,m(a))=s·a(1−s)=0 because binary s satisfies s(1−s)=0. Hence y(1,m(1))−y(0,m(0)) is 0 for both types, and its mean remains 0.
Incorrect multiplication: E[1−s]E[s]=1/4, whereas E[(1−s)s]=0. Discarding the correspondence between the two stage responses changes the quantity being calculated.

Conclusion and responsibility: this counterexample suffices to refute the universal claim that “two average effects can always be multiplied.” Multiplication in another model requires separate proof of structure, homogeneity, or appropriate joint conditions. The example cannot negate a total effect identified by an independent qualified design.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction from the original: two nonoverlapping response types
teachingExamples.text: Complete two-type table: when s=0, m(0)=0, m(1)=1, and y(a,0)=y(a,1)=0; when s=1, m(0)=m(1)=0, y(a,0)=0, and y(a,1)=1. Each type has terminal outcome 0 under the corresponding composition. With equal weights, both edge averages are 0.5, while the actual whole-chain average is 0.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An exact binary domain, two equally weighted types, and deterministic functions specified in the original, without random error or sampling.
teachingExamples.boundary: This expands the original formal counterexample; it is not an observational study and supplies no proportions or effects for an actual population.

counterexamples.text: In the original counterexample, one group responds only at the first stage and the other only at the second. Both edge averages are 1/2; the whole chain is 0.
counterexamples.effect: Limits unconditional “multiplication of average edges”: joint responses must be retained. It does not affect a separately identified total effect.

questionAnswers.question: Why does “the same population” still not guarantee that the two stage averages can be multiplied?
questionAnswers.answer: Responses may be heterogeneous even within the same population. One must know whether first- and second-stage responses overlap in the same objects.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Is the second stage's 1/2 in this example an average outcome observed under actual m(a)?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It is the average response to externally setting m from 0 to 1. Under actual composition, a does not change m for those with s=1.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Must finding this kind of composition problem revoke a bounded total effect from an independent randomized trial?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Failure of a compositional inference and the total effect from another qualified design have different grounds. Retain or downgrade each according to its own dependencies.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

2.5.title: 2.5 Evidence protocol
2.5.lead: “Having a source” answers only where material comes from, not what it establishes. Evidence is a support relation directed at a specific claim, requiring an account of why every step connects.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 331–336; original anchor section-2-5. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “The fact that material has a source does not permit omission of its support relation to the current claim.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

A source is a person, archive, instrument, or study; material is the text, signal, or data left behind; an observation record is a result organized by rules; evidence is those records' support for a claim. A counterexample challenges a particular claim; judgment combines grounds and uncertainty; authorization for action separately determines what may be done on that basis. One cannot leap from “a reliable institution exists” at the beginning to “I have authority to intervene” at the end.

Record, as appropriate to the task, the object, material-generation process, research design, measurement and selection, uncertainty, competing explanations, and extrapolation boundaries. A material's use may change its support relation: a notice can directly establish what its text says, but cannot alone show that the public understood, personnel implemented it, or outcomes improved. Formal root instances and foresight must also register N0, thresholds, and evaluation under their respective contracts. Do not fabricate a G contract for an ordinary historical text merely to make the form look complete.

Absence and silence have no default direction. An event's absence from a log may mean it did not occur, was not recorded, its record was lost, the record is inaccessible, or disclosure is prohibited. Corresponding negative information arises only when the event should demonstrably have left a detectable record. Evidential force against occurrence varies with recording and retrieval capability; the words “not found” do not automatically make it strong.

Protective nondisclosure is not an unconditional exemption from review. State the protective grounds, minimum scope, duration, and credible reviewer, and reduce the strength of conclusions that cannot be publicly supported. If no credible review is possible at all, privacy cannot become a pass for strong factual claims. Nor should unnecessary sensitive disclosure be compelled merely to complete a field.

When counterexamples and residuals appear after freezing, preserve the original record and downgrade, suspend, or withdraw according to the contract. Objects, subtypes, thresholds, and success criteria cannot be rewritten afterward as “we really intended a different question.” A new question may receive a separate version; the old failure remains under its original contract.

distinctions.leftText: The material and version can be found.
distinctions.rightText: One can explain how the material supports the specific claim and what it still cannot exclude.

distinctions.leftText: Nothing was found within the specified material and search scope.
distinctions.rightText: Requires a sufficiently reliable mechanism by which traces should be left and detected.

distinctions.leftText: Has explicit protective grounds, narrow scope, duration, and credible review.
distinctions.rightText: No such exemption exists; inability to review requires downgrading.

boundaries: Snow's record of unavailable information differs from respondents' reports of not drinking that water. Neither may be rewritten in this lesson as an error-free ground truth of exposure.

Counterexamples must target specific claims. One inconsistent number may affect a precise estimate without overturning all independent material; failure of a shared source or object boundary may affect more conclusions.
Material not frozen beforehand may honestly support exploration or historical explanation. Missing freezing cannot be repaired by fabricating timestamps.

caseLinks.title: Two different kinds of “did not drink” in Snow's investigation

caseNotes.title: Two different kinds of “did not drink” in Snow's investigation
caseNotes.text: Page 40 of Snow's 1855 original separately records six cases in which information could not be obtained because those concerned had died or left, and another six in which respondents reported that patients had not drunk Broad Street pump water before becoming ill. This section uses only that distinction: inability to know and obtaining a negative report are different statuses of material.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Snow, 1855 second edition, p.40
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed page 40, paragraph “With regard to the deaths occurring in the locality belonging to the pump”
caseNotes.boundary: The author's interview records are not omniscient exposure measurements. Unknowns are not filled in as negatives, and reports are not treated as having excluded indirect water consumption.

argumentSteps: Premise: material generation and visibility determine which possible situations it can distinguish. Authentic provenance does not ensure that measurement fits the target.
Connection: material becomes bounded evidence only by stating, item by item, “why this record supports this claim, and which alternative explanations it remains compatible with.”
Reverse check: if the same absence could result either from nonoccurrence or from nonrecording, absence cannot uniquely support nonoccurrence.

Conclusion: register evidence strength, competing explanations, and failures by claim. Opacity and missingness limit the corresponding conclusions rather than automatically eliminating all existing material.

Authorization responsibility: moving from judgment to action still requires norms, lawful authorization, an action ceiling, and stopping conditions. A chain of sources does not itself create authority.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: what does a blank log actually exclude?
teachingExamples.text: Suppose an event always causes the system to generate and retain a retrievable record, and the query scope is complete. Under these conditions, “no record” can count against occurrence. Now suppose the recorder operates only when connected, and the target period may include a network outage. The same blank cannot distinguish nonoccurrence from occurrence unrecorded during an outage. What changed is the material-generation condition, not the researcher's preferred answer.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Both logging systems are teaching assumptions; no claim is made that actual logs are 100% reliable.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual evidential force against occurrence requires material on recording rates, retention policies, permissions, and search coverage. It cannot inherit certainty from this construction.

counterexamples.text: In the historical record, Snow separately records six cases with unavailable drinking-water information and six reporting no consumption of pump water.
counterexamples.effect: “Unknown” must not be merged into “no”; interview reports themselves must still acknowledge limitations from recollection and omitted exposures.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: after discovering failure, changing the original target from “reduce total waiting time” to “allow more people into the queue,” then claiming the original plan succeeded.
counterexamples.effect: Different targets require new versions. Rewriting success criteria cannot erase the original failure.

questionAnswers.question: Can a formal announcement directly establish that every on-site worker followed it?
questionAnswers.answer: No. An announcement is textual material; execution is a separate event requiring corresponding records and connection evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If individual data cannot be disclosed for privacy reasons, may the public conclusion retain the highest certainty?
questionAnswers.answer: Not automatically. Provide protective grounds, minimum scope, duration, and credible review, and limit public conclusions according to what can actually be verified.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: After a counterexample appears following freezing, may the original indicator be deleted and replaced by a favorable one?
questionAnswers.answer: The original result cannot be erased. Preserve the failure, downgrade or suspend under the contract, and create a separate record for the new target.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

2.5.1.title: 2.5.1 Measurement Objects and Data Generation
2.5.1.lead: A score can be calculated very accurately without measuring what you actually care about. Measurement asks first about the target and data generation, then about error magnitude and comparability.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 337–344; source anchor section-2-5-1; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “First explain what is to be measured and how the materials are generated.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

The source distinguishes five kinds of object. Directly recorded quantities, such as counts under an established protocol, still entail responsibility for missed records and event definitions. Definitional composite indicators combine components by rule; correct calculation does not establish a latent attribute that the indicator reflects. Latent-attribute measurement must explain the model relating observable indicators to an attribute not directly visible, alternatives and validation. Formative conditions concern conditions that jointly constitute or affect the target; they need not rise and fall together as reflective indicators of one attribute would. A predictive proxy only needs predictive capability for a future target; it does not thereby become a direct measure of another target.

Thus a test score can reliably record performance in the current item domain without fully representing long-term capability. Declining service use may indicate unmet needs, and increasing diagnoses may result from easier detection rather than more disease. These are different data-generation paths; observing one direction must not automatically select the most appealing story.

Comparisons across groups or periods must fit the purpose. Estimating latent means requires interpretable correspondence in scale units and origins; making person-level threshold decisions also requires analysis of individual error and consequences. Using the same scoring formula in two groups does not establish identical item meanings, response strategies or measurement relations. If shared anchors drift, larger samples may only estimate the same unidentified problem more precisely; seek external anchors or perform sensitivity analysis.

Improvement in an indicator may have at least four causes: genuine improvement in the target; behavior that adapts to a narrow metric without improving the broader target; changes in sample or reporting composition; or fabricated records. These mechanisms can coexist, but indicator change alone must not trigger accusations of fabrication. Two valid indicators can also move in opposite directions while both being correct if one measures a total and the other a subgroup.

The actual algorithm case illustrates proxy mismatch: costs were the predicted label, and the study compared costs and health burdens across groups at the same risk score. Similar cross-group cost calibration does not mean small individual prediction errors or good aggregate prediction accuracy. When identifying care needs, the relationship between cost and need must also be validated as comparable in the target groups. Reconsidering the label does not declare all proxies invalid; it requires evidence of fit for the current purpose.

caseLinks.title: The 2019 study of a cost-prediction algorithm: proxy and need are different targets

caseNotes.title: The 2019 study of a cost-prediction algorithm: proxy and need are different targets
caseNotes.text: Obermeyer et al. analyzed data from a large academic hospital during 2013–2015. The audited algorithm predicted healthcare costs. At the same risk score, the study found similar costs in the following year for the two groups but a heavier health burden among Black patients. This indicates more consistent cross-group cost calibration, not necessarily high aggregate or individual prediction accuracy; calibration also cannot replace a test of fitness for care needs.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: Science 366 (2019), 447–453; printed pp. 447–449, Data and analytic strategy, Health disparities conditional on risk score, Mechanism of bias; PDF pp. 1–3
caseNotes.boundary: Interpret the paper within its specific sample, indicators and purpose. This guide has not recalculated individual data, makes no individual medical judgment and does not claim that changing the label has improved actual long-term outcomes.

argumentSteps: Premise: observed scores are jointly generated by the target attribute, measurement rules, opportunities for contact, selection and recording processes; different generation processes can produce the same score.

Classification: first register whether the measurement concerns a direct quantity, definitional composite, latent attribute, formative condition or predictive proxy, and identify which errors affect its current use.
Connection: accurate prediction of a label directly supports only that label's task; using it to judge need, capability or value requires separate evidence connecting measurement and purpose.
Comparison conditions: when groups or times change, check units, origins, anchors, individual errors and sample composition; an identical formula does not imply identical psychological processes.
Conclusion: when reporting indicator changes, retain competing generation mechanisms and propose discriminating checks; without sufficient materials, do not promote one explanation into fact.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: a changing mean or a drifting scale origin
teachingExamples.text: Assume an observed score S=θ+b, where θ is the attribute to be measured and b the scale origin. An observed mean rising from 4 to 6 over two periods could reflect θ increasing by 2 with b unchanged, or unchanged θ with b increasing by 2. Observing S alone cannot distinguish them. Even infinitely large samples and error-free observed means in each period still require external anchoring or testable constraints to interpret the change.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An additive measurement model, common units and no other error; used only to illustrate identifiability.
teachingExamples.boundary: Not measured facts about any scale or population; a particular measurement relation may be nonlinear and require a different model.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two correct indicators can move in opposite directions
teachingExamples.text: A service handles 10 cases in the first period, of which 2 are overdue, then 30 in the second, of which 3 are overdue. The total overdue count rises from 2 to 3, while the rate falls from 20% to 10%. Both calculations are correct: one answers total burden, the other the proportion of cases. Opposite directions alone cannot establish fabrication by either side.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Case counts are stipulated for teaching, and event definitions and windows are comparable; there is no sampling or underreporting.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not establish improvement in a real service; case difficulty, demand and people not served in the second period may still affect evaluation.

counterexamples.text: The study shows similar next-year costs in the two groups at the same risk score, indicating relatively consistent cross-group cost calibration, while Black patients have a heavier health burden.
counterexamples.effect: This limits the inference that “consistent cross-group cost calibration fairly identifies health needs”; it does not establish high individual cost-prediction accuracy or invalidate the cost-prediction task itself.

counterexamples.text: In the teaching construction, scale-origin drift and genuine attribute change produce the same observed change in means.
counterexamples.effect: More observations of the same kind cannot alone identify the two mechanisms; add anchoring or make sensitivity explicit.

questionAnswers.question: If a test is very stable on retesting, can one immediately conclude it measures long-term capability?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Stability is one property; construct content, generalization beyond the item domain, measurement relations and fitness for use still require argument.

questionAnswers.question: Can falling service use directly establish falling need?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Accessibility, price, supply, sampling and recording changes can all alter use; discriminating materials are required.

2.6.title: 2.6 Analogy Protocol
2.6.lead: The most useful role of “this resembles something else” is to suggest what to investigate next; it cannot directly import that other thing's causes, evaluations and solutions.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 345–350; source anchor section-2-6; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Analogy is only a tool for generating questions.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

An adequate analogy lists at least the source domain, target domain, shared structure, key differences, nontransferable conditions, variable mapping and discriminating tests, and explicitly calls itself an analogy in the main text. Comparing a queue to stored water, for example, may share an “inflow, stock, outflow” structure. But people can leave, change choices or respond strategically, and water volume and numbers of people must not be combined without specifying units and processes.

A variable mapping turns “similarity” from rhetoric into a checkable proposal: which source-domain quantity corresponds to which target-domain quantity, under which operations the relationship persists, and when it fails. Similar diagrams, identical words, appealing stories and similar outcomes do not complete this mapping. Treating “organizational immunity” or “social temperature” as measured mechanisms exemplifies the overreach to avoid.

An analogy can generate a checklist: which source-domain channels, boundaries or competing explanations merit investigation in the target domain? But empirical causal relations in the source do not automatically become target-domain facts. Corresponding operations, measurements and alternative explanations still need testing in the target, and analogy cannot replace formal G-instance requirements.

Contrary conditions must actually constrain the claim. If researchers say “it still looks similar” regardless of what they observe, the analogy cannot eliminate mistaken candidates. A reasonable formulation states that particular target-domain behavior, object identities or resource constraints invalidate the mapping; if discriminating tests are incomplete, retain only a heuristic candidate. Normative evaluations and action plans particularly must not transfer directly on resemblance alone.

distinctions.leftText: Some relations or indicators can correspond.
distinctions.rightText: Identical causal processes and operating conditions require new discriminating evidence.

distinctions.leftText: Deciding what to investigate first.
distinctions.rightText: Which relations the materials can already support has a different evidential force.

distinctions.leftText: A judgment reached under the source domain's value criteria.
distinctions.rightText: Targets, rights, risks and authorization must be made explicit anew.

boundaries: In actual research, similar statistics can result from different formation processes; two similar numbers cannot establish identical social institutions.
An analogy need not match in every respect to be useful, but the part claimed to transfer must be explicit; stop using it or narrow it when differences affect key premises.
This guide does not use biological analogies to assign standing, personality or governance arrangements to actual individuals or groups.

When comparing human behavior to water flow, what should be added first?
If an analogy faces counterevidence but can still inspire a question, must it be discarded entirely?

caseLinks.title: A 2022 ancient-DNA study's explicit limits on resemblance to great apes

caseNotes.title: A 2022 ancient-DNA study's explicit limits on resemblance to great apes
caseNotes.text: Skov et al. compared patterns of genetic diversity when studying Neanderthal communities, but explicitly warned in “Inferring social organization” that similar ratios of Y-chromosome to mitochondrial coalescence times do not necessarily imply the same social organization; multiple scenarios can produce similar statistics.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Skov et al., Genetic insights into the social organization of Neanderthals
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Nature 610 (2022), 519–525; PMC main text, Inferring social organization, the cautionary paragraph following the comparison of 47 human populations and 10 great-ape subspecies (this guide does not use its specific comparative values)
caseNotes.boundary: Only the authors' limitation on analogy is used; ancient DNA is not used to evaluate modern groups, and their demographic-history model is not recalculated.

argumentSteps: Premise: known relations in the source domain depend on its particular objects, variables and operating conditions; similarity covers only some of these.
Connection: writing down mappings and differences first permits judgment of which source-domain questions can be target-domain candidates and which observations would invalidate the mapping.
Conclusion: analogy permits asking questions and generating relations for testing, not directly declaring that target-domain mechanisms, value judgments or actions are established.
Evidential responsibility: target-domain support must come from its own materials and bridges; even reliable source-domain research cannot fill in unobserved conditions in the target.
Responsibility for failure: retain dissimilarities and counterevidence; mapping failures must not be explained away as target-domain “anomalies” while the analogy is never revised.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching analogy: when a queue stops resembling stored water
teachingExamples.text: The source domain is a water tank and the target a service queue. Mapping inflow to new arrivals, water level to queue length and outflow to completed service can generate the question to investigate: “Does the stock accumulate when arrivals exceed processing capacity?” But if people can leave midway, obtain duplicate queue numbers or decide not to arrive after seeing a long queue, additional channels are needed. Record arrivals, completions, exits and duplicate counts to test which conservation equation applies, rather than directly substituting tank parameters for a population.
teachingExamples.assumptions: This is an explicitly labeled teaching analogy; no real queue has been observed. The target domain must declare its own units and event rules.
teachingExamples.boundary: The analogy does not establish service effectiveness, still less that people should be controlled like water; empirical and normative conditions in the target domain require separate checks.

counterexamples.text: Skov et al.'s 2022 study explicitly warns that similar Y-chromosome/mitochondrial coalescence-time ratios in Neanderthals and great apes do not necessarily imply identical social organization; multiple scenarios can produce similar ratios.
counterexamples.effect: A real study itself distinguishes statistical resemblance from social explanation; similar indicators must not be used to bypass generation mechanisms.

questionAnswers.question: If two systems both have hub-and-spoke diagrams, can one directly conclude that the central nodes control all resources?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Similar-looking diagrams do not reveal the meaning of edges, actual flows, permissions, or alternative channels. Materials from the target domain must be checked.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: When comparing human behavior to water flow, what should be added first?
questionAnswers.answer: Specify mappings of variables and units, crucial differences such as people's exit and strategic responses, conditions that cannot transfer, and target-domain records capable of distinguishing these processes.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If an analogy faces counterevidence but can still inspire a question, must it be discarded entirely?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. Restrict or remove the failed part while retaining insights that clearly remain applicable. The original strong mechanism conclusion must not be retained.

2.6.1.title: 2.6.1 Analogy, Formal Instances, and Tested Comparisons
2.6.1.lead: Resembling something, belonging to the same class within a model, and being supported in the target world are three different statuses. Keeping them separate neither devalues analogy nor lends it evidential force it has not acquired.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source, lines 351–356; original anchor section-2-6-1. Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Heuristic analogy, a formal instance satisfying explicit mathematical premises, and a target-domain relation tested against independent materials are three different statuses.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the original research extract available for download preserves the historical manuscript.

The first is heuristic analogy: explain similarities and differences and propose a relation worth testing. The second is a formal instance: variables and operations satisfy all premises of a mathematical proposition, so the conclusion follows by proof within that model, irrespective of whether the stories seem alike. The third is a tested target-domain relation: independent materials together with bridges support the specific relation, and the support comes from those materials, not from calling it similar. The three can work together in one study, but must not automatically be upgraded from one status to another.

For example, the existence of a path in an abstract graph is a formal property. Mapping an actual link to the ability to send information requires checking that the corresponding channel is available. Claiming that information actually traveled through it and changed an outcome requires further evidence of events and effects. Even with isomorphic graphs, edges representing cooperation, power supply, or kinship have entirely different meanings for real-world operations.

Historical and archaeological materials require even clearer separation of layers: how traces physically formed is one layer; which activity or function they correspond to is another; the social relations and institutions involving participants are a third. Similar tool marks may raise questions about activities, but do not automatically identify the same power regime. Kinship identification can support a biological relationship without by itself showing who ruled whom. More accurate dating helps establish sequence, but does not by itself answer what an event meant.

Respecting different sources of knowledge does not mean giving them equal weight for every question. Dating measurements, genetic relations, local knowledge, oral accounts, and textual context may each answer non-interchangeable questions. Material unsuited to one claim is not thereby useless for every question. Conversely, the importance of a form of knowledge must not exempt it from criticism required for the proposed use.

This section continues using the ancient-DNA study but adds a new focus: the scope of support for identifying a relation. Kinship conclusions depend on genetic materials and interpretation, whereas conclusions about rule or normative standing need separate social evidence. This limit is the lesson's analysis of how the material may be used; it does not invent political conclusions that the study's authors never proposed and then refute them.

distinctions.leftText: The object and mapping satisfy specified mathematical premises.
distinctions.rightText: The target-domain mapping and premises have appropriate observational and design support.

distinctions.leftText: An evidential judgment about biological relatedness.
distinctions.rightText: Roles, rules, domination, resources, and institutional relations; these must not be inferred automatically from kinship.

distinctions.leftText: Clues to possible formation processes.
distinctions.rightText: Requires additional grounds concerning activities and social relations.

boundaries: The father–daughter conclusion in the ancient-DNA study does not by itself establish male rule, inheritance rules, or the community's full institutional arrangements. This lesson does not claim that such institutions were necessarily absent; this material is simply insufficient to decide.

Formal isomorphism preserves the registered structural properties, not every everyday meaning and causal parameter. More accurate dating likewise does not automatically recover an event's entire meaning.

Comparative research need not always be merely suggestive. After testing with independent target-domain materials, it may take on limited argumentative responsibilities according to its actual design.

caseNotes.title: The father–daughter relationship at Chagyrskaya: which relation do the materials support?
caseNotes.text: In Genetic relationships, Skov et al.'s 2022 paper combines first-degree relatedness with different mitochondrial genomes to identify Chagyrskaya H as D's daughter. This lesson distinguishes the scope of that finding: it is a kinship judgment supported by genetic materials. Ruling status or institutions must not be added solely on the basis of that relation.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: Nature 610 (2022), 519–525; the paragraph beginning “One adult male individual, Chagyrskaya D” in Genetic relationships in the PMC text, and Table 1
caseNotes.boundary: The statement that kinship does not automatically establish rule is this lesson's limitation on use. It does not claim that the paper's authors proposed or rejected a particular ruling system, or generalize from this site to all Neanderthal societies.

argumentSteps: Classification premise: specify whether the item is a proposal of similarity, an instance of mathematical premises, or an empirical comparison supported by target-domain materials.

Formal connection: if graph isomorphism or an instance of a proposition is claimed, verify one by one the objects, relations, and operations preserved by the mapping. Only preserved properties may transfer through the proof.

Empirical connection: real-world relations require examination of material generation, operations, timing, identities, and alternative explanations. Formal isomorphism does not directly establish actual use or causal effects.

Historical connection: moving from traces to functions and then to social relations requires listing new assumptions and discriminating materials at each step. Evidence at other layers must not manufacture truth for a missing layer.
Conclusion: tested comparison may enter an argument, but must precisely identify where support comes from and retain relations that have not been tested as such.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching mathematical construction: isomorphic graphs can transfer reachability, not power
teachingExamples.text: Let G₁ have nodes {a,b,c} and edges {a→b,b→c}, and G₂ have nodes {1,2,3} and edges {1→2,2→3}. The mapping a↦1, b↦2, c↦3 preserves each edge, so if a path exists from a to c in G₁, a path exists from 1 to 3 in G₂. If one graph is interpreted as an authorization chain and the other as contact among colleagues, graph isomorphism does not also prove the authorization semantics.

teachingExamples.boundary: The proof covers only reachability in the graphs. It does not establish that the actual relations exist, that information is transmitted, or who has authority to act.

counterexamples.text: Kinship evidence can support a father–daughter relationship, but by itself cannot distinguish multiple possible arrangements of social power.

questionAnswers.question: Are two perfectly isomorphic organizational charts enough to establish identical actual decision mechanisms in the organizations?

questionAnswers.question: Does identifying two ancient individuals as father and daughter directly justify writing that the father ruled the community?

2.7.title: 2.7 Source Protocol
2.7.lead: A source list is not better merely because it is longer. Each judgment should lead back to the precise location that supports it. Citing theory to explain how to test something does not mean that real-world test results have been obtained.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source, lines 357–364; original anchor section-2-7. Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Method definitions are not empirical support.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the original research extract available for download preserves the historical manuscript.

For each source, record the domain, case type, time and region, scope of support, limits of extrapolation, and relevant counterexamples. Separate original materials, secondary interpretations, and inferences made within this framework, so readers can trace a judgment to its original location and see which limited claims a given material is being used to support. Bidirectional links serve to check whether inference exceeds its bounds, not to label sources as authoritative.

Concept definitions, field mappings, and method explanations determine what to ask, how to record it, and where to stop. They must not enter empirical_evidence_records as object facts or support for mechanisms. For example, the book's definition of how G2 tests a specified channel does not establish that the channel exists in an actual object. Its account of how C combines results does not mean that actual materials already support every combined link.

Applications for formal empirical support require separately registered instance materials: object and scale, time window, research design, N0, results, uncertainty, review or replication, and evidential level. This follows the two-stage admission in §2.1; it does not force every archive into a modern experimental format. Ordinary domain evidence retains its original design, while formal G support is obtained under the corresponding contract.

C serves different purposes, including registering results, specifying mechanism conditions, and normative bridging. It must not uniformly be treated as additional causal facts. CM judgments about actual mechanisms still require corresponding instance evidence. Question catalogues, outcome contracts, and explanations of the framework itself can at most specify testing responsibilities. Repeated citation will not fill gaps in external materials.

Sources closer to the original generation of information generally make specific details easier to check, but original materials may also contain errors, omissions, or interpretation. Examine version, generation process, precise location, and correspondence to claims separately; primary must not mean beyond criticism. The next section addresses source relations and reading scope, and the following section addresses independence and how errors propagate.

2.7.1.title: 2.7.1 Relationships among sources and actual scope of use
2.7.1.lead: Sources have genealogies, and reading has a scope. Transcription, republication, or revision of a file does not automatically add independent evidence by multiplying URLs.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 365–372; source anchor section-2-7-1; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “Finding a link, completing a download, and understanding an argument are not the same act either.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

Record separately whether only the contents list, the abstract, relevant chapters, or the full text were read. Finding a link establishes discovery of an entry point; downloading establishes acquisition of a file; understanding a passage's argument still requires actually examining its premises and material. Reading only relevant passages can honestly support bounded facts within them; do not enlarge that reading scope into a claim of full-text review.

Preserve relationships among different analyses of the same data, preprints and final versions, and original reports and institutional retellings. Another algorithm may expose errors in the original analysis without automatically generating new observations; a final version may also change the sample, outcomes, or definitions. List changes before comparing: similar titles alone justify neither merging them nor treating them as replications.

The history of a theory also requires distinguishing actual adoption, mere mention, explicit limitation or rejection, compatibility with the current text, and a new connection proposed by today's analyst. Each historical claim needs its own record. “Compatible as seen today” does not establish that the author was influenced by it then; failure to find evidence of adoption is insufficient to say “the author never considered it.”

Absence from an archive follows multiple filters: whether an event generated a record, whether it was preserved or destroyed, whether it was opened to access, whether retrieval can find it, and whether the narrator ultimately selected it. Absence has corresponding counterevidential force only when events of that kind should have left discoverable traces. Failure to obtain a file within one research window does not mean other researchers or the entire project lack it.

Date errors in oral accounts should still be corrected, while the manner of narration may supply material about memory, experience, and meaning. One chronological error does not make the whole oral account worthless; the account's value does not justify refusing to correct factual misplacement either. Evaluate different uses separately.

This does not warrant inferring that the interviewee is lying, nor retaining the wrong year as a fact.

2.7.2.title: 2.7.2 Evidence independence and propagation of defects
2.7.2.lead: A different analysis of the same material may indeed add knowledge, but does not add an independent sample. Finding a discrepancy should initially suspend only conclusions that actually depend on it.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 373–378; source anchor section-2-7-2; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “Independence must be judged relative to the claim being supported.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

Independence is not an unconditional yes/no label. Long-term follow-up of the same randomized allocation adds information on time and outcomes, but not another randomization; rechecking the same material with another algorithm adds implementation and interpretation checks, but not a new original cohort. Conversely, two studies with the same topic name but different underlying samples must not be forcibly merged based solely on their titles.

Source relationships should preserve shared data, common measurements, version inheritance, and new observations. Specify which stage is independent: data may be shared while analytical implementations are independent; measurement methods may be shared while samples of objects are independent. Evaluating a particular claim requires identifying its dependence on these stages, not converting file counts into evidence scores.

On finding a numerical discrepancy, first determine whether it is a conflict about the same object, a legitimate difference between different objects, or an apparent difference in display precision. Cases versus person-occurrences, cumulative versus new counts, onset date versus death date, and the whole population versus a threshold-defined subgroup need not be equal. If a genuine conflict remains unexplained, suspend precise conclusions depending on that number and trace the chain “source value → transcription → model input → derived quantity → main text.”

Agreement of sums is a check, but cannot by itself certify every component. One component increasing while another decreases can leave the total unchanged; conversely, an anomaly does not immediately identify transcription error, fabrication, or actual change as its cause. First report the locatable discrepancy and affected scope; do not fill in causes on behalf of the evidence.

Other judgments with independent grounds can continue to be used within their scope. Only failure of a common source, key premise, or object boundary blocks all related outputs. Proposition-by-proposition handling allows correction without concealing a problem or inflating a local issue into an unsupported wholesale rejection.

distinctions.leftText: New underlying observations or cohorts.
distinctions.rightText: A different implementation on the same underlying sample; it may reveal errors but does not count another group of people.

distinctions.leftText: The claims still cannot coexist after aligning object, unit, and time.
distinctions.rightText: The objects, denominators, or indicators being compared were different to begin with.

distinctions.leftText: The sum of components matches the total.
distinctions.rightText: Each component has correct provenance, classification, and definitions; further checking is required.

distinctions.leftText: Affects particular values and derived conclusions.
distinctions.rightText: May block every output depending on it, with a broader scope.

boundaries: Snow's Table I gives 20 onsets of ultimately fatal cases on September 6 and 28 on September 7. Thus, the text's “decreased every day” cannot mechanically be read as a strictly monotonic sequence. This local counterexample does not erase the overall decline, nor determine the cause of a difference involving transcription or the original wording.

This lesson checks only the aggregate and these two daily values in the current digital transcription; it does not claim word-for-word collation of the original death registers. The 43 dated rows are not 43 independent studies.
571+45=616 does not establish that the 45 unknown dates can be allocated arbitrarily, or that the complete number of infections is known.
questions: Can adding three years of follow-up to the same randomized trial be described as conducting a new randomized trial?
If a table's total equals the sum of its components, does that establish that every component is correct?
If a figure for one day is disputed, why should every judgment in the same book not immediately be withdrawn?

caseNotes.text: Table I in the current transcription lists 45 cases with unknown onset dates; the other 43 dated rows sum to 571, for a total of 616. A further local check shows 20 on September 6 and 28 on September 7, so “decreased every day” cannot be used as a strictly monotonic numerical proposition. argumentSteps: Premise one: new information can come from new samples, times, measurements, or analyses; these additions are not the same kind of independence.
Premise two: derived conclusions depend only on their actual inputs and premises, so error propagation has specific paths.

Connection: first align numbers by object, definition, unit, window, and precision, then determine whether there is a genuine conflict or a legitimate difference; for a genuine conflict, suspend conclusions along the dependency path.
Conclusion: register both independence and downgrading claim by claim; unaffected independent grounds are not invalidated together with a local anomaly.

Actual calculation: the 43 dated rows for known onset dates in Snow's Table I sum to 571; adding 45 with unknown onset dates gives the table's total of 616. This agreement checks only aggregation, not the correctness of the allocation across dates.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: the same total with both components wrong
teachingExamples.text: Suppose the true components are 40 and 60, totaling 100. If transcribed as 45 and 55, the total is still 100. Passing the total check does not guarantee correct components. Text using only an independently checked total may be unaffected by this allocation error; text using the two groups' proportions or difference requires suspending the relevant inference.
teachingExamples.assumptions: These numbers are purely a teaching construction, not Snow's data or any actual dataset.
teachingExamples.boundary: Demonstrates error propagation without accusing any real author of fabrication or identifying a particular transcription error.

counterexamples.text: The values 20 on September 6 and 28 on September 7 in Snow's Table I are incompatible with a strictly monotonic reading of the subsequent “decreased every day.”
counterexamples.effect: Suspend the strict day-by-day monotonicity claim; a supported description of overall decline may remain, but cannot yield the net effect of handle removal.

counterexamples.text: Teaching construction: 40+60 and 45+55 both equal 100.
counterexamples.effect: Agreement of the total cannot independently certify every component; trace the particular derived quantities.

questionAnswers.answer: No. Additional information about time and outcomes is worth retaining, but neither allocation nor the original cohort has thereby been replicated.

2.8.title: 2.8 Core terminology lock
2.8.lead: ‘Cost’, ‘repair’, ‘choice’, and ‘responsibility’ are everyday words, but each carries different conditions for judgment. Fixing their meanings prevents a sentence from silently changing meaning during an inference.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 379–396; source anchor section-2-8; short quotation: ‘Their broad everyday meanings must not be substituted’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

Cost is first a quantity of some type: its type, unit, time window, accounting boundary, and cost-bearing position must be stated. Cash, working hours, risk, and attention cannot simply be added; conversion requires an explicit valuation, measurement, or accounting mapping. Lower spending in one place does not mean a cost of the same type necessarily shifts elsewhere, much less establish a universal conservation of cost across domains. Occupation of resources is an observation; comparability with other quantities is a separate task.

Externality here involves two steps: first establish a cross-boundary causal channel and the positions across which effects are distributed, then specify which impact an economic model or actual institutional or accounting rule excludes from decision accounting. With only the first step, call it a cross-boundary spillover or impact; terminology must not assign responsibility in advance. The second step does not require prior determination of legal liability; inability to determine who is legally liable does not prevent recording supported cross-boundary harm.

Cross-boundary analysis also requires the right contract. C7 addresses spillovers and distributional positions under its specified conditions, not every economic externality or instance of transmission. Check D3/E5 separately only where scale actually changes; test the corresponding G4 only when claiming formal support for closure failure or object or intervention conversion. The word ‘external’ alone must not trigger every scale procedure.

Repair requires disclosure, before outcomes, of the target identity K* or function F*: which object identity or function is to be recovered. Repair may allow a new implementation rather than reproduce the historical form; recovery of a specified function also does not equal an improvement in value. Whether the target is justified, who decides it, and who may implement it remain subject to N and O review. The target must not be changed after seeing results to declare any change a successful repair.

Choice has three meanings. System selection is a process of variation, differential retention, and reproduction; it need not involve intention. Choice by an acting subject involves a subject deciding under conditions and must not be equated with environmental selection. Governance choice additionally requires comparisons of options, normative premises, and authorization; observing that an outcome was retained does not mean someone justifiably chose it.

Responsibility and authorization separately register the uptake carrier, bearer of costs of the same type, beneficiaries, right to stop, and responsible party. Being the actual implementer, the most capable, the most affected, the most visible, or the best informed does not by itself make someone infinitely responsible. Expanded observation or confidence in explanation does not expand jurisdiction J either.

Reasons for obligations may include commitments, roles, causal contributions, benefits, capabilities, and applicable norms; disclose how they jointly support specific obligations and their boundaries. Bounded obligations do not turn anyone into a unilateral, unlimited uptake party with no exit; arrangements for stopping, handoff, duration, and remedy are themselves part of responsibility judgments.

distinctions.leftText: A change in an amount of money within a specified boundary, unit, and window.
distinctions.rightText: A stronger judgment across different cost bearers and quantity types, requiring grounds for conversion and allocation.

distinctions.leftText: Has causation and distributional positions.
distinctions.rightText: Additionally specifies the rule excluding the impact from decision accounting; this is not prior determination of legal liability.

distinctions.leftText: Meets K* or F* specified before outcomes.
distinctions.rightText: A justified target and acceptable consequences, requiring additional normative assessment.

distinctions.leftText: A process of differential retention.
distinctions.rightText: The former requires a subject's decision; the latter additionally requires norms and permissions.

distinctions.leftText: Records who actually bears or receives what.
distinctions.rightText: Bounded obligations supported by multiple reasons and norms; not automatically the same party.

boundaries: This section specifies specialized meanings and conditions of use; definitions do not establish a universal conservation of cost or a shared purpose in the world.
Failure to determine legal liability does not prevent recording harm; recording harm also does not establish burden shares or authority to act.

Observational capability and authorization are different scale axes. Even complete knowledge of the situation still requires checking permissions for the particular object, action, territory, validity period, and withdrawal conditions.
Repair targets must not be arbitrarily rewritten after results; necessary changes require a new version that preserves outcomes under the original target.
questions: If pollution is recorded as harming others across a boundary, must legal liability first be determined before its impacts can be reported?
Why does a function meeting its pre-specified target still not justify declaring ‘this is a good option and may be implemented immediately’?
If A benefits most and B performs most of the implementation, may that alone identify one sole responsible party?
argumentSteps: Premise: an everyday word often simultaneously carries descriptive, evaluative, and action-related meanings; mixing them allows a later step to borrow grounds the earlier step never supplied.

First connection: costs first require the same type and unit or a valid conversion; externalities first require causation and exclusion rules; repair first requires K*/F*; choice first requires specifying the system, subject, or governance meaning.

Second connection: where responsibility is involved, separately check roles, causation, commitments, benefits, capabilities, and norms instead of deriving total responsibility directly from one visible identity.
Conclusion: locking meanings makes each step's missing conditions visible; ‘successful repair’ must not bypass value review, and ‘I understand’ must not bypass authorization.

Evidential and normative responsibility: cross-boundary effects and cost-bearing positions require materials; exclusion rules require a basis in models or institutions; obligations and action ceilings require norms and valid authorization.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: budget savings and time burdens cannot simply be conserved
teachingExamples.text: Suppose an option reduces an institution's monthly spending by 100 yuan but makes a user wait an additional 3 hours. First record yuan/month and hours/person-visit separately, along with their bearers; do not write ‘total cost fell by 97’ or ‘100 yuan fully converted into 3 hours’. Only with an explicit valuation of v yuan per hour may 100−3v be written for a specified number of people and window. This v includes choices of value and measurement and must not be disguised as a universal constant of the world.
teachingExamples.assumptions: 100 yuan and 3 hours are teaching assumptions; an illustrative conversion is possible only after explicitly specifying conditions such as a single user and the same window.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not estimate the net welfare of an actual option or allocate legal liability from these numbers.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: functional repair does not mean everything returns to its old form
teachingExamples.text: Suppose the pre-specified F* is ‘reading error no greater than e under a given load’. If valid measurement after component replacement shows F* is met, this may count as functional recovery within that contract; there is no need to claim that every original component has been restored. If the new component introduces additional safety risks or infringes others' rights, meeting the function criterion does not by itself justify the option.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The equipment, load, error bound, and outcome are all conditional teaching assumptions, not a measurement report.
teachingExamples.boundary: Qualification as repair is limited to the specified function; justification, actual evidence, and implementation permissions are checked separately.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: the person who understands the system best is required to bear all maintenance costs permanently solely because ‘only you are capable’.
counterexamples.effect: Capability may be one reason for responsibility, but does not by itself imply an unlimited obligation with no exit.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: an organizational form survives competition, which is described as ‘the system intentionally selected the most justified institution’.
counterexamples.effect: Differential retention has been replaced by a subject's intention and normative superiority; both additional claims lack grounds.

questionAnswers.question: If pollution is recorded as harming others across a boundary, must legal liability first be determined before its impacts can be reported?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Recording causal harm, identifying accounting-exclusion rules, and determining legal liability are different tasks; supported impacts can be retained first.

questionAnswers.question: Why does a function meeting its pre-specified target still not justify declaring ‘this is a good option and may be implemented immediately’?
questionAnswers.answer: Functional repair does not settle values, risks, permissions, action ceilings, or stopping conditions; N and O require separate checking.

questionAnswers.answer: No. Disclose the relations among commitments, roles, causal contributions, benefits, capabilities, and applicable norms, and bound the obligations.
