3.2.title: 3.2 D1 Basic State Terms
3.2.lead: Changed, still here, and repaired sound simple, but use different criteria. D1 requires specifying the criterion and time window first, so observed change is not mistaken for progress, continued existence for health, or the word repair for permission to act.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source, lines 475–492; original anchor section-3-2. Short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Evolution does not entail a path, direction, or value.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the original research extract available for download preserves the historical manuscript.

Change requires only a detectable difference in registered variables between two observation positions. These may be two times or two measurements on the same basis; definitions, resolution, and error must be checked. Change does not specify who caused the difference, whether it persists, or where it is heading. If measurement error covers the difference, two nonidentical numbers alone must not be registered as a change in the process.

Operation is a transition in X while B, R, I, SP, and K still hold under the current contract. Queue increases and decreases under the same rules may count as operation. Persistence asks only whether the current K continues to hold throughout the specified window; it can coexist separately with active operation, suspension, or declining performance. Duration of existence alone says nothing about health, justification, progress, or whether something should continue.

Evolution concerns detectable changes over time in object-contract fields: boundaries, the set of variables, relations, interfaces, scale positions, or identity conditions, exceeding the predeclared fluctuation window. Distinguish changes in X's values from changes in X as a set of variables. Queue q changing from 2 to 3 is usually only a state change; incorporating new variables, nodes, or connections into the object contract concerns the criterion for evolution here. If K itself changes, record the contract version and reassessment of identity. Do not silently treat a new standard as though it had always been the old one.

The source deliberately does not add durable traces, path dependence, selection, or a direction of value to evolution. A structural change followed by recovery need not be excluded as never having evolved; the question is whether it crossed the prespecified fluctuation window at the time. Claims that history adds information about the future beyond the currently registered state require separate G3 testing. Claims of a selection mechanism involving variation, differential retention, and reproduction require C8/CM-SELECTION. Records of structural change alone do not imply these stronger mechanisms.

Dissolution means that the original K no longer holds. K may concern connectivity, compositional identity, or another prespecified condition, so dissolution may mean termination, object conversion, or reclassification, rather than automatic task failure. Deliberately dismantling a failed device or ending temporary cooperation are conceptual possibilities only. Whether they actually occurred and whether they were justified still require separate factual and normative judgments.

Repair means that a new state meets the predeclared target K* or F*, the latter being a functional criterion. Components, boundaries, relations, and carriers may be replaced; item-by-item return to a historical state is not required. Reaching just any new state is not automatically repair, and targets must not be arbitrarily lowered after the outcome. If repairing the old object differs from forming a new object that satisfies the function, retain an account of whether the old K failed and whether identity continues.

D1 itself neither defines structure nor validates a D0 candidate object. Using terms such as operation or persistence must not retrospectively prove grouping validity. Limited support from a formal G1-instance requires its preregistered threshold, a complexity-matched N0, and limits concerning SP/T/K and extrapolation units. Reliable domain records may still support facts within their original scope. N and O separately examine why to repair, toward which target, who decides, and who executes. Word meanings cannot generate real-world permissions.

Basic state terms may apply to objects supported by existing domain facts, without treating G1 as eligibility to exist. Saying a service has recovered under a specified functional criterion requires evidence about that function, object, and window. A further claim that grouping users this way improves prediction requires separate G1 testing. Keep state conclusions and grouping performance separate.

distinctions.leftText: Different values within the same set of variables.
distinctions.rightText: Changes in contract fields such as boundaries, variable sets, and relations exceeding the prespecified fluctuation window.

distinctions.leftText: K continues to hold within the specified window.
distinctions.rightTitle: Health or a reason to continue
distinctions.rightText: Additional judgments involving function, risk, and value.

distinctions.leftText: Changes in contract fields under specified detection conditions.
distinctions.rightText: Respectively require a historical contribution beyond the current representation, or evidence of variation–differential retention–reproduction.

distinctions.leftText: The original K fails, potentially leading to termination or conversion.
distinctions.rightText: An evaluation relative to a task objective; it cannot be inferred solely from identity failure.

distinctions.leftText: A new state meets K* or F* specified beforehand.
distinctions.rightText: Returning to the historical state is not necessary; the definition also does not determine who may execute the action.

boundaries: The six terms are neither mutually exclusive categories nor life stages every object must pass through. One operation may simultaneously involve state change, operation, and continued persistence. Check the criteria for each conclusion separately.
Criteria and fluctuation windows should be specified before interpreting outcomes, to avoid calling arbitrary noise evolution or changing K after failure to claim uninterrupted persistence.
Evolution must not automatically be labeled maturity, advancement, decline, or a necessary direction. Change may be temporary or reversible and may affect different tasks differently.

Keeping logs establishes only that records exist. Whether history still adds a conditional increment for the future requires separate examination. The absence of a G3 increment does not deny that past events formed the current state.
Meeting a functional criterion need not mean continuity of the old object's identity. Clarify how target K* and F* relate to the original K; do not use repair to conceal object conversion.
questions: If a machine reading changes from 10 to 11, has evolution necessarily occurred?
Does an object's persisting for ten years imply that it deserves to continue?
Is there a contradiction if structural rules repeatedly change according to an external clock while history adds no increment beyond the complete current representation?
How should one accurately describe replaced components meeting a predetermined function when the original identity has been interrupted?
Does repairable directly permit the person proposing an option to execute it?
After its 2017 incident, GitLab recovered service but permanently lost some data. Can both outcomes be reported together?

caseLinks.title: GitLab 2017: service recovered, but not all data were recovered

argumentSteps: Premise: state terms have testable meaning only when tied to detectable variables, a time window, and criteria specified beforehand.

Term-by-term connection: differences in X's values support change; transitions in X under a fixed object contract support operation; K holding within the window supports persistence; changes in contract fields beyond the fluctuation window support evolution.

Identity connection: failure of the original K supports registering dissolution under that contract. A new state meeting predetermined K* or F* supports registering repair relative to that target, without requiring a return to the historical state.

Non-entailment: these definitions do not imply causes, durable memory, G3 historical increments, selection, a direction of value, or a unified subject. Each stronger claim requires separate materials and a contract.

Normative connection: moving from a target is attainable to a particular person should and may execute the action additionally requires justification of the target, affected people, and authorization for decision and execution. N/O must not be omitted.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: judging the same connection change term by term
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a mathematical network has nodes a, b, and c, initial edge set R0={ab,bc}, and K requires connectivity among the three nodes; registered state X contains the node queues. If only the queues change from (1,0,0) to (0,1,0), with the object contract unchanged and the prescribed transition rules followed, this is change and operation; because K still holds, it is also persistence. If edge ab is removed and its absence exceeds the preset tolerance window for fluctuations, the relational contract undergoes evolution. Node a is no longer connected to the others, so the original K fails and dissolution is also registered under that K. Both terms can apply simultaneously; they are not mutually exclusive.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An entirely constructed discrete network; connectivity is defined by undirected edges; ordinary operation excludes edge deletion; deletion detection and the fluctuation window are fixed in advance.
teachingExamples.boundary: Establishes classification under the given definitions, not dissolution of a real organization, the cause of a deletion, or its value.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a new connection that satisfies the function does not mean returning to the original graph
teachingExamples.text: Using the same graph, define repair target F* as “a path exists between every pair of nodes.” Adding ac after deletion gives edges {ac,bc}, with path a-c-b from a to b. F* holds and the original connectivity K holds again, but the edge set has not returned to R0. If another identity contract strictly defines K as “the edge set is exactly R0,” that K still fails. Thus describe repair that meets a predefined function, without implying restoration under every identity standard.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Target F* is given before the edge is added; the three nodes are fixed and edges undirected; no real network operation is performed.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not establish that real-world repair is feasible, its price to be paid reasonable, or anyone authorized to implement it; different K criteria must be public and cannot be silently switched afterward.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: structural change need not produce additional historical information
teachingExamples.text: Suppose edges open and close according to an external clock rule disclosed in advance: open on even steps and closed on odd steps, with the current graph and required clock position fully registered. The preset criterion recognizes this as a change in contractual relations. The rule directly determines the next graph, so adding earlier graph history supplies no further predictive information. Evolution may therefore be registered without additional historical conditional increment under this mathematical representation.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The rule is deterministic, and the clock and current graph are known without error; time steps exceed the declared fluctuation tolerance scale; the external rule is not disguised as a fact about the world.
teachingExamples.boundary: Supplies only a conditional counterexample to “evolution implies G3”; real-world current states are often incomplete, so this cannot establish that real-world history is irrelevant.

counterexamples.text: The source explicitly permits an evolution record to hold without G3 or a selection mechanism holding.
counterexamples.effect: Evolution cannot be read as another name for path dependence, natural selection, or universal progress.

counterexamples.text: Teaching counterexample: after edges change from {ab,bc} to {ac,bc}, function recovers but the historical edge set does not.
counterexamples.effect: Repair may target functional adequacy; “return to every old detail” cannot be required, nor does this erase interruption of the original identity.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: K holds throughout the window, while the registered function continually deteriorates.
counterexamples.effect: Persistence may still hold, but cannot establish health or that continuation is warranted; functional and normative evaluation must be separate.

questionAnswers.question: If a machine reading changes from 10 to 11, has evolution necessarily occurred?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. First check whether resolution and error allow a difference to be identified; even a real change may concern only X values, without a contractual field changing beyond the fluctuation window.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does an object's persisting for ten years imply that it deserves to continue?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Persistence addresses only the specified K and window; health, justification, and continuation goals also require functional, risk-related, and normative material.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Is there a contradiction if structural rules repeatedly change according to an external clock while history adds no increment beyond the complete current representation?
questionAnswers.answer: There is no contradiction. D1 evolution follows only the contract-change criterion; G3 asks separately about historical conditional increment. The teaching rule provides a case in which they are separable.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: How should one accurately describe replaced components meeting a predetermined function when the original identity has been interrupted?
questionAnswers.answer: Describe a new state meeting F* or functional repair, while also recording failure of the original K and the identity transition; do not broadly claim that everything returned to its original condition.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does repairable directly permit the person proposing an option to execute it?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The justification of the target, decision-making authority, and execution authorization require separate review; technical or definitional feasibility grants no permission.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: After its 2017 incident, GitLab recovered service but permanently lost some data. Can both outcomes be reported together?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes: report separately by function, data scope, and time window. Data loss does not make restored service a false recovery, nor can restored service substitute for the target of data completeness. Repair here follows predeclared target criteria (K* or F*); the postmortem was written afterward and cannot retroactively establish repair.
questionAnswers.basis: GitLab incident postmortem (2017-02-10); §3.2, §6.6.

openQuestions: Real-world use requires measurement definitions, the original K, fluctuation window, target K*/F*, and records of identity changes; without these materials, the applicability of particular state terms should remain unresolved.

3.3.title: 3.3 D2 Effective feedback
3.3.lead: Receiving a comment does not yet answer what it changed; a comment actually changing action does not yet answer whether that change was good or bad. Effective feedback here means “a return causes a subsequent difference”; “effective” is not praise.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 493–500; source anchor section-3-3; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “D2 does not guarantee that feedback is truthful, timely, or beneficial.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

Effective feedback has four traceable positions: a prior state or output, a return channel, a receiving position, and a subsequent field that changes. What returns may be a physical signal or information with a carrier, but connect all four: what returns from where, who or which component receives it, and which subsequent state, transition probability, timing, or constraint it changes. Drawing a circle in a diagram does not establish an actual return chain.

Registering an effect requires comparison: does the subsequent field show a detectable difference relative to no return or a blocked channel? Real research may be unable to block a channel randomly; suitable controls, natural variation, mechanism evidence, or other identification designs may be used, but alternative explanations such as common causes, simultaneous interventions, and measurement changes must be addressed. If material shows only temporal sequence, not every subsequent change can be attributed to that return.

Acknowledgments, comment books, meeting minutes, and archives may establish arrival or a recorded trace, but cannot alone establish a change in a target field. Conversely, D2 does not require a lasting trace of the effect: a fixed controller may immediately change the next input using a newly received signal. Even if it later returns to its original state without a long-term parameter change, this can constitute effective feedback within that window.

Separate “effect,” “stability,” and “target improvement.” A return causing a difference is an effect; whether disturbances decay and states remain bounded or converge requires an explicit stability concept, rules, and parameters. Whether task targets are achieved additionally requires evaluating the price to be paid, transient peaks, and the distribution of benefits and harms. False, late, or amplified signals can still have effects while worsening outcomes.

Fixed rules can produce feedback; model retraining, human learning, and parameter updates are not necessary conditions. A further learning claim requires checking the relevant update, subsequent use, and task outcomes. The carried-learning branch CM-LEARNING-carried requires a locatable update, retention or continued updating through a carrier, actual use in repeated rounds, and task-outcome comparison; lasting retention does not automatically require G3. Only the stronger CM-LEARNING-history claim—that an additional historical conditional increment remains relative to an explicit current representation—separately requires a G3-instance. When the current carrier sufficiently retains what was learned, that additional increment can disappear while carried learning still holds (6.3, Chinese source lines 1384–1401). “No learning” must not be misclassified as “no feedback effect at all.”

A correction claim must disclose the target deviation, gain, execution delay, operating range, and instability criterion. Multiplying deviation by a minus sign does not guarantee self-stabilization in a real process. The linear derivation below holds only under assumptions including the given discrete model, no delay, and no saturation; delays, nonlinearities, external disturbances, and constraints in real processes require separate examination.

distinctions.leftText: Establishes signal arrival or a recorded trace.
distinctions.rightText: The return causes a detectable difference in a subsequent field relative to no return.

distinctions.leftText: An actual effect under the present definition.
distinctions.rightText: Direction and value are evaluated separately by targets, costs, and distribution.

distinctions.leftText: Can arise under fixed rules and can be transient.
distinctions.rightText: Requires the relevant update and subsequent-use conditions; the word feedback does not establish it.

distinctions.leftText: The control direction attempts to offset current deviation.
distinctions.rightText: Requires dynamic rules, gain, delay, and operating range; it is not synonymous with a minus sign.

boundaries: No state change after one return may reflect a current equilibrium, a dead zone, saturation, inadequate observation resolution, or an actual absence of effect. Distinguish these through the material; do not infer absence of feedback capacity in every window from one zero-difference record.
Blocking a real safety channel for research may carry serious risks; blocking here is only an identification reference or mathematical construction, not authorization to implement it.
Harm caused by feedback does not negate its effect; absence of a permanent trace does not automatically negate its having changed timing or transitions.
Lack of support for one target loop in an organization does not mean feedback is absent everywhere in the organization; local success likewise cannot establish effectiveness of every channel.
The mathematical stability range applies only to the stated model. Real-world delays, saturation, and observation errors cannot be omitted while retaining the same numerical thresholds.
questions: If a system automatically acknowledges every complaint, can effective feedback be established?
Does a fixed temperature-control rule lack feedback because its parameters are not retrained?
Is the k=3 mathematical example “ineffective feedback”?
If results worsen after blocking a channel, does that automatically establish that the original feedback was effective and beneficial?
Can observing no difference once at equilibrium establish that the system has never had feedback?
The Flint audit says the Report a Violation system can close cases. Does closure mean that the drinking-water risk indicated by a tip has been eliminated?

caseNotes.title: Columbia: requests and circulation of material do not establish the adequacy of the target judgment loop
caseNotes.text: In its 2003 investigation report, CAIB lists three independently initiated requests for on-orbit imagery and records the work of the Debris Assessment Team; it also states that analytical assumptions and uncertainties were not fully presented to the Mission Evaluation Room and Mission Management Team. This section adds attention to different positions in the return chain: sending requests, forming a team, and supplying sufficient material for the target risk judgment cannot all be replaced by a single “feedback provided.”

caseNotes.title: Flint complaints: response, referral, and risk handling are different fields
caseNotes.text: An audit by the US Environmental Protection Agency's Office of Inspector General records that, from May 2014 to January 2016, EPA Region 5 received 87 resident complaints about Flint drinking water, 30 mentioning lead. Officials replied with form letters directing residents to the state environmental department or local water personnel (11 had no located response record); Region 5 also did not use complaint volume as an indicator of water-supply problems. A 2022 follow-up audit separately examined two EPA intake channels: the drinking-water hotline acquired procedures in 2019 requiring risk assessment and documentation of handling outcomes; Report a Violation (RAV) could refer tips and open or close cases but lacked these two functions. Using this section's four positions, distinguish records showing complaint arrival from records showing rule changes, then ask whether the subsequent field of interest changed because of the return.

argumentSteps: Premise: an already occurring state or output has a traceable return channel and receiving position.
Candidate effect: specify the subsequent state, transition probability, timing, or constraint changed, together with a detection threshold and time window.

Comparative connection: propose a no-return/blocked-channel reference and examine whether an attributable difference exists relative to actual return; rule out competing causes sufficient to explain the difference.
Qualified conclusion: where material sufficiently supports a difference, register a feedback effect for that field and window; acknowledgments or archives alone cannot replace this step.

Additional responsibilities: stability, correction, improvement, and learning each add their own criteria and evidence; a minus sign, good intentions, complete records, or a happy or tragic outcome cannot substitute for them.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a minus sign does not guarantee stability
teachingExamples.text: Let x_t be deviation, with system x_(t+1)=x_t+u_t; measurement is exact and returns immediately, and the fixed control rule is u_t=-k x_t. Substitution gives x_(t+1)=(1-k)x_t, and recursion gives x_t=(1-k)^t x_0. Asymptotic convergence to zero for every finite initial value requires |1-k|<1, hence 0<k<2. Take x_0=1: without return, u=0 and the sequence stays at 1; with k=0.5, it is 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125; with k=3, it is 1, -2, 4, -8. Both k values create differences relative to no return, but the latter amplifies deviation. k=2 yields 1, -1, 1, -1, a constant-amplitude oscillation that does not approach zero.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A one-dimensional discrete linear model with no disturbances, execution delay, or saturation, a fixed feedback coefficient, and exact observation; these sequences are calculations, not observed data.
teachingExamples.boundary: Establishes only effects and the range of asymptotic convergence within this model; does not establish that a real controller is safe, has positive benefits, or has learned.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: what does a one-step delay do at the same gain?
teachingExamples.text: Without delay and with k=1, the preceding equation reaches zero in one step from any x_0. Change it to x_(t+1)=x_t-x_(t-1), with x_-1=x_0=1: then x_1=0, x_2=-1, x_3=-1, x_4=0, x_5=1, x_6=1, and the sequence repeats. The gain and minus sign are unchanged, but using information one step late no longer yields the same convergence conclusion.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Only an exact one-step delay is introduced; the mathematical model still has no noise, disturbances, or saturation, and all initial values are explicit.
teachingExamples.boundary: Provides a counterexample to ignoring delay, not a universal delay threshold for real processes.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an effect without a long-term parameter change
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a controller reads only the current sensor value at each step, applies a fixed formula, and discards that reading after acting, with parameters that never change. If the return causes a detectable difference in the next state, D2's effect can still hold; “no parameter learning and no persistent log” cannot cancel that difference. At x=0 without disturbance, both actions are 0, so this comparison supplies no witness to a nonzero effect.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Designed to distinguish instantaneous effect, learning, and detection windows; does not claim that a particular device is implemented this way.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not remove the responsibility to preserve necessary evidence in real research; absence of research evidence differs from absence of long-term memory in the system itself.

counterexamples.text: Mathematical counterexample: at k=3, u=-3x contains a minus sign intended to offset deviation, yet the magnitude of x doubles at every step.
counterexamples.effect: Limits the misreading that “negative feedback necessarily stabilizes itself”; an effect, failed convergence, and movement away from the target can coexist.

counterexamples.text: Mathematical boundary: a fixed formula immediately changes the next state, after which neither the reading is retained nor parameters changed.
counterexamples.effect: D2 requires neither lasting traces nor learning; evidence must still trace this particular return effect.

counterexamples.text: CAIB recorded both the Debris Assessment Team and imagery requests, as well as the failure to present key analytical assumptions and uncertainties fully to the relevant management meetings.
counterexamples.effect: Requests, teams, and meetings do not suffice to establish adequacy of the required risk-judgment loop; conversely, this does not establish that every return within NASA had no effect.

questionAnswers.question: If a system automatically acknowledges every complaint, can effective feedback be established?
questionAnswers.answer: Only generation of an acknowledgment field is established; it does not establish that the complaint changed the subsequent service or rule of interest. Specify the target field, return chain, and no-return reference, avoiding substitution of acknowledgment for the target effect.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does a fixed temperature-control rule lack feedback because its parameters are not retrained?
questionAnswers.answer: No. If a returned reading changes subsequent action or state, a fixed rule can satisfy D2; learning has another set of conditions.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Is the k=3 mathematical example “ineffective feedback”?
questionAnswers.answer: Under D2, it is not without effect: relative to no return, it changes the state, but amplifies the deviation and fails the model's conditions for asymptotic convergence. If everyday ‘ineffective’ means failing to achieve a target, explicitly identify that different evaluation.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If results worsen after blocking a channel, does that automatically establish that the original feedback was effective and beneficial?
questionAnswers.answer: It remains necessary to establish whether blocking also changed other channels or the environment, whether the comparison is credible, and the limits of the outcomes and distribution of costs; a confounded comparison must not become unconditional attribution.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can observing no difference once at equilibrium establish that the system has never had feedback?
questionAnswers.answer: No. That window merely failed to provide a detectable witness of an effect. Equilibrium, dead zones, saturation, resolution, and other conditions must be considered before judging effects in other windows or under perturbations.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: The Flint audit says the Report a Violation system can close cases. Does closure mean that the drinking-water risk indicated by a tip has been eliminated?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Closure is a case-management status; the audit also notes that the system lacked functions for assessing tip-related risk and tracking handling outcomes, so closure records alone do not show whether a problem was resolved. Conversely, this functional gap does not establish that everyone taking up a tip failed to act. Answering that question requires checking who took up the specific tip, what actions they took, and the outcome.
questionAnswers.basis: EPA OIG report 22-P-0046, printed page 16; source §3.3.

3.4.title: 3.4 D3 Scale Transformation
3.4.lead: Combining two devices into a total may suffice to report the total but not to identify which is overloaded; adding the maximum may still not identify which device to adjust. A scale transformation must be assessed against the specific question you intend to answer or operation you intend to perform.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 501–514; source anchor section-3-4; short quotation: ‘Static answers, dynamic progression, intervention responses, and feasible actions are judged separately’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

D3 requires registering M(SP0→SP1)=〈保留变量、改变变量、丢失变量、转换算子、误差、适用区间〉 (retained variables, changed variables, lost variables, conversion operator, error, and applicable interval). Source and target SP must first be explicit to specify ‘from where to where’. What is retained, changed, or lost is not a trio of slogans: identify the actual variables, units, relations, identities, and computations, and state when error would exceed the acceptable range.

Scale changes may occur along aggregation, time, space, observational resolution, and other axes; expansion on one axis cannot substitute for the others, particularly jurisdiction and authorization. Each M checks whether object K is preserved. If the result is a different object, record the identity conversion rather than conceal the change by retaining the same name.

The same term appearing at two levels does not supply a mapping. ‘Individual adaptation’ and ‘organizational adaptation’ are only two labels; without bridges for variables, relations, and tasks, they can only be described alongside each other. Aggregate statistics also cannot be assigned as attributes to every member: the same overall mean can conceal enormous internal differences.

Sufficiency involves at least four separate checks. First, can the target representation answer the current static query? Second, is there an update rule depending only on the current target representation that correctly advances it one step? Third, can that representation still evaluate responses after admissible interventions? Fourth, can the current information select an action that qualifies for every compatible state, is actually implementable, and is authorized? Answering one question does not mean being able to advance dynamics, evaluate actions, or act.

The formal mathematical connections are F1–F3 in 4.18: static tasks require merged states to give the same answer; dynamic and intervention closure require two source states initially sharing a representation to continue sharing the same target representation after updating under the same fixed dynamics or admissible intervention—not that the values before and after updating remain unchanged; a common feasible action requires an intersection of the eligible-action sets for all compatible states. These are formal results under assumptions, not a conversion of teaching calculations into real equipment evidence. Actual transfer still requires materials about measurement, mappings, environments, horizons, and errors.

Section 3.4.1 asks further: through which converter and rules is an expression rewritten for whom, and which meanings are compressed or added? This is representational recasting with source lineage and target-side review. It may include the scale transformation of this section, but a summation operator alone must not be presented as a completed explanatory contract for the target audience.

distinctions.leftText: The same name is retained at different levels.
distinctions.rightText: Supplies source/target, operator, losses, error, and task bridges.

distinctions.leftText: The current representation suffices to recover the specified q.
distinctions.rightText: Also requires computing the subsequent representation from the current representation alone.

distinctions.leftText: Distinguishes relevant outcomes after the specified operation.
distinctions.rightText: Additionally requires an intersection of eligible actions, real resources and capabilities, and permissions.

distinctions.leftText: May be entirely accurate for one statistical task.
distinctions.rightText: Positions, extremes, and heterogeneity may already have been lost.

boundaries: Zero error is meaningful only relative to an explicit target; an exact total does not imply exact local states or decisions.
Switching to an easier task may be a valid new question, but must not be used to declare the original, harder target complete.
A mapping may be computable while its inputs cannot be obtained in time, or predictive while action remains unauthorized; information, timeliness, and permissions require separate review.
Lack of an empirical bridge does not mean the objects at two levels were never related; it limits the transfer success that may currently be claimed.
Many local average responses must not simply be multiplied into an overall intervention; variables, joint distributions, couplings, and shared resources require separate checking.
questions: Why can an overload still be missed when total error is 0?
Why does knowing a total of 10 and a maximum of 9 still not determine whether node 1 or 2 should be treated?
What does it establish formally if both totals are 10 but become 5.5 and 9.5 on the next step?
Does another level's use of the word ‘feedback’ establish successful transfer of a feedback law?

caseLinks.title: Real-world case: which question did Hurricane Ian's forecast cone answer?

argumentSteps: Premise: specify the source-state domain, source/target SP, K, and task family, together with the horizon, environment, and admissible actions.
Register M: state the operator, retained/changed/lost variables, unit relations, error, and applicable interval, preserving a source representation that can be checked again.
Static test: find two source states mapped to the same target representation and check whether they still give the same answer for the target being asked about.
Dynamics and intervention tests: separately compare those states' target representations after fixed dynamics and each admissible action; passing the static test does not replace these checks.
Action test: even if each actual state has a solution, check whether a common eligible action exists across the set of unknown states, along with resources and valid permissions.

Conclusion: claim transfer sufficiency only within the tested tasks, horizons, environments, actions, and error ranges; if bridging materials are insufficient, retain parallel descriptions at the two scales.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: what a total mapping can do
teachingExamples.text: Let the source state x=(x1,x2) be nonnegative loads at two nodes, with K fixing the node set {1,2}. Source SP retains separate values for two identified nodes; target SP takes the whole on the aggregation axis and retains only the total in resolution. The time window is unchanged, and no expansion of causation or authorization is claimed. Define π(x)=x1+x2. M retains total load, changes the unit of expression to a whole-system value, loses allocation and position, and uses summation of quantities with the same unit. With exact inputs, total error is 0; the applicable domain is limited to these two comparably defined nonnegative quantities and the current window. For the total target q, recovery is simply q=π; for ‘does any node have load >8?’, (9,1) and (5,5) both map to 10 but yield true and false respectively, so π is insufficient.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All are mathematical assumptions, with identical units and no measurement error; unspecified SP axes are not expanded on this basis, and the model includes no real-world authorization to act.
teachingExamples.boundary: The exact conclusion for the total task does not establish any actual aggregation, measurement, or safety judgment.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: adding the maximum still does not preserve position and action
teachingExamples.text: Switch to π′(x)=(x1+x2,max(x1,x2)), which suffices to answer whether any node exceeds 8. However, x=(9,1) and x′=(1,9) are both represented by (10,9). The only admissible actions are a1 or a2: remove at most 3 units from the corresponding node, replacing its value with max(0,xi-3) while leaving the other unchanged. Action a1 gives (6,1) for x and (0,9) for x′, with different answers about remaining overload. If eligibility means both nodes are ≤8 after one step, A_ok(x)={a1} and A_ok(x′)={a2}, whose intersection is empty. Without knowing the position, the existence of a solution for each state still does not permit selecting one uniformly eligible action.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Only one node may be selected once; both cannot be acted on simultaneously. Actions are defined throughout the domain; eligibility concerns only this mathematical target, not real-world permissions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Establishes insufficiency of the current summary for directed responses and common actions, not that every detail must be identified before real-world action is possible.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: even fixed dynamics may fail to close
teachingExamples.text: Separately specify non-intervention dynamics F(x1,x2)=(x1/2,x2). At (9,1) and (1,9), the totals are both 10, but after updating they are 5.5 and 9.5 respectively. An update function F̄ using only the total would therefore require F̄(10) to equal two different values simultaneously, a contradiction. Thus the total answers the current total query but cannot independently advance these dynamics. Together with the previous example, this counterexample shows why each rule must be tested separately.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Halving acts only on identified node 1; the rule is fixed, there are no other inputs, and values are exact.
teachingExamples.boundary: Refutes automatic closure only, not closure of every macro-level aggregate; closure may hold under different dynamics or a sufficiently enriched representation.

counterexamples.text: The source states that a total may answer a total query exactly while omitting local overload; adding the maximum may still omit positional identity needed for directed operations.
counterexamples.effect: Information preservation must be tied to the task; saying ‘the main information is retained’ does not bypass separate static, dynamic, and operational checks.

counterexamples.text: Mathematical counterexample: with the same (total,maximum)=(10,9), an action on node 1 produces different overload outcomes under two allocations.
counterexamples.effect: Sufficiency for a static warning does not imply evaluability of a directed action, still less the availability of a common eligible action under current information.

questionAnswers.question: Why can an overload still be missed when total error is 0?
questionAnswers.answer: The total task considers only the sum; (9,1) and (5,5) have the same sum but different answers to the local >8 query. Losing allocation leaves the total unchanged but changes the warning target.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why does knowing a total of 10 and a maximum of 9 still not determine whether node 1 or 2 should be treated?
questionAnswers.answer: Positional identity has been lost. Both (9,1) and (1,9) fit the summary; the only eligible one-step actions removing at most 3 units are a1 and a2 respectively, with no common action.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What does it establish formally if both totals are 10 but become 5.5 and 9.5 on the next step?
questionAnswers.answer: No single-valued total update F̄(10) is correct for both source states. This is failure of closure under the specified F, not inevitable failure of all aggregation.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does another level's use of the word ‘feedback’ establish successful transfer of a feedback law?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Supply the scale mapping, correspondence of objects and return channels, target window, and error; without a bridge, only parallel descriptions are warranted.

3.4.1.title: 3.4.1 Representational and Discursive Recasting
3.4.1.lead: Explaining technical material to another group involves more than shortening it. State who rewrites it under which rules, which qualifications remain, what has been lost, and whether recipients independently checked it.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 515–522; source anchor section-3-4-1; short quotation: ‘The new representation must retain its parent record and source lineage’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

Representational recasting rewrites a sourced state, information, or model, through a named converter, bridging party, or rule, into a new representation for a target scale, circle, task, or vocabulary system. When the payload is mainly language, institutional texts, or explanation, it is discursive recasting. ‘Recasting’ here does not permit arbitrary changes of meaning; it requires clarity about responsibility for changes in expression.

Parent records and source lineage must be preserved. Readers should be able to return to the original materials to check context, versions, units, conditions, and edits or omissions. Multiple summaries from the same parent record must not be counted as multiple independent sources. Traceability also does not establish accurate rewriting; it merely makes accuracy review possible.

The minimum record can be understood in four groups. Input: source formulation, context, parent record, and route back to the source. Transformation: transformer or rule and version, preserved elements, permitted changes, collapsed distinctions, omissions, added interpretations, ambiguities, and errors. Reception: target circle, target task, and independent review. Life cycle: validity period, failure conditions, and withdrawal conditions. Missing any key item can cause ‘concise’ to be mistaken for ‘complete in meaning’.

Scale transformation adjusts SP and representational sufficiency; circle-relation transformation handles relations between circles; network propagation describes the nodes and edges traversed; compression reduces expression or data volume; lateral analogy attempts correspondences between different objects. These can participate in recasting, but none replaces the contract for sources, rewriting, and target-side review above. Forwarding unchanged may involve propagation without recasting; an explanation adapted to another task at the same scale may involve recasting.

Whether recipients actually understand or change their actions requires material from specified channels, not the rewriter’s self-assessment. Without independent target-side review, record only recasting awaiting testing. Review may compare answers and omissions for the same task, but this guide recruited no actual readers and performed no such measurement, so it cannot claim that readability has been validated.

If collapsed distinctions still change target answers, judgments of historical conditions, or operational results, return to the existing scale-closure and conditional-increment contracts; if different rewriting orders produce different results, check them against the same endpoint task, rather than introducing a new principle exempt from proof. F4 in 4.18.4 specifically reminds us that each stage achieving its local objective does not ensure that their composition preserves the same final objective.

distinctions.leftText: Information moves along channels and may even be copied unchanged.
distinctions.rightText: Rewriting expression for a target task, requiring rewriting rules and independent review.

distinctions.leftText: Reduces length or volume and may lose distinctions.
distinctions.rightText: Whether the required questions can still be answered; shorter or smoother wording does not guarantee this.

distinctions.leftText: Records SP, variables, operators, and loss.
distinctions.rightText: Also involves source lineage, interpretive additions and deletions, and target comprehension tasks.

distinctions.leftText: Parent material and versions can be checked.
distinctions.rightText: Still requires preserved elements and independent target-side checks; a link does not make it correct.

distinctions.leftText: A design judgment proposed by the rewriter.
distinctions.rightTitle: Actual change in understanding or action
distinctions.rightText: Requires actual reader or channel evidence; this guide has not implemented it.

boundaries: Changing ‘the model applies within the measured range’ to ‘the result is safe’ adds a conclusion the original did not warrant; this is a substantive semantic overreach, not ordinary simplification.

One cannot retain only sources supporting favorable conclusions while deleting uncertainty, applicability ranges, or failure conditions; the existence of a parent record cannot compensate for misleading body text.
Independent target-side review also has a defined scope; a single review cannot be generalized to every audience, language, task, and future version.
Order effects must hold the same final objective, units, and error standard constant; different answers to two different tasks cannot masquerade as a finding of noncommutativity.

Communication barriers in an actual case do not prove that one document format necessarily causes accidents; technical tools, organizational processes, and other causes cannot be replaced by a single formatting story.

caseNotes.title: CAIB’s examination of a damage-analysis briefing: preserve both the conclusion and what it refers to
caseNotes.text: On p. 191 of Volume I, the 2003 CAIB report examines a briefing used by the Debris Assessment Team. It observes that ‘conservative’ in the heading referred to the choice of test model, not the extent of predicted damage; the important qualification that the situation exceeded the test database appeared at the bottom. This section adds the question of how recasting affects the prominence of qualifying information: a heading cannot simply be carried over while losing its referent and applicability range.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: CAIB Volume I, Chapter 7, p. 191
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Volume I, Chapter 7, printed p. 191, first four body paragraphs of ‘Engineering by Viewgraphs’
caseNotes.boundary: The citation is to the investigation report’s analysis of an actual briefing; this guide has not repeated an audience experiment. Communication problems are not treated as the sole cause of the accident, and the demonstration rewrite is not claimed to have been validated by real readers.

argumentSteps: Premise: a locatable source representation and its context exist, and the target audience and task are explicit.
Transformation record: disclose the named transformer or rule version, permitted changes, and actual additions and deletions; preserve the parent record and route back to the source.
Semantic check: examine preserved elements, ambiguity, omissions, added interpretations, and errors; conditions in the original material must not be silently upgraded into unconditional conclusions.

Target review: the target side independently checks the answers required for its task; without this material, record the recasting as awaiting testing rather than substituting internal self-assessment.
Connection to results: a further claim of changed understanding or action requires actual channels and comparative evidence; source traceability does not automatically establish an effect.

Connection to withdrawal: recheck when changes in context, version, task, or material exceed the validity period; suspend or withdraw under the predetermined conditions if key conditions are lost or source return fails.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a complete record of rewriting a technical record as a management prompt
teachingExamples.text: Let parent record P1 specify current two-node loads (9,1), common units, and a threshold >8: a mathematical setup without actual measurement. The target reader is a dispatcher in a model exercise, and the task asks only whether an overload exists. The transformer is defined as ‘example rule v1’: use the total and maximum to write ‘There is currently a local overload; total 10, maximum 9; location has not been retained, so this cannot support targeted action.’ Preserved elements are the total, extreme value, threshold, and model status; the permitted change is the form of expression; node identities are collapsed; the full distribution is omitted; the operational restriction is an added interpretation; ‘current’ has an ambiguous window; error for this alert task is 0. The parent record is P1 in this paragraph, and returning to P1 permits recalculation; a change in time or load invalidates it. The target side has not yet independently reviewed it, so the example provides only a proposed recasting awaiting testing; if used to locate a target for action, its sufficiency claim should be withdrawn.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All fields belong to a teaching proposal; the parent record is this example’s setup, not a real archive, and no actual dispatcher participated.
teachingExamples.boundary: This shows how to record responsibilities; it does not establish that real audiences understand correctly or certify any system alert.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: premature rounding loses distinctions for the same final target
teachingExamples.text: Let r round to the nearest integer, with exact halves rounded upward. The source values are 0.49 and 0.50, and the final target is q=r(the mean of the two values). Averaging first gives 0.495, then rounding gives 0. Rounding each value first gives 0 and 1; averaging then gives 0.5, and rounding under the same rule gives 1. Both procedures ultimately output an integer, but the second fails to preserve the predetermined q. Each local step may look reasonable, yet the composition must still be checked for preservation of the common target.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Values are treated as exact decimal rational numbers; r(0.5)=1; the final target is fixed as rounding after averaging the original values.
teachingExamples.boundary: This is a formal counterexample in which premature compression changes the task, not a real-world rate of linguistic misunderstanding; it does not prove that all rewriting orders fail to commute.

counterexamples.text: Teaching counterexample: two summaries derived from the same parent record are counted as two independent supports.
counterexamples.effect: Recasting adds expression nodes, not independent factual sources; lineage should prevent double counting.

counterexamples.text: CAIB’s examination of the damage-analysis briefing notes that ‘conservative’ in the heading concerns model selection, not a guarantee about predicted damage; the crucial information that the situation exceeded the test database was at the bottom.
counterexamples.effect: The actual material shows that hierarchy and omission in presentation can change the qualifications available to readers; it does not justify attributing the accident to one slide alone.

counterexamples.text: Mathematical counterexample: after 0.49 and 0.50 are individually rounded prematurely, the final integer changes from the target value 0 to 1.
counterexamples.effect: A composition must be assessed against the same endpoint task; each step completing a different local job does not guarantee preservation by the whole.

questionAnswers.question: Is forwarding the same file unchanged to another department necessarily recasting?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. It is at least propagation; without rewriting expression for the target task, a change of recipient alone does not establish fulfillment of the recasting contract.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Is a summary accurate merely because it includes a link to the original?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Context, version, preserved elements, omissions, added interpretations, and the target task must also be checked; a link only provides a route back.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: The rewriter finds the text fluent, but the target side has not reviewed it; how should it be recorded?
questionAnswers.answer: Recasting awaiting testing. A design and expectations may be supplied, but effects on understanding or action cannot be claimed as established.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why must q be fixed first in the rounding example?
questionAnswers.answer: Otherwise, the two procedures may simply perform different tasks, and different answers do not show which one failed. Fixing q makes it possible to identify the distinction lost by the second procedure that was needed for the common endpoint.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can a briefing that downplays risk information establish that ‘slide format necessarily causes accidents’?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The case supports a problem with qualifying information in a specific expression; tool format, transmission chain, decisions, and accident causation still require separate checks.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

3.5.title: 3.5 Eleven Universal Structural Primitives
3.5.lead: This heading opens eleven distinct question cards: how an object is registered, where its boundaries lie, what is observed, what implements it, and how change, return, and history enter an explanation. The cards connect, but none can answer for another.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 523–524; source anchor section-3-5; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘Eleven universal structural primitives’. See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

Chinese source lines 523–524 contain only the parent heading, with no additional proposition or proof. This unit explains the reading entry point; the actual definitions are in 3.5.1 through 3.5.11, each explained independently below. This navigation does not replace the eleven sections themselves.

Following this part’s introduction and the account of composition in 3.6, U01–U03 concern candidate objects and observation; U04–U06 concern implementation locations, relations, and transmission; U07–U10 concern return, environment, load, and history; U11 concerns the operating ranges of the same object and loss of identity. This grouping assists reading; it is not a universal sequence of life stages from the first group to the fourth.

Here, ‘primitives’ are positions that explanation needs to distinguish. This does not mean that all eleven are indivisible physical entities, nor does it claim uniqueness, independence, or completeness. A sufficient subset may be selected for a task, with the effects of omissions explained; fields that are inapplicable, unknown, unobservable, or protectively undisclosed must be distinguished explicitly, not automatically filled in.

distinctions.leftText: Tells readers which questions are asked next.
distinctions.rightText: Supports particular object, channel, or historical claims; it cannot be obtained by counting contents entries covered.

distinctions.leftText: Different positions may supply inputs to each other.
distinctions.rightText: Inferring the others’ existence from one’s existence is not permitted by the original text.

boundaries: Do not use ‘more primitives employed’ as a score for a more advanced object, a more correct explanation, or a more justified action.
This heading contains no separate empirical proposition; no historical story is invented to prove the elevenfold classification.
questions: Once the parent heading is understood, can the eleven sections be skipped?
If a task uses only some primitives, how can arbitrary omission be avoided?
argumentSteps: Textual premise: this parent section contains only a heading; definitions must be read in the subordinate H3 sections. The guide writer’s additions cannot be treated as original text from the parent section.
Reading connection: first distinguish the responsibility of each question card, then return to the particular task and select the necessary interfaces.
Limit on conclusions: listing eleven names does not prove that any real object satisfies them, or that they are mutually independent or exhaust the world.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: choose cards by question first
teachingExamples.text: Suppose the current task merely describes a registered configuration at a particular moment. Checking the object, boundaries, and observation can support a description. If the next claim is that the object has learned a rule, material on return, retention, invocation, and task results is required; the static checklist cannot be reused to declare successful learning.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Only the responsibilities of two invented tasks are compared; there is no real object or experiment.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not claim that any task invariably needs only the first three items; specific omissions still require review.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary case: a table fills all eleven columns with ‘present’ and immediately declares the model complete and the organization mature.
counterexamples.effect: Filling fields is not validation, and the number of primitives is not a scale of stages or value.

questionAnswers.question: Once the parent heading is understood, can the eleven sections be skipped?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The parent heading is only a reading entry point; each section distinguishes different evidentiary responsibilities and conditions of inapplicability.

questionAnswers.question: If a task uses only some primitives, how can arbitrary omission be avoided?
questionAnswers.answer: State the target and required inputs, and explain item by item why an omission does not affect that conclusion, or leave unresolved the part that cannot consequently be answered.

3.5.1.title: 3.5.1 U01 Candidate object interface
3.5.1.lead: First give what you want to study a traceable identity and state clearly “what I mean.” Short duration, blurred boundaries, or the absence of a single center are all compatible with proposing a candidate, but these forms do not themselves guarantee usefulness.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 525–528; original anchor section-3-5-1. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Completing U01 does not guarantee in advance that G1 holds.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

U01 invokes D0's seven fields and adds an object-instance ID so that subsequent material, versions, and tests can refer to the same candidate. B, X, R, I, T, SP, and K must all be registered. Completeness means no silent gaps, not forcibly converting unknowns into knowns. Explain separately how unknown fields limit the question. Scale traceability means source, target, and identity remain traceable after changes in representation or scale.

Soft boundaries may be expressed through membership rules, probabilities, or thresholds, with sensitivity stated. Short-lived objects require short windows and identity criteria. Multicentered and distributed objects require actual connections and interfaces to be registered, not a supreme coordinator invented afterward. They are neither excluded for failing to resemble rigid entities nor automatically valid because they sound open or advanced.

Create a root-instance contract when entering a specific empirical judgment. Freeze N0 in the G-instance rather than inserting it into the object vector. A claim to G1 grouping gain requires the corresponding comparison. Completion of U01 permits only candidate proposals and questions for testing. Reliable domain records can still support their own facts about the object, but the interface cannot directly generate a unified will, value, responsibility, or authority to act.

U01 does not apply to a purely metaphysical object that refuses declaration of any empirical fields. “Not applicable” limits only the use of this empirical interface; it does not adjudicate the object's existence, philosophical meaning, or value.

U01 makes object candidates locatable and versionable; G1 tests grouping gain relative to a matched N0. If a school's identity and relations have reliable records, failure of that school grouping to improve a particular achievement prediction narrows only the grouping claim for that task. It cannot erase the school, students, or affected people.

distinctions.leftText: Distinguishes and enables reference back to a candidate.
distinctions.rightText: An ID only identifies; material is still required.

distinctions.leftText: Membership may vary gradually or be uncertain under explicit rules.
distinctions.rightText: Changes with results without rules, making it uncheckable.

distinctions.leftText: Permits distributed relations to be proposed.
distinctions.rightText: A stronger claim concerning a human subject, not inferred from form.

boundaries: The same ID must not silently refer to an object whose boundary, scale, or K has changed. Record versions and identity transformations.
When boundary sensitivity is insufficiently established, the candidate may be retained while comparison conclusions are limited. Do not manufacture observations for formal completeness.
questions: Does the absence of an overall responsible person make U01 unusable for a distributed object?
What does “not applicable” mean when a purely metaphysical question refuses observable fields?
argumentSteps: Provide an instance ID and seven fields so that each record and subsequent question has a definite referent.
Explain the boundary form, time, and cross-scale tracing method, and disclose how unknowns narrow claims.
For empirical comparison, create a separate specific root instance and N0. Completed registration does not establish G1 or other strong conclusions.
If the object refuses empirical fields, state that U01 is not applicable. Do not miswrite an interface's inapplicability as philosophical negation.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: short-lived queue candidate Q1
teachingExamples.text: Let Q1 be a virtual queue appearing within five steps. B includes the queue and service node; X is integer length at each step; R specifies exactly 1 item served per step when nonempty; I is external arrivals; T is steps 0 through 5; SP registers applicable axes such as discrete time, single-queue aggregation, and integer resolution, with reasons for nonapplicability on axes lacking spatial/organizational/authorization semantics; K is the fixed queue identifier and service rule. Stopping observation at step 5 does not mean an actual object has permanently dissolved: the short window belongs only to this contract.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All fields are mathematical assumptions. SP axes not expanded here must still be registered individually in a full application; difficult fields cannot be deleted.
teachingExamples.boundary: Illustrates how U01 admits a short-lived object, not G1 gain for this grouping or actual service efficiency.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: after Q1 receives a unique ID, the author writes “it now has a unified goal and responsibility.”
counterexamples.effect: Identification and seven fields only declare a candidate; they provide no argument for goals, responsibility, or authorization.

questionAnswers.question: Does the absence of an overall responsible person make U01 unusable for a distributed object?
questionAnswers.answer: It may be proposed, but nodes, relations, and interfaces must be registered from actual material without inventing a center. Effectiveness and responsibility remain separate judgments.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What does “not applicable” mean when a purely metaphysical question refuses observable fields?
questionAnswers.answer: It means only that this empirical interface, U01, does not fit; it does not establish that the question is meaningless or the object nonexistent.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

3.5.2.title: 3.5.2 U02 Boundaries and interfaces
3.5.2.lead: Drawing a boundary states what is included this time; describing an interface states how things cross it. Boundaries may leak, move, or overlap. An interface may only receive, without being under your control.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 529–532; original anchor section-3-5-2. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “The existence of an interface still less implies that any party has control.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

Boundaries distinguish inside from outside; interfaces describe cross-boundary processes. Record what is exchanged, its constraints, and direction. Merely drawing a circle does not establish closure. Filtering, delays, conversion, or blockage may occur at interfaces; their existence and magnitude still require records or tests.

A permeable boundary remains a boundary: inside and outside can be distinguished while exchanges occur. Moving boundaries require timestamps; nested boundaries require identifying the level at which inside and outside are distinguished; overlapping objects allow the same unit to belong to both. Spatial proximity does not automatically make one object, while long-distance connections may cross residential or administrative boundaries.

Cross-scale transformations must preserve the provenance of original inside/outside distinctions and channels. After aggregation, an interface crossing small units may become an internal relation in the larger object, while a former external environment may be included in the object. Record this reorganization rather than declaring that the interface mysteriously disappeared.

An interface is not a certificate of control. Receiving signals, carrying transmission, being affected, having the technical ability to close a channel, and having authority to close it are different things. U02 is inapplicable if no inside/outside distinction can be declared. If a distinction exists but material is insufficient, that is unknown, a different status.

distinctions.leftText: The division between the current object's inside and outside.
distinctions.rightText: The stronger condition that relevant cross-boundary exchanges are absent.

distinctions.leftText: Locations are close.
distinctions.rightText: Depends on membership rules for the object and task.

distinctions.leftText: A cross-boundary location exists or can be described.
distinctions.rightText: Technical controllability and valid authorization must be separately established.

boundaries: A boundary change may change the analytical representation or the object itself. Check K rather than treating every change as actual dissolution.
Overlap does not imply a shared will among all participants, and cross-boundary exchange does not mean all states are shared.
questions: If a boundary permits input, does that make it invalid?
If two sets intersect, does that establish their identity or communication among all their members?
Does the ability to observe an interface mean it can be closed?

caseLinks.title: Snow's record of water obtained across residential boundaries

caseNotes.title: Snow's record of water obtained across residential boundaries
caseNotes.text: On p.44 of the 1855 second edition, Snow describes a woman living in Hampstead who had not visited Broad Street for months and obtained bottled pump water delivered by a daily cart. This section's new observation is the actual connection beyond a residential boundary: when studying an exposure network, residential distance cannot substitute for an input interface.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: John Snow 1855，p.44
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed p.44, paragraph about the Hampstead woman introduced through Dr. Fraser
caseNotes.boundary: This is Snow's account linking family reports with death records. The lesson does not treat a single case as complete causal identification, infer modern medical advice, or conclude that anyone controlled the entire water network.

argumentSteps: First distinguish inside and outside under the current B and T; distance or names cannot replace membership rules.
Trace the items crossing each interface and any filtering, delay, or conversion. Claims of actual effects require corresponding material.
Redraw boundaries after scale conversion while retaining mappings to source-side inside/outside distinctions and channels.
The conclusion concerns only boundaries and exchange. Control capability and authorization require separate proof.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: overlapping boundaries do not make one large subject
teachingExamples.text: Let candidate A have members {1,2} and candidate B have members {2,3}, with intersection {2}. They may exchange registered information at 2, but a nonempty intersection implies neither A=B nor a direct channel between 1 and 3. If aggregated into {1,2,3}, the former cross-A/B process may become internal, but its original route through 2 must remain traceable.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The finite sets and relations are entirely teaching assumptions, without actual members or authority.
teachingExamples.boundary: Demonstrates only overlap and tracing, not any actual community or subject.

counterexamples.text: Snow records that a woman living in Hampstead, long absent from Broad Street, obtained that pump's water through a daily delivery cart.
counterexamples.effect: Defining water-access connections solely by residential proximity misses cross-boundary interfaces. Distance from a spatial center cannot be equated with absence of relevant connection.

questionAnswers.question: If a boundary permits input, does that make it invalid?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A boundary distinguishes inside and outside; permeability is recorded separately through interfaces. Absence of the corresponding exchanges must be checked only when closure is claimed.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If two sets intersect, does that establish their identity or communication among all their members?
questionAnswers.answer: No. In the example A≠B, and no direct 1–3 edge is given. Overlap must be interpreted through specific members and channels.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does the ability to observe an interface mean it can be closed?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Observation, technical control capability, and authority to close are different fields.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

3.5.3.title: 3.5.3 U03 States and observables
3.5.3.lead: A state is the configuration you want to describe; an observation is the record it leaves through a measurement process. Instruments, questionnaires, logs, and maps each make only some things visible and may also write their own biases into the record.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 533–536; original anchor section-3-5-3. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Unobserved does not mean nonexistent.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

U03 restricts state to a registered configuration at a given T and resolution, not the object's entire actual state. Observables are records obtained through measurement channels, requiring positions, times, definitions, and errors. An observable may directly correspond to a state variable, or be only a proxy or mixture.

An absent record has several possibilities: the process did not occur, occurred outside coverage, occurred but was filtered, or its record was lost. Retain unknown status when material is insufficient; an empty cell is not zero. A record's existence also does not mean that the object caused its entire value: instrument bias, question wording, or sampling time may contribute.

Scale changes can alter distinguishable states and observables. Compressing second-level records into daily averages may satisfy an averaging task while losing peaks. Changing variable definitions may make identically named columns incomparable. Definitions, measurement positions, and errors must travel with the mapping; otherwise actual state change cannot be distinguished from changed measurement.

This section does not assume that every study must endlessly add perspectives. Additional measurement depends on the target, error, risk, and task-relevant blind spots. If existing data suffice for a bounded question, retain that conclusion without claiming to have observed every state.

distinctions.leftText: The configuration selected in the representation.
distinctions.rightText: Cannot automatically be exhausted by finite fields.

distinctions.leftText: A zero value measured under a known protocol.
distinctions.rightText: No corresponding record; cannot substitute for zero.

distinctions.leftText: Visible values differ.
distinctions.rightText: Changes in protocol, bias, or coverage must still be examined.

boundaries: A contribution from measurement does not make every datum distorted and useless. Quantify or bound its effect on the current task.
Do not exceed authority to collect sensitive material in pursuit of omniscience. Something can be both invisible and inappropriate to obtain.
