questionAnswers.question: If the interfaces suffice for the current descriptive task, may macro-level dynamic closure be claimed?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Dynamic closure requires that states sharing a representation still share a representation after the specified update, checked separately under D3/F2.

questionAnswers.question: Should a key gap automatically trigger collection of as much data as possible?
questionAnswers.answer: No. First assess necessity, risks, permissions, and low-risk alternatives; if the gap cannot safely be filled, narrow the use or remain unresolved.

intro-04-part.title: Part 4 Empirical Questions, Outcome Contracts, and Conditional Formal Propositions
intro-04-part.lead: This part separates three things: questions about the world, evidential support for answers, and proofs within given models.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 579–584, original heading ‘Part 4 Empirical Questions, Outcome Contracts, and Conditional Formal Propositions’. This is an independent part introduction; the original task had no separate website route, but it can be assembled as intro-04-part before §4.1. Short quotation: ‘The question families are not themselves laws about all objects’ (translated from Chinese, line 581). The introduction continues the roles, objects, and terminology of Parts 1–3 and specifies how to read this part; it does not announce affirmative answers to all four question types in advance. [T-intro]

The four G questions can first be distinguished in ordinary language: whether grouping objects in a particular way is more useful than an appropriate comparison; whether a specified channel has an identifiable effect on a target change; whether historical information adds to the answer beyond the specified current representation; and for which tasks, changes, and interventions the current representation remains sufficient. These are four distinct directions of testing, not facts simultaneously answered by ‘everything has structure’. [T-intro；T-G]

A G-instance contains two kinds of content. The factual assertion under test states what difference occurs for which objects, conditions, and windows; evidential rules specify which study designs and outcomes count as support. An effect's existence does not depend on researchers completing registration, but whether support may reasonably be claimed is constrained by materials and methods. ‘Not yet tested’ must not become ‘absent in reality’, nor ‘design completed’ become ‘effect established’. [T-intro；T-roles]

G, C, and F have different responsibilities. G instances carry specific empirical tests; C contracts restrict permissible outputs from existing results plus necessary conditions; F propositions provide provable relations in explicit mathematical models. An F proof may expose an invalid unconditional inference without automatically validating real-world variable mappings; a G result does not automatically satisfy every additional condition of the relevant C, still less generate norms or permission to execute. [T-intro；T-roles；T-CF]

Repeated registration of the same result does not create independent evidence. Writing ten reports from the same data, or having multiple models reprocess the same input, may add analytical perspectives but is not ten new independent observations. If these analyses produce new inferential results, retain them according to their arguments; state where the contribution comes from instead of using quantity to impersonate stronger support. [T-intro；T-material]

The introduction also separates instance support from whether the framework as a whole is worth using. Even if several specific tests pass, this does not automatically establish that the framework is more accurate, easier to understand, or less costly than adequate specialist methods. That requires separately specified tasks, comparators, protections, and evaluation. Readers should ask separately ‘What evidence supports this factual claim?’, ‘How do these grounds permit its use?’, and ‘What are the premises of this formal conclusion?’, rather than accumulating passes into an overall score. [T-intro; T-eval]

The strongest objection is whether separating responsibilities fragments knowledge that was connected. Separation makes clear what the next step still needs when work is connected; it does not require researchers to do only one kind of work. A study can include model proofs, real-world measurements, and action recommendations, but each claim must still hold on its own grounds and within its own boundaries. [T-roles]
argumentSteps: Premise: empirical truth, current evidentiary support, and logical validity within a model have different conditions.
Inferential connection: putting them into a single pass flag conflates untested, unidentified, proved, and other distinct states.
Conclusion: G asks about specific facts, C manages bounded use and combination, and F checks proofs within models; connecting them requires adding each one’s conditions.
Evidentiary responsibility: repeated material does not add independent observations, and the number of passing instances is not the framework’s net utility.

teachingExamples.text: Suppose a fictional system uses a total item count to answer ‘How many items are there altogether?’ At the formal level, one can prove that an exact sum suffices for this question; at the empirical level, the completeness and accuracy of each record still need checking; allocating staff based on the total additionally requires distribution, capacity, normative objectives, and authorization. These three tasks can connect, but none completes another’s work.

4.1.title: 4.1 Root-Instance Contract
4.1.lead: Fix the question and decision rules first, then append results truthfully; failing the positive gate does not automatically pass the null-conclusion gate.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 585–624, heading ‘4.1 Root-Instance Contract’; assembly anchor /theory/part-04#section-4-1. Short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘Failure to meet the positive criterion does not mean that the null model has been supported’ (Chinese source line 617). This section supplies a standard recording procedure for confirmatory testing; it does not prescribe the sole legitimate research form for every field. [T-41]

Preregistration and results should be separate sections. Preregistration fixes the question and rules before accessing the relevant results; results are appended only after execution, preserving the original version. Adding a backdated table after obtaining results, or deleting the original plan, cannot establish prior constraint. An unrun study is not_evaluated; expected numbers cannot masquerade as observed. Nor does ‘guide completed’ in this deliverable mean that any actual G-instance test was implemented for this question. [T-41]

The single primary criterion prevents selecting the most favorable outcome after seeing results. The standard procedure first selects a subtype and then a success criterion from its allowed list; it does not run all routes and relabel the best-looking one the ‘original primary objective’. Joint-outcome, multiple-model, sequential, or exploration-followed-by-confirmation studies can nevertheless have valid designs, provided the overall rules, selection and stopping procedures, and applicable multiple-comparison handling are declared in advance. Research outside this procedure is assessed on its own design and does not lose knowledge value because its field names differ. [T-41]

The table’s first group, ‘identity and freezing’: instance_id distinguishes this particular test; root_id identifies its question family; contract_version specifies the contract version; preregistration_timestamp supplies an auditable freeze time. An attractively formatted ID is only a name; immutable versions and evidence predating result access are needed to support the procedural fact that ‘the rules were genuinely set first’. [T-41]

The second group, ‘candidate object’: candidate_object_id and object_contract_id point to the D0 candidate object and its declared boundaries, variables, relations, interfaces, time window, scale, and identity. This identifies which object is being tested and prevents a different object with the same name from passing as a replication. But D0 only fixes a candidate; a name, documents, or complete fields do not automatically supply G1 grouping gain. [T-41; T-D0]

The third group, ‘scale and targets’: scale_profile must register all nine axes individually. A genuinely inapplicable axis receives not_applicable with a reason, and insufficient material receives unknown; unexplained axes cannot be deleted. time_window bounds the time window, identity_criterion states when the object still counts as the same, and target_variables identifies the outcomes in question. What changes with ‘a new team’, ‘next quarter’, or ‘less misclassification’ must be explicit; one cannot retain only better-performing periods or members after seeing results and reuse the original conclusion. [T-41; T-SP]

The fourth group, ‘proposition instantiation’: selected_subtype and selected_success_criterion fix the test type and single primary criterion; candidate_specification makes the candidate proposition concrete; zero_model supplies an appropriate N0; controls specifies conditions to control; model_classes lists permitted model families. The null model is not a deliberately weak opponent, nor are more controls automatically better. Both depend on the target and identification design; one cannot control away the very effect claimed and then silently change the question. [T-41; T-baseline]

The fifth group, ‘sampling and generalization’: sampling_unit states whether material is obtained by person, institution, time block, or another unit; generalization_unit states where conclusions may extend. Many repeated measurements of one institution are not many independent institutions; generalization to new institutions or times requires matching splits and evaluation grounds. More sample records do not automatically enlarge the domain of applicability. [T-41]

The sixth group, ‘decision rules’, separates evaluation_metric, decision_threshold, decision_rule, and null_decision_rule. The metric says how to calculate; the threshold sets the standard; the positive rule says how all design conditions combine; the null-conclusion rule separately specifies support for N0. Multiple targets require a predetermined single primary target or aggregation; multiple models require predetermined selection or ensembling; multiple comparisons require predetermined correction. Without these rules, the standard instance permits only one primary target and one primary model. [T-41]

A null conclusion requires three gates: a qualified equivalence or sufficiency test, proportionate power or sensitivity, and predetermined tolerances. It asks ‘What grounds support N0 at the specified precision, domain, and tolerance?’, not simply ‘Is it significant?’ A wide interval allowing both important positive and negative effects does not establish ineffectiveness because it contains zero. Likewise, failure of a positive test may be strong counterevidence or merely insufficient precision; this must be reported specifically rather than flattened into one state term. [T-41]

The seventh group, ‘mode and failure’: evidence_mode declares exploration, confirmation, replication, or falsification; falsifier states which result would overturn the predetermined claim; pause_condition specifies when the corresponding execution must stop or pause. Exploration may discover valuable candidates, and a falsification design may strongly test the original assertion; neither can be renamed prior confirmation after favorable results appear, nor can contrary material already obtained be erased. [T-41]

The eighth group, ‘deviations and status’: deviation_record preserves each deviation’s timing, reason, and effect, using none when there are no deviations; preregistration_status distinguishes draft, frozen_before_evidence, completed_from_frozen, and deviated_after_evidence. Sound new knowledge may require design changes; the proper response is to preserve the old version transparently and explain the new version and the status of its conclusions, rather than pretending it was always so. Recording deviations makes interpretation more honest but does not automatically restore support eligibility under the frozen rules. [T-41]

The ninth group, ‘results and time’: result_timestamp must follow the freeze time; observed_primary_result records only actual results for the predetermined primary target; decision_rule_outcome records thresholds, observed values, passes, and analytical artifacts item by item; null_decision_rule_outcome separately records the three null-conclusion gates; result_state provides the four-state summary. The tenth group, evidence_refs and analysis_artifact_refs, connects judgments to actual resolvable sources, frozen data, code, models, or logs; internal concept IDs, self-reported ‘passes’, or string prefixes cannot replace these materials. [T-41]

The four states are not four simple truth values. supported means a qualified instance passes the positive gate; null_supported means all three null-conclusion gates pass; unsupported_or_undecided accommodates lack of support or an unresolved judgment, but explicit counterevidence, insufficient precision, and material gaps must be described separately; not_evaluated only means not yet run. Summary states aid location and do not permit deletion of contrary evidence. If null gates were not frozen or did not all pass, failure at the positive gate cannot be converted to null_supported. [T-41]

Further support for a C branch requiring formal qualification must also pass support_eligibility_rule. Positive support comes from confirmatory or replication mode, with an auditable frozen version and time, frozen_before_evidence before results, completed_from_frozen under the frozen contract, a passed positive gate, and resolvable actual evidence and analytical artifacts. falsification mode can support only the predetermined falsification or null-model judgment and cannot rescue a positive G claim in reverse; exploration, drafts, deviations after results, and undisclosed deviations retain candidates or unresolved claims according to their actual status, without furnishing positive eligibility for that formal C branch. [T-41]

This does not define the existence of knowledge by formal procedural eligibility. External research may have valid multiple-outcome, sequential, or other designs and should be assessed by its actual evidence; this question cannot retroactively fill in fictitious G timestamps for a published paper and declare that it passes every field in the book. Use as domain evidence requires explaining its design and limits; a claim to support eligibility in this standard procedure requires separately checking every applicable condition. [T-41; T-roles]

Scale transfer must preserve the preselected subtype, success criterion, and positive/null rules. Moving to another region, level, or window cannot incidentally lower thresholds while retaining a claim that the original test holds; a genuine task change requires a separate traceable version. Appeals may challenge candidate objects, subtype, criterion, N0, primary target or aggregation, model selection or ensembling, multiple comparisons, controls, positive/null thresholds and rules, data splits, generalization units, versions, preregistration status, deviations, and falsification conditions. A verified change after results reduces the corresponding support eligibility without overwriting the original record. [T-41]

The actual historical example is the public abstract of Camerer et al.’s 2018 replication study: the authors report 21 social-science experiments with analysis plans reviewed by original authors and registered before replication, separately reporting significant same-direction results and other replication measures. This illustrates advance plans and subsequent results as two layers of material. This guide checks only the public abstract, without auditing individual timestamps, code, or complete designs, and therefore cannot award qualification for the book’s C branches on that basis. [R-replication]

The strongest objection is whether preregistration prohibits discovering new phenomena. It does not. Exploration, revisions, and new candidates can be retained; the key is to let readers know which questions were specified before results and which arose afterward, then confirm them with appropriate new material. Another objection is that checklists add work; adopting this procedure for a declared use therefore requires separately examining procedural costs and errors actually reduced. A filled-out table does not establish the framework’s effectiveness. [T-41; T-eval]

The G1 result field in the root contract means ‘support for grouping gain’, not approval of an object’s existence. Object fields, grouping rules, and the null model are fixed separately: membership and relational facts rest on their existing material, and the test asks only what adopting this grouping adds for the preselected outcome.
argumentSteps: First determine the factual assertion to test, object, scale, targets, and generalization domain, then freeze the rules specifying what results count as support or refutation.

Before accessing relevant results, lock the subtype/primary criterion and rules for multiple targets, multiple models, multiple comparisons, and stopping, reducing room for favorable selection afterward.
After execution, append only actual results and deviations, separately recording the positive gate and three null-conclusion gates; an unrun test cannot have observed results entered.

Summarize with four states while separately preserving specific conclusions about counterevidence, insufficient precision, or missing material; failure at the positive gate does not imply support for N0.
To support a C branch requiring formal qualification, further check the mode, frozen/completion status, pass flags, and resolvable external material; complete fields are not empirical proof.
Scale transfer and appeal preserve original rules and versions; changes after results reduce corresponding support eligibility, and new versions must not overwrite old records.
Valid research outside the procedure is assessed by its own design; preregistration guarantees neither affirmative results nor the overall utility of the framework.

caseNotes.title: Historical study: report predetermined plans and results separately
caseNotes.text: The public abstract of Camerer and colleagues' 2018 study reports replications of 21 social-science experiments, with analysis plans reviewed by the original authors and registered before replication. Under the reported criterion of a significant effect in the same direction, 13 met the requirement. The abstract also reports other replication measures. This shows why prior arrangements and later results cannot be merged into a single “registered therefore successful” marker. [R-replication]

The subscription-only full text was not accessed, and the timestamps, code, or raw data of the 21 studies were not audited. 13/21 is not a universal proportion for all social-science research, nor does it confer formal G/C instance eligibility under this book.

teachingExamples.title: Logical teaching construction: positive-support and null-conclusion checks address different questions
teachingExamples.text: A purely rule-based demonstration: the predetermined positive-support check requires the lower endpoint of uncertainty interval I to exceed 3 units. The separate null-conclusion rule requires I to lie entirely within [−1,1], with the predetermined equivalence/sufficiency procedure and sensitivity check also passed as stipulated. Case A has I=[4,6] and passes the positive-support check if other eligibility conditions hold. Case B has I=[−0.4,0.4] and passes the two other null checks, so the null conclusion passes. Case C has I=[−2,4], satisfying neither the positive check nor the tolerance range; record unsupported_or_undecided with the specific information. If no run occurred at all, use not_evaluated and do not invent I.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Intervals, units, thresholds, and pass/fail conditions are artificial logical inputs. Each example assumes the relevant requirements for mode, frozen version, and material eligibility hold. No statistical estimation or power calculation was performed; the written intervals are not claimed to come inherently from qualified statistical procedures.
teachingExamples.boundary: Demonstrates conditional relations rather than universal statistical thresholds. Actual testing must choose methods proportionate to the error model, sample, and target, and separately check all three conditions.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: choosing after inspection differs from combining beforehand
teachingExamples.text: In a teaching model, suppose 5 mutually independent tests each have a false-pass probability of 0.05 when their null hypotheses are true. If any passing test is selected afterward as overall success, the probability of at least one false pass is 1−(1−0.05)^5=1−0.95^5=0.2262190625, approximately 22.62%, not 5%. This demonstrates the need to define an overall rule and applicable corrections beforehand. The example does not impose independence on actual correlated indicators.
teachingExamples.assumptions: 5, 0.05, and mutual independence are mathematical assumptions; all null hypotheses are stipulated true. No actual research data are used.
teachingExamples.boundary: The value generally differs for correlated tests. This example also cannot prescribe any single correction method as the sole method for all research.

questionAnswers.question: Before a run has occurred, may the expected mean be entered in observed_primary_result?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Retain not_evaluated; simulated or assumed values must retain their separate status.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 563 and 619.

questionAnswers.question: If the primary criterion fails, may one directly write null_supported?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Equivalence/sufficiency, power/sensitivity, and tolerance checks must be frozen beforehand and all passed. Otherwise retain unsupported or unresolved status and explain why.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 617–619.

questionAnswers.question: Is a strong relationship discovered in exploration worthless?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It can become a candidate for subsequent confirmation, but selection after seeing results cannot be presented as the original confirmatory instance.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 565 and 621.

questionAnswers.question: Can one hundred records from the same institution directly support extrapolation to new institutions?
questionAnswers.answer: Not from the count alone. Sampling units, dependencies, and extrapolation evaluation must each be checked.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 601.

questionAnswers.question: Is an instance ID with a formal version enough to support C?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Applicable conditions also include mode, prior freezing, completion under the frozen contract, a passed positive-support check, and resolvable evidence and analytical artifacts.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 621.

questionAnswers.question: Why can I=[−2,4] not support N0 under the teaching rules?
questionAnswers.answer: It does not lie entirely inside the predetermined [−1,1] tolerance range. Failure of the positive-support check cannot compensate for that failure.
questionAnswers.basis: Teaching construction and Chinese source line 617.

questionAnswers.question: What is the probability of a false pass if success is selected afterward from 5 independent null-hypothesis tests?
questionAnswers.answer: 1−0.95^5≈22.62%; this value depends on the artificial assumptions of independence and 0.05 for each test.
questionAnswers.basis: This section's mathematical derivation.

questionAnswers.question: Should an existing joint study with multiple targets be rejected because it does not use these fields?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Evaluate its actual joint rules, selection/stopping design, and evidence. A different format does not cancel knowledge.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 589.

figures.alt: Freeze the question and rules before results, then append actual results and deviations after execution. Confirmation or replication requires formal eligibility; exploration and post-result departures remain candidates rather than masquerading as positive C support.
figures.caption: An author-made standard-procedure diagram based on §4.1. The temporal sequence is a requirement, not a fabricated actual preregistration timestamp.

figures.alt: The four states—supported, null_supported, unsupported_or_undecided, and not_evaluated—respectively indicate the positive-support check, three null checks, lack of support or unresolved status, and no run yet, while retaining detailed conclusions.
figures.caption: The four states are summary indices, not replacements for specific counterevidence, precision, or material gaps. The diagram certifies no actual instance.

4.1.diagramBrief: Figure 2 shows freezing first, execution, and subsequent append-only results, along with eligibility boundaries concerning mode and departures. Figure 3 presents four summary states side by side, stressing that positive failure does not automatically become null support. All are static conceptual diagrams, not records of actual instance execution. If interaction is later implemented, it will highlight only artificial rule conditions.

applicability.reason: This unit concerns methodological judgment. Actual sources support only the listed facts; the diagram and teaching construction each retain their own status.

openQuestions: Whether an actual G-instance meets prior-freezing, statistical-design, and material-resolvability conditions requires auditing its original plan and results. This lesson conducted no such real study.
The distinction between lack of support and explicit counterevidence within the four states requires the specific design. A conceptual diagram cannot adjudicate it for the reader.

4.2.title: 4.2 Human empirical instance contract
4.2.lead: Discussion of humans may concern behavioral differences or persistent traces, or may only classify responsibility. This section first distinguishes proposition roles, then specifies falsifiable instances for three families of empirical questions.
explanation: Chinese source line 627 states, in translation, “Empirical truth belongs to these specific H-instances, not to abstract H propositions.” H1 “Meaning and coordination,” H4 “Power, mediation, and reflexivity,” and H5 “Historical trace carriers” are initially question families, not three labels proving that the world already works that way. An evaluable empirical assertion requires a specific, falsifiable question stating object, comparison, time, outcome, and criterion. “Contract” here is an agreement governing how research results qualify for support, not a legal agreement whose signing makes facts true. [T-42；T-Hroles]

The human empirical contract is separately named human_empirical_instance_contract. It replaces the generic root instance's root_id with claim_id, which permits only H1, H4, and H5. Other disciplines mirror §4.1: freeze the preregistration section before results and append the results section afterward; retain versions, phases, deviations, evidence references, analytical artifacts, and four outcome states. Missingness still distinguishes unknown, not_applicable, not_observable, and protected_not_public, with reasons appropriate to each. Unanswered cannot mean never occurred, nor may protected information be compelled merely to fill every field. [T-42；T-41]

The single-primary-criterion procedure requires selecting one subtype and its one success criterion before reading results. This table is a registration classification for the standard procedure, not an exhaustive account of every way meaning, power, or history exists. A reasonable question outside the table may separately specify its testable question and research design; it should not be forced into an easier-to-pass category. Valid multi-outcome or multi-model designs are not prohibited, but must freeze primary targets or aggregation, selection or ensembling, stopping, and applicable correction rules beforehand. The best result cannot afterward be called the original primary question. [T-42；T-41]

H1 requires preselecting one of three outcomes. Resource allocation asks how funds, time, materials, and similar resources are distributed, matching meaning_arrangement_resource_allocation_effect. Action choice asks which action is taken, matching meaning_arrangement_action_choice_effect. Coordination outcomes ask whether multiple people's actions coordinate, matching meaning_arrangement_coordination_outcome_effect. Conceptual explanation does not replace operationalization: the measurement, comparison, and required magnitude of difference still need registration. Improvement in any one does not establish success in all three. [T-42]

H1 yields a “conditional orientation anchor” within a specified object, scale, window, and outcome family. In ordinary terms: under these conditions, this candidate meaning arrangement connects with an evidenced difference in resources, action, or coordination. A further causal-mechanism claim requires a matching design and bridging evidence. Shared slogans or consistent behavior cannot establish that everyone has the same inner state, gives genuine consent, or shares a will. Group behavioral indicators and individual free expression are different measurement objects. [T-42；T-Hroles]

H4 preselects one of four types: evidence coverage, position_or_mediation_evidence_coverage_effect, asks which facts or positions become visible; expression safety, position_or_mediation_expression_safety_effect, asks about testable conditions for expression; object behavior, mediation_or_publicity_behavioral_response_effect, asks how action changes under mediation or publicity; reflexive response, observation_or_publication_reflexive_response_effect, asks how being observed or learning of publication changes the object in turn. These may be related, but a result for one does not automatically settle the other three. [T-42]

H4 must specify the particular position, mediation, publicity conditions, channel, outcome, and comparison. Labels such as “platform,” “power,” and “AI” are not intermediate mechanisms. Reduced reporting somewhere may concern coverage, expression, behavior, or other distinct questions; these distinctions cannot be skipped. The bounded conclusion extends at most to the corresponding obscuring, amplification, behavioral response, or reflexive response under those conditions. It does not directly establish malice or responsibility, still less authorize bans, punishment, or disclosure. When protected information is involved, register availability boundaries honestly. [T-42；T-Hroles]

H5 first selects a carrier family: institutional_or_textual_record, role_or_organizational_arrangement, habit_or_practice, trauma_record, or collective_memory_carrier. These are registration entry points. Naming “trauma” does not provide a diagnosis, nor does “collective memory” mean an identical inner state in everyone. Identify a specific observable, comparable carrier and trace quantity. [T-42；T-Hroles]

H5 also requires two mutually consistent fields: selected_carrier_family_id must exactly equal the selected subtype's carrier_family_id, and selected_carrier must be a nonempty atomic reference. For example, the teaching reference record:R17 identifies only the selected record; it cannot be filled with a list such as “all archives, positions, and habits.” This prevents searching many places and presenting the sole remaining difference as preselected. Atomic reference constrains the instance's registration target, not the actual object's internal structure. Multiple-carrier research requires a separately explicit design, not a fictitious atomic name concealing post-result selection. [T-42]

H5 then selects only one persistence criterion: threshold_persistence_over_preregistered_window requires a threshold persistence rule over the predetermined window; repeat_detection_across_preregistered_windows requires repeated detection across windows under predetermined rules; persistence_after_event_or_exposure_end concerns persistence after the event or exposure ends. These respectively constrain the window, detection, and ending time. Actual thresholds and observation methods must be stated beforehand. Code names do not provide statistical tests, durations, or default thresholds, nor permit selecting whichever criterion passes most easily afterward. [T-42]

H5 stops at “candidate traces within a specified carrier, observable, and window.” Distinguish three further questions: whether the trace persists under the rule; whether the current carrier affects later outcomes; and whether additional historical information improves explanation or prediction after controlling the current representation. The second requires separate evidence under §4.5; only the third requires an independent G3-instance. The same persistent trace may have subsequent effects or merely be retained without participating in the current process. A trace cannot leap directly into a path effect. [T-42；T-G3]

Outcome assessment still has two sets of checks. Failure of the positive-support check defaults to unsupported_or_undecided; “not significant” cannot mean null_supported. A null conclusion additionally requires passing the equivalence/sufficiency, power/sensitivity, and tolerance checks preregistered in null_decision_rule. supported, null_supported, unsupported_or_undecided, and not_evaluated distinguish positive support, support for a bounded null conclusion, lack of support or unresolved status, and no evaluation yet. Each retains specific information rather than labeling an abstract H family permanently true or false. [T-42；T-41]

An exploratory H-instance, one departing after evidence, or one with undisclosed departures produces only candidates or unresolved status. It cannot directly upgrade the HV03 meaning interface, HV08 conditional potential field interface, or H5 carrier route to empirical establishment. This limits formal support status under this standard procedure. It neither erases bounded knowledge obtainable from external studies under their own designs nor permits retroactively inventing preregistration records for historical research. [T-42；T-interfaces]

H2, H3, and H6 do not enter this contract because their roles differ, not because they “have not found data yet.” H2 classifies action uptake and responsibility; ability to take up does not imply obligation. H3 classifies institutional write-back: actual changes to records, rules, resources, and so forth, with execution records, permit registration under the rule, but classification alone does not establish long-term learning. H6 supplies normative boundaries for open-ended undertaking; it neither diagnoses who has love nor requisitions sacrifice. Rules can classify according to material, but successful classification is not support for an empirical mechanism. [T-42；T-Hroles]

Even an eligible, supported H-instance strengthens only its bounded description or explanation. Value, responsibility, obligation, justification, and authority to act have their own premises. Actual adjustments additionally require C12, explicit normative premises, J-axis authorization, and operational procedures. “A publicity condition affects expression” cannot directly become “I may disclose personal identity”; “someone truly has uptake capability” cannot become “they must continue carrying the burden.” [T-42；T-Hroles]
argumentSteps: First distinguish roles: only H1, H4, and H5 are empirical hypothesis families under this contract. H2, H3, and H6 follow operational, classificatory, or normative limitations respectively.
For a specific H-instance, specify object, scale, window, comparison, observables, and extrapolation scope. Abstract names and complete fields do not generate empirical truth.

Before reading results, uniquely select the subtype and matching success criterion; freeze positive and null checks and the overall decision rule. For H5, also check family consistency and one nonempty carrier reference.
Obtain evidence and analytical artifacts under the frozen design; disclose availability, deviations, and dependencies. Write results into the append-only section without overwriting preregistration.

Assign the four states according to actual checks and evaluation phase. Positive-check failure does not mean null-check success; exploration or post-result selection cannot rescue formal empirical eligibility.

Restrict supported conclusions to the selected outcome family, conditions, and window. Inner states, responsibility, subsequent carrier effects, additional historical increments, and actual action each require separate proof or authorization.

caseLinks.title: Actual research: counts of late pickups after a fine do not reveal parents' inner states

caseNotes.title: Actual research: counts of late pickups after a fine do not reveal parents' inner states
caseNotes.text: Gneezy and Rustichini's paper, published in 2000, studied daycare centers in Haifa from January to June 1998. Of the 10 centers reported, 6 introduced a fine and 4 served as controls. The paper reports an increase in late pickups, with counts remaining elevated after the fine was removed. §III explains that the recorded unit was each late-pickup event, not each parent's inner state; §IV separately lists possible explanations concerning interpretations of the situation. This section adds the observation that behavioral outcomes, meaning mechanisms, and historical carriers are distinct questions. “Counts changed” cannot directly be rewritten as “all parents considered late pickup a purchased service.” Nor does a difference persisting after removal of a measure alone establish that a specific trace carrier and its causal effect have been identified.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: Journal of Legal Studies 29(1), 2000:1–17; printed pp. 3–5, §II design and beginning of §III; p. 8, results; p. 10, §IV explanations (PDF pp. 4–6, 9, 11)

Behavioral persistence is also not directly upgraded to a G3 historical increment.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one carrier and three different questions
teachingExamples.text: Suppose the observable trace scores of fictional record R17 are 4 and 3 in two prespecified windows, with repeat_detection_across_preregistered_windows selected in advance and a simplified rule requiring both windows to reach 3. Both observations therefore satisfy the rule. If the second window instead scores 2, the rule fails; it cannot be changed afterward to “once reached the threshold.” Even when satisfied, this only means that R17 passes the trace rule under these logical inputs. Whether it affects the next decision, or provides a historical increment beyond the complete current record, remains unevaluated.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The numbers, windows, threshold, R17, and rule are teaching assumptions. To isolate the demonstration, accurate observations, a matching family, and satisfaction of the contract and other necessary conditions are assumed. This example is neither a statistical test nor an actual H5 study.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual trace judgments also require a historical event, baseline, measurement, comparison, uncertainty, and the complete positive-support gate. This comparison of two numbers must not be treated as the entire empirical method.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: the same behavior does not uniquely identify meaning
teachingExamples.text: Suppose two fictional participants both choose action A. One does so because they endorse the arrangement, the other because they fear losing resources. Their shared behavioral record gives only A, A; at least these two configurations of inner states can produce the same observation, so “shared consent” cannot be uniquely recovered from it. This is a nonuniqueness counterexample, not a survey of actual people's motives.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The two motives and their mapping to behavior are assumed; no psychological information has been collected from anyone.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not deny that proportionate voluntary expression, interviews, or other methods can provide further evidence; it only limits direct mind-reading from a single behavioral indicator.

questionAnswers.question: If H4 preselects expressive safety but the results show only behavioral change after disclosure, may the original instance be recorded as supported?
questionAnswers.answer: No rescue is possible solely through another outcome. Preserve the result for the original criterion and treat the behavioral difference as a clue for another question; a new confirmatory study should freeze its design anew.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 629–637; H4's four outcome categories and the prohibition on post hoc cherry-picking.

questionAnswers.question: May H5 specify its carrier as [record R17, position P2] and choose either one later?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A standard instance requires one nonempty atomic reference and an exactly matching family. A legitimate study of multiple carriers requires a separately explicit design, not a post hoc choice.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 635–637.

questionAnswers.question: If a carrier persists after a historical event ends, has G3 been established?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Persistent traces, subsequent effects of a current carrier, and a historical increment beyond the current representation are three different judgments. G3 requires a dedicated comparison and support for the third.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 635 and §4.5.

questionAnswers.question: Does failure to observe a significant difference mean null_supported?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Equivalence or sufficiency, power or sensitivity, and tolerance in the preregistered null rule must all pass; otherwise the result is not supported or unresolved, as the specific circumstances warrant.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 637.

questionAnswers.question: If H3 material proves that a rule was actually changed, may we automatically conclude that it improved and immediately extend its use?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Write-back classification, long-term effects, normative evaluation, and permission to extend use have different responsibilities.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 639; §7.1, Chinese source lines 1519 and 1566.

questionAnswers.question: Does a strong external behavioral experiment have no knowledge value because it did not use an H contract?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It still supports proportionate domain conclusions under its own design; it simply cannot claim formal support status under a standard procedure it did not actually complete.
questionAnswers.basis: §7.0, Chinese source line 1549; this section's instance discipline.

applicability.reason: This section concerns evidential boundaries for human behavior and mechanisms, using an original published field study to illustrate levels of observation and explanation. Explicit teaching constructions isolate the logic of H5 and consent questions without disguising them as actual cases.

openQuestions: The objects, indicators, thresholds, comparisons, and protective arrangements of actual H instances depend on specific studies. This lesson explains the contract; it does not invent research that has already been conducted for the reader.

4.3.title: 4.3 G1 Conditional Gain of a Candidate Grouping
4.3.lead: After calling several records a group, ask what additional contribution that grouping information actually makes under fair comparison and with new material. G1 separates “naming an object” from “obtaining a task gain from a grouping.”
explanation: Chinese source line 645 limits the question to whether a candidate grouping explains prespecified out-of-sample differences, rather than “whether this object ultimately exists in the world.” The object may first register its boundaries, states, relations, interfaces, time window, scale, and identity under D0; G1 then asks whether this way of grouping adds value for a particular task. Reliably recorded people, institutions, or events do not cease to exist because no G1 test has been performed; conversely, a name and coherent story do not prove predictive or intervention gain from grouping. [T-43; T-D0]

“Conditional gain” does not ask whether a group contains a few similarities. It compares an analysis using the candidate grouping against N0. N0 must be complexity-matched and must not use that grouping information. Otherwise, if one side has more parameters, more data, or access to outcomes, its advantage may arise from these extra opportunities rather than the grouping itself. Complexity matching is not mechanical parameter counting; an actual design must specify effective flexibility, tuning budgets, and comparison methods for its model class. This explains the research responsibility of implementing fair comparison; it does not claim that the original text specifies one unique complexity measure. [T-43]

The object, SP scale, T time window, K identity criterion, candidate grouping, and thresholds must all be preregistered. SP specifies the scale positions of the comparison, T its periods, and K what continues to count as the same object. Changing boundaries, membership, time, or identity changes the claim being tested. Failed members cannot be removed or a favorable period selected after seeing results while still claiming support for the original grouping. [T-43; T-D0]

G1a's sole success criterion is out_of_sample_predictive_gain: out-of-sample gain in the selected predictive evaluation. G1b's sole success criterion is out_of_sample_intervention_gain: out-of-sample gain in the intervention evaluation defined in advance. These cannot be exchanged after seeing results. Predictive discrimination does not automatically show that acting on this grouping improves outcomes; intervention benefit cannot fill in success for an unevaluated prediction task either. Both instance types are governed by the common discipline of freezing, controls, boundaries, and replication checks. [T-43]

A shared environment is an important competing explanation: similar changes among records in one group may simply reflect exposure to the same weather, equipment, or rules. Sampling procedures may place groups in different locations or imaging conditions; classification bias may favor assigning easily recognized samples to one category; grouping leakage allows outcomes to be predicted, test information, or near-direct proxies for them to enter grouping or training. A nominal training/test split does not automatically eliminate these problems. [T-43]

“Out of sample” means that evaluation information was not used to select, fit, or rescue this confirmatory claim. The specific split must fit the unit of extrapolation in question; near-duplicate records from the same source falling on opposite sides do not constitute independent new sources. After observing out-of-sample gain, the prespecified boundary perturbations must also be tested: does the gain persist under proportionate changes to allowable uncertain boundaries? Perturbation is not arbitrary destruction of the object; which changes remain within the original task and K must be stated in advance. [T-43; T-41]

Another gate is checking replication in independent time blocks or locations. Repeated random splits within the same collection conditions cannot automatically be called independent temporal or spatial replication. “Or” means the original text permits proportionate types of replication check; it does not permit selecting a favorable result afterward while concealing other failures. Replication units, rules, and recorded results should match the frozen contract. If a finding holds only at location A, retain the local material for A rather than automatically generalizing it to B. [T-43; T-41]

The minimum positive support in this section is a conjunction: prespecified evaluation metrics and thresholds, out-of-sample gain relative to N0, robustness to boundary perturbations, independent time-block or location replication, and the instance's own eligibility for support. Satisfying only one item is insufficient. In particular, “better than no model” does not mean “better than a complexity-matched N0 that does not use grouping information,” and “excellent on the original sample” does not mean “both perturbation and replication checks hold.” [T-43]

If gain fails the positive-support gate, or perturbation or replication results do not reproduce, the default is that this instance is not supported or remains unresolved. This may weaken its extrapolation claim, but does not automatically prove that the grouping is useless, much less that the object does not exist. Only when equivalence or sufficiency tests, proportionate power or sensitivity, and tolerance gates under the preregistered null-conclusion rule all pass may bounded N0 support or refutation of the corresponding G1 instance be established. The scope of refutation remains limited by the original contract. [T-43; T-41]

If the object, grouping, success criterion, N0, decision rule, threshold, data split, or leakage controls were not frozen before results, the original text requires suspending the instance. Suspension concerns eligibility for confirmatory support: information already obtained may be retained as exploratory material, with a separately explicit version or independent test, but cannot be presented as if prespecified. Existing domain methods remain evaluated on their own evidence; absence of registration under this framework cannot invalidate all knowledge. [T-43; T-41; T-D0]

Passing G1 permits, at most, recording the strength of support for grouping gain within the specified SP/T/K, the robustness of that gain to tested boundary perturbations, and the grouping's applicability window. It does not confer a shared will on a group of people, turn a class of devices into a responsible party, or authorize researchers to redistribute resources or act upon members. Grouping gain, mechanisms, intentions, values, and actions each have different evidential and procedural responsibilities. Nor may later F formal proofs replace external material for this section's empirical propositions. [T-43; T-roles]

The formal v2 results are the strength of support for grouping gain, the robustness of that gain to tested boundary perturbations, and its applicability window. “Robust” modifies the gain's performance under listed perturbations; it does not mean that boundaries are now real, unique, or beyond dispute. Changing outcome variables, extrapolation units, or boundary sets requires explaining whether the original support still applies.

Giving a membership list to researchers can establish identity facts supported by the list. If using that list as a predictive feature provides no gain, that finding limits this particular use. Members cannot be required to prove that they improve predictive accuracy before qualifying for recognition, services, or appeal.
argumentSteps: First specify the candidate grouping to be tested, the object, and SP/T/K; freeze G1a or G1b and its matching success criterion.
Design a complexity-matched N0 that does not use this grouping information, specifying controls for shared environment, sampling, classification bias, and leakage.
Compute the specified evaluation gain out of sample using the prespecified split, and assess the positive-support gate according to thresholds and uncertainty rules.
Test robustness under boundary perturbations allowed in advance, then check replication in proportionate independent time blocks or locations; preserve failures and locally valid scopes.

Only when all the above conditions and instance eligibility are met may bounded object identification and the robustness of that gain to tested boundary perturbations be strengthened. Failure defaults to not supported or unresolved; null conclusions must pass their own gates.
Finally retain SP/T/K limits; do not infer ultimate existence, shared will, value, responsibility, or permission.

boundaries: Original-text boundary: if out-of-sample gain falls below the threshold or boundary and independent replication checks do not reproduce, the default is not supported or unresolved; this is not an ultimate denial of the object.

Constructed conditional counterexample: using the test results themselves as high/low grouping labels, then claiming that grouping accurately predicts those results, is grouping leakage and cannot constitute the predictive gain in question.

Constructed conditional counterexample: a candidate model receives extensive tuning while N0 is allowed only an arbitrary constant. Even if the candidate wins, complexity differences have not been isolated.

Constructed conditional counterexample: a group of machines changes synchronously because they occupy the same temperature-controlled room. If comparison under the same environment removes the grouping difference, the uncontrolled shared variation cannot all be attributed to object grouping.

Author-constructed conditional counterexample: a group's behavior may be easy to predict while its members still disagree and have conflicting interests; support for a grouping does not establish a unified agent or common will.

G1 is this text's formal route for supporting object groupings, not the sole entry point for recognizing all object facts and domain knowledge. The real research case has not been retrospectively recognized here as a qualified G1 instance either.

caseLinks.title: A deliberate construction in real research: a wolf/husky classifier that looks at the background

caseNotes.title: A deliberate construction in real research: a wolf/husky classifier that looks at the background
caseNotes.text: Section 6.4 of Ribeiro, Singh, and Guestrin's 2016 paper describes a deliberately constructed bad-classifier experiment: training images of wolves had snowy backgrounds, while those of huskies did not; predictions on separately obtained images also largely followed snow or light backgrounds. The authors explicitly state that they deliberately created this model to study whether people could identify the problem; it must not be retold as an incident accidentally discovered in a real deployed system. This section uses it to illustrate how sampling backgrounds and categories can be entangled: names and some correct predictions are insufficient to establish that a model captures the intended grouping. LIME explanation images are not treated here as a substitute for all G1 conditions.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Ribeiro et al., Why Should I Trust You?, authors' arXiv v3
caseNotes.sourceLocator: arXiv:1602.04938v3, 2016-08-09; first and second paragraphs of §6.4, PDF page 8, and the Figure11 caption on page 9
caseNotes.boundary: This genuinely published experiment contains data deliberately selected by its authors. It provides specific research material on sampling-bias risks, not newly fabricated measurements in this lesson. Its G1 complexity matching, preregistration, boundary perturbations, and cross-site replication have not been audited. It is not used to deny the existence of animal categories or to claim that any explanation method can guarantee correctness.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: initial gain passes, but the boundary gate may still fail
teachingExamples.text: Suppose two frozen predictors each have two fitted means. The candidate groups by predefined g and is trained to predict 0 and 4; N0 does not use g, instead grouping by another predefined variable z and learning 2 and 2. Four independent teaching test records have Y=(0,0,4,4), g=(0,0,1,1), and z=(0,1,0,1). The candidate mean squared error is MSEg=(0+0+0+0)/4=0; the baseline is MSEN0=(4+4+4+4)/4=4; the gain Δ=4−0=4 exceeds the predefined threshold 1. Next, under a pre-allowed boundary-uncertainty scenario, change the second record's group membership to 1 while keeping the trained predictors and all other inputs unchanged. Candidate predictions become (0,4,4,4), MSEg=(0+16+0+0)/4=4, and Δ=0. Thus, passing the initial gain requirement does not satisfy this perturbation rule, and independent replication remains incomplete.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All data, trained means, model classes with two parameters each, thresholds, groupings, and perturbation rules are mathematically stipulated. The candidate's and N0's training sets exclude these four test records, and selection does not inspect test outcomes. The example assumes that the specified membership perturbation falls within boundary uncertainty accepted beforehand, rather than arbitrarily destroying the object.
teachingExamples.boundary: This demonstrates calculations and logical gates. Equal two-parameter counts illustrate matching only within the stipulated model classes; they are not a universal complexity criterion. Statistical uncertainty has not been estimated, nor has a formal G1 instance been completed.

teachingExamples.title: Conditional-counterfactual teaching example: a predictive marker is not an intervention benefit
teachingExamples.text: Let environment E take 0 or 1 with equal probability, with structural equations g=E and Y=E. Under observation, g=Y always holds, so predicting Y from g can be perfectly accurate. If an intervention only replaces the recorded variable g, leaving E and the equation Y=E unchanged, Y remains determined by the original E. This suffices to show that the inference from predictive association to ‘changing the group name changes the outcome’ is invalid.
teachingExamples.assumptions: E has a distribution with equal probabilities for 0/1; g=E and Y=E, with no g→Y; do(g) replaces only the g equation without changing E's distribution or the Y equation. These are all teaching causal assumptions, not a measured graph of any real organization.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not deny that actually changing the resources, interactions, or environment corresponding to a grouping may have effects; that requires specifying the actual intervention and gathering separate evidence.

questionAnswers.question: Why does a grouping outperforming others on a random test set still not establish that G1 is complete?
questionAnswers.answer: A fair N0, confounding and leakage controls, predefined boundary robustness, independent time-block or site replication, and instance eligibility are still required, among other conditions. A random holdout does not automatically satisfy these.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 643–647.

questionAnswers.question: After G1a fails, can the subtype be changed to G1b upon discovering a favorable intervention metric?
questionAnswers.answer: The subtype cannot be changed after the fact while retaining the original confirmatory status. The new lead may be retained and investigated further under an explicit version and independent design.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 621 and 647.

questionAnswers.question: Is the example's initial Δ=4 already sufficient?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Under the predefined boundary scenario, Δ=0, so the robustness gate fails; independent replication and other conditions have not actually been carried out either.

4.4.title: 4.4 G2 Specified-channel effects and dimension-by-dimension finitude
4.4.lead: Knowing that a treatment changed an outcome does not necessarily tell us which route carried the change. G2 specifically checks the specified channel; once a channel has an effect, each of its performance dimensions still requires separate measurement.
explanation: Chinese source line 653 limits the conclusion to ‘candidate causal bearer of that transition’ (translated from Chinese). This does not declare causation simply by drawing an arrow. First specify the carrier or channel, target state transition, and identification design, then test whether the preselected change produces a difference in the target exceeding the threshold. ‘Candidate’ retains competing explanations and withdrawal conditions; evidence for a channel in one transition does not mean it accounts for all changes. [T-44]

G2a is the controlled-identification subtype and requires exactly one preselected criterion: controlled_perturbation_effect or controlled_intervention_effect. In plain terms, a study may predefine an examination of responses to controlled perturbation or effects of controlled intervention, but it cannot try both and then say ‘either success establishes it.’ The specific operational meaning, intensity, object, and comparison must be defined in the plan; the name itself does not guarantee that the manipulation affects only the specified channel. [T-44]

G2b uses natural variation that satisfies identification conditions, with the sole criterion identified_natural_variation_channel_effect. ‘Naturally occurring’ does not mean ‘naturally random.’ The actual design must explain where the variation comes from, why it can distinguish the channel effect in question, and which common causes or selection processes might still explain the result. Calling something a ‘natural experiment’ cannot dispense with these identification conditions. Specific assumptions differ across designs; this section provides no universal set of conditions applicable to all natural variation. [T-44]

Both types must freeze the channel, target transition, quantity type and unit, comparison threshold, and dimensions to be measured before results are known. The null model concerns only the selected criterion: the perturbation, intervention, or identifiable natural variation does not produce a difference in the target transition exceeding the threshold. Unselected success criteria do not determine this instance's success or failure. Other favorable measured results may honestly be recorded as exploratory findings or separate questions, but cannot rescue the original confirmatory claim. [T-44；T-41]

The five dimensions must be separated individually. Capacity asks how much can be carried, at what rate or limit, under given conditions and within a given window; latency asks how long it takes from which starting point to which endpoint; reliability asks the frequency or probability of agreed success under which trial denominator and conditions; controllability asks which available operations can change the target over what range; loss asks how much of a same-type quantity decreases, transfers, or transforms after crossing a boundary. Each needs its own measurements, errors, and N0 or predefined baseline; a single instance of ‘it can get through’ does not establish all five performance dimensions. [T-44]

The title's ‘dimension-by-dimension finitude’ is not an unconditional law of the universe. Chinese source line 657 explicitly does not claim that every channel is finite in every dimension. Conclusions about finite ranges, upper bounds, or limits must concern actual channels and actually measured dimensions. A single latency measurement does not measure maximum throughput, long-term reliability, every controllable state, or loss. Unmeasured items remain unknown; do not write them as zero, infinite, or established. [T-44]

Tracing a ‘transfer’ also requires compatible quantity types. If 10 joules enter and 8 joules leave through a specified outlet, the destination of the remaining 2 joules can be discussed after clearly accounting for the boundary. They need not have disappeared; they may be stored within the boundary or exit elsewhere. If the input is electric charge and the output is a count of information items, the same conservation subtraction cannot be performed directly. Specify conversion relations, units, accounting boundaries, and accounting rules. Money, time, injury risk, and emotional burden do not become directly additive quantities of the same type merely because all are called costs. [T-44]

If common inputs, alternative channels, or measurement protocols suffice to explain a difference attributed to the specified channel, the corresponding channel support should be withdrawn, rather than preserved by switching to a favorable metric. For example, rising temperature can change two sensors together without their transmitting to each other; changes to statistical definitions can also create apparent differences. How the intervention is actually implemented, who is selected, and how common conditions and measurements change can all alter the original identification account. [T-44]

If the preselected criterion produces no difference exceeding the threshold, the default is that positive G2 is unsupported or unresolved, not automatically that ‘the channel is ineffective.’ The corresponding null conclusion or refutation must be registered beforehand and pass qualified equivalence or sufficiency tests, power or sensitivity requirements, tolerance rules, and related conditions. Tests that are too coarse, insufficient exposure, or unsuitable windows may leave the current material unable to distinguish effects. There may also be strong bounded counterevidence, which must be explained according to the actual design; these situations cannot all be written as a definite zero effect. [T-44；T-41]

The reverse direction is equally important: G2 is not the sole entry point for all causal knowledge. If a qualified comparison identifies a treatment's total effect but cannot yet distinguish intermediate paths, retain the total effect and the unresolved mechanism. Do not invent a mediator to fill a channel field; nor should a well-grounded total effect be deleted because its mediator remains unknown. The reliability of the total effect still depends on the original design and evidence; ‘mechanism unresolved’ is not a license to waive reviews of confounding and measurement. [T-44；T-domain]

A near-zero total effect also cannot by itself rule out every local process. Two paths may have opposite directions, or compensation may maintain an endpoint quantity. A mathematical sum of zero does not imply that every term is zero. But ‘possible cancellation’ is only a competing hypothesis, not proof that canceling channels actually exist; local processes still require independent evidence. Later, §11.6 also discusses why segment-level effects cannot unconditionally be combined into an effect of the entire chain: common support, timing, and correspondence must be retained. [T-44；T-chain]

Passing G2 at most locates a candidate causal bearer for a transition and limits in the measured dimensions. A device, procedure, or position transmitting effects within a causal chain does not thereby become a bearer of moral or legal responsibility; a person who actually transmits effects does not automatically bear all responsibility either. Knowledge, control, authorization, duties, and remedies still require separate judgments. Causal localization does not create a unified cost across domains or grant researchers real-world authority to operate. [T-44；T-CVRS]
argumentSteps: First specify the state transition to be explained and the candidate channel; freeze G2a or G2b and its uniquely matching criterion before results are known.
Explain identification conditions for the actual perturbation/intervention or natural variation, controlling explanations based on common inputs, alternative channels, selection, and measurement.
Compare target differences using the predefined type, units, window, and threshold; the corresponding evidence supports only the selected criterion.
Measure capacity, latency, reliability, controllability, and loss separately, each with its own baseline; a result in one dimension cannot fill in the others.
If the positive gate fails, retain unsupported or unresolved status; assess null conclusions independently under predefined rules. A new favorable criterion does not restore the original eligibility.
If only the total effect is identified, retain it and acknowledge that the channel remains unresolved; if the total effect is near zero, judge local channels only from independent evidence.
Stop at the candidate causal bearer and measured limits; do not automatically infer responsibility or real-world authority.

caseNotes.text: Section 4.2 uses Gneezy and Rustichini's 2000 daycare-fine study to distinguish behavioral counts from psychological claims. This section additionally checks the opening of the conclusion on printed page 15: after reporting behavior following the introduction and removal of fines, the authors explicitly state that the available data and theory still cannot rule out the two proposed explanations. Pages 10–14 discuss explanations involving information in incomplete contracts and social norms. This new location illustrates the difference between ‘a research report of a treatment effect’ and ‘a uniquely identified intermediate channel.’ The paper did not withdraw all reported observations merely because its mechanism explanations still competed.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: opposing paths produce a zero sum
teachingExamples.text: Let structural equations be M1=2X, M2=−2X, Y=M1+M2, with X equal to 0 or 1. Under do(X=0), the equations give M1=M2=Y=0; under do(X=1), M1=2, M2=−2, Y=0. The total effect Y(1)−Y(0)=0, while the two intermediate quantities change by +2 and −2. Under independent operations allowed in this model, setting M1 from 0 to 2 while fixing M2=0 changes Y from 0 to 2, showing that a zero total effect has not erased local effects.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The equations, common units, and operation domain allowing independent settings of M1/M2 are mathematical assumptions; there are no real channels or experimental samples.
teachingExamples.boundary: Refutes the unconditional inference “the sum is zero ⇒ every term is zero”; it does not establish offsetting real-world paths or confer ability or authorization to manipulate mediators.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one timing record cannot fill five performance dimensions
teachingExamples.text: A fictional transmission log records only one message sent at t=0 seconds and received at t=2 seconds, with synchronized clocks and consistent endpoint definitions. This record's delay can be calculated as 2 seconds; without more material, maximum capacity, success probability within an agreed window, reachable control range, and loss rate remain unknown. If intermediate buffering also exists, the relationship between capacity and delay needs an explicit model and cannot be inferred from one number.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The record and synchronization conditions are teaching inputs, not measurements of real equipment; the example illustrates measurement responsibilities only.
teachingExamples.boundary: One successful record can describe one success, but does not imply 100% long-term reliability, still less complete G2 channel identification.

questionAnswers.question: If controlled perturbation fails but another intervention succeeds, can the original G2a count as passing?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Judge only by the single preselected criterion; another result may generate a new question, but cannot retrospectively rescue confirmatory eligibility.

questionAnswers.question: If a naturally occurring power outage accompanies reduced output, can it directly be called G2b?
questionAnswers.answer: Natural occurrence alone does not confer identification. Actual exposure, common conditions, selection, alternative channels, and measurement must also be examined so the comparison supports the specified channel.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 629 and 657.

questionAnswers.question: How should one report a qualified randomized treatment comparison that finds a total effect but does not measure mediators?
questionAnswers.answer: Retain the bounded total effect, mark the channel unresolved, and invent no mechanism; also retain the comparison's actual limitations.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 659.

questionAnswers.question: If the mathematical example's total effect is zero, do both paths have no effect?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Changes of +2 and −2 in the two intermediate quantities offset each other; but this is only a conclusion of the given model, and real paths require separate evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 659 and this lesson's mathematical construction.

questionAnswers.question: Does measuring 2 seconds imply 100% reliability or a capacity of 0.5 items/second?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Two seconds is only the delay in this log entry; reliability needs an explicit denominator and conditions, while capacity needs corresponding load/concurrency/window and measurement. Inverse delay is not a universal capacity formula.
