4.13.3.title: 4.13.3 C10 human uptake and intertemporal reproduction
4.13.3.lead: C10 separates work, costs, benefits, the right to stop, and responsibility in human uptake. It also asks: someone did the work today, but can resources, capabilities, and succession actually keep up tomorrow?
explanation: Line 922 of the Chinese source first limits the objects to structures involving human action, care, maintenance, or institutional implementation. The basic hard dependency G2 locates the specified uptake channel; H2 is an operational typing gate requiring separate registration of uptake carriers, bearers of commensurate costs, beneficiaries, rights to stop, and responsible parties. Typing helps reveal differences; it is not an additional empirical cause, nor does completing the table prove an intertemporal mechanism. [T-C10；T-H2]

Who performs the work, who contributes time or resources, who benefits, who can stop, and who bears responsibility on what grounds may be different people or institutions. Equipment and procedures can also be uptake carriers, but performing a task does not give them human moral responsibility; organizational responsibility requires its standing and specific rules. Cost checks must preserve types, units, windows, and accounting mappings: work hours, money, and emotional expenditure cannot be added arbitrarily, nor can all responsibility be inferred backward from the most visible frontline performer. [T-C10；T-C2；T-human]

C10-current permits registration of a human uptake chain and its current distribution, but the full chain still requires bridges among objects and variables in the same case, a common scope of applicability, timing, capacity, and terminal outcomes. Seeing each person perform one segment does not mean the work successfully reached its final point of need; a substitute slot or shift roster is planning material, not evidence that succession actually occurred. Current help can be a real local contribution and need not be erased because the whole chain is incomplete. [T-C10；T-chain]

C10-carried-reproduction additionally tracks the retention, replenishment, replacement, and actual continuation of capabilities, rules, resources, or relationships over multiple cycles. Work must recur, resources may be exhausted, people need rest, and replacements must also have capabilities, resources, and functioning support. Corresponding G2 channel evidence must cover the subsequent outcomes and windows claimed; a single successful intervention cannot be expanded into long-term supply reliability. [T-C10；T-G3]

C10-intertemporal is the historical-increment intertemporal branch and additionally requires G3 support for a historical conditional increment beyond the currently registered state. C10-historical-carrier is more specific: a carrier restriction of this historical-increment branch, additionally requiring G3, H5, and a human historical-carrier instance. H5 establishes traces only for the selected carrier and window; it cannot alone establish future effects. The general carrier-continuation route is not forced to prove an additional historical quantity first. [T-C10；T-H5；T-G3]

Capacity for uptake does not automatically become an obligation to take up, nor does the existence of an uptake chain itself authorize requiring someone to sacrifice, continue, or withdraw. Withdrawal still requires considering the scope and duration of existing duties, handover, and the safety of affected people; protecting a right to stop does not remove every independently established obligation. Proposals for rotation, load reduction, or replenishment should disclose normative objectives, costs, and authority, rather than allowing C10 descriptions to decide social allocation directly. [T-C10；T-HV05；T-C12]

Where care or maintenance is involved, performing tasks may also be separate from the managerial labor of identifying needs, scheduling, reminding, checking, and remaining on call. Add corresponding records only when these burdens are relevant to the present target. Someone else completing one task can be real help, but this cannot establish that the entire managerial workload has been taken up. A heavy burden may arise from shared scarcity; burden alone cannot establish malicious requisition. These limits prevent classifications from making excessive conclusions in place of evidence or normative argument. [T-HV05]

The C10 row at the group's end requires proportionate comparisons involving replenishment, rotation, load reduction, withdrawal, or replacement. Failure of continuation to occur, long-term results explained by common inputs, and the current state absorbing historical differences each limit different branches. When H2 fields cannot be separated, record the specific gap; insufficient intertemporal materials do not warrant a reproduction-mechanism claim; missing G3 limits only the historical-increment type, while missing H5 prevents its formal trace qualification. Existing independent current contributions may be retained. [T-table]
argumentSteps: Confirm the human domain and the specified G2 uptake channel.
Use H2 to separate carriers, commensurate costs, benefits, rights to stop, and grounds for responsibility.
Check links within the same case, timing, capacity, and terminal outcomes; do not substitute plans such as rosters for actual continuation.
Intertemporal claims add causal and outcome materials covering capability/rule/resource retention, replenishment and replacement, and multiple cycles.
Historical increments additionally require G3; a specified historical-carrier restriction additionally requires H5. Traces must not substitute for future effects.
Argue normative objectives, duties, stopping, and actual authority independently.

distinctions.leftText: Who or what actually performs maintenance and transmission.
distinctions.rightText: Judged on the basis of the party's standing and specific responsibility rules.

distinctions.leftText: A real contribution on one occasion or within one window.
distinctions.rightText: Requires continuation over multiple cycles and relevant mechanism materials.

distinctions.leftText: Persistent differences in the specified carrier and window.
distinctions.rightText: Requires independent causal and task-outcome grounds.

distinctions.leftText: Has the capability or resources.
distinctions.rightText: Capability does not directly imply an obligation.

boundaries: Counterexample in the original text: if continuity did not actually occur or is explained by shared inputs, a plan cannot establish a cross-period mechanism.
Boundary in the original text: current states absorbing historical variables limits only the historical-increment branch; H5 does not substitute for future effects.
Boundary in the original text: the most visible executor is not automatically the responsible party, and capability does not automatically create unlimited obligations.
Teaching counterexample: the table says B takes over, but B lacks access and did not attend this round; a plan does not establish actual uptake.
Teaching boundary: B completes one task while A still schedules, reminds, and checks. The local assistance is real, but continuity of overall management remains incomplete.
questions: Does listing a substitute on a roster establish continuity of work across periods?
Can passing H5 alone establish the long-term effectiveness of a human uptake chain?
Does the person doing the most bear the most responsibility?
Does protecting a right to stop directly authorize arbitrary exit?

caseNotes.title: Apollo 13 canister adaptation: design, execution, and equipment have distinct roles
caseNotes.text: NASA’s Item 46 separately records ground engineers designing and testing an adaptation procedure, explaining it to the crew, and the crew constructing and connecting the canister. This section adds the division of uptake work: the ground plan, on-site fabrication, and physical device perform different tasks, which cannot all be hidden behind ‘the system repaired itself’.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a roster and actual continuity are different material
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a fictional service has 4 hours of same-type work each round. In round one, A actually completes 4 hours; in round two, the table assigns B 4 hours, but B has no system access yet and actual completion remains 0. Sufficient planned resources do not establish that service continued in round two. If access is obtained and the task completed later, record that round’s actual result separately without backfilling the earlier gap.
teachingExamples.assumptions: People, durations, permissions, and records are all teaching fiction; homogeneous work and absence of other substitutes are stipulated.
teachingExamples.boundary: This assigns no blame to actual employees or arranges anyone’s exit, nor does it establish that workload exhausts care quality.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: several positions in the same undertaking
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional arrangement, A raises the need and continually organizes, B performs one delivery, institution C supplies a vehicle, and D benefits. Who has a right to stop and who bears responsibility require separate grounds in actual rules. This separation cautions against merging executor, resource provider, beneficiary, and responsible party into one label; actual applications must identify real subjects and rules rather than copying fictional roles.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A, B, C, and D are illustrative roles with no specified legal or moral responsibilities.
teachingExamples.boundary: Classification itself proves neither causation nor long-term continuity and authorizes no additional obligation for anyone.

counterexamples.text: Counterexample in the original text: if continuity did not actually occur or is explained by shared inputs, a plan cannot establish a cross-period mechanism.
counterexamples.effect: A plan is not a continuity result.

counterexamples.text: Boundary in the original text: current states absorbing historical variables limits only the historical-increment branch; H5 does not substitute for future effects.
counterexamples.effect: Separate traces, effects, and increments.

counterexamples.text: Teaching counterexample: the table says B takes over, but B lacks access and did not attend this round; a plan does not establish actual uptake.
counterexamples.effect: Authority and execution must actually exist.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: B completes one task while A still schedules, reminds, and checks. The local assistance is real, but continuity of overall management remains incomplete.
counterexamples.effect: Local assistance does not complete management continuity.

questionAnswers.question: Does listing a substitute on a roster establish continuity of work across periods?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Check actual authority, resources, presence and execution, and terminal results.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 898, 906, and 952.

questionAnswers.question: Can passing H5 alone establish the long-term effectiveness of a human uptake chain?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It provides only bounded traces; future effects and continuity separately require evidence covering their outcome windows.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 922–932.

questionAnswers.question: Does the person doing the most bear the most responsibility?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. Actual uptake, costs, informed control, authorization, oversight, and other grounds of responsibility require separate judgments.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 926; H2.

questionAnswers.question: Does protecting a right to stop directly authorize arbitrary exit?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Existing duties, deadlines, handover, and affected people’s safety require independent argument; the uptake chain itself also authorizes neither continuation nor exit.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 926 and §7.3.5.

4.13.4.title: 4.13.4 C11 Institutional Write-Back
4.13.4.lead: C11 asks whether feedback has entered an institution’s actual operation. Receipts, field changes, and actual execution must be recorded separately; one write-back also cannot settle long-term learning, repair, or institutional legitimacy.
explanation: Chinese source line 938 requires ‘feedback causes field changes that are actually executed’. The object must have identifiable institutional fields, such as records, rules, resources, roles, responsibilities, memory, or stopping conditions. D2 defines return and change, G2 identifies the institutional return channel, and H3 classifies how far the process actually reached. H3 is a classification gate; labeling a table ‘written back’ does not create a real mechanism. [T-C11; T-H3; T-D2]

First distinguish acceptance, field change, execution, and duration. A receipt shows material was received; before-and-after field versions show which formal record or arrangement changed; execution records show whether the new field actually entered operation; timing material shows when it took effect, how long it persisted, and whether it reverted. A changed but inactive database draft does not mean the operational rule changed. If the target is publication of a public record, actual publication may execute that target, but does not imply that other operations updated simultaneously. [T-C11; T-HV07]

‘Feedback causes’ also bears a causal burden. Connect return inputs, receiving positions, field changes, and execution timing, using proportionate comparisons such as no return or blockage to rule out independent commands, shared external causes, or a planned revision. The fact that a new rule was actually executed can be retained first; if it cannot be identified as resulting from an appeal or audit, do not fill in a formal causal-feedback conclusion. [T-C11; T-table; T-causal]

Effective write-back need not correct error or improve matters. Incorrect feedback may genuinely change a rule and be executed, even with bad results; conversely, a review that justifiably upholds the original judgment may fulfill hearing and procedural responsibilities. If the target state does not change, do not record effective write-back for that target, but do not conclude that the review had no value. If the explanatory record changes, accurately record the item that changed. [T-C11; T-HV07; T-review]

One write-back is not learning. C3-carried-learning additionally checks retention of updates, subsequent invocation over multiple rounds, predetermined task comparisons, and corresponding causal evidence; the historical-increment branch C3-learning/CM-LEARNING-history additionally requires G3. Duration after write-back is something this contract must record, but length alone cannot establish task improvement, transfer, net benefit, or long-term repair. [T-C11; T-learning]

The concluding four-row table brings this group together. C8 checks variation and retention of differences across rounds; C9 checks observational arrival and persistence branches; C10 checks human positions and actual continuity; C11 checks return, fields, execution, and duration. Each has its own counterexamples; citing the same ‘update report’ under four headings does not constitute four independent validations. [T-table; T-source]

The C11 row’s failure boundaries are specific: a receipt or statement alone cannot establish field changes; changed but unexecuted fields count only as record updates; if independent commands explain changes, feedback attribution must narrow. Calling a case with no field change only ‘accepted’ is a record relative to this write-back target, not a denial of other procedural value. A cross-period mechanism especially cannot be extrapolated directly from one write-back. [T-table; T-HV07]

An institution’s genuine response does not automatically establish its overall legitimacy or expand its authorization. Expert opinions, audit reports, or high model confidence may enter comparisons of material, while action purposes, protection floors, jurisdiction, and correction procedures must remain explicit. C11 permits analysis of the stage an institution reached; it does not require participants to accept any goal or give up appeals. [T-C11; T-C12]
argumentSteps: Specify target institutional fields, original versions, return channels, and receiving positions.
Check acceptance, field changes, actual execution, and timing of effect, persistence, or reversion separately.
Use D2/G2 to compare return against no return or blockage, ruling out explanations such as independent commands.
Record only targets actually changed; do not dismiss all qualified reviews that uphold judgments as worthless.
Learning, intertemporal repair, net benefit, and institutional legitimacy carry separate responsibilities; one write-back cannot answer them all.

boundaries: Counterexample in the original text: a receipt or statement alone is insufficient to record effective institutional write-back.
Counterexamples in the original text: changed fields not executed, or changes explained by independent commands, limit the current formal write-back mechanism claim.
Boundary in the original text: one write-back does not equal long-term repair, positive improvement, institutional legitimacy, or expanded authorization.
Teaching counterexample: a draft scheduling rule changes after an appeal, but all actual scheduling still uses the old version; a draft change does not establish an operational update.
Teaching boundary: a review adequately justifies retaining the original decision and makes no target-state change. It may have procedural value but cannot thereby be called write-back to that target.
questions: Why does a receipt not yet establish write-back?
Does publishing a new rule establish that operations already follow it?
Is a review that upholds the original decision necessarily ineffective?
Does write-back equal improvement?
Does a published correction prove that all future papers will no longer omit citations?

caseNotes.title: A 1999 PNAS correction: public supplementation and long-term learning are separate
caseNotes.text: On September 14, 1999, PNAS published a correction to Eisen et al.’s 1998 clustering paper. The authors stated that two references had been omitted and provided sources for earlier work on data coloring and gene-expression clustering. The actually published supplement is evidence that content was added to a public record, beyond merely ‘someone raised a comment’. This section stops at that published addition and does not infer long-term improvement throughout the publication process.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: 1999-09-14; the sole body paragraph beginning ‘Genetics. In the article...’ and the following two References.
caseNotes.boundary: The checked material was the full short notice returned through the original page’s index; the direct page displayed browser verification on this attempt, which was not operated. No claim is made that every version of the original paper was rewritten. No material confirms the complete submission/acceptance process, a no-feedback counterfactual, or long-term prevention of recurrence, so full C11/G2 qualification is not granted.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: four records must not substitute for each other
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional service, r0 is a receipt acknowledging feedback; r1 is a draft proposed rule change; r2 is the new version approved for activation; and r3 is an execution log showing that version actually used in the next scheduling round. Possessing r0 alone does not establish a changed rule; r1 does not establish activation; even r2 still requires checking r3 for the operational target asked about. If the research target is only ‘formally publishing the new rule text’, an actual public record can establish that publication act but still cannot settle scheduling execution.
teachingExamples.assumptions: r0–r3 and the service are teaching assumptions; what effect each step has in a particular institution depends on actual rules. These four steps are not a universal statutory procedure.
teachingExamples.boundary: This makes no legal judgment about any actual institution, creates no authority for real modifications, and does not automatically establish feedback causation through a complete record.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: write-back can make outcomes worse
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a fictional dispatch rule originally handles a class of tasks correctly. Incorrect feedback changes it to an erroneous version that is actually executed. If causal material supports that feedback caused the change, this can be effective write-back; yet outcomes deteriorate under the predetermined accuracy task. Write-back, error correction, and net benefits of learning are therefore different conclusions.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Incorrect feedback, correctness of the original rule, error in the new rule, and actual execution are explicit conditions, not real-world accusations.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not establish that any actual review is harmful, nor justify universally abolishing feedback channels out of fear of error.

counterexamples.text: Counterexample in the original text: a receipt or statement alone is insufficient to record effective institutional write-back.
counterexamples.effect: Acceptance is not write-back.

counterexamples.text: Counterexamples in the original text: changed fields not executed, or changes explained by independent commands, limit the current formal write-back mechanism claim.
counterexamples.effect: Check execution and feedback attribution separately.

counterexamples.text: Teaching counterexample: a draft scheduling rule changes after an appeal, but all actual scheduling still uses the old version; a draft change does not establish an operational update.
counterexamples.effect: Drafts do not substitute for actual operation.

counterexamples.text: Teaching boundary: a review adequately justifies retaining the original decision and makes no target-state change. It may have procedural value but cannot thereby be called write-back to that target.
counterexamples.effect: Separate procedural value from target changes.

questionAnswers.question: Why does a receipt not yet establish write-back?
questionAnswers.answer: It establishes only acceptance; target-field change and actual execution remain necessary, along with checking the claimed feedback attribution.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 914–922 and 953.

questionAnswers.question: Does publishing a new rule establish that operations already follow it?
questionAnswers.answer: Not automatically; publication and operational execution are different targets, each requiring its actual records.
questionAnswers.basis: This guide’s four-record construction and H3 classification.

questionAnswers.question: Is a review that upholds the original decision necessarily ineffective?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. Sufficient reasons can fulfill procedural responsibilities; without a changed target, do not record write-back to it, while recording other changes as they actually occurred.

questionAnswers.question: Does write-back equal improvement?
questionAnswers.answer: No. An erroneous rule can genuinely be executed; accuracy, task outcomes, and net benefit require separate measurement.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 918 and 946.

questionAnswers.question: Does a published correction prove that all future papers will no longer omit citations?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It supports only the addition to the public record on that occasion; long-term learning and prevention of recurrence require subsequent process and task evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: This guide’s actual correction case and C3 branch requirements.

4.14.title: 4.14 Fourth Group: Normative Bridging Gates
4.14.lead: The first three groups describe objects, channels, and change. The fourth asks what else must be supplied when proposing choices or actions on that basis, so explanation does not exceed authority.
explanation: Chinese source lines 955–956 contain only the group heading ‘Fourth Group: Normative Bridging Gates’. Separating C12 reminds readers that normative choice is not a natural extension of the empirical mechanisms C1–C11. The next subsection supplies specific conditions; the parent section only explains this reading boundary and does not invent an empirical law absent from the heading. [T-414]

‘Bridging’ shifts responsibilities between two tasks: description says what may occur and how far evidence supports it; normative choice specifies what to pursue, what to protect, and who decides within what scope. Reliable explanation may provide consequences relevant to choice, but cannot itself specify values, allocate costs, or generate authority to act upon others. [T-C12; T-norm]

This group still permits analytical recommendations for deliberation. Analysts may compare options after making normative premises, evidence, and costs explicit; actual adoption additionally requires protections, J-axis authorization, and complete passage through O1–O4. Separating the two keeps discussion from masquerading as permission without treating a current lack of execution authority as a prohibition on all criticism, evaluation, or drafts. [T-C12; T-task]
argumentSteps: First recognize that this group contains only one subsection, C12.
Determine whether the current output is a description, an analytical recommendation for deliberation, or preparation for actual adoption.
Supply the corresponding normative and authority material for the task; empirical conclusions cannot directly bypass this step.

distinctions.leftText: Answers how something occurs or changes under given conditions.
distinctions.rightText: Constrains movement from description to choice and actual adoption.

distinctions.leftText: Material for discussion with explicit premises, evidence, and costs.
distinctions.rightText: Additionally requires complete protections, authorization, and operating procedures.

boundaries: Scope boundary in the original text: the parent section has no independent empirical content and must not be expanded into a new causal proposition.
Teaching counterexample: a model predicts that an arrangement is faster, but speed alone cannot decide who must bear its risks; evaluative premises and authority to act are still missing.
questions: Why is this group listed separately as the fourth group?
Can a proposal for public discussion be made without authority to execute it?

counterexamples.effect: Performance facts cannot independently determine values and authority.

questionAnswers.question: Why is this group listed separately as the fourth group?
questionAnswers.answer: C12 is a gate for normative and procedural validity and cannot follow automatically from the empirical mechanisms of the first three groups.

4.14.1.title: 4.14.1 C12 Normative bridging validity gate
4.14.1.lead: C12 requires laying out facts, values, protection, authority, options, and correction. It can block overreach, but does not automatically select the uniquely correct goal or create actual authorization because a form is complete.
explanation: The section's orienting sentence translates as “C12 is not an empirical inference” (Chinese source line 969). It is a procedural-validity gate before description enters real choice, not a causal effect proved by an experiment or a twelfth empirical mechanism inferred onward from G1–G4 or C1–C11. The minimum-evidence table requires proportionate material concerning frozen descriptions, explicit norms, protection, authorization, and operational procedures. Formal completeness and actual passage remain distinct. [T-C12]

The first hard dependency, N1, is “explanation does not authorize disposition.” It vetoes direct inferences from stability, efficiency, continued existence, selection, expert explanation, or high model confidence to an ought or authority to act. Alone, it permits only ceilings such as inaction, further evidence, or continued deliberation, without a positive objective. Even minimum harm or proportionality must have its principle, compared options, and reasons explicitly recorded for this case; unregistered principles cannot hide within the name C12. [T-C12；T-N]

O1 first freezes the description used, evidence status, uncertainty, scale, and descriptive action ceiling. Freezing does not mean never revising; it makes later choices traceable to an explicit version, preventing favored options from prompting retrospective changes to facts, thresholds, or evidence grades. New evidence requires traceable revision. High evidential confidence can strengthen description but cannot alone expand actual authority. [T-C12；T-O]

At runtime, O2 lists explicit_normative_premise_ids, specifying the goals, constraints, or veto gates adopted, who benefits, and who bears burdens, while retaining conflict and dissent. N2 prohibits lowering protection; N3 requires correctability of high-impact judgments; N4 prohibits requisitioning love and undertaking; N5 distinguishes continued existence and selection from justification. Each has a specific role; an abstract ID does not state a concrete objective. N4 also does not categorically cancel independently grounded bounded commitments, care, or remedial responsibilities. Different values can produce different recommendations under identical facts; conflict must remain visible rather than be erased by total scores or majority voice. [T-N]

O3 compares candidate options and inaction together, recording the authorizing subject, source, jurisdiction, duration, and J-axis. Here inaction means “not implementing this newly proposed candidate action,” not a static world or exemption from existing independent obligations. Account for natural changes along the baseline path, accumulating risks, maintenance costs, and distributional consequences. Actively maintaining the status quo must also be compared as a specific option if it requires new arrangements. [T-C12；T-options]

J-axis authorization must cover the same subject, object, single action, territory, and entire duration. Several permissions each missing an element cannot be spliced into authority for one action. Impact scope and technical capability are not jurisdiction. Legal validity, normative justification, and current authorization coverage are also checked separately; none alone settles the others. A divided procedure may connect steps performed by different subjects, each authorized for their own actions. Atomicity does not require one person to possess every procedural power. [T-J]

O4 turns bounded execution, monitoring, stopping, appeal, independent review, rollback, remedies, expiry, and reauthorization into arrangements capable of actually changing state. The action ceiling is the narrowest intersection of evidence, norms, protection, the selected option, J, pilot scope, reversibility, and duration. An unknown or failed gate cannot be offset by high scores elsewhere. Stopping must also account for safe withdrawal and independently continuing remedial duties. A rollback record cannot erase harm already incurred. [T-C12；T-stop]

Read the ten bridging components at Chinese source line 969 by responsibility: ①descriptive_or_explanatory_claim_ids specifies the descriptions used; ②current_evidence_and_epistemic_constraints records existing evidence and epistemic limitations; ③explicit_normative_premise_ids discloses value premises; ④normative_conflict_record retains conflicts; ⑤protection_floor_status states protection item by item. These five make explicit “on what grounds, toward what aims, and across which boundaries one may not go.” Merely writing “fully considered” is insufficient. [T-C12]

The remaining five are: ⑥authorization_and_jurisdiction_record checks who may decide what, where, and when; ⑦options_including_no_action retains genuine alternatives and inaction; ⑧operational_procedure_records connects O1–O4; ⑨action_ceiling bounds action scope and intensity; ⑩stop_review_rollback_and_remedy ensures stopping, review, rollback, and remedies. They are not ten arbitrary uploaded attachments: they must correspond to the same choice, action, and currently valid period, with substantively grounded content. [T-C12；T-J；T-PF]

PF-1 through PF-5 check, respectively: visibility of affected and low-power positions; availability of anonymous, representative, or low-exposure submission; effective refusal and stopping; time-bounded appeals able to change outcomes; and freedom from retaliation for evidence, dissent, refusal, stopping, appeal, and exit. PF-6 through PF-10 check: supplementary evidence, dispute marking, source-record correction, and downstream synchronization; external independent review for high impact, conflicts of interest, or failed internal correction; capacity for withdrawal, rollback, repair, and authoritative-version write-back; exit, transfer, and representation and alternative uptake for those unable to leave; and action ceilings, prohibited actions, stop triggers, responsible parties, and review times. Every item needs a mechanism, responsibility, evidence, and validity period. Empty labels do not pass. [T-PF]

When effects concern humans, sentient subjects, mixed objects, or unknown objects, all ten PF items must be active. pending, failed, and not_applicable cannot count as passing states for entry into authorized. Only when evidence restricts both the object and downstream uses to purely nonhuman processes may human-specific mechanisms be marked inapplicable with reasons. PF-10 and real action's J, responsibility, stopping, review, rollback, and expiry gates remain. Changed use requires review. The protection floor does not exhaust substantive rights, and a complete form does not automatically justify a specific distribution. Independently existing rights do not wait for this framework's form to take effect. [T-PF]

“A bounded recommendation eligible for actual adoption” and “an analytical recommendation for deliberation” stop at different points. The latter must disclose normative premises, evidence, costs, affected positions, and inaction, but does not require permission already obtained for execution that has not occurred. The former must fully pass explicit N, PF, J, and O1–O4. authorized is the framework's internal adoption state, not a replacement for actual institutional/legal validity, official powers, or personal consent. Pending review, suspension, requests for evidence, or preservation recommendations also do not themselves authorize data collection, freezing resources, or restricting others. [T-C12；T-task；T-J；T-stop]

The minimum-evidence table's four counterexample types identify breaks in values, objectives, authority, and correction: identical facts may yield different choices under different N; N1 alone lacks a positive objective; authorization may not cover the proposed action; stopping or rollback may be practically unreachable. A missing critical gate limits actual disposition but does not invalidate all factual research or require every deliberative recommendation to stop. C12 checks bounded bridging; it is not the sole proof for evaluating all social institutions, nor does description generate love, responsibility, demands for sacrifice, or authority to act. [T-C12；T-task；T-PF]
argumentSteps: Identify the descriptive propositions, evidence, scale, and uncertainty used here, creating a traceable O1 version.
List the normative IDs actually adopted and their roles as goals/constraints/vetoes. Explain conflicts, dissent, benefits, and burdens to form O2.
Compare genuinely feasible options with the baseline of no newly added action. Check valid J coverage and authorization sources for the same action to form O3.
Check PF-1–PF-10 individually for applicability, actual mechanisms, evidence, responsibility, and validity periods. Total scores cannot compensate among them.
Register O4 bounded execution, monitoring, stopping, appeal, independent review, rollback, remedies, and expiry. Specify the narrowest action ceiling.
Check that all ten bridging components are mutually bound and substantively grounded. Complete documents alone do not establish passage.
Retain analytical status when used only for deliberation. Actual adoption requires every hard gate to pass; internal passage still does not replace external legal validity or consent.

caseLinks.title: The 1979 Belmont Report: explicit principles and their application

caseNotes.title: The 1979 Belmont Report: explicit principles and their application
caseNotes.text: The US National Commission's Belmont Report was published on April 18, 1979. Part B explicitly lists respect for persons, beneficence, and justice; Part C discusses informed consent, risk–benefit assessment, and participant selection respectively. The report also notes that principles cannot always resolve concrete disputes without disagreement. This section uses that historical normative text to observe the practice of “disclosing principles and explaining their application,” rather than treating scientific benefit itself as the sole reason.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Original text of The Belmont Report hosted by HHS
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Report dated 1979-04-18; final paragraph of Ethical Principles & Guidelines; opening of Part B; opening of Part C and C.1.
caseNotes.boundary: These are facts about the content of a historical normative text, not proof that a study actually followed the principles, certification of complete C12, or current legal requirements. Sharing a source with earlier citations does not provide independent validation. This section adds observations about principles, specific applications, and unresolved normative disagreements.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: the same consequences, different explicit objectives
teachingExamples.text: Suppose two fictional feasible options produce gains in the same unit for positions A and B: option A=(9,3), option B=(5,5), baseline=(0,0). If the registered objective maximizes total gain within given constraints, A's total 12 exceeds B's 10. If it maximizes the smaller gain across the two positions, B's minimum 5 exceeds A's 3. Both calculations are correct; the ranking differs because of objectives, not erroneous facts. Without a positive objective, the numbers alone do not yield a unique choice.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Gains are additive, share units and windows, all other consequences are identical, both options are feasible, and independent protection constraints are assumed satisfied during comparison. All are artificial conditions, not actual authorization or conclusions about rights.
teachingExamples.boundary: Only a mathematical construction showing normative premises changing rankings. It does not establish universal priority for totals or the worst-position principle, nor equate greater benefit with actual permission to execute.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: incomplete permissions cannot be spliced
teachingExamples.text: Suppose fictional record J1 allows subject A to read object P during interval I, while J2 allows subject B to modify P in the same interval. The proposed action is A modifying P. J1 does not cover modification; J2 does not cover A. Together, neither covers the complete action, so it cannot be registered as authorized. In a separate conditional scenario, division of work can be argued only if A's reading, transmission/disclosure to B, and B's modification each have their own valid permissions, and inputs, uses, and timing connect. Transmission as a separate action also requires its own J check; reading and modification permissions do not authorize intermediate delivery.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The first counterexample includes only the two stated authorizations and no others. The second separately assumes each action obtains independently valid authority. People, object, and duration are teaching assumptions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Makes no judgment about actual legal powers and does not require one person to complete a complex procedure.

teachingExamples.title: Logical teaching construction: hard gates are not a weighted total
teachingExamples.text: Represent substantive passage of the gates needed for current actual adoption by D, N, P, J, and O. Necessary conditions can be illustrated as A⇒D∧N∧P∧J∧O. If D=N=P=O=true and J=false, the conjunction remains false: excellence on four items cannot offset absent authority. The arrow states only this framework's necessary gates, not a converse implication of uniquely correct value or legal validity.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Boolean values abstract already examined concrete gates. Unknown is not true, and field existence is not substantive passage.
teachingExamples.boundary: A procedural-logic example, not an empirical law or authorization for real action.

questionAnswers.question: May one act directly when a prediction has 99% confidence and expert support?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Even highly reliable description still lacks proportionate material for explicit norms, protection, authority, and O1–O4.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 963–969.

questionAnswers.question: Can N1 alone imply selecting the minimum-harm option?
questionAnswers.answer: No. N1 only blocks overreach. Minimum harm must additionally be registered as an explicit principle and used to compare actual options; it cannot be hidden.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 937, 939, and 969; §14.1 and 14.4.

questionAnswers.question: Which is better in the construction A=(9,3), B=(5,5)?
questionAnswers.answer: State the objective first: total gain selects A; minimum gain selects B. Numbers cannot themselves determine objectives or execution permission.
questionAnswers.basis: Teaching construction and Chinese source line 973.

questionAnswers.question: Without actual execution permission, is even criticism of options prohibited?
questionAnswers.answer: No. An analytical recommendation for deliberation may state explicit norms, evidence, and costs, but cannot execute a real action requiring permission.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 963; §15.1.

questionAnswers.question: Do filling in all ten PF names count as passing?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Check applicability, actual mechanisms, evidence, responsibility, validity periods, and reachable correction. Relevant gates cannot be mere strings.

questionAnswers.question: Does choosing inaction remove existing maintenance responsibilities?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Inaction means only not adding this candidate action. Existing independent duties and changing risks must still be registered.
questionAnswers.basis: §14.4, Chinese source line 3082.

4.15.title: 4.15 Composition Conditions and Evidence Routes
4.15.lead: These three conditional trees resemble route maps: starting from an evidenced point, each move toward a stronger conclusion requires corresponding additional material. The “+” signs do not mean that putting several names together automatically establishes a mechanism.
explanation: Chinese source line 977 calls this a “conditional tree”; line 1002 immediately limits it: “Merely listing G-instance names does not constitute sufficient conditions for a mechanism” (both translated from the Chinese). The trees are compressed indexes of earlier contracts and cannot be interpreted apart from them. For example, omitting repetition of all method gates, preselected criteria, task comparisons, and valid instance scopes does not remove those responsibilities. Each arrow points only to a bounded result that may be registered once the complete conditions are met. [T-415; T-contract]

The first tree begins with a G1-instance, an object/variable bridge, and a G2-instance. G1 supports conditional gain from the candidate grouping for a given task; G2 supports the effect of a specified channel. The object bridge makes the two bodies of material genuinely connect on the same object, variables, scale, window, and outcome. They cannot be joined merely because both say “organization” or “effect.” If objects differ, units are incompatible, or an upstream output is not the downstream input, the combined conclusion of a “candidate channel dependent on the specified organization” is not obtained. [T-415; T-G1; T-G2; T-chain]

Along the first return route, effective feedback requires additional checks of the return channel, temporal order, changed fields, and no-return or blockage counterfactuals. Feedback need only change at least one subsequent state, probability, or constraint; it need not leave a persistent historical trace and does not automatically mean something good or beneficial. Moving further toward learning, the carrier branch adds a current update carrier, retention or updating rules, subsequent use across multiple rounds, prespecified task comparisons, and causal evidence covering that window. “Feedback occurred” cannot replace “it was later actually used and changed task outcomes.” [T-415; T-C3; T-history]

Historical-increment feedback learning additionally requires G3, retainable updates, repeated rounds, and prespecified out-of-sample task comparisons. G3 tests whether history retains a conditional increment given the registered current representation; predictive and causal forms cannot be mixed. When the current state already carries all relevant historical information, carrier learning may still have independent grounds. Lack of G3 support blocks only the historical-increment route; it neither establishes the carrier route nor denies learning in general. Routes must not be switched after seeing results to rescue a claim, and known current states must not be deliberately omitted to manufacture an increment. [T-C3; T-history]

Another branch of the first tree combines G4a/G4b with D3/E5 mappings. The slash denotes different routes according to a preselected subtype: G4a asks about conditional increments from excluded scale variables; G4b asks about object or intervention conversion. It does not mean either can rescue success if it happens to “look significant.” Source and target scales, mappings, losses, comparison models, one preselected criterion, thresholds, and null-conclusion rules are required. Method gates are not empirical causes; crossing scales does not make higher scales truer or automatically confer wider permissions. [T-415; T-G4; T-D3]

The second tree moves from G2 and a mapping of demand/capacity of the same type to a candidate instantaneous overload. Matching types includes appropriate types, units, time windows, and accounting positions; total monthly capacity cannot answer whether a particular node is congested during a particular hour. Further claims of cumulative damage or delayed recovery require a current carrier, how load enters its state, accumulation/recovery across windows, subsequent effects, and proportionate causal comparison. An instantaneous gap itself proves neither persistent damage nor inevitable collapse. [T-415; T-C5]

The historical-increment branch of the load tree additionally requires G3 and a locatable historical carrier, addressing extra historical quantities beyond the current state. If current damage sufficiently explains subsequent recovery, an evidenced carrier recovery process may still be supported, but this is not a positive G3 result. A carrier's existence does not prove subsequent effects, and a positive G3 result cannot replace evidence for a specific carrier, window, and bridge. Current mechanisms, historical formation, and conditional residuals are three questions that may have different answers. [T-history; T-C5]

The third tree begins with D1 plus V, D, R, the next round, repeated rounds, and competition from drift, permitting registration of a variation–differential retention–reproduction pattern within a bounded environment. D1 defines a minimal grammar of change; it does not prove that the pattern has occurred in the world. V must distinguish variation in advance, D checks differential outcomes under comparable conditions, and R checks entry into later rounds and rechecks it. Competing explanations include drift, shared external causes, sampling, and a one-time shock. G2 is not imposed on the basic pattern; it is added only when a specified retention/reproduction channel is claimed. A historical-path candidate across rounds additionally requires G3 of the relevant type, but retention still does not imply superiority, a subject's intentions, or governance authorization. [T-415; T-C8]

Composition also has three noninterchangeable kinds of success: whether functional conversions give the same final answer; whether causal effects connect within jointly supported conditions in the same cases; and whether tasks can be jointly executed under shared resources. Positive average effects on every local edge do not guarantee a positive whole-chain effect; individual feasibility of every task does not guarantee joint feasibility before the same deadline. Conversely, when an existing design independently identifies a bounded total effect, every microscopic process need not first be exhausted before that effect can be retained. Additional connections are needed only when added uses—manipulating mediators, transferring across domains, or assigning responsibility—actually depend on them. [T-chain; T-composition]

Gap reports should be localized: identify the missing item, the branch it blocks, and narrower conclusions that retain independent support. Without multi-round evidence, stop at effective feedback; missing G3 does not erase evidenced carrier learning; without examining drift, a one-time difference cannot be registered as a C8 pattern. Even when conditions are complete, register only the bounded result under the specific contract. Even if a set of G1–G4 instances all pass, S0–S6 stage classification, direction, value, responsibility, choice, and authorization still require their own contracts. “All root questions passed” cannot become a universal closure stamp. [T-415; T-C12]
argumentSteps: First choose the bounded result in question and find its prerequisite route through the three trees.
Check each instance's actual eligibility and correspondence of objects, variables, scales, outcomes, and windows—not just its name.
Supply the return, carrier, multi-round, comparable-quantity, scale-mapping, V/D/R, or other conditions and method gates genuinely required by that branch.
Distinguish current-carrier transmission from historical increments beyond the registered current representation; do not automatically apply G3 because a label contains “learning” or “cumulative.”
Check joint responses, interfaces, temporal order, and resource constraints; local effects and individual feasibility do not automatically establish composition.
When incomplete, explain local blockages and independent results still retained; even when complete, register only contract-bounded conclusions.
Stages, values, responsibility, and actual adoption follow separate classification, normative, and procedural routes; they do not follow from the trees.

caseNotes.title: 1999 MCO: interface requirements exist, but connections still need verification
caseNotes.text: NASA's Phase I investigation report records that ground-based SM_FORCES outputs should have used N·s under the interface specification, but actually provided lbf·s. Downstream navigation used the data according to the expected units, which the report identified as the accident's root cause. This section adds the observation that an object/variable bridge must check actual delivery and use: an interface document and functional names at both ends do not mean that quantities are interpreted consistently along the actual chain.

teachingExamples.title: Original mathematical counterexample expanded: positive edge means, zero whole-chain effect
teachingExamples.text: Let type s be 0 or 1 with equal probability, with binary treatment a and mediator m, m(a)=a(1−s), and y(a,m)=sm. When s=0, treatment changes m from 0 to 1, but y remains 0. When s=1, m is 0 for every a; directly setting m could change y, but this is not a change actually brought about by a. Thus the average effect of treatment on m is (1+0)/2=1/2, and the average effect of directly setting m on y is (0+1)/2=1/2. Yet the natural chain gives y(a,m(a))=sa(1−s)=0, so the whole-chain effect is 0 for both types.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Exact structural equations, equal weighting of two types, and separation of direct intervention on m from natural transmission; entirely a formal construction from the original text.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not estimate effects in real populations. It only refutes unconditional multiplication, not total effects identified by independently qualified designs.

teachingExamples.title: Original mathematical counterexample expanded: shared deadline and capacity
teachingExamples.text: Tasks A and B each occupy one complete time period and must both finish before the end of period one. Period-one capacity is only 1, so required capacity 2 exceeds available capacity 1, and any schedule completes at most one task. Each is feasible alone; jointly they are infeasible. If period-one capacity becomes 2, they can finish in parallel. If valid grounds permit moving B's deadline to period two and period-two capacity is 1, they can finish sequentially. Merely increasing period-two capacity while retaining both original deadlines cannot repair the period-one constraint violation.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Unit tasks are indivisible, capacity units are identical across periods, there are no other resources, and advance processing is unavailable. Changing the deadline is only a conditional counterfactual, not actual authorization.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not establish real demand, capacity, or permission to delay; later resources cannot offset an earlier time limit.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: history transmitted through the current state
teachingExamples.text: Let a binary historical input H first form S=H, with future Y=S and no other path or noise. Intervening on H changes Y through S, and current S also determines Y. But given S, Y is already determined, so knowing H additionally does not improve prediction. Historical formation, current-carrier effects, and “historical increment conditional on S” may therefore respectively be present, present, and zero. If only correlation is observed and these structural equations are unknown, this causal conclusion is not yet available.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The equations and intervention semantics are artificially specified; the registered current state actually includes S, measured precisely.
teachingExamples.boundary: This model is not treated as actual learning or a G3 instance, nor does it permit deliberately omitting a known S from real-world analysis.

questionAnswers.question: If G1 and G2 both have research support, can they immediately be combined into the same organizational channel?
questionAnswers.answer: No. An object/variable bridge, corresponding windows and outcomes, and the specific contracts' additional gates are still required.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 979–1002.

questionAnswers.question: If effective feedback is evidenced but there is no material on multi-round use, where should the conclusion stop?
questionAnswers.answer: Retain bounded effective feedback; the learning branch remains a candidate or insufficiently evidenced.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 981–986; C3.

questionAnswers.question: If the current carrier is sufficient and G3 is unsupported, can we say that learning does not exist?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Carrier learning may be supported by independent evidence of retention, use, tasks, and causation. G3 failure also cannot establish carrier learning in reverse.

questionAnswers.question: If both average edge effects are 1/2, must the whole chain equal 1/4?
questionAnswers.answer: No. In the equally weighted type counterexample, the actual total chain effect is 0 because different types carry the effects of the two segments.
questionAnswers.basis: §2.4.2; Appendix C.12.

questionAnswers.question: Can sufficient capacity in period two recover a period-one deadline?
questionAnswers.answer: No, unless the deadline itself is independently and validly changed; later resources do not alter the original period's constraints.
questionAnswers.basis: Appendix C.12.

questionAnswers.question: Must the basic C8 pattern first have G2?
questionAnswers.answer: No. V/D/R, the next round, repeated rounds, and competing explanations require independent evidence; G2 is added only for claims of a specific mechanism.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source lines 997–1000.

4.15.diagramBrief: Four static diagrams explain the first tree, the two load routes, C8's independent pattern and added mechanisms, and the joint-response/resource counterexamples. Arrows indicate additional evidential responsibilities, not that empirical causation has occurred. Future branch switching would only highlight added material and retained conclusions, without automatically issuing a mechanism finding or authorization.

4.16.title: 4.16 Scope and Stopping Points of Empirical Judgments
4.16.lead: This section requires each conclusion to stop where the evidence can actually reach. Stopping does not mean refusing all judgment; it means precisely stating what is known, what holds only within a model, and which gaps cannot yet be crossed.
explanation: Chinese source line 1006 limits empirical judgments as “constrained by the object, scale, time window, evidence, and unit of extrapolation” (translated from the Chinese). A conclusion should simultaneously specify its object, representation and granularity, temporal scope, evidential material, and intended population or task for generalization. Writing only “verified” erases these limits. The same evidence may support a narrow proposition without supporting a broader one. [T-416; T-evidence]

G, C, and F have different roles. G question families organize testable specific factual claims that instances must answer; C records established results or combined mechanism conditions, requiring corresponding eligibility in particular branches; F provides proofs under given state domains, mappings, targets, operations, and logical premises. C12 is also a bridge through normative procedures; it must not be treated as an empirical mechanism merely because it is numbered C. Numbering marks responsibilities, not certification of all three categories by the same experiment or truth rule. [T-416；T-roles；T-C12]

Both the power and the boundaries of formal proof must be retained. If premises and derivation are valid, a within-model conclusion does not disappear because no real-world experiment has been performed; one exact counterexample also suffices to refute the unconditional inference it targets. Applying it to reality requires separate evidence for measurements, variable mappings, state domains, errors, and operational conditions. Repeated computation of the same constructed model does not continually add independent empirical samples; numerical enumeration also covers only the finite domain and precision actually specified. [T-formal]

Definitions, numbering, examples, and internal explanations cannot determine whether a real mechanism exists. Defining a process as ‘learning’ does not establish that it actually retains updates, uses them across multiple rounds, or produces a historical conditional increment. Registering a table as an instance likewise does not establish that its gates have substantively passed. Conversely, historical archives and existing studies not registered in this framework may still support domain conclusions under their own designs; formal instance eligibility cannot become a universal truth gate for all knowledge. [T-416；T-domain]

Stopping points must also distinguish ‘not studied,’ ‘evidence unresolved,’ and ‘an appropriately supported null conclusion.’ Failure to meet a positive criterion usually permits only unsupported or unresolved status. If prefrozen equivalence/sufficiency rules, sensitivity, and tolerances have not actually passed, no significant difference cannot be rewritten as zero effect. Failure of an identification assumption should narrow explanations depending on it, without canceling descriptions or bounded total effects that have other independent grounds. [T-instance；T-estimand]

Extrapolation requires appropriate bridging. A study sample is not the whole world, its original window is not forever, and an average result is not every individual's result. When adding objects, uses, interventions, or horizons, ask whether the original comparison still covers them. Shared words, identical indicators, or visual similarity cannot transplant causal conclusions. Nor must every microscopic mechanism be exhausted before retaining a narrow result identified by a qualified design. [T-evidence；T-estimand；T-analogy]

For further evaluations of value, responsibility, sacrifice, choice, or action, the source requires adding human-domain classification, normative reasons, and O1–O4 procedures. H is not an undifferentiated set of axioms about human nature: H2/H3 classify, H1/H4/H5 require instance evidence, and H6 has a normative-boundary role. Recommendations for deliberation and actual adoption remain separate; the latter additionally requires complete C12, PF, J, and operational procedures. Empirical correctness itself grants no authority to decide for people. [T-416；T-roles；T-C12；T-task]
argumentSteps: Separate the proposed conclusion into descriptive, causal, formal, classificatory, and normative/action components.
For the empirical component, specify the object, scale, window, evidence design, and unit of extrapolation.
For the formal component, state its premises, proof, and whether mapping to the real object has been checked, retaining its conditional status.
Under the specific G/C contract, distinguish supported, unsupported or unresolved, appropriately supported null conclusions, and unevaluated status; do not replace testing with a title.
Narrow only conclusions affected by the gap; retain other independent grounds.
When value or action conclusions are needed, add the corresponding human-domain, normative, and procedural responsibilities; otherwise stop at the existing description and bounded explanation.

caseLinks.title: The 2018 replication project: denominators and success criteria must not disappear

caseNotes.title: The 2018 replication project: denominators and success criteria must not disappear
caseNotes.text: Camerer et al. replicated 21 systematically selected social-science experiments published in Nature and Science during 2010–2015. The original abstract reports that 13 met the metric of a significant result in the same direction as the original study; other replication metrics produced different counts. This section adds the point that results must be reported with their selected study set and criterion. The fraction 13/21 cannot be renamed the proportion of true propositions in all of social science.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Abstract of Camerer et al.'s original paper, as hosted by PubMed
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Nature Human Behaviour2:637–644, published online 2018-08-27, DOI10.1038/s41562-018-0399-z; first two paragraphs of the Abstract.
caseNotes.boundary: Only the original abstract and bibliographic information were read; the 21 experiments were not individually redone. The fraction 13/21 is not the truth rate of all studies, and missing this criterion does not directly prove a zero effect or misconduct. This is the same study as S-4-1, not independent evidence; this section only adds questions about scope and metrics.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: how far a proof reaches, and why a changed task requires rechecking
teachingExamples.text: Let state x=(x1,x2), representation π(x)=x1+x2, and task q(x)=2(x1+x2). Define r(z)=2z; then for every specified state, r(π(x))=2(x1+x2)=q(x), a complete algebraic proof. If actual use changes to q′(x)=x1, states (1,0) and (0,1) both have π=1 but require answers 1 and 0 respectively. The same r′(1) cannot supply two different answers, so q′ cannot be recovered from π alone.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The state space contains these two states, numbers are exact reals, and there is no measurement error; both task and representation are constructed assumptions.
teachingExamples.boundary: The first proof remains valid; the second task does not satisfy its premises. Whether real variables actually correspond through these equations still requires evidence; calculation cannot replace investigation.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a scope statement for a qualified conclusion
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a fictional study measures an output difference between schemes A and B only for selected equipment, in a specified load range, at site A during one month. An appropriate statement retains these qualifications and uncertainty. Directly rewriting it as ‘A applies to all equipment and is always better’ adds four kinds of unsupported claims: object, time, load, and value. Extended research questions may be proposed, but they cannot be backfilled as already verified.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The study, location, and results are entirely hypothetical; no real data are supplied.
teachingExamples.boundary: This exercises scope statements. It neither claims that this study exists nor prescribes the same design for every real study.

questionAnswers.question: If a formal proposition has been proved, has it thereby been established that a real system satisfies it?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The proof's conditional conclusion holds, but whether the real system's variables, domain, operations, and errors conform still requires independent verification.
questionAnswers.basis: §2.1.2 and Chinese source line 1006.

questionAnswers.question: In the mathematical sum-representation example, why does changing the target to x1 fail?
questionAnswers.answer: The same representation value 1 corresponds to different answers 1 and 0; a single input cannot recover two target values. This is insufficient information after the task changes.
questionAnswers.basis: The explicit algebra and two-state counterexample in this lesson.

questionAnswers.question: Are all older studies invalid if they lack this framework's G registration?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Retain domain conclusions under their original designs. Formal G eligibility cannot be granted automatically, but neither does its absence negate existing grounds.

questionAnswers.question: Does a 13/21 result under one replication measure mean that only 62% of an entire discipline is true?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The denominator is that selected study set and the metric is that replication criterion; neither covers all studies or directly defines factual truth.
questionAnswers.basis: The original P-Camerer abstract and this section's extrapolation boundary.

questionAnswers.question: If experimental results are reliable, can one directly require someone to sacrifice?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Value, responsibility, protection, and bounded procedures each have their own requirements; empirical conclusions do not themselves create obligations or authority to act.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 1006; C12.

4.17.title: 4.17 Common method constraints
4.17.lead: The ‘laws’ here are methodological constraints that analysis should follow, not natural laws about how the world necessarily operates. They must also face a question in return: after actual use, do they really reduce errors and improve understanding at a proportionate cost?
explanation: Chinese source line 1010 explicitly states that methodological constraints govern how analysts construct, check, and use models and ‘do not claim how the world must operate’ (translated from Chinese). This section therefore adds no new empirical causal mechanism; it requires model use to retain boundaries of tasks, evidence, and authority. [T-417]

The three numbered subsections respectively require joint declaration of task and representation, traceability of material identity and scope of support, and separate establishment of facts, values, and eligibility to act. The fourth subsection then subjects the rules themselves to evaluation: they may be challenged and revised, and cannot escape comparison by calling themselves rigorous. [T-417]

Following rules can make analysis more transparent, but transparent records alone do not prove a judgment true or a method beneficial on balance. The source identifies actual error reduction, gains in understanding, and costs of use as comparative responsibilities. Without an appropriate comparison, one may describe only intended uses and verified local results. [T-eval]
argumentSteps: First distinguish methodological requirements governing analysis from empirical propositions describing the world.
Use the three laws to check task, material, and actual-adoption boundaries.
Separately design a comparison with a common task and budget to evaluate the method's own benefits and prices to be paid.

distinctions.leftText: Records are traceable.
distinctions.rightTitle: The method is effective on balance
distinctions.rightText: Actual comparisons of errors, understanding, and costs are still required.

Teaching counterexample: a report has complete fields but an incorrect core calculation. Completeness cannot settle correctness.

Is a complex set of rules sufficient proof that it is worth adopting?

questionAnswers.question: Are the common method constraints new empirical root propositions?
questionAnswers.answer: No. They govern the use of analytical methods, without claiming how the world necessarily operates.

questionAnswers.answer: No. Actual errors, understanding, and costs must be compared.

4.17.1.title: 4.17.1 Law 1: task and representation must be declared together
4.17.1.lead: To judge a representation, first ask what it is for. Omitting details need not impair the task, and retaining many details need not suffice for dynamic prediction or intervention.
explanation: Chinese source line 1014 requires binding objects, stratification, scale granularity, and target variables to the task, observational position, horizon, environment, and use. Judging ‘is this summary sufficient?’ must include the target: answering a static question, predicting several steps of evolution, and comparing a permitted operation may require different distinctions. [T-law1]

A transformation must separately state what it preserves, which states it merges, which variables it omits, and which estimates or assumptions it adds. Losslessness cannot be presumed, nor can the reverse claim that all compression causes task-relevant loss. If the target requires only a total, that total may suffice; if the target depends on an individual's location, the total may merge different answers. The method seeks to retain distinctions necessary for the task in question, not recover every task-irrelevant detail. [T-law1；T-F1]

Recovery of static answers, closure under natural dynamics, and closure under permitted interventions are different tests. A representation sufficient to answer the current total does not thereby determine the next period's total; that task also asks whether merged states update into the same representation. When new actions are allowed, action implementability and macro outcomes of different micro implementations may also need rechecking. [T-law1；T-F2]

Transformation order also cannot be presumed equivalent based on names. Rounding before adjustment may differ from adjusting before rounding; some mappings do commute on a bounded domain. Fix the actual versions of both operations, the input domain, and the final target before comparing them. One noncommuting example must not be expanded into ‘no transformations ever commute.’ [T-law1；T-G4]

Changes in horizon, environment, or use justify rechecking; they do not automatically establish that the old representation was always wrong. Supported success on the old task may remain, with distinctions required by the new task added. Variable measurement, error, information-acquisition timing, and operational permission in real models still need independent checks; formal sufficiency does not mean timely availability. [T-formal; T-law1]
argumentSteps: Register task, object, representation, target, observation position, environment, horizon, and use together.
List what is preserved, merged, omitted, and additionally assumed.
Separately test static recovery, dynamic progression, permitted operations, and conversion order.
Add only distinctions necessary for the current task; recheck corresponding responsibilities after changes.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: losing detail need not mean losing the task
teachingExamples.text: Let the state set be {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)}, with representation π storing only the sum of the two numbers. For counting task q=x1+x2, output π directly, correctly in all four states. For q′=x1, π=1 corresponds to both (0,1) and (1,0), so π cannot uniquely answer. Preserving the first component as an additional distinction supports q′; failure on one task does not imply that all compression is useless.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Binary finite states, exact observation, and a deterministic single query.
teachingExamples.boundary: A model illustration, not measurement of real-world data-compression quality.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: order must be calculated
teachingExamples.text: Let R(x)=floor(x) round downward and A(x)=x+0.6. At x=0.6, R(A(x))=floor(1.2)=1, whereas A(R(x))=0+0.6=0.6, so the two compositions differ. Changing operations or restricting the domain requires rechecking; one difference cannot establish that all mappings fail to commute.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Real-valued inputs and exact arithmetic; the two functions are defined in the stated versions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Only noncommutativity of functions; it neither automatically certifies real-world G4 nor grants intervention permission.

counterexamples.text: Source boundary: neither assume conversions are lossless nor assert that every conversion necessarily loses task-relevant information.
counterexamples.effect: Representation loss must be tied to the task.

counterexamples.text: Mathematical counterexample: a sum representation preserves counting but loses the first component; different tasks yield different conclusions.
counterexamples.effect: The same representation has different capabilities for different tasks.

counterexamples.text: Mathematical counterexample: rounding down and adding 0.6 do not commute at x=0.6; this example constrains only the specified operations, not every commuting case.
counterexamples.effect: Order requires checking case by case.

questionAnswers.question: Is keeping only a total necessarily unscientific?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily; it may suffice for counting but fail for a task depending on individual position.
questionAnswers.basis: Chinese source line 1014 and the teaching construction.

questionAnswers.question: Does recoverability of the current query guarantee prediction after intervention?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Check closure separately for the actual permitted operations, implementation, and updates.

questionAnswers.question: Why do R and A differ in order in the example?
questionAnswers.answer: Adding first gives 1.2, then rounding gives 1; rounding first gives 0, then adding gives 0.6.
questionAnswers.basis: The explicit functions and input.

4.17.2.title: 4.17.2 Rule 2: material status and scope of support must be traceable
4.17.2.lead: The same material may be carefully recalculated and yield new understanding; processing it ten times does not make ten independent observations. Reports, simulations, and execution results likewise support only their respective levels.
explanation: Chinese source line 1018 lists reports, observations, model beliefs, formal proofs, simulation outputs, and execution receipts, requiring preservation of their distinct statuses. A report is someone else's organization and judgment of material; an observation is a record under a protocol; a belief is a model's judgment; a proof is a derivation under premises; a simulation runs a specified model; a receipt documents an operation only within what it actually records. These can support one another but cannot be exchanged without labeling. [T-law2; T-evidence]

Every inference should identify new information, reused premises and rules, and what the conclusion adds to its inputs. Recalculating raw data, redrawing plots, or changing algorithms may reveal errors, boundaries, or better proofs: these are real gains in knowledge. The source remains the same dataset and cannot count as multiple independent empirical datasets. [T-law2; T-formal]

Recursive simulation can use one round's state as the next round's input, lengthening the model trajectory; recursion depth itself cannot increase real-world support or capability level. The model world is still generated by the given equations; adding steps may expose consequences within the model or accumulate error, and must be registered separately from new real-world measurements. [T-law2; T-F5]

Independence also concerns shared raw data, the same samples, common measuring equipment, model-training material, and personnel procedures. Two reports with different authors may cite the same observation. Source counts are not independent-evidence counts; identify overlaps and differences, reducing the force of mutual corroboration where necessary without erasing the original value of individual materials. [T-law2; T-evidence]

Execution receipts must not be overextended either. Successful sending differs from the recipient understanding; editing a draft differs from an operating rule taking effect. A recommendation report can indeed propose a recommendation without establishing that it was implemented or effective long-term. Conversely, failure to find implementation evidence does not make an attributable recommendation text nonexistent. [T-law2; T-writeback]
argumentSteps: Label each item's generation process, version, time, and observational or model status.
For every conversion, state new information, premises and rules, and the support ceiling.
Identify shared original material; do not count repeated computation as independent observation.
Check separate grounds for simulation outputs versus new real-world records, and recommendations versus actual execution.
