caseLinks.title: GAO explicitly limits the denominator for ‘fully restored’

caseNotes.title: GAO explicitly limits the denominator for ‘fully restored’
caseNotes.text: GAO’s 2019 report relays PREPA’s statement that power was restored after about 11 months to customers able to receive it safely. The report immediately explains that this does not mean all pre-disaster customers were restored, since some buildings remained unsuitable for safe connection. The original report actively preserved this scope limit; this guide is not exposing fraud.
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed pp. 6–7, Status of electricity restoration and Figure 1 note
caseNotes.boundary: This distinguishes the technically eligible denominator from the pre-disaster customer population; it estimates neither the number nor needs of excluded people and does not evaluate the legitimacy of particular actions.

argumentSteps: Before results, fix the population, temporal definition, and estimand, separating fixed cohort from current cross-section.
List unit-level membership, partitions, exclusions, entries and exits, weights, and missing states.
Recalculate totals or rates under public rules and retain enough information to trace source units.
Use task-appropriate alternative weights/rules to check sensitivity; report heterogeneity and losses separately.
If different definitions answer different questions, explain them side by side; if they claim the same question but conflict, examine selection and inference.
Retain those who lose visibility; do not jump from aggregate support to actions upon members.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: cross-sectional improvement with an unchanged cohort
teachingExamples.text: Four baseline scores are (0,0,10,10), with mean 5. Later, the first two people leave while the last two remain at 10; the current cross-sectional mean becomes 10. If all four people’s scores actually remain unchanged, the fixed-cohort mean remains 5. If the movers’ later scores are unknown, the follow-up cohort mean is unknown; they cannot be assigned zero as if measured, nor deleted before claiming that all four improved.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Identities are fixed and scores are fictional indicators with the same dimension; the second scenario explicitly has follow-up material and the third explicitly lacks it.
teachingExamples.boundary: Moving away is not attributed to a policy, and missing people’s actual needs are not set to zero.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: crude and standardized rates reverse while answering different questions
teachingExamples.text: Suppose A has 90/100 successes in the easy group and 1/10 in the hard group, yielding crude rate 91/110≈82.73%; B has 19/20 in the easy group and 20/100 in the hard group, yielding 39/120=32.5%. B is higher within both groups (95%>90%, 20%>10%). With reference weights of one-half each for easy and hard, A is 50% and B is 57.5%. The crude rate describes existing composition; the standardized rate describes fixed composition. They cannot be claimed as the same estimand.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Entirely fictional complete counts, two mutually exclusive and exhaustive groups, comparable outcomes, and reference weights fixed beforehand at one-half each.
teachingExamples.boundary: No causal effect is identified; the success rates are not used to screen actual people.

counterexamples.text: Mean 5 is written as ‘all members reach at least 5’; the source vector could be (0,10).
counterexamples.effect: The same aggregate value does not imply each person’s attribute; action upon members cannot follow directly from an average.

counterexamples.text: Delete nonapplicants, obtain a 100% applicant service rate, then report that all residents’ needs have been met.
counterexamples.effect: This changes the denominator and treats unobserved needs as zero; the original description cannot support the expanded claim.

questionAnswers.question: Does restoring power to every customer able to connect safely mean that all pre-disaster customers have power restored?
questionAnswers.answer: No; their membership conditions differ. Separately record the states of original customers unable to connect safely.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If two weighted rates point in opposite directions, must someone have calculated incorrectly?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. First check estimands and reference weights; different questions may both be answered correctly, whereas robustness claims for the same question require further scrutiny.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: How should the cohort mean be reported when movers have no follow-up records?
questionAnswers.answer: Retain unknown follow-up states and report coverage/missingness; zero-filling or deletion cannot masquerade as complete follow-up.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: After an aggregation bridge passes, may action be taken directly upon every person in a group with a worse mean?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Individual action requires corresponding material and independent normative, protection, and authority conditions.

5.5.2.title: 5.5.2 M02 Nesting
5.5.2.lead: “A team belongs to an organization” may be a clear descriptive fact, but it explains neither how the organization affects the team nor any inherent authority over team members.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1164–1175; original anchor section-5-5-2. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “boundary–membership embedding.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

M02 first checks boundary and membership embedding: who belongs to which level, when boundaries apply, whether membership overlaps, how exit works, and where cross-boundary interfaces lie. Two departments sharing a supervisor, building, or environment does not by itself establish membership embedding.

Descriptive nesting answers only those mapping questions and may hold without any identified cross-level causation. For example, finite set A={a,b} is indeed a subset of B={a,b,c}; that inclusion itself specifies no variable update law.

Cross-level causation separately requires channels, temporal order, and proportionate comparisons. Empirical effects follow G2 and CAUSAL; cross-scale mappings follow D3/E5. Add the corresponding G4-instance only for further claims of scale-closure failure, object conversion, or intervention conversion. Not all cross-level causation first requires a positive G4 result.

An insufficient increment after controlling current state and shared environment may reflect inadequate measurement, design, window, or precision, or a representation that already absorbs the relevant effect. A bounded null conclusion requires the predetermined null rule and equivalence/sufficiency, power/sensitivity, and tolerance checks to pass. Unresolved causation does not erase descriptive nesting.

The actual record must uniquely select descriptive_nesting, cross_layer_causal, object_conversion, or intervention_conversion, bound to the descriptive, causal, object-conversion, or intervention-conversion mode respectively. A boundary diagram supporting the first branch cannot be copied as support for the other three. Higher-level position also creates no priority of truth, lower-level obligation, or expansion of J.

argumentSteps: Fix objects, membership, boundaries, overlap, exit, and interfaces, and check the descriptive mapping.
If studying nesting only, stop at the descriptive branch and mark G-specific fields inapplicable with reasons.
If studying cross-level effects, separately specify variables, channels, timing, interventions/comparisons, and competing explanations.
Discharge G2/CAUSAL and D3/E5 responsibilities separately. Enter the corresponding G4 only for additional closure or conversion claims.
When no causal increment is supported, assess under the null checks; nonsignificance is not no effect.
Retain separate statuses for descriptive facts and unresolved causation, and separately check normative and J claims.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: identical nesting can have two different dynamics
teachingExamples.text: Let A={a,b}⊂B={a,b,c}, with organizational input u∈{0,1}. Model one keeps a and b's next states unchanged; model two sets both next states equal to u. Inclusion is identical in both, but cross-level effects differ. Membership embedding therefore cannot uniquely determine causation.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Finite sets and update rules are entirely artificial. The do(u) comparison in model two is only a formal demonstration.
teachingExamples.boundary: No actual organization is claimed to follow these rules, and no formal G2 or G4 instance is generated.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: sharing a supervisor does not mean membership inclusion
teachingExamples.text: Fictional teams A={person A,person B} and B={person C,person D} both report to supervisor E, but neither team's members are contained in the other. The diagram can register two reporting edges and a common superior node. It cannot draw team A inside team B or infer from E's presence that A has managerial authority over B.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Team sets and reporting relations are hypothetical; reporting edges are separate from membership edges.
teachingExamples.boundary: Shows only differences between relation types, without judging actual authorization.

counterexamples.text: Only an organizational membership tree is uploaded, yet cross_layer_causal is registered as supported.
counterexamples.effect: The tree may support descriptive nesting but lacks channels of effect and proportionate comparisons.

counterexamples.text: After a nonsignificant controlled result, the already verified membership inclusion is revoked and “no cross-level effect” is declared.
counterexamples.effect: Causal results do not rewrite description. A bounded null conclusion still requires independent null checks.

counterexamples.text: Requiring all cross-level causation first to prove object-identity conversion.
counterexamples.effect: This unnecessarily imposes G4's additional responsibility on every causal claim, misreading the section's branches.

questionAnswers.question: Does A being contained in B establish that B causes A to change?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Separate effect rules or empirical channels and comparisons are required. The same inclusion relation can have different dynamics.

questionAnswers.question: When does cross-level causation additionally require G4?
questionAnswers.answer: When additionally claiming scale-closure failure, object conversion, or intervention conversion. G4 cannot replace ordinary cross-level causation's G2/CAUSAL and D3/E5 responsibilities.

questionAnswers.question: If no conditional increment is detected, what should be stated next?
questionAnswers.answer: Check the null rule and three checks. If insufficient, retain unsupported or unresolved status rather than automatically announcing no effect.

5.5.3.title: 5.5.3 M03 Network propagation
5.5.3.lead: Knowing that two points connect establishes only a possible route. Whether something actually travels that route, arrives in time, and has sufficient capacity are separate facts to check.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1176–1181; original anchor section-5-5-3. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “transmission along temporal paths.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

M03 expands static links into temporal paths: what are nodes and directed edges, how are weights and capacities measured, where are sampling boundaries, which routes and alternatives are candidates, and what delays and losses occur along each segment? A message reaching the endpoint does not reconstruct the sequence of intermediate nodes.

Connection or synchrony supplies only a propagation candidate. Two people receiving the same notice simultaneously may have forwarded it to each other or both received it from a common source. An unchanged endpoint after cutting an edge may reflect an alternative route or insensitive measurement. Without passing null-conclusion checks, retain unsupported_or_undecided.

Strong ties, a central bridge position, high centrality, and actually mobilizable resources are different dimensions. Whether acquaintances will refer someone, channel capacity, costs, and deadlines may determine task usability. Counting contacts or drawing an attractive network is insufficient.

Four contacts at four institutions may share one message source, so four social-support relations do not equal four independent pieces of factual evidence. Conversely, one contact may provide the only real referral opportunity; few contacts do not mean no resource.

Sampling may miss weak ties, offline nodes, and bridges across networks. Disclose unobserved areas and candidate-only edges instead of drawing unknowns as absences. Centrality alone establishes neither intent, responsibility, nor authority to act; responsibility requires separate examination of participation, knowledge, and decision chains.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: an existing route can still miss the deadline
teachingExamples.text: A fictional message leaves S at t=0. Delays are S→A: 2, A→T: 3, S→B: 1, B→T: 8. Each edge can carry one message, with no queuing or loss. The two arrival times are 5 and 9. At deadline t=6, the first route is usable and the second is not. Recording only connectivity between S and T loses a task-critical distinction.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Delays are fixed nonnegative numbers; the message may use either route; the deadline includes t=6. No actual device is simulated.
teachingExamples.boundary: Connectivity is not timely reachability. Reality also requires checking queues, capacity, and changes.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: four forwards are not four independent observations
teachingExamples.text: Source S generates one report, which persons A, B, C, and D each forward to T. T has four contacts, but all four messages depend on S's same observation. Four transmission paths and support relations may be recorded; there remains only S's single independent observation of the original event. If person E independently observes it, register that source and its error separately instead of counting evidence by total contacts alone.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All people and events are fictional; all forwarding is assumed complete and source-traceable.
teachingExamples.boundary: Do not infer that actual contacts necessarily share a source; actual tracing is required.

counterexamples.text: After deleting S→A, the endpoint still receives a message, so the edge is declared forever ineffective; another route S→B→T actually remains.
counterexamples.effect: Alternative routes may explain the unchanged outcome. The task window and null checks are required; one cut cannot justify universal rejection.

counterexamples.text: The network's most central node is directly labeled the ultimately responsible person or lawful representative.
counterexamples.effect: Position is insufficient to determine knowledge, intent, decision responsibility, or J authority.

5.5.4.title: 5.5.4 M04 Temporal accumulation
5.5.4.lead: Numbers usually change over longer periods; the real question is under which time basis, window, and accumulation rule. Summing three days' events may be a correct description without proving an additional historical effect.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1182–1185; original anchor section-5-5-4. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “longitudinal composition with a window.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

M04 concerns longitudinal composition, not treating “it happened in the past” as a mechanism. Predetermine the clock, baseline, observation window, lag, duration required for persistence, and accumulation, decay, and recovery rules. Applying cumulative sums, rolling windows, or decaying stocks to the same input sequence yields different targets.

Cumulative event counts, current stocks, and future effects are not interchangeable. A count that only increases follows a counting rule; fatigue or inventory with recovery can decrease. Whether past inputs affect the future also depends on current carriers and target transitions. Comparing different quantities on one curve risks writing definition-driven trends as empirical mechanisms.

Common trends, seasonality, different cohorts, and alternative windows are necessary competing explanations. An increase over one period cannot alone be attributed to the specified accumulation channel. Changed results after a window change may reflect a changed estimand rather than the world suddenly having no effect. Disclose which comparisons still answer the same question.

Basic longitudinal composition does not establish G3 in advance. If current state records all relevant stocks, past inputs may affect the future through that carrier, while additional historical terms add nothing after controlling it. Link the corresponding G3-instance only when claiming a historical conditional increment beyond the current representation.

Disappearance of an effect after control or sensitivity to windows establishes only insufficient support for that positive claim. A bounded conclusion of “no accumulation” or “the current representation is sufficient” additionally requires a predetermined null decision rule and equivalence/sufficiency, power/sensitivity, and tolerance checks. Statistical nonsignificance is not proof of sufficiency.

caseNotes.title: Three days in Snow's table can be summed, but their definition cannot change
caseNotes.text: Snow's Table I lists “attacks in fatal cases” on September 6, 7, and 8, 1854 as 20, 28, and 12. Summing records within those three dates gives 60, a transparent recalculation by this lesson. The explanation after the table says some onset dates were inferred backward from illness duration. Thus 60 is neither deaths during those three days nor all infected people, and does not prove an additional historical mechanism.

argumentSteps: Fix whether the target is a count, a stock, or a future response, together with time units, baseline, window, and lag.
Disclose accumulation, decay, recovery, and persistence thresholds, ensuring that adjacent times use the same definitions.
Compare against shared trends, seasonality, cohorts, and proportionate alternative windows, explaining each change individually.
Identify which past effects the current carrier can preserve, avoiding conflation of carrier effects with additional historical increments.
Take on G3-instance responsibilities only when claiming a historical increment beyond the current representation.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: accumulation and decay are different targets
teachingExamples.text: Inputs u₀,u₁,u₂=(4,0,2), with baseline s₀=0. The rule sₜ₊₁=0.5sₜ+uₜ yields s₁=4, s₂=2, s₃=3; simple cumulative totals are 4,4,6. If the persistence threshold requires s≥3 for two consecutive steps, this sequence fails because the intermediate s₂=2. The intermediate time cannot be removed afterward to claim sustained attainment.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An exact deterministic model with equal time steps; decay 0.5, inputs, and thresholds are all artificially specified in advance.
teachingExamples.boundary: Proves only the calculation under this rule; it is not a measured cumulative effect in a body, device, or institution.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: different histories, the same current stock, the same future
teachingExamples.text: Again use sₜ₊₁=0.5sₜ+uₜ and s₀=0. History A with inputs (4,0) gives s₂=2; history B with inputs (0,2) also gives s₂=2. If future u₂ is 0 in both cases, both yield s₃=1. In this complete model, current s already suffices to predict the next step. History did form s, but retaining the two histories separately is unnecessary for calculating the future.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Current s is observed exactly, the rule is unchanged, and future inputs are identical; there is no hidden damage or difference in recovery parameters.
teachingExamples.boundary: One model cannot establish that real-world path dependence does not exist; if the current representation omits variables, the conclusion requires rechecking.

counterexamples.text: Calling a cumulative count's rise from 4 to 6 “current stock rising from 4 to 6,” although the model's actual stock is 4,2,3.
counterexamples.effect: The target variable has changed; cumulative totals and stocks require separate explanation.

counterexamples.text: After controlling for current stock, the historical coefficient is not significant, so someone claims that the past never affected the system.
counterexamples.effect: The past may already be written into the carrier; insufficient additional historical increment does not erase carrier formation.

questionAnswers.question: Why is the third-step stock not 6 in the first calculation?
questionAnswers.answer: At each step the rule first halves the existing stock, then adds new input. At the third step, 0.5×2+2=3; 6 is the cumulative count without decay.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does having a time series already provide G3?
questionAnswers.answer: No. G3 concerns an additional historical increment given the current representation; basic temporal composition does not establish it in advance.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If two histories reach the same s₂=2 and future inputs match, what happens next?
questionAnswers.answer: Both equal 1 under the fixed complete rule; this does not deny that both histories helped form the current state.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If the effect changes with the window, should one directly write “no accumulation”?
questionAnswers.answer: No. First check targets and competing explanations; a bounded null conclusion still requires the null rule and three gates.

All numbers belong to a fictional model. Basic temporal composition does not automatically establish G3, and the persistence window cannot be changed after seeing results.

5.5.5.title: 5.5.5 M05 Institutionalization
5.5.5.lead: An institution may actually exist while having serious governance problems. Acknowledging its existence allows accurate tracking of how it operates and affects people; this does not establish its legality, justification, or entitlement to continue.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1186–1191; original anchor: section-5-5-5; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “persistent institutional write-back.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

M05 concerns whether change is persistently written into records, roles, resource allocation, decision rules, or subsequent state transitions. A single verbal initiative may not yet form an institution; conversely, a rule with continuing execution and resources cannot be declared nonexistent simply because it is disputed or disliked.

This section requires separating five judgments: whether an institution factually exists, whether it is legally valid, whether it is normatively justified, whether protection holds, and whether it should continue. They may cite partly shared material but answer different questions. The existence of an institutional text is one piece of factual evidence; persistent effects also require subsequent records and cannot be established by a document's title alone.

Invalid authorization, insufficient participation, failed appeal or anti-retaliation mechanisms, and lack of rollback routes are grounds for findings of governance failure, normative dispute, and reduced action scope. They are not evidence that the institution does not exist. Accurately preserving existing rules and consequences is instead a prerequisite for accountability, stopping, and repair.

Institutional facts also do not automatically prove that the institution effectively improved outcomes. Studying causal effects requires separately selecting institutional_causal_effect and providing proportionate comparisons; claims of object or intervention conversion select institutional_object_conversion or institutional_intervention_conversion respectively.

When studying only factual existence, the branch is institutional_fact. Questions of “is it lawful,” “is it fair,” “is protection sufficient,” or “is it worth continuing” cannot masquerade as that branch's positive or null conclusions. Confirmed institutional existence and normative rejection can hold together; they should not be forced into a single overall success score.

distinctions.rightText: Requires independent verification under applicable law and permissions.

distinctions.leftText: Judgments concerning values, participation, and safeguards for affected people.
distinctions.rightText: An empirical-effect judgment; these judgments cannot substitute for one another.

distinctions.leftText: A question of normative choice, risks, and alternatives.
distinctions.rightTitle: Whether it existed in the past
distinctions.rightText: A historical-fact question; stopping it does not erase the past.

boundaries: This lesson provides no current legal opinion on any actual institution; approval records in historical reports do not replace a complete legal-validity review.
Persistence must be proportionate to the prespecified window and object of judgment; a written announcement does not automatically prove long-term execution.
Governance failure may limit eligibility for action; “unauthorized” cannot be used to delete facts and responsibilities already produced.

caseLinks.title: Signs of NESC institutionalization and unresolved questions in the 2004 ASAP report

caseNotes.title: Signs of NESC institutionalization and unresolved questions in the 2004 ASAP report
caseNotes.text: NASA's first-quarter 2004 ASAP report records that NESC's organizational charter was approved in August 2003 and it began operating in November. The report describes a core group of experts across centers, mobilization of mission resources, risk prioritization, and peer-review processes, stating that work had begun. The discussion also retains questions about reporting relationships, competition for resources, and long-term institutionalization.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: NASA Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel, First Quarterly Report 2004
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed pp. 37–39, NASA ENGINEERING AND SAFETY CENTER (NESC) passage
caseNotes.boundary: Supports signs of organizational formation and operation within that historical window; it does not prove long-term effectiveness, current legal validity, sufficient protection, or that the institution should continue.

argumentSteps: First determine whether the question concerns existence, effects, conversion, or legality/norms/protection/continuation.
For factual existence, trace persistent records, roles, resources, rules, and subsequent transitions, not just announcements.
Select a unique record under one of the four allowed branches, separating institutional facts from causal or conversion material.
List evidence and responsibilities for legality, norms, protection, and continuation separately; do not put them into institutional_fact outcomes.
When governance defects are found, preserve facts and consequences and stop or reduce action according to the relevant conditions.
Record changes after review or repair separately; new governance improvements must not retroactively alter the fact that the old institution existed.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: existence and protection failure can coexist
teachingExamples.text: A fictional organization operates under the same resource-allocation rule for four consecutive months, with complete records, roles, and payment documentation. At the same time, it lacks a safe appeal channel, and independent evidence confirms retaliation against people raising objections. The first body of material may support that the rule was institutionally operating within that window. The second requires protection review and stopping/repair. Neither changes the existence fact into “nonexistent,” nor does existence authorize continuation.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The organization and events are constructed; the different kinds of evidence are assumed to be as specified, without inventing actual victims.
teachingExamples.boundary: No real-world legal determination is made; a specific stopping plan still requires lawful permissions and protective arrangements.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an initiative without write-back and unresolved institutional effects
teachingExamples.text: A fictional group announces that “all purchases must be reviewed from now on,” but no new roles, records, or subsequent execution material exist. Only the announcement can be confirmed; persistent write-back of institutionalization has not yet been adequately assessed. If continuing review is later established, different total costs before and after still cannot alone establish savings. Effects constitute a separate causal question.
teachingExamples.assumptions: No actual procurement, funds, or institution is involved; only two evidential responsibilities are compared.
teachingExamples.boundary: Insufficient material must not be written as proof that the institution definitely does not exist, nor may subsequent effects be directly attributed to the new rule.

counterexamples.text: “The institution is unjust, so it never existed.”
counterexamples.effect: Confuses normative judgment with factual existence and obstructs preservation of historical effects and responsibility.

counterexamples.text: “The institution has documents and personnel, so it is lawful, protective, and should continue.”
counterexamples.effect: Existence material cannot replace the other four independent judgments.

counterexamples.text: Recording a missing appeal channel as null_supported for institutional_fact.
counterexamples.effect: Protection failure is not a null conclusion for institutional existence; record them separately and lower the ceiling on action.

questionAnswers.question: Can “the institution exists” and “the institution should stop” both hold?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes. Existence is a factual judgment, while stopping may follow from norms, risks, or protection failure; stopping does not erase existing facts.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If a new institution passes the factual branch, have its effects also been established?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Causal effects require selecting a separate branch and providing proportionate comparisons.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: How should a claim be limited when only an announcement text exists?
questionAnswers.answer: The announcement may be confirmed, but persistent institutional write-back still requires material on roles, resources, rules, and subsequent execution.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why preserve records of failed institutions?
questionAnswers.answer: Accurate records are the basis for tracing consequences, assigning responsibility, repairing, and preventing repeated errors.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: Institutional facts: persistent records / roles / resources, rules and subsequent transitions; legal validity: independent legal and permission grounds, not guaranteed by a document title; normative justification: reasons concerning values / participation / distribution, not inferred from existence; protection: safe appeals / anti-retaliation, stopping and repair conditions; continuation: risks / alternatives / correction, requiring a separate responsible choice. Five cards answer five questions. Governance failure does not erase institutional facts, and institutional existence does not guarantee the other judgments.

5.5.6.title: 5.5.6 M06 Emergence
5.5.6.lead: “The whole displays a new pattern” must be made testable: how do source units interact, what is the target pattern, and against which simple additive model is it compared? Merely calling the whole more complex supplies no bridge.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1192–1195; original anchor: section-5-5-6; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Interactions generate a pattern at the target scale.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

The key to M06 is not that an object becomes larger, but whether explicit interaction rules can generate a target-scale pattern. Register source units, interactions, the target object and pattern, and preselect a simple additive baseline. Comparison must use the same target metric, evaluation scope, and proportionate error. The interaction model cannot be asked to answer details while the baseline merely guesses a mean, followed by a declaration of victory.

An “additive model” requires an explicit function family and permitted information. Renaming any interaction function after the fact as the sum of a new unit destroys falsifiability; deliberately weakening the baseline means a win refutes only that narrow baseline. Disclose its rationale and alternative baselines.

Comparable model performance does not automatically establish additive sufficiency. Prespecified sufficiency or equivalence tests, power/sensitivity, and tolerance gates are needed to support the conclusion that addition suffices for the specified task. An undersized sample or overly coarse metric leaves the question unresolved.

A target pattern cannot uniquely identify its microscopic mechanism in reverse. The same macro quantity may arise from multiple source states and interactions. Seeking mechanisms from macro shapes can generate candidates, but material capable of distinguishing competing mechanisms must be found separately.

Emergence also does not automatically establish downward causation. A claim that macro constraints affect micro states requires specified actual channels, proportionate causal evidence, and D3/E5 mappings. Additional G4 responsibilities arise only with further claims of scale closure or object/intervention conversion. Treating “the whole determines the parts” as a complete explanation skips these specific questions.

distinctions.leftText: A task difference relative to a defined baseline.
distinctions.rightText: Non-additivity alone cannot establish a new object identity or ontology.

distinctions.leftText: There is a regularity at the target scale.
distinctions.rightText: Requires excluding other mechanisms that generate the same pattern.

distinctions.leftText: Has actual channels and proportionate causal evidence.
distinctions.rightText: Naming a pattern does not generate causal power.

boundaries: The finite binary model in this section is a rigorous formal counterexample, not a report that real-world “emergence has been proved.”
The baseline's scope determines the force of a counterexample; refuting one additive function family does not refute all simplified models.
Approximate equivalence on the same metric requires adequate sensitivity; a nonsignificant difference cannot masquerade as equivalence.
questions: Why must the affine additive model fail at the fourth point?
Does this proof exclude models with an interaction term?
Can q=1 determine which of the two units is active?
Why separate an emergent pattern from downward causation?
argumentSteps: Fix source units, interaction rules, the target object, and the measurable pattern.
Define the simple additive model family, permitted information, metric, error, and evaluation domain in advance.
Compare interaction and additive predictions on the same task, disclosing alternative models and witnesses of failure.
When performance is comparable, check sufficiency under the null gate; if it fails, retain unresolved status.
Use macro patterns only to propose mechanism candidates; separately seek evidence distinguishing microscopic mechanisms.
If further claiming downward causation or conversion, add causal mappings and corresponding G4 responsibilities respectively.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a product pattern cannot be represented exactly by an affine additive model
teachingExamples.text: Let two binary units x₁,x₂∈{0,1}, with target q=x₁x₂ and values at four points 00→0, 10→0, 01→0, 11→1. The prespecified baseline family is a+b₁x₁+b₂x₂, and the target requires exactness at all four points. Matching 00 gives a=0; matching 10 and 01 then gives b₁=b₂=0. Hence 11 can output only 0, contradicting 1. This affine additive family therefore cannot complete the task exactly.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The full four-point domain, an exact deterministic target, and a baseline allowing an intercept and two main effects but no interaction term; the common comparison metric is exactness over the entire domain.
teachingExamples.boundary: Proves only formal insufficiency relative to this baseline family; it certifies neither actual emergence, new object identity, nor downward causation.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: one macro value cannot uniquely recover the micro state
teachingExamples.text: If the target records only q=x₁+x₂, q=1 may arise from (1,0) or (0,1). Observing the aggregate value 1 cannot determine which unit equals 1. Identifying the active position requires additional information preserving position or other measurements; giving q a macro name cannot recover merged states.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A complete binary domain, exact summation mapping, and separation of the “total” and “position” targets.
teachingExamples.boundary: Nonunique recovery does not mean actual mechanisms are forever unidentifiable; additional material may distinguish them.

counterexamples.text: The interaction model uses all micro-level data, while the baseline sees only a truncated mean, followed by a claim that every additive theory has been defeated.
counterexamples.effect: The information and model scopes are mismatched; only a narrow comparison is supported, not universal generalization.

counterexamples.text: Successfully fitting the four-point pattern is taken to prove that the macro quantity can govern the units in reverse.
counterexamples.effect: Fitting a target pattern contains no downward intervention channel; causal and mapping evidence requires separate responsibilities.

counterexamples.text: A nonsignificant difference between the two models in the sample is directly recorded as additive sufficiency.
counterexamples.effect: Nonsignificance may reflect insufficient sensitivity; the prespecified null rule and three gates must pass.

questionAnswers.question: Why must the affine additive model fail at the fourth point?
questionAnswers.answer: Exact matching at the first three points already forces a=b₁=b₂=0, so 11 outputs 0 whereas the target is 1.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does this proof exclude models with an interaction term?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Adding x₁x₂ permits exact representation; the proof is limited to the prespecified affine additive family.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can q=1 determine which of the two units is active?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Both (1,0) and (0,1) give 1; additional material preserving position is needed.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why separate an emergent pattern from downward causation?
questionAnswers.answer: A target pattern's existence supplies neither an actual macro-to-micro channel nor an intervention comparison; these require separate evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: Four binary input points: 00,10,01,11, the complete exact state domain; product target x1·x2: 0,0,0,1, involving interaction between two units; affine additive baseline: a+b1·x1+b2·x2, first matching the first three points; those three force all coefficients to 0, so the fourth prediction is 0≠1 and the baseline cannot be exact everywhere. A purely mathematical construction. The counterexample concerns only the registered baseline family and does not automatically prove actual emergence, a unique mechanism, or downward causation.
figures.caption: A purely mathematical construction; the counterexample targets only the registered baseline family and does not automatically establish real emergence, a unique mechanism, or downward causation.

5.5.7.title: 5.5.7 M07 Delegation/representation
5.5.7.lead: ‘They did something on our behalf’ and ‘we validly authorized them to do it’ can have different truth values. The first statement's actions and consequences must be retained; the second statement's authority cannot be manufactured from facts after the event.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1196–1201; source anchor section-5-5-7; short quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Classification of representational facts and optional transfer of authorization.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

M07 first classifies claims to representation, actual acts on others' behalf, disputed or self-appointed representation, valid delegation, and transfers of J authority. Claiming to represent is a recordable expressive fact; an act on others' behalf is a behavioral fact; valid delegation requires corresponding grounds of authorization. Do not turn ‘someone exercises actual control’ into ‘therefore they are a lawful representative.’

The four branches are representation_claim, actual_acts, delegation_validity, and J_transfer. Even when supported, the first three cannot change J within that record. Expanding J requires the separate J_transfer route, simultaneously satisfying structured authorization tuples, independent evidence of validity, and j_authorization.

Authorization cannot merely say ‘may represent.’ Check its source, actor, object, action, territory, term, withdrawal conditions, and validity evidence, preserving complete pairings. Permitting A to report on project A does not permit A to contract for project B; two separately valid authorizations cannot be cross-combined into a third new authorization.

Majority support, visibility, influence, self-designation, and actual control do not replace valid delegation. They may provide evidence for studying representational claims or actual behavior, but must not become unconditional reasons for expanding authority. Representativeness also requires stating who is represented, on which question, at what time, and which positions are excluded.

Actions without authorization may still have actual effects and entail responsibility. Finding authorization invalid should stop or downgrade subsequent action while preserving acts already performed on others' behalf, affected objects, and consequences, and proceeding to appeal, review, and repair. Facts must not be deleted to sustain a narrative that ‘only lawful acts count as acts.’

distinctions.leftText: Someone claims, or is described as having, representative status.
distinctions.rightText: Valid authorization evidence matches the object/action and other conditions.

distinctions.leftText: An action has occurred and may have effects and entail responsibility.
distinctions.rightText: A change in authority confirmed through a dedicated branch and structured evidence.

boundaries: This lesson makes no unverified determination of any real individual's authorization validity; historical action records are not complete legal-authorization files.

Repair must not erase existing actions and consequences, or use consequences already caused to manufacture authority retroactively.

argumentSteps: Record separately who claimed representation, who actually did what, and who challenged the claim or was excluded.
Specify which branch this question selects; the actual-acts branch cannot substitute for authority transfer.
When claiming valid delegation, check the corresponding complete authorization content and validity evidence.
When claiming J expansion, additionally check that J_transfer, structured tuples, independent validity, and j_authorization are all satisfied.
Check objects, actions, territories, and terms through atomic pairings; prohibit cross-combination of multiple authorizations.
When authorization becomes invalid, limit subsequent actions while retaining existing facts, responsibilities, and correction routes.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: actions and objects must be paired atomically
teachingExamples.text: Suppose two fictional authorizations have independently verified validity: A may submit technical reports for project A during October; B may sign for receipt of supplies for project B during October. Neither authorizes A to sign for project B's supplies or B to report on project A. Taking the Cartesian product of actor set {A,B}, object set {A,B}, and action set {report,sign for receipt} would generate combinations never authorized.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The teaching example assumes both complete authorizations specify sources, territories, withdrawal provisions, and validity conditions. The three abbreviated fields here only illustrate pairing and cannot replace actual records.
teachingExamples.boundary: This is not a real authorization document and cannot be used for actual signing or action.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an unauthorized act has already occurred
teachingExamples.text: Fictional person C has published a statement on a team's behalf without valid delegation. Their self-appointed representational claim, publication action, and demonstrable effects may be recorded, while J remains without the corresponding transfer. Investigation, stopping further publication, and correcting the statement are a separate set of actions requiring lawful responsibility. Lack of authorization cannot delete the fact that the statement became public, and publication cannot retroactively establish authorization.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The people and events are fictional. Invalid authorization and occurrence of the action are stipulated, not claims about real individuals.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual allocation of responsibility for behavior still requires specific facts, procedures, and applicable norms.

counterexamples.text: ‘They signed for everyone once, so they have authority to sign from now on.’
counterexamples.effect: An actual act on others' behalf does not establish continuously valid delegation or authority for new actions.

counterexamples.text: ‘The authorization was invalid, so the statement and its effects never existed.’
counterexamples.effect: Judgments of authority cannot erase demonstrable actions, consequences, and repair responsibilities.

counterexamples.text: Passing delegation_validity automatically expands J within the same record.
counterexamples.effect: The first three branches cannot change J; authority transfer requires the separate J_transfer route and its simultaneous conditions.

questionAnswers.question: Without valid delegation, is it impossible to record representational acts?
questionAnswers.answer: Self-appointed claims, actual acts on others' behalf, and demonstrable effects may still be recorded; they cannot establish J expansion.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If A may report on project A and B may sign for receipt for project B, does that imply A may sign for receipt for project B?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Authorization consists of complete pairings; its fields cannot be split and cross-combined.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does passing the valid-delegation branch already complete a J transfer?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. The source requires J_transfer, complete tuples, independent validity, and j_authorization to pass together.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: When authorization is found invalid, should past actions be deleted?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Retain facts and consequences, restrict subsequent action, and arrange responsible correction.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

5.5.8.title: 5.5.8 M08 Compression/abstraction
5.5.8.lead: Compression need not impair the current task, but one must specify which answer is preserved and which distinctions are collapsed. Inability to recover the original and inability to answer the current question are different conclusions.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1202–1211; source anchor section-5-5-8; short quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Many-to-one representational compression.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

M08 maps multiple source states to the same representation. Track source material, algorithms, thresholds, versions, errors, unrecoverable information, and task-required invariants. Keep unknown, not_applicable, not_observable under current conditions, and withheld_for_protection distinct; none means nonexistent.

The exact condition is stated in terms of source state x, representation z=f(x), and final query q(x). If two states share a representation but require different answers, any decoder reading only z can give just one answer and cannot be correct for both. Conversely, if q is constant within every nonempty preimage, define g(z) as that common value, yielding q=g∘f. This is a proof in both directions, not merely a rule of thumb that ‘usually works.’

Here g may read only the declared representation; it cannot secretly use source-state identity, the original, or undeclared history. Existence of a set function does not imply an efficient algorithm, or guarantee sufficiency after changing the task, environment, or permitted intervention. For example, a sum can answer a total but not necessarily a maximum or which location exceeds a limit.

Approximate recovery first requires a fixed loss. Under four groups of premises—finite nonempty X, real-valued target q, arbitrary real-valued outputs, and global worst-case absolute error—take minimum a_z and maximum b_z within each nonempty preimage z. Any output c is at least (b_z−a_z)/2 from one endpoint, because the distance between endpoints is no greater than |a_z−c|+|c−b_z|. Thus every decoder's global error is at least half the largest preimage range.

Outputting midpoint (a_z+b_z)/2 for each preimage puts every target in its interval within half the range, with endpoints attaining that distance. Taking the maximum across preimages reaches the lower bound above. The optimal error is therefore exactly (1/2)max_z(b_z−a_z). For nonnegative ε, a decoder with error ≤ε exists if and only if every preimage range is ≤2ε.

This is not a universal loss score across domains. Integer outputs may exclude the midpoint; vector targets require a specified norm and geometry; average loss depends on a distribution; an unknown distribution does not allow population error rates to follow from this formula. Changed conditions require redefining and solving the optimization problem.

Successive compression must also retain the same final query. Let f:X→Z, h:Z→W, and q=g∘f. The composition can still recover q if and only if g is constant on every preimage of h restricted to the actual image f(X). Necessity: identical final representations can give only the same answer. Sufficiency: define k using the common g value in each reachable final preimage; then q=k∘h∘f. Intermediate values unreachable from any source state need not satisfy this constraint.

The first stage completing storage and the second completing counting cannot settle the original final task of ‘identifying the first position.’ Changing the task may produce another successful result, but it must be recorded separately, without overwriting failure on the old task. A representation with substantial task-relevant loss for a proposed high-impact action cannot support that action. Retaining the complete original provides a repair resource, but whether the implementer could obtain and use it in time at the relevant moment must still be checked.

distinctions.leftText: Requires information that distinguishes every relevant x.
distinctions.rightText: Requires only that q be constant in each representation preimage, which can be a weaker requirement.

distinctions.leftText: The correct answer can be mathematically defined from the representation.
distinctions.rightText: Also involves algorithms, budgets, input accessibility, and actual execution.

distinctions.leftText: That segment completes its own declared work.
distinctions.rightText: The entire chain remains sufficient for the same q; the question cannot be changed.

distinctions.leftText: A lower bound arising from conflicting answers within the same preimage.
distinctions.rightTitle: Additional errors from the actual rule
distinctions.rightText: May be introduced by inappropriate decoding and require separate checking.

boundaries: Use the half-range formula only for a finite nonempty domain with real-valued targets, arbitrary real-valued decoding, and global worst-case absolute error.
Exact recovery of q does not establish dynamic closure, feasible intervention, or satisfaction of premises by a real mapping, nor does it generate J authority.
Preimages contain only actually reachable states; unreachable intermediate values cannot manufacture a false failure.
Discovering an action error does not automatically attribute it to compression loss; the rule may be wrong. If the internal representation is unknown, retain that gap.
Substantial task-relevant loss cannot be ‘repaired’ for the original high-impact use by switching to an easier query.
questions: Why does constancy within preimages suffice to define g?
Why can a single preimage with q={0,4} not achieve worst-case error below 2?
Does successful recovery of the total establish that the maximum can also be recovered?
Why does the composition condition not constrain unreachable r?
Can completing a different local task in the second segment override failure of the original final task?
Can the half-range directly serve as a real-world average error rate?
argumentSteps: Predefine the final query, object domain, representation algorithm, and available inputs; record versions and missing-data statuses.
Partition source states into nonempty preimages sharing the same representation, and check whether answers agree within each.
For exact recovery, prove existence using preimage constancy or give a counterexample of two conflicting states.
For approximate recovery, first fix conditions such as real-valued outputs and worst-case absolute error, then calculate each preimage's range and midpoint.
Keep the same q across multiple transformations, checking whether final-stage merges retain identical answers only on the actually reachable intermediate image.
Separate representational sufficiency from actual algorithm correctness; prohibit covert access to undeclared source material.
For high-impact uses, recheck task-relevant loss, protection, norms, and authority; usability of a low-risk summary cannot simply carry over.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: the mean answers a total but not a local extreme
teachingExamples.text: Let X={(0,10),(5,5)} and f take the mean of the two numbers, giving 5 for both. If q₁ takes the sum, both states give 10, so set g₁(5)=10. If q₂ takes the maximum, the states require 10 and 5 respectively, so the same representation cannot answer exactly. The first success and second failure can both be retained without calling all compression useless.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A complete two-state domain, exact values, and a deterministic mapping; the decoder reads only the mean.
teachingExamples.boundary: The proof concerns only these two queries and cannot be extrapolated to unknown state domains, dynamics, or action.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a worst-case-error lower bound and an integer-output counterexample
teachingExamples.text: Suppose f partitions four source states into two preimages whose q values are {0,4} and {6,8}. Ranges 4 and 2 give a lower bound of 2; midpoint outputs 2 and 7 give worst-case errors 2 and 1 respectively, making the global optimum 2. ε=2 is achievable; ε=1.9 is not. Separately, take a single preimage with q={0,1}: arbitrary real-valued output permits 0.5, giving optimal error 0.5; if output must be an integer, both 0 and 1 give worst-case error 1, so the half-range value is no longer achievable.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A finite complete domain; the first part allows arbitrary real-valued outputs, and the second explicitly changes to integer outputs. Loss is consistently global worst-case absolute error.
teachingExamples.boundary: This is not a real measurement-error or population-risk estimate; different losses or output constraints must not be conflated.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: continuation checks only reachable values, but must not lose the final answer
teachingExamples.text: Let X={a,b,c}, f(a)=f(b)=u, f(c)=v, and q(a)=q(b)=0, q(c)=1. Z also contains unreachable r; set g(u)=0, g(v)=1, g(r)=99. If h(u)=A, h(v)=B, h(r)=A, the actual composition still recovers q exactly with k(A)=0 and k(B)=1; the value 99 at unreachable r causes no failure. If instead h(u)=h(v)=A, a and c merge despite having different q values, so the final task fails even though the second segment completes its local task of ‘outputting a unified label.’
teachingExamples.assumptions: Only f(X)={u,v} is allowed as actual intermediate input; all functions are constructed, and the original final query remains q.
teachingExamples.boundary: If r becomes reachable in reality later, reassessment is required; the old-domain proof cannot simply be reused.

counterexamples.text: Encoding unknown, unobservable, not applicable, and withheld for protection all as 0, then interpreting 0 as factual nonexistence.
counterexamples.effect: This compresses away distinct missing-data statuses and adds an unsupported negation; both representation and conclusion require correction.

counterexamples.text: A decoder given mean 5 secretly checks the originals and supplies maxima 10 and 5 respectively, while claiming exact recovery from the mean alone.
counterexamples.effect: This violates the decoding-input constraint; the actual system uses a richer representation.

counterexamples.text: The first segment retains two positions and the second only counts them, yet the original task ‘is the first position active?’ is declared complete.
counterexamples.effect: A local task is not the final task; merging (0,1) and (1,0) leaves conflicting answers.

counterexamples.text: Continuing to claim optimal error 0.5 for the {0,1} preimage when outputs must be integers.
counterexamples.effect: That midpoint is not an allowed output; the actual optimal worst-case error is 1.

questionAnswers.question: Why does constancy within preimages suffice to define g?
questionAnswers.answer: Each nonempty preimage has a unique common target value. Defining g by that value is unambiguous and yields q when substituted for any source state.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why can a single preimage with q={0,4} not achieve worst-case error below 2?
questionAnswers.answer: The sum of an output's distances to both endpoints is at least 4, so at least one distance is ≥2; midpoint 2 reaches this lower bound.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does successful recovery of the total establish that the maximum can also be recovered?
questionAnswers.answer: No. They are different queries; mean 5 corresponds to (0,10) and (5,5), whose maxima differ.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why does the composition condition not constrain unreachable r?
questionAnswers.answer: No source state reaches r through f, so r is not an actual input in q=k∘h∘f; an expanded reachable domain requires review.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can completing a different local task in the second segment override failure of the original final task?
questionAnswers.answer: No. F4 requires preserving the same final q throughout the chain; changing the question produces only a new problem.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can the half-range directly serve as a real-world average error rate?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It is worst-case absolute error in a specified finite model; average risk requires a distribution and a different loss definition.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: Two source states, (0,10) or (5,5), form the complete teaching state domain; their shared representation is mean 5, so the source state cannot be uniquely recovered. A total query requires 10 for both and is exactly recoverable; a maximum query requires 10 and 5, conflicting within the same preimage. For arbitrary real-valued answers, the minimax midpoint is 7.5 and optimal radius 2.5. Purely formal construction; the figure's 2.5 concerns preimage {5,10}, while the separate textual example {0,4} has optimal radius 2. Do not mix them.
figures.caption: Purely formal construction; the figure's 2.5 concerns preimage {5,10}, while the separate textual example {0,4} has optimal radius 2. Do not mix them.

5.5.9.title: 5.5.9 M09 Lateral transfer
5.5.9.lead: Success in a source domain gives reason to ask a better question in the target domain; it cannot answer that question on the target's behalf. Clearer mappings reveal what is comparable and what must be checked separately.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1212–1215; source anchor section-5-5-9; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “cross-domain analogical transfer.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

M09 registers relational mappings between source and target, not merely similar nouns. Specify source object, target object, preserved relations, key differences, possible breaks, prohibited mappings, and differences in target responsibility chains and J. Comparability is a bounded candidate, not certification that the target claim holds.

Source-domain material can generate only target candidates. Both supported and null_supported in the target require an independent target instance and corresponding material; “many source studies” cannot fill gaps in target object, measurement, boundaries, or comparison. No target run means not_evaluated; evaluation with insufficient bridge or evidence remains unsupported_or_undecided.

Structural isomorphism need not mean a shared mechanism. Identical input-output tables can arise from different internal processes, and similar statistical ratios may have multiple causes. Transfer should propose target-domain observations or comparisons that distinguish those mechanisms, rather than seeking only support for the analogy.

Insufficient target material does not mean the target mechanism is absent. Rejection of an analogy need not overturn the original source conclusion; the mapping may break, target conditions may differ, or the task may change. Preserve each domain's known facts and conclusion boundaries, avoiding “one side fails, so delete both.”

Analogy grants no target action permission. Transferring machine-control strategies to an organization or one community's support network to another cannot copy value tradeoffs, representative standing, or intervention authority, even where descriptions resemble one another. Register target responsibility chains and affected-person protections anew.

distinctions.leftText: Material exists for the source object and conditions.
distinctions.rightText: The mapping supplies a question for testing; an independent target instance is still needed.

distinctions.leftText: Certain relations or indicators are close.
distinctions.rightText: Requires ruling out different processes producing similar results.

distinctions.leftText: Not run or insufficiently supported.
distinctions.rightText: A stronger denial that does not automatically follow from insufficient evidence.

boundaries: Independent target material concerns the target object; it is not source material relabeled and reposted.
Source analogies offer only bounded guidance; identical physical, social, or normative terms do not constitute cross-domain proof.

Preserve domain authors' actual conclusions, without retrospectively awarding this framework's G-instance eligibility or denying their independent achievements because the framework has not certified them.
questions: Why can abundant source-domain research still not fill the target-instance requirement?
If both systems show only (0,0) and (1,1) observationally, must intervening on x have the same result?
Which status applies if the target has not yet been run?

caseLinks.title: Neanderthal research explicitly warns against turning similar ratios into identical social organization

caseNotes.title: Neanderthal research explicitly warns against turning similar ratios into identical social organization
caseNotes.text: After comparing ratios concerning Y-chromosome and mitochondrial diversity, Skov and colleagues specifically note that similar ratios in apes and Neanderthals need not imply the same social organization: ape data have heterogeneous sources, and different processes can generate similar ratios. The paper separately uses Neanderthals' own genetic material and model comparisons to propose a female-migration explanation.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Skov et al., Nature 610（2022），Genetic insights into the social organization of Neanderthals
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Main: Inferring social organization, warning paragraph after the cross-species ratio comparison and adjacent model-comparison passage
caseNotes.boundary: Supports the authors' explicit limits on cross-species analogy while retaining their local explanation from target data; does not extend to all Neanderthals or political rule structures, nor retrospectively award a formal G-instance.

argumentSteps: First delimit the actual scope of source-domain conclusions and the target task without enlarging source support.
Construct relational mappings item by item, also listing differences, breaks, and prohibited mappings.
Propose target candidates and target observations or comparisons that can distinguish alternative explanations.
Obtain independent target material and register status according to actual execution, the positive gate, and the zero gate separately.
When an analogy fails, identify whether it limits the mapping, target claim, or source conclusion; do not impose unsupported collateral rejection.
Check target responsibilities, protections, and J differences; transferring knowledge cannot transfer unauthorized power.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: the same static table, different intervention targets
teachingExamples.text: The source system specifies y=x; the target system first sets hidden c to 0 or 1, then x=c and y=c. Natural observations in both systems may show only (0,0) and (1,1), but changing only x while holding c fixed in the target does not change y. Identical natural static tables do not suffice to transfer the source rule “changing x changes y” to the target.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Two deterministic structural models are stipulated; target intervention replaces only the x equation, preserves c, and measurement is error-free.
teachingExamples.boundary: A formal counterexample to analogy, not a test of any actual causal system.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: transferring a queueing method does not transfer punitive authority
teachingExamples.text: A fictional laboratory predicts waiting time from task-queue length and proposes the same-named indicator for community services. Arrivals, service capacity, and waiting windows may be mapped as candidates; people's ability to exit, hidden demand, priority rules, appeals, and responsibilities differ. Even if independent target material validates prediction, this confers no permission to deny services or punish people.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Domains and proposal are teaching assumptions; no claim of actual community implementation or measured effects.
teachingExamples.boundary: Offers no actual intervention advice; target action still requires independent value, protection, and permission conditions.

counterexamples.text: Intervening on x works in the source, and the target has identical observational correlations, so the target can do the same.
counterexamples.effect: The same observation table can arise from a common cause; target causation needs independent material.

counterexamples.text: Insufficient target evidence is used to declare that the source mechanism can never exist in the target.
counterexamples.effect: Not evaluated or unresolved cannot replace a bounded zero conclusion, still less a universal denial.

counterexamples.text: Support for an analogous indicator is followed by transferring source-domain control authority directly to the target operator.
counterexamples.effect: A knowledge mapping does not generate target J authorization.

questionAnswers.question: Why can abundant source-domain research still not fill the target-instance requirement?
questionAnswers.answer: Source material answers questions about the source object; target conditions, measurement, and responsibilities may differ, requiring target-specific material.

questionAnswers.question: If both systems show only (0,0) and (1,1) observationally, must intervening on x have the same result?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily: common cause c may determine both x and y in the target, so changing x while holding c fixed does not change y.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Which status applies if the target has not yet been run?
questionAnswers.answer: not_evaluated; if run but the bridge or evidence is insufficient, it may be unsupported_or_undecided, not automatically null_supported.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does analogy failure overturn the source research?
questionAnswers.answer: Not automatically. Check whether failure lies in the mapping or target conditions, retaining the source research's independent standing within its original scope.

5.6.title: 5.6 Scale boundaries of general primitives
5.6.lead: Naming an interface “feedback,” “memory,” or “phase” begins to clarify a question; it does not automatically establish learning, historical increment, or object conversion. Claims of different strengths need their own proportionate evidence.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1216–1229; source anchor section-5-6; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “General primitives are D-class interfaces.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

General primitives are D-class definitional interfaces, carrying no empirical null models or falsification templates of their own. They help register objects, channels, states, and windows; complete fields alone cannot obtain G-family empirical support. Discussing an actual mechanism requires a specific question and corresponding evidence; minimum definitional conditions must not be mistaken for complete mechanism identification.

Basic U07 feedback requires only a return channel and subsequent state update. An output observed without returning, or a return that does not change subsequent state, cannot establish effective feedback on that basis. Conversely, a transient update can constitute basic feedback without a mandatory cross-round memory or G3 requirement.

Feedback-mediated learning adds a chain beyond basic feedback: updating a locatable carrier, retaining or continually updating it across rounds, actually using it later, and corresponding evidence for predefined task outcomes. One parameter change, one success, or one archived item does not complete the chain. Carried learning does not first require additional historical increment; G3 is added only for a claim of historical conditional increment beyond the currently registered state.

U09 first separates instantaneous demand-capacity shortfall, accumulated damage, and delayed recovery. Demand 8 and capacity 5 now define a current shortfall of 3, not prior proof of G3 or long-term damage. Claiming overload causes damage and delays recovery requires tracing the current damage or capacity carrier, its formation, and subsequent recovery. Only a further need for history beyond the registered current state enters G3.

U10 registers candidate traces, carriers, and retention windows without guaranteeing use of the trace or pre-establishing path dependence. Archive existence, retrieval availability, actual reading, entry into decisions, and task differences are separate links. G3 further tests historical conditional increment after controlling for the registered current state; “an old file exists” is not increment evidence.

U11's basic phase pattern describes differences in operating modes without requiring G3 or G4. Explaining what triggers a mode change separately requires G2. Persistence or delayed recovery maintained by a current carrier follows the carrier route of 4.5; a claim of hysteresis involving historical increment beyond the current representation separately requires G3; an object-identity conversion claim separately requires G4. A switch moving from on to off does not necessarily become another object simply because its state differs.

Three other reminders matter equally: U01 registers a candidate object without guaranteeing G1 grouping support; U05 defines relations without proving causation; U06 registers channel fields without proving their corresponding effects. Candidates are valuable, but candidate status cannot be switched into a successful conclusion.

Keep three questions separate in research across time: how the past formed a current carrier, how that carrier continues to affect the future, and whether history adds usefulness given the current representation. Independent process and comparison material may establish the first two while the third fails; failure of the third's positive gate cannot establish the first two in reverse. Formal carrier-mechanism support also requires proportionate G2/H instances under 4.5, while existing domain evidence retains its own conclusions and limitations without retrospective framework eligibility.

distinctions.rightText: Also requires evidence for retention/updating, actual use, task outcomes, and related conditions.

boundaries: Do not require G3 for all feedback or all persistent learning; only the additional-historical-increment branch needs it.
Failure of G3's positive gate establishes neither absence of historical formation nor carrier sufficiency, and does not automatically support a bounded zero conclusion.

Stipulating a complete state in a model can supply an exact counterexample, not deny omitted variables or path dependence in reality.
Preserve established general learning or behavioral change in domain research; do not cancel it because formal-mechanism status under this framework was not sought.
