6.4.title: 6.4 A Fictional Appeal Example of Feedback, Institutional Write-Back, and Learning
6.4.lead: The same appeal may stop at “received,” change case fields, be implemented, or even influence processing across later rounds. Every additional level of claim adds an evidential responsibility; one acknowledgment cannot cross every step.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1402–1415; original anchor: section-6-4; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “This example only demonstrates a classification method.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

The original text explicitly posits a fictional institution, so the following teaches classification rather than reporting an actual appeal or providing external empirical proof. We fix the same object, appeal, and observation window, varying subsequent conditions to see how far a claim may go. This is not a maturation ladder that real institutions necessarily follow.

In the first scenario, the appeal is received and an acknowledgment generated, while the registered records, rules, resources, roles, responsibilities, memory, and stopping conditions all remain unchanged. The acknowledgment establishes signal arrival, not automatic change in any relevant subsequent field. Define acknowledgment metadata and the institutional fields in question beforehand. If an actual acknowledgment itself triggers scheduling or stopping conditions, it is no longer this example's “all unchanged” case; actual channels and effects require rechecking.

In the second scenario, the appeal changes a case-status field through a specified channel, but execution has not begun. Given proportionate causal comparison, this can satisfy D2's return effect: a status field is also a subsequent state, and feedback need not await a changed final outcome. H3, however, requires field change and actual execution, so complete institutional write-back cannot yet be claimed. A field changing later in time is not itself evidence that “the appeal caused it.”

The third scenario carries the field change into actual execution, separately recording acceptance, before/after field versions, execution, and duration, satisfying the example's write-back classification. Duration is part of the contract; one execution does not imply permanent validity. H3 is a classification rule, not an abstract empirical truth or permission to alter an institution. C11 additionally requires G2 and D2 comparisons for the specified feedback channel. Successful classification and complete empirical-mechanism support must not be conflated.

The fourth scenario additionally requires a retainable rule or state update, actual use in multiple later rounds of similar cases, prespecified task comparisons, and corresponding causal grounds before a carrier-based feedback-mediated learning candidate can be proposed. One write-back does not automatically establish preservation and use across rounds. Repeated identical later outcomes may also arise from continuing external instructions or shared environments; proportionate competing explanations must be excluded. A further claim of an additional historical increment beyond the current state is tested separately by G3.

Evidential gates increase with claim strength in this example, but this does not mean learning in every field must first pass through institutional write-back. The fixed route here is “how an appeal changes an institution and affects later cases.” Learning generally may occur in other carriers, assessed separately under 6.3. Diagram arrows also do not guarantee that receipt eventually leads to learning; every connection may stop.

A write-back fact guarantees neither institutional justification nor long-term repair. Executing an improper rule may still involve actual field changes and implementation; record facts and normative issues separately. A rule's unjustified character cannot erase effects that occurred, and successful execution cannot endorse its justification. Repair targets, responsibility, authorization, and implementation procedures remain separate judgments.

For actual material, list “already occurred,” “insufficient evidence,” and “plan only” individually. An open entry point, public response, field modification, actual execution, retained use, and task effects each have their place. Missing execution evidence cannot justify inventing implementation, while missing long-term material cannot deny an evidenced short-term change. Teaching tables merely organize material; entering “yes” is not the material itself.

distinctions.leftText: Confirms arrival or the start of processing.
distinctions.rightText: Requires locating before/after differences in relevant fields and checking their source.

distinctions.leftText: A specified return produces differences in subsequent states or related quantities.
distinctions.rightText: This example additionally requires institutional-field changes to enter actual execution, with duration recorded.

distinctions.leftText: The modification in this round has been implemented.
distinctions.rightText: A retainable update is repeatedly used later and changes the prespecified task.

distinctions.leftText: Distinguishes acceptance, modification, and execution under given rules.
distinctions.rightText: Requires corresponding evidence or norms/procedures; classification cannot replace them.

boundaries: This section has no actual appeal object; its constructed states, counts, and losses must not be treated as administrative statistics.
The successive added conditions here concern only the appeal route, not a claim that all learning depends on H3 institutional write-back.
Field change can coexist with lack of execution; incomplete final implementation cannot cancel evidenced state feedback.
One execution guarantees neither persistence, learning, repair, nor justification; duration cannot be left blank and then assumed permanent.
Knowing that no relevant change occurred differs from lacking material observing change. With insufficient material, retain unresolved status rather than treating missing records as absent events.
questions: If a case field changes from 0 to 1 but execution has not occurred, why can we not simply say “nothing happened”?
If an announcement says a new rule was approved but implementers still use the old rule, at which level should the claim stop?
Does version D's three uses automatically establish a historical increment independent of the current state?
If the original target is correct review, old output is 0, and new output is 1, what are the mean squared losses across the three cases?
Must all feedback learning first undergo institutional write-back?
argumentSteps: Declare this to be the author's fictional classification example; fix the object, fields, time window, and appeal route without fabricating an actual case.
First check arrival/acknowledgment, then field changes caused by the specified return; do not merge the two.
A field change with proportionate return comparison may constitute feedback. If it has not entered execution, stop there without upgrading to complete write-back.
After actual execution, separately record acceptance, versions, execution, and duration, classifying under H3 while separately checking causal-mechanism eligibility.
Only after checking retention, multi-round use, prespecified task comparisons, and causal material should a carrier-learning candidate be proposed.
If an additional historical increment is claimed, check G3 independently; do not make it a mandatory gate for every write-back or learning claim.
Finally distinguish write-back facts, learning, long-term repair, justification, and permissions, locating gaps at specific levels.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: distinguishing four versions item by item
teachingExamples.text: A fictional system defines case status s=0 as awaiting the original process and s=1 as entering review. It also registers actual execution e, rule retention p, and subsequent use count n. Version A only receives the appeal, with s=0, e=0, p=0, n=0: arrival only. Version B changes s to 1 under the given return rule, but e=0: state feedback within the model, without complete write-back. Version C adds review execution e=1 to B, recording acceptance, field change, execution time, and a two-day validity period: it permits a one-time write-back classification. Version D additionally retains the update p=1, uses it in three later similar cases n=3, and adds task and causal comparisons: only then does the material reach the level needed to propose a carrier-learning candidate.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Entirely constructed. B's rule explicitly states s=1 with this return and s=0 without it, holding other conditions fixed. The flags are given model states, not certification produced by filling out a real-world form.
teachingExamples.boundary: Even D cannot establish an actual mechanism merely from p=1 and n=3; corresponding actual material is required, and neither additional history nor net benefit has thereby been proved.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: task comparison needs explicit rules
teachingExamples.text: Continue with version D. For all three new cases, the prespecified task is correct entry into review, with ideal output y*=1. The old rule outputs 0 for all three specified inputs; the new retained rule outputs 1. Old mean squared loss is [(0−1)²×3]/3=1; new loss is 0. In the model, replacing only the rule with the old version before use returns loss to 1; restoring the new rule returns it to 0. This provides a computable connection between use and outcome. “Used three times” without these comparisons cannot directly count as success.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Inputs, targets, both rule versions, and the meaning of replacement are artificially fixed; no shared external instruction changes outputs.
teachingExamples.boundary: The model contains no actual case rights, resource costs, or legal effects; it cannot adjudicate an actual institution.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an acknowledgment may trigger an effect, but the question must change
teachingExamples.text: A fictional system stipulates that generating a receipt acknowledgment pauses the case-deadline clock for 24 hours. If this rule is actually executed, a stopping condition has changed, so the case cannot remain in version A, where “all relevant fields remain unchanged.” Register the changed field and channel, distinguishing the clock pause from subsequent substantive review. The pause alone proves neither ultimate appeal success nor long-term learning.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An explicit conditional counterfactual, not a description of any current appeal system; 24 hours is a teaching assumption.
teachingExamples.boundary: Not every actual acknowledgment can be presumed to suspend deadlines, and this provides no advice on legal time limits.

counterexamples.text: Original fictional example A has only an acknowledgment; all relevant institutional fields remain unchanged.
counterexamples.effect: An entry point or response alone cannot establish effective feedback and write-back.

counterexamples.text: Original fictional example B changes a field but has no execution.
counterexamples.effect: State feedback in D2's sense may exist, but complete H3 write-back cannot be claimed.

counterexamples.text: An appeal prompts modification and actual execution of a harmful rule, so the institution is declared justified and repair complete.
counterexamples.effect: Factual classification, normative evaluation, and long-term repair cannot replace one another.

counterexamples.text: No subsequent execution record is found, so it is concluded that execution never occurred in reality.
counterexamples.effect: Missing evidence does not automatically mean an event was absent; distinguish verified nonexecution from non-observation.

questionAnswers.question: If a case field changes from 0 to 1 but execution has not occurred, why can we not simply say “nothing happened”?
questionAnswers.answer: If proportionate evidence supports the specified return's effect, the state has changed; it still fails the execution condition for complete institutional write-back.

questionAnswers.question: If an announcement says a new rule was approved but implementers still use the old rule, at which level should the claim stop?
questionAnswers.answer: Preserve the announcement/approval fact and check specific field changes; an announcement cannot masquerade as actual execution and complete write-back.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does version D's three uses automatically establish a historical increment independent of the current state?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A carrier update may sufficiently contain what was learned; additional increments require separate G3 testing relative to an explicit current representation.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If the original target is correct review, old output is 0, and new output is 1, what are the mean squared losses across the three cases?
questionAnswers.answer: The old loss is 1 and the new loss 0, holding only within the given model, target, and three-input scope.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Must all feedback learning first undergo institutional write-back?
questionAnswers.answer: No. This section fixes an institutional appeal route; learning in other carriers is tested independently under 6.3.

6.5.title: 6.5 CM-MAINTENANCE Maintenance and preservation–dissolution
6.5.lead: A machine that keeps running or a service that stays open may depend on someone continuously replenishing, replacing, correcting, or clearing obstacles. Maintenance analysis identifies how those specific inputs preserve identity or function, while asking what is preserved, who bears the work, and whether a backup can actually take over when failure occurs.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1416–1431; source anchor section-6-5; short quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Redundancy is tested against failure conditions, not merely by counting backups.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

The basic dependencies are D0 and G2: first specify the complete object contract, in which K is only the identity criterion, then identify the specified maintenance channel. D1 bounds state terms such as persistence, disintegration, and repair, while E4, CAUSAL, and EVIDENCE review explanations and evidence. Declare the current K or functional criterion F and the window in advance to determine what maintenance preserves. ‘It still seems to be there’ does not automatically mean every function is normal.

The mechanism chain is wear, drift, loss, or component exit → specified maintenance channel → replenishment/replacement/correction/clearance → changed duration of K or F preservation or failure probability. The result may extend usable time or change failure risk without returning the state to its initial value each time. Minimum comparison requires more than ‘a work order exists’: appropriate evidence across maintenance, reduced-maintenance, mismatched-maintenance, and stopping conditions, with G2 channel identification, is also needed. Real comparisons involving stopping maintenance are constrained by risk and authority; essential services cannot be arbitrarily shut down for verification.

The current branch asks about current inputs' effects on preserving K/F within the current window. The carried-cumulative branch additionally traces how earlier inputs form current wear or capability carriers, how they are retained/replenished across windows, and the longitudinal and causal grounds for maintenance changing subsequent preservation. cumulative is the additional historical-increment branch: add G3 only when claiming that history has extra effects given the current representation. When current wear already sufficiently takes up the past, there may be no additional historical increment.

If an object preserves K/F without sustained maintenance within the target window, maintenance necessity cannot be extrapolated into that window. If changes to maintenance inputs do not change relevant outcomes, or supposed wear actually comes from an independent shock, narrow or withdraw the corresponding claim. If comparisons lack sensitivity, retain unresolved status rather than treating unmeasured differences as zero effects. Continuing to use an old criterion after K has changed conflates maintenance with object transformation; recheck the object contract.

A need for maintenance is not a normative reason for permanent persistence. A replenishment channel's existence does not automatically assign its burden to someone or create an obligation to sacrifice. Mismatched maintenance may sustain an old object's K while damaging the target F; orderly stopping, transformation, or disintegration may also be permitted outcomes. Whether to maintain, toward which target, and who decides and executes remain questions for norms, authorization, and procedures. Technical feasibility does not imply obligation.

Normal operation, migration, failure, and recovery are different tasks. Interface standards describe conditions for possible interoperability; implementation versions, operational semantics, environmental loads, testing, and on-site adaptation determine actual compatibility in this instance. Parts in storage still require checking specifications, quality, transportation, on-site skills, and shutdown authority. ‘Exists’ cannot be collapsed into ‘usable in time.’ Replaceability under ordinary conditions also differs from completing replacement within an emergency window.

Maintenance may move outside the original object boundary and be supplied by users, families, outsourced workers, or other institutions. Fewer central work orders with maintained output need not mean less total maintenance labor. Record where external burdens are borne, the workload, time, support, and right to stop. Only same-type quantities may be summed under explicit definitions; heterogeneous labor, risk, time, and rights must not be compressed into a unitless universal cost.

Redundancy must address failure conditions, not merely count backups. Two paths may share power, software state, transportation, suppliers, operators, or approval nodes. They may substitute for one another normally yet fail together during a fault. Check backup capacity, common-cause exposure, switching time, on-site skills, and actual switching authority separately; do not presume that two units mean independent reliability.

Recovery also depends on communications, roads, fuel, spare parts, and personnel, whose accessibility must be checked within the same failure window. If lost communications prevent obtaining switching permission, or blocked roads prevent parts from arriving, a backup on paper may not become actual recovery. Adding backups, reducing coupling, and retaining locally independent operation are all candidate designs; their net effects still depend on failure types, maintenance costs, and specific tasks.

distinctions.leftText: The object continues to satisfy the declared identity criterion.
distinctions.rightText: Continue to meet specific functional requirements; the two can diverge.

distinctions.leftText: Another component or path is present.
distinctions.rightText: Capacity, common exposure, switching, arrival on site, and authority all fit the current window.

distinctions.leftText: Specifies types and rules for possible interoperability.
distinctions.rightText: A usable connection under specific implementations, semantics, environments, and loads.

distinctions.leftText: Function depends on certain inputs within a specified scope.
distinctions.rightTitle: Someone must continue bearing the burden
distinctions.rightText: Still requires norms, responsibility, and authority; it does not follow directly.

boundaries: No need for sustained maintenance in a short window does not imply no need in every longer window; long-window evidence also cannot replace the original short-task conclusion.
Current wear may sufficiently take up the past; G3 need not be required before recognizing cumulative carrier effects.
If one still says ‘maintaining the same object’ after the original K fails, check whether transformation or disintegration has occurred; do not silently retain the old contract.
Redundancy tests under normal power and transportation conditions do not automatically cover common-cause failures and recovery phases.
Improved central metrics may accompany increased external labor; maintenance capability does not directly create an obligation for any named person.

Why can model B's dual failure not be calculated as 0.1×0.1?
If maintenance is necessary to preserve function, does that suffice to designate a particular employee to continue bearing it?
Why might recovery targets remain unmet despite an existing backup with enough capacity?
If current wear fully reflects the past and additional history provides no increment, does this exclude cumulative maintenance effects?

caseLinks.title: STS-114: spare parts must enter actual replacement

caseNotes.title: STS-114: spare parts must enter actual replacement
caseNotes.text: NASA's mission record states that during the second extravehicular activity on August 1, 2005, Noguchi and Robinson removed failed CMG-1, moved a new control moment gyroscope out of the payload bay, and installed it. The record then reports four working CMGs on the space station. This section adds the distinction among a spare part's existence, transportation to position, personnel operations, installation, and operating state, rather than repeating the image-feedback case.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: NASA STS-114 mission page, updated 2025-05-01
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Mission Highlights, EVA No.2 (Aug.1) entry; for CMG function, see the sentence following the preceding EVA No.1 entry
caseNotes.boundary: This supports the mission record of that replacement and the operating count at the time. It does not quantify long-term reliability, independent redundancy, or every counterfactual concerning maintenance necessity, and does not confer formal G2 eligibility.

argumentSteps: Fix the complete object contract, K/F, window, and normal/migration/failure/recovery task, avoiding conflation of identity and function.
Locate the wear carrier, maintenance input, and effect path; predefine outcomes such as preservation duration or failure probability.
Identify channels using appropriate maintenance, reduced-maintenance, mismatch, and stopping comparisons, addressing independent shocks, selection, and measurement limitations.
Register current, carrier-cumulative, and additional historical-increment branches separately; only the last additionally requires G3.
Check actual interface compatibility, part quality and arrival, personnel skills, and shutdown/switching authority, not just inventory.
Include externally taken-up labor and recovery dependencies within the boundary; give explicit definitions for same-type quantities and list heterogeneous costs separately.
Evaluate redundancy against common failure conditions and switching deadlines; then separately deliberate on whether to maintain, replace/stop, and assign responsibility and authorization.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: maintenance changes preservation time; windows must not be swapped
teachingExamples.text: A fictional device starts with wear w₀=0, gains 2 per step, and receives maintenance input m that offsets wear, following w_{t+1}=max(0,w_t+2−m). Predefined function F requires w≤3 at every inspection time. No maintenance, m=0, gives 0,2,4, first failing at step two; reduced maintenance, m=1, gives 0,1,2,3,4, first failing at step four; maintenance m=2 keeps wear at 0 and preserves F throughout the chosen four-step window. If the task window is only the first step, all three satisfy F. Differences over a longer window cannot establish that first-step function necessarily requires sustained maintenance.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Wear and compensation use the same units, rules are fixed, and there are no additional shocks. Only F is compared; this single variable is not claimed to validate the complete object contract or identity criterion K.
teachingExamples.boundary: Entirely a mathematical model; real wear, maintenance timing, and failure thresholds require independent measurement. No maintenance amount is prescribed on this basis.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: the same two backup paths, but different independent and common-cause failure
teachingExamples.text: Assume function is achieved when at least one of two paths is available. In model A, each path fails independently with probability 0.1, so dual-failure probability is 0.01. In model B, a common event with probability 0.05 causes both paths to fail; absent that event, each path fails conditionally independently with probability 1/19. Each path's marginal failure probability is still 0.05+0.95/19=0.1, but dual-failure probability is 0.05+0.95×(1/19)²=1/19≈0.052632. The number of paths and individual marginal probabilities are identical, but system-failure probabilities differ. Counting backups cannot replace examination of shared conditions.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Both probability models are entirely stipulated, with instantaneous switching and sufficient capacity; model B is independent only conditional on no common-cause event.
teachingExamples.boundary: These are not reliability statistics for actual equipment; reality also requires switching time, authority, skills, and capacity.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: enough backup capacity can still miss the functional window
teachingExamples.text: A fictional service allows at most 2 minutes of interruption. Its backup has sufficient capacity but requires on-site personnel to switch it over, taking at least 5 minutes. A backup's existence does not satisfy F of ‘interruption no longer than 2 minutes.’ Restoring service after 5 minutes is still another real result; the backup is not therefore entirely useless, nor can late recovery be written as meeting the original window.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Deadlines, capacity, and switching rules are teaching assumptions, with no real shutdown or personnel experiment.
teachingExamples.boundary: This is not a real safety threshold or switching recommendation; task requirements must be fixed beforehand.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: lower central workload may coincide with more external replacement work
teachingExamples.text: Suppose maintenance labor for the same registered activity in the same week initially totals 8 person-hours centrally and 0 externally. After a change it totals 3 centrally and 7 externally. Central labor falls by 5 person-hours, but total labor under this accounting definition rises from 8 to 10 person-hours. External replacement work can explain maintained output; central work orders alone cannot establish reduced total maintenance.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Constructed same-type labor time, covering both sides without double counting. Person-hours serve only as time accounting, without assuming equal fatigue, opportunity losses, or rights across people.
teachingExamples.boundary: Time, health, risk, and responsibility are not combined into a universal cost; no real family or institution is described.

counterexamples.text: Two backup units share the same power source and sole approver, yet are declared two fully independent recovery paths.
counterexamples.effect: Common exposure and switching authority may block both simultaneously; test against failure conditions.

counterexamples.text: An old process retains its identity while its task function remains impaired, so continued maintenance of the old process is called repair.
counterexamples.effect: Preserving K differs from meeting F; mismatched maintenance may require stopping or transformation.

counterexamples.text: Someone continually fills gaps to keep a service normal, so they are presumed permanently obliged to continue.
counterexamples.effect: Separate empirical uptake from normative obligation; check voluntariness, responsibility, and the right to stop.

counterexamples.text: Having purchased parts conforming to an interface standard, declaring that the on-site fault can immediately be solved.
counterexamples.effect: Implementation versions, semantics, environment, quality, arrival, skills, and shutdown authority may still be inadequate.

questionAnswers.question: Why does the wear model with m=1 first fail at step four?
questionAnswers.answer: Wear proceeds through 1,2,3,4. F permits ≤3, so the threshold is first exceeded at step four.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why can model B's dual failure not be calculated as 0.1×0.1?
questionAnswers.answer: The two paths are conditionally independent only in the absence of the common event; overall, they are coupled by the common cause. First condition the probability calculation on that event.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If maintenance is necessary to preserve function, does that suffice to designate a particular employee to continue bearing it?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Maintenance mechanisms, responsibility, obligation, voluntariness, and authority are different judgments.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why might recovery targets remain unmet despite an existing backup with enough capacity?
questionAnswers.answer: There may be common failure, switching delays, gaps in on-site skills or authority, and recovery dependencies may be unavailable within the same window.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If current wear fully reflects the past and additional history provides no increment, does this exclude cumulative maintenance effects?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The carrier-cumulative route holds on separate longitudinal/causal evidence; only the additional historical branch requires G3.

6.6.title: 6.6 CM-LOAD Load, capacity, and recovery
6.6.lead: ‘We cannot keep up’ and ‘recovery is complete’ both need explicit definitions. Where, during which period, for what demand, and with how much available capacity? Has the day's output recovered, identity and function, or depleted reserves? A single overall percentage cannot answer these questions.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1432–1449; source anchor section-6-6; short quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘A recovery judgment should state what has recovered, for whom, under which supporting conditions, and as of when.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

CM-LOAD first uses D0 to specify objects and locations, then G2 to identify measured channels and relevant dimensions; E4, CAUSAL, and EVIDENCE are methodological gates. Demand and capacity must be of the same type, or have explicit units and conversion mappings, measured at the same location and within the same window. Tasks per hour cannot directly be subtracted from total inventory, nor headcounts from budgets. Processing time, task types, accounting boundaries, and mappings must be provided before comparison becomes possible.

The mechanism chain is comparable demand entering a specified channel, occupying available capacity, and producing an immediate shortfall or cross-boundary spillover, followed by load reduction, replenishment, or expansion changing the shortfall. The instant branch registers only demand-capacity and immediate shortfall within the same window; one shortfall does not automatically imply accumulated damage. carried-cumulative additionally traces historical exposure forming current damage/capacity carriers, retention or recovery across windows, subsequent outcomes, and proportionate causal comparisons; only the cumulative branch for additional history separately adds G3.

Load need not accumulate monotonically. Capacity may expand with demand and absorb the increment; a brief shortfall may end without persistent differences. Delayed recovery or later collapse requires explaining how damage, reserves, backlog, or another carrier connects one window to the next. “Was once overloaded” cannot be a sufficient cause of every later problem.

Averages cannot replace location and distribution. Total demand below total capacity does not ensure that every location avoids overload. Spare capacity that cannot reach the shortfall location within the window cannot directly offset it. Distinguish peak from sustained capacity, alternative-channel capacity, and replenishment rate; a brief peak cannot silently promise long-term supply. Register where cross-boundary spillover lands rather than deleting it from central indicators.

Recovery has at least three targets: whether output returns, whether original K or predefined F recovers, and whether internal margins are replenished. Normal output quantity may coexist with differences in quality, continuity, or accessibility. A restored F may coexist with unrestored staff rest, spare parts, maintenance backlog, or funding continuity. Conversely, confirming an accurately bounded function need not wait for every other life outcome to improve.

A recovery claim must specify what recovers, for whom, under which support, and through what date. Quantity, quality, continuity, and accessibility of physical or service outputs require separate evidence. Internal rest/spares/backlog/funding, external caregiving/commuting/borrowing/alternative-service burdens, and later interruptions and near misses cannot be inferred from central output alone. List unlike burdens separately; the need for recovery does not itself generate duties of sacrifice or operational authorization.

The denominator is part of the claim. Predisaster population, current population, eligible people, and actual users answer different questions, and the numerator must belong to the corresponding set. “100% service connection among those meeting safety conditions” can be true without meaning “100% recovery of all aspects of life for all predisaster residents.” Explain reasons, timing, and excluded positions when changing denominators; do not overwrite the old definition with the new.

Temporary premises, continued external aid, or assistive equipment can support genuine functional repair. Dependence on support is not failure; check how long support can last, its expiry, whether replacement uptake is actually operating, and peak loads, seasonal exposure, or maintenance cycles not yet experienced. Support does not mean recovery can never count, nor may supported success be generalized into independent success after withdrawal.

“False recovery” should identify only a claim exceeding evidence for objects, populations, functions, or persistence conditions, without thereby presuming deception. Later renewed instability requires comparing continuing old damage, unreplenished reserves, interrupted support, new shocks, and changed definitions. A new failure may reveal boundaries without erasing earlier accurately bounded achievements; necessary support must not be withdrawn to test recovery.

distinctions.leftText: Demand exceeds available capacity at the same location and in the same window.
distinctions.rightText: Requires a carrier bringing past exposure forward; it does not follow directly from a shortfall.

distinctions.leftText: A particular output, such as quantity, returns to a predefined level.
distinctions.rightText: Restoring reserves, rest, backlog, and continuity capacity is another task.

distinctions.leftText: Temporary aid can form part of genuine function.
distinctions.rightText: Requires proportionate later material; the former cannot substitute.

distinctions.leftText: Explicit population, numerator and denominator, function, and time.
distinctions.rightText: Covers more objects and outcomes; one percentage does not automatically establish it.

boundaries: Quantities of different types, times, or locations cannot be directly subtracted; dispatchability is also a bridging condition.
Brief overload may leave no long-term damage; long-term capacity shortage may also have other independent causes.
A bounded function holding does not mean every outcome has recovered, nor must every outcome recover before that function is acknowledged.
If support will expire without an operating successor, persistence remains unresolved; do not invent future supply.
Renewed instability does not automatically overturn earlier bounded success, establish deception by prior personnel, or require withdrawing support.

caseLinks.title: Puerto Rico electricity restoration: denominators and temporary support jointly bound recovery

caseNotes.title: Puerto Rico electricity restoration: denominators and temporary support jointly bound recovery
caseNotes.text: GAO's 2019 report relays PREPA's estimate that, by August 2018, all customers who could safely receive electricity had service restored. The report explicitly says this did not mean all predisaster customers, because some buildings were unsafe to reconnect. GAO also records that, as of December 11, 2018, USACE still supported 7 generators powering microgrids on Vieques and Culebra. This section focuses on recovery denominators and conditions of continued support: electricity service can genuinely recover without establishing full restoration of all old customers, original grid configurations, and long-term continuity.
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed pp.6–7: Status of electricity restoration and the temporary-generator passage after Figure 1; PDF pp.10–11
caseNotes.boundary: The report itself openly limits its definition; it is not evidence of deception. Connection counts do not establish recovery of personal lives, health, or all reserves, and no judgment is made about the current grid.

argumentSteps: First declare object, location, population, time window, and demand/capacity types and units, supplying necessary conversion mappings.
Measure actually available capacity, demand, replenishment, and spillover by location, distinguishing peak from sustained capability.
State immediate, carrier-cumulative, and additional-historical-increment claims separately; the latter two require cross-window material, and the last separately requires G3.
Provide proportionate identification grounds for load reduction/replenishment/expansion effects, addressing common shocks and alternative channels.
Recovery claims separately register output, K/F, and internal reserves, listing quantity/quality/continuity/accessibility and internal/external burdens.
Fix numerator and denominator; disclose support conditions, expiry, whether successor uptake is operating, and stress windows not yet experienced.
For renewed instability, distinguish old damage, reserves, support, new shocks, and measurement changes; preserve bounded successes and separately review authority to act.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: overall surplus conceals local shortfall
teachingExamples.text: At two fictional service points in the same hour, demands are 8 and 0 items and available capacities 5 and 5, for comparable tasks. Total demand 8 is below total capacity 10, but if transfer between sites is unavailable that hour, local shortfalls are max(0,8−5)=3 and 0, leaving 3 unfinished. An additional instantaneous, lossless, authorized dispatch channel could move those 3 tasks to the second site and clear this window's shortfall. That is an extra condition, not something totals automatically provide.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Capacity units are items/this hour and demand has a fixed task type; permission for intersite transfer is explicitly separated into two constructions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Not actual organizational data; mathematical dispatchability does not imply real permission or lossless channels.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: output returns before reserves
teachingExamples.text: A fictional system has rated capacity 5, with current damage z reducing available capacity to c=5−z; z stays between 0 and 5 throughout this example. Initially z₀=0. Round 0 demand is 7, giving shortfall g₀=max(0,7−5)=2. This round has no recovery, and the shortfall is written into damage, so z₁=2. Thereafter demand is 3 each round, shortfall max(0,3−c), and recovery is 1 unit through z_{t+1}=max(0,z_t+g_t−1). Round 1: c₁=3, output 3, z₂=1; round 2: c₂=4, output 3, z₃=0; round 3: c₃=5. Output already meets demand in round 1, but available capacity and margin have not returned to 5 and 2.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Stipulated damage-formation and recovery rules; output=min(demand,capacity), with no other shocks, inputs, or capacity adjustments.
teachingExamples.boundary: Real overload need not produce this damage; the model establishes only that “output meets target” and “reserves restored” can occur at different times.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: immediate shortfall need not leave damage
teachingExamples.text: Consider another fictional system with rated capacity 5, capacity fixed at 5 every round, and no retained damage. Demand is 7 in the first round and 3 in the second, giving outputs 5 and 3, with 2 unmet tasks in the first. If unfinished tasks terminate under an explicit rule instead of accumulating, the second round retains no state difference from that shortfall. The prior example's damage equation cannot be imposed merely because a shortfall of 2 occurred.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Explicitly no backlog or persistent damage; unmet tasks still entail loss within that round and are not called impact-free.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not apply to actual objects known to have backlog, persistent harm, or other carriers.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: three true ratios answer different questions
teachingExamples.text: A fictional community had 100 predisaster accounts, now has 90, and 80 meet this round's safe-connection conditions and have all reconnected; there are 70 actual users. Assume the sets and times have been checked with no double counting. Eligible connection rate is 80/80=100%; the reconnected share of predisaster accounts is 80/100=80%; actual usage among current accounts is 70/90≈77.8%. Each numerator and denominator has its own meaning; 100% cannot be rewritten as restored use by every predisaster account.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Pure teaching numbers; connected accounts, actual use, and safety eligibility are different fields. All 80 reconnected accounts are assumed to belong to both predisaster and current sets.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not correspond to actual Puerto Rico population counts or evaluate power quality, continuity, or health outcomes.

counterexamples.text: Average demand is below average capacity, so every location has no load problem.
counterexamples.effect: This does not eliminate local overload or inability to dispatch resources.

counterexamples.text: Temporary generation or continuing external aid remains, so local function never genuinely recovered.
counterexamples.effect: Support can form genuine functional recovery; specify its conditions, continuity, and scope.

counterexamples.text: A new shock causes another interruption, so all earlier records of supply recovery within a bounded period were false.
counterexamples.effect: Different windows and shocks require separate checks; do not erase accurate facts backward or directly presume deception.

counterexamples.text: Central output recovers, so staff rest, spare parts, maintenance backlog, and external caregiving burdens have all recovered.
counterexamples.effect: Obtain separate evidence for output, internal/external reserves, and distribution.

questionAnswers.question: Why can 3 tasks remain unfinished when capacities at two sites total 10 and demand totals 8?
questionAnswers.answer: Demand is concentrated at the first site with capacity 5, and dispatch is unavailable in this window; its local shortfall is not automatically offset by spare capacity at the second site.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: In the damage example, why does output 3 meeting demand in round 1 not establish margin recovery?
questionAnswers.answer: Capacity was only 3 against demand 3, leaving margin 0; the margin of 2 for the same demand at rated capacity 5 had not returned.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If function meets its target with assistive equipment, must the equipment first be removed for recovery to count as real?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Recovery may already hold under the original support conditions. Independent maintenance after withdrawal is a separate claim; necessary support must not be removed merely for validation.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does a 100% connection rate among eligible people imply 100% among predisaster accounts?
questionAnswers.answer: No: the denominators differ. In the construction the former is 80/80, the latter 80/100.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Which explanations should be compared for renewed instability?
questionAnswers.answer: Continuing old damage, unreplenished reserves, support interruption, new shocks, and changed measurement definitions, checking the timing and carriers for each.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: Load definitions: same type/unit/location/window, separating peak and sustained capacity; immediate shortfall: demand enters a specified channel without automatically leaving accumulated damage; cross-window carriers: damage/reserves/backlog, with G3 added only for an additional-history claim; what recovers and for whom: output/K or F/internal margin, without switching numerators or denominators; support and continuity: temporary support can be genuinely effective, with expiry and operating successor uptake checked; distribution and renewed instability: internal rest, external burdens, and separate comparison of old damage/new shocks. Six cards distinguish same-window shortfall, carriers across windows, and recovery conditions; support dependence does not cancel bounded function, nor does bounded function become comprehensive recovery.

6.7.title: 6.7 CM-PHASE Phases and threshold conversion
6.7.lead: A system may operate differently in different ranges, but a kinked curve alone does not show that a particular cause triggered it, still less an inevitable upgrade. First confirm that it remains the same object, then distinguish the evidence required for patterns, triggers, persistence, and history.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1450–1463; source anchor section-6-7; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “The same curve shape cannot supply evidence for any route by proxy.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

The basic dependencies are D0 and D1. Fix the same candidate-object contract and K, preregister state variables, candidate parameters or triggering conditions, and thresholds, and check robustness to noise and binning before testing at least two reproducibly distinguishable operating ranges. “Same K” means more than unchanged wording: the object must continue to satisfy that identity criterion across the compared ranges. If old K has failed, phase terminology cannot conceal object change.

The pattern branch registers only a range–threshold pattern. Its shared methodological gates are E4 and EVIDENCE, requiring treatment of continuous trends, noise, measurement classification, and other competing explanations, but not causal identification as a prerequisite for every pattern classification. Reproducibly observing different ranges does not establish what caused the transition.

Only the causal-trigger branch requires a specified triggering channel, channel intervention or natural variation with identification conditions, and a separate G2-instance locating the triggering effect, adding CAUSAL responsibility. Temporal sequence, changes near a threshold, or predictive accuracy alone cannot eliminate common inputs, reverse effects, or selection; causal claims carry additional material responsibilities beyond pattern registration.

The carried-persistence branch explains how a current carrier maintains a phase, persistence across windows, or delayed recovery under the same K, requiring carrier, timing, longitudinal comparison, and proportionate causal evidence. In this book hysteretic specifically means hysteresis involving historical increment: history still supplies conditional increment relative to an explicit current representation, separately requiring G3. A hysteresis loop in a domain may have its own physical or empirical explanation, but its looped shape alone cannot retrospectively award eligibility for this branch.

If the current carrier already records states determining what follows, the current state may fully take up path effects and additional historical increment may disappear. Basic reversible phases need no historical path at all. A predictive historical comparison does not automatically become historical causation because it is called “hysteresis”; causal triggering, carrier-persistence mechanisms, and historical causal explanations each add proportionate CAUSAL responsibility.

Three contrary situations require different records: if a continuous trend within one state distribution already suffices, discard unnecessary phase partitioning; if thresholds shift with arbitrary binning, prioritize measurement-classification effects; if K fails before transition, examine object conversion, dissolution, or reclassification. A further formal object-conversion claim still follows its corresponding mapping and G4 contract; changing the wording of K cannot automatically certify it.

Robustness does not require every threshold to be identical; it requires specifying in advance the noise ranges, binning choices, and observation windows under which results remain reviewable. Where classification near boundaries is unreliable, retain transition/unresolved regions rather than deleting inconvenient points afterward. Repeated appearance of a region also does not automatically make it an irreversible stage of maturity.

Phases in this section are not a mandatory S0—S6 sequence. A new phase need not be more efficient, more normatively justified, or more authorized; reversal is not automatically regression. Comparing merits, bearing costs, and implementing interventions still require predetermined tasks, norms, and authority, not a direction on a graph.

distinctions.leftText: A repeatably distinguishable region–threshold relationship within the same object.
distinctions.rightText: A change in a specified channel causes a transition between regions; additional identification is required.

distinctions.leftText: The current internal state takes up the past and maintains the phase.
distinctions.rightText: An increment exists beyond the explicit current representation, additionally requiring G3.

distinctions.leftTitle: A loop in a physical curve
distinctions.leftText: May suggest path or state memory, but the model and measurements must be checked.
distinctions.rightText: Cannot be determined solely by shape and is not automatically causal.

distinctions.leftTitle: Different regions of the same object
distinctions.leftText: The object continues to satisfy the original K.
distinctions.rightText: The original K fails or the contract changes; judge separately.

boundaries: The basic pattern has no hard requirement for G3 or every causal gate; an appropriate descriptive pattern may be retained without identifying a trigger.
Repeated regions cannot be artificially manufactured through arbitrary binning; known continuous relationships must be included as competing explanations.
When the current state is already sufficient, zero additional history does not cancel carrier persistence or reversible phases.
K cannot be rewritten after results to obtain a phase conclusion; identity must be checked against the original task and materials.
Physical phases in nature and operating regions in social systems have no automatic equivalence or stage mapping.

Does every phase study require CAUSAL as a basic gate?

caseLinks.title: NIST's triple-point cell: first distinguish physical phases from object boundaries

caseNotes.title: NIST's triple-point cell: first distinguish physical phases from object boundaries
caseNotes.text: NIST's triple-point cell description, published on December 21, 2016, describes a sealed glass container holding water of a specified isotopic composition and a state of equilibrium among solid, liquid, and vapor phases inside the cell. For this section, ‘this sealed container and its contents’ can explicitly be selected as the candidate object before studying its internal phases. This object delineation is the analyst's declaration; the appearance of different internal states of matter cannot automatically be written as replacement of the container object.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: NIST Triple-Point Cell，2016-12-21
caseNotes.sourceLocator: The webpage's single body paragraph (Triple-Point Cell description) and Uploaded On date; this lesson uses the textual description and does not claim to review video measurements
caseNotes.boundary: The source supports a phase-state description of an actual metrological apparatus; it supplies neither complete preregistered threshold/noise tests under this framework nor evidence that any organization has the same phases or a maturity sequence.

argumentSteps: Fix the complete object contract and K, checking that comparison regions continue to satisfy identity; do not change K afterward to preserve the conclusion.
Register states, parameters, thresholds, noise tolerances, and binning tests beforehand, first judging the reproducible pattern.
A pattern reports only relationships between regions; a claim about triggering causes additionally requires G2 for specified channels and proportionate causal identification.
To claim persistence or delayed recovery, locate the current carrier and its cross-window effects; to additionally claim a historical increment, check G3.
Separate predictive historical gains from historical causation; curve shape does not replace branch materials.
Reclassify continuous trends, binning effects, and K failure into their appropriate results; formal conversion claims require a separate check of their contracts.
Preserve the respective scopes of patterns, mechanisms, task merit, and action authorization; do not draw an automatic staircase of maturity.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: two reversible regions without historical memory
teachingExamples.text: A fictional control unit continues to satisfy a predetermined K, with input p∈[0,4] and state rule x=0 when p<2 and x=1 when p≥2; measurement is y=x+ε, with |ε|≤0.1. The two output intervals are [-0.1,0.1] and [0.9,1.1], distinguishable by any classification boundary h∈(0.1,0.9). Inputs 1.5→2.5→1.5 give states 0→1→0, depending only on current p without retaining history. The rule is stipulated within the model, showing that a pattern and reversibility can exist without additional history.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A deterministic state rule with bounded measurement error; p is measured exactly, threshold 2 and the noise bound are specified before calculation, and K does not change with x being 0 or 1.
teachingExamples.boundary: The two regions are mathematical stipulations rather than actual repeated measurements; real-world pattern or causal-trigger qualification still requires its own materials.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: binning can create a false impression of a jump
teachingExamples.text: Let the underlying model instead be y=p, with p varying continuously over [0,4] and no state jump. The reporter publishes only labels L=0 when y<2 and L=1 when y≥2, making the plotted label jump abruptly. Changing the bin boundary to 3 moves the label's jump to 3, while the original y=p remains unchanged. A classification threshold moving with reporting rules is insufficient to establish a phase conversion of the object.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The continuous function is completely known, and the label rule is the analyst's artificial binning; there are no actual observational data.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not deny that discrete classifications can be useful; it shows only that classification use and identification of object phases are different.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a current carrier can sufficiently take up a hysteresis loop
teachingExamples.text: Let state s∈{0,1}, with rule s′=1 when p≥2, s′=0 when p≤1, and s′=s when 1<p<2; output is s′. Path A enters 1.5 from p=0.5, with current s=0; path B enters 1.5 from p=2.5, with current s=1. The same p=1.5 can yield different outputs, but the complete current representation (p,s) already determines the next step; recording only p omits the known carrier s. This model with memory explains why a hysteresis shape does not automatically require additional history beyond the complete current representation.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The rule and initial endpoints are artificially given, with no other noise or hidden states; s must be disclosed, not deleted to manufacture historical gains.
teachingExamples.boundary: Mathematical carrier sufficiency does not deny real-world historical increments; actual comparisons still collect evidence according to the selected representation and G3 conditions.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: identity criteria determine the question's boundaries
teachingExamples.text: For a fictional lamp, if the predetermined K requires that the same numbered housing and wiring components still constitute the apparatus, on/off can be states within the same object. If a different task takes ‘this particular burning flame’ as its candidate object, K may cease to hold when the flame goes out; a newly lit flame cannot universally be called the original object changing phase. The specific K must be stated with the task in advance, rather than chosen freely after observing results.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The objects and criteria are teaching constructions; no K is claimed to be the uniquely natural boundary.
teachingExamples.boundary: Field definitions only declare candidates; they do not establish empirical object validity or formal conversion.

counterexamples.text: First divide a continuous score into two groups using an arbitrary threshold, then use the two groups to prove natural phases.
counterexamples.effect: The classification rule itself cannot serve as independent evidence of an object's regional pattern.

counterexamples.text: Observe a hysteresis loop and declare historical-increment causation established without measuring the current carrier.
counterexamples.effect: Curve shape cannot replace carrier control, G3, and proportionate causal grounds.

counterexamples.text: The original object's identity has already failed, yet it is still described as the same object entering a more mature phase.
counterexamples.effect: This exceeds both object boundaries and the bounds of value upgrading; check conversion/dissolution and evaluate objectives separately.

questionAnswers.question: If a pattern recurs but the triggering channel has not been identified, must the entire pattern description be deleted?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Register the regional relationships in a bounded way under pattern; record triggering causation separately as unresolved.

questionAnswers.question: Why can h=0.5 distinguish noisy states in the first construction?
questionAnswers.answer: The low interval's maximum is 0.1 and the high interval's minimum is 0.9; 0.5 lies in the gap. Any h in (0.1,0.9) works.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: In the hysteresis model, can the next step be uniquely calculated given p=1.5 but unknown s? What if (p,s) is given?
questionAnswers.answer: Knowing only p is insufficient, since s may be 0 or 1; knowing complete (p,s) gives s′=s, so the current carrier determines the future.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does every phase study require CAUSAL as a basic gate?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The pattern branch's common gates are E4/EVIDENCE; claims of causal triggering, carrier-persistence mechanisms, or historical causal explanations add proportionate causal responsibilities.

questionAnswers.question: Why does the appearance of a new phase not directly mean improvement?
questionAnswers.answer: A phase only classifies operating regions; task benefits, costs, norms, and authority require separate judgments.

figures.alt: Common starting point: the same candidate contract with K satisfied, variables, thresholds, noise, and binning. pattern: repeatable regions–thresholds without first claiming triggering causation. causal-trigger: a specified channel and identification comparisons, adding G2 and causal responsibilities. carried-persistence: a current carrier maintains effects across windows, with temporal and causal materials. hysteretic increment: check G3 relative to the current representation; prediction does not automatically become causation. Reverse checks: continuous trends/binning effects, with object checks reopened if K fails. The four branches cannot masquerade as one another; the same curve shape does not establish every mechanism, and a new phase is not automatically better or more authorized.

6.8.title: 6.8 CM-SELECTION variation—differential retention—reproduction
6.8.lead: Seeing a practice or type persist makes it tempting to reason backward that ‘it must be better’. This section first sets aside judgments of merit to examine what variations exist, how outcomes differ, whether the differences actually enter the next round, and whether sampling luck alone is sufficient to explain them.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1464—1477; source anchor section-6-8; short quotation: ‘one instance of persistence is not differential retention’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

D1 only provides rules for using state terms such as change and evolution; ‘evolution occurred’ cannot directly imply selection. CM-SELECTION is a separately operationalized conditional mechanism: E4, CAUSAL, and EVIDENCE handle competing explanations, causation, and material review, while conceptual stories do not generate empirical support. The basic pattern has no hard dependency on G2 or G3, but still requires complete checks of V, D, R, the next round, repeated rounds, and competition with drift explanations.

V consists of distinguishable variations and their sources defined before outcomes; one cannot identify winners first and then treat their shared features as prior variables. D is a differential outcome exceeding a predetermined threshold in comparable environments, with proportionate denominators, exposures, and opportunity conditions; increased population size is not directly equivalent to improved per-unit retention or reproductive capacity. R is the retention that carries this difference into the next round, with repeated rounds available for review, not merely a statistical difference in the current round.

The pattern branch registers a selection pattern with these connections and must compare drift, common external causes, and sampling bias. Random sampling can also produce long-term dominance of a type, and failure to observe another type in a sample may simply reflect missed sampling. If a drift model explains the observations under proportionate sufficiency conditions, do not register a selection pattern beyond it; mere nonsignificance likewise does not establish drift sufficiency, so retain judgment precision and failure records.

Beyond the pattern, the carrier branch identifies which retention or reproduction channel carries the difference, locating it through channel perturbation or natural variation satisfying identification conditions and a G2-instance. If perturbing the candidate channel leaves retention unchanged, it cannot continue to be treated as the claimed specific mechanism; also check whether the perturbation actually took effect, alternative paths, and measurement conditions. Lack of support for a specified channel does not automatically cancel a pattern supported by other materials.

Beyond the pattern, the history branch separately tests conditional increments of cross-round historical terms after controlling for the current state, with G3 support. Repeated rounds are a basic-pattern requirement; an additional historical increment is another requirement. Recurrence does not imply that history remains additionally useful given the complete current state. Conversely, a predictive historical variable alone does not establish V/D/R or selection channels.

When items are missing, stop at the appropriate level: with change but no D, record change; with only one difference but no R, next round, or replication, record a one-time outcome; if drift is sufficient, do not add a selection explanation; if a specified reproductive mechanism has not been distinguished, retain the pattern or candidate without inventing a channel. Results departing from expectations do not permit changing V, thresholds, environments, or historical controls afterward to rescue the original claim.

Being retained does not mean being more advanced, more normatively justified, or even better in every environment and task. A type replicating more under particular conditions is only a bounded process result; environmental changes, tradeoffs, frequency dependence, and coexistence can all limit narratives of ‘winning forever’.

System selection, an agent's choice, and collective governance choices are three different matters. System selection may have no unified decision-maker; agent choice requires a specific agent, options, and decision evidence; collective governance additionally requires normative premises, J-axis authorization, and O procedures. ‘The mechanism retained this institution’ cannot decide public consent on people's behalf or authorize eliminating people and allocating resources.

caseLinks.title: Coexistence in the long-term evolution experiment: selection need not leave only one winner

caseNotes.title: Coexistence in the long-term evolution experiment: selection need not leave only one winner
caseNotes.text: In their original 2008 study, Blount, Borland, and Lenski report in the results section on frequency-dependent selection that, after combining Cit− and Cit+ types at different initial proportions, both coexisted over subsequent rounds; Cit− approached a minority share rather than being completely eliminated by Cit+. The authors interpreted this result as negative frequency-dependent selection maintaining diversity. This section focuses on evidence containing types, trajectories across rounds, and competitive conditions, rather than merely on who remained at the end.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Blount and colleagues, PNAS 105(23):7899–7906, issue dated 2008-06-10
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Results: ‘Frequency-Dependent Selection Maintains Ecological Diversity’, first two paragraphs; Methods: ‘Test for Frequency-Dependent Interaction’
caseNotes.boundary: Retain the ecological conclusion under the original study's bounded conditions; do not retrospectively grant the paper formal G2/G3 status under this framework, extrapolate to every environment, or call retained types more advanced or more normatively justified.

argumentSteps: Before results, define variations and sources, comparable environments, differential outcomes, thresholds, and next-round units.
Separately check D's denominators and opportunity conditions, R's retention connections, and multiple subsequent rounds.
Make proportionate comparisons with drift, common external causes, and sampling bias; do not rely solely on a one-time advantage or long-term existence.
Report the pattern level first; a specified retention/reproduction mechanism additionally requires channel identification and G2. Do not treat names as causation.
For additional cross-round history, separately control the current state and check G3; do not treat repetition itself as a historical conditional increment.
When items are missing, narrow the result to change, a one-time outcome, a pattern, or an unresolved result; explicitly preserve every failure condition.
Moving from process support to values, agent intentions, and governance authority always requires separate bridging materials; no automatic upgrading.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: how differential replication enters the next round
teachingExamples.text: Take fictional marker types A/B, initially 4 each. Each round, each A marker produces 2 same-type successors and each B produces 1, under one rule with no capacity limits, mutation, or random sampling. Round one gives A=8,B=4, with A proportion 2/3; round two gives A=16,B=4, proportion 4/5. Generally, for current proportion p∈(0,1), p′=2p/(1+p), and p′−p=p(1−p)/(1+p)>0. V is the two types defined beforehand, D is their per-unit copy counts 2 and 1, R is retention in same-type successors, and repeated rounds follow the same recurrence.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A fully specified nonbiological marker-copying model, with no actual experiment; deterministic rules exclude random drift by assumption rather than testing it away with data.
teachingExamples.boundary: Proves only differential retention in the specified model, not a real mechanism, indefinitely available resources, or any value superiority of A.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a one-round difference without retention across rounds
teachingExamples.text: Keep the model, but after each round an external rule discards every successor and reinstates 4 A and 4 B. The intermediate 8-to-4 difference remains visible each round, but never enters the next round’s initial state; starting proportions stay at 1/2. If the predetermined question concerns frequency evolution across rounds, intermediate outcomes cannot stand for a completed R chain.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The reset rule is explicit; the unit of analysis is a complete round and the start of its successor. Numbers are constructed.
teachingExamples.boundary: A different question about within-round copying differences can retain the corresponding conclusion; failure across rounds does not deny every local fact.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: pure drift can also fix rapidly
teachingExamples.text: Take a fictional population containing one A and one B. Each generation independently samples twice with replacement, equally likely from either parent marker, copying their types into a next generation still of size 2. The types have no capability difference. The probability that the next generation is all A is (1/2)²=1/4; once all A, absence of mutation keeps it all A. Thus persistent all-A fixation may result from pure sampling rather than a higher per-unit reproduction rate for A.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Sampling rules and no mutation are mathematical assumptions, with equiprobable parents; no actual sampling occurred.
teachingExamples.boundary: ‘Drift is also possible’ does not directly reject all actual selection; reality requires probability comparisons, repeated material, and predetermined criteria.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: repeated selection needs no additional history
teachingExamples.text: In the first construction, current p and the fixed copying rule uniquely determine p′=2p/(1+p). Any two histories reaching the same p yield the same next proportion; history can explain how current p arose but adds nothing to this predetermined next-step prediction. Unrecorded heritable differences, environments, or carriers in reality prevent direct reuse of this sufficiency result.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The current representation contains every state and rule needed in this example, hiding no further differences.
teachingExamples.boundary: The model’s zero additional increment is not evidence for a real G3 null conclusion.

counterexamples.text: Seeing one type persist for a long time is taken to imply necessarily superior differential-retention capability.
counterexamples.effect: Equiprobable drift can produce persistent fixation; other explanations still need comparison.

counterexamples.text: In the relevant ecological comparison in Blount et al.’s 2008 study, Cit+ did not fix; Cit− remained a minority and coexisted with it.
counterexamples.effect: This limits the universal claim that a new advantageous type necessarily eliminates all others; advantage and retention depend on specific environments and frequencies.

counterexamples.text: An institution survived prolonged competition, so everyone chose and consented to it and ought to obey it.
counterexamples.effect: System retention cannot establish agents’ decisions, public consent, or governance authorization.

counterexamples.text: One difference without subsequent tracking is declared an identified cross-round pathway mechanism.
counterexamples.effect: R, the next round, repetition, and current-state controls require distinct missing material; stop at the single outcome.

questionAnswers.answer: A=32,B=4, proportion 32/36=8/9; alternatively substitute p=4/5 into 2p/(1+p).

6.9.title: 6.9 Conditions for Coevolution
6.9.lead: Two people, institutions, or species changing together need not be shaping each other. Coevolution requires checking how each direction acts separately; even if both ultimately return to the same point, their speed, risks, and intervention points along the way may differ completely.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1478–1485; source anchor section-6-9; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘The same final state is not the same mechanism.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

A coevolution candidate requires two candidate objects to change one another’s environments, feasible paths, specified channels, or retention conditions, with both directions traceable in their respective windows. ‘Co-’ refers to an interaction structure, not two rising curves, and guarantees no mutual benefit.

Register two complete D0 object contracts, each with its own identity criterion K and SP/T. One overall system name cannot replace the two objects, and K cannot be called the whole contract. They may have different time resolutions, update cycles, and visible ranges; align event timing and explain when A’s change to B might return to affect A, avoiding a synchronous mechanism invented from surface correlations between daily and annual data.

The two G2 directions carry separate identification responsibilities. Support for A→B does not establish B→A; one intervention changing both simultaneously may not distinguish directions either. Record transmitted content, effect locations, temporal order, comparison conditions, and speed differences, and proportionately test common third-party environmental changes, one-way dependence, and synchronized measurement protocols.

For cross-round effects, follow 4.5 to examine both sides’ current carriers, retention/updating, actual invocation, and longitudinal comparisons separately. Add corresponding G3 only for a further claim of historical conditional increment beyond the current representation. Increment in one direction does not automatically establish increment in the other; persistent carriers on both sides also need not yield extra historical gains on both sides.

Coevolution need not be symmetric. Transmission strength, speed, costs, dependence, and ability to exit can differ greatly; the relation may be antagonistic rather than mutually beneficial. Even established two-way influence does not directly imply aligned values, public consent, an obligation to continue the relationship, or either party’s authority to act upon the other.

The same final state is not the same mechanism. A fixed point remains unchanged after updating; its existence alone does not guarantee trajectory convergence. Only separate proof of convergence permits discussing a trajectory’s long-term limit; update rules also determine return speed, transient peaks, and intervention responses. A simpler representation may suffice if the task asks only for a long-term limit under certain conditions. Once it asks about meeting a threshold within two steps, peaks, whom to change selectively, or performance after support removal, relevant distinctions must be retained and tested again.

Recovery, coevolution, and cross-circle continuity can all share terminal values while differing in process. Two curves eventually approaching each other cannot identify two-way channels; nor can an accurate original long-term summary handle new action tasks automatically. Preserve the scope of ‘which representation suffices for which target, horizon, and operation’ so model simplification is not mistaken for the world’s only mechanism.

A terminal-value summary sufficient for one task is not automatically usable for deadlines, peaks, or targeted intervention.
A relationship’s ability to persist creates no obligation to maintain it; two-way effects can also amplify harm.
