caseLinks.title: Bacteria and bacteriophages: coevolution can be antagonistic

caseNotes.title: Bacteria and bacteriophages: coevolution can be antagonistic
caseNotes.text: The public abstract of Buckling and Rainey’s 2002 original paper reports sustained reciprocal adaptation in bacterial-host resistance and phage infectivity: hosts developed resistance to a broader range of parasite types, while parasites gained infectivity against a broader range of host types. Replicate communities also diverged in their paths of change. This case directly limits the interpretation that coevolution equals mutually beneficial synchrony.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Buckling & Rainey 2002，DOI 10.1098/rspb.2001.1945
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Original paper’s public Abstract, paragraphs two and three; Proc. R. Soc. B 269:931–936, 2002-05-07
caseNotes.boundary: Only the bounded conclusions reported in the authors’ public abstract are retained; this guide did not independently review full methods and data, recertify two-way G2/G3 from the abstract, or generalize to obligations in human relationships.

argumentSteps: Declare complete object contracts for A and B separately, with K, scale profiles, and time windows, ensuring each remains independently traceable.
Specify A→B and B→A channels and changed fields separately, with timing, speed, and comparisons.
Check the two G2 directions separately, distinguishing shared environments, one-way dependence, and synchronized measurement protocols.
For cross-round claims, first examine each carrier route; declare and test additional historical increments separately rather than passing them together.
Treat long-term limits, arrival deadlines, transients, and targeted interventions as different tasks, checking representational preservation for each.
Allow asymmetric or antagonistic coevolution to be reported; values, obligations to continue, and authority require separate consideration.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: the same endpoint, different speed and intervention response
teachingExamples.text: Let two state deviations be z=(x,y). Model A updates x′=0.25x+0.25y, y′=0.25x+0.25y; model B updates x′=0.75x+0.125y, y′=0.125x+0.75y. Maximum row sums are 0.5 and 0.875 respectively, so for every finite initial state ||z_t||∞≤r^t||z₀||∞→0, and both have unique fixed point (0,0). Starting at (1,0), however, A gives (0.25,0.25) after one step and (0.125,0.125) after two; B gives (0.75,0.125) and then (0.578125,0.1875). If the task requires second-step maximum absolute deviation ≤0.2, A passes and B fails. If current y alone increases by δ while x stays fixed, next-step x changes by 0.25δ and 0.125δ respectively, so targeted intervention responses differ too.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Fully specified fixed linear two-state models without external shocks or execution limits; r is the corresponding row-sum bound, and variables are deviations rather than headcounts.
teachingExamples.boundary: This construction proves that terminal values cannot recover a mechanism; it does not independently establish coevolution of real objects or supply an actual intervention proposal.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: shared input can synchronize two curves perfectly
teachingExamples.text: Let external condition U_t vary arbitrarily, with x_t=U_t and y_t=2U_t and no links between them. They synchronize perfectly and may be highly correlated; yet replacing y alone while keeping U and the other rule fixed does not change later x. Testing a two-way relation requires asking separately whether change in each direction is caused by input from the other, rather than omitting the shared U.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An explicit shared-input structure with no hidden cross-terms; all sequences are constructed.
teachingExamples.boundary: A shared environment and two-way relations can coexist in reality; naming a shared input does not automatically negate coevolution.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one contemporaneous table cannot replace two clocks
teachingExamples.text: Fictional A adjusts its supply interface weekly, while B revises its usage rules quarterly. A’s change this week need not appear in B’s report that same week; B’s change next quarter may also arise from other conditions. Record separately when supply actually changes B’s feasible paths and when B’s rules return to affect A, then compare within their respective windows. Copying quarterly totals into weekly rows cannot create more independent evidence merely through more table rows.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Purely a teaching timeline with no institution observed; update cycles are declared beforehand.
teachingExamples.boundary: Neither deny delayed effects from short-run nonsynchrony nor attribute every later change to the earliest A.

counterexamples.text: The two sides are correlated long term, so they necessarily shape each other and both benefit.
counterexamples.effect: Shared input can explain correlation, while mutual benefit is an additional value/outcome judgment.

counterexamples.text: Models A and B both limit to 0, so two-step recovery and targeted intervention are equivalent too.
counterexamples.effect: Second-step values and response coefficients differ; the terminal-value summary has exceeded its use.

counterexamples.text: Only A-to-B causal evidence exists, yet two arrows are drawn and both G2 directions declared passed.
counterexamples.effect: The missing direction must remain unresolved; a diagram adds no evidence.

questionAnswers.question: Why do two models converging to 0 differ on meeting a second-step threshold?
questionAnswers.answer: Maximum row sums bound convergence rates; the particular two-step differences follow from matrix recurrence. From the given initial state, A’s second-step maximum is 0.125 and B’s 0.578125, giving different results against threshold 0.2.

6.10.title: 6.10 Dissolution, object conversion, and repair boundaries
6.10.lead: Repair need not restore every old component, and dissolution need not mean failure. First specify what is to be preserved or regained, then compare which new states achieve that target and who has authority to choose.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1486–1491; original anchor section-6-10. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “It does not turn time back to the old state.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

Dissolution is judged by failure of the original contract's K. K is an identity criterion, not the entire object contract; unchanged wording does not guarantee that the object still meets it. If original K fails while another object contract may hold, distinguish termination, conversion, and reclassification. Continued use of an old name does not establish continued existence of the original object.

The distinction between phase change and dissolution is whether original K still holds. The same object may change operating regime, but when its original identity fails, that change cannot silently be called a “new phase.” A new candidate contract also cannot certify actual object conversion merely by definition. Formal conversion claims require corresponding scale mapping, preservation/loss, G4-route material, and related conditions.

Dissolution does not automatically mean failure, nor continued existence success. Success requires prior objectives, costs, and evaluation criteria. Orderly termination may be a permitted objective, while preserving an old identity may continue harming functions or others. What remains and what has ended must be answered separately from whether preservation is worthwhile.

Repair is judged against K* or F* targets disclosed before results. It may use old traces or replace components, boundaries, relations, interfaces, carriers, or scale positions. A new state meeting the target need not exactly reproduce the past. Conversely, restored appearance, an old name, or recovery of one output does not alone ensure that predetermined K*/F* are met. If only F* was selected, report only that functional achievement without additionally proving original object identity.

“An available repair window” is a more specific empirical claim. Beyond the target, compare how intervention timing affects reachability and cost, specifying permitted measures, resources, delays, and alternative paths. A plan becoming infeasible after some time does not imply every possible plan is permanently hopeless. New resources or technologies change the feasible set and must be disclosed, not used to rewrite the original window conclusion.

Historically formed damage, connections, or capabilities may act as current constraints; trace their formation and present effects through the carrier route. Whether history adds usefulness conditional on complete current constraints is a separate question, and only that question adds G3. Historically caused current damage does not require every repair comparison to prove an additional historical increment.

Empirical reachability confers no implementation authority. Target justification and who chooses, bears responsibility, or may execute require N, J, and O1–O4 review: freeze description and evidence; disclose normative premises and conflicts; compare options including inaction and check authorization; then bound execution, monitoring, stopping, appeal, rollback, and remedies. Technical comparisons for deliberation may be completed first without masquerading as authorized actual disposition.

caseNotes.title: Temporary island microgrids: functional repair need not restore the original connection exactly
caseNotes.text: GAO's 2019 report records that Vieques and Culebra previously received power through submarine transmission lines connected to Puerto Rico's main grid. argumentSteps: Check the original object contract and K, specifying which states still satisfy it and when satisfaction ends.
If K persists, examine phase. If K fails, separately examine termination, conversion, or reclassification; formal conversion additionally requires contract and evidence checks.
Disclose K*/F* before results, listing changeable components/boundaries/relations and task conditions that must not be lost.
Test candidate repaired states against each target rather than requiring every old state to return or judging appearance alone.
A repair-window claim requires comparison of intervention times, permitted measures, reachability, and costs, with the feasible set explicit.
Separate current historical carriers from additional historical increments. Action selection additionally passes N, J, and O1–O4.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: replacing one edge can repair a function
teachingExamples.text: A fictional undirected service network has nodes a,b,c and original edges a—b and b—c, each capacity 4. Task F* is delivery of 4 units of the same quantity type per period from a to c; K* is connectivity among these three specified nodes. Only a supplies and c receives, b conserves flow, and there is no additional flow. The original sole path a—b—c carries 4. If b—c breaks, c is isolated, K* fails, and delivery is 0. A repair adds capacity-4 edge a—c while retaining a—b, reconnecting all three and directly carrying 4. The new edge set differs from the original while satisfying the K*/F* predetermined here.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Graph structure, capacities, and targets are artificial. Inputs/outputs share units and windows, capacities are realizable, and there are no additional losses. K* is only this construction's declared criterion; complete actual objects require further material.
teachingExamples.boundary: Mathematical reachability certifies neither actual networks, deployment authority, nor costs. If original K required preserving every old edge, the conclusion would differ; this must be specified beforehand.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: timing changes reachability, not historical inevitability
teachingExamples.text: Let fictional damage z_t=t for integer times starting at 0. The sole permitted measure removes m damage units once, with 0≤m≤2. After treatment z*=max(0,z_t−m), costing m budget units under budget cap 2. Target F* is z*=0. At t=1, m=1 achieves it at cost 1; at t=2, m=2 achieves it at cost 2. At t=3, every permitted m leaves at least 1, so the target is unreachable. The window under these measures/budget is therefore t≤2, not impossibility of every future repair.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Damage formation, measure range, and cost rule are explicit. There is no additional recovery while waiting or new measure, and t≥0.
teachingExamples.boundary: Only a target-reachability calculation, not a diagnosis of irreversible human conditions. New resources/measures require a newly declared question.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: renaming cannot erase affected positions
teachingExamples.text: Using the disconnected network, registering only a and b as a new two-point service object permits study of that new candidate, but does not restore the original service target for c. Disclose how the new contract handles c, original obligations, and exit losses. Establishing a smaller object does not automatically replace the original object's task.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Pure teaching regrouping; no boundaries of actual organizations or populations are adjusted.
teachingExamples.boundary: A new object's empirical validity, conversion eligibility, and normative adoption require separate evidence, not renaming.

counterexamples.text: The three-node network achieves its target through a new direct edge, so it is declared unrepaired because the old path was not restored.
counterexamples.effect: If the repair target permits relational change, the new state can achieve K*/F*. Historical exactness is not necessary.

counterexamples.text: Failure of original K is taken to mean every social objective failed and the old object must be restored.
counterexamples.effect: Dissolution does not itself supply objectives or obligations; independent evaluation is required.

counterexamples.text: The same repair plan no longer works when applied late, so repair is declared impossible under any technology, resources, or future conditions.
counterexamples.effect: This extrapolates beyond the registered feasible set. Window conclusions must retain their conditions.

counterexamples.text: A plan is feasible in a technical model, so the team claims authority immediately to modify actual records or infrastructure.

6.11.title: 6.11 Overall gate for mechanism outputs
6.11.lead: After writing a mechanism explanation, ask again: what evidence have we actually delivered, and how far may the conclusion go? This overall gate prevents “the system has feedback” from quietly becoming “the system has learned, recovered, and deserves preservation.”
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1498–1501; original anchor section-6-11. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “When items are missing, retain only candidate mechanisms or questions to check.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

The six conditional mechanisms here are feedback, feedback-mediated learning, maintenance, load, phase, and selection. They share eight checks: object and scale declaration, inferential dependencies, enabling conditions, mechanism chain, minimum evidence, competing explanations, counterexamples, and failure boundaries. A common framework does not mean the same evidence for every mechanism or G3 for every branch.

Object and scale declarations specify who is discussed and within which SP/T/K scope. Inferential dependencies state what the conclusion logically relies on; enabling conditions state what the process needs; the mechanism chain connects actual sites of effect. Minimum evidence specifies supporting material; competing explanations check alternatives that could change judgment; counterexamples specify conditions limiting or refuting the claim; failure boundaries state when extrapolation stops or contracts change.

The eight items cannot substitute for one another. Drawing a chain does not supply evidence; listing competing explanations does not exclude them; stating a time window does not establish observational coverage; complete fields do not guarantee semantically correct variables, channels, or authorization references. The overall gate requires substantive proportionality, not certification merely because a table has no blanks.

Each mechanism retains its own conclusion ceiling. Feedback establishes an effective return without cross-round learning. Immediate load concerns a same-window gap without accumulated damage. Basic phase patterns do not include historical-increment hysteresis. Selection patterns do not include specified carrier mechanisms, still less value superiority. Maintenance and repair do not create perpetual preservation duties. Further claims may be proposed, but require the material they actually need.

Missing items leave candidate mechanisms or specific questions to check; broad narratives cannot fill blanks. What pauses is complete mechanism registration at the claimed level, not independently established observations, domain conclusions, or lower-level results. If parameters demonstrably changed but evidence of use is insufficient, for example, retain the update fact and mark carrier-mediated learning insufficiently identified.

Also distinguish “explicit counterevidence” from “material not yet available.” Proof that a necessary condition fails blocks that particular mechanism route. An undetermined necessary condition remains unresolved rather than establishing that the mechanism does not exist in the world. Null conclusions require their own comparisons, sensitivity, and tolerance; failure of positive support is no substitute.

Conceptual explanations and teaching constructions show how contracts work. Exact reproducibility within a construction does not mean an external object follows its rules. Adding one real fact does not automatically empirically validate an entire model. The overall gate helps readers locate gaps without claiming actual reader testing or automatic replacement of domain judgment.

distinctions.leftText: Readable text addresses all eight responsibilities.
distinctions.rightText: Each item has proportionate material and actual tests; existence of text does not establish this.

distinctions.leftText: An explanation worth further examination according to its specific gaps.
distinctions.rightText: Meets the corresponding scope and branch conditions, permitting a bounded conclusion.

distinctions.leftText: For example, a learning-mechanism chain still lacks evidence of actual use.
distinctions.rightText: For example, the parameter change itself may already be confirmed and does not disappear.

distinctions.leftText: A necessary condition cannot yet be confirmed.
distinctions.rightText: Proportionate material refutes a condition or claim; closure differs.

boundaries: The overall gate is a set of substantive responsibilities, not a field counter or a ninth cause in the physical process.
The eight items unfold in logical order; new counterexamples may require revisiting premises. One linear completion does not promise permanent validity.
Failure of one branch does not automatically establish another; each requires its own prior claim and material.
Teaching examples generate no external empirical support, and passing machine validation certifies neither facts nor norms.
Missing items do not erase independently established facts, but prevent combining those facts into a complete claim that remains unsupported.
questions: What is the appropriate conclusion for a report with a parameter file but no use records?
Why do eight c_i values of 1 not imply eight e_i values of 1?
After observing one overload, what must be added to claim delayed recovery?

argumentSteps: First specify which of the six mechanisms, which branch, and which conclusion level is at issue, avoiding interchangeable names.
Check all eight common responsibilities individually, connecting each to material for this object and window.
Explicitly add conditions where stronger claims require them; do not impose G3 or governance permissions indiscriminately on every route.
Distinguish a written explanation, proportionate material, completed testing, and the result obtained.
When items are missing, identify specific candidates/questions and stopping points, preserving independently known facts.
Record counterevidence and unknowns separately; retain distinct statuses for concepts, formal constructions, and actual empirical support.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: locating gaps in a “learning report”
teachingExamples.text: A fictional report accurately records feedback arrival, parameter change, and storage of the parameter file, but contains no material showing that later tasks read that version. The overall gate should neither declare “nothing happened” nor announce completed learning: update facts can be preserved, with gaps in actual use and task differences explicitly listed. If additional material shows that the program always reads the old version, this is more than missing evidence: the use claim has counterevidence.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A fictional arrangement of material, unrelated to an actual organization. Arrival/change/storage are checked by assumption; use is considered in two cases, unknown and known not to hold.
teachingExamples.boundary: This construction is not a diagnosis of actual learning and does not replace evidence collection in real domains.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: eight nonempty fields do not mean eight resolved requirements
teachingExamples.text: Let c_i=1 mean field i contains text, and e_i=1 mean its substantive condition has proportionate support. A model record may have (c₁,…,c₈)=(1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1) while (e₁,…,e₈)=(1,1,1,1,0,0,1,1): minimum evidence and competing explanations remain unresolved. Thus ∏c_i=1 while ∏e_i=0; formal completeness cannot replace substantive completeness. Here e_i is only a teaching logic marker; actual support cannot be created by the author entering a 1.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Binary markers demonstrate logical non-implication. Reality also requires multiple states such as unresolved; 0 cannot uniformly be read as empirical counterevidence.
teachingExamples.boundary: This product is not a recommended automatic fact-certification algorithm; it is only a counterexample.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: blocking smuggled-in conclusions individually
teachingExamples.text: Six fictional statements: return changes a state once → permanent learning; one hour's demand exceeds capacity → cumulative damage must exist; two threshold ranges → additional history must exist; differential-retention pattern → a particular inheritance channel is proved; a device needs maintenance → someone has a permanent obligation; functional repair is feasible → an institution may implement it immediately. Every arrow lacks different bridging material; “complete system mechanism” cannot supply them all.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Composed entirely of constructed inferential leaps, not descriptions of actual people or events.
teachingExamples.boundary: This illustrates gap identification only, without prejudging all conclusions as necessarily false once material is supplied.

counterexamples.text: Eight headings are complete and the JSON passes, so all six mechanism classes hold in reality.
counterexamples.effect: Syntactic completeness generates no object facts, causal support, or normative authorization.

counterexamples.text: The learning route lacks use material, so the earlier parameter-change record must also be false.
counterexamples.effect: Missing higher-level evidence cannot erase lower-level known facts.

counterexamples.text: A claim has not yet been tested, so a null mechanism is recorded as supported.
counterexamples.effect: Not run, unresolved, and null conclusions must remain distinct.

6.12.title: 6.12 Operation Across Asynchronous Multiple Clocks
6.12.lead: A sentence can be heard within seconds, relational expectations may change only after several interactions, and organizational resources and institutional execution have their own cycles. Stamping all changes with the same date both misjudges delayed effects and inflates temporary responses into lasting achievements.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1502–1518; original anchor: section-6-12; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Cross-clock bridges must specify carriers, execution, confirmation, and failure conditions.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

A multi-circle joint state distinguishes at least five clocks: immediate, interactional, organizational, institutional, and long-term. A clock here specifies when a class of variables updates and within what window it is observed, not a fixed universal duration for each event type. One event may first change fast variables, then affect relational expectations through repeated interaction, then change resources through organizational decisions, and finally possibly enter institutional write-back. “May” does not mean that every step necessarily occurs.

The minimum immediate→interactional bridge requires a state difference to persist across multiple rounds and alter the other party's response. A single fading emotion cannot count as a stable interaction rule; equally, before the next round arrives, ineffectiveness cannot be declared prematurely. Record what carrier retains the state, whether subsequent contact occurs, and the other party's actual response.

Interactional→organizational transition requires relational or strategic changes to enter roles, processes, resources, or records. Verbal agreement and a meeting's atmosphere cannot replace implementation; role adjustments, scheduling, budgets, and work-record versions and execution each have their place. A judgment of organizational change still cannot leap directly to all institutional constraints having changed.

The organizational→institutional bridge requires verifiable changes in rules or procedures, arrangements for responsibility, and actual execution. Authorization, legal validity, and normative justification are listed separately. Publishing a document cannot replace execution; unauthorized or disputed conduct also cannot justify omitting institutional effects that actually occurred. Recording facts is neither endorsement nor permission to implement them again.

Institutional→long-term transition requires tracing continuing execution, maintenance, learning, and alternative routes, including checking for rebound after short-term compliance. Long-term is not a label stamped in advance: coverage periods, seasons, demand fluctuations, membership changes, and continuity of support must fit the claimed outcome. If observation ends on a particular date, persistence after that date cannot be fabricated.

Every cross-clock bridge specifies its carrier, execution, confirmation, and failure conditions. The carrier may be parameters, records, schedules, rules, or other states, but must be located. Execution specifies how an update actually enters a process; confirmation specifies where change is independently checked; failure conditions specify when the bridge fails to connect. Reposts sharing one publication source do not automatically add independent confirmation of execution.

Relatively fast results such as industrial expansion, signed agreements, cessation of public violence, completed facilities, and public cooperation may all have real value, yet cannot settle long-term living conditions. Continue checking execution, distribution, rights, relations, and persistence. When material is insufficient, preserve locally known results and stop distant extrapolation, neither canceling local achievements nor inventing final success.

Factual clocks and normative states cannot be merged. If rule changes or execution actually occurred, record them in the process timeline with their corresponding status, even if they violated rules, exceeded authority, or were disputed. Conversely, authorization, publication of an announcement, or an institution's declaration of completion does not mean actual execution at every local position. Both confusions distort causal timelines.

Thus distinguish no short-term change from delayed effects not yet reaching the observation window, and short-term fluctuation from long-term evolution. Update times and observation times may differ; missing records do not automatically mean absent events. But a promise of future effects cannot replace evidence missing now. Report according to each claim's horizon and stop where bridges remain unverified.

boundaries: The five clocks impose neither a universal sequence nor fixed numbers of days; actual processes may interleave, return, or stall.
Every cross-clock bridge can fail. Success at an earlier level does not guarantee the next, and aggregate labels cannot bypass them.
Illegality, excess of authority, or dispute does not turn actual effects into non-events; explaining their formation grants no permission to implement them.
Approval and plans cannot replace execution; temporary non-observation of later effects also cannot justify declaring permanent ineffectiveness without a window.
When long-term material is not yet available, retain unknowns; do not forcibly withdraw necessary support or create dangerous interruptions for verification.

caseNotes.title: Maryland renewals: submission, actual use, and approval have different dates
caseNotes.text: Maryland's 2024 report separately records submission of the mitigation plan to CMS on September 13, 2023, use of the updated renewal process beginning in November 2023, and approval of the plan in February 2024. This section adds the observation that these three event types do not share one timestamp; implementation, plan approval, and long-term results require separate evidence. Temporal order alone cannot determine the legal status of every action at the time, and the report does not use this timeline to establish long-term health effects.

argumentSteps: Declare update clocks and observational coverage separately for immediate, interactional, organizational, institutional, and long-term variables.
For immediate-to-interactional transition, check repeated rounds, state retention, and the other party's response; a single emotion cannot replace them.
For interactional-to-organizational transition, check actual entry into roles/processes/resources/records; for organizational-to-institutional transition, check rules, responsibility, and execution.
For institutional-to-long-term transition, check continuing execution, maintenance, learning, and alternative routes, preserving rebounds and uncovered periods.
For each bridge, locate carriers, execution, confirmation, and failure conditions, distinguishing event time, record time, and publication time.
Register factual records alongside authorization, legal validity, and justification; neither erase events through illegality nor manufacture execution through approval.
Preserve locally known achievements; stop extrapolation beyond the horizon or population and to ultimate effects on living conditions.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: compressing several dates into one produces errors
teachingExamples.text: A fictional system receives feedback on day 0. Two interactions on days 1 and 3 show that the update persists and changes the other party's response. The organization decides on day 5, resources are actually allocated on day 6, a new procedure is published on day 8, and actual execution begins on day 10. If the task requires institutional execution by day 9, this construction fails; the day-8 announcement cannot substitute. If the question is only whether execution had occurred by day 11, one may answer that it had begun. The long-term target runs to day 90, but material covers only day 30, leaving 60 days unobserved. Beginning execution on day 10 is not sustained success through day 90.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Dates, events, and coverage are teaching assumptions. Every bridge is given in the example's text; no actual institution is claimed to operate this way.
teachingExamples.boundary: Meeting a deadline, beginning execution, and sustained attainment differ; lateness relative to day 9 is not permanent ineffectiveness.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: factual and authorization bits do not imply one another
teachingExamples.text: Let E=1 mean an action was actually executed and J=1 mean the construction's prespecified permission contract was satisfied. Case A, (E,J)=(1,0): the action occurred but permission conditions failed; both the fact and the excess-of-authority status must be recorded, without changing E to 0. Case B, (E,J)=(0,1): authorization exists but execution has not occurred, so E cannot become 1. Discussion of legal validity or normative justification requires separate fields; one J bit cannot handle them all.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Explicitly given binary teaching records, not a determination of any actual conduct's legal status.
teachingExamples.boundary: “It happened” cannot imply “it may continue to happen,” nor can authorization establish actual achievements.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an unexperienced season does not cancel current attainment
teachingExamples.text: A fictional facility meets prespecified service-quality targets for one month under ordinary load, with complete records; the next season's peak has not yet arrived. Its function for this month and load range may be confirmed, but year-round peak stability cannot be declared. Conversely, an unverified peak does not turn verified ordinary-period service into zero achievement.
teachingExamples.assumptions: No actual facility or performance data; loads and windows are teaching conditions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Peak evaluation must be safe, feasible, and authorized; the construction does not demand forced stress testing or withdrawal of support.

counterexamples.text: Long-term institutional repair is recorded as complete on the day feedback arrives.
counterexamples.effect: Different update clocks are compressed into one instant, without cross-bridge material.

counterexamples.text: The organization approved the rule, so every local position has implemented it.
counterexamples.effect: Approval differs from execution; positions and times require actual confirmation.

counterexamples.text: The rule change was unauthorized, so it had no effect on the real process.
counterexamples.effect: Normative status does not cancel event facts; record them separately.

counterexamples.text: No long-term effect was seen within one month, so the feedback must have had no effect.
counterexamples.effect: The horizon may be mismatched, or the feedback may truly be ineffective; compare according to the claimed window and bridging evidence.

6.13.title: 6.13 Cross-circle cascades and coevolution
6.13.lead: A message crossing a bridge does not mean people, resources, and action cross along with it. Cross-circle analysis must separate every hop: what exactly was transmitted, on what grounds does the next location change, and where does the process stop?
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1519–1530; source anchor section-6-13; short quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘At every level, recheck the object, channel, scale, and evidence.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

A cascade occurs when a local change in one circle triggers changes in others through channels. Channels may include overlapping membership, bridging interfaces, shared resources, network transmission, or downward institutional action. Membership overlap may let the same person take up two positions; shared resources may transmit use at one location into shortage elsewhere; downward institutional action may change local procedures. These are mechanism types requiring specific identification; their names do not establish that they have occurred.

Re-register objects, channels, scales, and evidence at each level. A change at A and support for A→B do not imply B→C, much less C's long-term outcomes. Observational units, tasks, states, windows, and identity criteria may change across circles; specify their correspondence instead of reusing the first location's effect size or threshold. Insufficient capacity, filtering, delay, cancellation, and local exclusion zones can all interrupt continuation.

First ask what spreads: message arrival, opinion confirmation, adoption, actual cooperation, receipt of funds, and equipment supply are different state variables. A message may cross a single bridge; action may require multiple participants to be available in the same window, confirmation from different sources, and safe on-site conditions. A network path establishes only possible connectivity in the model, not the feasibility of real action.

The same message arriving through three channels may still have only one original basis. Confirmation by different people also requires checking their source relationships and cannot automatically count as statistically independent samples. Even genuine confirmation from separate sources does not mean these people have actually cooperated. A bridge's endpoint determines where signals concentrate; sequence and duration determine whether conditions can be satisfied simultaneously; safety and authority have separate responsibilities.

A failure triggering another requires checking channels, alternative explanations, and effects hop by hop in temporal order. Multiple failures jointly obstructing recovery require checking which recovery resources must arrive together. A shared external cause damaging multiple locations requires checking common exposure. These three graphs may coexist in one accident, but multiple locations having problems cannot uniformly be written as serial contagion.

People's adoption through multiple sources and facilities' supply dependencies may influence one another, but using the same threshold cannot dispense with explanation. The former concerns information sources, trust, intentions, and action conditions; the latter may concern power capacity, logistical accessibility, and material specifications. ‘Needs two neighbors,’ if merely a model rule, is neither a universal law of human behavior nor a physical law of a power grid.

Clustering describes connections among local neighbors, not whole-network coverage directly. Local closure may reinforce signals while concentrating contact in groups already reached, reducing cross-group endpoints and effective multi-source access. A real experiment finding better diffusion in one kind of clustered network can coexist with limited cross-group coverage in another explicit model. Neither may be elevated into a monotonic law for all networks.

Coevolution additionally requires at least two objects to mutually change choice environments, transition probabilities, or constraints over a period, while retaining their respective independent identity criteria K and corresponding object identities. K is only the identity criterion within the complete object contract, not the whole contract. Synchronization from a common external cause alone, one-way influence alone, or return signals that do not alter subsequent states are insufficient for coevolution as defined here.

If the original two objects are merely merged or absorbed, first check nesting, interrupted identity, or object transformation; ‘they are now hard to distinguish’ is not the strongest proof of coevolution. Descriptive object change still differs from formal G4 transformation eligibility, which requires its own transformation evidence. Independently supported domain observations do not become invalid for lacking formal instance status in this framework.

Cascades and coevolution carry no inherent value direction. Tight coupling may aid coordination or amplify vulnerability and diffusion of responsibility; decoupling may sacrifice efficiency or protect autonomy and limit losses. Knowing a channel exists does not permit using it to manipulate people or intervene. Evaluation and action still require the normative level to judge targets, prices to be paid, rights, responsibilities, and authorization.

distinctions.leftText: Information has entered the target's receiving position.
distinctions.rightText: The target possesses and actually satisfies conditions for adoption, cooperation, and resources.

distinctions.leftText: May originate from the same original basis.
distinctions.rightText: Requires checking origins and dependencies, and does not automatically equal actual cooperation.

distinctions.leftText: An earlier failure triggers a later one through a channel.
distinctions.rightText: Multiple supplies jointly determine whether recovery is possible, without necessarily causing each other's initial failure.

distinctions.leftText: The same exposure causes changes in multiple locations.
distinctions.rightText: Each object changes the other's subsequent conditions, requiring separate evidence for each.

distinctions.leftText: A structural feature of connections among neighbors.
distinctions.rightText: Also depends on seeds, bridging, dynamic rules, and action duration.

distinctions.leftText: Object identities are retained separately, with continuing mutual change.
distinctions.rightText: Original object relations or identities undergo a different kind of change; names alone cannot settle it.

boundaries: An established earlier level does not remove later levels' need for their own evidence. Failure may interrupt a chain locally; the choice is not all success or all failure.
The number of source people is not inherently the number of independent samples, and the number confirming is not the number present to cooperate.
Temporal order is one type of information required for mechanism identification; order alone does not establish a causal edge.
Human threshold models, facility-supply constraints, and counts of same-source messages have different semantics and cannot be reused directly by relabeling.
High clustering may strengthen local access or reduce cross-group coverage; both models and experiments must specify their networks, rules, and observed objects.
Check K within each object contract separately; unchanged criterion text does not mean an object still meets it or continues to exist independently.
Serial failure transmission, recovery dependencies, and common causes may mix; do not force every real event into just one graph type.
Edges with insufficient evidence remain unresolved. Failure to find transmission is not proof of no transmission, and model reachability is not observed occurrence.
Explanation, evaluation, and permission have separate responsibilities; efficient coupling does not automatically confer authority to implement.
questions: Can four people forwarding the same report directly count as four independent confirming sources?
If each of two collaborators appears for one hour, why might they still fail to complete one hour of collaboration?
What is the final coverage of the threshold-2 models on a triangular prism and a complete bipartite graph, and why?
Does this overturn real experiments in which clustered networks spread behavior better?
When multiple failures coexist, which three explanations must at least be checked?
A and B exchange information, but B's information never changes A's subsequent conditions. Is that enough for coevolution?
If lower coupling reduces transmission, should decoupling automatically be adopted?

caseNotes.title: The 2010 online-forum experiment: diffusion of registration behavior, not health outcomes
caseNotes.text: Centola randomly assigned participants to clustered lattice and rewired random networks while preserving node degree. The behavior being diffused was registering for a health forum; registered neighbors each triggered invitations. The study reports wider, faster diffusion in the former. The additional point here is signals from different neighbors who have adopted and the network structure; total message-forward counts cannot replace them.

Forum registration does not equal improved health, and the paper establishes neither a universal hard threshold nor a monotonic clustering law. The main text was checked; supplementary material and raw data were not independently verified.

caseNotes.title: Restoring power after the 2017 hurricanes: logistical supply as a condition of recovery
caseNotes.text: In its 2019 report, GAO identifies recovery barriers from documents and interviews: ports and airports in Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands lacked power after the hurricanes, hindering delivery of repair materials; simultaneous recovery in many locations also raised material demand and strained supply. This section adds attention to continuity of recovery resources rather than repeating power-restoration percentages.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: U.S. Government Accountability Office, GAO, report dated 2019-04-18
caseNotes.sourceLocator: GAO-19-296, printed pp.18–19, ‘Logistical challenges’ and ‘Availability of materials’ (PDF pages 22–23)
caseNotes.boundary: The report supports logistical and material constraints during recovery. It cannot establish that every initial failure propagated hop by hop, or justify applying human multi-source-adoption thresholds to electricity and logistics; the complete causal network has not been independently reconstructed.

argumentSteps: Fix the change to explain, starting point, target objects, and window, registering states and scales separately at each level.
Identify whether each edge actually transmits messages, resources, behavior, or rules; specify channels and enabling conditions.
Check starting-point change, arrival, target response, and competing explanations hop by hop. Retain unresolved status at bridges not yet checked; do not continue the chain automatically.
For multi-source claims, check original sources, dependencies, and endpoints; for cooperation claims, check personnel, timing, duration, and feasibility conditions.
Separate serial failure transmission, joint recovery dependencies, and common-cause exposure; map them together if needed, without exchanging edge meanings.
Place clustering, edge counts, and shortest paths within the declared dynamic rules; model calculations prove only within-model results.
When claiming coevolution, check both independent object contracts, mutual change, and the sustained window, excluding one-way effects, common external causes, and absorption.
Report interruption points, local knowns, and out-of-scope unknowns; evaluation or real action requires separate normative and authorization responsibilities.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: three relays, two confirmations, and one action window
teachingExamples.text: Fictional target T receives three messages from P, Q, and R, all traceable to the same record O. If the rule requires two distinct original verification sources, the current source count is 1; three arrivals still fail the requirement. Adding source V later raises the source count to 2, but still does not satisfy a separate ‘two people cooperating simultaneously’ rule. Let the action window be [0,3), with P available only during [0,1) and Q only during [2,3). Their availability intervals have an empty intersection, so action cannot start under this rule. If Q instead is available during [0.5,1.5), the intersection is [0.5,1), only 0.5 units. A requirement of 1 continuous unit still fails; a requirement of 0.5 units is feasible if all other conditions are met.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The fictional rules separately define source deduplication, personnel availability, and duration. Time uses abstract units. Safety, equipment, and authorization are assumed satisfied only in the final feasibility judgment, without claiming actual occurrence. Distinct sources are not additionally assumed statistically independent.
teachingExamples.boundary: This establishes only the nonequivalence of arrival, confirmation, and cooperation; two sources or 0.5 time units cannot be treated as universal real-world thresholds.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: with the same six nodes and degree three, high clustering can still stop at half the network
teachingExamples.text: Take nodes 0–5 in undirected simple graphs. Graph P is a triangular prism with edges 01,12,20,34,45,53 and 03,14,25. Graph B is complete bipartite with partitions {0,1,2} and {3,4,5}, every cross-partition edge and no within-partition edges. Both graphs are connected, have 9 edges, and give every node degree 3. Define a node's local clustering coefficient as the number of edges among its three neighbors divided by 3. In P, every node has exactly 1 such edge, so average clustering is 1/3; in B it is 0. Let the initial active set be A₀={0,1}, with synchronous permanent-activation rule Aₜ₊₁=Aₜ∪{v:|N(v)∩Aₜ|≥2}. In P, only node 2 activates in round one, giving A₁={0,1,2}; each node in the other triangle receives only one cross-group connection, so activation stops at 3 nodes. In B, nodes 3,4,5 each receive from 0 and 1 in round one, giving A₁={0,1,3,4,5}; in round two, node 2 has three active neighbors, bringing the final count to 6. Thus higher clustering does not guarantee greater whole-network coverage in this complex-threshold model. P's node 2 receives local reinforcement in round one, while B's node 2 activates only in round two, also showing that local early progress differs from whole-network success.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Threshold 2, seed positions, synchronous updating, and permanent activation are explicit teaching assumptions. Node identities are fixed, with no outside seeds or decay. The construction can be enumerated exactly; it is not data from a human experiment.
teachingExamples.boundary: This refutes the unconditional rule ‘more clustering means more coverage.’ The two topologies also change cross-group endpoints, so the difference cannot be attributed to an independently controlled causal effect of the clustering coefficient alone. It also does not refute Centola's results under that study's design.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: different equations for three kinds of ‘problems in multiple places’
teachingExamples.text: In the serial-transmission model, failure bit aₜ is fixed at 1, bₜ₊₁=aₜ, and cₜ₊₁=bₜ. Starting from (a₀,b₀,c₀)=(1,0,0), states become (1,1,0) and (1,1,1), with failure entering hop by hop. The recovery model uses p and q for availability of two resources and recovery-feasibility bit r=p∧q: r=0 for 00,01,10 and r=1 for 11. This does not state that p's failure causes q's failure. The common-cause model lets external shock u determine a=u and b=u: when u=1, both fail, still without a→b. All three models can have two failure bits simultaneously equal to 1, but offer different explanations.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Binary deterministic rules serve to distinguish the logic. The serial-transmission example has no repair; the recovery example assumes the two resources are necessary and jointly sufficient; the common-cause example ignores other paths. Here r is the model's recovery-feasibility bit, not evidence that recovery was actually executed.
teachingExamples.boundary: Real events may include all three mechanisms simultaneously; a cross-sectional state alone cannot select one. Model equations also do not themselves establish real causal direction.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two-way information lines are insufficient, and so is a common shock
teachingExamples.text: Two fictional independent organizations A and B each retain complete object contracts. A changes scheduling, changing B's available resource periods; B adjusts supply accordingly, actually changing A's available schedules in the next round. Only this supplies a candidate mechanism of mutual change. If B's reply is archived without entering later scheduling, there is only communication return. If both stop work because of the same external shutdown order, first examine the common cause. If B has lost independent object identity and become an internal unit of A, examine nesting or object conversion instead.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An entirely fictional conditional comparison; “actually changes” is a construction assumption. Reality requires checking versions, execution, alternatives, and both identities, not substituting two drawn lines.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not establish real organizational coevolution or infer normative justification for any restructuring from mechanism feasibility.

counterexamples.text: A network has a shortest path, so it must permit simultaneous action by multiple people.
counterexamples.effect: A message path does not supply an overlapping cooperation window, duration, or action conditions.

counterexamples.text: Three retellings all originate from O but are counted as three independent confirmations.
counterexamples.effect: Repeated sources inflate confirmation counts; successive arrivals may still be real facts.

counterexamples.text: The triangular prism has average clustering 1/3, above the complete bipartite graph's 0, so threshold-2 diffusion must reach more nodes.
counterexamples.effect: The stated models have equal node counts, degrees, and edge counts and are both connected, yet yield 3 versus 6, limiting unconditional generalization.

counterexamples.text: A port power outage obstructs delivery of repair materials, so the port must have caused the grid's initial damage.
counterexamples.effect: A recovery constraint cannot be rewritten as the initial fault's cause; check timing and channels separately.

counterexamples.text: Two objects change simultaneously, or have merged into one object, so coevolution is established.
counterexamples.effect: Common external causes and identity conversion require separate checks; synchronization or merger does not imply mutual change between two objects.

questionAnswers.question: Can four people forwarding the same report directly count as four independent confirming sources?
questionAnswers.answer: No. First deduplicate original grounds and check source relationships. Arrival of four forwards can remain a fact; independent support cannot be accumulated by headcount.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If each of two collaborators appears for one hour, why might they still fail to complete one hour of collaboration?
questionAnswers.answer: If available periods do not overlap, joint duration is 0; even a half-hour overlap fails a one-hour requirement. Total presence time cannot replace simultaneous conditions.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What is the final coverage of the threshold-2 models on a triangular prism and a complete bipartite graph, and why?
questionAnswers.answer: 3 and 6, respectively. In the former, each node of the other triangle has only one active cross-group edge, so diffusion stops. In the latter, all three opposite-side nodes receive both seeds in the first round, then activate the remaining node in the second.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does this overturn real experiments in which clustered networks spread behavior better?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The teaching model supplies a counterexample with different topology, seeds, and deterministic rules; the experiment retains bounded results under its own design and behavioral indicators. Neither automatically becomes a universal law.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: When multiple failures coexist, which three explanations must at least be checked?
questionAnswers.answer: Sequential fault triggering, multiple conditions jointly obstructing recovery, and exposure to common external causes; examine timing, resource dependence, and common-cause material. These may coexist in reality.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: A and B exchange information, but B's information never changes A's subsequent conditions. Is that enough for coevolution?
questionAnswers.answer: Insufficient. Communication return has not produced effective mutual change; independent object identities, persistence windows, and actual effects in both directions must also be checked.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If lower coupling reduces transmission, should decoupling automatically be adopted?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Lost coordination, resource costs, rights, and responsibilities must also be compared under normative and authorization conditions; mechanism effects do not replace reasons for action.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: Sequential faults: A fails → B fails → C fails; check timing and channels at each step. Recovery dependence: resource P and resource Q → feasible recovery R, requiring both together, without inferring P causes Q. Common external cause: shock U → A fails; U → B fails; check common exposure, without automatically adding A→B. Teaching mechanism diagram: sequential effects on the left, jointly necessary conditions in the middle, and common external cause on the right. All three can coexist; multiple faults together do not allow arbitrary choice among explanations.

intro-07-part.title: Part Seven: The Human Structured World
intro-07-part.lead: The same resource channel may appear in machines, organizations, and caregiving arrangements, but human questions additionally ask who understood what, who can decide, who bore the price, and who has the right to refuse. Part Seven connects these questions to the general structural language.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1545–1552; source anchor part_7; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “These interfaces and type definitions do not carry empirical truth on their own.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

H-World is the human adaptation layer. The general layer describes objects, relations, channels, states, and so forth; the human layer addresses intention, meaning, power, institutions, authorization, responsibility, and value. Adding adaptation does not make the general layer automatically produce people's inner states and rights, nor turn human-specific judgments back into universal rules of nature.

The eleven human variables HV01–HV11 and eleven general primitives U01–U11 are managed separately. Equal counts, similar names, or similar functions do not establish item-by-item equivalence. Formal human-interface references use human_variable:HV01 and so on, with claim_type H and contract_role human_variable_interface. Naming the role identifies the kind of question being asked; it does not stamp the variable “fact established.”

GC, GS, GE, CV, RS, IS, IM, and IB are strong type definitions with role strong_type_definition, formally referenced as human_strong_type:GC and so forth. They separate conditions, subjects, events, uptake, responsibility, sources, mechanisms, and behavior, developed individually in the next section. Entering a name in the correct field forms only a judgment to check; classification wording cannot generate causal or responsibility evidence.

Formal G-instances and H1/H4/H5 instances have their own evidence contracts. Internal definitions, interface explanations, and H2/H3/H6 rules cannot themselves support these empirical instances. Domain studies meanwhile retain bounded conclusions actually supported by their objects, designs, and evidence; not using this framework's format does not invalidate all their randomized studies, process records, or direct observations. Formal-instance eligibility and the value of domain evidence are different levels of question.

Before human judgments, register the D0 object contract and scale: specify effective objects, comparison conditions, time windows, observation positions, evidence coverage, affected positions, and J-axis authorization. K within the complete object contract is the identity criterion. Observed populations, visible executors, and affected people may differ; focusing only on the most visible people can wrongly concentrate uptake, costs, intention, and responsibility in one position.

Technology, crises, resources, institutional conditions, or statistical trends do not acquire intention merely by having effects. People, groups, or dissenters do not automatically become destabilization mechanisms, sources, or responsible parties because they are visible, disagree, or stand near a disturbance. This does not deny causal effects of human action; effects, sources, and responsibility each need material relevant to the specific claim.

distinctions.leftTitle: HV and U have equal counts

distinctions.rightText: Requires specific mappings of meaning and effects; equal counts do not supply them.

boundaries: The adaptation layer does not reduce every human experience to one indicator or make framework fields eligibility thresholds for ordinary help and services.
Successful naming or classification carries no empirical truth, but a domain fact need not await a framework label to be acknowledged.
Human judgments must retain J-axis boundaries; seeing someone does not confer authority to collect all their information or intervene.
The same material may bear on multiple questions; preserve source dependence without recounting it as independent verification.
questions: If two catalogs each list eleven items, can their numbering be directly translated item by item?
How should a reliable domain study without a framework instance be cited?
If service software screens out some applications, what should be asked next?
argumentSteps: First determine whether the question is human; where intention, meaning, permission, or responsibility is needed, connect H-World without changing the status of general primitives.
Specify what interfaces, strong types, empirical hypotheses, classification rules, and normative boundaries each do.
First register D0 and SP, separating observation, affected, and execution positions from authorization scope.
Support empirical conclusions with actual object material; separately check formal-instance contracts, without filling evidence gaps by framework self-citation.
Preserve bounded conclusions of independent domain research; reject equating “no eligibility under this framework” with “no evidence.”
Prohibit inferring intention from effects, responsibility from visibility, or interface equivalence from equal counts or names.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: separate a service desk into different questions
teachingExamples.text: At a fictional service desk, software queues applications under rules, staff explain materials, an institution determines resource allocations, and visitors bear waiting costs. The general layer can describe queues and channels; H-World further distinguishes understanding, authority to interpret, decision-making authority, uptake, and cost. Software performing screening is not software with malice; desk staff being most visible does not mean they set allocations or bear all responsibility.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All positions and actions are fictional stipulations; no actual responsibility is adjudicated. Real application requires checking specific roles, knowledge, control, and rules.
teachingExamples.boundary: A teaching example separating questions, not proof of real fault by any institution, software, or staff member.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: eleven items each still allow many pairings
teachingExamples.text: Let U={u₁,…,u₁₁} and H={h₁,…,h₁₁} be sets of names only. There are 11!=39,916,800 different bijections. Equal counts at most allow pairings to be designed; counting cannot select the semantically grounded one. Even specifying u_i paired with h_i still requires explaining what is and is not preserved.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Finite sets illustrate logic only; actual HV and U are not said to require one-to-one correspondence.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not establish any real semantic-equivalence mapping; it demonstrates precisely why counting cannot replace semantic argument.

counterexamples.text: A platform changes behavior, so the platform “wants” those outcomes.
counterexamples.effect: Conditional effects cannot directly be personified as a subject's intention.

counterexamples.text: A study lacks H-instance forms, so all its direct observations and randomized comparisons are worthless.
counterexamples.effect: Formal-eligibility limits cannot revoke the original bounded support of independent domain evidence.

counterexamples.text: People in a queue complain most visibly, so they are the mechanism causing congestion.
counterexamples.effect: Visible expression cannot replace evidence on arrival rates, service capacity, rules, and channels.

questionAnswers.answer: No. The 11! formal pairings do not select the semantically correct mapping, and actual correspondence need not even be one-to-one.

questionAnswers.question: How should a reliable domain study without a framework instance be cited?
questionAnswers.answer: Retain conclusions within the study's design and scope, citing the source accurately; neither retrospectively award unearned formal G/H-instance status nor revoke its evidence.

questionAnswers.question: If service software screens out some applications, what should be asked next?
questionAnswers.answer: Check specific rules, inputs, channels, outcomes, and positions for rulemaking/execution/oversight. Screening effects alone cannot assign intention to software or attribute responsibility to people.

7.1.title: 7.1 H1–H6: role boundaries of human propositions
7.1.lead: ‘This will have an effect’, ‘which category is this?’, and ‘who has a duty to do it?’ are three different questions. H1—H6 are grouped so each bears its own responsibilities, not to treat all six as established laws.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1553—1571; source anchor section-7-1; short quotation: ‘their roles differ, and so do the ways they are established’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

H1, H4, and H5 are empirical hypotheses awaiting instance testing; H2 is an operational rule for typing action uptake and responsibility; H3 is a classification rule for institutional write-back; H6 is a normative boundary for open-ended bearing. Empirical questions require proportionate comparisons and evidence, rules explain how to classify, and normative boundaries restrict what cannot be imposed. The three roles cannot be conflated through one meaning of ‘established’.

H1 tests whether a candidate arrangement of meaning, relative to comparison conditions, produces a difference beyond a predetermined threshold in resource allocation, action selection, or coordination outcomes. An instance preselects only one outcome family and its corresponding criterion; support reaches only a conditional orientation anchor for the specified object and window. Shared slogans, the same language, or successful coordination do not automatically establish a unified inner life, genuine consent, or common will.

H2 separates the actual uptake carrier CV, bearers of commensurate costs, beneficiaries, rights to stop, and responsible parties RS. Who completes a task, who spends time, who benefits, who can stop, and who is responsible on what grounds may occupy different positions. Clear classification does not establish intertemporal reproduction of the work or turn capacity to bear into a duty to bear forever.

H3 registers institutional write-back only when appeals, audits, or feedback change records, rules, resources, roles, responsibilities, memory, or stopping conditions and actual implementation records exist. Acceptance, statements, textual changes, and actual implementation must be separated item by item; one write-back is not feedback-mediated learning, and one update is not long-term repair. Implementation is judged relative to the registered target: if the target is the authoritative record itself, an actual correction with an implementation record permits checking that record's write-back without waiting for another downstream outcome; if the target is a downstream operating state, actual use or execution must be checked. Classification identifies the type of change but cannot establish all its causes or net effects.

H4 tests effects of positions, mediation, or conditions of publicity. Positions, mediation, publicity conditions, outcome quantities, comparison conditions, and thresholds must be explicit beforehand, with one outcome preselected from evidence coverage, safety of expression, object behavior, and reflexive responses. Power, platforms, metrics, and AI are only clue labels requiring actual channels and counterfactual comparisons; silence cannot replace consent, nor can public compliance automatically replace inward agreement.

H5 tests whether a historical event leaves a difference exceeding a threshold in a specified carrier and persistence window. First specify the event, candidate carrier, baseline, trace quantity, threshold, and window; select exactly one of five families—institutional/textual records, role/organizational arrangements, habits/practices, trauma records, and collective-memory carriers—then supply one matching nonempty atomic carrier reference and preselect one persistence criterion. Lists of multiple carriers or mismatched families lack procedural instance qualification before results are even read.

H5's ceiling of support is a candidate trace, not a future path effect. History forming a current record, the current record subsequently being used and changing outcomes, and history retaining an increment beyond the given current representation are three different questions. The second collects evidence through §4.5's current-carrier route; only the third additionally requires a G3-instance. When a carrier sufficiently explains later effects, the additional historical increment may disappear; this does not cancel the carrier's historical formation or actual effects.

H6 requires examining actual costs, voluntariness, direction, alternative explanations, structural consequences, and rights to stop, but does not diagnose whether someone ‘has love’, treat sacrifice as proof, or requisition one party's continued bearing. Absence of high costs or detectable structural success does not deprive concern, mourning, refusal, or other experiences of value; this normative boundary also does not itself authorize deciding for those concerned.

H1/H4/H5 have evidence status requires_instance_evidence; the instance-identity field is claim_id and permits only H1, H4, and H5. They have two phases—freezing before results and reporting results—and four statuses: supported, unsupported_or_undecided, null_supported, and not_evaluated. Positive gates, null-conclusion gates, deviation disclosures, evidence references, and analysis artifacts must actually correspond. Freezing provides a fixed basis for comparison, but actual execution and deviations must still be checked; a file's existence cannot count as success.

Unselected criteria must not rescue a claim afterward; failing the positive gate does not automatically support a null. A null conclusion additionally requires predetermined equivalence or sufficiency judgments, power or sensitivity, and tolerance to pass in practice. Exploration, post hoc deviations, or undisclosed deviations cannot masquerade as formal confirmatory support. The four statuses summarize only; what was refuted and what merely lacks precision or materials must still be explicit.

All six produce only bounded descriptions, classifications, gaps, or normative requirements, without themselves authorizing real adjustments. H2 does not authorize redistribution or attribution of responsibility; H3 does not authorize changing records or rules; H6 does not automatically implement protection or stopping. Actual adoption separately passes C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O1—O4. Analysis and recommendations for deliberation may be offered under explicit premises without pretending permission for actual execution has been obtained.

distinctions.leftText: Await comparisons, evidence, and criteria within instances.
distinctions.rightText: Bound classification and responsibility, without becoming proof of effects through form completion.

distinctions.leftText: Change an institution-related state and actually implement it.
distinctions.rightText: Additionally requires retention, use, task comparisons, and corresponding cross-window evidence.

distinctions.leftText: A specified carrier retains a detectable difference within the window.
distinctions.rightText: Actual carrier effects or additional historical increments each require separate evidence.

distinctions.leftText: The claim is unsupported or unresolved.
distinctions.rightText: Separate null-conclusion materials were frozen and actually passed.

distinctions.leftText: Having the resources or skills to complete a task.
distinctions.rightText: Cannot be inferred directly from capacity, outcomes, or the cost of sacrifice.

boundaries: Support for one H cannot close all six; H2/H3/H6 also do not enter claim_id for H empirical instances.
The same fact may have classificatory value without a causal-mechanism conclusion; correct classification does not replace mechanism evidence collection.
H5's unique carrier does not mean the world can contain only one carrier; it means this formal instance cannot retrospectively select the survivor among multiple candidates.
A null conclusion does not mean there is forever no meaning, power, or history in reality; it is limited to the registered outcome, window, and criterion.
High costs, long-term contributions, and structural success do not independently establish free consent, fair allocation, or unlimited obligations.
Reliably established external domain conclusions may continue to be cited; they are neither revoked for lacking the framework's format nor repackaged retrospectively as preregistered H instances.
