7.3.3.title: 7.3.3 HV03 Orientation anchors
7.3.3.lead: A slogan, memory, or designation can be meaningful without actually changing resources or action. HV03 first understands what it does in practice, then tests whether it has a bounded effect on the selected outcome.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1630–1637; source anchor section-7-3-3; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “Expression itself is not a structural anchor.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

HV03's candidates include goals, identities, memories, commitments, fears, and shared problems. Appendix A3 commonly uses the HV01 interface with E2, EVIDENCE, and SOURCE. R0 may first register meaning-related material, heterogeneous expression, disputes over interpretive authority, and evidence needs; H1 is not a prerequisite certificate for understanding expression. A few positive expressions also do not directly represent group-wide sharing.

The R1 effective-anchor route requires an H1-instance to achieve supported on a uniquely preselected criterion concerning resource allocation, action choice, or coordination outcomes, and to pass corresponding CAUSAL and E4 gates. If the preselected action outcome lacks support, resource changes or coordination signals cannot be selected afterward as success of the original test; a new question may be newly registered without changing the old conclusion.

Meaning is more than belief hidden inside individuals. Public forms may make an expression a request for help, refusal, agreement, or standing to dispute. Separate three questions: how people understand it in context; who has interpretive authority with institutional consequences; and what actions or resource changes actually follow that interpretation. A reasonable interpretation does not establish causal effects, and coordination does not establish shared ultimate beliefs.

Translation across traditions requires more than similar names. Preserve the questions asked in the original practice, interpretive authority, duties, and disputes. One translated term may refer to religious identity, a normative source, legal standing, or personal belief; shared wording cannot combine them into one variable. Results may be partial comparability, local nonalignment, or insufficient material, without labeling a whole tradition “incomparable.”

Translation loss concerns both analytical tasks and affected people's practical questions. Counting two categories as “members” may suffice for headcounts while losing who may draw water, inherit, speak, or refuse. Correct administrative counting does not guarantee a classification fit for allocating rights. HV03 gives no permission to forcibly unify meaning.

boundaries: Strong expression does not imply majority sharing or identified structural effects.
The same word across contexts need not mean the same thing; local nonalignment does not mean entire practices are mutually unintelligible.
A classification fit for one use is not automatically fit for another.
Disputes over interpretation must not justify forcibly unifying participants' meanings.

caseNotes.title: Game names and choices under the same payoff structure
caseNotes.text: In Study 1 of their 2004 paper, Liberman, Samuels, and Ross studied 48 Stanford male undergraduates nominated by dormitory resident assistants. Seven rounds of a prisoner's dilemma used the same payoff matrix under the names Wall Street Game or Community Game; the authors reported more cooperative choices under the latter. In this experiment the name did more than provide a literal description.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Liberman, Samuels, and Ross, 2004, original paper uploaded by an author
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Study 1, Method and Results, printed pp.1176–1177
caseNotes.boundary: The methods and results of this study were read and checked; other studies in the full paper were not counted as reviewed. The selective sample and particular game limit extrapolation. No shared inner beliefs are presumed, no preregistered H1 qualification is retrospectively granted, and arbitrary renaming is not treated as an effective intervention.

argumentSteps: First record expressions, contexts, heterogeneous positions, and interpretive authority, retaining candidate status.
Specify which of resources, action, or coordination is to be tested and its fixed criterion.
Obtain proportionate materials under H1 and its method checks; do not use unselected outcomes to rescue the claim.
When translating, map the original questions, obligations, interpretive authority, and disputes item by item.
Evaluate information loss separately for analytical use and the practical questions of those concerned, bounding the conclusion.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: identical counts cannot determine different water-access entitlements
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional practice, a is a registered member entitled to draw water from a public source, while b is an associated member who participates only in rituals and lacks that entitlement. The analytical mapping f(a)=f(b)=‘member’ correctly counts two people, but the rights function is w(a)=1 and w(b)=0. If one tries to obtain w using only f, the same input ‘member’ must output both 1 and 0, making a correct single-valued function impossible.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The original practice explicitly stipulates these two different entitlements within this construction; this describes no actual religion or culture.
teachingExamples.boundary: This establishes only that the coarse mapping is insufficient for this rights task; it does not claim that the two practices are incomparable as wholes.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: the same reply in different contexts
teachingExamples.text: Fictional interface A asks ‘Have you received the file?’, while interface B asks ‘Do you authorize public release of the file?’; both buttons say ‘I agree’. The two clicks cannot be treated as the same authorization based on identical wording alone; the question, object, consequences, and interpretive rules must be checked.
teachingExamples.assumptions: This is only a semantic and interface-design construction; no actual contract's validity is judged.
teachingExamples.boundary: It cannot replace checks of specific authorization and law.

counterexamples.text: All respondents used ‘responsibility’, so they must share an understanding of the scope of obligations and rights to refuse.
counterexamples.effect: A shared word form cannot replace materials on actual contexts, interpretive authority, and disputes.

questionAnswers.question: Why can a correct “member” count of two people fail to allocate water-drawing rights?
questionAnswers.answer: The mapping erases the distinction between a and b, while the water-access function needs it; one mapping value cannot uniquely determine two different rights outcomes.

figures.alt: a in the original practice has water-access entitlement w(a)=1, by teaching stipulation. b in the original practice has water-access entitlement w(b)=0, by teaching stipulation. Common mapping f records both as ‘member’, still correctly counting 2 people. Can w be determined from f alone? The same input would have to output 1 and 0, preventing a correct single-valued function. a, b, and the water-access rule are teaching constructions; suitability for counting people does not mean suitability for allocating rights.

7.3.4.title: 7.3.4 HV04 generative nodes
7.3.4.lead: The appearance of resources, someone initiating action, and the formation of a new state are often bundled into ‘it was born’. HV04 requires three separate contracts so what is known and what remains conjectural can be seen clearly.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1638—1641; source anchor section-7-3-4; short quotation: ‘three independent contracts: GC, GS, and GE’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

GC comprises generative conditions, GS the agent who understands and performs initiation, translation, or transfer actions, and GE the state transition that occurs. Each separately registers its nine-axis scale, object, window, and materials; a coherent story does not justify sharing one unchecked scale. Technology, crises, and resource windows may be GC candidates but cannot be assigned intentions.

Basic R0 in Appendix A4 has no common hard inferential premise and is constrained by EVIDENCE and SOURCE; it does not have a hard dependency on an effective HV03 anchor. One may first record changes in conditions, agents' capabilities and actual actions, states before and after events, and local-to-whole bridging without a unified agent. An unknown GS is not proof that no agent exists, nor does it invalidate an observed GE.

The R1 mechanism route additionally requires a G2-instance, CAUSAL, and E4 before registering a candidate generative mechanism within the specified channel. Completing strong types separates questions; it does not automatically prove that the three are causally connected by the arrows written. An agent acting without the event occurring, and an event occurring with its mechanism unresolved, may each retain their own statuses.

Cross-scale bridging is especially important: a person's decision, execution of a departmental procedure, and change in the entire organization's state may occupy different organizational levels or time windows. A mapping must show how the local enters the whole and which intermediate positions were unobserved; macroscopic consequences cannot imply a personified ‘system will’.

distinctions.leftText: Resources or institutions make certain actions possible.
distinctions.rightText: Answered through an agent capable of understanding and relevant materials.

distinctions.leftText: The state transition is checkable.
distinctions.rightText: Why it formed requires a separate test and cannot be inferred automatically backward.

distinctions.leftText: The three categories are clearly recorded, including unknowns.
distinctions.rightText: Requires corresponding support for the mechanism route.

boundaries: A technical system may actually affect an event, but GC effects do not confer GS intentions.
A macroscopic event does not guarantee that a particular person designed it.
The three contracts at different scales need explicit bridging; matching names alone cannot connect them.
questions: If the mechanism is unresolved, does GE automatically revert to ‘the event did not happen’?
If GS materials are absent here, may ‘absolutely no agent exists’ be written?
Why must all three contract types register scale?
argumentSteps: Separate a mixed narrative into three questions: conditions, agents, and events.
Record each object's nine-axis scale, direct materials, and unknowns.
Basic typing cannot automatically fill gaps from expressions of objectives or other types.
If a generative mechanism is proposed, check G2 channels and competing explanations, then explain local-to-whole bridging.

teachingExamples.title: Structural-equation construction: conditions and events change together without specifying an acting agent
teachingExamples.text: In an author-constructed system, let an external bit U take 0 or 1, resource condition C=U, two devices output synchronously under fixed rules, and event bit E=U. Recording C and E describes change; no variable represents an agent who understands and initiates action in this window, so the model itself supplies no GS materials. If someone separately established the old rules, that is historical action in another window and cannot silently be treated as the current agent.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The model addresses only the current window and permits prior human design of the devices, although that history lies outside the current contract.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not establish that nobody is responsible in reality or equate an unmodeled agent with an excluded agent.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: three scales must be connected
teachingExamples.text: A issues a start instruction within one minute; a department completes scheduling within one day; the whole station changes service coverage after one week. Even if all three records are true, establishing the specified generative mechanism requires checking whether the instruction entered that schedule, whether the schedule actually ran, and what other changes occurred simultaneously.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Fictional temporal levels; no assumption is made that the three records already satisfy causal bridging.
teachingExamples.boundary: An unclear mechanism does not deny any independently established record.

counterexamples.text: The GC, GS, and GE fields all contain text, so ‘conditions produce events through agents’ is established.
counterexamples.effect: Complete fields do not establish arrows; common external causes, misaligned timing, or different objects may still be present.

questionAnswers.question: If the mechanism is unresolved, does GE automatically revert to ‘the event did not happen’?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Direct state evidence remains valid within its own scope.

7.3.5.title: 7.3.5 HV05 the action-uptake layer
7.3.5.lead: Who actually keeps things going is often hidden in maintenance, reminders, care, and filling gaps. HV05 makes this uptake visible while preventing ‘you can do it’ from becoming ‘you must do it forever’.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1642—1651; source anchor section-7-3-5; short quotation: ‘capacity for uptake also does not generate an unlimited obligation to take up’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

Objects of action uptake may be people, positions, procedures, facilities, or institutions, and the work includes execution, transmission, maintenance, recording, care, and repair. Basic R0 in Appendix A5 has no hard dependency on HV04. Under H2's classificatory restrictions, it separates actual uptake CV from grounds for responsibility RS, recording tasks, resource capacity, costs, rights to stop, alternative arrangements, and positions of decision, authorization, oversight, benefit, and remedy. Facilities may perform functions without thereby becoming responsible parties; organizational responsibility separately depends on institutional standing.

R1 functional effects additionally require G2, CAUSAL, and E4 to explain how a particular carrier affects outcomes. R2 historical-increment reproduction additionally requires G3 to test historical increments beyond the current representation. R3 persistent traces independently depend on an H5-instance, obtaining support for a uniquely preselected specific atomic carrier reference with consistent family/subtype and a persistence criterion. It confirms only traces in the specified carrier and window and may submit a candidate historical variable; it does not itself establish future path effects.

R4 carrier-based intertemporal reproduction requires G2 covering subsequent outcomes and windows, along with §4.5 evidence of formation, retention, maintenance, replenishment or replacement, and actual continuation. It differs from R2: when the current carrier sufficiently carries historical effects, an additional G3 residual is not required. Effectiveness in a previous round also does not automatically cover subsequent rounds; later resources, losses, and replacements must be checked in practice.

Completing a care task and taking over its management are different: identifying needs, scheduling, reminding, checking, and being on call may remain with the original position. Add necessary records only when the research target concerns these burdens, without expanding limited help into unlimited monitoring of the whole person. Claims of ‘overall burden reduction’ must include performers' and managers' costs and their transfer within the same evaluation scope.

Alternative arrangements must also examine replacements' resources, support, refusal, and exit conditions. Heavy burdens may arise from common scarcity; hardship alone cannot establish malicious requisition. The scope and duration of existing duties, continuation requirements, and victims' safety still require separate arguments. A right to stop does not mean arbitrarily shifting risks to others, and existing duties do not automatically become unlimited obligations.

caseLinks.title: Four activities in household cognitive labor

caseNotes.title: Four activities in household cognitive labor
caseNotes.text: In the abstract of her 2019 paper, Daminger states that the study draws on 70 in-depth interviews with 35 couples and distinguishes household cognitive labor into anticipating needs, identifying options, making decisions, and monitoring progress. This section uses those four activities to remind readers that different managerial labor may remain beyond completion of visible tasks.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Daminger，The Cognitive Dimension of Household Labor，2019
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Abstract, published online July 9, 2019, American Sociological Review 84(4):609—633
caseNotes.boundary: Only the original author's published abstract was checked; the full methods were not independently obtained. No actual times, population proportions, or causal effects are calculated, later samples from the researcher are not merged with these 35 couples, and individual malice or love is not judged from burden.

argumentSteps: Record actual uptake and positions of decision, authorization, oversight, benefit, and remedy, typing them under H2.
Clarify whether the question concerns current function, intertemporal reproduction, persistent traces, or additional historical increments.
Supply materials for the complete corresponding R1—R4 route; do not substitute H5 traces for future effects or impose G3 as a hard requirement on the carrier route.
If claiming overall burden reduction, include relevant managerial labor and replacements' costs measured on the same basis.
Separately specify duty scope, resources, duration, stopping, and safe continuation.

teachingExamples.title: Arithmetic construction: transferring execution is not transferring all management
teachingExamples.text: A fictional daily task requires 30 minutes of execution and another 20 minutes in total for identifying needs, scheduling, reminding, and checking, with no overlap in this example. Initially A does everything, totaling 50 minutes. After B takes over execution, A still spends 20 minutes managing and B spends 30 minutes executing. A's 30-minute reduction is real help, while the two-person total remains 50 minutes; ‘A no longer manages anything’ is false.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The same day and quality target, with additive nonoverlapping minutes; emotions or future opportunities are not converted into minutes.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not represent time values in actual households, nor does an unchanged total negate A's bounded benefit.

teachingExamples.title: Logical construction: traces can exist while subsequent effects remain unestablished
teachingExamples.text: Training leaves a version-v1 manual preserved for three months, which may be a trace candidate in a specific document carrier. If nobody consults it and execution procedures do not use it, the manual's continued existence alone cannot imply improved subsequent tasks. Conversely, if a checkable update is repeatedly used and affects tasks, and the current version sufficiently represents the effect, carrier learning or reproduction may hold while the additional historical increment is zero.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The document example is author-constructed and does not claim to satisfy actual H5 or G2; use and effects are conditional statements.
teachingExamples.boundary: Preserving a file is not treated as certification of learning, nor is no G3 gain treated as absence of carrier effects.

counterexamples.text: B performed 30 minutes of tasks, so all A's care management has been taken over.
counterexamples.effect: This omits the 20 minutes of management still borne by A; the local help is real but the conclusion of complete transfer is false.

questionAnswers.question: In the example, A's burden falls by 30 minutes while the two-person total stays unchanged. Is this contradictory?
questionAnswers.answer: No contradiction: an individual's burden and the total within the evaluation scope are different quantities.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If H5 supports persistent traces in a manual, may the next step directly claim improved future tasks?
questionAnswers.answer: No; future use and outcomes require evidence along the corresponding carrier or historical route.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If the carrier sufficiently represents past effects, does no G3 increment deny reproduction?
questionAnswers.answer: It does not deny the carrier route, which requires its own cross-round maintenance, continuation, and causal materials; G3 concerns additional historical increments.

figures.alt: R0 uptake typing: actual CV work/RS grounds, capacity/costs/rights to stop. R1 functional effects: specified carriers change outcomes, with G2 and corresponding causal gates. R3 persistent traces: a specific atomic H5 carrier, without directly establishing future effects. R4 carrier reproduction: maintenance/replenishment/replacement across rounds, later outcomes, and actual continuation. R2 historical increment: gains beyond the current representation, additionally requiring G3. Teaching time: A goes from 50 to 20, B adds 30, total 50; the help remains real. R2, R3, and R4 are different routes, not a numerical hierarchy; the time example must preserve managerial labor and evaluation scope.

7.3.6.title: 7.3.6 HV06 the drive–uptake chain
7.3.6.lead: Having a goal, a start, and people doing the work may still fail to reach the endpoint. HV06 asks whether each segment's output actually becomes the next segment's input, rather than drawing several pieces of good news as a chain already operating successfully.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1652—1657; source anchor section-7-3-6; short quotation: ‘edge means obtained separately cannot be multiplied directly’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

The drive–uptake chain turns orientation and generation into traceable action. R0 in Appendix A6 permits initial registration of local chain segments without requiring all three upstream interface types to be established. Each segment retains inputs, outputs, delays, losses, interruption points, resources, and costs; ‘everyone is highly motivated’ cannot replace missing personnel, funds, or actual handovers.

Only R1’s complete candidate chain requires HV03, HV04, and HV05 interface records connected segment by segment within the same object, scale, window, and quantity mappings. Auditable records are required; three card IDs cannot establish empirical confirmation of each component. If quantity changes, explain conversion, loss, denominators, and applicability conditions; budget amounts are not directly final service volumes.

R2’s effective channel additionally requires G2, CAUSAL, and E4. Besides effects at each segment, it needs correspondence within the same case, common support scope, joint responses, timing, capacity, and terminal outcomes. Two average edge effects may come from people or states that cannot connect; even in the same population, their means cannot be multiplied unconditionally. §11.6 gives an explicit counterexample.

This limit adds proof responsibilities for a specific chain mechanism without revoking a bounded total effect already identified by a qualified design. Terminal effects can hold independently while the intervening channel remains unclear; local changes can also remain valid without passing the entire chain. One successful connection covers only that window; intertemporal reproduction requires subsequent uptake. Additional historical increment separately requires G3, while H5 supplies only historical-carrier candidates.

distinctions.leftText: One segment’s inputs and outputs are checkable.
distinctions.rightText: Segments connect within the same case and quantity mappings, without automatic causal support.

distinctions.leftText: The population average of a local relation.
distinctions.rightText: Whether preceding and following responses meet in the same object states.

distinctions.leftText: A qualified comparison can directly support a bounded terminal difference.
distinctions.rightText: Requires identifying the chain and its bridges as well.

boundaries: The same population does not mean the same responding subgroup; multiplying edge means requires additional conditions.
Upstream spending does not automatically mean downstream receipt, and receipt is not effective use.
An unclear mechanism cannot revoke an independently supported total effect; conversely, a total effect cannot fabricate a mechanism.
A chain working once does not mean resources can be replenished or positions sustainably replaced long term.

caseLinks.title: Ugandan primary-school grants: central government, districts, and schools are different endpoints

caseNotes.title: Ugandan primary-school grants: central government, districts, and schools are different endpoints
caseNotes.text: Reinikka and Svensson’s WPS3239 explains that the 1996 tracking survey covered 250 government primary schools and related administrative records. Researchers obtained detailed central-government and school data. At district level they found records of receipts from the center but no records of disbursement to individual schools. This section concerns differing evidence for receiving endpoints and intermediate bridges.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Reinikka and Svensson, The Power of Information, WPS3239, cover dated December 2003
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed pp. 5–6, II. The pre-campaign situation, survey-design and record-availability passages
caseNotes.boundary: These passages support tracked objects and record gaps; they do not establish embezzlement by specific people, equate missing disbursement records with funds necessarily not arriving, or re-estimate the newspaper campaign’s causal effect in this guide.

argumentSteps: Record actual inputs, outputs, units, timing, losses, and resources for each segment, first allowing local facts to hold.
Record HV03/04/05 interface mappings within the same case, distinguishing unknown from observed bridges.
Check whether actual output from the preceding segment enters the following segment within the same support scope, including capacity and timing.
Whole-chain effect claims require joint and terminal evidence, not substitution of multiplied average edge effects.
Retain independent total effects, local facts, and specific-mechanism gaps separately; cross-period claims need added evidence.

teachingExamples.title: Explicit mathematical development of the original counterexample: two means of 1/2, whole-chain effect 0
teachingExamples.text: Following §11.6, take two equally weighted object types with structural equations M=aX and Y=bM. Type one has a=1,b=0; type two a=0,b=1. Setting X from 0 to 1 changes first-segment M on average by E[a]=1/2; independently setting M from 0 to 1 changes second-segment Y on average by E[b]=1/2. But the whole-chain change in Y caused by X is E[ab]=(1×0+0×1)/2=0, not E[a]E[b]=1/4.
teachingExamples.assumptions: X,M,Y are constructed binary variables, with fixed equations, no other channels, and equal type weights; the second-segment effect concerns a comparison directly setting M.
teachingExamples.boundary: A deductive expansion of the original formal counterexample, not a real causal estimate; it does not say all chain products are wrong, only that sufficient connection conditions are required.

teachingExamples.title: Capacity construction: upstream dispatch does not guarantee timely terminal receipt
teachingExamples.text: A fictional upstream process prepares 8 items in one day, an intermediate stage can review at most 5, and the endpoint needs 8 that day. Each item must pass that review and no alternative path exists. Even if all 8 are submitted upstream, the endpoint receives at most 5 that day, delaying at least 3.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Strict same-day window, one review per item, fixed work-quality and capacity definitions, and no bypass.
teachingExamples.boundary: No actual person is presumed at fault; capacity constraints and normative attribution are separate.

counterexamples.text: Two average edge effects are each 1/2, so the whole chain must be 1/4.
counterexamples.effect: The original two-type construction with mismatched responses gives whole-chain effect 0, refuting unconditional assembly.

questionAnswers.question: Why is the product of two means not this example’s whole-chain effect?
questionAnswers.answer: The whole chain needs a and b simultaneously equal to 1 for the same object; each type’s product here is 0, while separate means lose the joint structure.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If the intermediary handover person is unknown, may a terminal effect supported by an independent trial be denied?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Retain the effect while leaving the specific mechanism unresolved.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: With intermediate capacity 5 and upstream quantity 8, how many items at minimum cannot reach the endpoint that day?
questionAnswers.answer: At least 3 under the listed no-bypass and other assumptions; this does not establish any individual’s dereliction.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: Type one, weight 1/2: externally set X:0→1, a=1,b=0; mediator M=aX gives M:0→1, a first-segment response; outcome Y=bM gives Y:0→0, no second-segment response. Type two, weight 1/2: externally set X:0→1, a=0,b=1; mediator M=aX gives M:0→0, no first-segment response; outcome Y=bM gives Y:0→0, since the responsive second segment received no change. E[a]=E[b]=1/2, but E[ab]=0, not substitutable by E[a]E[b]=1/4; a,b are fixed structural parameters.

7.3.7.title: 7.3.7 HV07 Feedback Write-Back
7.3.7.lead: Receiving comments, opening a work order, changing a draft, and actually bringing a new rule into effect are different events. HV07 traces actual change in the selected target without treating the number of reversed decisions as review quality.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1658–1663; source anchor section-7-3-7; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘One write-back is not learning.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

Feedback write-back means return channels can change subsequent institutional states or transitions. Basic R0 in Appendix A7 depends on D2; H3 sits under specializes, without a hard dependency on HV05. Submission, acceptance, before-and-after field versions, actual execution, taking effect, duration, stopping, and withdrawal require separate records. Return must originate from a prior state or output; an arbitrary external message is not feedback merely because it is input.

Whether something was executed depends on the target. If the target is the authoritative record itself, a formal correction with an execution record may complete write-back for that target. If only a draft exists, or the claim concerns a downstream operating configuration not yet implemented, textual modification cannot substitute for execution. Not all targets must wait for the final downstream action, and not all textual changes are operational changes.

R1 causal feedback additionally needs G2, CAUSAL, and E4, comparing corresponding state changes with return, no return, or channel blockage. R3 carrier-based learning further requires retained updates, invocation over multiple rounds, predetermined task comparisons, and causal evidence covering the claim; see C3-carried-learning and §4.5. Only R2 historical-increment learning adds G3; with sufficient current carriers, extra increment may disappear without negating carried learning.

Hearing and fair procedures may have value while the final target decision stays unchanged. Justifiably upholding the original decision may fulfill review responsibilities and change explanations or records; record these actual changes separately without claiming write-back to an unchanged target. An erroneous reversal may also genuinely change a state, so ‘write-back occurred’, ‘error correction succeeded’, and ‘value improved’ cannot substitute for one another.

distinctions.leftText: Information received and answered.
distinctions.rightText: The specified target’s subsequent state or transition has actually changed.

distinctions.leftTitle: The target is an authoritative record
distinctions.leftText: Formally correcting the record itself may constitute execution.
distinctions.rightTitle: The target is an operating configuration
distinctions.rightText: Check that operating state; drafts or announcements are insufficient.

distinctions.leftText: The decision actually changes.
distinctions.rightText: Requires separate judgment of reasons, evidence, and applicable standards.

boundaries: Do not fabricate a target change to prove procedural value.
Do not delete actual changes to reject an erroneous reversal.
Feedback does not require persistent traces; learning’s stronger requirements cannot be imposed backward on every feedback instance.
Repeating the same slogan many times does not prove invocation of updates.
questions: If the target is the official eligibility record, formally corrected on day 4, why is waiting until day 6 unnecessary?
Why is a control example resetting each round feedback without demonstrated learning?
Must upholding the original decision mean the review has no value?

caseNotes.title: Different process dates in Maryland’s renewal changes
caseNotes.text: Maryland’s health department report states that the relevant mitigation plan was submitted on September 13, 2023, the updated process was used for November 2023 renewals, and CMS approved the plan in February 2024. These three events show why submission, actual use, and approval records cannot be merged into one date.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed p. 9, item 3 (mitigation plan) under Medicaid Mitigation of Ex Parte Renewals and the updated ex parte systems process paragraph following item 5; report April 2024, letter May 14, 2024

argumentSteps: Specify which earlier output the return comes from and the target field or state.
Trace submission, acceptance, draft, formal version, execution, and taking effect by time, judging according to the target definition.
For causal feedback claims, compare return and blockage, checking channels and competing explanations.
For learning claims, check retention, multiple-round invocation, and task comparisons; add G3 only for the extra-history route.
Report procedural quality, write-back facts, correctness, and value direction separately.

teachingExamples.title: Timeline construction: write-back timing depends on the target
teachingExamples.text: A fictional appeal is submitted on day 1, accepted on day 2, drafted awaiting effect on day 3, formally corrects the authoritative eligibility record on day 4, and is actually used by a downstream system on day 6. If the target is only the authoritative record, its actual write-back may be recorded on day 4; if it is downstream processing, check day 6’s execution. The day 3 draft suffices for neither.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Each time point has fictional checkable logs; record correction and downstream processing are two explicit targets, without a claim that processing is necessarily correct.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not prescribe these stages or deadlines for actual institutions.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: one correction does not guarantee learning across rounds
teachingExamples.text: A constructed control task has target r=1 and initial output a=0. A comparator uses actual output to calculate e=r−a=1 and sends it back through a return channel, updating a←a+e=1. Effective return correction occurs this round; if every new round resets completely to a=0 and retains no update, the next round again begins with error 1, so one correction cannot imply lasting learning.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Exact arithmetic, feedback actually produced from the output, complete reset each round, and no hidden memory.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not claim that every system without logs cannot learn; the example explicitly excludes any retained update.

counterexamples.text: More reversals mean higher review quality.
counterexamples.effect: Erroneous reversals also increase the count, while reasoned decisions to uphold may fulfill procedural responsibilities.

questionAnswers.question: If the target is the official eligibility record, formally corrected on day 4, why is waiting until day 6 unnecessary?
questionAnswers.answer: This target was actually changed on day 4; only claims about downstream processing need the corresponding later evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why is a control example resetting each round feedback without demonstrated learning?
questionAnswers.answer: Error returns from the preceding actual output and is corrected, but the update is neither retained nor invoked in the next round.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Must upholding the original decision mean the review has no value?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. Examine reasons and procedures; explanations and records may change, but do not falsely report write-back to an unchanged target.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: Day 1 submission and day 2 acceptance: neither equals a changed target; day 3 draft: revision awaiting effect, not formal execution; day 4 formal record: if the target is the authoritative record, record its write-back; day 6 downstream processing: if the target is an operating state, separately check this execution; learning additionally requires retention/invocation over multiple rounds and predetermined task/causal material; procedure and correctness: upholding may be justified, and erroneous reversal may still write back. These dates are a teaching construction, not Maryland’s actual dates; different targets require different execution evidence.

7.3.8.title: 7.3.8 HV08 Conditional Potential Field
7.3.8.lead: Scores, eligibility, and spatial arrangements may change what people can do, dare to say, or even how they understand themselves. Yet ‘field’ carries no mechanical unit by itself and does not explain how change occurs.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1664–1673; source anchor section-7-3-8; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘The name itself supplies no physical mechanism.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

HV08’s valid object is a set of conditions that changes action probabilities, expressive safety, or evidence distributions through testable channels. Basic R0 in Appendix A8 is constrained only by E2, EVIDENCE, and SOURCE, without a hard H4 requirement. Conditions, heterogeneous positions, blind spots, and additional-evidence needs may first be listed; that list is not an identified unified causal force.

R1 positional or mediating effects require an H4-instance supported on one preselected criterion among evidence coverage, expressive safety, or object behavior, plus CAUSAL and E4. R2 reflexive response also needs E3, showing observation, naming, scoring, or publication actually reaching the object through a channel. A researcher labeling a database cannot establish reflexive change if the object never encounters it and the label affects neither resources nor institutions.

R3 sustained reflexive response additionally traces change into current carriers, checking cross-window retention, later invocation, and sustained effects, and comparing continued external observation, repeated stimuli, shared changes, and other explanations. One behavioral response cannot automatically imply lasting identification. Sustained effects carried by current carriers differ from additional historical residuals beyond the current representation; the latter requires G3.

‘Field’ is only a working name and presupposes no common units, conserved quantities, potential function, or additive forces. A physical-style model requires additional variables, units, mappings, falsifiable predictions, and applicability boundaries. Names such as platform, power, or algorithm cannot replace channels or give conditions wills that ‘want’ or ‘punish’.

Power may also constitute actual feasible options, recognized capabilities, and standards of normal behavior through eligibility, examinations, archives, training, space, and rewards or penalties. Trace category proposal, institutional adoption, resource/opportunity allocation, participants’ responses, and feedback segment by segment. A category’s existence does not guarantee execution, nor does execution guarantee universal acceptance. People may accept, use strategically, conceal, reinterpret, or refuse; public compliance cannot establish identification in reverse.

Capability, communication, legal validity, legitimacy beliefs, and normative legitimacy require separate evidence. Classification may help provide services and appeal channels or produce exclusion. Compare specific practices, alternatives, and positional consequences rather than presuming all classification false or harmful. These are candidate mechanism questions and do not replace H4’s evidence conditions.

caseNotes.title: The difference between a cost proxy target and health needs
caseNotes.text: Obermeyer et al.’s 2019 study notes that a health-management algorithm predicts healthcare spending; at the same risk score, two groups have similar next-year costs but different health needs. This section asks how an adopted classification target affects resource-allocation questions, without equating cost calibration with fairness to needs.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: Science 366, printed pp.447–449, passages on cost as a proxy target and comparisons of costs and health needs at the same risk score

This example did not examine patients changing self-understanding after learning their scores, so it cannot support R2 reflexive identification or R3 sustained reflexive response.

argumentSteps: Distinguish four levels: condition inventory, selected positional effect, actual reflexive channel, and sustained response.
Fix H4's single outcome criterion; results from other families cannot rescue it.
Check how classification enters institutions and resources and actually reaches the object. Without reach, invent no response.
For persistence claims, trace retention and use while excluding repeated stimulation and shared changes.
Separate public behavior, internal acceptance, legal validity, and normative judgment. The word “field” does not waive units or mechanism explanations.

teachingExamples.title: Identification construction: identical compliance can correspond to different acceptance states
teachingExamples.text: Let artificial binary A represent internal acceptance and P visible compliance. Model one has P=A with A=1; model two has A=0 but P=1 to avoid punishment. Observing only P=1 fits both models and does not uniquely imply A=1. Additional distinguishing material is needed; silence is not default consent.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Both models are logical possibilities only. The second motive is a constructed assumption, not a diagnosis of any actual person's motives.
teachingExamples.boundary: The counterexample shows only insufficient observation, not that all compliance is motivated by fear.

teachingExamples.title: Channel construction: separate publication from actual exposure
teachingExamples.text: A fictional researcher labels a group “high potential” in an unpublished table that enters no one's information or resource process. This act alone gives the object no new input. If another version passes the label to an institution and changes training places, trace institutional adoption, place allocation, and actual contact with the object before discussing corresponding reflexive or conditional effects.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Version one explicitly has no direct or indirect reaching channel. Version two specifies only a candidate process without prejudging effects.
teachingExamples.boundary: Absence of direct notification does not exclude all indirect mechanisms.

counterexamples.text: A group label is added to a database, so the group is declared to have adopted that identity.
counterexamples.effect: Evidence of actual reach, adoption, and response is missing, as is evidence of internal identification.

questionAnswers.question: If an object never sees its score but the score changes its training allocation, is a channel necessarily absent?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Resource allocation can be an indirect channel, but actual adoption and consequences still need checking.

questionAnswers.question: Why does P=1 not uniquely imply A=1?
questionAnswers.answer: Internal acceptance and strategic compliance can both generate the same public behavior.

figures.alt: Category proposed: naming/scoring/records do not mean adoption. Institutional adoption: entry into eligibility or resource rules requires actual-execution checks. Actual reach: direct information or indirect opportunities; the reflexive route separately checks E3. Participant response: acceptance/strategic use/refusal; public compliance is not identification. Sustained response: carrier retention/use across windows, excluding explanations such as repeated stimulation. A potential field is not a physical certificate: units/mapping/falsifiable predictions and additional models need additional argument. This is an inventory of channels to test, not a claim that every category takes effect. The original study example did not validate changes in patients' identity identification.

7.3.9.title: 7.3.9 HV09 Structural load
7.3.9.lead: An overall judgment of “enough staff” may coexist with someone continually covering a gap. HV09 compares tasks, capacity, recovery, and positions within one window so averages do not conceal local burdens.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1674–1681; original anchor section-7-3-9. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Retain local overload concealed by averages.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

HV09 relates task and coordination demands to capacity and recovery margins. Appendix A9's basic R0 does not hard-require G2, CM-LOAD, HV05, or HV06. First record margins, backlogs, delays, errors, personnel resources, hidden labor, exit, and recovery within matching windows, positions, and task-type mappings. These facts may have independent domain evidence without prior framework-mechanism eligibility.

Only R1 overload mechanisms add CM-LOAD, G2, CAUSAL, and E4. R3 carrier-mediated cumulative damage or delayed recovery further requires §4.5's current damage/capacity state, formation process, cross-window comparisons, and corresponding causal evidence. R2's historical-increment route beyond the current representation additionally adds G3. Not every long-term burden is an extra historical residual, and unsupported G3 cannot negate directly visible damage.

Capacity must match task type and specific position. Total capacity exceeding total demand does not ensure demand can move to a position with spare capacity; transfer also needs interfaces, skills, resources, time, and authority. Averages cannot be assigned as each person's actual burden. Relief in one place may transfer burden to other households, positions, or the future. Conclusions apply only to the current scope of net evaluation.

Task duration, simultaneous activity, standby, cognitive management, lost sleep, and future opportunities have different units and overlap relations. Elapsed-time accounting cannot simply add overlapping activities; activity-input accounting must specify its meaning and cannot claim to be clock time. Without reasonable conversion, minutes, opportunity losses, and psychological states cannot be added into one social “entropy.”

When tasks require continuous time blocks, record usable block length and predictability in addition to total free time. Default-contact, standby, and last-minute cover responsibilities may rarely activate yet prevent someone committing uninterrupted time to learning, rest, or exit preparation. Add this variable for the specific task, without unlimited collection for every activity.

Teaching scenario: two people each have four free hours daily; one has a continuous two-hour block, while the other has only unpredictable ten-minute gaps. A course requiring two continuous hours has different feasibility for them. “Unable to form a continuous block” cannot be converted into another four hours and added to recorded working hours. Record duration, continuity, predictability, and responsibility arrangements separately.

caseNotes.title: Retaining management labor beyond “making decisions”
caseNotes.text: The abstract of Daminger's 2019 paper distinguishes anticipating needs, identifying options, deciding, and monitoring in material from 70 interviews with 35 couples. It states that gender distributions differ across stages. This section uses that only to caution against treating one stage's allocation as the distribution of all management burdens.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: Abstract, four cognitive activities and explanation of their stage-specific distributions
caseNotes.boundary: The same study is cited under HV05; this is not independent replication. Only the abstract was checked. No mean is assigned to every person, and no clock time, lost sleep, or universal causal mechanism is inferred.

argumentSteps: Fix window, position, task type, capacity units, and recovery indicators.
First register facts and gaps, retaining low-visibility labor and uncollected statuses.
Check local transferability before judging whether totals can serve a specific position.
Distinguish additive quantities, overlapping quantities, and quantities lacking direct conversion.
Choose the corresponding route only when proposing overload, cumulative-damage, or additional-history mechanisms.

teachingExamples.title: Local-capacity construction: total surplus, but position A still lacks 3
teachingExamples.text: Artificial same-day demand is (9,1) and capacity (6,6), measured in counts of the same task type. Total demand 10 is below total capacity 12, but if tasks cannot transfer across positions, the first lacks 9−6=3 while the second has 6−1=5 spare. Total surplus 2 cannot directly close the first position's gap. Feasible handoff would change the question but requires additional conditions.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Tasks cannot transfer across positions, with no overtime, replacement, or advance processing. Both positions use the same unit.
teachingExamples.boundary: A capacity deficit is not automatically attributed to a person, and no claim is made that real reallocation is impossible.

teachingExamples.title: Set construction: simultaneous activities cannot double-count elapsed time
teachingExamples.text: Within a fictional one-hour window, caregiving occupies 40 minutes and telephone coordination 30, with 20 overlapping. Their occupied-time union is 40+30−20=50 minutes. The activity-duration sum 70 minutes may serve as another indicator, but cannot be called 70 elapsed minutes. Whether overlap adds fatigue requires extra evidence and is not determined by the union formula.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Both durations and overlap are known within the construction. Only time is calculated; psychological burden is not equated with minutes.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not imply that parallel labor has no additional cost. The formula does not estimate health consequences.

counterexamples.text: Average capacity exceeds average demand, so overload is declared impossible at every position.
counterexamples.effect: The nontransferable local construction has a deficit of 3 alongside spare capacity 5; an average conclusion is insufficient.

questionAnswers.question: Why can a deficit of 3 remain when total capacity is 12 and total demand 10?
questionAnswers.answer: Demand is concentrated in the first position and cannot transfer. Spare 5 elsewhere is not usable capacity here.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If 40 minutes and 30 minutes overlap for 20 minutes, what is elapsed occupied time?
questionAnswers.answer: The union is 50 minutes; 70 is the sum of activity durations, not elapsed time.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If damage is measured but G3 adds no increment, does the damage disappear as a fact?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Direct states and carrier routes have their own evidence; G3 tests only additional historical information.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: First position: demand 9, capacity 6, deficit 3 when transfer is impossible. Second: demand 1, capacity 6, spare 5 not automatically borrowable. Total: demand 10, capacity 12; surplus 2 does not erase the local gap. Activity A: 40 minutes, overlapping B by 20. Activity B: 30 minutes; union 40+30−20=50. Two measures: summed activity duration 70, elapsed occupied time 50. All values are teaching constructions; 50 minutes does not directly measure fatigue, and a local deficit does not automatically assign responsibility.

7.3.10.title: 7.3.10 HV10 Evolutionary phase
7.3.10.lead: “Forming,” “operating stably,” and “facing conversion” can describe a collective but easily become a supposed ladder everyone must climb. HV10 first limits applicable objects, then checks specific prototypes and stronger phase claims.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 1682–1689; original anchor section-7-3-10. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Naming a phase does not authorize advancement, elimination, or moral grading.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

S0–S6 and X0 apply only to human intentional collectives forming or operating, not similarity-defined categories, populations without evidence of intentionality, or technical systems, nor maturity grading of individual personalities. Meaning, generation, uptake, and institutionalization are dimensions to examine, not components that must all mature before description begins.

All routes in Appendix A10 use auditable assessments of HV03, HV04, HV05, and HV07. The requirement is records, not supported empirical conclusions for all four components. Records may be missing, not_applicable, or unsupported. R0 judges only applicability, inapplicability, or missing components. Filling four names does not assign an S level, while gaps do not prohibit discussing applicability.

R1 descriptions of S0–S6 prototypes check entry conditions, observations, counterexamples, and falsification material item by item under §8.2–8.3 and pass E4. They do not require prior observation of a second operating regime or CM-PHASE. A prototype's own cross-window conditions must still be met: “no universal hard requirement for a second regime” does not mean “temporal evidence is never needed.”

R2's further causal phase-transition claim requires CM-PHASE and G2; R3's phase differences involving additional historical increments require CM-PHASE and G3. R5's current-carrier-maintained phase persistence or delayed recovery requires CM-PHASE, G2 covering the corresponding outcome, and §4.5 longitudinal carrier evidence, without hard-adding G3. Prototype labels cannot replace the mechanism's required multiple regimes and thresholds.

R4's X0 is an independent conversion path, checked against all §8.5 conditions and enterable from any registered origin. No S0–S6 level is a universal prerequisite, and CM-PHASE is not hard-required. Skipping, parallel paths, mixtures, reversals, splitting, merging, dormancy, absorption, and functional transfer may all occur; linear advancement cannot be imposed. No phase name authorizes advancement, elimination, decisions for others, or moral ranking.

distinctions.leftText: Auditably state known, missing, inapplicable, or unsupported statuses.
distinctions.rightText: A stronger empirical judgment, not guaranteed by the former.

distinctions.leftText: A bounded description meeting the specific prototype's conditions.
distinctions.rightText: Requires the mechanism's regimes, thresholds, and corresponding support.

distinctions.leftText: Checks complete conditions such as exit and handoff.
distinctions.rightText: This section supplies no such moral or linear ladder.

boundaries: Human-collective prototypes cannot directly be applied to individuals, populations, or merely similar technical structures.
Missing material is not a “mixed phase.” Mixture also requires positive support for its components.
Prototypes have no universal second-regime requirement, but their individual temporal conditions cannot be omitted.
Phase descriptions grant no authority to exclude members, force advancement, or replace a collective.
questions: Does observing only one operating regime universally prohibit every S-prototype description?
Can a not_applicable record count as one of the four interface assessments?
After classifying a phase as a prototype, may one force advancement to the next stage?
argumentSteps: First check whether this is a human intentional collective and register actual assessment statuses for the four components.
For applicability alone, stop at R0. For a prototype, check its corresponding conditions item by item under §8.2–8.3.
For causal transition, carrier persistence, or additional historical differences, add their respective CM-PHASE and G conditions.
Check X0 as an independent conversion path with complete conditions, not stage numbers as eligibility.
Retain nonlinear paths and missing statuses. Do not promote labels into action or personality verdicts.

teachingExamples.title: Logical construction: assessment records do not mean components are true
teachingExamples.text: A fictional collective's four fields state: HV03 candidate expression recorded; HV04 event evidence missing; HV05 uptake logs recorded; HV07 not_applicable to this question, with reasons. All four are auditable without all components being supported. Applicability and missing requirements can still be assessed, but “4/4 filled” does not establish an S prototype.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Demonstrates record statuses only. No actual object's complete S-prototype entry and falsification material is provided.
teachingExamples.boundary: Neither an empirical phase determination nor a prohibition on collective formation by those lacking material.

teachingExamples.title: Construction against a ladder: a path graph need not have monotone numbering throughout
teachingExamples.text: An artificial allowed-state graph includes S1→S3, S3→S1, and S1→X0. If each arrow has its own conditions, jumps, reversals, and conversions can all be represented. Number changes alone cannot assign moral goodness or badness to actions. X0 completion still requires independent handoff conditions; drawing its arrow is not completion.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A pure path illustration, not a claim that the original book permits every specific object to follow these arrows unconditionally.
teachingExamples.boundary: Shows that linear numbering is not a necessary law, not a prediction about any actual collective.

counterexamples.text: One component is missing, so even applicability to this group is declared undiscussable.
counterexamples.effect: The shared requirement is four kinds of auditable assessment record; missingness can itself be registered. Higher-level conclusions still require further evidence.

counterexamples.text: X0 can occur only after S6.
counterexamples.effect: The original defines X0 as an independent conversion path enterable from a registered origin. Check its conditions rather than imposing a numerical-stage threshold.

questionAnswers.question: Does observing only one operating regime universally prohibit every S-prototype description?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Judge the prototype's specific entry conditions and material, without universally adding CM-PHASE's multiple-regime requirement.

questionAnswers.question: Can a not_applicable record count as one of the four interface assessments?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes, if specifically reasoned, auditable, and genuinely consistent with this question's applicability. It does not mean the component is supported.

questionAnswers.question: After classifying a phase as a prototype, may one force advancement to the next stage?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Description creates no authorization to advance, eliminate, or decide for others.

7.3.11.title: 7.3.11 HV11 Open-Ended Undertaking Action
7.3.11.lead: Some people undertake something voluntarily without succeeding; others act under coercion yet produce effects. HV11 separates voluntariness from consequences, neither using success to prove consent nor failure to deny a real undertaking.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1690–1697; original anchor: section-7-3-11; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Structural success is not an entry condition for R1.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

HV11 reviews actions, costs, direction, voluntariness, real conditions for refusal, and consequences in particular human undertaking arrangements; it does not rigidly depend on HV05. The common protocol gates in Appendix A11 include N4, EVIDENCE, and SOURCE. H6 and H2 serve as normative and classificatory limits, not empirical support; this card itself grants no protection or action authority.

R0 may first register action and cost facts, direction, coercion risks, and gaps in stopping rights. Neither voluntariness nor exclusion of coercion risks must be proved before registering R0 basic facts. Where R1 is unmet, suspend descriptions of open-ended or voluntary undertaking. An R1 bounded description of voluntary undertaking requires evidenced actions and costs, clear direction, and separate support for voluntariness and real conditions for refusal, exit, or negotiation, while examining competing explanations involving dependency, fear, interests, and performance. Verbal willingness or sustained contribution is not an automatic pass certificate.

Record outcomes as actually achieved, not achieved, harmful, or unknown. Structural success is not an R1 entry condition: bounded voluntary undertaking may fail its target. R2 causal judgments of structural consequences separately require G2, CAUSAL, and E4. Coerced behavior may also have identifiable effects; R2 cannot fill in voluntariness retrospectively, and R1 cannot guarantee effects. Facts from different routes must not impersonate one another.

This category is neither a definition or detector of love nor a personality ranking. Easy companionship, concern from people with limited abilities, unsuccessful creation, private mourning, and refusal that creates no new structure do not lose value for lacking high costs or detectable consequences. Conversely, high cost, self-reported goodwill, and long persistence do not automatically prove free consent, fair distribution, or justified obligation.

When material is insufficient, weaken external labels while preserving the person's standing to be heard, protected, and to refuse. Identified risks may warrant further consideration of protection; this does not mean the interface automatically authorizes a measure. Affected people, specific actions, deadlines, and normative grounds still require separate checking. One individual's undertaking cannot be elevated into a whole group's or permanent obligation.

distinctions.leftText: Evidenced actions, costs, direction, and conditions for refusal within a specific arrangement.
distinctions.rightText: A separate judgment about consequences, not an admission ticket to R1.

distinctions.leftText: May actually change outcomes.
distinctions.rightText: May still be coerced despite effectiveness; check independently.

distinctions.leftText: A risk signal warrants considering protection and support.
distinctions.rightText: Specific measures have separate normative and procedural conditions.

boundaries: Costs need not imply free consent, and effects need not imply fair obligations.
Failure does not automatically erase supported voluntary undertaking, and success does not wash away coercion.
This category must not rank love, personality, or group value.
Insufficient material does not cancel standing to be heard or refuse, much less force people to prove sincerity through continued contribution.
questions: Can V=0, Y=1 qualify as bounded voluntary undertaking?
Is V=1, Y=0 logically contradictory?
After observing coercion risk, does this interface automatically authorize any protective measure on the person's behalf?
argumentSteps: First list verifiable actions, costs, direction, and risks without rushing to label a personality or relationship.
For an R1 bounded voluntary description, separately examine consent, refusal, exit or negotiation conditions, and competing explanations.
Independently record whether outcomes were achieved, not achieved, harmful, or unknown; outcomes cannot replace material on voluntariness.
For an R2 causal-consequence judgment, check G2 and causal gates; do not backfill R1 consent.
Limit labeling and action intensity, preserving protection, being heard, refusal, and the boundary between individuals and groups.

teachingExamples.title: Logical construction: voluntariness and effects are two axes
teachingExamples.text: Construct three arrangements: A voluntarily contributes with a real option to refuse, but the target is not achieved, recorded V=1, Y=0; B is coerced into completing a task and achieves the result, V=0, Y=1; C acts voluntarily and achieves the result, V=1, Y=1. These combinations are mutually consistent, showing that Y=1 does not imply V=1 and V=1 does not imply Y=1. Whether each arrangement satisfies formal R1 or R2 still requires corresponding material; binary values illustrate only non-implication.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Voluntariness and outcomes are stipulated facts in the construction. Reality also includes unknown and harmful states and should not be forced into binary form.
teachingExamples.boundary: These three logical points are not assessments of actual people; failure does not imply less love or inferior personality.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching boundary: limited ability and low-cost concern
teachingExamples.text: A fictional person can devote only a little energy to companionship, creates no new institution, and has no quantifiable structural effect. This cannot establish that their concern has no value; the framework's bounded action classifications are not tasked with exhausting human emotional experience.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Illustrates only a classification boundary, without diagnosing any actual relationship.
teachingExamples.boundary: “This interface cannot evaluate it” does not imply “no evaluation is possible.”

counterexamples.text: B's contribution produces a significant result, so B must have freely consented.
counterexamples.effect: Effects and voluntariness are independent; coercion may produce effects while remaining coercion.

counterexamples.text: A failed the structural target, so the earlier voluntary undertaking never existed.
counterexamples.effect: Outcome failure does not automatically refute established facts of action, voluntariness, and conditions for refusal.

questionAnswers.question: Can V=0, Y=1 qualify as bounded voluntary undertaking?
questionAnswers.answer: Effects cannot supply missing voluntariness. Behavioral consequences may be discussed independently, but R1's voluntary condition is unmet.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Is V=1, Y=0 logically contradictory?
questionAnswers.answer: No contradiction: voluntary contribution can fail; honestly record that the result was not achieved.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: After observing coercion risk, does this interface automatically authorize any protective measure on the person's behalf?
questionAnswers.answer: No authorization is granted. Need for protection and permission for specific measures are separate; being heard, norms, and corresponding procedures are still required.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

figures.alt: A: V=1, Y=0, voluntary contribution without success; failure does not erase voluntariness. B: V=0, Y=1, coerced action with effects; success does not supply consent. C: V=1, Y=1, each requires its own evidence, with neither automatically implying the other. R0 basic facts: actions / costs / direction, risks and gaps in stopping rights. R1 bounded voluntariness: real refusal / exit / negotiation, with competing explanations checked. R2 causal consequences: separately requires G2 and causal gates, without diagnosing personality or love. V and Y are teaching binaries; reality also includes unknown and harmful outcomes. Need for protection does not automatically authorize measures.

7.4.title: 7.4 Elevation, Evidence, and Limits on Action
7.4.lead: Seeing more broadly and explaining with greater confidence does not mean being allowed to decide for more people. Section 7.4 separately fixes scope expansion, evidential ceilings, and action permissions, and requires mistaken judgments to be safely challenged and actually withdrawn.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1698–1707; original anchor: section-7-4; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “The level of action must not exceed authorization on the J axis.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

When human variables transfer across scales, compare SP0 and SP1 axis by axis: A aggregation, X space, T time, O organization, C causation, R resolution, I influence, N network, and J jurisdiction and authorization. For each, specify source and target, applicability, actual mappings, preservation, change, loss, and uncertainty, then check low-visibility positions and bounded exclusion zones. Non-applicability needs reasons; insufficient information cannot be called equal, and larger scope cannot uniformly be marked expands.

The six prohibitions on elevation are six missing bridges, not conservative slogans: individual experience to group state lacks aggregation and representation material; local mechanism to the whole lacks extrapolation and coverage; a member's undertaking to group obligation lacks normative and consent grounds; carrier function to responsibility lacks eligibility for attribution; behavior to source or mechanism lacks process and causal evidence; stage or load to moral rank lacks justified norms, and the prototypes themselves do not perform personality judgments. Each fact may be retained without settling a different judgment.

All variables' appeal and rollback fields reference the common appeal_and_rollback_rule. An appeal route cannot be merely a public inbox: it must be safely accessible, protect against retaliation, and provide anonymous, proxy, low-exposure, or delayed methods according to risk and context. The aim is not mechanically identical channels everywhere, but real opportunities for low-power positions, evaluated people, those taking up work, excluded people, dissenters, and those unable to speak publicly to submit counterevidence.

Appeals must also enter review independent of the original judgment or decision chain; closure after the original decision-maker confirms their own decision does not satisfy this. Independence concerns actual personnel, permissions, and dependencies, not renaming the same decision chain. Safety, independent review, and corrective outcomes also require separate checks. Variables describe these procedural needs without themselves establishing or operating real channels.

Once rollback is authorized, specify an executor, completion deadline, target state, version trail, and completion verification. Which objects, records, rules, resources, tasks, rights, and downstream judgments must change depends on the authorized rollback scope. Publishing an apology, accepting an appeal, or promising improvement next time does not mean the specified state has been restored. Irreversible losses cannot be presented as fully rolled back; separately record residual harm and authorized remedies.

Judgment strength is constrained by evidence coverage; action strength by atomic J authorization. These are not one shared high-to-low scale. H1/H4/H5 support strengthens only the corresponding description or explanation, not automatic normative justification. Actual protection, harm reduction, repair, attribution of responsibility, resource reallocation, or formal action still requires C12, explicit runtime N premises, a protection floor, J, and O1–O4. N1 alone can prevent overreach but cannot create a positive proposal from nothing.

C12 also distinguishes analytical recommendations for deliberation from bounded advice already authorized for actual adoption. The former should specify normative premises, evidence, costs, and objections without pretending future execution is already authorized; the latter must satisfy complete authorization and implementation conditions. Lack of execution permission must not erase analysis useful for discussion, nor may an analytical recommendation be treated as permission for actual action.

argumentSteps: First declare source and target objects, nine-axis states, and conclusions; check preservation, loss, and unknowns axis by axis.
Identify required aggregation, extrapolation, attribution, or normative bridges; adjacent facts cannot replace them.
Check whether low-visibility positions can safely submit counterevidence and whether review is independent of the original chain.
Register judgment ceilings separately from J permissions matched to action–object–window combinations.
For proposed actual adoption, check C12, explicit N, the protection floor, and O1–O4; unauthorized actions remain unavailable for execution.
If rollback is authorized, execute and verify explicit targets; announcements or promises cannot close the case.

teachingExamples.title: Set construction: broader observation of objects does not expand atomic permissions
teachingExamples.text: Let a fictional valid authorization set be J={(file A,read),(file B,withdraw)}, with other fields—source, subject, territory, duration, revocability, and so on—fixed and valid. The object set is {A,B}, and action set {read,withdraw}, but their Cartesian product cannot supply four pairs: J does not contain (A,withdraw) or (B,read). If analysis later observes file C, expansion of I or R likewise adds no permission to act on C.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A construction solely about pairing permissions. The tuples abbreviate complete atomic records; no actual file operation is authorized.
teachingExamples.boundary: No actual legal permissions are judged; new atomic authorization requires an independent valid source.

teachingExamples.title: State construction: an explanatory statement and local revision do not equal full-scope rollback
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional authorized correction, three error flags are s=(original record,resource restriction,downstream label), where 1 means the error remains at that position. Initially s=(1,1,1). Publishing a statement without execution leaves s=(1,1,1). Correcting only the original record yields s=(0,1,1), permitting only that portion to be reported complete. Only correction and verification of all three specified states yields (0,0,0). If an already lost opportunity is irreversible, list it as a residual; zeroing the three flags does not mean every harm has disappeared.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All three positions fall within the fictional approved rollback scope and have verifiable states. 1/0 denotes only these error flags, not complete lives or institutional states.
teachingExamples.boundary: Illustrates completion conditions without claiming that every actual correction must restore an identical historical world.

counterexamples.text: A system identifies a person's high load and therefore automatically has authority to resign from their position on their behalf.
counterexamples.effect: A load description supplies neither the person's consent, a positive normative premise, nor authorization for that specific exit action.

counterexamples.text: The original decision group creates a “review group” and reconfirms its conclusion; the new name is treated as independence.
counterexamples.effect: The substantive decision chain is not independent; a label cannot replace independent review.

counterexamples.text: A correction statement has been published, so all downstream rights and resources must already be restored.
counterexamples.effect: A statement guarantees neither execution nor downstream updates; verify each state within the approved scope.

questionAnswers.answer: No. The Cartesian product of object and action sets cannot be taken; that object–action pair requires its own valid authorization.

questionAnswers.question: If one member's experience cannot represent the entire group, does that mean it has no evidential value?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Preserve the facts at that position; elevation to a group requires separate representation, aggregation, or transmission mechanisms.

questionAnswers.question: Must advice for discussion claim that actual execution is already authorized?
questionAnswers.answer: It should not. Normative premises, evidence, and costs may be made explicit for deliberation; complete authorization procedures are required when moving to actual adoption.
