10.5.title: 10.5 Multiple memberships and role conflict
10.5.lead: “Who belongs where” is only a starting point. Knowing who can do what and bear which costs also requires recording entry, participation, exit, and authorization to represent others.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2259–2272; original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-5. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research originals and excerpts remain downloadable in their original versions.

The original states, in translation, “Membership is neither binary nor permanent.” Binary registration may answer whether someone is on a list on a given date, but insufficiently explains actual action. Formal members may lack execution capability; unlisted people may bear key labor or losses. This calls for completing the membership object contract, not rejecting every explicit list. A reliable list can suffice for a narrow task. [T-main；T-simple]

The table distinguishes voluntary, employment, kinship, legal, platform-rule, shared-exposure, and forced entry. These suggest different responsibilities and exit conditions, not specific obligations inferable from identity labels alone. Legal duties require applicable-rule checks, employment requires contracts and actual circumstances. Common exposure means being drawn into effects, not consent to join. “Being in it” is not an authorization document. [T-main]

Participation ranging from core, intermittent, peripheral, and nominal to passively affected locates different positions of information and impact. Core personnel may see only part, while peripheral people may possess unique information. Roles further distinguish decision, execution, care, bridging, supervision, affectedness, and dissent. A core–periphery axis cannot replace these functions, nor can dissent automatically imply low commitment. [T-main]

Commitment may be high, medium, low, disputed, or unknown, but is a task- and time-conditioned record, not a personality grade. High commitment without time, resources, or rights does not establish action capability; unknown cannot be filled as low. Once actual participation is separated from expressed commitment, ask whether mismatches arise from resource limits, role conflict, risk, or material gaps rather than directly attributing motives. [T-main；T-M]

Exit capability distinguishes free exit, costly exit, approval-dependent exit, and practical inability to leave. It is not just a leave-group button: departure may cost income, care, identity, or safety. Inability to leave informs the protection floor and action ceiling, without authorizing researchers to decide for the person or imposing greater responsibility on those unable to exit. Distinguish exit protection from specific responsibilities that remain. [T-main；T-floor]

Multiple identities may create role conflict when simultaneous demands cannot both be met, or one role requires confidentiality and another disclosure. But multiple identities alone do not establish conflict. Identify specific matters, role requirements, deadlines, conflict mechanisms, and possible division of work or recusal. Two coexisting labels do not fill in hostility or dereliction. [T-main；T-rel]

The final paragraph separates cross-boundary connection into three levels. Identifiable interfaces support potential bridging capability; transmission records with recipients and times support process; changed choices or states require separate comparisons. Limited information transmission may genuinely occur even when recipients do not act. Representation also requires specific authorization, and responsibility requires the corresponding matter. Neither follows from “knows people on both sides.” [T-main；T-bridge]

Reusing NASA's report adds the observation that one person's posts cannot collapse into one camp label. The report lists Armstrong's Board, group-oversight, and MSC positions together, establishing only those listed positions. Separate organizational-coordination records cannot all be individually attributed to him, and dual positions cannot invent inner conflict. Historical material supplies both an example and an inferential boundary. [P-NASA]

The strongest objection is excessive cost and possible privacy intrusion from multidimensional person-by-person records. First select necessary fields and windows according to the question, retain unknowns, and allow safe aggregation or self-reports. A five-row table does not compel everyone to disclose their entire history. Simplification is acceptable if it preserves task-necessary exit, authorization, and harmed positions; if these are lost, the original question cannot be claimed completed. [T-main；T-M；T-simple]
argumentSteps: Specify task, observation date, actor, and circle, first identifying necessary membership fields.
Record entry basis, participation, role, commitment, and exit capability separately, plus start/end times and disputes.
Look for incompatibility of specific requirements in matters or timing; multiple identities do not directly establish conflict.
Separate bridging capability, transmission, and outcomes; check authorization and responsibility independently.
Retain unknowns and protections for those unable to leave, using necessary, bearable material for bounded judgments.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: four hours and two role requirements
teachingExamples.text: Within the same four-hour Tuesday window, A's role A requires 3 hours of nonparallelizable work and role B 2 hours. No delegation or postponement is allowed, so total demand 3+2=5 exceeds available 4, leaving a 1-hour gap. The conflict comes from the stipulated window and nonparallelizability, not A's two identities. If B can move 1 hour to Wednesday with permission, same-window demand falls to 4 and this temporal conflict disappears. Confidentiality or authority conflicts still require separate checking.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All people, tasks, and deadlines are artificial. Work can be split by hour without quality changes, and permission is assumed in the counterfactual.
teachingExamples.boundary: A conditional calculation only, not a judgment of actual members' negligence, laziness, or susceptibility to forced overtime.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a message arrives without changing plans
teachingExamples.text: A has explicit contacts in both circles A and B, sends a public meeting time to B's contact, and receives acknowledgment. B already knew the time, so plans do not change. The premise supports actual limited transmission but not an additional action effect. Without representative authorization, it also cannot establish that the sender committed circle A to anything.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Sending, acknowledgment, prior information, and unchanged plans are stipulated. No actual communication was conducted.
teachingExamples.boundary: Separates process occurrence from causal increment, without claiming all information ineffective.

questionAnswers.question: May a caregiver lacking formal membership credentials be removed from analysis?
questionAnswers.answer: Credentials alone cannot justify exclusion. If care is task-relevant, record actual role, cost, and entry basis.
questionAnswers.basis: Multidimensional membership records.

questionAnswers.question: If A sends information to another circle, does that establish she represents the original circle?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Representative authorization for the specific matter requires separate checking.
questionAnswers.basis: Separate bridging, representative authority, and responsibility.

questionAnswers.question: May a highly committed member who failed a task directly be judged dishonest?
questionAnswers.answer: No. First check capability, resources, time, conflicting requirements, and material gaps. Commitment is not a personality verdict.
questionAnswers.basis: The original separates commitment from actual participation.

questionAnswers.question: Suppose two volunteer teams receive the same public warning on the same day. L is listed in both teams, but no cross-team transmission is recorded. May one register “one team transmitted information to the other”?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Both teams receiving the warning establishes only common exposure, registered as shared environment. L's membership in both also does not establish actual bridging. Identifying a usable cross-team interface supports potential bridging capability; actual transmission records establish this limited transmission; any change in the other's arrangements requires corresponding comparisons.
questionAnswers.basis: Final paragraph of §10.5; see §10.3.1 for common exposure versus cross-circle propagation.

10.6.title: 10.6 Material conditions and experience–meaning conditions
10.6.lead: Equipment, money, and time tell us what can be done; experience, trust, and meaning tell us how circumstances are understood. They may interact, but neither can erase the other.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2273–2286; original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-6. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research originals and excerpts remain downloadable in their original versions.

The original requires, in translation, “maintaining M and Ψ together.” M includes body, time, space, funds, energy, equipment, infrastructure, property rights, supply, care, and actual action capability. Ψ includes feelings, expectations, memory, identity, trust, shame, hope, fear, commitment, value conflicts, and perceived legitimacy. The former is more than money, the latter more than emotion and certainly not evidentially inaccessible “subjective noise.” Preserve task-relevant distinctions without demanding common units. [T-main]

The platform example first distinguishes how traffic-rule changes affect visibility and income, then how members interpret falling income, and only afterward whether interpretations change exit, protest, or cooperation. Establishing the first mechanism does not fill the next two. Some may interpret seasonal fluctuation; others may suspect exclusion. These experiences require material, not mind-reading from income curves. Feelings may be directly reported, while their external causes still require comparison. [T-main]

The table's M→Ψ bridge begins with resource, spatial, bodily, or temporal changes and reaches altered experience through perceived safety, control, or identity interpretation. The counterfactual question “Can interpretations differ under the same material change?” guards against treating material quantity as the sole sufficient cause, though observing differing interpretations does not itself isolate all confounding. The Ψ→M bridge requires meaning changes to alter resource flows, labor, property rights, or facility use through cooperation, refusal, migration, care, or protest. Attitude questionnaires without behavior and carriers cannot substantiate that bridge. [T-main]

A closed loop is not decorative double arrows. After M affects Ψ, evidence must show return changing subsequent M or constraints before effective feedback can be registered under D2. Delays, directions, carriers, and counterexamples capable of cutting the chain require separation. Path dependence or phase conversion are candidate outcomes needing additional conditions, not inevitable results of correlation between the two sides. [T-main; T-feedback]

Proportionate treatment of both sides does not mean equal weights. Reliable quantity summaries may suffice for equipment inventories; questions about members' control, welfare, or relationships cannot be answered solely with resource totals if identical resources coexist with different actual control or dignity. Nor may all private experiences be demanded for “complete Ψ.” If material cannot be safely obtained, retain unknown or withheld-for-protection status and narrow conclusions, rather than recording missingness as nonexistence. [T-main; T-simple; T-floor]

The original Cash and Counseling report separately measures service use, satisfaction, and quality of life, suitably illustrating noninterchangeable endpoints. Its intervention combines the opportunity for an allowance, spending plans, counseling, and financial support. Reported group differences cannot be decomposed into pure cash effects or pure perceived-control effects. The observation used here is research design and endpoint separation, not proof of this framework or a causal M↔Ψ loop inferred from simultaneous improvement. [P-CC]

The next two subsections develop differences within M that also cannot be collapsed: §10.6.1 asks how resources become actual opportunities through institutions and positions; §10.6.2 asks how assets, cash, contracts, and financing transmit effects. They supply specific material-path mechanisms rather than reducing this section again to a single monetary indicator. [T-resource; T-finance]
argumentSteps: Specify material and experiential-meaning endpoints and observation windows separately.
For each bridge, list starting points, mediators, outcomes, carriers, directions, delays, and counterexamples.
Distinguish personal reports, others' accounts, and analysts' interpretations; do not fill in one side directly from the other.
Register effective feedback only when return changes subsequent states; retain an unproved closed-loop candidate.
Stop collection according to the task; when differences on both sides matter, totals cannot replace them.

caseNotes.text: The original 2005 report records random assignment of eligible volunteers in three states, followed by a nine-month survey of service use, unmet needs, satisfaction, and quality of life. Allowances came with spending plans, counseling, and financial support. Distinct endpoints and the combined intervention require separate interpretation.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two bridges that need not close
teachingExamples.text: Suppose an artificial platform changes A's visible opportunities from 10 to 6 per week. A reports unease but continues cooperating as usual, and platform metrics do not return any change. The assumptions support an M change and a Ψ report, not Ψ causing resource changes. If B interprets the same change as merely seasonal adjustment, the same material input permits different interpretations; these differences are not estimates of actual psychological effects.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The platform, counts, reports, and behavior are artificial assumptions; succession is not treated as causation.
teachingExamples.boundary: Illustrates evidential levels only, without judging actual users' motives or welfare.

questionAnswers.question: Can increased satisfaction directly replace records of service receipt?
questionAnswers.answer: No. They are different endpoints and should be measured separately.
questionAnswers.basis: The distinction between M and Ψ.

questionAnswers.question: Does one project improving both use and satisfaction suffice to prove a closed loop?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Mediators, direction, return, and comparisons are still needed; a combined intervention also cannot be decomposed into single-component effects.
questionAnswers.basis: Cross-channel bridges in the table and D2.

questionAnswers.question: Must an inventory question involve interviews about every employee's emotions?
questionAnswers.answer: No. If a sufficient inventory summary exists and the task does not concern experience, one may stop.

10.6.1.title: 10.6.1 Resource Conversion and Multiple Positions
10.6.1.lead: Identical nominal resources need not yield identical available options. Trace the eligibility, timing, transport, care, and institutional rules through which resources become usable.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2287–2294; original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-6-1. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain downloadable in their original versions.

“Resources form available opportunities only through specific conversion conditions” (translated from the Chinese) separates resource amounts from feasible options. Income is a period flow that can pay current expenses; wealth is a point-in-time stock that may supply buffers or collateral. Wealth may also be illiquid or unavailable for disposal, qualifications and skills require recognition by relevant institutions, and contacts require others to be capable and willing to help. Having a contact or certificate cannot directly establish that something can be accomplished. [T-resource]

The original list—transport, time, care, legal status, information, and costs of refusal—seeks conversion conditions, not a preliminary vulnerability label for everyone. A free course incompatible with care duties, for example, remains infeasible despite a zero nominal price. Actual disposability depends on ownership, use restrictions, and execution conditions, not just an award notice. [T-resource]

Before adding different quantities, declare units, conversion rules, double counting, weights, and purposes. Income, assets, education, and contact counts cannot be added unqualified into capital or power. Evidenced monetary valuations or task-specific indices may be used, but totals do not supply personal control, eligibility, or welfare. An index's answerable scope comes from its original contract, not the grandeur of its name. [T-resource]

Multiple positions need not be intersections of several circles. One institution may first determine entry timing through admission rules, then rank accumulated seniority, distribute opportunities through uniform evaluation standards, and finally shape correction through remedy conditions. Each rule may look consistent in isolation while early entry differences propagate later. But sequences, denominators at every stage, comparison groups, and absent positions must be traced; endpoint gaps alone cannot identify one rule as the cause. [T-resource]

Category counts, one regression interaction term, or group means are not explanations of individual causes. Groups may contain different positions, periods, and support conditions; people outside the sample especially must not disappear. Additional sensitive classifications must answer an explicit question, have sufficient material support, and impose tolerable privacy costs. If a position cannot be safely observed, record the gap without compelled disclosure or treating the person as nonexistent. [T-resource; T-floor]

This section reuses Cash and Counseling with a new focus on procedural conversion from nominal eligibility to actual receipt. The original report describes spending plans and support processes and finds at nine months that only 39% of elderly treatment-group respondents still living in the community in Florida had recently received an allowance. Preserve that denominator and the “interview month or preceding month” window; it is not a statewide elderly receipt rate. Several candidate explanations exist for interstate differences; the proportion alone cannot identify a personality or single rule as their cause. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that complete records of every conversion condition are difficult to achieve. Work backward from one key option to the most likely constraints, first testing low-cost modifiable items. If a total already sufficiently answers a bounded question, stop. But if the simplified question still asks about control or welfare, preserve conversion differences that change its answer. [T-resource; T-simple]
argumentSteps: Begin with the actual option to be explained, distinguishing nominal from disposable resources.
List units, timing, ownership, uses, and conversion conditions, preventing double counting.
Trace institutional rule sequences and entry denominators at every stage, rather than comparing only those present at the endpoint.
Use appropriate comparisons to judge mechanisms; averages or interaction terms do not automatically establish individual causation.
Collect sensitive positions only according to necessity, safety, and material support.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: nominal 100 and available 20
teachingExamples.text: A and B each receive a one-time 100-yuan training subsidy. Suppose A has no associated costs, while B must first pay 40 yuan for transport and 40 for substitute care; the subsidy permits both uses and no other resources exist. Available course fees are respectively 100 and 100−40−40=20 yuan. A 50-yuan course is feasible for A but not B. An additional 40-yuan care subsidy gives B 60 yuan, crossing that price threshold.

teachingExamples.text: Positions A and B use the same promotion rule, “eligible to apply after two years.” Artificially set A's entry in 2020 and B's in 2021 due to earlier admission conditions. In 2022 A has two years while B does not. A uniform endpoint rule does not erase different starting points. Explaining B's later entry still requires checking admission grounds; years alone cannot establish discrimination.

10.6.2.title: 10.6.2 Balance Sheets, Contracts, and Credit Transmission
10.6.2.lead: Having assets on paper, cash when payment is due, and access to further borrowing are three different things. Trace credit transmission through contracts step by step; co-movement of prices and spending does not itself identify an amplification mechanism.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2295–2302; original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-6-2. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain downloadable in their original versions.

This section first separates measurement definitions: point-in-time stocks are assets or debt on a date, while period flows are income, expenditure, or net financing. Asset valuation is not immediately available cash, principal due is not interest, and net worth is not refinancing capacity. Assets minus liabilities yields meaningful net worth only in the same currency, under the same valuation basis, and on the same date. Positive net worth may still coexist with default due to insufficient cash at maturity; new borrowing increases both cash and liabilities without automatically repairing lost asset value. [T-finance]

Collateral market value, contractual lending limits, actual loan balances, and default recovery respectively address value, ceilings, usage, and recovery after default. Actual limits may depend on haircuts, priority, covenants, and lender judgments. Market value cannot all be treated as borrowable cash, nor loan balances as guaranteed recovery. Missing currency, maturity, contract, repayment priority, or observation-window information may change the comparison. [T-finance]

The candidate amplification chain runs from asset or cash-flow changes through net worth and pledgeable capacity to quotes, credit limits, extensions, or margin requirements, then to net financing, consumption, investment, employment, and subsequent income, returning to asset demand. Each arrow requires a carrier and delay. If constraints are not binding, cash, equity, or alternative loans remain available, or risk-bearing arrangements interrupt transmission, the same strength of self-reinforcement claim should not be retained. [T-finance]

Identifying financial acceleration requires excluding shared drivers. Profit expectations, interest rates, or policy may simultaneously move asset prices and spending; temporal order and positive correlation remain insufficient. Bernanke's 2007 personal review of research discusses both mechanisms and identification difficulties, including cash flow as a possible proxy for investment returns and alternative lending weakening bank transmission. This is a fact about historical research discussion; the speech does not establish that the mechanism caused any particular crisis. [P-FED; T-finance]

At the network level, five paths differ: common exposure means multiple parties hold the same risk source; direct-credit default is a contractual connection through debt nonpayment; guarantee calls activate contingent payment obligations; fire-sale price spillovers affect parties without direct lending ties through market prices; and information-induced withdrawals alter financing through beliefs and actions. These may coexist but cannot be drawn as one generic “contagion” edge that loses contracts, timing, and denominators. [T-finance]

Risk transfer changes the holder without necessarily reducing overall risk. Continue examining the recipient's capital, contingent obligations, and ultimate loss-bearing. Face values of reciprocal claims and debts within one system also cannot be added into system net wealth. Separate four final outcomes: restored payments, restored capital, restored borrower cash flow, and restored living conditions. Completing short-term payment does not mean an asset shortfall disappears, much less that life has recovered. [T-finance]

The strongest objection is that complex financial chains can become hindsight stories. Start with explicit contracts and a particular maturity window, testing which constraint actually binds. If constraints or return effects lack evidence, retain no-amplification or unknown results. The following are accounting teaching constructions only, not real borrowing, investment, or action recommendations. [T-finance]
argumentSteps: Freeze currency, time point, term, valuation, and contracts; separate stocks from flows.
Calculate net worth, available cash, amounts due, and actual financing balances separately.
Check step by step whether mediators such as credit limits, quotes, or extensions change and whether constraints bind.
Distinguish five kinds of network transmission, comparing explanations such as shared expectations, interest rates, and policy.
Evaluate payment, capital, income, and living outcomes separately; without evidence of a return, do not register self-reinforcement.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: positive net worth with a payment shortfall
teachingExamples.text: On the same date, a constructed entity holds cash of 5 yuan, equipment worth 95 that cannot be liquidated by tomorrow, and liabilities of 80, of which 20 falls due tomorrow. Net worth=(5+95)−80=20 yuan, but tomorrow's cash shortfall=20−5=15 yuan. Borrowing 15 raises cash to 20 and liabilities to 95, leaving net worth=(20+95)−95=20 yuan. Repaying 20 of old debt leaves cash 0, equipment 95, and liabilities 75, still net worth 20 yuan. New borrowing fills the cash shortfall for a specified horizon without creating net worth.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Entirely constructed, using one currency, without interest, fees, or valuation changes. Borrowing is genuinely approved and received; equipment cannot be liquidated before tomorrow.
teachingExamples.boundary: An accounting identity does not establish that real refinancing is feasible or can continue indefinitely.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: credit limit and balance
teachingExamples.text: Collateral has market value 100 yuan and the contract permits a maximum loan-to-value ratio of 60%, so the credit limit is 60 yuan. An outstanding balance of 50 leaves 10 unused. If market value becomes 80 and contractual revaluation takes effect immediately, the limit becomes 48 while the balance remains 50, a shortfall of 2. Immediate top-up pressure arises only if the contract actually requires it and provides no grace period or substitute collateral. If the borrower has another 2 yuan in cash, the shortfall can be met without a forced sale.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A constructed contract with a fixed ratio and one valuation update; market value, credit limit, and balance must not be conflated.
teachingExamples.boundary: No subsequent asset-price feedback has been established; the 2-yuan shortfall cannot directly be called systemic financial acceleration.

10.7.title: 10.7 Five clock types and asynchronous updating
10.7.lead: Events on the same day do not update every state simultaneously. Distinguish what an event reaches, how a process advances on its own, and when a change is actually observed.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2303–2318; original site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-7. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain downloadable in their original editions.

The source distinguishes at least five clock types: immediate, interactional, organizational, institutional, and long-term. They are analytical categories for recognizing updating mechanisms, not five fixed speeds or a requirement that every object follow one rhythm. Minutes, rounds, quarters, deliberation cycles, and years are merely typical examples; actual duration depends on evidence and task. [T-main]

The immediate type includes emotions, attention, bodily arousal, and local prices, triggered by signal arrival or shocks; short fluctuations cannot directly become long-term changes. The interactional type concerns trust, strategies, relational expectations, and local norms, advancing through multiple action–feedback rounds. Equal total counts may yield different results with different sequences and memories; each interaction cannot be treated as an independent, identically distributed reset. [T-main]

Organizational roles, budgets, processes, and indicators advance through decisions, execution, and review; a decision is not implementation. Institutional rules, rights, responsibilities, appeals, and records require checking actual procedural changes, write-back, and execution. Verbal promises are insufficient, and authorization and legal validity require separate recording. A procedure running does not automatically establish valid authorization; ‘the institutional clock has arrived’ cannot generate authority. [T-main]

Long-term capability, identity, infrastructure, culture, and intergenerational change involve accumulation, learning, maintenance, and replacement. Short-term observations cannot guarantee lasting change, but classifying an object as long-term also does not establish that it cannot change today. Some long-term accumulation may become visible at thresholds, requiring specific dynamic grounds. [T-main]

The source separates two kinds of updating: external events directly update only variables reached through channels under satisfied conditions; endogenous processes, expiration, accumulation, and recovery advance according to their own clocks and registered rules. Unreached does not mean unchanged. Without new grounds, retain the last observed value with its time and uncertainty, or mark unknown, rather than stamping an old value with today's time. An observation becoming stale changes knowledge status, not necessarily the entity for better or worse. [T-main]

The financial passage shows how asynchrony changes effects: prices may change before credit limits await revaluation or renewal; fixed- and floating-rate contracts adjust payments differently; public guarantees may first relieve cash shortfalls and later allocate losses. Compare when constraints become effective, alternative financing arrives, recovery occurs, and irreversible harm arises, not just final amounts. Prolonged short-term support is not restored long-term solvency. [T-main；T-finance]

This section's additional Cash and Counseling observation is that variables in the same nine-month interview do not share one observation window: care use looks back two weeks, while equipment and modifications cover nine months since enrollment. Different allowance start dates further mean that a nine-month observation date does not imply nine months of intervention for everyone. The report's short-term limitations also prevent interpreting that satisfaction measurement as a lasting institutional effect. This supports window discipline, not empirical exhaustiveness of the five clock categories. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that multi-clock states are difficult to maintain. Begin with explicit expiration dates, actual records, and necessary validity-period management, refining only when the task depends on finer dynamics. Without dynamic estimates, do not draw smooth decay curves. For indeterminate variables, retain the last observation and an unknown current value rather than generate a complete but false real-time snapshot. [T-main；T-snapshot]
argumentSteps: For each variable, list updating triggers, time units, observation time, lookback window, and validity period.
First check the event's direct channels, then concurrent endogenous, expiration, accumulation, or recovery processes.
Tie each update to grounds; unreached variables neither reset automatically nor are automatically assumed constant.
Compare constraint activation, alternative resources, and harm windows, distinguishing short-term support from long-term recovery.
Retain historical values and uncertainty in stale records; mark the current value unknown without current grounds.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: prices change first, contracts update later
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a constructed collateralized loan has balance 50 yuan and is revalued at 60% of month-end market value, initially 100 yuan. On day 1, price falls to 80, but the contract keeps the old limit of 60 through day 30. Day-30 revaluation sets the limit to 48, yielding a contractual shortfall of 2 if the balance remains 50. If alternative cash of 2 arrives on day 10 and is repaid on day 29, the balance becomes 48, so there is no such shortfall on day 30. If cash arrives only on day 31, day-30 consequences depend on contractual grace provisions. The day-1 price shock is not equivalent to a margin call that day.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Entirely constructed, single currency, no fees; revaluation and effective dates and permission to repay are stipulated.
teachingExamples.boundary: No actual contracts or default behavior were measured; price feedback and long-term solvency are not inferred.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: expiration can occur without new events
teachingExamples.text: A constructed device has 10 battery units today and a registered consumption rule of 1 unit/hour without charging. Even without external messages for three hours, its battery becomes 7 under this deterministic model. Another variable, ‘member trust,’ has only last week's interview and no credible evolution rule; one cannot likewise subtract 3 or declare it still equal to last week's value. Retain the historical report and mark the current judgment unknown.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Constant battery consumption is a constructed rule, not measured equipment data; the trust example has no numerical scale.

10.8.title: 10.8 Joint-state snapshot
10.8.lead: A snapshot is like a state card with sources and times: it fixes projection's starting point and identifies unknown cells, preventing later events from being secretly written back into the beginning.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2319–2324; original site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-8. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain downloadable in their original editions.

The source calls a snapshot ‘the frozen starting point of projection’ (translated from Chinese). What is frozen is one version of a representation and its evidence cutoff for a specified task, not reality itself. Snapshot time specifies the time being described; evidence cutoff determines which acquired materials may be used. Times of historical occurrence, record creation, and researcher access may differ. Later evidence should create a new version or correction record, not erase what was unknown in the old version. [T-main；T-clock]

Read the field list by responsibility: actor and circle references identify whom we discuss; relations and membership mappings specify who relates to whom and how; M/Ψ retain resources and experience; channels and constraints specify which changes can propagate; five clocks declare separate updating times; scale profiles prevent mixing axes into a size ranking; unknowns, residuals, and identity criteria identify unexplained aspects and whether the object remains the same across time. Complete fields provide checkability, not completeness of reality. [T-main；T-joint]

Label each value separately as observed, supported hypothesis, candidate, disputed, unknown, or not applicable. Observed means a record through a specific channel, without guaranteeing no measurement error; a supported hypothesis has evidence and reasons but is still not direct observation; candidates await testing; disputes preserve both conflicting sides and grounds; unknown means insufficient basis for a current judgment; not applicable must follow the task contract, not reluctance to address an item. These distinct statuses cannot be inserted into one numerical series as equally reliable measurements. [T-main]

This section's evidence statuses must not be conflated with §5.8's vocabulary of missing-data statuses. The latter additionally separates unobservable through the current channel/window and withheld for protection, alongside unknown and not applicable. An experiential field may be withheld for protection while supporting material exists; ‘no public value’ does not imply no experience or loss. Snapshots should retain necessary statuses without exposing specific private content. [T-missing]

When sources conflict, first retain values, generation methods, and versions side by side. If two records actually measure different objects, windows, or units, correct comparability first; if they measure the same quantity, a combination model is still required before listing an aggregate estimate and uncertainty separately. Arithmetic averaging can help under appropriate models but is no automatic arbiter. Original conflicts cannot be deleted merely because an intermediate number is generated. [T-main]

Internal differences cannot be represented only by circle means. Use distributions, quantiles, positional records, or subcircles with object grounds. A distribution representation need not add an entity; naming a subgroup an independent circle requires renewed admission for boundaries, roles, interfaces, windows, and identity. Neither labels nor means can invent individual facts. [T-main; T-entry]

This section adds comparison definitions from Cash and Counseling: the report defines “elderly” as 65 and over in two states but 60 and over in Florida, and excludes some proxy opinions under specified rules. Copying each state's elderly satisfaction rate into one snapshot would lose denominator differences. Record them without implying a calculation error or automatically prohibiting all model-based pooling. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that frozen snapshots become outdated. Retain observation time and validity duration in each version, choosing reobservation timing by task risk. Freezing makes projection starting points traceable; updating prevents later judgments from expiring. If unknown key fields could change conclusions, give only conditional paths or stop the affected strong judgments rather than filling values for formal completeness. [T-main; T-clock]
argumentSteps: Specify snapshot time, material cutoff, task scope, and version, recording relevant times separately.
Reference actors, circles, and relations, registering M/Ψ, constraints, clocks, scale, W, and K.
Label evidence status value by value; treat sensitive missingness under its protection status.
Retain conflicting sources and generation processes, adding a combined estimate only with model support.
Check internal differences and readmit new subobjects; create traceable new versions for updates.

10.9.title: 10.9 Boundary perturbation and object conversion
10.9.lead: Change how the boundary is drawn and see whether the conclusion holds; then check whether the real object's structure changed. Analyst redrawing and actual object transformation need separate records.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2325–2330, original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-9. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research originals and extracts remain downloadable in their original editions.

The source warns, in translation, against “treating the chosen boundary as a natural boundary.” Membership thresholds, observation times, and adjacent objects usually involve analytical choices requiring task and material grounds. Perturbation is not arbitrary selection for a preferred result; it changes choices within defensible ranges to reveal a conclusion's dependencies. Where an explicit legal or contractual boundary is required, surrounding sensitivity analysis remains possible, but another boundary cannot impersonate the original question. [T-main; T-entry]

The first perturbation changes membership thresholds, for example slightly raising participation frequency and tracing who leaves the denominator, which channels disappear, and whether the outcome changes. The second moves the time window, checking event-only relations or expired records. The third replaces or removes a circle, checking whether joint-model gain disappears or whether the circle merely duplicates another variable. These ask different questions; performing one does not establish comprehensive robustness. [T-main]

If slight, reasonable boundary changes reverse important conclusions, downgrade corresponding grouping-gain support and report sensitivity. Reversals may also reflect real thresholds or changed task definitions; they do not mechanically make all objects nonexistent. Explain where change occurs and which window/use is supported. Reduced explanatory or foresight gain cannot delete independently supported affected people, organizations, or responsibility relations. [T-main; T-entry; T-complex]

Object conversion instead means original identity conditions K fail after an event. Source examples include formalizing a temporary rescue group, project splitting, platform migration, and care reorganization. Whether a genuinely new object exists depends on old K: renaming need not change the object, and limited member turnover may remain within tolerance. Even without renaming, breaks in roles, interfaces, or continuity may require conversion or dissolution records. [T-main; T-entry]

Conversion records should retain old ID, old contract, break time, and grounds; create a new contract for the new object and specify inherited, changed, and unresolved connections. The new object cannot overwrite old failures, responsibilities, and historical traces. This preserves responsibility questions; it does not let the framework decide that every responsibility necessarily carries over or disappears. Legal, contractual, and actual responsibilities still need matter-specific verification. [T-main]

Cash and Counseling is reused here to show how boundary choices may change comparison objects: some opinion questions exclude paid-caregiver proxies, and the report explicitly notes unequal exclusion between groups, potentially biasing corresponding estimates. It warns that sample boundaries and original random-assignment groups are different sets. Without individual data, this lesson cannot claim completed perturbation analysis or an actual conclusion reversal. [P-CC]

The strongest objection is that sensitivity checks make every boundary endlessly suspect. Predeclare reasonable perturbation ranges, key outcomes, and stopping standards: changes beyond the task contract become new questions, known irrelevant dimensions are not perturbed without limit, and decisive unchecked boundaries retain limitations. This preserves testability without equating lack of unconditional robustness with inability to make any bounded judgment. [T-main; T-complex]

When grouping gain disappears after boundary perturbation, downgrade the corresponding gain support and state applicable boundaries; independently supported organizations, relations, or responsibilities remain facts. Changed K also requires an independent object-conversion record; better prediction after redrawing cannot retroactively mean the old object never failed.
argumentSteps: Preserve original boundaries, window, object K, and key conclusions.
Within justified ranges, separately perturb membership thresholds, time windows, and circle sets.
Trace changes in denominators, channels, and conclusions rather than reporting only the best result.
Downgrade and qualify sensitive conclusions while retaining independently established object and responsibility facts.
When real K fails, register conversion/dissolution; new object contracts do not overwrite old records.

10.10.title: 10.10 Complexity gate for joint states
10.10.lead: An added layer of explanation must state which additional question it answers. Better prediction needs comparison; real responsibilities need preservation without predictive scores proving their existence.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2331–2336, original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-10. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research originals and extracts remain downloadable in their original editions.

The source's concise conclusion is, in translation, “Complexity is not maturity.” Adding circles or relations adds representational freedom, parameters, error sources, and data needs; better storytelling may merely fit already-seen material better. This does not prove complex models necessarily worse; it makes extra complexity a choice requiring explanation rather than a default reward. [T-main]

Answer five questions individually: which residual of the original model it explains, preventing aimless expansion; whether an independently observable channel exists, preventing label-only links; whether it improves out-of-sample explanation or foresight, preventing circular explanation of old material; what measurement costs and privacy risks arise, preventing losses exceeding gains; and whether deleting it changes the conclusion, checking duplication. The last tests task contribution; any numerical change after deletion does not automatically prove usefulness. [T-main]

Against a simple single-focus or single-circle baseline, both must answer the same target using comparable cutoffs, samples, and evaluation methods. A complex option cannot exclusively use later-known outcomes or extra labels and credit the difference to structure. Out-of-sample explanation also needs predefined targets and failures; explaining any new material afterward is not automatically support. Numerical prediction, mechanism explanation, and normative description still have different evidential responsibilities. [T-main; T-entry]

If there is only a complete narrative within already seen materials and no stable comparative support, lower the claimed explanatory or predictive gain and prefer a sufficiently simple model. Stable comparison may be bounded to specific tasks and intervals and does not require every new case to collect a large independent training set; when adequate comparison is infeasible, honestly retain gain as unestablished rather than claiming validation. [T-main]

The source preserves a key exception: describing established responsibilities, membership differences, or lawful authority can independently justify retaining an object without first proving predictive gain. For example, two people may have the same average income but different care obligations; describing those responsibilities is not intended to improve prediction of tomorrow's returns. The exception still requires independent grounds, an explicit question, and cost control; ‘responsibility matters’ cannot justify unlimited collection of everyone's private information. [T-main]

The added point from the NASA report here concerns the use of duty records themselves: the board and Panel 1 each had explicit tasks. If the question tracks who was required to investigate and report, documentary reasons justify retaining those levels without first proving improved prediction. Conversely, duties written in documents still establish neither performance effects nor optimality of that organizational configuration. [P-NASA]

The strongest objection is that simple baselines flatten weak positions. The right response is to clarify the target rather than abandon the baseline: if the original task includes membership differences or responsibility, a ‘simple model’ deleting them no longer answers the same question. Sufficient simplicity must preserve key distinctions; complexity and simplicity should concern sufficiency rather than a contest in object counts. [T-main；T-snapshot]
argumentSteps: State the current question, simple baseline, and its residuals or unanswered matters.
For each added circle, explain its channel, task contribution, costs, and privacy implications.
When claiming gains, make fair independent/out-of-sample comparisons, retaining failures and uncertainty.
If only an in-sample narrative is obtained, lower the gain claim without automatically denying object facts.
If retaining complexity for responsibility or authority records, explain its independent grounds and stopping scope.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: lower training error, higher unseen error
teachingExamples.text: Artificial training points are (x,y)=(0,0),(1,1). The simple constant prediction m=0.5 has training mean squared error [(0−0.5)^2+(1−0.5)^2]/2=0.25; the two-parameter line y=x has zero training error. Add a test point (2,0) not used for fitting: the constant has squared error 0.25, while the line has (0−2)^2=4. This example refutes only ‘better training performance necessarily means better unseen performance’; under a different actual generating law, the line could win.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Training and test data are entirely artificial, assessed under the same squared loss, with the test value unused in fitting; no claim is made to represent an actual probability distribution.
teachingExamples.boundary: This is a logical counterexample, not an estimate of how often multi-circle models win or lose; one test point also supplies no stable empirical conclusion.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: deleting a responsibility field with no predictive contribution

teachingExamples.assumptions: Entirely artificial, with the failure function and authorization facts given separately; no actual shutdown occurred.

10.11.title: 10.11 A joint-object example
10.11.lead: This section uses a public resignation to connect the preceding fields. Its focus is preserving potentially different relationships, resources, meanings, and times, then letting evidence determine which paths hold.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2337—2344; original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-11. The current complete text is in the theory-v2 source; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available in their original versions for download and checking.

The source is not an investigation record of a company but an example of ‘analyzing an employee's public resignation’. The agent, team, management, household care, occupational community, and platform public discourse may all be candidates; listing them in a sentence does not give them object admission. An actual case must find boundary, role, channel, time, and identity materials item by item; household conditions or personal feelings lacking materials cannot be invented. [T-main；T-entry]

The relationship layer retains, in turn, the team's local nesting within the company, the agent's multiple memberships, platform bridging to external audiences, the distinct relations of resource competition and reputational cooperation, and the temporary nature of solidarity circles during the event. Management need not equal the entire company, and employee and family are not the same agent. A platform may spread messages without representing either side; ‘possible competition/cooperation’ is also not factual confirmation. [T-main；T-rel]

The M side lists pay, work hours, care, contracts, positions, and traffic; the Ψ side lists dignity, feelings of betrayal, professional identity, coworker trust, and perceived legitimacy. The latter must retain reporting subjects, times, and material identities; all feelings cannot be inferred backward from resignation. The former also cannot consider only total pay: exit costs vary with contracts, care, opportunities, and resource-conversion conditions. [T-main；T-channels]

The temporal layer runs from immediate attention and emotion through interactional trust and handovers to organizational processes and potentially later institutional write-back. ‘Weeks’ and ‘later’ are illustrative pacing, not universal durations. A public post may change public attention without reaching the company's actual budget, appeals procedure, or household resources; meanwhile, endogenous processes such as existing contract expiry can still occur. [T-main；T-clock]

The source proposes four conditional paths: when only public relations changes while hours/appeals do not, public attention and internal trust may diverge; when resources change but meaning repair fails, staying and commitment may diverge; when care pressure is relieved, the person's option set may expand; when occupational communities provide usable bridging resources, exit costs may fall and imitation may follow. Each is a conditional path requiring checking, not a known ending, and none supplies a probability of occurrence. [T-main]

‘Resignation is due to personality’ and ‘it is entirely determined by company structure’ cannot close the question by labels. Yet the joint model does not win automatically either: compare it fairly with adequate simple explanations, checking whether added household, platform, or community circles supply independent increments. If it only draws more circles and makes the story coherent afterward, lower the gain claim. Criticism of single-line determinism cannot become universal denial that a simple mechanism may suffice for a narrow task. [T-main；T-complex]

As a bounded real-world comparison, Bray's public resignation account includes organizational position, expected material costs, and his own feelings, while distinguishing internal communication from public expression. The material supports occurrence of these expressions, not completion of household-care details or others' experiences. The artificial employee model below refers neither to him nor to his company; none of its paths can be transferred into subsequent facts of that case. [P-BRAY]

This section stops at making the joint snapshot and candidate paths visible. How transmission occurs, where branching appears, and which path is supported require the next part and event sequences and comparative materials. Who should bear costs, whether others' information may be disclosed, and what actions are authorized also cannot be inferred directly from a relationship diagram. [T-main；T-stop]
argumentSteps: Mark the source-book example's status, freeze the actual case's information cutoff, and admit objects individually.
Distinguish the agent, team, management, and household/community/platform, without combining them into one unified agent.
Register evidence separately for membership, nesting, bridging, competition/cooperation, and temporary relationships.
Tie M, Ψ, and the five clocks to materials item by item; do not read minds from actions.
Write the four subsequent paths as conditional candidates and compare them with simple explanations; stop before sequence materials exist.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: changed exit costs do not mean inevitable resignation
teachingExamples.text: Artificial employee A has a discretionary buffer of 12 units. Immediate resignation would require 10 units of living expenses until the next income and 5 units for a care transition, leaving a gap of 3. If reliable care support covers 5 units, total demand becomes 10, which the buffer covers with 2 left. The stipulations establish only removal of one financial constraint, not that A necessarily resigns or stays, or that professional meaning has been repaired.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Person, expenses, support, and time window are entirely artificial; units are common, no costs are double-counted, and support is actually available.
teachingExamples.boundary: This corresponds to no actual person's budget and provides no resignation advice or judgment of motives.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an observation checklist for the book's four paths
teachingExamples.text: Artificial option A changes only external messages, checking public attention and internal appeals separately; B adjusts resources and separately checks commitment; C changes care availability and checks feasible options; D has the occupational community supply actual job information, first checking receipt and usability, then exit costs and subsequent behavior. The four may combine; they are not mutually exclusive probabilistic branches.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Only a research checklist constructed from the source, with no actual implementation or observed results.
teachingExamples.boundary: Listing possible mechanisms does not mean they occurred; do not assign fabricated probabilities to paths.

10.12.title: 10.12 Where this part stops
10.12.lead: Part Ten can now deliver a bounded joint state. Knowing who is connected to whom and how does not determine the inevitable future or grant a right to act for others.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2345—2354; original-site anchor /theory/part-10#section-10-12. The current complete text is in the theory-v2 source; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available in their original versions for download and checking.

This section closes six answerable question types: which circles need simultaneous representation; how the six relationships hold along specified dimensions; how memberships and roles are distributed across circles; how M and Ψ run in parallel; which clocks are asynchronous; and whether a complex representation gains on a simple baseline for the task. ‘Can answer’ defines methodological scope, not adequate evidence in every analysis; gaps should remain as unknowns, candidates, or disputes in the snapshot. [T-main]

The future cannot be determined directly from a structural diagram: a relationship's existence only constrains possible channels; whether transmission starts, capacity suffices, delays exceed the window, and feedback returns requires additional event and dynamic materials. Part Eleven addresses event transmission, branching, and cascades; it receives a frozen state rather than automatically inferring a unique destiny from scattered labels. [T-main；T-clock]

Conditional foresight and bounded choice enter Part Twelve. Foresight adds targets, horizons, baselines, and evaluation; choice additionally compares action, delay, trials, exit, and inaction, including outcomes and implementability. Entry into the next part’s methods does not mean these evidentiary responsibilities are already met here, nor that every understanding task must escalate to prediction or intervention. [T-main]

High graph position, centrality, or propagation strength does not decide which circle deserves greater protection, who should bear costs, or who may act. These are questions of norms, authorization, and protection requiring independent grounds. Known connections may help identify whom to ask but cannot replace consent, due process, or specific authority. [T-main; T-floor]

NASA material offers a bounded comparison: the report records the Board’s mandate separately from its working relations. Researchers may describe roles and interfaces from it, but an added coordination edge creates no added authority and predicts no later measure’s effect. Only this recording boundary is used here, without evaluating every consequence of the investigation. [P-NASA]

The final simplification principle does not demand building complexity first and deleting everything afterward. If an event involves only one actor and one stable circle, with no additional information from adjacency, overlapping membership, bridging, or cross-boundary spillovers, do not activate the full joint model. Specify the task first: simplification sufficient for equipment counts may not answer member control or responsibility. Retaining necessary objects for independently grounded responsibility questions need not first prove predictive gain. [T-main; T-complex]

The strongest objection is that stopping may miss important distant relations. Preserve reopening conditions such as new independent channels, key model residuals, reversals under boundary perturbation, or upgraded use. Stopping produces a bounded answer within current material and task, not a pledge that adjacent layers will never matter; reopening also should not add imagined background indefinitely. [T-main; T-boundary]

Separate structural facts, event paths, future judgments, values/responsibility, and authorization.
Enter Part Eleven for dynamic propagation; meet Part Twelve’s responsibilities for foresight/choice.
Actively use a simple representation when one object/circle suffices.
State reopening conditions and preserve the current version; stopping does not erase uncertainty or history.

intro-11-part.title: Part Eleven: Event-Driven Dynamic Projection
intro-11-part.lead: Dynamic projection is not continuing a fluent story; it asks what is currently known, where an event type changes things first, and through which conditions it affects somewhere else. Begin by preserving the status of facts, hearsay, plans, and model assumptions.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2355–2358; source anchor part_11; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘Actions that actually occur may change reality whether or not they were authorized.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

This part starts from a joint state with explicit evidence status. It connects actors, circles, relations, material conditions, and experiential-meaning conditions for a task, without claiming observation of the world’s full state. Every item retains its source, window, support, and unknowns; subsequent inference cannot merge them into equally reliable starting points.

The introduction lists five entry types: observed, reported, planned, hypothetical, and simulated events. Observed events still have measurement-contract limits; a report may truly occur while its content remains unchecked; plans may affect preparation without being executed; hypotheses and simulations support only their conditional consequences. Updating event status with new evidence must retain relations and versions rather than erase original uncertainty.

After an event, distinguish at least directly confirmable state differences, conditional consequences inferred from mechanisms, and signals supporting or weakening the corresponding paths. Receiving a message, for example, is a separately checkable reception event; changed belief, action, or institutional fields require corresponding material. Observing two successive events does not automatically identify the channel between them.

Actual action may change reality even without authorization. Analysis must record actions and consequences that actually occur, separately retaining normative evaluation, legal or institutional authority, and execution permission for this occasion. No right to act does not mean no action; action taken does not confer the right. Recording facts neither excuses the action nor permits the model to implement it.

This connects to §11.3’s notation: u(t) specifically denotes externally authorized actions that actually occur; observed or reported unauthorized actions enter e(t) with their event status and separately recorded authority status. Unperformed unauthorized scenarios may be analyzed while remaining hypothetical or simulated. Separate notation must neither delete reality nor apply the same shock twice.

The following sections set event contracts, joint updating, the nine-step closed loop, propagation and cascades, path graphs, variable candidates, counterfactuals and recursion, stopping, and write-back. Part Twelve then takes responsibility for preregistered foresight and bounded choice. A conditional path obtained now does not establish predictive benefit or authority for real adoption.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: zero authority while the state actually changes
teachingExamples.text: A fictional door has state d=0 (closed) at t0; a credible direct record establishes that an actor opens it at t1, giving d=1. A separate explicit premise says the action lacked this occasion’s permission, J=0. Correct recording retains both d:0→1 and J=0 and analyzes it as an observed event. A rule that ‘J=0 makes changing d impossible’ conflicts with the stipulated facts.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Door, record, and permission are teaching assumptions; no actual door opening, sanction, or legal classification is involved.
teachingExamples.boundary: Shows logical independence of fact and authority, not permission to execute unauthorized action.

teachingExamples.title: Logical construction: believing a report does not make it true
teachingExamples.text: A fictional report r=1 means a statement ‘the door is open’ was actually received. Actual door state may still be d=0 or d=1. Suppose additionally that the listener initially believed it closed and, under this example’s rule, directly trusts the report, changing belief b from 0 to 1. Both d values fit the same r,b. Report arrival and conditional belief change can therefore be discussed without inventing an open-door fact.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The listener’s trust is an explicit rule here, not a claim that everyone necessarily believes reports; actual belief change needs separate material.
teachingExamples.boundary: Report or belief values cannot directly recover the actual door state.

11.1.title: 11.1 Projection versus Narrative Continuation
11.1.lead: A story often selects a smooth ending; structural projection must state which other endings fit current material equally well. Its credibility lies not in always sounding certain but in traceable conditions at every step and knowing where to stop when key conditions are missing.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2359–2372; source anchor section-11-1; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘If multiple continuations fit the available evidence, retain branching.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

Narrative may select one coherent continuation for literary purposes; structural projection on factual tasks cannot treat coherence as support. Preserve conditions, transmission channels, competing paths, and failure meanings: what permits continuation, which observation refutes, and which gap leaves judgment unresolved. More branches are not inherently better, but grounded differences cannot be flattened by a fluent story.

Minimum input has eight items: frozen snapshot, event records, mechanism hypotheses, parameter ranges, clock policy, propagation policy, unknowns, and stopping conditions. Freezing identifies the version used in this run, not absolute correctness. Explicit unknowns may also be frozen. Late material creates a new run rather than flowing backward into the old starting point.

The joint snapshot freezes actors, circles, relations, M/Ψ, clocks, and evidence cutoff, preventing post-result object changes or access to future information. M and Ψ separately retain material and experience–meaning conditions. Genuinely inapplicable items may have reasons stated; symmetrical forms do not justify invented psychological states.

Events freeze type, time, source, reached objects, and channels, preventing rumors, plans, observations, and simulations from being mixed. Mechanisms freeze direction, carrier, delay, threshold, and failure conditions, preventing an explanation from retrospectively reshaping itself for every result. If only a candidate mechanism is available, say candidate; the procedural act of freezing cannot promote it to causal fact.

Parameters may be points, intervals, grades, or explicitly unknown, depending on material and task. Intervals do not automatically carry probability distributions, nor do two branches automatically split equally. Clock policy specifies sequence, update rhythm, and concurrency handling; propagation policy specifies transmissible channels and blocking conditions, rather than allowing every node to update simultaneously after one event.

Stopping conditions cover insufficient information, risk, use beyond scope, and resource limits. A local channel gap pauses dependent inferences, while independently established direct facts or bounded total effects may remain. Failure of shared premises or overall use conditions stops all relevant runs. Stopping does not force unknown into failure or erase known facts.

Minimum output also has eight items: path graph, state differences at each step, support status, early signals, contrary signals, residuals, variable candidates, and write-back requirements. The graph shows grounded subsequent differences; state differences specify fields; support status distinguishes factual and conditional status; the two signal types strengthen and weaken paths respectively, rather than collecting only favorable news.

Residuals are differences unexplained by the current representation and mechanism, not arbitrary random noise or immediately nameable hidden motives. Variable candidates turn gaps into testable questions. Write-back requirements specify when and from which sources results are appended, how original branches, competing paths, and baselines are compared, and how failures remain recorded.

If material permits several continuations, retain parallel branches. Without grounded probabilities or rankings, do not force an ordering. Consequence severity or a tight observation window may prioritize investigation of one branch, but research priority is not occurrence probability. Clear supported scope is stronger than unsupported decimals or directions creating an impression of certainty.

caseNotes.title: Snow retained the decline before pump-handle removal
caseNotes.text: In the 1855 second edition, Snow records removal of the Broad Street pump handle on September 8, 1854, while explicitly noting that incidence had already declined markedly before use of the water stopped and discussing population departures. The history cannot therefore be reduced to “decline began only after handle removal.”

This section estimates no independent removal effect, nor infers complete ineffectiveness from insufficient identification. The book is retrospective and does not establish that this lesson reconstructed the complete information set available then.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: retain two queue paths from one starting point
teachingExamples.text: Let fictional q0=2 items, with 1 additional arrival at t0. Each window first adds registered new tasks, then a single service point processes exactly min(queue,c) items. Capacity c remains fixed over two windows but is known only as c∈{1,2}; there are no new arrivals in window two. Thus q1=max(0,2+1−c). For c=1, q1=2 and q2=1; for c=2, q1=1 and q2=0. Both paths fit the starting point. A smooth story of “definitely empty next window” cannot be selected, nor may each branch receive 50% without probability material. Actual first-window completions distinguish the branches.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Homogeneous tasks, a work-conserving service rule, fixed c, no hidden entries/exits, and common within-window order are explicit. Numbers are teaching constructions.
teachingExamples.boundary: If first-window records show 3 completions or a queue greater than 2, at least one original condition needs review. c cannot quietly be changed while retaining success of the original run.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: late information creates a new version
teachingExamples.text: Fictional V1 closes information at noon Monday, knowing only c∈{1,2}. Tuesday brings a credible record establishing actual Monday c=2, allowing reconstruction of the past and creation of V2. V1 retains its contemporaneous two branches and unknown. Backfilling V2's c=2 into V1 and claiming a unique Monday prediction of an empty queue rewrites the starting point after results.

11.2.title: 11.2 Event contract
11.2.lead: “Occurred,” “someone says it occurred,” “planned,” and “suppose it occurred” have very different implications for the next judgment. An event contract gives each input a status card so a retold claim cannot become an unverified fact after repeated transmission.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2373–2386; original anchor section-11-2. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Occurrence of a report does not mean its content is true.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

The five event types distinguish use and evidential status, not a low-to-high credibility ranking. One real process may produce different records: publication of a plan is a real publication event, while its future action remains unexecuted; publication of a simulation report is a real transmission event, while its internal failure does not thereby become real. Distinguish the recorded objects, cross-referencing when necessary without duplicating impacts.

Observed events may enter explanation, replay, and forward projection, but only within their observation contracts. Sources, observation positions, omissions, and measurement errors are required. Seeing “complete” on a screen directly supports that display or record; external execution still needs task-appropriate execution material. Visible interfaces are not categorically invalid: the observed field determines the evidence ceiling.

Reported events permit analysis of belief propagation and conditional paths. The report's occurrence may be established while content truth remains under review. Reporter position, accessible information, disputes, and source lineage matter; repeated forwarding is not multiple independent witnesses. Reports may change recipient expectations, but actual reach and belief need evidence; identical reactions cannot be prescribed for everyone.

Planned events may change preparation, resource reservations, and strategic interaction without meaning the future action is complete. Register proposer, object, planned time, authorization, resources, and cancellation conditions. Approved plans may remain unexecuted because of resources or subsequent events; unapproved plans may genuinely affect expectations. Register plan existence, execution authority, and actual occurrence separately.

Hypothetical events serve counterfactual and scenario comparisons, requiring conditions, purpose, and feasibility. Conditions may distinguish mechanisms without claiming actual permission or inevitability. Infeasible scenarios used as logical boundaries must retain that status rather than become actual recommendations.

Simulated events belong only to specified model runs, requiring model version, initial conditions, parameters, and prohibited-extrapolation boundaries. Calculated trajectories expose conditional consequences, but repeated sampling still comes from the same model. Without new external material, it cannot raise the evidential status of a claim that a real event occurred.

Fourteen minimum-record items each bear responsibility: event ID preserves reference; occurrence time/window locates the object event; observation time states when it became known; source supplies grounds; affected actors and affected circles separately retain scope; channel explains reach; direct change specifies actual altered fields; evidence status marks support and unknowns; disputes retain inconsistent material; competing explanations prevent a single-story monopoly; reversibility distinguishes what can be undone; duration prevents extrapolation from an instant; subsequent observation specifies review. Event type must also remain explicit, not hidden in narrative tone.

Occurrence time may be an interval or a report's claimed time; invent no precise timestamp. Observation time differs from occurrence time, and §11.3.2 additionally distinguishes model-entry time. Late material may revise today's understanding of the past, but cannot give past forecasts records unavailable then.

Affected objects are not automatically “everyone relevant.” A message reaching a department does not establish every member read it; changed quantity fields do not establish changed trust, authority, and relations. Reversibility also has multiple dimensions: replenishable resources do not mean transmitted information, elapsed deadlines, and damaged trust can be fully restored.

After verification supplies new material, append sources and correction relationships and revisit branches depending on the content. Later falsity of content does not erase the report's occurrence or actual effects; later truth does not erase its then-unverified status in earlier evaluations. None of this analysis independently authorizes real collection, experiments, or interventions.
