teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: five statuses for the same “decrease of 4 items”
teachingExamples.text: Suppose fictional initial inventory is 10 items with no other inflows or outflows. Correct direct counting confirms removal of 4, yielding 6. If only an unverified report says “4 removed,” and this example allows only truth or falsity with no removal when false, inventory belongs to {6,10}. If removal of 4 is planned for tomorrow, current inventory remains 10; only the conditional post-execution value is 6. Hypothetical removal yields conditional consequence 6; a simulator calculating 6 under the same rule produces only a model value. Identical numbers do not confer identical evidential status.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Inventory units, correct counting, no other changes, and only two report possibilities are explicit construction premises; no actual warehouse or experiment is involved.
teachingExamples.boundary: An unverified report cannot automatically yield mean 8 because no truth probabilities are supplied; simulated output 6 is not actual inventory 6.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching event card: separating claimed time from observation time
teachingExamples.text: Fictional ID=Toy-E1, type=reported; claimed occurrence day 1 at 09:00, report received at 10:00, model entry at 10:05; source=fictional team message Toy-S1; affected actor=fictional custodian A, circle=fictional warehouse group W; channel=received team message; direct change=message received, physical inventory awaiting verification; evidence status=report exists, content unverified; dispute=stocktake incomplete; competing explanations=actual removal or message error; reversibility=stock can be replenished, but propagated information cannot be presumed fully retractable; duration=removal and effect duration unknown; subsequent observation=check stocktake and withdrawal records within this example's permitted scope.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All IDs, people, times, and permission scopes are teaching constructions, never actual event cards or valid authorization documents.
teachingExamples.boundary: A completed card does not prove its content; the direct change cannot be written as an established inventory reduction of 4.

teachingExamples.title: Set construction: two forwards do not add two physical shocks
teachingExamples.text: A fictional original message about removal of 4 items is forwarded twice; all three materials refer to one candidate event. If eventually verified as one removal, inventory changes 10→6. Applying a reduction of 4 for every message yields −2, duplicating the shock and potentially violating inventory bounds. If two independent withdrawals actually occurred, create separate events and verify their times and quantities.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Message lineage and one withdrawal are stipulated here. Actual deduplication requires evidence; textual similarity alone cannot justify merging.
teachingExamples.boundary: Material counts differ from event counts, but deduplication needs cannot cancel actual repeated events.

11.3.title: 11.3 Joint-State Update Equation
11.3.lead: The update equation is a responsibility checklist: the states, events, actions, disturbances, assumptions, and history used at this step should each be traceable. Writing F does not discover the world's unique operating formula; putting unknowns inside symbols cannot pretend to explain them.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2387–2402; original anchor: section-11-3; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “This equation only specifies recording responsibilities.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

The original joint state is Ω(t)=<A(t),C(t),R(t),M(t),Ψ(t),Q(t),E≤t,SP(t),W(t),K(t)>. A retains actors, C circles, R relations, M and Ψ material and experiential-meaning conditions respectively, Q channel constraints, E≤t events through the corresponding time, SP scale profiles, W evidence, and K identity criteria. It is a task-relevant representation, not omniscient access to every variable in the world.

The update is Ω(t+Δ)=F[Ω(t),e(t),u(t),ξ(t)|θ,h]. Δ is the declared progression interval; e is an event; u is an externally authorized action that actually occurred; ξ is an exogenous disturbance or unmodeled residual; θ is frozen mechanisms and parameters; h is a historical term. Each may have internal structure. The function symbol means only “the next step depends on these inputs”; actual rules, parameters, scope, and evidence cannot be omitted.

F is not claimed to be the unique true function. Different mechanisms may be equivalent on current material, and some parameters may have only intervals. Retain multiple candidates, ranges, or unknowns rather than disguising one computed output as the unique real consequence. Specify which terms are observable, inferred, or scenario assumptions only.

The definition of u is a recording convention; it cannot make unauthorized actions disappear from reality. Observed or reported violations, overreach, refusal to execute, or unauthorized proxy action enter e with corresponding event status, separately recording actors, consequences, and permission status. Violations not yet occurring belong only to hypothetical or simulated branches. Factual occurrence, normative judgment, and execution permission remain separate. An actual action referenced in several fields still applies its corresponding state effect only once.

ξ cannot become a universal black box for things one prefers not to explain. Preserve sources and scopes for identified exogenous disturbances; if it is only an unexplained residual, retain that status. Random-error models need grounds. Missing records, refusal to disclose, and unmodeled mechanisms cannot all be called zero-mean noise. Nor does writing h into a formula establish additional historical effects; current-carrier effects and G3 historical increments beyond the current representation still require separate evidence routes.

Each step's outputs distinguish at least four statuses: directly observed state differences, inferences supported by mechanism contracts, exploratory scenario values, and unexplained residuals. All may coexist in Ω without transferring evidential status to one another. A simulated future used as the next round's input retains its conditions and unknowns; it cannot be renamed current reality.

The parent section specifies update symbols and status responsibilities. Section 11.3.1 further separates actual states, observation rules, and identification sets, explaining when existing material suffices for a bounded question. Section 11.3.2 manages three times, late material, source corrections, and concurrent ordering. Together they constrain updating, not add automatic truth certification to F.

distinctions.leftText: Specifies dependencies and recording responsibilities.
distinctions.rightTitle: The actual mechanism has been found
distinctions.rightText: Still requires concrete rules, discriminating evidence, and an applicability domain.

distinctions.leftText: An externally authorized action that actually occurred.
distinctions.rightText: May still change reality and are registered as observed/reported.

distinctions.leftText: A difference left unexplained by the current account.
distinctions.rightText: Has a corresponding probabilistic meaning only under an appropriate error model.

distinctions.leftText: A record position whose content and use must be specified.
distinctions.rightText: Separately requires incremental evidence beyond the current representation; symbols do not create it.

distinctions.leftText: Observed, supported inference, scenario value, and residual, each with a separate trail.
distinctions.rightText: Coexistence in Ω does not give them equal evidential status.

boundaries: Formal completeness is not completeness of the world; a computable function does not prove a correct mechanism.
Do not force unknown parameters into point values or upgrade simulated continuations into real facts.
Keep factual records of actual unauthorized events without using analysis to carry out the action.
If a total effect has been independently identified, retain its bounded result; lack of unique identification of the internal F does not erase it.
ξ and h must not absorb every counterexample and make the model incapable of failure.

If F_A and F_B both fit 1→2, can the next step be uniquely predicted?

Does adding historical term h mean G3 is supported?
argumentSteps: Register Ω's ten components individually, with task, scale, evidence, and K; state whether unlisted fields are irrelevant, omitted, or unknown.
Write the F and θ actually used, specifying Δ, input sources, ranges, and failure conditions.
Distinguish e and u by definition. Actual unauthorized actions enter events rather than being deleted; repeated references do not apply them repeatedly.
Declare ξ and h statuses and the effects they can support. Unknowns do not default to randomness, nor history to G3 support.
Preserve each step's observed, inferred, scenario, and residual state differences separately.
Retain multiple Fs or output ranges where needed, constrained by identification sets and event-continuation rules.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: preserving event status and output ranges within one update equation
teachingExamples.text: Let fictional resources s0=5 units, with confirmed but unauthorized consumption e=−2 and authorized replenishment that actually arrives u=+1. Freeze the local rule s1=s0+e+u+ξ, explicitly allowing only two unknown extra-loss scenarios ξ∈{0,−1}, hence s1∈{4,3}. If extra loss is unverified, this output range is a conditional model result, not observed resources of 3. Nor may e be deleted because consumption was unauthorized, yielding 6 or 5.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Units match, events are counted once, and no other inflows/outflows exist. h has no separate effect in this local model; the ξ set is a teaching assumption, not an estimated real distribution.
teachingExamples.boundary: The example does not treat all events as linearly additive or authorize actual resource transfers.

teachingExamples.title: Logical construction: identical observations can still admit different Fs
teachingExamples.text: Suppose only one transition x0=1, x1=2 is observed. Both F_A(x)=x+1 and F_B(x)=2x fit it, but next yield 3 and 4 respectively. Without additional conditions, calling either the “unique true F” exceeds the material. Retain both candidates and seek subsequent records capable of distinguishing them.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The two rules are only a finite candidate set; actual models may be more numerous. All dynamics have not been estimated from one datum.
teachingExamples.boundary: Identical current fit guarantees neither identical next steps nor equal one-half real-world probabilities for the models.

counterexamples.text: Ω and F are fully written, so the model has read every state in the world.
counterexamples.effect: Complete symbols specify only a representational interface; they do not guarantee complete observations, mechanisms, or hidden variables.

counterexamples.text: The action in e was unauthorized, so deleting it is more normatively appropriate.
counterexamples.effect: Normative limits do not permit deleting confirmed facts; otherwise later resource and risk judgments become distorted.

counterexamples.text: Calling all deviations ξ and all persistence h validates the model.
counterexamples.effect: Naming provides neither error-model nor historical-identification evidence; preserve counterexamples and unknowns.

11.3.1.title: 11.3.1 States, Observations, and Identification Sets
11.3.1.lead: We obtain records, not the world itself. The key is not whether every hidden variable can be guessed, but whether all situations still compatible with the records already give the same answer to the current question.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2403–2410; source anchor section-11-3-1; short quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘The current evidence is already sufficient for that question.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

Let z(t) denote the actual state to be inferred and o(t) the obtained record, with observation rule o(t)=H[z(t),m(t),ε(t)]. H describes record generation; m includes who can enter the record, when measurement occurs, and which fields are protected from disclosure; ε is used only with a corresponding error model. Selection, protective missingness, and unknown mechanisms cannot all be lumped into random measurement error.

Numerical data may use additive error under appropriate conditions, while text and categories follow their record-generation rules. If observation coverage expands from half to all, record counts may rise while object counts remain unchanged; changed coding rules may also alter category frequencies. Ω must distinguish object changes from changes in how we observe them.

Given an explicit model and permitted errors, Z(o) is the set of states still compatible with the record. It is neither an unspecified confidence interval nor automatically an equal-probability distribution over states. Changing the model or error range changes the set; reported answers must retain this conditional status.

For task question q, if q takes the same value on every state in Z(o), the evidence suffices to answer this bounded question even if many components of z remain unidentified. If values differ, retain the range, identifiable direction, or genuinely unknown parts. Direction cannot be assumed either: if both positive and negative values remain compatible, do not force a direction merely to ‘say something.’

This is not ‘no difference found in the sample means everything is identical.’ Finite samples, measurement noise, and model limits may make differences hard to detect. Claiming a common answer across the set requires proving its range under model constraints or appropriate sufficiency, equivalence, and sensitivity support. Nonsignificance cannot directly become zero effect or sufficient identification.

The next observation should prioritize state differences that would change the current answer or action comparison. If the task asks only for a total, knowing exact container proportions may be unnecessary; if it asks whether both endpoints have a minimum reserve, distribution matters. The same evidence's value changes with the question; no variable table is eternally most complete and necessary.

Observation design remains constrained by purpose, necessity, privacy, and protection. Being able to identify a state does not confer authority to collect corresponding personal information. Without filling every latent variable, there may already be a commonly acceptable action; or the answer may be sufficient while no feasible action exists. Sufficient conditions for action are separately addressed in §12.10.1; authorization cannot be silently completed here.

distinctions.leftText: The world state the task seeks to infer.
distinctions.rightText: Generated by rules, selection, timing, and error conditions.

distinctions.leftText: q gives the same answer across compatible states.
distinctions.rightText: Requires uniqueness of all relevant hidden variables, often unnecessary for the task.

distinctions.leftText: The possible answer range under an explicit model.
distinctions.rightText: Additionally requires a corresponding probability model and inferential procedure.

distinctions.leftText: Limited evidence reveals no difference.
distinctions.rightText: Requires corresponding rules, tolerance, and sensitivity; there is no automatic upgrade.

distinctions.leftText: It may narrow current branches.
distinctions.rightText: Also requires purpose, protection, and authority conditions.

boundaries: Unlisted states may exist beyond the model's domain; set-based answers retain modeling boundaries.
Text, categories, refusal to disclose, and selective records do not all admit additive noise.
An identifiable total and unidentified distribution can coexist without canceling each other.
If compatible answers include positive and negative directions, direction is also unknown.
‘Wanting to recover the entire state’ does not justify demanding unnecessary or unauthorized information.
questions: Given only nonnegative integers x+y=10, how many elements does Z contain, and what can be said about the total and the difference's direction?
Why does the Boolean check 3≤x≤7 suffice to determine whether both containers have at least 3?
If coverage rises from half to all while the true count stays 20, why does the record change from 10 to 20?
Does uniquely identifying a state justify collecting all personal information?
argumentSteps: Declare z, H, m, and the applicable error model, separating actual state from record generation.
Construct Z(o) under these conditions, retaining unidentified components without assuming probabilities.
Write the current question as q(z), and calculate or establish its range across the entire compatible set.
Give a bounded answer when all agree; otherwise retain ranges/directions/unknowns. Failure to detect a finite-sample difference is not proof of identical answers.
Select the minimal observation that changes the answer or option comparison, rather than increasing precision indiscriminately.
Check observational purpose, risk, and authority; information needs do not generate permission to collect.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a known total with an unknown distribution
teachingExamples.text: Two fictional containers hold nonnegative integer amounts x and y, with correct total record o=x+y=10 and no other information. Z(o)={(0,10),(1,9),…,(10,0)} has 11 points. The total question q1=x+y is always 10 and already answerable; first-container quantity q2=x ranges from 0 to 10; difference q3=x−y ranges from −10 to 10 with both signs, so direction is unknown. Knowing x is unnecessary for recognizing total 10.
teachingExamples.assumptions: No omissions, error-free total measurement, exactly two containers, and fixed integer units are all teaching assumptions.
teachingExamples.boundary: If the real total itself has measurement error, enlarge the compatible set; constant 10 cannot carry over.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: choose less observation according to the question
teachingExamples.text: Continuing the example, change the task to ‘does each container hold at least 3 units?’ Since y=10−x, this is equivalent to 3≤x≤7. If a permitted check in this example reliably returns the Boolean ‘is x in [3,7]?’ it answers the task without measuring x exactly. If the task changes to how long each container will last, that Boolean information may be insufficient.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Error-free observation and permission for the check are constructed premises, not authority for real data collection; actual equipment costs are not compared.
teachingExamples.boundary: Information sufficiency is question-relative; the Boolean record cannot be called sufficient for every later task.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: the observation rule changes while the object does not
teachingExamples.text: Let true object count z stay at 20, with model recording rule o=mz. Coverage m changes from 1/2 to 1 without other error, so the record changes 10→20 while the true count stays 20. If only o=10 is observed and m∈{1/2,1} is known, z may be 20 or 10. Both growing records and identical records require interpretation through coverage rules.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The proportion is this example's exact record-generation rule; actual random sample counts are not equated to their expectations.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not rule out actual growth; it only refutes the claim that record changes necessarily equal object changes.

counterexamples.text: The total is 10 but the distribution is unknown, so no question can be answered.
counterexamples.effect: The total question has the same answer on all 11 states; a bounded answer can hold.

counterexamples.text: The sample difference is nonsignificant, so compatible mechanisms are identical for every question.
counterexamples.effect: Nondetection does not establish a common answer across the set; sufficient grounds specific to the question and tolerance are required.

counterexamples.text: Record counts doubled, so the true object count must have doubled.
counterexamples.effect: Changing coverage rules alone produces the same record pattern in this construction.

questionAnswers.question: Given only nonnegative integers x+y=10, how many elements does Z contain, and what can be said about the total and the difference's direction?
questionAnswers.answer: 11 elements. Total 10 is identified; the difference ranges from −10 to 10, with unknown direction.

11.3.2.title: 11.3.2 Event handling and state continuation
11.3.2.lead: A new message may mean the world just changed, or that today we learned what happened yesterday. An updating system must separate those cases while handling corrections, repeated relays, and order conflicts, without replacing actual event order with message-arrival order.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2411–2418; source anchor section-11-3-2; short quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Both kinds of updating can jointly change Ω.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

Retain three times for every input: event occurrence, record acquisition, and model entry. Occurrence may be known only as a window or a reported claim; do not invent exact seconds. Late evidence can change current judgments about the past, but the information available then cannot be rewritten, or replay will masquerade as prediction made at the time.

For corrected sources, append the correction relationship and recalculate states and paths depending on that source. Dependencies determine recalculation scope; unrelated conclusions are not all revoked. Retain old versions so the basis of the original judgment and where it failed remain visible.

Multiple items may relay the same event. Retain multiple sources with one candidate event identity to avoid applying the shock repeatedly. Similar wording may also describe distinct events; similar names alone cannot merge them. The times, objects, sources, and event identities supporting deduplication may themselves remain unchecked.

Evidence updating revises knowledge of z(t); mechanism advancement estimates changes from time t onward. If a credible record that ‘work stopped yesterday’ arrives today, today's events are learning and updating model evidence; the stoppage belongs to yesterday. Rerunning a model to obtain ‘work may stop’ produces only new simulation material, not an actual work-stoppage event.

Both operations may change Ω, but for different reasons. More accurate knowledge of yesterday's inventory is not another warehouse delivery today; projecting future inventory by an explicit rule is not seeing the future. The same state field can therefore carry both an object time and a knowledge version.

Concurrent events can be combined in arbitrary order only if operations commute, shared resources do not conflict, and neither changes the other's conditions. Check commutation on the relevant complete state and permitted domain; identical final totals alone do not establish identical authority, resource occupation, or intermediate harm.

When two actions compete for capacity, overwrite the same record, or change each other's available actions, retain order branches or explicit concurrency rules. Nearby timestamps do not establish simultaneity, and an executor returning first does not establish earlier real occurrence; transmission and processing delays may differ. If order is unidentified, output the corresponding result set rather than secretly choosing an order for reproducibility.

distinctions.leftText: Revising judgments about past or current states today.
distinctions.rightText: Estimating subsequent changes from a state according to rules.

distinctions.leftText: Affected by transmission and processing delays.
distinctions.rightText: Requires event-time and channel evidence; neither order can be directly inferred from the other.

distinctions.leftText: Multiple records or relays.
distinctions.rightText: Distinguishable actual occurrences, which may be interdependent; check event identity and deduplication.

distinctions.leftText: Local results happen to agree.
distinctions.rightTitle: Complete operations may be combined arbitrarily
distinctions.rightText: Also requires no conflicts in resources, conditions, or other key states.

distinctions.leftText: Repair relevant judgments.
distinctions.rightText: Local results independent of the erroneous source remain.

boundaries: Late facts must not be fed back into old prediction information sets; replay is valuable but has a different status.
Regenerating a model narrative alone is not a new real event or observation.
Deduplication does not delete sources; retain source lineage and grounds for merging. Similar events may genuinely occur more than once.
Executor completion order cannot be treated as real causal order.
Arbitrary combination is conditionally permissible, not the default for every near-simultaneous event.

caseLinks.title: Snow records deaths and registration at different times

caseNotes.title: Snow records deaths and registration at different times
caseNotes.text: Snow's 1855 book explains that some deaths in the relevant area during the first two days of September 1854 were not registered until the following week. Death records from hospitals and other locations also required distinctions in data scope. This section uses only the first fact to show that actual event time and record-creation time cannot be collapsed into one clock.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: John Snow, 1855 second edition
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Original printed pp.40–41, the paragraph containing ‘not registered till the week following’ in the Broad Street outbreak discussion
caseNotes.boundary: This is Snow's retrospective reconstruction of registration delays. This lesson lacks model-entry times for individual death records, does not equate death dates with infection dates, and does not calculate transmission parameters for the entire epidemic.

argumentSteps: For every input, distinguish occurrence, acquisition, and model-entry times, including precision and evidence.
Treat new evidence as knowledge updating, register real events at their object time, and separately retain conditional status for model advancement.
Append source corrections and recalculate along dependencies, retaining independent local results and old versions.
Check candidate event identity for deduplication, neither applying repeated shocks nor casually merging similar events.
For concurrency, check commutation, resources, and effects on conditions, specifying the permitted domain and intermediate states.
When arbitrary combination is impossible, retain order or concurrency branches and output uncertainty ranges and discriminating evidence.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: operation order changes the answer
teachingExamples.text: A fictional state x starts at 1, with f(x)=x+1 and g(x)=2x. Applying f then g gives g(f(1))=4; applying g then f gives f(g(1))=3, so the operations do not commute. If evidence establishes only that both occurred in overlapping windows with unknown order, the final candidates are {3,4}; whichever tool message returns first cannot select the answer.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Operation definitions, absence of other updates, and overlapping windows are teaching assumptions; no real probabilities for the two orders are given.
teachingExamples.boundary: Coincidence at a particular initial value or agreement in one field also cannot generally establish commutation.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: different fields may still compete for one resource
teachingExamples.text: Fictional tasks A and B each need one on-duty worker continuously for one hour and must finish within the same hour. Only one worker is available, cannot work in parallel, and neither task can be split. Their completion flags occupy different fields and appear independently updatable to complete; once shared capacity is included, both cannot finish within the window. Retain branches prioritizing A or B, or another actually feasible schedule.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The window, indivisibility, inability to parallelize, and capacity are constructed premises; no real staffing arrangement or authorization exists.
teachingExamples.boundary: Different fields do not guarantee independent resources; adding staff next hour also cannot restore a completion window already missed.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a local source correction does not erase independent records
teachingExamples.text: A fictional inventory is 5. Report E1, ‘2 were taken yesterday,’ produces knowledge version V1 with inventory 3 and subsequent predictions based on it. An independent system has its own reliable temperature record of 20. Today E1 is verified as erroneous; append correction V2, restore the inventory estimate to 5, and recalculate dependent projections. Temperature 20 is not revoked by the unrelated E1 correction. Updating the model today does not physically add 2 items back to the world.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The fictional evidence explicitly specifies E1's error, no other inventory changes, and temperature evidence independent of E1. Real dependencies require checking; different names alone do not establish independence.
teachingExamples.boundary: Correcting knowledge is not new physical replenishment. If the original removal was real and items were later returned, record a separate real event.

counterexamples.text: Two operations have close timestamps, so they may be processed arbitrarily in return order.
counterexamples.effect: Commutativity, resources, and conditions require checking; the f/g construction gives different consequences.

counterexamples.text: Two news reports say work stopped yesterday, so the model should apply two stoppages.
counterexamples.effect: First check whether they concern the same candidate event; more material does not mean more real occurrences.

counterexamples.text: Correcting an inventory message requires withdrawing an independent temperature record.
counterexamples.effect: Recomputation follows dependencies; independent local facts should not be collaterally deleted.

questionAnswers.question: Starting at 1 with f=x+1 and g=2x, what do the two orders produce?
questionAnswers.answer: f then g gives 4, while g then f gives 3; unknown order should therefore preserve {3,4}.

questionAnswers.question: If a credible record of yesterday's work stoppage arrives today, which day contains the evidence update and which the real event?
questionAnswers.answer: Evidence is obtained today; the stoppage is registered as yesterday's event, with model entry possibly at another time.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why can two tasks with different completion fields still not be directly merged in parallel?
questionAnswers.answer: They may share capacity or change one another's conditions; examine the complete task constraints.

questionAnswers.question: How is recalculation scope determined after a source correction?
questionAnswers.answer: Recompute states and paths actually supported by that source, retaining independent results and old versions.

11.4.title: 11.4 Nine-step projection loop
11.4.lead: The nine steps connect a dynamic analysis: establish its starting point, explain how events change conditions, and let real outcomes correct earlier judgments. They do not guarantee that reality follows the diagram or require filling nine boxes with invented knowledge.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2419–2420; source anchor section-11-4; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “Nine-step projection loop.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

This parent section contains only a navigational heading; substantive requirements lie in nine subsections. Step one freezes the starting point; two checks actors and circles; three separates M and Ψ by task; four declares clocks and channel constraints. These prepare a checkable starting point and grounds for propagation, not replaceable by an attractive relationship diagram.

Step five registers actual status of events or actions; six analyzes changes along supported channels; seven preserves branches at genuine uncertainties; eight records signals, residuals, and candidates; nine adds write-back from later actual outcomes. Each output becomes a bounded premise for later judgments; completing the procedure does not make false premises true.

A closed loop does not feed expected outcomes back as starting evidence. Save the old run, then incorporate new material in a new version; otherwise what was said at the time and comparison with a simple baseline cannot be recovered. Actual outcomes may support local paths without automatically certifying every mechanism.

These nine steps organize event projection. The book's XK0–XK11 is a broader analytical process, IG's seven gates address thresholds such as individual generation, and dynamic eligibility has its own checks. Counts cannot be merged merely because they are called steps, nor can finishing nine steps imply passing every gate.

The explanations use an explicitly fictional repair queue throughout: 6 pending items at 08:00, originally 2 arrivals and 3 processed per hour. Personnel, events, and later readings are teaching stipulations, not a business investigation. Sharing the starting point across subsections compares responsibilities; it does not turn one construction into several empirical cases. Apollo 13 material is separately inserted as bounded historical evidence, without claiming participants used Xikari or empirical superiority of the nine steps.

distinctions.rightText: No such guarantee: evidence may be missing, mechanisms wrong, or boundaries exceeded.

teachingExamples.text: If the repair queue's 08:00 state and arrival rate are known but actual processing is only known to be either 1 or 3 items/hour, the queue after two hours is respectively 8 or 4. 11.4.1.title: 11.4.1 Step one: freeze the current state
11.4.1.lead: Freezing is a dated snapshot of the analytical starting point, preserving what was known, unknown, and which model version was used. It does not require the world to stop changing.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2421–2424; source anchor section-11-4-1; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “Information acquired after the cutoff cannot be fed backward into the starting point.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

Evidence cutoff means “the latest acquisition time of material allowed in this run,” not that all described events occurred then. A record of yesterday's event received today becomes knowledge usable only today; event, acquisition, and model-entry clocks remain separate under 11.3.2.

A snapshot specifies at least objects, task, variables, values and their status, unknowns, disputes, sources, and model version. Equal values may differ in status: measured inventory 6 and inventory stipulated as 6 for projection are not the same evidence. Disputes are not blanks that must vanish; two compatible states may remain.

Freezing the model includes actual rules and key parameters, not just a filename. If a queue originally assumes 3 processed per hour and later 1, specify whether knowledge, actual capacity, or only a new scenario changed. Otherwise a seemingly continuous curve may splice different models.

Late evidence can of course be used, but in a new run version. The old version evaluates judgments under information then available; the new version serves the current task. Both may coexist. Reconstructing an accident from later evidence is retrospective explanation, not a relabeled preaccident prediction.

Freezing enables comparison, not guaranteed starting accuracy. If material is wrong, append corrections and recompute dependencies; “already frozen” cannot justify refusing correction, nor may the corrected starting point replace old records to erase the original error.

caseNotes.title: Apollo 13: a fault not yet understood at the time
caseNotes.text: When the 1970 Apollo 13 accident first occurred, its cause and severity were unknown. The report then describes ground personnel progressively checking electrical and oxygen readings. This section focuses on the temporal development of knowledge: retrospective findings cannot be inserted into the first alarm moment.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: NASA，Report of Apollo 13 Review Board，1970-06-15
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Chapter 4 Part 5, printed pp.4-44,4-46; PDF pp.153,155, Understanding the Problem
caseNotes.boundary: Supports only incomplete initial understanding and subsequent checking. This lesson has no complete second-by-second information sets and did not reconstruct prediction accuracy at the time.

argumentSteps: Specify task, object, and evidence cutoff, preserving actual acquisition times item by item.
Register variable and unknown status, sources, and disputes without zero-filling missing values.
Freeze rules, parameters, and versions so derivational responsibility for the same inputs is traceable.
Create a new run for later material while keeping the old one traceable; corrections propagate along dependencies.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a late fault notice
teachingExamples.text: At 08:00 freeze V1: 6 pending repairs, arrivals 2/hour, processing 3/hour. Under B_next_hour=max(0,B+arrivals−processing), 09:00 projects to 5. At 08:30 a credible notice reports that the machine slowed to 1/hour at 07:50. Create V2 and recalculate 08:00–09:00 as 7. V1 derives from material available then; V2 is a retrospective correction incorporating late information, not proof that 7 was predicted at 08:00.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Fault time, capacity change, and notice credibility are fictional assumptions; no real machine is involved.
teachingExamples.boundary: V2 does not mean the machine slowed again at 08:30; do not count the event twice.

counterexamples.text: Since the fault is later known to have occurred at 07:50, it can be inserted into material known at 08:00.
counterexamples.effect: Earlier occurrence does not mean earlier knowledge; preserve knowledge timing.

questionAnswers.question: Why must V1 and V2 both be retained?
questionAnswers.answer: V1 answers how judgment was made then; V2 answers how new material revises it. Deleting V1 destroys grounds for evaluation and correction.

questionAnswers.question: If inventory 6 proves a recording error after freezing, may it no longer be corrected?
questionAnswers.answer: Append a correction and create a new version, without overwriting the old run or treating the correction as a new inventory arrival.

11.4.2.title: 11.4.2 Step two: identify actors and circles
11.4.2.lead: A shared roster, label, or one collaboration need not form a circle with stable boundaries; one choice need not reveal fixed personality. First establish whom we discuss and how they connect.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2425–2428; source anchor section-11-4-2; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “Do not forcibly reify merely to complete the graph.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

Part Nine brings actors' slow, mid, and fast states and conditional action sets into analysis. Part Ten examines establishing circle-object facts from documents, relationships, and interactions, separately testing grouping gain for the task. This section uses those results, not permanent personality types assigned to everyone.

Actors may be individuals actually having effects or supported collective objects. Before graph inclusion, state evidence for task-relevant responsibilities, capabilities, resources, and relations. A name's appearance or shared job title does not automatically establish decision-making authority for the same action; inferring psychological motives from office also exceeds the boundary.

Candidate circle groupings remain analytically useful for proposing connections, shared resources, and boundaries to check. But a candidate cannot first become an established collective node whose assumed will explains member behavior; that makes object and mechanism circularly certify each other.

Retaining variable candidates when personality evidence is insufficient means “this difference may matter and remains to be distinguished,” not permission to collect more private experiences. Prioritize task-required observable behavior and conditions such as schedules, authorization, and equipment availability; do not misattribute equipment constraints to poor responsibility.

Circle boundaries may be nested, overlapping, or parallel by dimension. Maintenance and purchasing teams sharing a coordinator does not mean they merged into one object; examine people, budgets, permission, and task chains separately. Documents, membership, sustained interaction, or shared exposure can also support corresponding object facts without unified will in every circle. Only grouping-related explanatory or foresight gain claims separately require G1; untested G1 cannot erase independent object facts. When scale changes, reconfirm meanings of nodes and edges.

This step keeps two material accounts: facts about agents' and circles' identities, membership, and relationships; and gains from using those groupings in the current projection task. Reliable documents and interaction records may support the former; only formal support for the latter checks G1. When both are missing, retain candidates, but do not misstate absence of G1 as absence of these people in reality.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one person across groups is not unified capacity
teachingExamples.text: Fictional repair team Alpha has technicians A and B; procurement team Beta has purchaser C and coordinator B. A is qualified to repair, C has procurement authority, and B only transmits paperwork. Roster overlap supports only overlap in personnel; C cannot be counted as repair capacity, nor B regarded as authorized to approve purchases. If all that is known is that the three share a chat group, even these groupings remain to be checked.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Roles and authority are wholly stipulated in the construction; no actual person's capabilities or psychology are judged.
teachingExamples.boundary: Communication in one group may supply an information channel but does not directly establish shared budgets, unified will, or action permission.

counterexamples.text: Because B belongs to both groups, they can be merged into one agent with unlimited complementarity.
counterexamples.effect: Shared membership does not remove skill, authority, time, or resource constraints.

questionAnswers.answer: No. The roster may provide candidate entry, but task-relevant connections, boundaries, and operating materials are still required.

11.4.3.title: 11.4.3 Step three: separate dual-channel conditions
11.4.3.lead: Material feasibility and how people understand, experience, or accept something are two kinds of conditions. When one kind of material is missing, pause inferences depending on it without necessarily stopping every other independent judgment.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2429—2432; source anchor section-11-4-3; short quotation: ‘pause only propagation that depends on the missing channel’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

M records task-relevant material conditions such as quantities, equipment, work hours, interfaces, and budgets; Ψ records experience–meaning conditions such as expressed feelings, interpretations of meaning, or understandings of justification. These are neither mutually exclusive worlds nor default mirror images, and evidence for one does not automatically establish the other.

A cross-channel bridge explains which material change affects which experience–meaning variable through what distinguishable mechanism, or conversely how it produces action and material consequences. Restored repair equipment does not mean restored employee trust; a survey expressing support does not mean actual increased processing capacity. Connection requires a corresponding bridge and temporal materials.

Missing and not applicable differ. If the question asks only the number of items a specified machine can complete under fixed settings, personal experience may be inapplicable to that local calculation, with reasons stated. If the question asks willingness to work overtime, experience, meaning, and autonomous choice may alter the answer; missingness cannot be filled as willingness through an assumption of symmetry.

A local pause protects evidential boundaries. Unknown willingness to work overtime does not prevent reporting checked machine capacity, but it blocks continued inference along ‘the machine has spare capacity → employees will stay → the backlog must clear’. Separate the supported capacity path from the behavioral path awaiting checking, preventing both spread of unknowns throughout the system and bypassing of unknowns.

Do not collect experiential materials for formal completeness. Questions about psychology, health, or private life require actual necessity and appropriate boundaries; marking task-irrelevant Ψ fields not applicable is more honest than filling guesses or creating intrusive surveys.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one result known, another unknown
teachingExamples.text: A fictional device has two idle hours, processes at most 3 items per hour, and has sufficient materials. Its equipment ceiling is therefore 6 items. The equipment-capacity ceiling of 6 may be given, but not guaranteed actual completion of 6. Unknown willingness and unknown permission also cannot replace each other.

11.4.4.title: 11.4.4 Step four: declare clocks, thresholds, capacities, and delays
11.4.4.lead: ‘It will get through’ is insufficient: ask how long it takes, how much can pass at once, what is lost en route, and whether the window has already been missed. An arrow without a clock easily turns possible into timely and available stock into adequate supply.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2433—2436; source anchor section-11-4-4; short quotation: ‘mark an update clock for every variable’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

Variable-update clocks may use fixed intervals, event triggers, batch settlement, or slow, intermediate, and fast cycles at different levels. Inventory checked hourly, instantaneous alarms, and work hours recorded only the next day cannot be treated as simultaneous states without alignment. Observation frequency also differs from actual change frequency.

Thresholds need triggering direction and equality conventions; capacities need units and windows; delays must distinguish execution, transmission, and recording. Register losses, saturation, reversals, and recovery windows only when relevant and supported by materials. Unsupported details remain unknown rather than assuming identical nonlinearities in every system.

A capacity of 3 items per hour does not mean 3 items can be completed immediately; total stock of 10 also does not mean 10 can be obtained at a particular location within 10 minutes. If a channel waits an hour before transport, a recovery action may arrive too late for the current task window. Temporal constraints can change option rankings without changing the eventual total.

Near thresholds, distinguish measurement error and hysteresis: crossing an alarm value may differ from actual harm, and if cooling is still needed after a rise before recovery, recrossing a threshold in reverse cannot instantly erase downtime. These are recording responsibilities, not a claim that every object exhibits hysteresis.

Declaring parameters is not accurately estimating them. Sources may be equipment specifications, current observations, or model assumptions, whose statuses should be separated. High-consequence settings require conservatively retained uncertainty ranges; teaching formulas cannot become real control instructions directly.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: late replenishment cannot recover a missed window
teachingExamples.text: A fictional repair task requires completing 3 items during 08:00—09:00, each consuming 1 part; stock at 08:00 is 1 part. Replenishment of 2 parts arrives only at 09:00, and the task definition requires completion strictly before 09:00. Even if equipment can process 3 items per hour, parts limit this window to at most 1 item; cumulative parts reaching 3 at 09:00 does not make 3 completed in the earlier window.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Parts cannot be borrowed in advance, each completed item must already have consumed a part, and both arrival time and the strictly exclusive deadline are construction assumptions.
teachingExamples.boundary: If the contract permits completion after arrival at 09:00 or extends the task window, the question must be rewritten; the deadline cannot be silently changed to rescue the conclusion.

counterexamples.text: The final resource total is sufficient, so demand can be met at every intermediate moment.
counterexamples.effect: Inventory and throughput are not temporally aligned; an early gap may be irreversible.

questionAnswers.question: What are processing 3 items per hour and currently having 3 spare parts, respectively?
questionAnswers.answer: The former is capacity within a time window, the latter inventory at a time point; they constrain jointly but are not interchangeable.

11.4.5.title: 11.4.5 Step five: inject events or actions
11.4.5.lead: First ask whether something happened, then who did it, to whom, with what consequences, and with what authority. Unauthorized acts may still actually occur, while things written into plans may never happen at all.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2437—2440; source anchor section-11-4-5; short quotation: ‘first establish whether the action occurred’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

A run may contain multiple events and actions; real chains need not be deleted to ‘look at one at a time’. Each retains independent sources, times, and identities before being connected through grounded temporal order. When order cannot be determined, retain branches under 11.3.2 rather than substituting the order in which tool messages return for real-world order.

Agent, object, consequences, and authorization status are different fields. Observing a machine shut down does not identify its operator; confirming the operator also does not establish their motives or authority. Leave each missing item unknown rather than deleting the entire fact.

Under 11.3's notation, u is reserved for authorized actions that actually occur; observed or reported actions that occurred without authorization may enter e as events, with authority listed separately. This registers world changes without endorsing behavior; multiple references to the same action still apply its corresponding effect only once.

Plans, recommendations, and simulated actions that have not occurred retain conditional status. For example, ‘if another shift is added’ generates hypothetical consequences only and cannot automatically add staff to the baseline state. Approval also does not mean arrival; execution still requires occurrence evidence.

Forming a recommendation for deliberation and executing for someone are two levels of behavior. Recommendations may be offered after making evidence, value premises, costs, authority gaps, and revision conditions explicit. A model actually initiating real action requires separate valid authorization and corresponding protection checks. ‘This option is best’ cannot become an authorization letter, nor can lack of execution authority justify rejecting every bounded analysis.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: unauthorized withdrawal and pending replenishment
teachingExamples.text: A fictional warehouse starts with 5 items. Reliable records show someone took 2 without permission; another 3-item resupply is approved but has not arrived. If resupply later actually arrives, register it separately; only then does stock become 6 under these assumptions.

11.4.6.title: 11.4.6 Step Six: Propagate along Declared Channels
11.4.6.lead: One place changes and another changes later; this is not yet a causal arrow. Preserve known changes first, then ask segment by segment which channel, which period, and which competing explanations were distinguished.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2441–2444; source anchor section-11-4-6; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘Unknown internal mechanisms remain unknown.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

Direct state differences also have evidence status: keep measured differences, record-supported inferences, and conditional model calculations separately. ‘Direct’ does not automatically mean a causal effect identified by randomized experiment; uncontrolled before-and-after differences may include shared background changes.

Feedback requires material on return and subsequent state or rule changes; a message’s arrival is not learning. Indirect effects need valid intermediate transmission, and cross-circle cascades need each boundary and resource interface checked. Crossing one layer does not automatically inherit the preceding layer’s efficacy.

Separate total effects from internal mechanisms. A bounded intervention effect on a final outcome identified by an appropriate design may be retained despite unclear mediators; unknown mediators cannot be filled into a unique chain. Conversely, knowing one feasible mechanism does not automatically determine actual total-effect magnitude.

Correlation and co-occurrence may prompt investigation, but shared shocks, selection into records, and reverse effects may produce similar patterns. Specific propagation requires matching timing, interfaces, and flow evidence and explaining how alternatives are distinguished; absent material, mark candidate edges.

Mathematical propagation depends on explicit functions, parameters, and feasible domains. Even positive average gains on each edge may yield no total gain when windows, subgroup selection, or intermediate states do not match; 11.6 develops these interface issues. This step cannot mechanically multiply arrows as facts.

caseNotes.title: Apollo 13: an evidenced energy–water-use connection
caseNotes.text: The report connects reduced Lunar Module power consumption, lower heat production, and reduced cooling-water use. Compared with the consumption-rate window in the preceding subsection, this adds that propagation explanations need specific intermediate links, not simply ‘save electricity → everything improves’.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: NASA，Report of Apollo 13 Review Board，1970-06-15
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Chapter 4, Part 5, Return to Earth, printed p. 4-48, final paragraph on PDF page 156
caseNotes.boundary: The report supports this specific engineering explanation, not attribution of all psychological, organizational, or safety outcomes to saving power; this guide independently estimates no causal-effect magnitude.

argumentSteps: Confirm the starting point and direct state differences’ status and timing.
List channel, conditions, scope, sources, and competing explanations for every edge.
Retain identified total effects separately from unknown internal mechanisms.
Store model derivations separately as conditional results without upgrading them to actual observations.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: queue calculation and observation are separate
teachingExamples.text: Fictional B0=6 with 2 arrivals per hour. If a breakdown fixes processing capacity at 1, B1=6+2−1=7 and B2=7+2−1=8. If another branch retains capacity 3, B1=5 and B2=4. This is a conditional difference of 4 items under the specified recurrence. Without an actual breakdown intervention or observations, it cannot be reported as ‘breakdown empirically increased backlog by 4’.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Arrivals precede processing each hour; capacity stays fixed for two hours, no other flows exist, and both branches share initial value and arrivals.
teachingExamples.boundary: If actual breakdown also changes arrivals or measurement rules, this difference cannot transfer directly.

counterexamples.text: Two simulations differ by 4, so an actual breakdown’s causal effect has been measured as 4.
counterexamples.effect: A simulation comparison is only a model-conditional difference, lacking actual identification design and observation.

counterexamples.text: The total effect is reliable, but one internal link is unknown, so the total effect must be deleted too.
counterexamples.effect: Retain the independently valid bounded result and mark the unknown mechanism separately.

questionAnswers.question: Why are successive changes insufficient for a causal edge?
questionAnswers.answer: Shared background, record selection, and other mechanisms can produce the same sequence; corresponding channels and discriminating material are needed.

questionAnswers.question: Does an identified total effect permit completing the internal mechanism graph?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Preserve the bounded total effect while leaving unknown mediators unfilled.

11.4.7.title: 11.4.7 Step Seven: Generate Paths at Branch Points
11.4.7.lead: Branching is not about writing many stories; it preserves conditional differences that may still change the answer. Distinguish ‘only one can occur’ from ‘they may occur together’, then decide between separate and parallel branches.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2445–2448; source anchor section-11-4-7; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘Separate mutually exclusive paths.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

Branches may arise from condition values, near-threshold states, actors’ choices, external disturbances, or mechanism uncertainty. State triggering differences, not merely emotional labels ‘optimistic, ordinary, pessimistic’. Branches also need one frozen starting point; otherwise the comparison may silently change initial values.

Mutually exclusive paths cannot both count toward one actual result. An indivisible task choosing either machine A or B within one window has exclusive choices; procurement delay and machine failure may coincide, so forcing them into either/or omits their joint branch.

Co-occurrence also does not mean independence. Branches sharing workers or budgets, or affecting one another’s conditions, need joint states and shared-resource constraints. Separate feasibility cannot establish joint feasibility.

Merge nodes require an explicit contract: which key states, remaining resources, history dependencies, authorities, and future actions are sufficiently identical or equivalent for a bounded task? Equal final stock does not automatically permit merging; failure debt or missed commitments may still affect the next step.

Branch counts are not credibility; ten generated scenarios do not automatically form a frequency distribution. Without probability grounds, retain conditional paths and preserve key branches by impact and distinguishability where necessary. Diagram neatness cannot justify deleting a high-loss branch with substantive possibility. Section 11.9 later addresses path lineage and pruning records.

argumentSteps: Generate branches from specific conditional differences that change the task answer.
Determine exclusivity, co-occurrence, or sequential dependence, constructing joint states when needed.
Keep starting points, triggers, and resource limits traceable for every branch.
Merge only when key states meet explicit merger conditions, without default probabilities.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: two disturbances form four joint conditions
teachingExamples.text: Fictional B0=6 and B1=B0+arrivals−processing after one hour. Arrivals may be 2 or 4, processing 3 or 1. Joint conditions yield (2,3)→5, (2,1)→7, (4,3)→7, and (4,1)→9. Listing only exclusive stories of ‘more arrivals’ and ‘slower processing’ misses their joint 9. The two 7s also arise from different arrival/capacity states; if later conditions persist, current equality at 7 alone does not permit merging.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All four combinations are allowed in the construction; no actual probabilities are given. If conditions persist next hour, both 7s become 8, but flows and intervention responses still differ.
teachingExamples.boundary: If only first-hour backlog matters and subsequent mechanisms genuinely do not, the two 7s may share an outcome class while retaining their source branches.

counterexamples.text: Both branches reach 7, so they remain equivalent forever.
counterexamples.effect: Equal terminal values do not guarantee equal resources, mechanisms, or feasible interventions; merging needs a bounded task.

questionAnswers.answer: Increased arrivals and reduced capacity may co-occur; forced exclusivity misses joint conditions.

11.4.8.title: 11.4.8 Step Eight: Register Signals, Residuals, and Variable Candidates
11.4.8.lead: An unexplained model difference calls for checking, not inventing a new real-world variable’s value. Each path should specify which signals support it and which would change the judgment.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2449–2452; source anchor section-11-4-8; short quotation translated from Chinese: ‘Actual values cannot be generated automatically.’ See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloadable original research excerpt retains the historical draft.

Early signals need observation definitions, windows, sources, and associated branches—for example, first observing an actual processing decline, then whether backlog follows the corresponding path. A supporting signal is not absolute proof; check whether competing paths also produce it. A contrary signal is a distinguishable observation weakening the path, without waiting for the endpoint before recognizing failure.

Residuals first depend on model and observation definitions. Observed 8 versus predicted 7 gives residual 1, indicating only this discrepancy. It may reflect unrecorded arrivals, processing-capacity error, mismatched windows, observation error, or omitted mechanisms. Without discriminating material, ‘difference 1’ cannot establish a real variable called collaboration resistance with value 1.

A variable-candidate ledger should record definition, reason for proposal, observation method, supportive and contrary material, competing explanations, and upgrade conditions. It turns questions into testable work, not a new freely adjustable factor for every residual.

Residuals are not automatically random noise. Inference using means, variances, or distributions needs corresponding sampling and error conditions; selective missingness or changed definitions cannot usually be assigned to independent identically distributed error without explanation. Repetition strengthens reasons to investigate, not direct identification of a mechanism.

Prioritize the smallest discriminating observation that changes the current answer or action comparison. More candidates are not inherently better; if a simple recording-definition issue suffices, check it before adding hidden variables to preserve complexity.

A new variable cannot merely be defined to absorb every error exactly.
If observation definitions change, update the observation model before rushing to change the world’s mechanism.

When should contrary signals be registered?

Design minimal discriminating material, then upgrade, retain, split, or withdraw candidates according to results.

Explanation B: one processed item was erroneously recorded, actual processing 0. Both give 8. Actual completion records may distinguish them; directly setting ‘team friction=1’ neither excludes these record explanations nor provides a measurable definition.

11.4.9.title: 11.4.9 Step nine: outcome write-back
11.4.9.lead: When outcomes arrive, honest comparison matters: what was right, what was wrong, and which simple method was better. Inserting the ending into the original draft is not learning. Preserving that draft and letting new evidence change the next version makes scrutiny possible.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2453–2456; original anchor section-11-4-9. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Write-back does not overwrite the original run.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

Write-back first appends actual outcomes with sources, object-event times, and acquisition times, then matches them to the original run. A news narrative or rerunning a model is not equivalent to actual outcomes. If outcomes have not arrived or definitions do not match, retain unresolved status rather than forcing closure.

Support for a path does not make every mechanism true. Different mechanisms can yield the same outcome, and errors may cancel into apparent success. Examine timing, magnitude, key intermediate signals, and contrary material together. Locate local departures through dependencies; one failure does not make the entire framework useless, nor one success universally effective.

Compare simple baselines for the same target, window, available information, and scoring rule. A queue task might initially use the last observation carried forward. If the complex model performs worse, record it honestly and examine whether complexity adds actual gain. Do not select a baseline afterward merely to lose to the model.

Calibration is a long-term or grouped correspondence property of probability predictions, not one hit. If this run offered conditional branches without probabilities, assess coverage, timing, conditions, and distinguishing power; do not invent probabilities afterward to claim good calibration. Part XII further specifies forecast contracts.

Write-back may downgrade mechanisms, split variables, narrow boundaries, or retire items, rather than merely add explanations. State which new evidence changes which dependency, how the next version handles it, and what remains unknown. Source corrections revise epistemic lineage; changed real conditions require event registration. Do not conflate them.

Creating a next version does not establish improved learning. Claiming it is better requires later independent or appropriately held-out testing. Repeatedly tuning to the same outcome for closer fit demonstrates only adaptation to seen material.

distinctions.rightText: Competing mechanisms may still produce the same outcome.

distinctions.rightText: Destroys the evaluation baseline and may disguise hindsight.

Do not record only hits while omitting failures and unresolved cases.
One failure may require local revision without automatically proving the whole theory invalid.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a complex model loses to a simple baseline
teachingExamples.text: Fictional pending repairs at 08:00 are 6. Beforehand, freeze a model prediction of 4 at 10:00, a carry-forward baseline of 6, and absolute-error scoring. Later, a consistently defined measurement is 7. Model error is |4−7|=3; baseline error |6−7|=1. The baseline wins this occasion. Changed arrivals or processing conditions may be investigated, but rewriting the original prediction to 7 cannot establish perfection.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All values, measurement status, and scoring are teaching constructions. No actual queue experiment occurred, and one sample does not estimate average performance.
teachingExamples.boundary: Probability calibration would additionally require prior probabilities and a multi-case evaluation contract. This example concerns point-prediction error only.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: matching final values can conceal an incorrect temporal path
teachingExamples.text: The original prediction is backlog 5 at 09:00 and 4 at 10:00; observations later give 8 and 4. Endpoint error is 0, but intermediate congestion was missed. If the task's protection condition requires no hourly value above 7, the path judgment failed. Endpoint success cannot conceal an intermediate breach.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Threshold and observations are constructed. Hourly checkpoints are stipulated and do not imply no larger peaks between them.
teachingExamples.boundary: If only an endpoint prediction was declared, its hit may remain; it cannot expand into successful prediction of safety throughout.

counterexamples.text: The final value was guessed correctly, so every mechanism, path, and calibration is confirmed.
counterexamples.effect: An endpoint hit does not identify intermediate paths, probability calibration, or a unique mechanism.

counterexamples.text: Changing the old prediction to the correct value using new material completes a learning loop.
counterexamples.effect: That overwrites the evaluation reference. Retain the old prediction and test a new version separately.

questionAnswers.question: With prediction 4, baseline 6, and actual 7, which is better under absolute error?
questionAnswers.answer: Model error is 3, baseline error 1; the baseline wins this occasion, without establishing long-term superiority.

questionAnswers.question: If endpoint 4 is correct but actual 09:00 value 8 exceeds threshold 7, is the whole path successful?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The endpoint task can succeed while path-protection conditions fail. Register them separately.

questionAnswers.question: May scenario branches alone be retrospectively declared well-calibrated probabilities?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Prior probabilities and corresponding evaluation data are required. Conditional coverage is not probability calibration.

11.5.title: 11.5 Propagation, delays, and thresholds
11.5.lead: A message arriving, being understood, changing a mind, and producing action are different changes. Propagation analysis must specify what changed, through which channel, how long effects take, and within which window they fail.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2457–2472; original anchor section-11-5. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Net effects must not conceal distributional differences.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

The first level is arrival: a system receives a message, presents it, or a person sees it. This supports only the corresponding arrival fact, not changed subsequent transitions. The second is experience–meaning change, such as evidenced belief revision. Retain that change even without action rather than declaring “nothing happened without behavior.” The third concerns changes to resources, behavior, rules, or relations, each registered by material rather than bundled as “effective.”

These levels are not a mandatory linear staircase. Resources can transfer before a person understands, and reading can alter understanding without behavior. Explain cross-channel bridges individually; exposure rates cannot directly become agreement rates or institutional-implementation rates.

The table's first item, channel, asks what carries the process: circuits, logistics, face-to-face exchange, rule implementation, or platform presentation each have objects and interfaces. Closure, filtering, and substitution change who receives what. An email's existence does not establish that its recipient read it; reading does not establish execution authority.

Capacity is measured per unit time and may saturate, queue, or congest. Delay distinguishes arrival from onset: one-second forwarding, one-day understanding, and one-week approval may coexist. No outcome before the predetermined effect window is not immediate proof of ineffectiveness. No response beyond a reliable maximum delay should count as contrary material. If the maximum delay is unknown, invent no deadline.

Thresholds specify conditions for state transitions, potentially with jumps or hysteresis. Loss concerns resource dissipation, information omission, and meaning transformation; the latter two may lack a common percentage measure. Direction reminds us that A affecting B does not imply equally strong B→A influence; opposing effects may also cancel.

Recovery asks how an object returns or enters a new state after a shock. Elastic recovery, cumulative damage, and lock-in are patterns to distinguish, not defaults for all systems. Separate recovery onset, local availability, and complete recovery. Availability of one core service does not instantly clear backlogs and downstream effects.

The same event may have opposite effects on different circles through different channels. The original resource/public-explanation example describes possible mechanisms, not grounds for declaring a group's shame or distrust without actual experiential material. Register by channel and position. Net totals may serve a specified statistical task without hiding burden bearers or protected constraints.

The requirement is responsibility for propagation statements, not complex simulation every time. A receipt or suitable log may suffice to establish document arrival; changed rules require decision, execution, and actual-outcome material. Task evidence requirements cannot be arbitrarily escalated, nor may an easily obtained indicator silently replace the question.

distinctions.rightText: Requires a reasonable predeclared window and adequate detection capability.

No short-term change is not automatically ineffectiveness, but endlessly extending windows cannot protect a model either.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: separate capacity and delay
teachingExamples.text: A fictional information-processing queue starts with 4 messages, receives 2 per minute, and processes at most 3. Under Q_next=max(0,Q+2−3), queue lengths are 3,2,1 in the first three minutes and 0 in the fourth. If arrival additionally requires a fixed 2 minutes before downstream state changes, clearing the queue does not mean the last message's effect has occurred. Queue waiting and effect delay are registered separately.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Arrivals, processing order, constant capacity, and fixed effect delay are teaching assumptions. Processing is lossless and newly arrived messages may be processed in the same minute.
teachingExamples.boundary: Understanding or executing actual messages need not follow fixed minute delays; this example estimates no human response speed.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: hysteresis is not one threshold applied both ways
teachingExamples.text: A fictional device shuts down at T≥80 and, once stopped, restarts only at T≤70, retaining its prior state between them. For 75→82→76→69, states are running→stopped→still stopped→restarted. Recording only current 76 without prior shutdown misclassifies recovery.
teachingExamples.assumptions: 80 and 70 are teaching thresholds, not equipment safety standards. Initial operation at 75 is stipulated.
teachingExamples.boundary: Offers no actual device-control advice and does not claim hysteresis in every system.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: net burden reduction cannot hide positional differences
teachingExamples.text: The same fictional resource reallocation reduces group A's weekly waiting by 10 hours but increases group B's by 8. If the task declares the groups' hours additive, net reduction is 2 hours, while B still worsens. If B faces a nonwaivable deadline constraint, net reduction 2 does not automatically make the option acceptable.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Values, comparable units, and causal differences are constructed, not measured in actual groups.
teachingExamples.boundary: Whether waiting across people can be added and which weights to use require separate normative explanation. This example authorizes nothing for stakeholders.

counterexamples.text: Read receipts reach 100%, so the institution is declared implemented.
counterexamples.effect: Arrival evidence cannot certify execution or actual write-back.

counterexamples.text: Temperature falls from 82 to 76, below 80, so operation must have resumed.
counterexamples.effect: The explicit hysteresis construction still requires reaching 70. Historical state changes the current judgment.

counterexamples.text: The two groups improve by 2 hours in total, so each group benefits.
counterexamples.effect: Aggregate conclusions do not imply individual or positional improvement; B's waiting still increases by 8 hours.
