Create the five-part stopping record and specify new material permitting reopening.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one false message recalculates only dependent branches
teachingExamples.text: A fictional warehouse has measured stock 10 and an independent temperature record 20. Report E predicts resupply 5, producing modeled tomorrow stock 15 and downstream allocation branches. E is later confirmed misissued. Stop or withdraw 15 and allocation inferences dependent on resupply, retaining measured 10 and independent temperature 20. If both sensors and the report later prove to use the wrong object ID shared by the whole model’s object identification, suspend the relevant runs together.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Independence of material and error scope are explicitly stipulated; no actual warehousing action occurs.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual independence cannot be inferred merely from different field names; check real sources and dependencies.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: equal baseline performance cannot be beaten by complexity
teachingExamples.text: Two fictional frozen models predict (4,6) for two targets, with actual outcomes (5,5). Regardless of the complex model’s node count, both have mean absolute error (|4−5|+|6−5|)/2=1. This use has no evidence of predictive increment; separate explanatory uses require their own evidence, not counting nodes as accuracy.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Predictions, outcomes, and scoring are teaching constructions; two samples cannot establish long-term statistical equivalence.
teachingExamples.boundary: ‘Equal this time’ does not rigorously prove equal future performance; it limits only gain claims supported by this material.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a complete stopping entry
teachingExamples.text: Location: stock→timely-delivery path. Obtained: reliable initial stock 10. Unknown: whether transport is open. Block: no usable channel material, so next-day arrival cannot be asserted. Next observation: check corresponding transport status and window within existing authority. Continuation risk: treating unknown as open may create unfulfillable commitments. Give only ‘arrival is possible if the channel is open and delay≤window’, without actually promising or dispatching.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The complete entry is a teaching proposal; no actual logistics query or commitment was sent.
teachingExamples.boundary: An independent local task unaffected by the channel may continue its analysis.

counterexamples.text: The resupply report was false, so independent temperature 20 must also be deleted.
counterexamples.effect: No dependency means no collateral erasure; stopping scope follows sources and mechanisms.

counterexamples.text: The global object ID is wrong; pausing one graph node suffices.
counterexamples.effect: Failed shared object premises require stopping all relevant dependent runs.

counterexamples.text: Both models have equal error, but the complex graph looks more professional, so foresight capability improved.
counterexamples.effect: Complexity and foresight increment differ; test under the same contract.

questionAnswers.question: When must all relevant runs stop?
questionAnswers.answer: When shared premises or overall use conditions fail and relevant paths all depend on them, not whenever any local unknown occurs.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If both predictions are (4,6) and outcomes (5,5), what is mean absolute error?
questionAnswers.answer: Both equal 1; current material supplies no gain for the complex model and does not prove long-term equivalence.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Is the most valuable post-stop observation necessarily permissible to obtain?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Necessity, privacy, safety, and authorization need separate checks; otherwise retain unknowns or return to a bounded question.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If the shared object ID is wrong, all related premises fail and every dependent run stops while object identification is repaired. Stopping records still state local knowledge, gaps, and material needed to reopen. Entirely teaching constructions; source independence and shared dependencies require actual verification, not guesses from field names.

11.11.title: 11.11 An example of a cross-circle cascade
11.11.lead: This is not an investigation of an actual company but the original text's continuing public-resignation teaching scenario. It lays out possible paths through the team, management, family, professional community, and platform, focusing on where conditions break rather than choosing a path for the company.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2562–2571; original anchor section-11-11. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “These enter only the variable-candidate ledger.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

Long hours, care pressure, declining team trust, management's reputational concerns, and community opportunities are all original scenario assumptions, not researcher measurements. Unformed platform public opinion is also just the starting premise. §10.11 first draws the joint objects and dual channels; this section injects publication of a resignation statement to show conditional branching of subsequent states.

The resignation statement contains checkable facts and personal narrative with different support scopes. Relevant working-hours, institutional-text, or handoff-record components may be independently verified. Feelings are material about the person's experience and claims, neither categorically noise nor substitutes for others' inner states or every fact of the event. No specific text is supplied here, so accusations, dialogue, and legal conclusions cannot be invented.

Direct effects also need separate channels: team receipt is arrival; platform receipt of the text creates propagatable material; pressure on management to respond is a stipulated consequence. Propagatability is not wide propagation, nor receipt belief. Actual applications must separately check visibility, responses, and subsequent states.

Path one begins with public denial: external attention may subside briefly or intensify. Further resignations along this branch require internal members to interpret denial as suppression, trust to fall further, and the professional community to create actual opportunity bridges. Every “if” bears independent evidential responsibility. Public denial is not automatically suppression, nor is everyone's interpretation identical.

Path two begins with acknowledgment and verifiable adjustments, distinguishing promises from execution. Only actual changes to resources and appeal procedures allow registration of working-hours and process changes on the organizational clock. Experience–meaning trust may recover more slowly or not at all. Better announcement wording does not establish resources in place, and resources in place do not automatically establish repaired meaning.

Path three improves family-care conditions, potentially reducing post-resignation pressure and changing the employee's available actions. It does not directly change the team. Further return requires channels such as continued information or resource bridging. The original avoids coloring the whole company as improved from one person's better state.

The three paths are neither mutually exclusive nor exhaustive histories. Family conditions may improve alongside company denial or actual adjustment. Management may deny first and reform later; create time- and evidence-specific nodes rather than compress all actions into one moment. These are meaningful mechanism entry points, with other supported paths possible in reality.

Early signals include changes in appeals, working-hours implementation, public expression, recruitment, and resignation. Each needs windows, denominators, and record-generation processes. More appeals may mean more problems or greater willingness to report through improved channels. Public silence may mean no objection, fear, platform exit, or something else. One indicator cannot decide every mechanism.

Contrary signals must target paths: a published policy without resource changes weakens “adjustment implemented”; reduced exposure with increased internal silence does not establish repaired trust; absent actual professional-community bridging blocks that opportunity-transmission segment. Contrary material weakens a specific explanation without automatically proving opposite motives.

Key managers' states, recommendation mechanisms, and legal constraints remain residual candidates. Without actual measurements or legal material, this section fills in no personalities, algorithm parameters, or responsibility verdicts. Projection yields conditional consequences and distinguishing signals only. “Which should be chosen” additionally needs normative premises, option comparison, and foresight responsibilities; execution further requires valid authorization.

boundaries: The original three branches supply no actual occurrence probabilities. Enumeration counts are not probabilities.
One event may produce opposite outcomes in different circles. External exposure is not a proxy for internal trust.
Unperformed resource changes cannot be recorded as complete. No actual personnel or legal disposition is executed in this example.
Resignation does not diagnose personality, nor are personal choices entirely dissolved into structural determination.
questions: Do appeals rising from 5 to 10 directly imply that actual problems doubled?
Can path one and family path three occur together?
May evidenced working-hours reductions be acknowledged before trust recovers?
Does this projection authorize a company to take a personnel action?
argumentSteps: Label the whole example an original teaching scenario, separating assumptions, checkable fact types, and personal narrative.
Enter subsequent conditional paths separately from information receipt, available text, and response pressure.
Check internal interpretations, actual resource adjustments, opportunity bridges, and family spillovers segment by segment. Arrival is not effect.
Register positive/contrary signals and competing explanations in different windows, retaining parallel paths.
Residuals enter only the candidate ledger. Normative preferences and execution require explicit conditions and authorization procedures.

teachingExamples.title: Reading branches in the original teaching scenario
teachingExamples.text: If a company announces a new appeal channel without changing budget, on-duty personnel, or processing authority, register only the announcement and its arrival. “Actual appeal-uptake capacity improved” remains to be checked. If later actual records show resources in place, update the corresponding organizational state without waiting for everyone's trust to recover before acknowledging resource changes.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Announcement and resource arrangements are teaching additions to the original fictional scenario, referring to no actual company.
teachingExamples.boundary: Obtain separate evidence for resources and trust; lack of verification for one cannot categorically negate the other.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: appeal counts depend on reporting channels
teachingExamples.text: Suppose each of two fictional weeks has 20 actual unresolved problems. In week one exactly 1/4 enter the records, yielding 5; in week two 1/2 enter, yielding 10. Doubled observed appeals do not mean doubled problems. With unknown recording probabilities, changed counts may also include changed problems; one cannot conclude everything merely reflects improved channels.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Coverage proportions here are exact aggregate recording fractions, not random sample realizations passed off as expectations. Problem counts and proportions are fictional.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual use must check definitions, denominators, duplicates, and selection. This example does not deny that actual problems may increase.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: the family branch can run in parallel without direct spillover
teachingExamples.text: A fictional employee gains caregiving support and more discretionary time each week while the company continues public denial. If the employee has left the team and transmits no further information or resources, this model has no edge from family improvement directly to team trust. If the professional community later creates a new bridge, new material must establish a separate path.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Exit and bridging status are stipulated. No care details are requested from actual families.
teachingExamples.boundary: Absence of the specified edge limits only this explanation, not all possible actual indirect connections.

counterexamples.text: Public exposure falls, so internal trust must have recovered.
counterexamples.effect: External visibility differs from internal meaning. Silence and exposure each have competing explanations.

counterexamples.text: The company says adjustment began, so working hours and appeal resources should immediately be marked improved.
counterexamples.effect: An initiation statement is not actual execution; corresponding records are required.

counterexamples.text: Care pressure decreases, so the company's team state automatically improves.
counterexamples.effect: A specific bridging channel is required; individual changes do not directly fill collective states.

questionAnswers.question: Do appeals rising from 5 to 10 directly imply that actual problems doubled?
questionAnswers.answer: No. In the construction, actual problems remain 20 while recorded coverage changes from 1/4 to 1/2. Reality requires separate checking.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can path one and family path three occur together?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes. They are not mutually exclusive options; retain parallel paths and check interfaces.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: May evidenced working-hours reductions be acknowledged before trust recovers?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes. Retain material/organizational change and separately check meaning recovery. Neither erases the other.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does this projection authorize a company to take a personnel action?
questionAnswers.answer: No. This is conditional analysis of the original fictional scenario, not a substitute for normative comparison or actual authorization.

11.12.title: 11.12 Outputs of this part
11.12.lead: A projection deliverable cannot consist only of a final route map. Readers should see starting points, events, assumptions, stepwise changes, unknowns, and stopping points, and know which elements are conditional preparation and which lack forecasting or action eligibility.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2572–2577; original anchor section-11-12. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “An explicit separation statement for prediction and action.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original; downloaded original research excerpts retain the historical draft.

The frozen joint snapshot specifies object, task, scale, time, evidence cutoff, and key states. Event types and evidence distinguish actual occurrence, reports, plans, and simulations; mechanism and parameter assumptions specify propagation dependencies. Without these three entry points, it is hard to tell whether later paths derive from the same start or switch premises segment by segment.

Update steps and the path graph jointly explain how changes occur. Each path retains conditions, clocks, support status, and early/contrary signals rather than merely “success” or “failure.” Ungrounded probabilities remain unassigned; a complete graph does not require invented numbers. Path lineage and identity continue under preceding contracts.

Residuals and variable candidates expose unexplained areas. Stopping conditions state when extrapolation ends. The outcome write-back plan specifies how future material will be compared with the original run and baseline. Plans are not observed outcomes; a completed write-back field does not mean learning occurred.

Projection helps structured preparation for changing conditions, but “improved foresight capability” is a separate testable claim requiring registration before outcomes, a reasonable simple baseline, corresponding calibration, and continuing write-back. Without these, say only that paths and signals for checking were organized, not that predictions improved. Where material supports a local conclusion, procedural modesty should not prevent a clear answer.

Explain prediction, normative judgment, and execution authority separately. Likelier occurrence does not imply something should be brought about. Under explicit normative premises, analysis may recommend, veto, or defer, fully stating evidence, costs, the opposing case, and revision conditions. Such deliberative judgment does not automatically receive actual execution authority.

“No claim that action should be executed without norms and authorization” does not mean analysts can never recommend. Norms premise comparison of goals, floors, and distribution; authorization determines who may implement actual actions. Missing execution permission still permits an analytical preference with gaps stated, but the two statuses must remain distinct. The next part separates prediction registration from option selection in detail.

Complete output is necessary for checkability, not sufficient for theoretical or empirical correctness. A file with every field may still contain faulty observations, mismatched mechanisms, or uncovered risks. Conversely, explicitly marking necessary fields inapplicable or unknown is better than filling them without grounds.

distinctions.leftText: Knowing which conditions change paths and what to observe.
distinctions.rightText: Requires a prior contract, baseline, and outcome evaluation.

distinctions.leftText: A commitment about comparing future material.
distinctions.rightText: Actual outcomes have arrived and changed corresponding records.

distinctions.leftText: A deliberative opinion under explicit norms and evidence.
distinctions.rightText: Requires separate valid authority, not automatically generated by preference.

distinctions.leftText: Content is locatable and checkable.
distinctions.rightText: Still requires support from facts, mechanisms, and applicability conditions.

boundaries: Do not invent parameters, measurements, or authorization to fill every field.
A preference with objections and costs is still a position. State the conditional judgment clearly.
Later factual changes require appended versions, not overwriting the original run.
questions: If the actual 09:00 outcome has not arrived, may residual 0 be registered?
With equal effects and risks and an explicit low-cost objective, how may A costing 2 and B costing 5 be compared?
What should a prediction-separation statement distinguish?
argumentSteps: Retain frozen snapshots, input statuses, and mechanism parameters so the starting point remains traceable.
Display update steps, path graphs, and each branch's conditions/clocks/support/positive and contrary signals.
List residual candidates, stopping conditions, and the write-back plan for actual outcomes when they arrive.
Declare separately conditional preparation, predictive-capability evaluation, normative opinions, and execution-authorization status.
Fully explain recommendation grounds, costs, objections, and revision conditions. Complete delivery does not replace factual testing.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a minimal but substantive projection summary
teachingExamples.text: The object is a fictional repair queue, frozen at 08:00 with B=6 and arrivals of 2/hour. The event is “if equipment slows,” not an event already occurring. The rule is next B=max(0,B+2−c), with assumed c=1 or 3. One-step path A gives 7 at 09:00, path B gives 5; the clock is one hour, support is conditional derivation, and no probabilities are supplied. The early signal is actual completions in the same window; the contrary signal is a record corresponding to the other capacity. Both branches share a starting point and are mutually exclusive. No actual reading yet permits residual calculation; the candidate set is empty, not numerical zero. Stop at 09:00 or when channel/object/permission conditions fail. The write-back plan is to obtain actual records with matching definitions, compare absolute error against the prespecified persistence baseline 6, and append a version. Separation statement: no predictive-gain score exists, and no repair or scheduling action is executed.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Numbers, event, and rules are teaching assumptions; no actual system was operated.
teachingExamples.boundary: Real-world support for candidate c is unknown and subsequent records have not arrived; “calibrated” or “zero residual” must not be recorded in advance.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: conditional recommendation is not execution
teachingExamples.text: In another fictional comparison, option A costs 2 and B costs 5; all relevant effects and risks are stipulated equal, and the explicit norm is “choose lower cost when the same protection conditions are met.” A may be analytically preferred because it costs 3 less. The counterargument is unexamined hidden maintenance cost; revision conditions are A's additional costs exceeding 3 or differing protection conditions. No actual permissions are supplied, so the advice remains for deliberation, without purchasing or scheduling.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Equal effects and risks are strong teaching assumptions, not a claim that real options require only financial comparison.
teachingExamples.boundary: The preference cannot be copied without explicit values or comparative evidence; cost definitions and rights floors also require actual verification.

counterexamples.text: A snapshot and path diagram exist, so foresight capability has improved.
counterexamples.effect: Without preregistration and outcome/baseline evaluation, this is organizational preparation, not evidence of gain.

counterexamples.text: Without execution authority, even a conditional preference cannot be proposed.
counterexamples.effect: Advice for deliberation may be offered where evidence and explicit norms permit, retaining the permission gap.

counterexamples.text: Results have not arrived, so enter 0 for the residual to complete the table.
counterexamples.effect: Not yet calculable means unknown or not applicable, not zero difference.

questionAnswers.question: If the actual 09:00 outcome has not arrived, may residual 0 be registered?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The residual is not yet calculable and must remain unresolved.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: With equal effects and risks and an explicit low-cost objective, how may A costing 2 and B costing 5 be compared?
questionAnswers.answer: Under these strong assumptions, analytically prefer A, saving 3, while stating the counterargument and revision conditions; do not execute without authority.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What should a prediction-separation statement distinguish?
questionAnswers.answer: Conditional derivation, observed fact, predictive performance, normative judgment, and actual execution permission must remain separate; one level does not automatically upgrade to the next.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

11.13.title: 11.13 Action Choice and Conditional Updating
11.13.lead: Action is more than choosing from a fixed menu. Acting changes resources, rules, relationships, and what others can do; the next step must begin from these new conditions rather than ask the model to reevaluate the same old menu.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2578–2587; original anchor: section-11-13; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Generating another narrative cannot replace state updating.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

At each step identify currently available and excluded actions, specifying whether limits come from capability, resources, time, relationships, institutions, or permissions. Exclusion may mean currently impossible or impermissible; distinguish them. Technically feasible unauthorized actions do not thereby enter the model's implementable action set.

Capability, belief, willingness, and actual action require separate evidence. Ability does not imply willingness; willingness does not imply belief in effectiveness; public intention does not mean execution; and an analyst's recommendation certainly does not mean adoption by the actor. Retain conditional paths for uncertain choices rather than decide for actors to advance another round.

Place possible choices within the actor's information, resources, relationships, habits, and objectives at the time. These may constrain or support strategies without completely determining the person absent identification; group tendencies also cannot fill all individual states. When anticipated responses of others change present strategy, anticipated reflexivity may be explicitly included while retaining its model-assumption status.

For each evidenced choice, specify triggering mechanisms, first changed states, transmission interfaces, affected objects and clocks, and calculate how these differences change the next action set. Concrete state differences may include reduced balances, new rule restrictions, changed relational commitments, updated beliefs, or more/fewer feasible tasks; “the system improves” is insufficient.

Later projections inherit new conditions along with unresolved unknowns and limits. Selecting a hypothetical branch does not mean reality has excluded the others; resources not yet arrived belong only in conditional branches. Giving another model the same material generates another narrative version; without new inputs, rules, or state differences, it cannot be registered as progression of the world.

When actual feedback arrives, first check source, event status, time, and duplicated underlying sources, then compare original and competing paths and simple baselines. Deviations may come from incorrect initial facts, mistaken mechanisms, an actor choosing differently, execution departing from plan, or changed external conditions. These five categories point to different revisions; not every deviation means “people are uncooperative” or “the model needs more complexity.”

Correction should change the states, parameters, mechanism scope, or paths actually used next round. Discovering that approval does not mean arrival, for example, requires revising resource availability, not merely logging “pay attention to authorization.” Saving feedback text while keeping choice rules and used states unchanged does not establish learning. Even an actual rule change still requires testing whether it improves future tasks.

This section connects dynamic projection to Part XII's choice and calibration. It automatically supplies neither value targets nor actual execution permission. Analysis may clearly identify a preferable branch or recommend delay under declared targets, while evidence, norms, feasibility, and authorization remain separately registered.

distinctions.leftText: Capability, resources, and other conditions make an action technically feasible.
distinctions.rightText: Willingness, choice, and actual occurrence each need grounds.

distinctions.leftText: The actor actually takes another available branch.
distinctions.rightText: The chosen plan is implemented differently; this is a different error.

distinctions.leftText: Actual changes need factual material; simulated changes need explicit conditions, each retaining its status.
distinctions.rightText: Rewording or redescribing with another model does not mean the state changed.

distinctions.leftText: Material is preserved.
distinctions.rightText: The revision actually enters later use; effectiveness still requires testing.

distinctions.leftText: Compares options under explicit targets.
distinctions.rightText: Actual decision and execution material cannot be replaced by a recommendation.

boundaries: Do not choose for an actor because the model requires a definite action.
Technical feasibility cannot override permissions; actual unauthorized behavior still enters factual records.
Behavioral explanation automatically neither excuses nor blames; deviations do not diagnose personality.
An implemented revision does not prove permanent immunity to failure; extrapolation remains bounded.

What evidence shows that correction entered the next round?
Does a changed rule establish general learning success?

caseNotes.title: 2017 S3 retrospective: explicit reported changes in tool rules
caseNotes.text: In its retrospective of the 2017 S3 incident, AWS stated that it modified the tool to remove capacity more slowly and added safeguards preventing subsystems from falling below required minimum capacity. This section uses only the point that “revision should enter actual operating rules.”
caseNotes.sourceLabel: AWS incident review
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Main text paragraph 3, beginning “We are making several changes…”
caseNotes.boundary: The operator's report of a modified tool, not an independent audit by this lesson or proof of zero future failures. It does not establish completion of every improvement plan.

argumentSteps: List available and excluded actions from current conditions, distinguishing sources in capability, constraints, and permissions.
Separate beliefs, willingness, and evidence of occurrence, retaining conditional branches for uncertain choices.
Specify mechanisms and concrete state differences triggered by each choice, then recalculate the next feasible set.
Inherit unknowns and limits; repeated generation is not state change.
After verifying actual feedback, distinguish facts, mechanisms, choices, execution, and external changes; revise items actually used next round and test them separately.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: choice changes the next menu
teachingExamples.text: A fictional robot has charge 5; task A consumes 3, B consumes 4, and permitted waiting consumes 0. Every task must leave nonnegative charge. Initially A, B, and waiting are all technically feasible. Actually doing A first leaves charge 2, making both A and B infeasible next; only waiting or a separately grounded replenishment action remains. Doing B first leaves 1, also preventing A. Treating “both tasks are feasible initially” as permission to perform both sequentially ignores shared resources.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Deterministic consumption, no automatic replenishment, indivisible tasks, and corresponding operating permission are stipulated; this is not actual robot control.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual charging or resource changes must be registered before updating; replenishment cannot be presumed afterward.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: five deviation types must not collapse into one cause
teachingExamples.text: A fictional queue predicts 5 awaiting repair next hour, but the actual record is 8. Factual error: the initial count may not have been 6. Mechanism error: processing rates may vary. Different choice: personnel selected another allowed task. Execution deviation: repair was chosen but tools did not arrive. External change: arrivals suddenly increased. These are competing diagnostic tasks, not grounds to select a cause without material. If tool nonarrival is verified, revise execution and resource states without first changing personality parameters.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Teaching candidates, not events established as having occurred; several may act together.
teachingExamples.boundary: The causal categories are neither mutually exclusive nor exhaustive; actual revision requires sources and discriminating material.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: storing feedback and changing rules can be distinguished explicitly
teachingExamples.text: A fictional old rule chooses action a consuming 3 even when stock x=2, violating nonnegativity. After receiving a verified failure record, merely adding “be careful next time” while retaining the rule selects a again. If the allowed set becomes {a:consumption≤x} and is actually used next round, a is excluded at x=2. Rule change is checkable, but its overall performance in other future contexts still requires testing.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Actions, states, and failure records are teaching assumptions; no actual actions were executed or systems trained.
teachingExamples.boundary: Proves only exclusion of a under the given constraint, not global optimality or general learning success.

counterexamples.text: A and B are both initially feasible, so A followed by B is also feasible.
counterexamples.effect: Shared charge changes later options: 5−3=2 is insufficient for B's 4.

counterexamples.text: The model received and saved a failure report, so it learned to avoid failure.
counterexamples.effect: If next-round states and rules remain unchanged, archiving is not the relevant correction; even changed rules need effect validation.

counterexamples.text: An actual outcome differs from prediction, so the actor must lack willingness.
counterexamples.effect: Facts, mechanisms, choices, execution, and external changes are competing explanations; responsibility cannot be assigned to one cause.

questionAnswers.question: With charge 5, after A consumes 3, can B consume 4 next?
questionAnswers.answer: No; 2 remains. Actual new replenishment evidence is required to change this judgment.

questionAnswers.question: Is a plan failing because tools did not arrive the same as personnel actively choosing another plan?
questionAnswers.answer: They differ: the former concerns execution or resource conditions, the latter a different choice path, requiring revisions at different points.

questionAnswers.question: What evidence shows that correction entered the next round?
questionAnswers.answer: Evidence that the states, allowed set, parameters, mechanism scope, or paths actually used next round were appropriately changed; storing text alone is insufficient.

questionAnswers.question: Does a changed rule establish general learning success?
questionAnswers.answer: No. First confirm actual application of the change, then examine gain using corresponding later outcomes and baselines.

intro-12-part.title: Part XII: Conditional Foresight and Bounded Choice
intro-12-part.lead: The previous part mapped possible paths; this part asks which future judgments will submit to tests at resolution, and under which values and protective conditions actions may be compared and recommended. These questions connect, but prediction confers no power to make others bear costs.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2588–2591; original anchor: part_12; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Separate the two into different contracts.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current original text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

Conditional foresight undertakes fallible future judgments within targets, deadlines, and evidence boundaries. Fallibility requires explicit support, non-support, or unresolved conditions at resolution; not every path may count as success, and deadlines cannot extend indefinitely. Sections 12.2–12.7 specify registration, local predictability, baselines, expression, evaluation, and failure semantics.

Bounded choice compares what can be done, how, when to stop, and when not to act within explicit value, protection, and authorization boundaries. Section 12.8 onward connects foresight to options, distributional consequences, reversibility, and procedures for actual adoption. Inaction also requires comparison and cannot be presumed costless.

Together they form a working loop: predictions provide conditional consequences for choices; actions and responses may change future material; outcomes then help correct judgments. Separate contracts prevent cross-level substitution: a likely consequence does not mean it ought to be produced, or that anyone may compel others to bear costs to avoid it.

A comparative recommendation may itself be a complete analytical deliverable. With explicit evidence, normative premises, costs, and limits, grounded preferences, rejection, or delay recommendations are possible; lack of execution authority need not reduce the output to questions alone. Actual adoption and execution separately require applicable protection, review, and valid authorization. “Only advice” also cannot conceal foreseeable high-impact uses.

This part promises neither universal predictability nor a model that unifies every value. It permits bounded answers, unknowns, incomparability, multiple options, and current nonaction, requiring explicit material that could change the judgment.

12.1.title: 12.1 Separating four types of output
12.1.lead: “I think this will happen, so that should be done” may quietly cross several gates. This section requires identifying whether we are explaining the past, unfolding conditions, predicting the future, or proposing a normative choice: each answers to different questions.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2592–2604; source anchor section-12-1; short quotation translated from Chinese: “explanation, projection, conditional foresight, and bounded choice must be labeled separately.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

Explanation answers what happened and why it may have happened, requiring objects, scales, evidence, mechanisms, and counterexamples. Its upper bound is a bounded mechanistic account. A coherent account of the past does not prove that the future will unfold the same way. An explanation may also retain several mechanisms; unknowns cannot be narrated as a unique cause.

Projection starts from a frozen snapshot, update rules, clocks, and branches to provide conditional paths and distinguishing signals. It can say, “if working-time and resource conditions remain, this branch may unfold.” Listing multiple paths does not give each a probability, and selecting the realized branch after the fact cannot establish predictive success for the entire projection.

Conditional foresight adds registration before the outcome, a simple baseline, target indicators, and feedback-record obligations. It asks which path is better supported as an expectation within a specified deadline. Its expression may be an evidence-based probability, ranking, or direction, or remain unknown when evidence is insufficient. Being open to calibration and failure is not the same as having demonstrated excellent calibration; the two cannot be merged into a single “reliable” label.

Bounded-choice analysis requires normative premises, evidence, genuinely comparable options, prices to be paid, and affected parties. Real-world adoption separately requires N explicit norms, PF protection floor, J jurisdictional authorization, O1–O4 processes, and C12 bridging qualifications. This invokes the source text's division of work; it is not a model inventing public authority. Even when these premises remain unmet, explicit analysis for deliberation is possible, but it must not claim to be ready for execution.

Connecting successive gates does not automatically upgrade status: explanation generates projection candidates; projection generates foresight candidates; foresight supplies consequences for comparison; norms and procedures support bounded choice; actual execution still requires stopping, rollback, and feedback records. Any layer with sufficient material can provide a clear bounded answer. Answering an explanatory question does not require completing every action procedure.

A single deliverable can contain all four output types, but their status must be labeled by sentence or paragraph, with sources and support ceilings stated separately. For example, discovering a processing-capacity decline after the fact is explanatory material; assuming continued low speed tomorrow is a scenario; registering the probability that tomorrow's 09:00 backlog exceeds a threshold is foresight; recommending maintenance first is normative analysis. They can share material without sharing all qualifications.

Accuracy is performance relative to a target and evaluation contract, not a moral, legal, or representative qualification. A weather model's smaller positional error does not authorize its publisher to determine how anyone evacuates. Real-world protective action has its own actors, permissions, and procedures. This non-entailment does not deny weather prediction's usefulness; it prevents usefulness from expanding into unlimited power.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: assigning four statements to their proper places
teachingExamples.text: Fictional records show 2 arrivals yesterday, 1 completion, and a starting value of 6. Under the assumption of no other flows, the endpoint is 7: a conditional explanation of records of past events. If the same conditions hold tomorrow, the endpoint will increase by another 1: a projection. Conditional foresight requires freezing, before the outcome, the target “whether it exceeds 7 tomorrow at 09:00,” the information cutoff, baseline, scoring, and signals, and giving an evidence-based judgment. If the stated norms are safeguarding deadlines and respecting personnel's minimum protections, and a recommendation follows comparison of maintenance, delay, transfer, and inaction, this is bounded-choice analysis. It still does not mean maintenance has been authorized or completed.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The entire example is a teaching structure and supplies no real-world probability; yesterday's records are also constructed stipulations.
teachingExamples.boundary: Correct arithmetic does not prove an actual mechanism. Without actual registration and outcomes, no foresight gain can be claimed.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: likelihood and preference can rank in opposite directions
teachingExamples.text: Fictional events A and B have probabilities 0.8 and 0.2, stipulated by the example. The value premise considers A seriously harmful and B harmless. A's greater likelihood does not mean it should be promoted; it may instead be something against which protection is warranted. If a response harms third parties, rights and distribution require separate comparison; 0.8 alone cannot determine coercive measures.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The probabilities and values are purely constructed; no real-world event risk was estimated.
teachingExamples.boundary: No specific action follows, nor is expected benefit treated as the only norm.

counterexamples.text: Mechanism A holds in explaining the past, so A must occur next time.
counterexamples.effect: Applicability conditions and future inputs may change; a separate foresight contract is required.

counterexamples.text: One of ten scenarios occurred, so all ten count as successful predictions.
counterexamples.effect: Exploring multiple branches does not equal ten successes; evaluation must follow the target and expression specified beforehand.

counterexamples.text: The model predicts accurately, so it is qualified to decide others' destinies.
counterexamples.effect: Performance does not generate norms, representativeness, jurisdiction, or authorization.

questionAnswers.question: Does registering foresight mean excellent predictive performance has been proved?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Registration only specifies a contract open to failure; performance still requires actual outcomes, baselines, and review.

12.2.title: 12.2 Registering conditional foresight
12.2.lead: First specify what counts as the prediction, when it ends, and how correctness is judged, then await the result. Otherwise, “the relationship will improve” can forever mean a slight improvement somewhere, and no model can genuinely fail.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2605–2620; source anchor section-12-2; short quotation translated from Chinese: “each foresight entry is frozen after the input cutoff and before the outcome appears.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source text; the downloaded original research excerpt preserves the historical draft.

Registration time, input cutoff, and target deadline play three different roles. First close the entry point for material usable in this run, then freeze the judgment, without having already seen the target outcome. The deadline may be a window; the input cutoff need not equal the target's start. Late evidence can inform a new version but cannot backfill the old run. If the target outcome is already known, the work is retrospective explanation or backtesting and cannot be renamed foresight registration.

The foresight ID and model version ensure traceability. The target, deadline, object, and circle scope determine who and what will be evaluated at the deadline; the baseline time specifies the starting point for measuring change. If the original target covers the whole team, narrowing it after the outcome to high-performing members changes the contract and cannot retain the original success status.

The target must be adjudicable, specifying at least the observable quantity, observer or source, threshold, and treatment of missingness. For example, if “relationship improvement” uses a particular scale, it evaluates only change under that measurement contract, not whether the whole relationship or everyone's life improved. First check whether the target definition actually corresponds to the task; do not replace the outcome the user cares about merely to make scoring easier.

A simple baseline prevents complex stories from declaring their own victory. The candidate mechanisms and path set specify mutual exclusivity, parallelism, or incomparability. Probabilities, intervals, grades, or directions must match the strength of their grounds. Without grounds for ranking, state unknown; mandatory registration does not justify invented numbers. Fill in decision thresholds only when used for decisions; otherwise they may be marked not applicable with a reason.

Early and contrary signals provide material for distinguishing paths. Suspension conditions specify when to stop using a model or variable; retirement conditions specify when to withdraw it. Calibration and outcome-feedback plans specify the actual labels, timing of appended records, and evaluation rules. A single prediction's score is not long-term calibration; the plan must also specify consistent conventions and uncertainty handling across accumulated tasks.

The original table's seven minimum questions address vague success, endless waiting, complexity as self-proof, retrospective branch selection, false precision, seeking support alone, and disappearing failures. A filled table is not a certificate of immunity to failure. Honest unknowns in its fields may also mean the entry is not yet qualified for release as foresight.

Subsection 12.2.1 bounds local capability claims by object, scale, resources, and expression; 12.2.2 requires independent evaluation of each recursive order. The parent section governs registration entry. One overall prediction ID cannot combine results from different orders, populations, or cutoffs as a single item.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: one complete foresight registration
teachingExamples.text: ID=Ptoy01, model v1; object=fictional repair queue Q, circles=no circle grouping used for this local task; baseline 08:00 B0=6; input cutoff 08:00, registration 08:01; target is recorded B≥8 at 10:00, horizon ending at that day's 10:00 count, labels verified at 10:05, with missing counts unresolved. Stipulated generating mechanism: arrivals 2/hour for two hours, processing rate c constant throughout, c=1 with probability 0.6 and c=3 with probability 0.4; endpoints are thus 8 or 4, target probability 0.6. Simple baseline p0=0.5 is an independently predefined teaching comparator. Paths are mutually exclusive; calibration plan accumulates tasks under the same mechanism and records Brier scores and event frequencies in equal-probability groups, without certifying calibration from one case. Decision threshold is inapplicable because only prediction is evaluated. Early signal=09:00 backlog 7 or 5 under the same definition; contrary signal=inconsistent values or changed generating conditions; suspension=changed input definition or object; retirement=long-term failure to outperform the baseline in later same-contract tests, after review. Write-back=append count source, label, loss, and deviations after 10:05; evidence reference=public stipulation Etoy in this example, not a real record.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Probabilities are a stipulated formal generating distribution, not estimates from actual repair data. All times, records, and calibration plans are constructed; repeated tasks were not actually conducted.
teachingExamples.boundary: Using the new 09:00 signal for updating requires a new frozen run; Ptoy01 remains evaluated on 08:00 information.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: operationalizing a vague target must preserve unresolved status
teachingExamples.text: “Team relationships improve” may be operationalized for a particular measurement task as “the same voluntary measurement on a fixed member set at two predefined times, using predefined scoring and missingness rules, with an indicator change reaching a threshold.” If members exit or refuse disclosure, do not default to improvement or deterioration; register missing/unresolved under prior rules and check target identity.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Design principles only, without a real psychological test or personal-data collection. No threshold or scale is supplied, so no values are assigned.
teachingExamples.boundary: One indicator does not represent every relationship, dignity, or life outcome; real adoption requires construct and protection checks.

12.2.1.title: 12.2.1 Boundaries of local predictability
12.2.1.lead: Do not ask only “can this model predict?” Ask which object, which state region, how far ahead, what error is allowed, and with what information and resources. Good performance on one task is not a license for every future.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2621–2626; source anchor section-12-2-1; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “not a ladder of precision every task must climb in sequence.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

Local predictability binds at least object, state region, scale and circles, window, tolerance, available information, computation and observation resources, version, baseline, abstention, and failure conditions. A model effective one hour ahead under normal load need not work under extreme load or a year ahead; expanding boundaries needs new evidence.

Predictability of the world as a whole exceeds this framework's directly testable scope. What is permitted here is bounded increment within particular tasks: local success does not establish complete foreknowledge, and long-term unknowns do not negate all short-window questions. Bounded capability may genuinely exist under its corresponding constraints.

Classification, ranking, intervals, and probability have different meanings. Classification identifies categories; ranking gives grounded order; intervals preserve admissible values or explicit coverage contracts; probability concerns event generation or empirical estimation. They are not a universal ladder from low to high. A task may need only a category, and probability need not suit the use better than a correct interval.

Choose expression after checking target, units, generating method, identification conditions, and calibration status. If even direction is unidentified, state unknown rather than “at least judge the trend.” A formal model may have known probabilities, explicitly supplied by assumptions; empirical probabilities need real data and applicable scope, not AI converting sparse prose into parameters.

Borrowing mathematical or physical theory also requires its original object, assumptions, limits or scaling laws, error, effective domain, object mapping, counterexamples, and exit conditions. Calling a community a fluid or information energy does not automatically apply the equations. Metaphors can prompt questions; quantitative laws require real mappings and validation.

Resource limits are part of capability. Backtesting with material available only later does not establish real-time predictability then; computation exceeding the decision window may prevent delivering the claimed lead time. Abstention preserves the ability to withhold judgments outside the applicable domain. Report abstention scope in evaluation rather than showing only easy cases the model answers.

12.2.2.title: 12.2.2 Evaluation of recursive foresight by order
12.2.2.lead: A correct first order and incorrect third order cannot be blended into an attractive total and called “effective recursion.” Each order has different questions and informational dependencies, requiring separate freezing and comparison with reasonable shallower methods.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 2627–2632; source anchor section-12-2-2; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “cannot be combined into one overall hit rate.” See the corresponding section on this page for the current source; the downloadable original research extract preserves the historical draft.

Register object, target, horizon, input cutoff, expression, and evaluation rules separately for first, second, and third orders. If they predict different targets, adding hits into an opaque total rate is invalid. Any combined metric needs its own prior definition and weights while retaining order-specific performance; it cannot replace original contracts.

Each order needs three comparators: state continuation without further recursion; direct judgment of the same distant target; and a shallower order plus simple continuation. These distinguish genuine need for reentry structure from mere passage of time. Comparing second-order errors on a difficult distant target directly with an easy first-order short-term target cannot establish recursion as harmful or beneficial.

Fair comparison matches target, horizon, available information, and evaluation rules, with a reasonable account of computation and tuning opportunities. Extra evidence, computation, and richer structure can each generate gain and should be distinguished as far as possible. A simple baseline need not be artificially made as large as the complex system, nor deliberately denied available information.

Without new external material, every child run's evidence lineage still returns to the same frozen starting point. Postprocessing may reveal previously underived logical consequences, sensitivities, or hidden conditions—a real inferential increment—but does not add a real sample or independent evidence source.

When actual intermediate outcomes arrive, create a new-cutoff run. Compare “projecting all the way from the original start” with “updating using later actual conditions,” but the latter uses more material. Gains cannot all be credited to recursion, nor fed backward into old paths to make them perpetually correct.

If three orders add only stories without stable out-of-sample increment, retain exploratory scenarios without foresight-capability eligibility. One better or worse performance establishes no universal rule. Judge stability within registered use and independent evaluation scope, narrowing windows or retiring when necessary.

distinctions.leftText: Score each order's own task against reasonable comparators separately.
distinctions.rightText: May conceal differences in task difficulty, horizon, and failure.

distinctions.leftText: Reveals consequences implied by original inputs.
distinctions.rightText: New real material appears, with different status.

distinctions.leftText: Reestimated using a new cutoff.

boundaries: Do not count regenerated child texts as independent samples.
Out-of-sample evaluation also needs protection against target, time, and source leakage.
Exploratory scenarios may be useful even without supported foresight gain.

Distinguish differences in information, computation, and structure, preserving order-specific scores.
Child runs without new external material do not increase real-evidence counts.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: recursion does not beat baselines on the same target
teachingExamples.text: A fictional third-order target is the hour-3 queue value, actual label 10. Predictions are recursive 14, direct distant-target 11, current-state continuation 12, and shallower-plus-continuation 10. Under predefined absolute error, scores are 4,1,2,0. This instance does not support recursive superiority; a correct first-order answer to a different short-term task cannot offset the third-order error.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All four predictions, the label, and the rule are teaching constructions, not a real experiment; all comparisons concern the same hour-3 target.
teachingExamples.boundary: One sample cannot establish that every recursive method is worse; it gives only this instance's bounded comparison.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: new actual conditions cannot leak backward into old orders
teachingExamples.text: Suppose three-order predictions are frozen at 08:00 and a new count arrives at 09:00. A new run from that count may improve the 10:00 prediction, and the updated result can be reported while retaining the 08:00 forecast. Writing the 09:00 value into the old first order, recomputing old second and third orders, and claiming “predicted at 08:00” is information leakage.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Times and data flow are constructed; no real forecasting system was run.
teachingExamples.boundary: An update's value does not make the old run valueless; evaluate the two information sets separately.

counterexamples.text: Generating 100 child runs from one starting point equals 100 independent observations.
counterexamples.effect: The source lineage is shared; more computation adds no real samples.

counterexamples.text: The first order is accurate and the third inaccurate; averaging proves overall three-order effectiveness.
counterexamples.effect: Tasks and horizons differ by order; retain separate scores and same-target comparisons.

questionAnswers.question: Third order 14, direct 11, continuation 12, shallow-plus-continuation 10, label 10: what are their errors?
questionAnswers.answer: 4,1,2,0. Recursion does not dominate here, without a universal long-term judgment.

questionAnswers.question: Can improvement from new intermediate actual conditions be attributed entirely to recursion?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It adds information; use a new version and distinguish informational from structural contributions.

questionAnswers.question: Is postprocessing without new observations entirely valueless?
questionAnswers.answer: It may add reasoning, sensitivity analysis, and conditional understanding, but real-world evidence does not grow by itself.

12.3.title: 12.3 Simple baselines and incremental capability
12.3.lead: A complex model must answer a plain question: with the same information, target, and cutoff, what would a simpler method do? Richer stories, more diagrams, or more variables cannot replace that comparison.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 2633—2640; source anchor section-12-3; short quotation: ‘the simple model should be preferred’ (translated from Chinese). The current source appears in the corresponding subsection on this page; the downloadable original research excerpt preserves the historical manuscript.

Incremental capability is a difference relative to a task-appropriate baseline, not an attractive error figure reported by the model alone. A baseline may extend a trend, retain the most recent state, use historical frequencies, use only agent state or the main circle's state, or adopt an established domain method. Selection should fit the data and task, without deliberately choosing an obviously unsuitable weak opponent.

Fair comparison first requires the same information, cutoff, target, horizon, and evaluation rules. If the complex model receives later events while the simple model uses only earlier materials, the difference cannot be attributed to multi-circle structure. If the complex model is scored only on easy samples while the baseline is scored on the whole set, that is not the same comparison either.

Materials, reasoning budgets, and tuning opportunities should be as proportionate as possible, without forcing a simple baseline to become a complex model. Explain separately the contributions of added information, computation, and structural assumptions. Restricted controls or ablations may help, but one overall score cannot complete causal attribution. State honestly when contributions cannot be isolated.

Predictive systems usually require independent testing or out-of-sample review, with protection against temporal, object, or source leakage. In time series, future materials cannot enter past prediction inputs, and related records should not be treated as fully independent samples. Without available tests, retain capability as unestablished; training fit or retrospective explanation cannot count as foresight performance.

Separate explanatory gain from predictive gain. A model may clarify mechanisms, cost-bearing positions, or constraints without predicting better than the baseline; if that explanatory gain has corresponding materials, retain it while stating that foresight gain is unsupported. Whether explanation actually improves also needs criteria; longer text cannot certify itself.

Complexity carries costs of missingness, mismeasurement, privacy, overfitting, and maintenance. Collecting more people's information adds risks, and model versions need continuing maintenance. Limit use if effectiveness holds only in a small state domain; downgrade or retire when gains decline; if performance is equal and no other sufficient reason exists, prefer the simpler model rather than paying needless costs for a larger terminology.

Equal performance is a bounded conclusion about the current comparison and need not establish population-level statistical equivalence. One win for a simple method does not mean complex methods are always worse; one win for a complex method does not establish universal superiority either. The final report should state samples, error uncertainty, applicability domain, tuning opportunities, and costs, not merely name a winner.

distinctions.leftText: Evidence-backed improvement in understanding mechanisms or constraints.
distinctions.rightText: Better performance on unseen outcomes under the same contract.

distinctions.leftText: Comparable budgets and tuning opportunities, with differences transparent.
distinctions.rightText: A simple method need not expand to the same scale.

distinctions.leftText: Richer or newer inputs.
distinctions.rightText: A difference from representations and mechanisms under corresponding information conditions.

distinctions.leftText: Explains records already used for tuning.
distinctions.rightText: Evaluation on materials not used for model selection, still requiring leakage prevention.

distinctions.leftText: Improvement in a loss relative to the comparator.
distinctions.rightText: Different quantities; percentage signs do not make them interchangeable.

boundaries: Without independent testing, capability cannot be treated as established and test results must not be fabricated.
A baseline must not deliberately be denied available materials, and the complex model should not receive future labels.
Cross-domain extrapolation requires review; an out-of-sample advantage in one domain is not victory everywhere.
Equal complexity is not the sole fairness criterion; actual maintenance and protection costs also matter.

caseLinks.title: The 2024 North Atlantic verification: skill requires a comparator

caseNotes.title: The 2024 North Atlantic verification: skill requires a comparator
caseNotes.text: The Met Office reports North Atlantic T+24-hour Track skill of 68%; its official error definitions explain that this compares model position forecasts with the CLIPER climatology–persistence baseline, with positive values indicating lower model error. The added point here is that 68% is neither event probability nor case-by-case hit rate.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Met Office, 2024 verification report and error definitions
caseNotes.sourceLocator: §3.3 table, Track skill(%) row, T+24 column; accompanying definitions, Track skill in the terminology list and the same item under Sign conventions
caseNotes.boundary: This restates only the report's relative metric and definition, without reverse-calculating exact baseline errors from rounded summaries or inferring performance for every storm or universal long-term superiority. The definition source also appears as metdefinitions in sources.

argumentSteps: Choose a task-appropriate simple or domain baseline and freeze the comparison contract first.
Give methods the same target, information cutoff, horizon, samples, and scoring.
Reasonably balance computation and tuning, separating information, computational, and structural contributions.
Test with independent or out-of-sample materials; without them, capability remains unestablished.
Limit the applicability domain by gains and costs, downgrade when gains disappear, and prefer simplicity under equal performance.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: comparing average errors for the same target
teachingExamples.text: Fictional independent test labels are y=(10,12,8), complex-model predictions (9,13,9), and simple-model predictions (10,10,10). Under the predetermined mean absolute error, the complex model has (1+1+1)/3=1 and the simple model (0+2+2)/3=4/3. On this test set the complex method's average error is lower by 1/3; if collection costs also exist, the net choice still requires normative comparison. These three samples alone cannot establish a stable advantage across the entire domain.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All data and their independent status are teaching stipulations; no actual test was performed.
teachingExamples.boundary: Error improvement holds only for this sample and metric, not in place of confidence intervals or tests of long-term gain.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a skill percentage is not a hit rate
teachingExamples.text: In a teaching task, the baseline's average loss is 10 and the model's 8. Define relative skill S=1−L模型/L基线 (S = 1 − model loss/baseline loss), giving S=1−8/10=0.2, or 20%. This means loss is 20% lower than the baseline in this example, not that the event has probability 20% or that 80% or 20% of predictions hit individually.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Loss units are consistent, the baseline is nonzero, and the skill definition is this example's publicly stated rule.
teachingExamples.boundary: Different domains may use different skill scores; this formula cannot be forced onto every report.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: later information creates an unfair win
teachingExamples.text: Fictional A predicts 10:00 inventory at 08:00 using only 08:00 materials; B predicts the same target at 09:30 after seeing most incoming stock and has lower error. One may say B made a later prediction with more information, not that B's structural model is stronger under the same cutoff. Compare separately using common 08:00 or common 09:30 materials.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Times, information, and performance are a teaching scenario, with no actual operational data.
teachingExamples.boundary: Later updating may be useful, but remaining lead time, the decision window, and information costs require separate evaluation.

counterexamples.text: The complex model's diagram is more complete, so it proves improved foresight even with identical error.
counterexamples.effect: Structural richness is not predictive gain; results must be compared under the same contract.

counterexamples.text: The baseline uses old materials and the complex method new materials, but the entire difference comes from structure.
counterexamples.effect: Information contributions are mixed in, preventing isolated attribution.

counterexamples.text: Skill relative to the baseline is 20%, so 20% of events will occur.
counterexamples.effect: Relative loss is not event probability.

questionAnswers.question: What are the two methods' MAEs in the example, and how strong a conclusion follows?
questionAnswers.answer: 1 and 4/3; the complex method is lower by 1/3 on this test set. Three constructed samples do not establish a stable advantage.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: How can added information be distinguished from added structure?
questionAnswers.answer: Set controls under the same information conditions and disclose budget and tuning differences; if isolation is impossible, do not attribute everything to one contribution.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What if the complex method improves only explanation?
questionAnswers.answer: Retain grounded explanatory gain, state that foresight gain is unsupported, and decide continued use according to purpose and cost.

Probabilities or probability intervals must correspond to decidable events and specify the generative model, priors where applicable, data, boundaries, and calibration status. With insufficient probability grounds, evidence-backed grades or path comparisons may be given, but ranking itself may also be unknown; ‘no probability’ cannot automatically become ‘at least a direction can be given’. Sample size is only one condition and does not determine output type alone.

The source table's four evidence statuses have different ceilings: probability grounds permit probabilities; grade-only grounds require retaining incomparable items and contrary signals; direction is given only with identification grounds, otherwise unknown plus the minimum discriminating observation; unstable targets or objects prohibit issuing foresight until the contract is redefined. They are not a mandatory sequential downgrade ladder.

Time windows follow mechanism clocks; short-term emotional responses, organizational processes, and institutional changes cannot share one default horizon. Forcing a slow mechanism into a short window may wrongly judge ineffectiveness before it could take effect; extending short-term signals indefinitely mistakes transients for trends. Multiclock tasks may register separate horizons for intermediate and final outcomes while retaining their respective evaluations.

Real-world probability concerns event occurrence under corresponding conditions and needs estimation or calibration grounds; subjective belief records an agent's judgment under particular information; decision weights come from a descriptive model or value premises; path rankings hold only under their comparison relation; computational priorities state what limited resources should examine first. Even the same 0.8 across all five cannot make them prove one another.

High consequences, a short window, or easy discrimination may give a path with unknown probability high checking priority. Disclose priority reasons and budgets rather than invent a percentage to appear rational. Most worth checking does not mean most likely, and most desired does not mean most likely either; recommendation rankings additionally require norms and distributional considerations and do not follow directly from occurrence probabilities.

Model sampling frequencies are computational results under given parameters, sampling methods, and rules. They may estimate model-conditional probabilities, but real-world probabilities additionally require mappings, parameter support, and calibration. More samples cannot repair a wrong model or unobserved variables. If sampling deliberately oversamples a risk branch, its frequency may not even equal probability under the model's original distribution; preserve weights and methods.

A small sample can produce a posterior under explicit priors and likelihoods, but that posterior remains assumption-dependent; the small sample itself cannot certify real-world parameters. Large samples may also share incorrect definitions or selection bias; precise estimation of the wrong quantity is not the probability of the event being asked about.

Publish probability judgments, empirical calibration, and normative priorities separately. High personal confidence is not calibrated long-run frequency; good calibration on comparable tasks also does not automatically satisfy protections for every subgroup or action authorization. Strength of expression rests on evidence and use, not readers' desired certainty or model fluency.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: one datum can yield a conditional posterior
teachingExamples.text: Let unknown success rate θ∈[0,1] have an artificially stipulated uniform prior density 1, with conditionally independent identically distributed trials and one observed success, giving likelihood θ. The normalization constant ∫ from 0 to 1 θdθ=1/2, so posterior density is 2θ and next-trial posterior predictive mean is ∫ from 0 to 1 θ·2θdθ=2/3. This calculation depends on prior, observation, and generative assumptions, not ‘one observation reveals actual success rate 2/3’.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Entirely a mathematical construction, with one success only inside the model; no actual trial or justification of a real-world prior.
teachingExamples.boundary: Different priors, selective observation, or nonidentical distributions change the answer; neither small sample size nor the formula itself establishes real calibration.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: severity sets checking priority without assigning probability
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional system, path A may cause irreversible harm with a 10-minute response window, while B causes only reversible delay and can wait a day. Both probabilities are unknown, but explicit protective goals and current checking resources can prioritize A. Report ‘A checked first because of consequences and window; probability unknown’, not an invented ‘A has 80%’ to justify ranking.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Risk types, windows, and resources are constructed; no actual emergency is described and no action authorized.
teachingExamples.boundary: Checking itself still needs authority and safety boundaries; severe consequences are not an unconditional excuse to act.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: oversampling frequency is not the original model probability
teachingExamples.text: A fictional model specifies P(A)=0.1 and P(non-A)=0.9. To examine A’s consequences, researchers deliberately generate 50 A and 50 non-A scenarios. The sample’s 50% A reflects a design quota, not a model probability changed to 0.5, much less a real probability. Estimating an expectation under the original model requires combining branch-conditional results with original weights 0.1 and 0.9.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Probabilities and quotas are stipulated, with no actual sampling; this shows only the distinction between design and target distributions.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual importance sampling also needs corresponding support and weight conditions; the example does not replace a full estimation procedure.

counterexamples.text: An outcome appears in 80 of 100 generations, so its actual probability is 80%.
counterexamples.effect: The generation distribution, parameter grounds, and real-world mapping must be known; generation frequency alone is insufficient.

counterexamples.text: There is only one sample, so no posterior is possible under any explicit probability model.
counterexamples.effect: The construction gives 2/3, strictly dependent on prior and model; small sample size alone does not determine computability.

counterexamples.text: The path most worth checking must be the most likely.
counterexamples.effect: Consequences, windows, and discriminatory value may change priorities and cannot be conflated with probability.
