15.4.title: 15.4 Minimum Output for Application Records
15.4.lead: An application record should let readers trace each judgment to its object, material, protection, and ceiling. A complete execution chain is added when entering real-world action; self-referential summaries cannot impersonate external responsible persons.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 3450–3457; original site location /theory/part-15#section-15-4. For the current full text, see the theory-v2 source; historical research manuscripts and excerpts remain available for checking in their original downloadable versions.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: “Tasks that stop at explanation or diagnosis end at their corresponding evidentiary boundaries.” This section specifies a minimum traceable output without pushing every inquiry toward real-world intervention. Minimum does not mean the shorter the better; it means no necessary item determining “what may be said and what may be done” can be omitted. Completeness of an explanatory text and completeness of qualifications to execute are different responsibilities. [T-main]

The first group fixes identity and evidence: module ID; object, scale, K, and window; individually supported propositions, external evidence, coverage status, consequences of missing material, and material and tool inputs. Merely saying “the material is sufficient” is inadequate: identify which version supports which proposition and which inference each gap narrows. A domain name or an entire bibliography does not replace proposition-by-proposition support. [T-main; T-domain]

The second group fixes risks and protection: domain risks; affected, low-power, weak-signal, and unable-to-exit positions; the complete protection floor; diagnostic conclusions and action ceiling; and how evidence gaps lower confidence and level. Low-power positions cannot be treated as null values because they lack formal representatives or cannot express themselves fully. Even when weak signals have not become facts establishing responsibility, they still require protection pending verification. [T-main; T-protection]

The third group adds responsibilities according to use: where choice is needed, leave a normative-choice record or comparison with inaction; where intervention is needed, leave candidate T types; explain why any item is inapplicable. A text-only explanation may state that no option adoption is involved; an execution action must not be invented just to fill a form. Conversely, actually changing rights or resources cannot mark choice and authorization “not applicable.” Use is determined by actual consequences, not self-declared titles. [T-main; T-chain; T-strong]

Once real-world action begins, append the complete 17-field choice-record wrapper, structured selected_action, C12, explicit N, O1–O4, unique J atomic authorization, and provisions for stopping, anonymous/proxy appeals, anti-retaliation monitoring, rollback, and an execution-state log. This paragraph requires a complete record consistent with the corresponding engineering contract; this explanation neither reworks its semicolon-separated list into an invented “17 fields” nor certifies that particular software implements it. Actual implementations must check fields and semantics against their frozen versions, not rely solely on field counts. [T-main; T-permission; T-types]

In all records, including diagnosis-only records, references to evidence, positions, channels, and responsible persons must resolve to the runtime registry. Resolution requires more than a string's existence: it must reach the specific referenced object, source, and responsibility position. When context is omitted, GHOST, none, self, or self:* summaries cannot replace external records; those responsible for appeals, independent review, and rollback cannot be the decision-making actor. Changing aliases while retaining the same actual controller does not achieve the required separation. [T-main]

Resolvable references do not establish that their contents are true, that responsible persons are effectively independent, that channels are reachable, or that a decision is legally valid; they merely make further checks possible. Diagnosis also requires resolution: not executing yet does not exempt material and affected positions from traceability responsibilities. Conversely, complete diagnostic references do not confer execution authority. [T-main; T-domain; T-permission]

Module outputs missing these necessary fields can only be reading prompts and cannot enter real-world action. Proposed action requires a bounded action chain that counterexamples, safety positions, and real consequences can change, rather than repackaging the original conclusion to make it harder to refute. Stopping, correcting records, downstream write-back, and actual remedy require separate checks; a file displaying completed does not independently establish recovery for harmed positions. [T-main; T-state]

This section specifies records; this discussion does not treat an institution's “having a ledger” as a success case. The teaching examples below concretely test boundaries involving references, use, and state. They generate no actual permission, real personnel list, or executable action record, and do not disguise this research package as the registry of a real-world task. [T-main]
argumentSteps: First fix whether this output ends at explanation, diagnosis, choice, or execution.
Leave an object, source, scope, and gaps for each conclusion.
Register protected positions and ceilings; inapplicability requires proportionate reasons.
Resolve all references to external runtime records; separate key review roles from the decision-making actor.
Append a complete choice-and-execution contract only when entering action; missing necessary items prohibit action.
Let counterexamples and consequences genuinely change states; check correction effects beyond traceability.

distinctions.leftText: Necessary responsibilities cannot be omitted; configure them by task.

15.5.title: 15.5 Dynamic entry into application modules
15.5.lead: Enable dynamic analysis according to the question, first specifying agents, circles, conditions, clocks, and event status. Simulations remain simulations; complex procedures add no actual authority.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 3458—3467; original-site location /theory/part-15#section-15-5. The current complete text is in the theory-v2 source; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available in their original versions for download and checking.

Short quotation: ‘the existence of a complex process cannot become pressure for actual action upon an object’ (translated from Chinese). The nine modules add dynamic entry records only when dynamic analysis is needed. Dynamics does not upgrade every matter into multi-circle prediction; when a question involves change, cross-level transmission, or delay, it makes update grounds explicit. Explanation alone does not force foresight, and sufficient simple baselines permit simple records. [T-main]

Required additions are the main agent, main circle, adjacent circles, relationship types, M/Ψ conditions, five clocks, events, a simple baseline, and result write-back. M denotes material conditions and Ψ experience–meaning conditions; both need observational or interpretive grounds. Subjective experience cannot be read directly from external resource quantities, nor experiential narratives automatically converted into a complete account of external facts. [T-main；T-MP]

The five clocks are immediate, interactional, organizational, institutional, and long-term. Immediate attention may change with signals; interactional trust takes rounds; organizational budgets follow decision/execution cycles; institutional change concerns rules and actual write-back; long-term capability depends on accumulated maintenance. Time units are typical examples, not fixed minutes or years for a variable. An event directly updates only variables reached through channels with conditions satisfied; unreached does not mean eternally unchanged in reality. [T-clock]

Four domain emphases must not be flattened together: relationships/households examine role activation, inability to exit, and slow/intermediate/fast states; organizations/platforms examine metrics, bridging, transmission, and institutional write-back; public governance/public discourse/very large scale examine representation, low-visibility positions, cross-level aggregation losses, and calibration drift; spatial/emergency tasks examine material channels, capacity thresholds and delays, and emergency authorization. Each emphasis is an entry to questions, not a mechanism established before evidence. [T-main]

Events must retain factual status. Model-generated scenarios are hypothetical or simulated and cannot be written back as observed; an actual historical starting point also does not turn synthetic subsequent trajectories into occurred facts. Result write-back should distinguish observation, prediction, and error; predictions cannot be entered into training data/files and then counted as external validation. [T-main；T-event]

‘The situation is urgent’ cannot bypass event factual status, and ‘only a recommendation’ does not exempt privacy and affected-person protection. Emergency actions use only external emergency rules for minimal protection, restoring review, appeals, and rollback promptly; the framework creates no emergency powers. Existing professional life-saving duties must not be delayed by structural analysis, while the model cannot use them to take over the scene. [T-main；T-emergency]

When foresight is unregistered or uncalibrated, output stops at path indications. Calibration is not making one story sound plausible, but a checkable comparison of corresponding predictions and later outcomes under conditions and windows. A simple baseline shows whether complexity is worth using; if a simple approach sufficiently answers the current question, unverifiable parameters need not be added for procedural completeness. [T-main；T-forecast]

Incomplete authorization stops actual execution while permitting action needs, analytical recommendations that create no execution authority, and draft institutional plans to remain. Analysis may have an explicit preferred option, but cannot package it as an approved command or pressure agents with ‘the whole process ran, so not executing would waste it’. Actions supported by independently valid professional duties in prior materials follow their own scope, not authority borrowed from model recommendations. [T-main；T-permission]

Mansoury and colleagues' 2020 paper explicitly defines ‘time’ as successive offline interaction iterations rather than calendar time and generates subsequent responses in simulation. This concrete design distinguishes model clocks from real events: actual initial data and synthetic continuation may coexist, but round 20 cannot be called an actual user's day 20. This lesson neither reproduces the computations nor uses the paper to establish this framework's predictive capability. [P-MANS]
argumentSteps: First ask whether dynamic or multi-circle foresight is actually needed.
If needed, fix agent/circle identities, relationships, M/Ψ, five clocks, and event grounds.
Retain a simple baseline and specify the most important domain risks and protections.
Separate observations, hypotheses, and simulations; result write-back must not turn them into facts.
Unregistered/uncalibrated foresight is reduced to path indications; incomplete authority stops execution.
Retain grounded analysis and conditional recommendations without pressuring action through procedural complexity.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two clocks cannot be forced into synchrony
teachingExamples.text: An artificial organization receives a service alert today, so immediate risk records may update; a budget adjustment still requires next week's meeting and has not been implemented. Today's alert therefore cannot also be recorded as ‘budget reallocated’. If backend operations provide necessary support in advance under an established independent procedure, record its grounds and actions separately rather than inferring a budget resolution from a risk record.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Dates, procedures, and organization are fictional, illustrating asynchronous responsibilities only.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual organizations are not required to wait for meetings; emergency duties and valid independent authority require separate checks.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an observed value and two continuations
teachingExamples.text: The artificial starting observation is inventory 10; model A predicts 8 next round and model B predicts 6. Only starting value 10 is observed within the stipulation; both continuations are simulated. Only after later actual verification gives 7 may a new observation be added and errors compared as 1 and 1. One cannot first enter 8 into a file and then use that file to ‘confirm’ model A.
teachingExamples.assumptions: 10, 8, 6, and 7 are teaching values; absolute errors |8−7|=1 and |6−7|=1.
teachingExamples.boundary: Identical one-round errors establish neither equal overall calibration nor authority over inventory.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: static explanation suffices
teachingExamples.text: A fictional task asks only what ‘expires on the due date’ means in a public rule. If the source and period information suffice, no ten-year forecast of adjacent circles is needed. Only a later question about intertemporal effects of exit arrangements on different dependents calls for clocks, events, baselines, and protections under the new task; the earlier simple task was not incomplete.

intro-16-part.title: Part Sixteen: Governance
intro-16-part.lead: A framework that explains others may itself expand, become rigid, or be exploited. Governance means more than another sentence welcoming criticism: criticism must have a chance to change assertions, releases, uses, and the framework itself.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 3468—3479; source anchor part_16; short quotation: ‘the framework cannot prove its own safety in its own language’ (translated from Chinese). This lesson's source excerpt is separately attached verbatim as source-slice.md, keeping explanation and source distinct.

The introduction establishes governance as an actual interface: concepts may be downgraded, assertions suspended, releases blocked, versions rolled back within permitted boundaries, and the framework replaced. If these changes remain on paper without reaching authoritative text or actual uses, governance has not been shown to operate. Later terminal-state rules prohibit rollback; ‘rollback possible’ cannot restore old qualifications already revoked.

The framework itself may face document expansion, conceptual rigidity, power capture, and dependence on linguistic identity. These are risk types requiring checking, neither automatically present because the framework is adopted nor automatically absent because maintainers mean well. Greater prior investment may increase reluctance to exit, reminding governance to permit external replacement rather than rewarding only added concepts.

This part governs four objects: current texts and templates, conceptual relationships, actual practices, and the community of maintainers, critics, and affected people. Textual consistency answers one documentary question, not whether users avoid misuse; an active community also does not certify empirical assertions. Section 16.1 separates these objects and minimum self-diagnostic records, while later governance modules handle authority, objections, release, and replacement.

Internal consistency, stress tests, validator passes, and complete reports can establish bounded completion of corresponding process products. For example, parsable JSON establishes format validity, not that recorded harms occurred or were repaired; a simulation pass establishes model results under stipulated conditions, not actual safety, consent, or authorization. Explicitly separating these endpoints neither disparages formal checks nor permits them to testify beyond their scope for facts.

Tools should turn boundaries into checkable constraints: internal statuses do not certify reality, governance records do not mint external authority, terminal states preserve history, and formal adoption requires proportionate external review or approval. Aliases, self-declared independence, and circular references cannot supply reviewers' external independence. Writing these requirements establishes only their existence, not implementation or execution in particular software.

This part's state and authority rules constrain the framework's own text, modules, formal assertions, governance changes, and related high-impact uses. An external organization not using these forms does not mean it legally does not exist or that its decisions are necessarily invalid. External legal validity, normative justification, actual protection, and framework endorsement require separate judgments; the framework cannot turn its format into universal jurisdiction.

Governance therefore retains the capacity both to affirm and to reject: correction of a particular documentation error may be recognized as completion of that narrow task; actual protection remains unknown until verified; serious misuse may lead to suspension of the relevant use; and a better alternative may take over. Recognition that a typo has been corrected need not wait for proof of every real-world consequence, but fixing a typo must not be used to declare an institution safe.

distinctions.leftText: The text contains governance requirements.
distinctions.rightText: Requires evidence of implementation, operation, and state changes.

distinctions.leftText: The structural conditions it actually checks are satisfied.
distinctions.rightText: Requires additional evidence about objects and uses, external evidence, and protection.

distinctions.leftText: Its usage rules withhold eligibility for adoption or publication.
distinctions.rightText: Cannot be inferred directly from whether it adopts the framework’s format.

distinctions.leftText: Governance permits termination of its own errors and uses.
distinctions.rightText: Terminal-state and authorization boundaries still apply.

boundaries: Governance provisions are not themselves evidence of implementation; internal approval cannot independently prove consent, safety, or repair.
The external independence of review must be checked against actual relationships and authority, not merely by changing the reviewer’s name.
Framework governance cannot replace legal procedures or erase the distinction between facts and norms.
Rollback does not undo history; a terminal state must not be used to revive old authorization through rollback.
questions: Why must governance allow the framework to be replaced?
Can two structurally identical repair records establish the same reality?
Why not simply say all repair is complete once the guide is corrected?

argumentSteps: First distinguish the governance object and intended judgment endpoint, avoiding a blanket certification of the entire framework’s health.
Specify downgrading, suspension, blocking, rollback, and replacement as interfaces capable of changing the relevant states.
Distinguish process products, real effects, and external authorization, requiring proportionate evidence for each.
Check independence and the accessibility of citations; aliases and circular self-validation do not count as independent external review.
Limit the framework’s own scope, and examine external institutional validity and actual protection separately.

teachingExamples.title: Formal construction: a correct record does not mean its contents are true
teachingExamples.text: A fictional record contains status="repaired" and a valid timestamp format, so schema validation can pass. Construct world A, where the equipment has actually been repaired, and world B, where it has not but someone has entered the same fields. The two records have the same structure but different real states; therefore structural validation does not entail that repair holds. What is needed is external evidence of equipment state or effects proportionate to the task’s endpoint.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Both worlds and the fields are formal constructions; there is no real equipment or audit record.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not deny that a schema can detect missing fields or type errors; it only limits what it can prove.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: local completion and unresolved matters can coexist
teachingExamples.text: A fictional maintainer corrects a unit error in a guide and verifies that the authoritative document has been updated; textual correction can be called complete. If the software still reads the old configuration, operational migration is incomplete. If the error affected service, whether remedies have reached those affected requires a separate check. These three states may respectively be complete, incomplete, and unknown; they need not be merged into a single overall “repaired.”
teachingExamples.assumptions: The documentation, software, and service are teaching assumptions; no real modification occurred.
teachingExamples.boundary: The actual extent of propagation and responsibility for remedies must follow real dependencies; this example does not imply that every system is faulty.

counterexamples.text: All self-diagnostic reports are complete, so the framework is safe.
counterexamples.effect: Report completion and real-world safety are different endpoints.

counterexamples.text: An external organization did not fill in this framework’s forms, so its procedures do not exist.
counterexamples.effect: Internal adoption rules do not replace judgments about external institutional facts and validity.

counterexamples.text: Because rollback is available, any retired module can directly regain its old authorization.
counterexamples.effect: Terminal states and authority must follow their respective rules; rollback cannot erase the history of revocation.

questionAnswers.question: Why must governance allow the framework to be replaced?
questionAnswers.answer: To prevent a maintainer identity, investment in concepts, or commercial returns from becoming reasons to preserve erroneous uses.

questionAnswers.question: Can two structurally identical repair records establish the same reality?
questionAnswers.answer: No. One actual device may work while the other is broken; structural evidence cannot determine facts about the world.

questionAnswers.question: Why not simply say all repair is complete once the guide is corrected?
questionAnswers.answer: Documentation, operational consumption, and real-world remedies have different endpoints, each requiring verification.

16.1.title: 16.1 GOV-01 Framework Self-Diagnosis and Separation of Objects
16.1.lead: Self-diagnosis first asks, “Which object has which problem?” In the same activity, the guide, concepts, operators, and group holding interpretive authority may have different states; a single health score cannot replace all of them.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3480–3493; source anchor section-16-1; short quotation translated from Chinese: “First state what is being examined.” The source excerpt for this topic is separately reproduced verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and source text are kept separate.

Document objects include text, directories, definitions, templates, and rules; checks cover contradictions, version references, and expression. Evidence may consist of specific passages and change diffs. Finding a correct reference in a document does not establish the empirical fact it cites; repairing a conflict in definitions does not automatically repair real misuse.

Concept objects require examining whether empirical problem families, universal variables, human adapters, normative choices, and action procedures overstep their boundaries. Typical risks include treating classification labels as entities, descriptive results as normative commands, or intentional human collective states as applicable to all systems. Counterexamples must pinpoint the domain of application and inferential leap; merely counting occurrences of terms is insufficient.

Practice objects concern how users actually diagnose, manage, teach, communicate publicly, and invoke AI. A guide saying “appeals are available” differs from evidence about whether accepting an appeal can change its outcome; a course saying not to label people differs from whether labels are used to sanction people in practice. Actual records and testimony from affected positions are needed, rather than interviews solely about maintainers’ ideals.

Community objects concern who holds the power to name, merge, interpret, and publish, and who bears the consequences of misuse. Membership, activity, and apparent agreement cannot certify governance eligibility. Check whether low-power positions can safely submit counterexamples, whether independent review is accessible, and whether maintainers’ interests override correction. These are questions for review, not a presumption of capture merely because a community exists.

Each minimum record contains seven items: object type, version, rights holders, counterexample entry point, observed harm, falsification conditions, and judgment ceiling. Object type and version identify what is being checked; rights holders are not synonymous with a list of maintainers; the entry point must be usable; harm must be distinguished as observed, reported but awaiting verification, or unknown; falsification conditions make judgments revisable; and the ceiling prevents a local finding from expanding into a verdict on the whole framework.

Use failure conditions proportionate to each object. A documentary proposition may be refuted by conflicting passages; practice judgments require relevant observations; community-safety conclusions need material on protection and expression; and normative procedures require eligibility, not merely statistical validation. The source’s term “falsification conditions” does not mean disguising every value premise as a natural law refutable by a single empirical observation.

If dependence on terminology, cognitive lock-in, expert monopoly, commercial accommodation, or AI compliance packaging has caused identifiable harm, the relevant module may be narrowed, its use suspended, or alternatives assessed. The response should match the evidence: a local textual error receives a local correction; a high-impact practice risk leads to suspension of the relevant use; systemic burdens call for comparing alternatives. Neither attribute every problem to the core nor universally conclude that users failed to learn it.

distinctions.leftText: Definitions and rules have none of the conflicts checked.
distinctions.rightText: Actual use, consequences, and protection need independent material.

distinctions.leftText: The objects to which terms and reasoning apply, and their ceilings.
distinctions.rightText: Who decides naming and interpretation, and who bears the costs.

distinctions.leftText: Has specific sources and verifiable outcomes.
distinctions.rightText: Warrants review but cannot be directly recorded as harm that has occurred.

distinctions.leftText: Specific positions affected with respect to the relevant rights.
distinctions.rightText: Control of documentation or a brand does not represent everyone affected.

boundaries: Approval of one object does not certify the other three; no single overall health score can replace their separate judgments.
Falsification or revision conditions must fit the kind of judgment; normative values must not be passed off as empirical facts.
People harmed must not be required to learn the terminology before submitting a counterexample; safe entry points with low exposure need separate safeguards.
Narrowing or suspending a module does not erase historical harm or automatically remove responsibility for remedies.

argumentSteps: Select a document, concept, practice, or community object, and specify its version and intended judgment scope.
Record the seven minimum items individually, limiting judgments according to dependencies on missing information.
Test with material proportionate to that object; do not substitute approval at one level for approval at another.
Check identifiable harm and relationships of power and cost, retaining counterexamples and competing explanations.
Narrow or suspend affected modules, or compare alternatives, while preserving independently established facts and responsibilities.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: the four objects can have opposing states
teachingExamples.text: A fictional training project’s guide explicitly says, “Stage labels must not be used to sanction individuals,” so the document has no contradiction on this point. The instructor nevertheless labels learners as being at a low stage and excludes them on that basis, producing practice records of possible overreach requiring examination. At the conceptual level, applying a collective state to individuals is found to be a domain error. At the community level, there is no independent appeal material, so the safety of expression is unknown. A correct guide cannot justify declaring the project healthy; nor can one misuse justify claiming that every definition in the book is wrong.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The project, learners, conduct, and records are teaching constructions, not allegations against a real organization.
teachingExamples.boundary: A real case would require checking the material, the identities of the objects, and responses; motives should not be inferred from surface labels.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one minimum self-diagnostic record
teachingExamples.text: The object type is a document, version v1.2, with the scope limited to unit consistency in one table. Rights holders are readers who use that table to make judgments and those affected. The counterexample entry point permits specific line numbers to be submitted with low exposure. The observed issue is inconsistent units in two rows; real-world harm is unknown. The revision condition is credible original specifications showing an explicit conversion relationship between the units. The judgment ceiling is an unexplained inconsistency of measurement conventions in that table, not a claim that the author is dishonest or the system unsafe.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The version, table, and entry point are teaching templates; no protective channel has actually been created.
teachingExamples.boundary: The existence and safe usability of an entry point still require empirical evidence; filling every minimum field does not prove that rights are protected.

teachingExamples.title: Formal construction: four checks cannot be arbitrarily averaged
teachingExamples.text: Suppose four propositions—documentary consistency, conceptual applicability, protection in practice, and community correction—are respectively true, true, false, and unknown. Without a specified scale and valid aggregation rule, unknown cannot be treated as 0 to report “50% healthy,” nor can a majority passing among the first three establish overall safety. Preserve evidence and consequences separately, and limit the corresponding use because of the defect in protection in practice.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The four truth states are artificially assigned, not the results of real checks.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not deny that particular justified indicators may be statistically summarized; it rejects arbitrarily compressing heterogeneous responsibilities into an overall certification score.

counterexamples.text: Growth in community membership shows that an empirical problem family is valid.
counterexamples.effect: Membership is activity data, not an empirical test of a particular instance or evidence of net benefits from a classification.

counterexamples.text: The guide provides for appeals, so actual appeals must be effective.
counterexamples.effect: Real evidence is still needed of acceptance, independent review, the actual capacity to change erroneous outcomes through reasoned review, and protection against retaliation. A reasoned decision to uphold a correct outcome can also constitute an effective appeal.

counterexamples.text: A misuse can only mean that the user failed to learn properly.
counterexamples.effect: Also examine inducements in the documentation, conceptual overreach, practice, and power conditions; do not exclude the framework’s responsibility in advance.

questionAnswers.question: What are the seven items in a minimum self-diagnostic record?
questionAnswers.answer: Object type, version, rights holders, counterexample entry point, observed harm, falsification conditions, and judgment ceiling.

questionAnswers.answer: Use and misuse may affect readers, people being judged, and low-power positions; ownership of documentation does not encompass these rights.

questionAnswers.answer: They cannot be arbitrarily aggregated. Unknown is not a pass, and heterogeneous responsibilities require separate judgments.

16.2.title: 16.2 GOV-02 Consensus Procedures and Version Authority
16.2.lead: The test of consensus is not how many opposing hands remain raised when a meeting ends, but whether objections can enter safely, receive proportionate answers, and change the decision when they actually identify a problem. Preserving dissent and reaching a limited decision can coexist.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3494–3517; source anchor section-16-2; short quotation translated from Chinese: “‘Everyone agreed in the end’ is not valid consensus.” The source excerpt for this topic is separately reproduced verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and source text are kept separate.

The original first separates the appearance of outcomes from procedural capability. A room without opposing voices may reflect reasoned acceptance, fatigue, fear of retaliation, or exclusion from the agenda; visible unanimity alone cannot identify these mechanisms. Effective consensus requires actual relations of access, recording, response, and capacity for change; signatures or atmosphere cannot substitute for them. These are normative procedural requirements for adopting the framework in governance, not an empirical law about all groups.

The seven links address different breaks. Issue registration makes changes and counterexamples traceable; material disclosure makes reasons checkable, while remaining subject to protective nondisclosure; identification of affected objects prevents maintainers alone from having seats; objection channels allow low-power users, people being judged, nonprofessional readers, and external critics to enter; graded decision authority prevents copyediting powers from directly changing core concepts; retention of minority opinions prevents counterevidence from being deleted after passage; version write-back states what actually changed and what new evidence would cause withdrawal. These are not seven synonymous attendance forms.

The allocation of power must match the type of change. Correcting punctuation, redrawing a concept’s domain of application, changing empirical question families, and publishing high-impact assertions require different review capabilities and involve different risks. The original supplies no universal staffing, terms, or durations for all organizations; these parameters must be set beforehand under applicable organizational, jurisdictional, risk, and resource conditions. Procedures cannot be lengthened, shortened, or reset after an unfavorable objection appears to force passage in the case at hand.

nominal_only means that the institution excludes the possibility of objections triggering necessary corrections. This is stronger than “no one changed the draft this time”: where all necessary corrections would be refused, the entry point is merely nominal. If review finds that an objection does not identify an error and reasonably maintains the original decision, however, a zero-change rate alone does not establish an empty procedure. Capacity for change must be checked through rules, actual authority, material handling, and execution capability; a maintainer’s “criticism welcome” does not prove it.

Each objection must record its disposition, meaning the handling outcome, reasons, evidence, and impact on text, process, or action ceilings. Adoption must be bound to a real change_id and actual change; reasoned nonadoption must also be retained. An objector’s continued dislike of a conclusion differs from unanswered key issues concerning facts, protection, or authority. The original does not demand symbolic acceptance of one opinion to obtain applied, nor give any objector an unconditional permanent veto.

applied means a governance change meets the framework’s internal adoption conditions; it certifies neither real effects nor external action authority. Read with 16.19: this is a change state, so a real change in text, process, or action ceilings must still exist. Reasonably maintaining a correct proposition can complete its review, but “no change counts as change” cannot fabricate a new version change. If substantive objections affecting adoption remain without proportionate treatment, necessary independent review is absent, or nonwaivable rights or legal conditions remain unmet, pause the affected adoption. Standards must be public beforehand, appealable, and independently reviewable, not self-certified unilaterally by proposers or a majority.

The strongest objection is that endless consultation prevents maintenance from finishing and may let a minority delay protection. The response is not to abolish objections, but to distinguish answered value disagreements, repeated arguments, and decisive reasons not yet addressed; publish closure rules and reopening conditions; and limit the affected portion. Emergency duties operate under their own valid authority, scope, and period without waiting for theoretical perfection, but cannot use urgency to restore all old authority. Procedures must compare the costs of waiting, expression, and maintenance; this connects to threshold debt in 16.16 and scenario parameters in 16.25.

From a feedback perspective, this section cannot ask only whether opinions were received. If an objection changes understanding but not target fields, retain the achievement in understanding; if a draft changes while operation still consumes the old version, only document write-back is confirmed; if operation changes, whether protection improves still requires independent evidence. These layers prevent the general value of participation, causal feedback, textual change, internal adoption eligibility, and real protection from collapsing into a single “consensus success.”

distinctions.leftText: May reflect genuine endorsement, or the costs of exit and expression.
distinctions.rightText: Requires reasons to enter safely and receive proportionate treatment capable of changing decisions.

distinctions.leftText: Retain the objection and explain evidence, tradeoffs, and review paths.
distinctions.rightText: No change is permitted whatever the reasons: a nominal procedure.

distinctions.leftText: Can fulfill responsibilities to hear and argue.
distinctions.rightText: Additionally requires corresponding real change and all internal adoption conditions.

distinctions.leftText: Limits eligibility for use within this framework.
distinctions.rightText: Supported separately by valid external grounds and materials on actual outcomes.

boundaries: Neither adoption rates nor agreement rates are sufficient statistics for consensus quality; zero changes alone cannot prove procedural emptiness.
Whether an unresolved objection is decisive requires predeclared, appealable standards; a majority cannot unilaterally certify it as unimportant.
Material disclosure remains subject to privacy and protection; safe participation cannot become a requirement for fully public real-name disclosure.
Without real change, change_id cannot be fabricated; adoption of a change proves neither software consumption nor real protection.

caseLinks.title: Actual normative literature: RFC 7282 on rough consensus

caseNotes.title: Actual normative literature: RFC 7282 on rough consensus
caseNotes.text: In June 2014, the IETF published informational RFC 7282. Its abstract explicitly says it does not change IETF procedures. Section 3 distinguishes seriously addressing objections from necessarily accommodating every objection, requiring reasons for nonadoption and retaining appeals. It provides a real textual instance of “addressing reasons rather than counting votes.”
caseNotes.sourceLabel: P. Resnick，RFC 7282，2014
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Final abstract paragraph and Status of This Memo (printed p1); §3, printed pp7–9, especially the responsibility for consideration on p8 and the paragraphs on reasoned explanation and appeals on p9.
caseNotes.boundary: A normative explanatory text, not minutes of a particular meeting; it provides no causal evidence that every practice is effective or that the rule improves outcomes, and is not equivalent to all GOV-02 conditions.

argumentSteps: Premise: the same appearance of agreement can result from deliberation, fatigue, or suppression, so agreement proportions cannot independently identify an effective procedure.
Connect the seven links as issue, materials, impact, access, authority, retention, and write-back, assigning a checkable result to each.
Check each objection’s reasons, evidence, and relevant impacts; necessary corrections actually occur, and nonadoption is grounded and appealable.
Where decisive reasons remain unaddressed or necessary review or nonwaivable conditions are missing, pause dependent portions without erasing other independent conclusions.
Close internal adoption, actual change, operational consumption, and real protection separately; adoption creates no external authority.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two meetings with zero changes
teachingExamples.text: Group A receives an objection about mismatched units but allows only the original proposer to withdraw, while that proposer refuses to inspect the materials. Group B receives the same objection, independently establishes an explicit conversion relation, explains every formula, and opens an appeal path; no textual change is needed. Both groups have 0 changes, but A may involve institutional blockage while B may reasonably maintain the text. If B separately finds and corrects an erroneous link at the end, that particular change may be recorded; this minor correction cannot settle the major dispute.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The A/B meetings, objections, and texts are teaching constructions, not assessments of real organizations.
teachingExamples.boundary: The story cannot label any real organization as having nominal consensus; actual materials and authority still require checking.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: connecting objection records to versions
teachingExamples.text: Suppose proposal v1.4 excludes all anonymous comments. Objection O1 identifies how this blocks low-exposure feedback; review adopts it under safety requirements, and change_id=C1 binds new text permitting proxies and low-exposure channels. Objection O2 requests only a preferred title; it is not adopted after reasons concerning intelligibility and location are explained, and is retained. Only C1’s actual insertion into v1.5 supports textual change; whether the channel is genuinely safe and users dare to use it remains unknown.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Version numbers, IDs, and decisions are design examples, not governance or protection experiments already run.
teachingExamples.boundary: Changes in fields and hashes alone do not certify correct semantic change; actual adoption requires all relevant conditions, not merely two records.

teachingExamples.title: Formal construction: reply rates do not identify substantive handling
teachingExamples.text: Suppose all 10 objections receive automated replies: the reply rate is 10/10=100%. Four contain key factual gaps, with no materials supplied in response; in this explicit construction, the proportion of key reasons addressed is 0/4=0%. The denominators and targets differ; correct calculation of the former cannot replace the latter. One cannot infer a real organization’s probability of malice from 0/4.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The numbers 10 and 4 are constructed; “key” is an explicit assumption in this example, not an actual review finding.
teachingExamples.boundary: In reality, classification of key objections must itself be appealable; maintainers should not choose denominators retrospectively.

counterexamples.text: Everyone signed, so objections need not be retained.
counterexamples.effect: Signatures may not reveal safety of expression; minority opinions and exit conditions still require preservation.

counterexamples.text: Effective review requires accepting at least one objection.
counterexamples.effect: The original explicitly rejects symbolic adoption; reasoned maintenance and necessary correction are judged separately.

counterexamples.text: One person’s continued opposition can permanently block any decision.
counterexamples.effect: Unresolved substantive issues differ from answered value disagreements; qualified rules permit bounded closure.

questionAnswers.question: If two procedures both make zero draft changes, can they be judged equally ineffective?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Check whether objections actually identify defects, whether treatment was proportionate, and whether necessary correction was possible.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can 10 automated replies prove that 4 key gaps were addressed?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A 100% reply rate and a 0% rate of addressing key reasons can coexist in the teaching example.
questionAnswers.basis: The two ratios have different numerators, denominators, and tasks.

questionAnswers.question: May a proposer cancel independent review merely by declaring it unnecessary?
questionAnswers.answer: It cannot be self-certified unilaterally; determine this through predeclared risk rules and appealable independent review.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: After a new version is adopted, may it immediately be used to impose dispositions on others?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Internal adoption issues no real-world authority; high-impact use also requires its protective review and authorization.

16.3.title: 16.3 GOV-03 Correcting empirical assertions and retaining or discarding question families
16.3.lead: When a counterexample appears, first determine whether it refutes a particular answer, a range of generalization, or indicates that the entire way of asking questions is not worth retaining. Without these distinctions, it is easy to oscillate between “the whole theory collapses” and “no failure has anything to do with the theory.”
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3518–3541; original anchor section-16-3. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Correction first distinguishes three objects.” The source excerpt for this lesson is separately attached verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and original text are distinct.

The first object is a concrete instance proposition, such as whether a grouping improves prediction for a specified sample, window, and target. Proportionate counterevidence can refute it; a preregistered test failing its check with inadequate power may instead leave it unresolved. These must not be conflated. The second is generalization across instances: within a declared scope, one counterexample can restrict an “all are so” claim, but a single failure cannot determine occurrence rates elsewhere. The third is a question classification such as G1–G4, asking about grouping, channels, historical increments, and representational closure, not four natural laws every system must satisfy. A negative answer does not make the question meaningless; nevertheless, if the questions persistently omit key issues or impose burdens, they may be simplified or replaced.

The five management states for question families express use policies. normal_use continues use within declared purposes, without treating common usage as established gain; boundary_restricted narrows objects, tasks, scales, or settings where omissions or burdens arise; suspended pauses relevant uses causing locatable misjudgment or high-risk misuse while retaining independently established facts; replacement_competition compares professional, simplified, and alternative classifications on the same task and materials with proportionate resources; retired_from_core removes the classification from the common core without prohibiting grounded local tools from remaining as domain resources or historical records.

These states are not interchangeable with the four empirical-instance states such as supported and null_supported. A question family may be in normal_use while an instance within it is refuted; suspending a module does not automatically erase bounded facts previously independently supported within it. Empirical truth, evidential strength, and maintenance policy are three dimensions. “Retirement” especially cannot mean every earlier fact was false, nor “still in use” count as a positive test.

Public assertions normally proceed through internal_draft, open_assertion, and publishable, but may also be downgraded, paused, blocked from publication, withdrawn, or replaced. The framework as a whole separately moves among active, boundary_restricted, suspended, replacement_competition, replaced, and retired. These manage assertions and the whole respectively; they are not a unified maturity ladder linking every node. publishable means eligibility for publication only: it neither proves every sentence correct nor creates real-world action authorization.

retired_from_core, withdrawn, replaced, and retired are terminal states. Restoring historical files cannot make the original identity active again, still less restore old authorization. If a new method reenters, it needs an identifiable new identity, renewed relevant external authorization, and preservation of old records. This is a governance design choice, not a claim that the text can no longer be read or correct mathematical results must be forgotten. Terminal states restrict revival of old eligibility while preserving knowledge and responsibility trails.

Repeated counterexamples, stable misjudgments about particular types of subjects, continually expanding explanatory scope, and repeated evasion of failure through “not long enough,” “not deep enough,” or “the object is not a system” trigger suspension review. But every anomaly cannot be forcibly attributed to the core. First check objects, measurement, auxiliary conditions, mechanisms, and extrapolation scope to find which dependency the anomaly actually penetrates. Local revisions require independent reasons and new testable consequences, not a condition added only after failure that conveniently excludes the case.

The strongest objection is that complex theories always need auxiliary-condition revisions and premature retirement can stifle progress. This reminder is valid: what matters is not whether patches exist, but whether they have independent evidence, take risks on new materials, and retain old failures. Conversely, proponents cannot invoke science’s revisability to reject all retirement. A constructive approach predeclares conditions for changing judgments and permits local retention, scope contraction, suspension of risky uses, and comparison with alternatives simultaneously. Comparisons must also count inappropriate abstention, waiting, and maintenance burdens, not select only successful cases.

This section connects with 16.2 and 16.19: grounded maintenance of a correct claim also counts as qualified handling, while established counterexamples should actually change the text, processes, or action ceilings that depend on them. Even if the core remains temporarily unchanged, local scope restrictions and failure records must enter the version. A framework calling itself “falsifiable” but never allowing substantive consequences has not fulfilled this governance commitment.

caseNotes.text: CERN’s release of September 23, 2011, and its subsequent updates preserve the sequence of changes: the initial anomaly was submitted for broad scrutiny; the February 2012 update recorded possible instrumental problems affecting timing; the June 8 update reported that time-of-flight measurements from four experiments were consistent with the speed of light, and attributed the original OPERA measurement anomaly to a faulty element of the fiber-optic timing system.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: CERN, successive updates in 2011–2012
caseNotes.sourceLocator: ORIGINAL PRESS RELEASE, paragraph 2; UPDATE 23 February 2012, first two paragraphs; UPDATE 8 June 2012, first two paragraphs.

argumentSteps: Identify the proposition and original scope struck by the counterexample, distinguishing clear counterevidence from insufficient evidence.
Distinguish an instance answer, generalization across instances, and the use of a question classification; do not automatically revoke the other two when one fails.
Trace dependencies on measurement, auxiliary conditions, mechanisms, and extrapolation; local revision requires independent reasons and new testable consequences.
Write proportionate handling back into use policies and publication states; terminal states preserve history and cannot restore old eligibility.
Use comparisons with alternatives under the same task, materials, and proportionate resources to decide restriction or exit; without comparison, do not announce a winner.

teachingExamples.title: Formal construction: which level does a counterexample strike?
teachingExamples.text: In the constructed finite domain X={a,b,c}, let proposition P be “every object has a benefit greater than 0,” with benefits (2,1,-1). c has refuted P, but the positive benefits of a and b still hold; revising it to “a and b are positive” gives a narrower true proposition, but cannot retrospectively turn the original P into a success. The question “which objects have positive benefits?” remains meaningful. Whether to continue using the current classification depends separately on its ability to distinguish differences and its costs; P’s failure cannot directly settle that issue.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The finite domain and values are stipulated, not real benefit data.
teachingExamples.boundary: This establishes only logical scope, not the usefulness of a real-world classification, and does not permit post hoc narrowing while retaining the original confirmation status.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: suspension is not forgetting
teachingExamples.text: Suppose module M repeatedly treats missing responses from users with low literacy as negatives; existing verifiable cases trigger suspension of that use. An equipment latency independently measured in the past is still preserved. Successor module M2 distinguishes unobservable from negative, and must be checked on new materials and receive applicable approval; renaming it or restoring old files cannot establish that the problem is solved. If M is still merely suspended, resumption must meet the corresponding review and valid authorization conditions; only if it has subsequently been retired must its successor have a new identity.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The module, sample, and results are all teaching assumptions; no system trial was conducted.
teachingExamples.boundary: The scope of an actual suspension must follow the evidence and risks; this example does not certify M2 as better.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: added conditions must also risk failure
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a model fails under high load. If a capacity threshold that was previously omitted but independently measured explains results in a new window, it may support a grounded scope revision; if all failed cases are merely relabeled “non-systems,” with no independent boundary or new test, this is untestable exclusion. Both revisions remove old failures from the new scope, but their epistemic standing differs.
teachingExamples.assumptions: No system was actually measured; this is a conditional example comparing reasons for revision.
teachingExamples.boundary: The number of added conditions alone cannot establish bad faith; reasons, evidence, and testable consequences must be checked.

counterexamples.text: A G3 instance has no historical increment, so historical research is meaningless.
counterexamples.effect: G3 checks only for an increment beyond the current representation; historical formation, effects of current carriers, and the value of the question are judged separately.

counterexamples.text: Removing all failed cases from scope establishes that the old claim succeeded.
counterexamples.effect: The new scope does not change the old resolution; revision still requires independent reasons and new testable consequences.

counterexamples.text: After a module is retired, its old files can be restored and its old authorization reused.
counterexamples.effect: A terminal state cannot return to active service; a successor needs a new identity and corresponding authorization.

questionAnswers.question: If -1 occurs among three benefits, does it follow that all benefits are negative?
questionAnswers.answer: No. It only refutes the claim that all are positive; the other two positive values remain.
questionAnswers.basis: Item-by-item judgment in a finite domain and the logic of universal propositions.

questionAnswers.question: Does normal_use mean all instances are supported?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The former is a management policy; the latter is an instance’s evidence status.

questionAnswers.question: Can failure to pass the positive-support gate directly count as counterevidence?
questionAnswers.answer: Not automatically; distinguish refutation by proportionate evidence from an unresolved result due to insufficient precision.

questionAnswers.question: How can one tell whether a revision merely protects the theory?
questionAnswers.answer: Check for independent grounds, new testable consequences, failure records, and comparison with alternatives, rather than merely whether the revision explains old cases.

16.4.title: 16.4 GOV-04 Tracking Cases, Counterexamples, Claims, and Foresight
16.4.lead: A compelling case does not mean all cases are like it; a fully registered prediction does not mean it will come true at resolution. This section separately preserves what happened, what is claimed, what is predicted, and what subsequently changed, allowing others to check judgments along the record.
explanation: Original location: Chinese source lines 3542–3561; original anchor section-16-4; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “The five types of authoritative records are interconnected but do not replace one another:”. A verbatim source excerpt for this topic is separately attached in source-slice.md, keeping explanation apart from the original.

COUNTEREXAMPLE-REGISTRY records the object, scale, and window targeted by a counterexample, actually observable facts, why it cannot simply be treated as noise, the original and alternative explanations, requested handling, and subsequent signals. A counterexample is not just any disliked story: it must engage the conditions or conclusion of the original claim. Registering a counterexample is not an immediate verdict either; insufficient materials, mismeasurement, or different objects still need checking. However, a person raising it should not have to prove an entire alternative theory before pointing out failure in the existing explanation.

CASE-REGISTRY preserves successes, failures, early dissipation, unresolved processes, counterexamples, indeterminate cases, and excluded cases. Only survivors who eventually succeed must not be called cases while those that disintegrated early are treated as never having existed. For excluded records, also ask whether insufficient materials are accidental missing pages or whether the current observation method systematically fails to see certain subjects or early processes. The latter may require changing collection or narrowing claims; deleting records cannot eliminate blind spots. Unresolved and failed are also different: an observation window that has not ended does not establish failure.

When records are used to compare mechanisms of formation, failure, or dissipation, or to estimate proportions, first specify the object, outcome, spatiotemporal window, and inclusion rules. Processes in which the corresponding outcome had an opportunity to occur but did not are informative negative cases; every nonoccurrence unrelated to the outcome does not automatically enter the denominator. Opportunity for occurrence and detectability in materials are two separate judgments: when an opportunity existed but records were lost, retain unknown rather than entering zero; when evidence shows an actual occurrence, it cannot be excluded solely because the theory calls it impossible. Where reasonable boundaries are disputed, show the conclusions under each scope and how they change. Textual understanding of a single case does not require inventing a population for frequencies; existing professional case-selection records can be cited when they fulfill the same responsibilities.

CLAIM-REGISTRY binds each claim to its type, object, scale, affected positions, evidence and counterevidence, alternative explanations, withdrawal conditions, action ceiling, and public status. One case can support several claims of different strengths; one claim can depend on multiple cases. Connections must not erase differences in strength: a factual record does not mean a mechanism is identified, still less that authorization exists to change others’ lives on that basis. A formal judgment made in the framework’s name must have the corresponding record to qualify for public release or high-impact use under this framework; this is a necessary threshold, not one satisfied sufficiently by completing a form. Ordinary discussion, independent domain research, and supported local opinions do not lose their epistemic standing because they lack this identifier.

FORECAST-REGISTRY preserves in advance a prediction’s window, triggering conditions, early and reverse signals, and competing predictions, then records results at resolution. “If A occurs, B may occur in a future window” is conditional foresight, not an immutable label of fate attached to a person. Distinguish whether the trigger occurred, whether the outcome occurred, whether the outcome is measurable, and whether the window has ended; a trigger’s nonoccurrence need not equal refutation of the prediction. Nor may one change the window or wording after resolution and register the old prediction as a hit. New assumptions get a separate version, while the original record remains.

VERSION-LOG connects these records to actual handling: how counterexamples lead to boundary restriction, downgrading, suspension, publication blocking, withdrawal, replacement, retirement, rollback, or remedy. Adding a log entry alone does not establish implementation of the promised change; rollback does not erase harm already caused or revive eligibility in a terminal state. More cases provide traceability, not automatic generality; internally selected cases cannot claim to be external validation. Organizational actions and automated decisions must also meet the conditions for strong judgments, protection, and external authorization.

Governance changes also need seven types of runtime registry: canonical actor, evidence, interests, authorization, external review, dissent, and a structured VERSION-LOG. They address runtime questions such as “Who exactly is this ID, can the evidence be resolved, who authorizes whom, and who has interests linking them to whom?” The five preceding knowledge records cannot replace them. The two classifications have different responsibilities, and VERSION-LOG forms a junction; they must not mechanically be counted as twelve unrelated tables. evidence_ref must resolve to evidence whose integrity is verified; integrity verification does not make every interpretation supported by the evidence true, and content fit requires separate checking.

Reviewers, decision-making members, and authorizing parties must resolve to canonical identity IDs; aliases assist retrieval only. Their funding, evaluation, identity, promotion, control, and commercial-interest relationships with proposers must also be checked pairwise; an unfilled relationship field does not establish the absence of a relationship. An authorization issuer cannot also be its holder or proposer. The strongest objection is that more registration can increasingly consume time in formalities: this section responds by limiting records to the task, allowing citations to professional records, and not mandating identifiers for ordinary research. Implementation should reduce duplicate entry while preserving necessary verifiable traces; convenience cannot justify dropping identity, conflict-of-interest, or factual checks, nor can complete paperwork be treated as effective governance.

caseNotes.text: In their author manuscript dated January 19, 2004, Mahoney and Goertz treat selection of negative cases and population boundaries as methodological problems; they also devote a section to cases where “what was judged impossible nevertheless happens.” This shows that selection scope itself must be tested, rather than automatically deleting counterexamples according to theoretical expectations.

argumentSteps: First distinguish the respective objects of cases, counterexamples, claims, foresight, and version handling, then connect them through explicit references.
When comparison or proportions are needed, state opportunities for occurrence, inclusion scope, observation window, and detectability conditions; do not rewrite unknown as zero.
Check the scope struck by counterexamples and alternative explanations, retaining exclusion reasons and changes in reasonable boundaries.
Register the corresponding claim for formal framework judgments; assess publication eligibility, empirical support, and real-world authority to act separately.
At governance runtime, resolve evidence, reconcile identities, check relationships pairwise and separate authorization roles, and write actual handling back into the records.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: what does the denominator change?
teachingExamples.text: Suppose 10 processes all have the corresponding opportunity and are observable: 4 produce the target outcome and 6 do not, so the proportion in this set is 4/10=40%. A further 90 objects lack the corresponding opportunity; incorrectly adding them changes it to 4/100=4%. If the original 10 actually comprise only 4 positives, 4 negatives, and 2 unknown outcomes, the observed subset is 4/8=50%, while the proportion for the entire opportunity set of 10 is known only to lie between 4/10 and 6/10, or 40%–60%; unknowns cannot be filled with zeros to report 40% as a point estimate. This interval is only a logical bound for a finite set, not a statistical confidence interval.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All quantities, opportunities, and observability conditions are stipulated; no real cases were collected.
teachingExamples.boundary: The real-world mechanism producing unknowns may be nonrandom, so the observed 50% cannot directly represent the whole; the opportunity boundary also needs substantive justification.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: linking one case to different records
teachingExamples.text: A hypothetical team predicts “repair will be completed within four weeks after trigger T.” Case C records that T occurred and the four-week window ended, but missing log pages leave repair status indeterminate; forecast F retains its original deadline and competing predictions; claim Q can say only that completion has not been established in the currently verifiable materials; counterexample R checks whether this refutes the original promise of guaranteed completion; version V records withdrawal of the unconditional guarantee while retaining this outcome as unresolved. Missing logs cannot be forced into completion or failure, nor can a new deadline overwrite F.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The team, events, and IDs are teaching constructions.
teachingExamples.boundary: When facts are insufficient, retain unresolved status while allowing risk-based suspension of operations dependent on that proof of completion.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: aliases do not create external review
teachingExamples.text: One person uses accounts A and B to propose and review respectively; after canonical identity resolution, this is still one person. Another person C has a different identity but depends on the proposer for promotion; the relationship must still be recorded and handled under applicable independence rules. A separate issuer account likewise cannot bypass restrictions on the issuer being the same person as the authorization holder.
teachingExamples.assumptions: People and accounts are hypothetical; no actual institution is identified.
teachingExamples.boundary: How a relationship is handled depends on specific rules; this story cannot establish that any actual person acted unlawfully or dishonestly.

counterexamples.text: Ten thousand success cases establish general effectiveness better than ten cases with complete failure records.
counterexamples.effect: Quantity cannot supply missing entry rules, omission mechanisms, or external validation.

counterexamples.text: The theory says this event is impossible, so material showing it actually happened may be deleted from the sample.
counterexamples.effect: Theory cannot be the sole reason for excluding real counterexamples; verify the facts and consider revising boundaries.

counterexamples.text: An independent domain paper lacks a CLAIM identifier, so it has no knowledge value.
counterexamples.effect: The framework's publication qualifications do not monopolize the knowledge standing of all research.

questionAnswers.question: With 4 positives, 4 negatives, and 2 unknowns, why can one not directly report an overall 40%?
questionAnswers.answer: That defaults the two unknowns to negative. The finite-set bound for the overall proportion is 40% to 60%, while the observed subset's proportion is 50%; they have different denominators.
questionAnswers.basis: Within the constructed finite set, the unknowns can contain 0 to 2 positives.

questionAnswers.question: Should a project only halfway through its observation period be recorded as failed because it is unfinished?
questionAnswers.answer: This alone cannot establish failure. Record the process as unresolved under the predetermined outcome and window, separately noting early danger signals if necessary.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If an evidence reference exists and is marked verified, can it automatically support high-impact action?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Completeness, content support, publication qualification, and external authorization are different thresholds.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: After a forecast fails at resolution, can one change the deadline and keep claiming that the original prediction was correct?
questionAnswers.answer: The old window cannot be overwritten. Create a separate version for the new prediction, preserving the original result and reasons for revision.

16.5.title: 16.5 GOV-05 Pre-conceptual Gate and Ceiling on Conceptual Validity
16.5.lead: First explain what you actually observed, then decide whether a broad concept can explain it. Giving people one name does not prove they form one structural domain. Even when a concept fits, it cannot slide directly into deciding for others.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3562–3577; source anchor section-16-5; short quotation translated from Chinese: “Before formal mapping, first answer in plain language:”. The source excerpt for this lesson is attached verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and source text are separate.

The pre-conceptual gate prevents circular reasoning: labeling an object with structural-domain vocabulary, then treating that label as evidence that the object really is a structural domain. Before formal mapping, explain whether the object can be observed jointly, where its minimum boundary lies, whether internal actions repeatedly affect one another, whether there is a shared problem, direction, risk, or constraint, who bears maintenance costs, and whether outcomes or bad news can change subsequent practices. Plain language does not imply absence of theoretical background. It requires making the proposed objects, relationships, and facts checkable without prior acceptance of this framework.

“Observable jointly” does not merely mean fitting into a column in one table, and a “minimum boundary” need not mean closure without exchange. Labeling all people in blue clothes together creates a classification, not proof of repeated mutual influence. Conversely, repair collaboration across locations may have verifiable links through tasks, tools, responsibilities, and risks without sharing enclosing walls. Shared problems, directions, risks, or constraints are different connections listed by the source; do not arbitrarily require unanimous views or one central will. Maintenance costs also require asking who bears unpaid work, waiting, or exposure, rather than observing only the nominal organizational leader.

The final question specifically checks whether bad news can change subsequent practice. Receiving information, issuing receipts, and collecting data do not mean information can influence later action; this connects to the distinctions among feedback, learning, and repair. Conversely, change does not establish successful repair, and one adjustment does not prove full structural-domain qualification. The pre-conceptual gate is a minimum review for entering formal mapping, not a few questions that complete all causal, value, and power judgments at once.

If the gate is not passed, the source permits phenomenon description, risk registration, and narrative analysis; indications of harm, local facts, or questions requiring observation can still be stated. The limit concerns how strongly material may be formally mapped into framework objects, not a prohibition on independent professional research. Those experiencing a situation do not need to prove a structural domain before they may describe it. If material is insufficient, specify the missing connection, boundary, or response evidence; distinguish actual contrary material from insufficient observation.

After the gate passes, five strengths of concept use remain. Expressive use helps articulate feelings or similarity without claiming an identified mechanism. Exploratory use turns intuitions into questions and observation signals without posing as diagnosis. Diagnostic use has externally observable material and permits low-to-moderate-confidence judgments, while still specifying objects and possible misjudgments. Strong judgment requires passing the object, evidence, scale, responsibility, and observation gates; confident tone or numerous evidence files alone cannot upgrade it. This section supplies no formula converting the five levels to percentages and does not claim that any domain material necessarily leads upward.

The action level additionally requires external review, appeals, protection against retaliation, compensation, and withdrawal, as well as Part Fourteen's normative choice, J authorization, and O procedures. Switching accounts for self-review cannot replace external review; appeals cannot be merely a mailbox; withdrawal cannot merely delete a report while leaving consequences untouched. Even a strong factual judgment still requires separate grounds for a reasonable target, who may decide, and what procedures permit execution. Concept-use ceilings must be assessed together with current use and evidence. The same material can support a low-strength observation without supporting a different high-impact action.

The strongest objection is that the pre-conceptual gate may exclude genuinely harmful but difficult-to-observe relationships. Vocabulary proficiency cannot resolve this risk. Preserve phenomenon and risk material, investigate why observation is difficult, and allow appropriate professional methods and low-exposure expression while preventing premature whole-object diagnosis. Conversely, relaxing the gate until any similarity passes would make concepts incapable of failure. A workable approach states what external material answers each question, what remains unknown, and the maximum currently supportable level, allowing contraction or upgrade when new facts appear.

The five strengths here are ceilings on concept use, not levels of human worth, institutional rankings, or aliases for the S0–S6 state prototypes in Part Eight §8.3. The diagram's order shows increasing evidential and protective obligations, not automatic real-world growth through stages. Professional classification examples can illustrate that naming requires conditions and scope, but astronomy's use of classification does not turn celestial bodies into personified governance subjects bearing responsibilities and appeals. Cross-domain analogy must stop at the small step it supports.

caseNotes.title: Actual classification text: scope and conditions in the IAU planet definition
caseNotes.text: IAU Resolution B5 of 2006 specifies the Solar System as its scope and lists conditions including orbiting the Sun, being nearly round, and clearing the orbital neighborhood. B6 classifies Pluto as a dwarf planet under that definition. What is directly observable here is a professional institution organizing names through explicit scope and conditions, rather than using an old name to prove its own classification.

argumentSteps: First describe the object, boundary, repeated influence, shared conditions, costs, and consequences of bad news without structural-domain labels.
Check the external material needed for these questions; record unknowns or failures, avoiding concepts used to prove themselves.
When the gate is not passed, retain descriptive, risk, and narrative responsibilities while stopping unsupported formal mapping.
Even after passing, set the expressive, exploratory, diagnostic, or strong-judgment ceiling by evidence and use; labels do not permit direct jumps.
For action, separately check normative choice, J permissions, O procedures, and review, appeal, and other protections; insufficient conditions preclude executing high-impact judgments.
