B observes repair workers across cities repeatedly sharing parts, taking up work orders, and bearing waiting costs, with error feedback changing subsequent allocations. This provides material for further checks of formal mapping. B still gains no qualification to diagnose every member's motives or discipline members.

teachingExamples.text: A hypothetical process has a complaints mailbox, but all messages are automatically archived and decision-makers lack the authority or channel to adjust accordingly. The mailbox's existence supports only a description of an entry point, not the claim that bad news can change subsequent practice. If review is later enabled and an error actually corrected, the material supports only that particular change. General effectiveness needs later observation.

teachingExamples.boundary: Absence of a particular change does not alone establish an absence of correction capacity; a correct original decision can be retained after reasoned review.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: diagnosis cannot jump into discipline

The diagnosis and unknowns can be stated; a supervisor cannot immediately revoke people's eligibility based on this conceptual label. 16.6.title: 16.6 GOV-06 Absence Signals, Protective Opacity, and Suppressive Opacity
16.6.lead: No complaints in a place may mean the relevant problem is genuinely absent, or that people fear speaking, lack somewhere to speak, or cannot leave a lasting record. Judging whether hidden information is justified requires more than “how much was disclosed”: ask whom it protects, who benefits, who can review it, and when the protective rationale is reconsidered.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3578–3593; source anchor section-16-6; short quotation translated from Chinese: “Invisibility is not absence of information.” The source excerpt for this lesson is attached verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and source text are separate.

The signals of absence listed in this section are possible explanations to distinguish, not a diagnosis of suppression whenever silence appears. An absent anchor may mean a shared orientation never formed; absent feedback may mean no channel exists or people fear speaking; absent conflict may reflect fear, dependence, or punishment; absent repair may mean there is no interface; absent exit may mean the price of leaving is unbearable; absent language may mean a lack of expressive tools. They shift inquiry from “whether a surface record exists” to the conditions of formation, expression, transmission, and detection. One explanation cannot cover every setting.

For example, “nobody exits” is compatible with at least two situations: people want to stay, or they find leaving difficult. Distinguishing them calls for checking alternatives, exit costs, punishment risks, anonymous views, and subsequent responses, rather than forcing people to state their positions publicly on the spot. Likewise, lacking formal language does not mean lacking experience, and lacking conflict records does not mean agreement. Absence has research value, but its interpretation depends on observation conditions. This connects both to 16.4's prohibition on filling missing evidence with zeros and to Part Seven's point that observational intervention can change the object.

protected concerns protecting vulnerable actors, privacy, witness safety, experience not yet fully formed, and low-power feedback. Concealing reporters' identities can coexist with preserving verifiable content; privacy does not exempt powerful people from responsibility. Protection should consider indirect identification: even after names are removed, combinations of rare roles, dates, and places may expose individuals. This states the need for proportionate protection, not a promise that any anonymization method is absolutely safe, nor a requirement that people first expose themselves to prove harm.

functional is the bounded opacity needed to reduce information overload, preserve professional judgment, ritual space, buffer zones, or quiet space for decisions, while permitting subsequent review and tracing of responsibility. Temporarily withholding discussion from public view can prevent unprocessed speculation from immediately harming others; it cannot justify making decision grounds permanently uncheckable or responsible persons forever unanswerable. Professional expertise is no substitute for independent review either; specify who can see what under which authorization and protection.

suppressive is characterized by concealing responsibility, blocking feedback, evading review, creating fear, maintaining monopolies of power, or preventing harmed people from proving harm. Judgment requires material about relevant conduct and consequences, rather than only managers' accounts of their motives. A real arrangement may reasonably keep some content confidential while blocking verification of other content. Examine these separately by object and use instead of applying a permanent label to an entire organization. Once proportionate material establishes suppressive opacity, the source requires triggering anti-capture measures, external review, and a block on public release; it must not continue to be treated as a healthy boundary.

All three classifications must answer four questions: whom does it protect, who benefits, who can independently review it, and when is it lifted? Without complete answers, independent review, time boundaries, and lifting conditions, it must not be registered as a healthy boundary. This does not require publishing the real names of protected people on a public page. Appropriate role descriptions and controlled verification can identify protected positions, authorization, and the responsibility chain while maintaining safety. Blocking public release also does not mean publishing sensitive material to punish failures of duty. Restrict eligibility for the relevant public judgments that depend on this opacity, and follow proportionate review and protection procedures.

Durations and lifting conditions manage continuing review of confidentiality grounds; they are not countdowns to exposing private information. An expiry review may conclude that protection remains necessary or that only the portion needed to support a bounded judgment should be disclosed. Preserve responsibility records of who maintained, adjusted, or lifted protection on what grounds. Failure to confirm justification does not establish suppression; conversely, a confidentiality label cannot shield fabrication, evasion of responsibility, or obstruction of credible verification. There is an important third state: justification remains unconfirmed, so suspend healthy-boundary certification while continuing inquiry.

The strongest objection is that greater requirements for records and review can expose the very people meant to be protected. This risk is real, so access to material and public disclosure must be minimized, and reviewers must also be constrained by corresponding protection and authority. The solution is neither to abolish review nor to disclose everything to everyone. Distinguish sensitive content, evidence needed to support bounded conclusions, independent verifiers, and explanations visible to the public. Assessment should also consider the exposure and burdens that further questions impose on participants; when information is insufficient, narrow the conclusion rather than compel disclosure.

Unconfirmed justification does not mean suppression has been established, but the arrangement cannot be registered in advance as a healthy boundary.
Privacy protection and fact-checking can be arranged in layers; victims' identities need not be made public.
Confidentiality labels cannot excuse fabrication or evasion of responsibility; independent review does not automatically authorize full disclosure either.

caseLinks.title: An actual mechanism: NASA ASRS de-identified reports

caseNotes.title: An actual mechanism: NASA ASRS de-identified reports
caseNotes.text: The official NASA ASRS website explains that reports are voluntary, personal and organizational names are removed before database entry, and dates, times, and other potentially identifying details are generalized or removed. This example shows that preserving safety information and reducing identity exposure can be designed separately. The website also lists confidentiality exceptions, so the mechanism description cannot be understood as a guarantee of absolute confidentiality for all material.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: Paragraphs 1–2 of Confidentiality and Incentives to Report; for exceptions, see the first separately listed Caveat
caseNotes.boundary: Only the official mechanism description was checked. This does not independently certify successful protection of every report or improved accident rates, nor discuss individual waiver eligibility. The two pages do not suffice to certify all four GOV-06 questions.

argumentSteps: Separate visible records from actual states and list multiple distinguishable explanations of absence.
Check conditions of expression channels, prices to be paid, detection, and observational intervention; silence does not directly establish health or suppression.
Assess the object and use of protected, functional, or suppressive classifications item by item, checking the four questions and independent review.
When conditions are incomplete, first refuse healthy-boundary certification; when suppression is actually evidenced, trigger the corresponding anti-capture measures, review, and release block.
Review timing and lifting conditions do not mean automatic disclosure; maintaining protection also requires proportionate reasons and a responsibility trail.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two sources of zero complaints
teachingExamples.text: All ten members of team A can safely raise objections at low cost, yet no complaints arise; team B also has zero complaints, but its manager punishes reporters. The figure “0” alone cannot distinguish them. Check channels, risks, retention of material, and safe feedback. If that information is also unavailable, the conclusion should be that zero records cannot certify health, not that suppression of team B's kind has directly been established.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The two teams and their membership counts are hypothetical; no real personnel survey was conducted.
teachingExamples.boundary: Even observing an available channel cannot guarantee every problem will be reported; no statistical detection model has been established.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: maintaining protection when review is due
teachingExamples.text: Suppose the confidentiality grounds for a witness report are reviewed every three months. At review time, credible material indicates that identity-exposure risk persists. Independent review can maintain protection while publishing de-identified conclusions and bounded supporting grounds. Reaching the date does not authorize publishing the name; responsibility for the next review and conditions for lifting protection remain.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The duration and report are design examples, not a real case or regulatory requirement.
teachingExamples.boundary: Three months is not a universal duration; specific arrangements depend on risks, authorization, and applicable procedures.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: different responsibilities within one document
teachingExamples.text: Imagined meeting minutes contain statements identifying harmed people and the grounds for managerial decisions. Public disclosure of the former may be restricted; if even authorized independent review of the latter is blocked, merely saying “protecting privacy” is insufficient. Material and access permissions can be separated to support responsibility tracing with less exposure; unverified facts still cannot be treated as confirmed accusations.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The meeting is constructed; no actual identity or document is disclosed.
teachingExamples.boundary: Separation may not achieve complete anonymity; if re-identification remains possible, publicly disclosable content should be narrowed further.

counterexamples.text: Nobody left, so everyone wants to stay.
counterexamples.effect: Unbearable exit costs are a competing explanation; check the conditions of choice.

counterexamples.text: The grounds for confidentiality have not been proved, so the responsible person must be suppressing others.
counterexamples.effect: Lack of certification differs from established counterevidence; first restrict certification and investigate.

counterexamples.text: The confidentiality review is due, so the system should automatically publish the original testimony.
counterexamples.effect: The duration manages review rather than forcing exposure of sensitive material; protection may continue for stated reasons.

This module's bounded reference is governance.module.GOV-07 → hsp.domain.human_intentional_collective → hsp.state.S6. The arrows indicate references to the domain of application and state, not a causal chain or evolutionary ladder. An independent runtime record must establish that the object is a human intentional collective and that its state includes S6. Individual humans, nonhuman systems, and collectives not meeting S6 cannot be directly included. A record number or internal assertion cannot replace Part Eight's required object evidence, identity, scale, window, independent review, and counterevidence checks.

“A state includes” does not require masking differences with a single label for the whole. Part Eight permits evidence-based distinctions among single_dominant, mixed, parallel, and unknown; the two multi-prototype configurations, mixed and parallel, require positive material, and the unknown cannot masquerade as a mixture. If one subsystem meets S6 while other positions do not, preserve the corresponding scope rather than extrapolating local recovery to the entire institution. All states remain descriptive judgments: they generate no action authorization and do not imply greater worth than other people or collectives.

S6 requires corresponding evidence of problem detection, error correction, functional recovery, and continuity of those taking up the work within specified functions, objects, and bounded windows. §8.3.7 additionally requires distributed uptake, effective feedback, recovery and renewal, and new generative capabilities: multiple positions can correct errors with little central intervention, and successors genuinely gain knowledge, authority, and protection and can change old arrangements. Low fluctuation, constant firefighting by a central figure, frequent personnel turnover, and polished annual reports can produce similar appearances and cannot alone certify S6.

Stage 6 is not transcendence of entropy increase, absence of conflict, or permanent immunity to failure. The source's dynamic equilibrium means bounded maintenance of functions through continuing calibration; regression, splitting, transition, exit, or collapse remain possible. Good current operation supports the corresponding functional judgment but may not test recovery from disturbances or continuity of uptake. Conversely, genuine recovery is not automatically invalid because it needs continuing support. Distinguish autonomous, transferable resource backing from irreplaceable, hidden, single-point firefighting. Safety support must not be withdrawn without authorization merely to demonstrate adaptation.

Record detection delays, repair delays, recurrence rates, resource margins, and load distribution separately. Delays have starting and ending times and time units; recurrence rates have events and opportunity denominators; margins specify resource types; load also concerns who bears it. Do not add hours, proportions, inventories, and headcounts into one “unified speed,” or use averages to conceal prolonged overload at peripheral positions. Causal effects also require proportionate identification; observing recovery during support does not automatically establish that any one measure caused it.

Observational recursion means the object responds to diagnosis, and the response enters the next observation round. Further expansion has an entry point only when a new response changes boundaries, identity, resources, action channels, uptake relations, feedback write-back, risks, or public memory, or provides a new high-cost signal. More similar statements, changed wording, or additional documents from the same source do not automatically count as new discriminating evidence. Even when an entry point appears, safety and stopping conditions still constrain further tracking.

Five situations require closure: two consecutive rounds yield only responses of the same kind; the object starts manipulating diagnostic rules; tracking increases exposure; information gains fall below structural disturbance; or the diagnostician can no longer distinguish object states from products of observation. These are procedural stopping conditions, not proof that the object is permanently unintelligible, nor that anyone adjusting behavior when questioned intends deception. Manipulation of diagnostic rules requires specific material; refusal of unsafe disclosure cannot be treated as malice. Two rounds of same-kind responses is this section's explicit rule, not an empirically calibrated optimal number of rounds for every study.

After closure, do not keep asking what the object ‘really is.’ Instead, give a conditional result: a certain response pattern can be confirmed under the current observational conditions; stronger judgments require external review or new external evidence with discriminatory power. Retain established local facts, while limiting the relevant classification where crucial material is insufficient. The strongest objection is that stopping could allow hidden problems to persist. The response is to retain the risks, evidence, and access to safe external review, rather than create new exposure through endless repeated questioning and then treat the resulting reactions as the object's essence.

Keep local and overall judgments, and current functioning and continuity of uptake, separate; unknown is not mixed.
Do not remove necessary support or create disturbances without authorization to test recovery capacity.
The two-round rule is a governance condition stipulated by the text, not a natural law or a universally optimal sample size.
A history of technical repair does not establish an S6 runtime classification for the organization concerned.

caseNotes.text: NASA Goddard's archive records that the SM4 mission serviced Hubble on May 11–24, 2009, repaired the previously failed STIS and ACS instruments, and installed equipment including batteries and gyroscopes. This official historical account supports discussion of specific repairs. It does not support classifying the telescope itself as a human collective at S6, or certifying uptake and governance throughout NASA solely on the basis of the mission's success.

argumentSteps: Check the applicable domain of GOV-07 using independent runtime evidence of the object and its state; stop applying it if the requirements are unmet.
Freeze the function, scale, window, and identity, and examine discovery, correction, recovery, and continuity of uptake separately.
Check similar appearances and counterevidence, distinguishing continuing support, dependence on a single point, and current effective operation.
Record lags, recurrence, margins, and loads separately in their respective units; causal claims and extrapolation require additional, proportionate evidence.
Expand only when new responses exhibit the specified structural changes. Stop recursion when any closure condition is triggered, and report a conditional pattern and the evidence needed next.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: even identical time units require an explicit chain of events
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a fault occurs at t=0 hours, is discovered at t=2, and the specified repair is completed at t=7. If discovery lag is defined as the interval from occurrence to discovery, and repair lag as the interval from discovery to completion, these are 2 hours and 5 hours respectively, with 7 hours elapsed overall. If recurrence separately occurs in 2 of 20 appropriate observation opportunities, the recurrence proportion is 2/20=10%. The 7 hours and 10% cannot be added to obtain a ‘repair speed.’ The first two durations can be combined into total elapsed time only if their start and end points are explicit and the intervals are contiguous.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The time points, counts, and set of opportunities are all stipulated, not observed repair data.
teachingExamples.boundary: Completing a repair does not automatically establish subsequent functioning or long-term absence of recurrence; the actual denominator and observation window require separate verification.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: recovery without withdrawing support
teachingExamples.text: A hypothetical collaborative team restores a service while backup resources continue to be supplied, and its successors have acquired the knowledge and authority to stop. The fact that support has not been withdrawn does not erase the recovery. Whether S6 is reached still requires checking autonomy across multiple positions, actual handover, and counterevidence. Another team's stability depends entirely on one leader secretly firefighting. An identical appearance does not justify the same prototype judgment.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The teams, recovery, and permissions are conditional assumptions; no organizational experiment was conducted.
teachingExamples.boundary: This example does not recommend withdrawing resources as a challenge experiment; verification must proceed under safe authorization.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: when to stop questioning
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a hypothetical investigation receives only defensive answers of the same kind in two consecutive rounds, with no new material about boundaries or channels; further questioning could expose members with little power. The conclusion should be limited to ‘this kind of response occurs under the current interview conditions.’ Retain the known risks and seek safe, independent material. Do not keep pressing until a story matching the diagnostician's expectations emerges.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The interviews and responses are a teaching construction, not actual research records.
teachingExamples.boundary: Defensive answers do not by themselves prove deception, repression, or failure to reach S6; external material is needed to distinguish these possibilities.

counterexamples.text: The device can recover automatically, so it has entered S6.
counterexamples.effect: A device falls outside the applicable domain of human intentional collectives. Its recovery can be established for a domain-specific task without receiving an S6 classification.

counterexamples.text: Resource support has not been withdrawn, so all recovery is fake.
counterexamples.effect: Continuing support does not automatically negate genuine recovery; autonomy, continuity, and dependence on a single point must be checked.

counterexamples.text: The more questions we ask, the better we understand the essence; refusal to answer also proves the diagnosis correct.
counterexamples.effect: Recursion can create exposure and observational artifacts. Judgment must be limited once closure conditions are met.

questionAnswers.question: Can an emotionally stable individual be assessed as S6 under GOV-07?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The applicable domain is limited to human intentional collectives and excludes individuals.

questionAnswers.question: How should discovery after 2 hours, repair over the following 5 hours, and 10% recurrence be recorded?
questionAnswers.answer: Record discovery at 2 hours, repair over 5 hours, total elapsed time of 7 hours, and a recurrence proportion of 10% separately; they cannot be added into a single speed.
questionAnswers.basis: Durations whose endpoints meet can be added; quantities with different dimensions cannot be directly added.

questionAnswers.question: What S6 evidence is still missing after a single successful repair?
questionAnswers.answer: Evidence of perception and correction across multiple positions, feedback write-back, recovery and renewal, and genuine continuity of uptake, together with scale, window, counterevidence, and independent runtime verification, among other requirements.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What should happen next if two consecutive rounds produce responses of the same kind and further tracing would increase exposure?
questionAnswers.answer: Stop recursion and report only the pattern confirmed under current conditions. Stronger judgments require safe external review or new evidence with discriminatory power.

16.8.title: 16.8 GOV-08 Malicious compliance and selective evidence auditing
16.8.lead: Forms, evidence chains, and appeals can all appear complete while only favorable material is allowed into the conclusion. This section examines whether these procedures are used selectively, rather than whether they have names. The risk rules first limit strong judgments; they do not convict people by counting checked boxes.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 3604–3611; source anchor section-16-8; short quotation: ‘Three and five items are procedural thresholds for initiating protection and review’ (translated from Chinese). The source slice for this topic is attached verbatim in source-slice.md, keeping the explanation separate from the source.

Malicious compliance means selectively completing forms, evidence chains, reviews, and appeals while manipulating sources, filtering weak signals, dressing up inaction, or laundering responsibility. It differs from openly refusing rules and must not be confused with ordinary incomplete material, inexperience, or reasonable protective confidentiality. Auditing requires material about actual sources, permissions, actions, and consequences. ‘Many formalities’ alone prove neither honesty nor malicious intent.

The ten signals must be checked individually. First, a single source: do apparently numerous documents all trace back to one supplier, without proportionate external material? Second, counterexamples downgraded to noise or emotion: are there verifiable reasons for excluding them, or are they deleted simply because they are unfavorable? Third, open assertions turned into labels: statements that were conditional and revisable become fixed judgments of a person's or object's nature. Fourth, appeals never change outcomes: investigate whether reasoned corrections of errors are institutionally blocked, rather than demanding a reversal on every appeal. Reasoned confirmation of a correct original decision can still make the appeal effective.

Fifth, independent parties controlled by the same chain of power: different identities do not ensure independence if funding, evaluation, promotion, or control relationships make independence difficult. Sixth, AI reports without original material and external verification: polished language and numerous citations do not fulfill evidentiary responsibilities; the availability of source documents and their consistency with claims still require checking. Seventh, diagnostic language used to justify inaction or avoidance of accountability: analysis becomes an excuse to delay authorized, necessary, feasible action on responsibility, rather than proportionate risk control. Conversely, not every reasoned suspension of high-risk action should be treated as malicious.

Eighth, potential fields, entropy increase, or stages used to dress up inaction: abstract inevitability erases responsibility conditions that could have been changed, without examining specific channels and constraints. Ninth, love, mission, the greater good, or expertise used to continue extracting from low-power actors: examine loads, exit, compensation, feedback, and permissions, rather than convicting on the basis of attractive words alone. Tenth, appellants relabeled as irrational because they appeal: the act of objecting is circularly treated as grounds to deny their credibility, creating a label that prevents correction. Whether their actual statements are inaccurate can still be examined, but ‘you object, so you are the problem’ cannot close off appeals.

At three or more signals, block strong judgments. At five or more, register a high risk of malicious compliance and output only risk registration, requests for external review, and protective probes. The second threshold incorporates the first threshold's restrictions; reaching five does not restore permission for strong assertions. Fewer than three signals is not a certificate of health either: one serious instance of fabricated evidence or missing permission may already suffice under another contract to block the corresponding output. Protective probes here must remain within authorized, safe, low-exposure boundaries; auditing cannot be used as a pretext for punishment, deception, or intrusion.

Three and five are procedural thresholds chosen by the text, not natural constants, and no calibration is supplied that converts counts into probabilities of malicious intent. Five signals does not mean 50% maliciousness, nor eight signals 80%. Signals may also depend on a common source: one chain of power controlling material and review can simultaneously produce a single source, nonindependent reviewers, and ineffective appeals. Registration must explain the factual grounds for each item and the relationships among them. It must neither count one repeated sentence as several signals nor assume that the ten signals are independent trials and multiply probabilities.

Triggering a threshold means only that continuing strong judgments is currently inappropriate and that protective review is needed; it does not establish that someone deliberately deceived others. Review must also consider the costs and contexts of false positives and false negatives. False positives may harm those audited and legitimate confidentiality; false negatives may allow disadvantaged people to remain exposed to harm. If thresholds need adjustment, the grounds should be explained through a public versioning procedure, rather than changing the number after seeing a case's outcome so that it just avoids triggering. External authorization and appeal protections cannot be arbitrarily canceled by a threshold.

An audited party cannot certify its own reviewer's independence. Auditors may use identity and relationship information supplied by that party, but judgments of independence also require verifiable material and an appropriate independent procedure. The strongest objection is that these signals are so broad that they treat all caution and professional confidentiality as malicious. The response is to record evidence for each signal, retain competing explanations, distinguish risk from intent, and narrow outputs according to dependencies, rather than label people by an overall impression. A genuine audit must allow its own signal judgments to be found mistaken and corrected, instead of becoming another tool of malicious compliance.

distinctions.leftText: Documents such as forms, reviews, and appeals exist.
distinctions.rightText: Unfavorable facts can enter the process, reasoned errors can be corrected, and consequences can be borne.

distinctions.leftText: Initiate protection, restrict outputs, and conduct review.
distinctions.rightTitle: Probability of malicious intent or a finding of guilt
distinctions.rightText: These require different evidence and procedures; counts cannot establish them automatically.

distinctions.leftText: Different checklist items may simultaneously have factual support.
distinctions.rightText: A list alone does not justify assuming independence or multiplying probabilities.

distinctions.leftTitle: A decision upheld on reasoned appeal
distinctions.leftText: After checking the material, a correct decision is maintained on sufficient grounds.
distinctions.rightText: Even valid evidence of error cannot change the outcome.

boundaries: Fewer than 3 signals does not confer a safety certificate; other evidence, permission, and protection checks can still independently block an output.
Neither 3 nor 5 signals is a natural constant or a calibrated risk probability.
Do not count unknowns as either no problem or a triggered signal; insufficient evidence can separately limit the corresponding strong judgment.
Dissent, withholding sensitive material from public disclosure, or a reasonable pause in action does not itself prove malicious intent.
This lesson has not scored any real actor on the ten signals or found deliberate deception.

caseLinks.title: An actual regulatory record: the appearance of compliance under test conditions

caseNotes.title: An actual regulatory record: the appearance of compliance under test conditions
caseNotes.text: On September 18, 2015, the EPA issued a press release about its notice of violation concerning Volkswagen. It described software in certain vehicles that detected official emissions tests and fully activated emissions controls only during testing; it also explained that the agencies pursued their investigation after outside research raised questions. This record illustrates how ‘performance within the test’ can diverge from normal operation and the role of external material.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: US EPA, press release of 2015-09-18
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Press release of 2015-09-18: opening paragraph; paragraph beginning As described in the NOV; paragraph beginning EPA and CARB uncovered
caseNotes.boundary: This records the investigation and allegations announced by the EPA at that time. It does not rescore Volkswagen using the ten signals, or infer individual subjective motives, all vehicle models, final adjudications, or current legal effects from that page.

argumentSteps: Examine the ten signals and original material individually; do not substitute the number of formalities or writing style for actual effects and relationships.
Record the facts, alternative explanations, and signal dependencies for each item; do not force unknowns into boxes marked as having occurred.
At 3 signals, block strong judgments; at 5, enter the stricter scope of risk outputs. Even below a threshold, check other stopping conditions.
Preserve the distinction between procedural risk and a finding of deliberate deception, and use independent review and safe protections.
If changing a threshold, explain the grounds through the versioning procedure and retain the original rule and the case's history.

teachingExamples.title: Formal construction: a threshold boundary is not a probability
teachingExamples.text: Define n as the number of distinct signals among the ten supported by proportionate material. Under this counting rule, n=2 does not trigger the three-signal check; n=3 and 4 block strong judgments; n=5 through 10 restrict outputs to the high-risk scope while continuing to block strong judgments. n=0 through 2 does not qualify a case for strong judgment, because object, evidence, authorization, and other checks must still be met. If 3 signals are correlated, the count can still trigger the rule, but one cannot claim that three independent pieces of evidence multiply the probability of malicious intent to a particular value.
teachingExamples.assumptions: n is an integer input for teaching, not an actual audit result, and no probability model has been fitted.
teachingExamples.boundary: Unknown signals and dependencies must be recorded separately; three copies concerning the same checklist item cannot be counted as three signals.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: many documents, one source
teachingExamples.text: An imagined AI report lists 20 links, but tracing them shows they all reproduce the same organization’s press release, with no original observations. Their common source and the gap in verification of original material can be recorded. The 20 links cannot alone count as independent evidence, nor do they automatically establish malicious intent by the writer. If the report’s task was only to study how that organization describes itself, these texts may still be useful within that limited task.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The report and number of links are constructed; no real AI product was audited.
teachingExamples.boundary: The risk significance of a single source depends on the specific task. Material from a common source may serve as discourse evidence, but cannot pose as external verification of facts.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: justified suspension and laundering of responsibility
teachingExamples.text: An imagined manager suspends punishment because evidence is insufficient and the action irreversible, and starts a time-limited independent inquiry: this is a defensible stop. Another arrangement repeatedly says, “The system is in a certain stage, so investigation is unnecessary,” and refuses an authorized inquiry into responsibility. That supplies a clue of inaction requiring further audit. Neither has imposed punishment yet, but their reasons, procedures, and consequences differ.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Both management situations are teaching assumptions, not decisions concerning real organizations or legal advice.
teachingExamples.boundary: Without material, wording alone cannot establish motives; risk registration does not authorize punishment either.

counterexamples.text: Checking five items establishes a 50% probability that the person responsible deliberately deceived others.
counterexamples.effect: The source provides no probability calibration, and a risk trigger is not a finding of intent.

counterexamples.text: Only two items were found, so all strong judgments may continue.
counterexamples.effect: Other evidence, protection, and authorization conditions may still block them.

counterexamples.text: An appeal that does not change the decision proves the appeal is a sham.
counterexamples.effect: A correct decision may be upheld with reasons; what matters is whether errors can actually be corrected.

questionAnswers.question: How do the procedural outputs differ at 4 and 5 signals?
questionAnswers.answer: Four items already block strong judgments. Five additionally require registration of high risk and limit outputs to risk registration, requests for external review, and protective probes; they do not restore strong judgments.

questionAnswers.question: How should three republications from the same source be counted?
questionAnswers.answer: They are not three independent signals. Record them according to the ten specific checks, trace their common source, and explain their dependencies.

questionAnswers.question: Is it enough for the audited party to designate someone in the same promotion chain and declare them independent?
questionAnswers.answer: No. The audited party cannot independently certify independence; verifiable relationships and appropriate independent procedures are needed.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: How should a three-signal threshold regarded as too strict be changed?
questionAnswers.answer: Provide reasons, revise publicly through the version procedure, and preserve the old rules. Do not temporarily relax the threshold for a case after seeing its outcome.

16.9.title: 16.9 GOV-09 AI Boundaries and the Non-Proof Status of Process Products
16.9.lead: An AI report may offer excellent arguments and help choose an option. But writing “verification completed” cannot make a nonexistent source real or turn unimplemented protection and repair into reality. The question is what actually grounds each conclusion.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3612–3621; source anchor section-16-9; short quotation translated from Chinese: “Process products are not proof of reality.” The source excerpt for this topic is separately reproduced verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and source text are kept separate.

This section allows AI to do substantive work: organize material and verify its identity; propose and compare mechanisms; formulate grounded, refutable judgments and criticism; recommend options under public goals and normative constraints; and draft institutions, plans, and commentary for deliberation. It does not require AI always to summarize or abstain. Analysis performed should be presented as a full, inspectable substantive argument: what is currently chosen, why, its costs, the strongest opposing case, and what conditions would change the choice. What is required here is verifiable reasoning and analytical results, not self-scoring or empty announcements of process in place of content.

AI must not fabricate sources or protective conditions. Even complete source titles, URLs, and citation formats require checking the object’s identity, version, and actual scope of support. “There is an appeal procedure” requires examination of accessibility and substantive review and correction capacity. Fluent prose cannot prove a commissioning party’s integrity, effective protection against retaliation, or real repair; internal scores and process completion cannot replace independent review and responsibility. AI can distinguish a source’s existence from its support for different propositions, but cannot end this verification by issuing its own certificate.

An analytical recommendation is not actual adoption, and drafting an institution does not mean an authorized actor has approved it or it has taken effect. High-risk real-world decisions and execution still require procedures for strong judgments, protection, normative choice, and authorization. AI cannot make such decisions independently or pass off “the process passed” as a decision by an authorized actor. Even when recommendation conditions hold, who may decide, how appeals work, and what is revocable require separate checks. When people’s rights or opportunities are affected, automatically generated conclusions must especially not be converted directly into action against them.

Task-evidence checks cover eight groups of material: original facts, testimony from affected positions, counterexamples, low-power feedback, external review, records of appeals changing outcomes, relationships of control over evidence, and AI’s own selection and rewriting of material. Original-fact checks trace initial objects and versions; testimony and low-power feedback supply positions invisible in central narratives; counterexamples test whether only positives were selected; external review checks actual independence; appeal records check whether errors can be changed; control relationships check who can delete, alter, or obstruct evidence; and AI selection and rewriting checks for omitted qualifications, correlation rewritten as causation, or unknown rewritten as negative.

Not every item applies equally to every task. For each, explain its relationship to the current conclusion, whether it is available, and what its absence limits. “Not applicable” needs a reason. For example, checking only whether a formal derivation is valid under explicit assumptions may not require real appeal cases; claiming that an institution is fair or feedback is safe may make those materials critical. Difficulty obtaining material does not make it inapplicable, and vulnerable people must not be forced into exposure to fill evidence gaps. Keep unknown, unobservable, and not applicable separate, narrowing the conclusion where necessary.

Missing material limits conclusions according to dependencies, rather than uniformly downgrading every output based on the number of missing fields. Missing key factual evidence prevents that factual finding; missing evidence distinguishing causes leaves competing explanations open; insufficient protection and review prevent certification of actual safety, consent, fairness, repair, or eligibility for high-impact adoption. Unaffected assessments of textual arguments, local factual judgments, and conditional recommendations under explicit premises may still hold separately. If a shared critical premise fails, several dependent conclusions may lose their grounds together, but explain the shared dependence rather than rejecting or approving everything on an overall impression.

Process products include fluent text, automated scores, internal stress tests, consistency matrices, validator passes, report counts, and complete tables. They may establish limited process facts, such as JSON satisfying structural constraints or a set of artificial tests returning no errors, but not real-world repair, consent, safety, or effectiveness. A validator can check only the rules and inputs supplied to it; passing is unsurprising when the rules omit actual risks. Conversely, a process defect does not automatically negate a fact supported by independent material.

The strongest objection is that these requirements would leave AI unable ever to advise. The response is to state a recommendation as a clear current choice under the available material, explaining its conditions, costs, opposing case, and revision points: derive what can be derived, verify what can be verified, and preserve boundaries where certification is unavailable. Trustworthy advice is not uncertainty-free; it does not hide uncertainty in fluent language. The value of AI-assisted analysis and authority for real-world execution can be judged separately, avoiding both overreach and abandonment of all grounded assistance merely because independent execution is unavailable.

distinctions.leftText: Provide a choice and reasons under the stated goals, premises, and material.
distinctions.rightText: Require authorized actors, normative procedures, and applicable protections.

distinctions.leftText: Fields, types, or particular procedural constraints are satisfied.
distinctions.rightText: Requires proportionate evidence about the object; form cannot validate itself.

distinctions.leftText: Blocks conclusions depending on that material.
distinctions.rightText: Unaffected derivations, textual assessments, and conditional recommendations may hold.

distinctions.leftText: The item is genuinely unrelated to the bounded task, and the reason is given.
distinctions.rightText: Inapplicability cannot be used to erase relevant risks.

boundaries: AI may offer grounded judgments, criticism, and recommendations, not just summaries; high-risk real-world decisions cannot be made independently.
Gaps in material and protection limit conclusions by dependence; a total count of gaps does not replace substantive judgment.
An appeal that upholds a correct decision may still be effective; do not demand a symbolic reversal to prove that appeals are useful.
Formal test results support only what was actually tested; artificial constructions must not be reported as real experiments.
This lesson has not verified the real-world safety of an AI system and offers no advice on specific litigation or high-impact action.

caseLinks.title: A real judicial record: fabricated cases in Mata v. Avianca

caseNotes.title: A real judicial record: fabricated cases in Mata v. Avianca
caseNotes.text: On June 22, 2023, the US District Court for the Southern District of New York recorded in its sanctions opinion in Mata v. Avianca that lawyers submitted AI-generated nonexistent cases and false quotations, and persisted after being challenged. Paragraph 6 of the Findings of Fact also records that the signatory checked style only and did not read the cited cases. The case makes concrete the distinction between reviewing prose style and verifying sources.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Mata v. Avianca，Opinion and Order on Sanctions，2023-06-22
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Opinion p1, opening paragraph; p4, Findings of Fact ¶6; p34, signature date. The document is hosted on the website of the US District Court for the District of Connecticut
caseNotes.boundary: The guide uses the court’s original opinion only for the historical findings above. It does not claim to have read all 43 pages or reexamined the case file, offers no current legal advice, and does not estimate AI’s overall error rate from one case.

argumentSteps: First specify the task, intended conclusion, and action use, rather than assuming that every AI output has the same strength.
Connect each of the eight material groups and AI selection and rewriting to the task, marking availability, absence, or reasoned inapplicability.
Limit conclusions according to factual, causal, protective, and authorization dependencies, preserving unaffected local arguments.
Give the current choice, key reasons, costs, strongest opposing case, and revision conditions, fully presenting the substantive analysis performed.
Separate process validation from real-world evidence; check the respective authority for recommendations, formal adoption, and high-risk execution.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: three conclusions in one report
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a report contains Q1, “The source’s second paragraph has an unstated premise”; Q2, “The new process caused accidents to decline”; and Q3, “The institution has effectively protected feedback providers.” Reading the source may support Q1. Before-and-after accident totals without a proportionate causal design do not directly support Q2. Without material on protection against retaliation and independent review, Q3 cannot be certified. Restrictions on Q2 and Q3 do not automatically erase Q1; a correct Q1 does not endorse the other two either.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The report, paragraphs, and indicators are teaching constructions; there are no real accident data.
teachingExamples.boundary: Each conclusion still needs its own accuracy check. This example does not prove that before-and-after comparisons are never useful; it limits a particular causal claim.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a correctly formatted false source
teachingExamples.text: An imagined JSON record contains correctly formatted source_url, title, and date fields, all of which pass validation. But if the link does not exist, or the page exists without the claimed fact, structural validation does not supply source authenticity or semantic support. The proper response is to retract the dependent factual assertion and complete verification, not add a declaration of “rigorous verification completed.”
teachingExamples.assumptions: The links and records are abstract constructions; no specific document that could be passed off as real has been fabricated.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual validation tools differ in capability; accurately state what the tool actually checked.

teachingExamples.title: Conditional-recommendation construction: it may be proposed but not declared adopted
teachingExamples.text: Under the public goal “reduce duplicate entry” and constraint “do not increase identity exposure,” AI may recommend first conducting an offline field-mapping assessment, listing costs and opposing arguments. If mapping is found to permit reidentification of rare roles, the recommendation should change. Without authorization, real sensitive data must not be uploaded, nor may the institution be said to have adopted the plan.
teachingExamples.assumptions: This is an example of a design recommendation; no assessment, upload, or institutional process change was performed.
teachingExamples.boundary: The feasibility and safety of the conditional recommendation still require proportionate material; protection cannot be described as already achieved.

counterexamples.text: The validator says pass, so all facts, consent, and repair hold.
counterexamples.effect: The validator covers only its actual rules and inputs; real-world conclusions require separate evidence.

counterexamples.text: There is no testimony from affected people, so even algebraic derivation under explicit assumptions cannot be discussed.
counterexamples.effect: Check the relationship between testimony and the specific conclusion. Formal validity can be judged independently; do not silence discussion by counting missing items.

counterexamples.text: AI cannot be responsible for execution, so it should not recommend any choice.
counterexamples.effect: The source allows grounded, refutable analytical recommendations; execution authority is checked separately.

questionAnswers.question: If only one of three conclusions has independent evidence, should all pass or all be rejected?
questionAnswers.answer: Judge separately by dependence: retain the proportionately supported conclusion and limit the others. If a shared premise fails, explain the extent of the consequences.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: How do we distinguish “the link exists” from “the fact has a source”?
questionAnswers.answer: Also check the page’s identity, version, and correspondence between specific passages and the claimed fact. Existence alone is not support.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why does “not applicable” require a reason?
questionAnswers.answer: To prevent difficult evidence collection, unknowns, or real risks from being disguised as irrelevance; reasons should come from the relationship between task and conclusion.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What must a current recommendation show at minimum?
questionAnswers.answer: Choice, key reasons, costs, strongest opposing case, and revision conditions; high-risk adoption also requires independent procedures and authorization.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Limit conclusions by dependence while retaining independently supported parts. Process products—scores, tables, validation—prove only what was actually checked. Real-world certification needs separate evidence: safety, consent, and repair cannot be self-certified by AI. Give an explicit choice and reasons, costs, opposing case, and revision conditions; high-risk execution needs a separate authority check. 16.10.title: 16.10 GOV-10 Six-Part Protection for Weak Signals
16.10.lead: Willingness to hear a complaint is only a beginning. Whether information providers can enter safely, who receives their information, whether they are punished afterward, and whether the issue actually changes rules all determine whether “being heard” can lead to “being protected.”
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3622–3639; original anchor section-16-10. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “Weak signals cannot depend solely on a diagnostician’s ‘willingness to listen.’” The source excerpt for this lesson is separately attached verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and original text are distinct.

Weak signals are indications easily overlooked by mainstream records, averages, or positions of power. This section does not treat low frequency, anonymity, emotional expression, or incomplete formatting as automatic grounds for deletion. An indication cannot directly produce a final conclusion, but can identify facts and risks requiring checking. Responsibility for protection cannot be placed entirely on the speaker either: requiring a standardized report, public identity, and personally borne consequences before declaring a willingness to listen makes precisely what most needs visibility disappear first.

WS1 requires anonymous or low-exposure entry: submitting facts need not first expose identity. Assess actual usability, indirect identification, and control of materials, not merely whether a form has an anonymous option. Anonymity makes content neither inherently credible nor automatically invalid; checking can continue through factual indications and low-exposure methods. Collectors must also avoid recording task-irrelevant information merely to confirm identity.

WS2 requires an independent recipient who can take up the signal, not merely routing it to the challenged power chain. Changing the recipient’s job title does not guarantee independence: check funding, evaluation, control, interests, and whether they have appropriate capability and authority. Independent uptake does not permit arbitrary expansion of disclosure; information must be handled according to need and authorization so low-power providers are not identified through transfer. Receiving a report and having authority to change an institution are connected but distinct roles.

WS3’s anti-retaliation register tracks loss of authority, isolation, stigmatization, punishment, and resource changes after feedback. A promise of “no retaliation” is not actual protection; subsequent windows must allow changes to be detected and proportionate review and remedies arranged. Temporal proximity between a change and feedback is a clue, not automatic proof of retaliatory causation. Competing explanations and safe evidence gathering are required, while incomplete causal identification cannot justify ignoring grounded protective risks. Registration must not become another exposure of sensitive information.

WS4 requires group-level calibration so overall satisfaction or average performance does not conceal deterioration among marginalized groups. Grouping must relate to affected positions and the task, attending to sample size, opportunities to participate, and missingness mechanisms. Overall improvement cannot declare everyone better off, nor may disaggregation reidentify small groups. No universal fairness metric or threshold is supplied here; required groupings and publicly disclosable granularity depend on proportionate materials and protective conditions.

WS5 requires delayed disclosure: when safety risks exist, protect the provider before discussing publication. Connected to 16.6, delay does not mean hiding risk records forever; appropriate review, responsibility, and conditions are required. Review at expiry does not automatically disclose identity either. Verified bounded conclusions or handling outcomes may be disclosed in layers while original sensitive materials remain protected. Emergency protection and factual determinations must both respect applicable authority, not cross safety boundaries in the name of good intentions.

WS6 requires visible actual changes to rules, resources, responsibilities, or authoritative records after a signal is adopted. Receipts, summaries, meetings, or statements of “taking this very seriously” cannot substitute for change; change numbers must bind real versions and content. Accepting a fact does not mean accepting every recommendation, nor must every signal change an institution. Reasoned nonadoption requires a retained proportionate explanation; a symbolic one-word change cannot manufacture the appearance of feedback. Established actual change still differs from final net benefit or complete repair, which require outcome evidence separately.

All six items must be registered individually. If any is missing, one may say only that weak-signal risks have been recognized, not generally that weak signals have been protected. Completed local work can still be described truthfully—for example, an entry channel exists or independent uptake has occurred—but cannot stand for the entire protection package. Records for all six are not a permanent safety guarantee beyond actual verification; operation and consequences must be checked. The strongest objection says small teams cannot manage six elaborate items. Proportionate, low-burden arrangements are possible, but scarce resources cannot cancel key protections or transfer form-filling burdens to feedback providers already in low-power positions.

distinctions.leftText: A personal attitude or intention to provide entry.
distinctions.rightText: All six responsibilities must be individually checkable, including subsequent consequences and write-back.

distinctions.leftText: An indication worth retaining and checking safely.
distinctions.rightText: Requires proportionate evidence; one indication cannot automatically settle the case.

distinctions.leftText: The aggregate indicator rises under stated weights and sample.
distinctions.rightText: Requires group-level checks; the whole cannot establish the result for every group.

distinctions.leftText: Rules, resources, responsibilities, or authoritative records actually change.
distinctions.rightText: Still require evidence of outcomes, competing explanations, and related matters.

boundaries: The six items cannot replace one another; an anonymous mailbox does not also supply independence, protection against retaliation, and write-back.
One missing item prevents certification of overall protection, but should not conceal other verified local work.
Retaining weak signals is not immediately reaching a final conclusion; protecting providers does not require prior proof of all causation.
Grouping and follow-up registration must avoid additional exposure; do not collect irrelevant private information in the name of safety verification.
Substantive write-back does not require every opinion to change the result, nor allow minor edits to conceal key gaps.

caseLinks.title: Actual channel description: ASRS alerting messages and authority to act

caseNotes.title: Actual channel description: ASRS alerting messages and authority to act
caseNotes.text: NASA ASRS’s Program Outputs page explains that reports of hazardous situations may lead to alerting messages to authorized parties for investigation and necessary corrective action. It also explicitly states that ASRS has no direct operational authority and must work through cooperation with others. This section adds a distinct observation: the website’s described alert-transfer mechanism does not prove that recipients completed institutional write-back.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: NASA ASRS, Program Outputs, checked 2026-10-14
caseNotes.sourceLocator: The Alerting Messages item under Program Outputs and the immediately following sentence stating that ASRS has no direct operational authority
caseNotes.boundary: The same system as in 16.6, but different original passages and arguments are used. This lesson did not audit all six conditions or obtain real rule changes or anti-retaliation records linked to particular alerts; a mechanism description is not effectiveness certification.

argumentSteps: Retain low-frequency, anonymous, emotional, or incomplete indications, distinguishing risk entry from final factual conclusions.
Check WS1 low-exposure entry, WS2 independent uptake, and WS3 follow-up anti-retaliation registration individually.
Check WS4 group-level changes, preventing aggregate indicators from concealing marginalized harm and preventing reidentification of small groups.
Check WS5 disclosure arrangements prioritizing safety and WS6 real write-back after adoption.
Refuse overall protection certification if any item is missing, while truthfully retaining local work completed and materials still needed.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical construction: a rising average with deterioration at the margins
teachingExamples.text: Assume a fixed 100 people on the same satisfaction scale from 0 to 100. Group A has 90 people whose mean rises from 70 to 80; group B has 10 whose mean falls from 60 to 40. The overall mean rises from (90×70+10×60)/100=69 to (90×80+10×40)/100=76: an increase of 7 points, while B falls by 20. Reporting only that 76 exceeds 69 misses the latter. The calculation demonstrates only the nonequivalence of averages and group-level results; it proves neither a real institution’s fairness nor causal harm to a group.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Groups, weights, scores, and complete observation are constructed assumptions; there is no real survey.
teachingExamples.boundary: Reality also requires comparable measurement, treatment of missingness, and grounds for grouping; publishing small samples may reidentify people. This example is not a universal metric recommendation.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: after anonymous entry
teachingExamples.text: An imagined organization provides an anonymous mailbox but forwards original messages, including identifying job details, to the person complained about; afterward, no one records changes in the feedback provider’s shifts or resources. “An anonymous entry is open” cannot certify all six protections. First check actual exposure, independence of uptake, and subsequent protection; do not keep forcing more affected people to submit real-name materials to complete forms.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The organization and incident are constructed, not allegations against a real organization.
teachingExamples.boundary: Whether role details are identifying depends on context; removing names cannot be assumed sufficient for safety.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: write-back is content, not a receipt
teachingExamples.text: An imagined member identifies an application rule that excludes those unable to attend at fixed times. After checking and adoption, there should be a verifiable new rule, usable alternative times, or corresponding responsibility arrangements. Merely sending “received” is not write-back. Even a changed rule cannot immediately establish that actual burdens disappeared; execution and subsequent materials from affected positions are still needed.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The member, rule, and change are teaching designs; no real institutional change was implemented.
teachingExamples.boundary: Real recommendations may be rejected after reasoned review; changes cannot be manufactured for counting purposes.

counterexamples.text: The provider is anonymous and highly emotional, so the indication need not be retained.
counterexamples.effect: Degree of identity disclosure and writing style do not automatically cancel factual-checking and protective responsibilities.

counterexamples.text: Overall satisfaction rose, so the small group’s decline need not be examined.
counterexamples.effect: Aggregate and group-level results are different propositions; deterioration at the margins cannot be hidden by an average.

counterexamples.text: Only anti-retaliation registration is missing from the six items, so all protection can still be called successful.
counterexamples.effect: Any missing item prevents overall protection certification; completed portions can be reported specifically.

questionAnswers.question: Why does the example’s overall average rise while group B deteriorates?
questionAnswers.answer: With fixed weights, A’s larger positive contribution masks B’s decline. The overall mean moves from 69 to 76 and B from 60 to 40; both can be true simultaneously.
questionAnswers.basis: Weighted-mean calculation and group differences.

questionAnswers.question: May an unconfirmed signal simply be deleted?
questionAnswers.answer: A signal cannot be deleted merely for being weak, anonymous, or emotional. Retain it as an indication and check it under safety and evidential conditions without immediately reaching a final conclusion.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: How should independent receipt with no write-back evidence yet be reported?
questionAnswers.answer: Truthfully report receipt and verified local measures, identify gaps such as WS6, and do not claim all six protections are complete.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does a rule update after adoption prove final repair?
questionAnswers.answer: It supports only the corresponding actual change; execution, burdens, and effects still require subsequent materials, without skipping levels.

16.11.title: 16.11 GOV-11 An intermediate path without institutional infrastructure
16.11.lead: Small teams, friends, and families may lack independent review and appeal bodies. Without those facilities, they should not pretend formal adjudication is complete; people can still record knowable facts, identify risks, and seek safer support without first risking themselves to prove who is absolutely wrong.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3640–3645; original anchor section-16-11. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “do not forcibly simulate institutions that do not exist.” The source excerpt for this lesson is separately attached verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and original text are distinct.

NO-INFRASTRUCTURE-PATH applies to relational settings lacking independent reviewers, stable appeals, and complete evidence chains. Families, intimate relationships, friendships, small teams, and temporary communities may involve ongoing harm, information control, dependency, and reputational or safety risks, but inclusion among these types does not mean every relationship involves suppression. First state which facilities are actually missing and which materials and risks exist; relationship labels cannot replace investigation.

The intermediate path rejects two extremes: inventing an institution by calling oneself or the same power chain within the relationship an independent adjudicator, and claiming that no facts can be recorded because formal review is impossible. Specific events, parties’ statements, and preservable existing materials may be recorded separately with sources and uncertainties marked. Recording is not closure, and a record’s existence does not automatically prove an explanation of all events or motives. If gathering evidence increases exposure, affected people should not have to risk danger to earn belief.

The permitted output is a protective open assertion with six components fully developed. Current materials state what is actually known now, its sources, and gaps; the continuing pattern of greatest concern states recurring indications and competing explanations; prohibited uses make clear that this judgment cannot punish or deprive; escalation signals identify new facts that would make protection or external checking more urgent; withdrawal signals identify materials that would limit, revise, or withdraw the current explanation; low-risk next steps identify bounded actions to consider under existing safety and authority. Openness is not license to say anything: it retains conditions for changing the judgment and ceilings on use.

The action goal shifts from proving who is wrong to reducing exposure, preserving records, restoring support, seeking outside perspectives, and observing subsequent signals. Low risk must be judged relative to the specific context: an apparently ordinary screenshot, inquiry, public request for verification, or contact with family and friends may be monitored or escalate risk. Do not give everyone the same action list, still less recommend manipulating the other person, secretly accessing accounts, or deliberately provoking conflict to obtain evidence. If necessary, first reduce the details collected by this analysis rather than turn the person into research material.

This path cannot be used for punishment, dossiers, eligibility, public characterizations, or resource deprivation. “Preserving records” must be read together with “dossiers” among prohibited uses: safely retaining factual indications is not putting unresolved explanations into formal records used for evaluation, disciplinary action, or eligibility. Otherwise the two statements may be misread as simultaneously requiring and forbidding records. Subsequent formal disposition requires appropriate independent materials, grounds of authority, norms, and procedures; a protective open assertion cannot be directly upgraded into adjudication.

An outside perspective may help distinguish information and patterns, but any friend does not automatically qualify as an independent reviewer. Their ties to both parties, capability, confidentiality, and conflicts of interest must be considered. Accessing support does not authorize the supporter to decide for the person, nor mean support-seeking requires immediate departure, direct confrontation, or public disclosure. Connected to 16.12: inability to exit is not consent; protection should expand future choices rather than impose idealized action demands.

The strongest objection worries that open assertions are too weak to prevent real harm; another worries they enable unverified labels to spread. Both risks require limits on use. One may explicitly identify current facts as concerning and prioritize safety support while refusing verdicts on motives or public characterizations. When new external materials support or refute the account, revise the specific pattern and next steps; factual portions still grounded need not be erased. The intermediate path neither replaces formal emergency protection or lawful procedures nor certifies their existence; it avoids concealing missing infrastructure behind a fictitious complete institution.

distinctions.leftText: Stable independent review, appeals, and similar arrangements are missing.
distinctions.rightText: Local facts and risks may still be safely recorded; institutional absence cannot erase them all.

distinctions.leftText: Specifies materials, patterns, ceilings on use, and conditions for changing the judgment.
distinctions.rightText: Fixes an unresolved explanation as a conclusion about a person; this path does not authorize it.

distinctions.leftText: Safely retaining knowable facts and indications.
distinctions.rightText: Using unresolved assertions as formal grounds for evaluation or deprivation: a prohibited use.

distinctions.leftText: Proceed in a bounded way according to specific exposure and permission conditions.
distinctions.rightText: Requiring screenshots, confrontation, or disclosure regardless of context may increase risk.

boundaries: The type of relationship does not establish ongoing harm; facts and interpretations must be distinguished using current materials.
The absence of formal review does not make all facts unrecordable, nor does it permit one to appoint oneself judge.
Protective open claims must not be used for punishment, formal personnel records, eligibility, public characterization, or deprivation of resources.
Do not require risky evidence collection, direct confrontation, or immediate exit; low risk must be assessed against actual safety conditions.
This lesson is textual research; it does not diagnose risks in, or give action instructions for, the reader’s or any real relationship.

caseNotes.title: A real support guide: consider safety before documenting
caseNotes.text: NNEDV Safety Net’s guide to documenting technology abuse states that existing materials may still be useful even if they do not meet best-practice documentation formats; it also warns that discovery of documentation may lead to escalation, so safety should come first. When listing possible methods, the guide also says that an item’s appearance on the list does not establish that it is happening in a particular reader’s situation.
