caseLinks.title: A real project announcement: LibreOffice’s new identity in 2010

caseNotes.title: A real project announcement: LibreOffice’s new identity in 2010
caseNotes.text: In its original announcement of September 28, 2010, The Document Foundation explained changes to the project structure and explicitly stated the LibreOffice name and that development would be coordinated by the foundation. This public record lets readers identify the relationship between the new project and its OpenOffice.org background, rather than infer unchanged commitments solely from a shared name.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: The Document Foundation announcement, 2010-09-28
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Announcement date; first body paragraph; paragraph beginning “Oracle”; paragraph beginning “The Foundation will coordinate”
caseNotes.boundary: The original announcement is a participant’s own account. It supports the facts of its public announcement and naming, not agreement by the entire community, effective subsequent independence, or the inevitable superiority of a fork over its predecessor. This lesson does not evaluate current software.

argumentSteps: Specify the product or service’s actual uses and affected positions, and list the eight retained capacities for correction and protection.
Check the status of templates, certification, AI, and independent investigations, preventing process products from being rewritten as empirical evidence.
Separate customer satisfaction, actual effectiveness, and protection of affected people; when material is insufficient, allow downgrading or stop delivering strong judgments.
Examine payer control over evidence and publication, preventing eligibility monopolies and weaponized uses.
For persistent core disagreement, establish a clear fork and disclose what is retained, abandoned, modified, and newly risky; do not evade responsibility through renaming.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: the customer is satisfied but the conclusion is unproven
teachingExamples.text: An imagined consultant delivers a report satisfying management, but all material comes from management and employee appeals cannot reach an independent recipient. Satisfaction may be recorded as that customer’s feedback; it cannot certify the report’s conclusions or employee protection. If the material only supports an account of management’s own statements, delivery should remain within that scope rather than manufacture a diagnosis because the customer demands a “clear conclusion.”
teachingExamples.assumptions: The consulting engagement and report are constructed and do not target a real institution.
teachingExamples.boundary: A single source can support facts about its own statements; it does not automatically become an independent investigation of every object concerned.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a button is not human review
teachingExamples.text: Imagined software places “human confirmation” beside an automated label, but the reviewer sees only a total score, cannot access the original grounds, and has no authority to withdraw it. Clicking does not establish substantive review. A verifiable design should specify material, capability, authority, and appeal-based correction before determining what the button actually represents.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The software and button are design counterexamples; they were neither deployed nor evaluated.
teachingExamples.boundary: Real procedures may divide labor, but that division must not leave critical verification responsibilities unfulfilled.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a fork description requires more than a new name
teachingExamples.text: An imagined fork B retains problem families G1 and G2, abandons an existing dissemination boundary, changes the ceiling of the term “diagnosis,” and introduces a risk of misuse of simplified scoring. These changes and corresponding usage limits should be disclosed individually, rather than merely saying “B is more advanced.” If an abandoned boundary concerns affected people’s safety, disclosure does not replace actual protection and authority.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The fork, modifications, and risks are teaching constructions, not an actual Xikari version release.
teachingExamples.boundary: No model comparison was performed; the example cannot establish that B is better than the original.

counterexamples.text: The customer paid and is satisfied, so the independent investigation succeeded.
counterexamples.effect: The paid experience does not establish independent evidence or valid investigative findings.

counterexamples.text: Adding a human-confirmation stamp to AI output makes it external review.
counterexamples.effect: Real material, relationships, capability, and corrective authority are required; a stamp does not supply the conditions.

counterexamples.text: A fork need not explain how original commitments have changed.
counterexamples.effect: It specifically must disclose retention, abandonment, modification, and new misuse risks.

questionAnswers.question: How can a lightweight tool remain honest?
questionAnswers.answer: Limit the actual task and judgment ceiling, retain necessary evidence, protection, and correction, and do not sell it as a complete diagnosis.

questionAnswers.question: Why can the payer not unilaterally determine every aspect of publication framing?
questionAnswers.answer: It may filter out unfavorable material and affected positions; independent verification, feedback, and corresponding governance conditions are needed.

questionAnswers.question: What risks arise when different frameworks share the same name?
questionAnswers.answer: Users may apply old evidence, authorization, or evaluations to new rules and be unable to identify the actual commitments.

questionAnswers.question: Does a transparent fork automatically gain external eligibility?
questionAnswers.answer: No. A version description provides transparency about identity and scope only; actual eligibility, protection, and authorization still need independent grounds.

16.18.title: 16.18 GOV-18 Exit from Power Capture of Open Assertions
16.18.lead: Once “this is our provisional view” is cut down to “this is what this person is,” the use has changed. An open assertion cannot gain permanent immunity because its original author once called it provisional. When it is found to be used for sanctions, exclusion, or resource deprivation, endorsement must explicitly stop, and records and consequences must be addressed.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3702–3707; source anchor section-16-18; short quotation translated from Chinese: “An open assertion is only a revisable target within uncertainty.” The source excerpt for this topic is separately reproduced verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and source text are kept separate.

An open assertion is a target revisable amid uncertainty and challengeable by material, not a strong conclusion covertly accomplished through weaker wording. Its openness requires preserving evidence boundaries, competing explanations, withdrawal conditions, and a ceiling on use together. Repeated citation adds no evidence; multiple reprints or repeated AI summaries may merely amplify one source. Observation over a period can have justified uses, but “observe first” must not become grounds for indefinitely restricting opportunities.

This section lists use shifts requiring exit: repeated citation becoming an established conclusion; entry into assessments, files, sanctions, eligibility, resource allocation, or public memory; use to suppress appeals; truncation into labels by media, organizations, or AI; prolonged exclusion and resource deprivation in the name of observation; or retention of the judgment while its withdrawal conditions disappear. These concern the actual power acquired by a judgment, not just whether its original wording was cautious. Using a provisional label to decide someone’s eligibility is still an act affecting them; the word “possibly” does not change its nature.

Exit here concerns an open assertion’s eligibility to serve as an improperly used basis and its position in dissemination; it does not declare that all related facts are nonexistent. State explicitly that it must no longer be used for the action concerned, and restate the known evidence scope, alternative explanations, and withdrawal conditions. Local facts with independent grounds may be retained within their original scope. If content errors are also found, they must be corrected or withdrawn too. Disqualification of use and factual truth are separate lines requiring separate handling.

Deleting or marking misused records must address specific records under the corresponding authority; it does not encourage covert destruction of evidence of responsibility. Visible misused labels need to stop circulating and being used, while historical action trails should be retained within safe, necessary, and compliant limits for accountability and repair. If records cannot be directly deleted, clear withdrawal labels, dependency links, and downstream notification may restrict continued use. Adding a note at the bottom of one’s own webpage while actual execution systems keep citing the claim is insufficient.

Where harm has occurred, proceed to repair, compensation, and examination of responsibility chains. Withdrawing a sentence does not automatically restore lost eligibility, resources, reputation, or support connections. Trace who took what action on which record, which effects remain, and how the corresponding authorized actors can remedy them. The framework can raise and delimit these responsibility questions, but its own interpretation cannot by itself adjudicate compensation, deprivation, or other real-world actions.

If misuse cannot be stopped, the framework must refuse endorsement. The refusal must be clear enough for readers to identify the specific assertion and prohibited uses; “I cannot control other people” cannot justify continuing to supply labels. At the same time, do not falsely claim that external systems have stopped, downstream records have been corrected, or harm has been repaired. A boundary is not an effect: declaring refusal to endorse is a position taken; actual removal still needs evidence.

The strongest objection is that any misunderstanding would require deletion of all open research, eventually making discussion impossible. The response is to distinguish ordinary corrigible discussion from the shifts into power-bearing uses specified here, stop improper eligibility according to specific dependencies, correct records, and retain grounded facts. Another objection assigns all responsibility to those repeating a claim, requiring no action by the original author. Those repeating it have their responsibility, but a framework discovering that its content is persistently used for suppression still cannot continue endorsing it. Both responsibilities can coexist; mutual deflection does not make them disappear.

16.19.title: 16.19 GOV-19 Version write-back and closed feedback loops
16.19.lead: “We changed it” requires asking where the change reached: authoritative text, calculations, software builds, actual operation, or affected people’s circumstances? Version numbers and hashes help locate changes but cannot replace checking these different endpoints.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3708–3719; original anchor section-16-19. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “The version log is not an appendix to release notes.” The source excerpt for this lesson is separately attached verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and original text are distinct.

The version log is the authoritative write-back object for counterexamples and governance decisions, not a promotional list of new features. Counterexamples, boundary contractions, downgrades, pauses, blocks, withdrawals, replacements, retirements, rollbacks, and remedies must all be recorded. Each entry contains event, time, responsible person, affected IDs, old/new states, evidence, counterexamples, textual consequences, process consequences, action-ceiling consequences, and downstream write-back. The point is to trace counterevidence to the conclusions, procedures, and permissible actions it actually changes, not merely store “feedback received” in an attachment.

Archiving counterexamples without effective review does not close a correction loop. An established counterexample should change affected text, processes, or action ceilings; an unestablished one may be rejected with reasons, retaining handling grounds and review paths. Symbolically adopting an irrelevant opinion to appear open is impermissible, as is treating every unchanged draft as failure. Grounded maintenance of a correct decision can be qualified review; if a decision changes without implementation, confirm only the changed decision, not repaired consequences.

A prolonged absence of actual feedback handling can trigger review of channel failure. An unchanged version log alone proves neither perfection nor failure; what matters is whether relevant materials required handling and received proportionate review. Correct logs through new entries without deleting old entries and failure trails. Rollback retains what happened and why a state was restored; it does not turn time back as though harm never occurred. Restoring files cannot automatically revive terminal-state eligibility either.

At runtime, VERSION-LOG must be parsed structurally and precisely bind the governance record_id, subject, source/target version, transition, old state, new state, and event type. A few apparently correct IDs in free text are insufficient: references must resolve to actual objects and point to the same log as reviews, objection effects, and downstream repairs. Logs for different topics or objects cannot be mixed merely because version numbers match.

Version numbers accept only canonical numeric versions. source_version must equal the schema_version of the framework currently being validated, and target_version must strictly increase. none, aliases, or fabricated versions cannot prove a chain merely by cross-referencing within one package. Numeric increase must also follow the chosen specification, not arbitrary string ordering or treating 1.10 as decimal 1.1. This text’s example illustrates only a teaching comparison with three fixed nonnegative integer components; actual rules remain determined by the corresponding structured contract.

applied requires at least one real change in text, process, or action ceilings, with distinct before_hash and after_hash locating actual write-back. Different hashes show only that corresponding bytes changed; they cannot independently prove correct revision, valid authorization, or real execution. A space change also alters a hash without necessarily providing the required semantic repair. Therefore check actual before/after content, change type, evidence, and responsibility; random strings or unsaved strings cannot impersonate authoritative file versions.

Text identity, theory version, structured-contract version, software version, and the version actually consumed at runtime are registered separately with resolvable correspondence. Renaming a theory or changing its major version neither automatically resets software versions nor proves migration of installed content. For example, documentation may state a new rule, build artifacts contain an old rule, and a running service load a different file; check all three separately rather than eliminate the distinction with a version poster. Skill versions also cannot be conflated with the identity of the theory being explained.

Separate five validation endpoints: text written back, engineering build completed, runtime consumption achieved, response performance qualified, and real task benefit. A successful build may not be deployed; deployment may not load new dependencies; loading does not guarantee correct use; a correct response does not prove practice occurred or net benefit exists. Report only actual completion and checkable scope at each step. Gaps in dependencies restrict corresponding downstream assertions without erasing confirmed earlier changes.

Endpoints must match the problem. Typo correction requires checking authoritative text and propagation; source-data correction also requires recalculating dependent values; unauthorized use must be traced to actual execution and remedies. If a system wrongly rejects someone, corrected documentation does not restore eligibility. If report figures are wrong, changing the database without updating cited charts leaves the corresponding correction incomplete. Logs and hashes provide location, not substitutes for semantic, propagation, and real-effect evidence.

The strongest objection worries that complete write-back chains overwhelm small changes. Set validation endpoints and necessary records according to consequences, rather than treating every typo as a real-world experiment; simplification must not leave serious authority overreach at release notes alone. Another objection notes that genuine correction may occur without logs. Independently evidenced local real-world facts can still hold; this section requires checkable eligibility for formal framework governance write-back, not treating record systems as the sole source of knowledge.

caseNotes.title: Actual software interface: Python separates language and implementation versions
caseNotes.text: Python’s official sys documentation separately describes sys.implementation.version and sys.version_info: the former is the current interpreter implementation’s version, while the latter is the Python language version it follows; sys.version also contains build and compiler information. This actual interface design shows that one runtime environment can have different version identities; one string cannot replace them all.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical and code construction: limits of version comparison and hashes
teachingExamples.text: Fix a teaching version format of three nonnegative integers: source=1.9.0 and target=1.10.0. Parsed as (1,9,0) and (1,10,0), the latter is strictly greater; string ordering may give the wrong direction. Also let text A be “Waiting ceiling: 10 days” and text B “Waiting ceiling: 5 days.” After actually saving both files, distinct SHA256 values can be calculated. This proves only that these teaching files differ, not that 5 days is reasonable, authorized, or adopted by a real organization.

16.20.title: 16.20 GOV-20 External Review Package and Public Release Gates
16.20.lead: Setting one’s own questions and answering them all correctly establishes only that internal checks were performed; bringing a judgment into public space also requires qualified, protected external reviewers who can disagree. Even permission to publish cannot directly justify disciplining others or reallocating their resources.
explanation: Original location: Chinese source lines 3720–3729; original anchor section-16-20; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Passing all gates yields only publishable and still produces no authorization to act.” A verbatim source excerpt for this topic is separately attached in source-slice.md, keeping explanation apart from the original.

Internal stress tests resemble a wind tunnel: misuse of terminology, erroneous paths, and internal contradictions can be deliberately introduced to check whether the framework detects them. But questions, environment, and scoring may all come from the same setup, so success does not establish real-world reliability, superiority to alternatives, or any external certification. The limit here concerns extrapolation of evidence, not denial of internal tests’ value in finding problems; promoting real-world superiority through internal pass rates exceeds this section’s explicit ceiling.

An external review package first needs to specify what is being reviewed. List each claim under review, use a traceability matrix to link claims to materials and reasoning, state which items are public and which are only candidates, and do not hide known defects. Then provide review questions and standards so different reviewers can make reasoned assessments of the same object. Reviewer identities and conflicts of interest, how feedback is written back, and how reviewers are protected are also parts of the package, not closing formalities. Defect records and revision trails mean reviewers need not continue the work solely on the author’s assurance that “everything has been fixed.”

The six review types have different responsibilities: source tracing checks whether the material chain holds; affected-position review checks what the judgment conceals when applied to relevant subjects; domain experts check domain knowledge and methods; a misuse red team seeks paths to labeling, overreach, or evasion of restrictions; public-language review checks for exaggeration and stigmatization in communication; and release-gate review checks whether this outward-facing strong judgment may be published. A person may have relevant expertise, but receiving one expert opinion does not establish coverage of all six responsibilities. Persistent absence of one type, especially affected-position review, itself blocks publication.

Here, “externality” means reviewers’ external independence from decision and authorization chains, not the economic sense of costs or benefits falling on third parties. Independence cannot be established by self-description as an “external expert.” Runtime registries must resolve reviewers, decision-making members, decision bodies, authorization issuers, authorization scopes, subjects, target versions, validity periods, and interest relationships. Different spellings of a name, institutional aliases, or seal appearances do not change the underlying identity and interest dependencies. Identity resolution does not establish absence of conflicts of interest either; relationships and specific roles must still be checked.

External approval must bind to the current governance record, subject, target version, transition, and dissent list. An old version may omit new risks, and approval for another subject or another transition may not cover the current change. applied may consume only external reviews whose decision is approved; pending, unresolved opinions, rejections, or internally self-signed materials cannot be translated into approval. This external approval serves a specific governance change and cannot be expanded into an indefinite pass across versions or objects.

The nine gates for public strong judgments are checked individually: traceability completeness asks whether each claim’s grounds can be found; source quality asks whether those grounds are reliable and applicable to the current claim; counterexample handling asks whether adverse materials were seriously addressed; affected positions asks whether relevant subjects’ dissent and circumstances entered; burden shifting asks whether benefits rely on uncounted costs borne by others; misuse red-teaming asks about foreseeable abuse paths; public language asks whether wording exceeds the evidence; external review asks whether independent and valid scrutiny has been completed; and the eight-part strong-judgment package asks whether the high-responsibility materials required by 13.5 are complete and hold. These nine are parallel necessary thresholds, not a total score whose components offset one another.

The state after all gates pass is called publishable: this strong judgment meets publication conditions, but this does not mean it has been published, its facts are eternally correct, all outsiders agree, or real-world action is authorized. New counterexamples after publication can still trigger revision or exit. Action involving others’ rights and interests must also enter applicable choice, permission, authorization, and responsibility chains; approval of a manuscript cannot be treated as approval of an action. Publication permission also applies only to the reviewed object, version, and wording, and cannot be transferred to unreviewed stronger wording.

The strongest opposing position worries that the gates will permanently silence small teams. The response is that this section addresses evidentiary and use responsibilities for outward-facing strong judgments, not a requirement that all everyday discussion complete the same institutional process. One may honestly retain candidate status, open questions, or lower-impact uses, but cannot rename a substantively high-impact judgment an ordinary opinion while keeping its original use. Another risk is making participation by affected positions decorative: their materials must have actual channels into dissent, review, and write-back, while reviewers are protected from retaliation for adverse opinions; names on a roster do not establish effective channels.

caseNotes.text: Nature’s public peer-review policy states that editors first screen manuscripts, then generally send potentially interesting ones to two or three reviewers; editors decide in light of the reviews and explicitly do not decide by vote counts or numerical rankings. Writing the review asks reviewers to identify parts they cannot assess fully; Anonymity says identities are generally not disclosed to authors or other reviewers unless reviewers volunteer to sign. These provide specific public text on review questions, decision-making roles, competence boundaries, and protective arrangements.

16.21.title: 16.21 GOV-21 Benign Demise of the Framework and Interfaces for Replacement
16.21.lead: A map can help people travel, but should not demand that every road bend to fit it. When a framework no longer helps judgment, preserving records, handing over responsibilities clearly, and letting a more suitable method take over matter more than adding terminology to prove its eternal usefulness.
explanation: Original location: Chinese source lines 3738–3745; original anchor section-16-21; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “The maturity of a framework lies not in explaining everything, but in knowing when to step aside.” A verbatim source excerpt for this topic is separately attached in source-slice.md, keeping explanation apart from the original.

Benign demise first means allowing concepts, modules, and empirical question families to exit core use, rather than destroying all texts or erasing the past. Old manuscripts with historical interpretive value may remain as archives, but their archival existence cannot keep them performing judgment responsibilities whose grounds have been lost. Local exit does not automatically refute all other modules either; trace specific dependencies to check which uses must stop and which independently supported uses may remain.

The five triggers target different self-preservation mechanisms. Persistent availability of a simpler, less harmful, more falsifiable alternative suggests that the original module may have lost relative value; concepts that increase comprehension costs without improving diagnostic capacity suggest terminology burdens without corresponding benefits; empirical question families that continually depend on exception patches in key domains suggest that scope and refutability need reassessment; users suppressing outside theories or real counterexamples show identity protection eroding correction; and framework-related identity, commercial, or power benefits exceeding gains in judgment quality suggest an interest structure that may reward preservation rather than improvement. A trigger is a reason to initiate grounded governance, not to destroy the entire framework automatically after one failure.

Comparing simplicity, lower unintended harm, and falsifiability requires explicit tasks, objects, and observation windows, not merely counting terms or examining promotion. A simple method that omits necessary safeguards may not cause less harm; a complex method that adds testable distinctions need not exit merely because it is complex. Exceptions sometimes arise from reasonable clarification of boundaries, but if every counterexample is excluded by temporary added conditions so that no possible material can touch the core, the problem is continual evasion of failure conditions.

The replacement interface must specify seven things: how far this framework can judge; where it begins to fail; what the successor method takes over; how the two cross-check; which records and unresolved harms are transferred; who bears responsibility for the transition; and when it takes effect. The first two delineate old boundaries, takeover scope defines new responsibilities, and cross-checking examines handoff gaps; records and harms prevent a restart from wiping the slate clean, while responsible persons and effective times prevent both sides saying it is not yet their turn. The interface cannot promise that the successor automatically solves all old problems; unknowns and unrepaired matters must also be explicitly transferred.

The six decisions are not a mandatory escalation chain. restrict limits uses; suspend pauses use pending review; compete compares methods under explicit conditions; replace substitutes a successor for relevant responsibilities; retire removes the old object from the corresponding current eligibility; handoff makes transfer responsibilities and materials explicit. The actual choice must meet specific evidence and governance conditions; competition cannot disguise indefinite delay of exit, nor can handoff be used to dump harms with no responsible party onto someone else. A terminal object’s successor identity and authorization also require checks under the relevant governance clauses; renaming does not restore old powers.

Creators, maintainers, and commercial beneficiaries may provide materials and explain costs and risks, but must not unilaterally veto replacement. This does not forbid them from speaking; it prevents their interests from becoming a permanent privilege to block exit. Correspondingly, another party cannot impose replacement beyond its authority merely by preference; valid procedures and authorization are required, and evidentiary responsibilities do not disappear because the original author has a conflict of interest. Unlimited addition of concepts to ensure the framework always holds is the self-preservation explicitly excluded here.

The general principle raises capability and responsibility together: stronger explanatory scope requires more readily triggerable withdrawal; greater communication power requires more protection for counterexamples from low-power positions; higher automation requires greater restraint against letting AI outputs take over human decisions directly. Supporting materials may help organize and compare, but sources, boundaries, dissent, and permissions still require checking. This does not claim every AI output lacks value; it rejects upgrading them into self-sufficient adjudication through scale and convenience.

Structural language must not swallow specific people and responsibilities. Stages, potential fields, entropy increase, or love may enter appropriate explanations, but identifiable decisions, harms, and remedies cannot be described as natural processes for which no one is responsible. An affected person’s actual resource interruption, blocked appeal, or unfinished repair does not disappear when the framework declares a benign exit. Whether the exit is benign depends on preserving traceable accountability and necessary support in the handoff, not merely an elegant announcement.

16.22.title: 16.22 GOV-22 Multi-Circle Complexity and Foresight Governance
16.22.lead: The more variables and the more elaborate the story, the more one must ask: what did it actually know in advance, how much did it add over a simple method, and who bore the errors? Foresight governance is not a collection of successful prophecies; it continually brings each forecast face to face with later verifiable outcomes.
explanation: Original location: Chinese source lines 3746–3751; original anchor section-16-22; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Publishing only successful cases is not permitted.” A verbatim source excerpt for this topic is separately attached in source-slice.md, keeping explanation apart from the original.

The five governance debts are outstanding responsibilities accumulated through capability expansion, not a directly summable numerical debt. Object debt comes from naming a circle and then treating it as an independent entity while overlooking boundary and interaction evidence; variable debt comes from automatically treating unexplained residuals as proof of a hidden variable’s existence; complexity debt comes from growing variables and paths without out-of-sample gain; calibration debt comes from publishing predictions without registering outcomes; power debt comes from predictions entering screening, surveillance, punishment, or manipulation. Each needs its own evidence and preset thresholds; a high overall model score cannot conceal power risks.

Object debt and variable debt are especially easy to manufacture through language. Naming a group’s similar responses as a circle does not establish unified intentions or stable boundaries; observing model residuals does not establish occurrence of a candidate mechanism explaining them. Additional materials must identify boundaries, coupling, alternative explanations, and testable variables; otherwise retain candidate or unknown status. Feeding an explanatory label directly into prediction and then using predictive results to establish the label’s reality creates a loop without independent testing.

Complexity debt must be tested through out-of-sample gain, not attractive training-set fit. Out-of-sample materials used repeatedly for tuning cannot still be passed off as unseen data; information obtained after the input cutoff certainly cannot be backfilled as prior knowledge. Comparisons should use the same target, available information, observation window, and preset metrics, and include simple baselines. A baseline must not be a deliberate straw man; it should represent a reasonable simple method available for the task. Without added benefits from the complex model, more parameters and terminology cannot prove value by themselves.

Calibration concerns the correspondence between stated probabilities and observable outcomes—for example, whether outcome frequencies across repeated events assigned similar probabilities match those expressions. It is neither picking a few correctly guessed events nor the entirety of prediction quality. The Brier mean squared loss below is affected by several performance factors; a small-sample score cannot directly establish long-term calibration. The original requires continuous outcome registration so deteriorating calibration can be detected, rather than promotion reporting only hits.

The forecast registry must retain successes, failures, unresolved cases, invalidated targets, and unevaluable cases. Success and failure should be judged by preset targets and evaluation rules; unresolved means the observation window or outcome has not yet arrived; target invalidation means the originally registered evaluation object or conditions no longer hold; unevaluable means relevant evidence or assessment conditions are insufficient. The last three must neither be silently deleted nor forced into success for an attractive denominator. Metric reports must state which records are scorable, which are excluded, and why, while displaying the complete registration scope.

External reviewers should be able to recheck model versions, input cutoffs, simple baselines, metrics, and outcome write-back. The version states which rules generated the forecast; the input cutoff prevents post hoc information from masquerading as prior knowledge; the baseline constrains whether complexity adds gain; metrics limit cherry-picking favorable evaluation methods; outcome write-back subjects each declaration to later testing. Reasonable updating is allowed, but new information, models, and predictions should have new records rather than overwrite the original prediction to erase failure.

If any debt exceeds its preset threshold, the model should be narrowed, outputs downgraded, high-impact uses paused, or the relevant module retired. Long-term calibration deterioration, errors concentrated across groups, complex models no longer outperforming baselines, or results continually depending on post hoc variables automatically downgrade claims of foresight capability. This automatic downgrading is the framework’s governance requirement, not an already implemented software feature, and does not authorize real-world punishment. Thresholds should be set before results are seen to avoid changing evaluation scales after failure.

Concentration of errors across groups reveals how averages may conceal the positions bearing costs. Even if overall performance improves, groups suffering more misjudgments still require disaggregated materials, sufficient samples, and impact assessment; totals alone are insufficient. Prediction accuracy and justified use are also separate: accurately estimating what someone will do does not authorize surveillance, manipulation, or punishment. High scores cannot replace either error governance or power governance.

The strongest opposing position argues that openly retaining failures makes a model look worse than competitors reporting only successes. This is precisely why shared transparent registration and comparison conditions are needed; deleting failures undermines the testability of capability claims. Another objection says every unevaluable case should count as failure for rigor, but this too fails: rigor is not fabrication of known outcomes. Separately show the scale and reasons for inability to evaluate, downgrading capability claims where necessary rather than forcing unknown facts to zero.

caseLinks.title: Actual methodological documentation: warnings about data leakage and simple baselines

caseNotes.title: Actual methodological documentation: warnings about data leakage and simple baselines
caseNotes.text: Section 12.2 of scikit-learn's official documentation defines using information unavailable at prediction time in model building as data leakage and notes that it leads to overly optimistic performance estimates. Section 3.4.8 introduces simple DummyClassifier strategies as a basic check for comparing complex estimators. Citing the evaluation arrangements in actual documentation shows that the time when inputs become available and comparison with a baseline can be made concrete.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Official scikit-learn documentation, page marked 1.9.1, accessed 2026-10-14
caseNotes.sourceLocator: First three paragraphs of Common pitfalls §12.2; also the opening and strategy list in model_evaluation §3.4.8
caseNotes.boundary: Only methodological documentation was checked. Its simulated examples are not treated as historical observations, and no claim is made to have run them or validated any actual model; this lesson's numerical example is independently constructed.

argumentSteps: Register evidence and prior thresholds separately for five kinds of debt: object, variable, complexity, calibration, and power.
Fix the model version, input cutoff, reasonable simple baseline, and evaluation metric, avoiding the intrusion of hindsight information into prospective predictions.
Retain every prediction as success, failure, unresolved, target invalidated, or unevaluable, with its respective grounds.
Compare out-of-sample performance under the same evaluation conditions, checking long-term changes and error distributions across groups.
Once downgrade conditions are met, restrict the corresponding capability claims and uses; complexity, averages, or individual hits cannot maintain eligibility for high-impact use.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: a complex model loses to a constant baseline
teachingExamples.text: Let the outcomes of four registered binary events be 0, 0, 1, 1. The complex model's prior probabilities are 0.8, 0.2, 0.8, 0.2; the simple baseline always reports 0.5. Use binary Brier loss L=Σ(p−y)²/4, where lower is better. The complex model's four squared errors are 0.64, 0.04, 0.04, 0.64, giving L=1.36/4=0.34; all four baseline errors are 0.25, giving L=0.25. Only for these constructed records and this metric is the complex model worse by 0.09.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All four data points and model names are teaching constructions; probabilities are fixed before outcomes; every event is evaluable and equally weighted.
teachingExamples.boundary: This establishes neither the uselessness of actual complex models, statistical significance, nor long-term calibration; the binary definition does not automatically match the scaling of multiclass software metrics.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: registering everything does not mean everything can be scored
teachingExamples.text: Imagine five forecasts, one each marked success, failure, unresolved, target invalidated, and unevaluable. Show all five and their reasons. If only the first two currently meet scoring conditions, state that two rather than five are scorable; do not display only the single success and claim every forecast was correct.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Status assignments are purely hypothetical for teaching, not a measured success rate.
teachingExamples.boundary: Failure and target invalidation must be distinguished through prior definitions and actual material, not arbitrarily reclassified afterward.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: hindsight variables undermine eligibility as foresight
teachingExamples.text: Imagine predicting at the start of a month whether a project will finish by month-end, while using the month-end acceptance conclusion as an input. Even a perfectly correct recalculation merely organizes results using an already known answer; it cannot count as foresight at the month's start. The correct handling preserves the original input cutoff and prediction and adds a record explaining subsequent information, rather than overwriting the old inputs.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The project and dates are constructed; no actual organizational data is used.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not deny the independent use of retrospective explanation; it only prevents it from masquerading as prior prediction.

counterexamples.text: The model residual is large, so some latent circle must exist.
counterexamples.effect: Residuals show only that the current explanation lacks coverage; specific variables and objects remain candidates.

counterexamples.text: Publishing only ten correct predictions suffices to evaluate foresight capability.
counterexamples.effect: Without a complete registry of failures and other states, selective presentation and the actual denominator cannot be identified.

counterexamples.text: The overall score is higher, so concentrated errors against a minority group can be ignored.
counterexamples.effect: Average performance cannot offset where errors and burdens concentrate; the corresponding governance review should be triggered.

16.23.title: 16.23 GOV-23 Governance of Personality, Privacy, and Automation Overreach
16.23.lead: Someone clicking confirmation on an interface does not mean they genuinely understand, have enough time, or can prevent an error. Once personality material and AI advice enter a decision chain, material identity, privacy uses, people's actual control capabilities, and subsequent correction must be examined together.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 3752–3759; source anchor section-16-23; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “A single click on the interface is not enough.” An exact source excerpt is separately attached in source-slice.md; explanation and source text remain separate.

Personality hypotheses are material with high misuse risk because explanations of local behavior can easily become enduring, cross-context labels of a person's essence. This section requires checking collection purpose, authorization, privacy level, permitted uses, cross-circle dissemination, appeals by the person concerned, deletion or correction, model version, and downstream effects in turn. Material originally collected for reflection on one collaboration is not automatically usable for hiring screening, public rankings, or risk labels in other circles. Purpose, authority, and recipients must be specific; “internal use” cannot cover everything indefinitely.

This framework prohibits using personality hypotheses for clinical diagnosis, judgments of personality essence, discriminatory screening, or unauthorized risk scoring, and prohibits treating silence as evidence. Silence may reflect safety concerns, pressure, lack of time, a missing entry point, or unwillingness to expose privacy; it cannot establish personality, admission of fault, or consent. The restriction concerns uses of this framework and its material. It makes no clinical judgment about anyone here and does not deny qualified professional services' duties within their own authority and evidentiary standards.

AI may propose and compare candidate variables and paths, check material identities, form refutable judgments, and give recommendations under public normative premises. Each capability has limits: candidates still need external material; identity checks do not establish content truth; refutable judgments must preserve failure conditions; normative recommendations must explain the value premises they depend on. AI cannot certify reality by generating another explanation of its own, diagnose personality, decide others' values, or issue authority on its own. Multiple models repeating the same fictional source are still not independent verification.

Three kinds of identity escalation must be blocked and audited: candidate becoming observed disguises a mechanism awaiting verification as observation; simulated becoming a real event treats a teaching example or simulation as something that happened; a foresight result becoming authorization converts descriptive capability into authority to act. Audit records should state where this occurred, which dependent outputs are affected, and the handling status, while respecting minimum necessity and privacy boundaries. Logging must not cause unlimited further copying of sensitive personality material. Blocking must follow dependencies; merely changing a displayed label while continuing the same downstream actions is insufficient.

The first condition for effective human review is visibility and comprehensibility: evidence, counterexamples, and uncertainty must be visible to reviewers, rather than only a score or green button. The second is capability and resources: relevant knowledge and skills, time available before action, and a manageable workload. The third is actual power: the ability to refuse, modify, and pause, with those signals reaching the actuator in time to change the action. Signatures, training records, or job titles support only limited conditions and cannot independently establish that review as a whole is effective.

Time must be assessed within the window before the action occurs. If a system executes instantly and review comments reach the backend only afterward, this may support retrospective checking but does not establish prior human control. If one person must handle many complex cases in an extremely short time, even a formal refusal button may provide no practically usable capability. System design, managed workload, information interfaces, and transmission of authority jointly determine oversight; failure must not be blamed entirely on the person who clicks last.

Oversight effectiveness requires observing four things together: whether correct recommendations are appropriately adopted, incorrect recommendations are blocked, problems the system did not flag are discovered, and affected people can correct results. Looking only at override rates can mislead in opposite directions: rejecting everything may discard correct recommendations too, while following everything may pass errors through. Reasonably retaining correct results can also be effective; frequent reversals are not themselves a quality metric. Moreover, even a correct final result leaves questions about missed unflagged risks and blocked appeals.

For narrow actions faster than case-by-case human judgment, machine-checkable constraints and least privilege may be studied, but this is only a research and design direction, not a declaration here that automation is safe. Specify what machine rules test and omit, who chooses the objectives, when anomalies are escalated, and who can stop the system and bear responsibility for remedy. Small actions in a long chain can still produce systemic high impact, so narrow permissions cannot be separated from overall objectives, cumulative effects, and the responsibility chain.

The strongest objection is that having a human involved should permit continued operation, or automation becomes impossible. The response is that human presence matters only when control conditions substantively hold; nominal oversight creates false reassurance. Another objection demands a human click for every machine action, which may also be unsuitable for fast, narrow operations. A more appropriate discussion designs verifiable constraints, anomaly takeover, and clear responsibilities according to risk, rather than choosing between responsibility-free full automation and ceremonial clicks at every step.

caseLinks.title: Actual governance guidance: NIST explicitly distinguishes human–AI roles and oversight responsibilities

caseNotes.title: Actual governance guidance: NIST explicitly distinguishes human–AI roles and oversight responsibilities
caseNotes.text: GOVERN 3.2 in the NIST AI RMF Playbook calls for defining and distinguishing human–AI configurations and oversight responsibilities. Suggested Actions lists competency standards, training, risk-information tracking, and transparency; Transparency and Documentation asks whether personnel have skills, training, resources, and domain knowledge. GOVERN 2.3 also assigns responsibility for AI risk decisions to organizational leadership. This provides concrete guidance that does not place all responsibility on endpoint operators.

argumentSteps: First register personality hypotheses as high-risk material, specifying purpose, authorization, privacy, use, dissemination, appeals and correction, version, and downstream effects.
Keep candidate, observed, simulated, real, and authorized identities separate; when escalation occurs, block dependent operations and retain the necessary audit trail.
Check what reviewers can see and understand, how much time they have before action, and their actual workload.
Verify that refusal, modification, and pause signals reach the actuator within the corresponding window and change the action.

Separately evaluate appropriate adoption, error blocking, discovery of unflagged problems, and correction by affected people; fast, narrow actions still require responsibilities for objectives, omissions, takeover, and remedy.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: escalation of a candidate label
teachingExamples.text: Imagine AI labels “a possible lack of clarity in handovers” as candidate, but an interface conversion writes “members observed to be unreliable” and sends it to a scorer. This both turns a candidate into observation and converts an event explanation into a personality judgment. Block dependent actions and retain the necessary correction trail; merely lowering the score is insufficient.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The text and scorer are entirely constructed, with no real person involved.
teachingExamples.boundary: This must not be used to create personality profiles or actual risk scores for anyone.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: more overrides need not be better
teachingExamples.text: Suppose ten recommendations contain eight correct and two incorrect ones. Reviewer A rejects all ten, overriding ten but also rejecting eight correct recommendations; B retains the eight correct ones and blocks the two incorrect ones, overriding two while doing better on these two dimensions. This alone still does not tell us whether either reviewer can discover unflagged problems or enable affected people to correct outcomes.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Correctness, recommendation counts, and review behavior are teaching assumptions; there are no actual participants.
teachingExamples.boundary: The example does not estimate actual oversight effectiveness; the latter two capabilities remain unknown.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a button that cannot reach the actuator
teachingExamples.text: Imagine a system executes immediately after submission. Ten minutes later the reviewer sees complete evidence and clicks pause, but the interface only logs it and sends no signal to the actuator. Even with an available button and correct review reasons, prior control of the action has not been achieved. Check the control channel that actually takes effect and subsequent remedies.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The duration and system are constructed.
teachingExamples.boundary: No real system was operated or paused; specific designs should be assessed according to risks and permissions.

counterexamples.text: If the person does not respond to the label, they have tacitly accepted it.
counterexamples.effect: Silence cannot serve as personality evidence or authorization; safety, access routes, and permitted uses must be checked.

counterexamples.text: A staff member clicks on every result, so human oversight must be effective.
counterexamples.effect: Visible evidence, ability, time, a reasonable workload, and actual authority to change actions are also required.

counterexamples.text: A zero override rate means the system is reliable; a high override rate means review is rigorous.
counterexamples.effect: Neither alone evaluates oversight. Check appropriate acceptance, interception of errors, detection of unflagged problems, and correction through appeals.

16.24.title: 16.24 GOV-24 Model degradation, retirement, and replacement
16.24.lead: Shortening a long text and incorporating candidates into a formal text can be real changes without making judgment easier for readers or genuinely improving work. Deciding whether to retain a model requires fair comparison of quality and all burdens, and a clear handover of responsibilities and unresolved matters when it is retired.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 3760–3767; source anchor section-16-24; short quotation: ‘Line breaks, character counts, and file counts can be verified, but cannot substitute for measuring readers' costs or work outcomes’ (translated from Chinese). The source slice for this topic is attached verbatim in source-slice.md, keeping the explanation separate from the source.

This section continues the replacement interface in 16.21, focusing more closely on comparison and retirement. If a simpler method consistently performs better in explanation, foresight, protection, and accessibility, hand over rather than defend the existing framework. Consistently better performance requires actual comparison; a single convenient use or a preference for brevity does not establish it. Accessibility also means more than short text: it includes whether different users can obtain material, understand it, and exercise the relevant routes for correction.

On retirement, cases, contracts, failure records, and appeals must be handed over through an interface. Preserve necessary source chains, responsibility records, and remedies for harm; stop using the retired model for new decisions; and publicly distinguish conclusions that remain valid, have been downgraded, or cannot be transferred. The validity of old conclusions depends on their original evidence and versions; retirement does not automatically nullify them all. Nor can old conclusions be migrated wholesale to a successor model and falsely described as revalidated. Transfers involving contracts and actual responsibilities still require applicable permissions; this lesson does not terminate or amend any contract on anyone's behalf.

Comparison first fixes the task, material, input cutoff, resources, and evaluation method. Different tasks may mean the two methods answer different questions; different material may let additional information masquerade as a methodological advantage; different cutoffs may let hindsight masquerade as foresight; different resources may hide differences in time and labor; and choosing the evaluation method afterward may favor a particular result. A reasonable comparison need not mechanically equalize every cost, but must disclose conditions, control or analyze differences, and limit the attributions that can be made.

Comparators must include at least sufficiently strong domain methods and accurate references back to the source. Domain methods should represent genuinely available competitive options for the task, not deliberately weak methods chosen to flatter the framework. Accurate source references help examine what additional value an explanation offers over direct, faithful presentation of the original material. If it merely restates the same information in different terminology while making the basis harder for readers to locate, its added burden cannot be ignored. The actual strength of comparators still requires domain evidence, not an author's declaration of fairness.

Assess judgment quality and total burden separately. Misjudgment means making an inappropriate judgment; omission means failing to recognize a problem that should have been recognized; unjustified abstention means retreating without reason when the material and task permit a reasonable answer. Also examine time, disclosure, and maintenance labor. Disclosure burdens concern how much information the method forces users to supply and who bears the risks. Maintenance labor includes actual work such as updates, corrections, migration, explanation, and training. Without reasonable weights and units specified beforehand, these dimensions should not be compressed into an arbitrary total score that conceals regressions.

Incorporating a candidate into the text establishes only editorial adoption. Whether that adoption makes judgments more accurate, reduces unwarranted harm, or improves usability requires actual comparison. If several candidates from the same source share one modification, its benefit cannot be counted repeatedly by candidate count. For example, if five suggestions identify the same typo, correcting one location is one modification, not five independent work benefits; a change's positive effect cannot be multiplied by its citation count either. The number of candidates covered may be a separate description, but must remain distinct from independent changes and effects.

Line breaks, character counts, and file counts are verifiable attributes of an artifact; readers' costs and work outcomes concern task completion, misunderstandings, time, support, and actual consequences. Fewer characters sometimes improve clarity but sometimes remove important restrictions and force extra searching. Fewer files sometimes improve findability but sometimes bury crucial material in a giant document. Relationships between these two kinds of measure can be studied, but equivalence cannot be assumed. Even a complete file structure for this lesson does not establish verified teaching outcomes for real readers.

Without actual comparison, none of three conclusions can be claimed: the framework is superior to alternatives, the two have been proved equivalent, or the framework has been proved useless. Lack of evidence of superiority is not evidence of equivalence or ineffectiveness. Existing historical comparisons should retain their actual versions, tasks, and denominators including failures. Local improvements can be established, but regressions on other dimensions, nondelivery, and failures cannot disappear; the successfully delivered subset cannot be used as the denominator for all tasks.

When theory, software, and material change together, results can evaluate that combination, but the whole difference cannot be attributed to one theoretical sentence or one form of packaging. Identifying separate contributions requires appropriate controls, ablations, or another suitable identification design, together with an account of interactions. If contributions cannot be separated, honestly reporting the combination's result is more accurate than attributing every improvement to the framework's identity. The strongest objection is that such caution impedes action. In fact, comparison can support bounded, reversible choices: the strength of conclusions need only match the material, without first inventing precise causal attribution.

distinctions.rightText: These involve independent changes, task outcomes, and human burdens, and cannot be directly converted from counts.

distinctions.leftText: Strong comparative conclusions cannot be supported.
distinctions.rightTitle: Equivalence or uselessness has been proved
distinctions.rightText: These also require corresponding material and cannot follow from lack of evidence.

distinctions.leftText: An overall result obtained when theory, software, and material change together.
distinctions.rightTitle: The causal contribution of a single factor
distinctions.rightText: This requires controls or an appropriate identification design; it cannot all be attributed to one theoretical sentence.

distinctions.leftText: Preserve sources, responsibilities, and the status of original conclusions.
distinctions.rightText: The old model has lost eligibility for this use; the archive's existence does not authorize continued use.

boundaries: Being simpler and consistently better requires explicit comparison; brevity, fewer files, or convenient use does not directly establish it.
Protection and accessibility cannot be replaced by one speed metric.
Historical comparisons must preserve actual versions, tasks, and denominators including failures; nondeliveries cannot be erased from the sample.
Retirement does not automatically delete old facts or complete remedies for harm, and a successor cannot inherit all conclusions without verification.
This lesson has not conducted a real reader study, a model comparison experiment, or a contract handover.

Why can B's 7/8 in the numerical example not directly outrank A's 8/10?
Does cutting the character count in half prove that readers save half their time?

caseLinks.title: An actual benchmarking regime: MLPerf distinguishes comparative scope and conditions

caseNotes.title: An actual benchmarking regime: MLPerf distinguishes comparative scope and conditions
caseNotes.text: The official MLCommons explanation of MLPerf Inference Datacenter defines benchmarks through datasets and quality targets. The Closed division requires the same model as the reference implementation for comparable comparisons, while the Open division permits different models or retraining. The page also states that published results may be modified or invalidated and provides a change record. It illustrates the need to specify comparison conditions and result status, rather than using one score to compare all systems indiscriminately.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Official MLCommons MLPerf Inference Datacenter page; accessed on 2026-10-14
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Opening paragraph of Benchmarks; both items under Divisions; the paragraph in Results beginning Published results are sometimes modified…
caseNotes.boundary: Only the official explanation of the benchmarking regime was checked. No particular submitted scores were read, no benchmark was run, and no system was certified. This benchmark also does not cover all the human disclosure and maintenance burdens discussed in this section.

argumentSteps: Fix the task, material, input cutoff, resources, and evaluation method; choose sufficiently strong domain methods and accurate source references as comparators.
Record misjudgments, omissions, unjustified abstentions, time, disclosure, and maintenance labor separately, preserving all tasks and denominators including failures.

Distinguish editorial adoption, independent modifications, and actual effects; avoid repeatedly counting benefits from candidates sharing a source or using file attributes instead of measuring readers' costs.
If theory, software, and material change together, register only the combination's performance; without an identification design, do not credit any single component.

When a consistently better alternative appears, hand over through the interface and stop using the old model for new decisions; disclose valid, downgraded, and nontransferable conclusions and unresolved responsibilities.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: candidates sharing a source cannot yield repeatedly counted benefits
teachingExamples.text: Suppose five hypothetical suggestions all originate from the same source and identify a missing qualification in the same sentence, and an editor adds it once. Register five candidates and one independent modification; do not count five independent improvements, let alone announce a fivefold increase in work outcomes.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The five candidates and the modification are stipulated for teaching.
teachingExamples.boundary: The modification may be useful, but its actual effect size has not been measured.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: local improvement and the full denominator
teachingExamples.text: Suppose two hypothetical methods are each assigned ten tasks. A delivers all ten, with eight meeting the prespecified correctness standard. B delivers eight, of which seven are correct, with two others undelivered. B's rate in its delivered subset is 7/8, but correct delivery over all tasks is 7/10, while A's is 8/10. Preserve both delivery rate and quality among delivered tasks; comparing 7/8 directly with 8/10 cannot establish that B is better overall.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Tasks and correctness judgments are constructed; all tasks have equal weight. Nondelivery explicitly does not count as correct delivery, but no inference is made about the truth or falsity of undelivered content.
teachingExamples.boundary: Statistical significance cannot be inferred from this small sample; time, disclosure, maintenance, and other dimensions remain unevaluated.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: combined changes cannot support separate attribution
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a hypothetical new version simultaneously changes theoretical terminology and retrieval software and adds primary sources, after which omissions decrease. One may report fewer omissions for the new combination on the specified tasks, but cannot determine which change caused them. Separate attribution requires a corresponding comparative design.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The changes and outcomes are conditional assumptions, not an actual experiment.
teachingExamples.boundary: Even further decomposition requires checking interactions and transfer across tasks; generalization is not automatic.

counterexamples.text: The formal text has adopted ten suggestions, proving that the framework produced ten independent benefits.
counterexamples.effect: Separate adoption from effects; suggestions from the same source that share a modification cannot yield repeatedly counted benefits.

counterexamples.text: No one has made a comparison, so the framework and its alternatives have been proved equivalent.
counterexamples.effect: Absence of comparison only limits conclusions; it does not prove equivalence or uselessness.

counterexamples.text: The new combination performs better, entirely because of one sentence in the new theory.
counterexamples.effect: When software and material change simultaneously, initially only the combination can be evaluated; attribution to one component requires an identification design.

questionAnswers.question: Why should accurate source references also serve as a comparator?
questionAnswers.answer: It tests what the framework's additional explanation adds over faithful presentation of the material, preventing complexity introduced by rewriting from masquerading as value.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why can B's 7/8 in the numerical example not directly outrank A's 8/10?
questionAnswers.answer: The denominators differ. B has two undelivered tasks, so its overall correct delivery is 7/10; delivery rate and conditional quality should be reported separately.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does cutting the character count in half prove that readers save half their time?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Character count is an artifact attribute; reading and judgment costs require material from actual tasks.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: What must be publicly distinguished after retirement?
questionAnswers.answer: Conclusions that remain valid, have been downgraded, or cannot be transferred, while retaining necessary sources, responsibilities, and incomplete remedies.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

16.25.title: 16.25 Context-specific parameters and handling missing values
16.25.lead: A framework may require an observation window, but cannot arbitrarily determine how many days each organization should observe, who has decision authority, or who should receive private material. When parameters are missing, identify which step cannot currently proceed while preserving supported conclusions that do not depend on them.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 3768–3775; source anchor section-16-25; short quotation: ‘A missing parameter blocks only judgments and uses that depend on that parameter’ (translated from Chinese). The source slice for this topic is attached verbatim in source-slice.md, keeping the explanation separate from the source.

Context-specific parameters connect general requirements to particular organizations and authorities. The source lists five groups that must be determined through external procedures for the particular context: consensus participants and time limits; the observation window, sample, and decision-makers needed to restore an empirical problem family; safe weak-signal channels, custodians, and remedy institutions; risk weights among missing AI items; and standards for comparing alternatives across disciplines, cultures, and jurisdictions. The framework can identify questions and evidentiary responsibilities, but cannot generate a valid threshold merely because its text needs a number.

These parameters require external determination because they involve actual participation eligibility, risks, resources, authority, and comparisons of values. Decision cycles, jurisdictions, and protective needs differ between organizations. Without participants and time limits, consensus completion is difficult to determine; without a restoration window and sample, an empirical problem family cannot arbitrarily be declared reliably eligible again; without safe channels and custodial responsibility, submitting weak signals may increase exposure; without risk weights and comparison standards, tradeoffs among gaps or alternatives lack public grounds. External procedures must themselves have concrete validity: asking an arbitrary person for a number is not adequate external determination.

Registration must specify seven applicability conditions: organization, jurisdiction, object, risk level, evidentiary basis, validity period, and review conditions. Organization and jurisdiction limit the institutional settings of use; object prevents mixing different populations or tasks; risk level explains the required rigor; evidentiary basis states the grounds for the parameter; and validity period and review conditions prevent old values from being retained forever. Thirty days being valid in one place does not establish thirty days elsewhere. Significant contextual change within the same organization also requires review, rather than reliance on the unchanged name.

When fields are missing, conclusions remain downgraded, suspended, or competing; the framework or AI must not fill them automatically. Pending items may be listed explicitly, with who should obtain them and which outputs they affect, but casually assigned defaults must not be hidden as already authorized context-specific parameters. Assumed values for teaching or sensitivity analysis are permissible if consistently labeled assumptions without acquiring eligibility for real-world clearance. A calculation running does not establish the parameters’ governance validity.

The scope of blocking from missing information follows dependencies. An undetermined restoration window blocks a restoration judgment that depends on it, but does not automatically invalidate a date independently supported by an original record. Conversely, when the gap concerns a shared source’s identity, lawful use conditions for the entire task, or a parameter shared by all outputs, blocking may be extensive. The principle of localization must not be used to evade shared gaps by splitting or renaming; nor should one local gap crudely erase all grounded content.

Four kinds of absence must remain separate: protective unknown means information is not obtained or disclosed for justified protection such as safety or privacy; lack of observational capacity means there is currently no corresponding measurement or acquisition route; genuine inapplicability means the item has no applicable object within the task boundary; and awaiting supplementary evidence means relevant evidence still needs to be obtained. None automatically means nonoccurrence or a value of zero. Protective unknowns especially must not justify forced disclosure. Genuine inapplicability needs a scope explanation; unwillingness to check cannot be packaged as inapplicability.

Records must also be proportionate. Whether a new field may change a judgment or reduce harm must be compared with waiting, exposure, and maintenance costs. A record that merely repeats an existing identity without adding verification value, yet requires another disclosure of sensitive experiences, may be inappropriate. Proportionality is not an excuse to delete necessary appeal, authorization, or risk records either. Consider reusing already authorized and applicable material, limiting collection, narrowing use, or retaining unknown status, rather than choosing only between unlimited collection and no records.

The strongest objection is that external determination of all parameters would prevent the framework from working. The response is to first complete material checks, candidate explanations, and comparison designs that do not depend on those parameters, while specifying which conclusions carrying greater responsibility cannot yet hold. This locates actual work better than pretending every parameter is available. Another objection says different contexts may set different values arbitrarily. That also fails: external procedures still must register evidence, applicability scope, and review conditions. Contextualization is not arbitrariness, nor does it turn normative gaps into author preferences.

distinctions.leftText: A value or rule determined through an applicable procedure, with scope, evidence, and a validity period.
distinctions.rightText: May serve as an explicit teaching assumption, but does not automatically acquire real-world validity.

distinctions.leftText: Blocks judgments and uses specifically depending on that item.
distinctions.rightText: Only failure of a shared or global premise extends to all dependent outputs.

distinctions.leftText: Justified protection restricts acquisition or disclosure.
distinctions.rightText: Evidence still needs supplementation; authority and safety still apply, and disclosure cannot be forced.

distinctions.leftText: The object and task scope make the item inapplicable; an explanation is required.
distinctions.rightText: The item may apply, but acquisition or measurement capacity is currently absent.

distinctions.leftText: The judgment and protection benefits of added material are sufficient relative to its costs.
distinctions.rightTitle: More is always better, or less is always better
distinctions.rightText: The number of records does not itself establish governance quality.

boundaries: A value from one context must not be copied into a universal threshold, nor may risk weights be automatically generated for real-world clearance.
The four kinds of absence mean neither zero nor factual negation; protective unknowns must not be forcibly converted into disclosure.
A local gap limits local dependencies, but missing shared global conditions affect every dependent output.
Inapplicability requires grounds in object scope; it must not become a label for evading checks.
This lesson determines no real organization’s deadlines, risk weights, authorized personnel, or remedy institutions.
questions: May the framework casually fill in a set of risk-weight numbers to make the procedure run?
