A.3.title: A.3 HV03 Orientation anchor (complete interface card)
A.3.lead: HV03 retains sourced expressions of meaning and heterogeneous goals; only support for a preselected H1 outcome permits registration of a bounded effective anchor. Effects prove neither shared inner states nor goal justification.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 3950–4033; original site location /theory/appendix-a/a-03#section-a-3. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research drafts and excerpts remain available for checking in their original downloadable versions.

Short quotations translated from Chinese: “candidate meaning materials” precede “conditionally effective orientation anchors.” Goals, identities, memories, commitments, fears, and common problems may all be sourced meaning materials, but how they alter resources, actions, or coordination requires separate evidence. A widespread slogan is not necessarily effective, still less proof of identical inner states or a justified goal. [T-main]

HV03-R0-candidate-anchor requires traceable expressions and forms of carriage without an eligible H1-instance yet, permitting registration of heterogeneous expressions, representational disputes, and H1 supplementary-evidence needs. Pause conditions prohibit R1 registration when there are only slogans, interpreter projection, or coerced agreement, while explicitly retaining R0 registration of sourced expressions, heterogeneity, and coercion risks. Insufficient strong support cannot be rewritten as no materials to analyze. [T-main]

HV03-R1-effective-anchor requires a preregistered H1-instance to obtain supported on the uniquely preselected criterion among resource allocation, action choice, or coordination outcomes, adding CAUSAL and E4. The outcome family among these three must be selected beforehand: if resources do not change, one cannot switch to actions, then select a favorable coordination measure when actions do not change. If multiple goals, models, or comparison rules need combining, freeze them beforehand too, rather than fishing for significance after results. [T-main；T-H1-contract]

R1 supports a conditional anchor only for that instance, selected outcome family, scale, and window. It does not extrapolate to unselected outcomes, imply genuine consent or unified inner states, or justify coercive meaning. An effective direction of coordination may arise from fear or pressure, making the distinction between established effects and normative justification especially important. Unresolved/unsupported results that fail the positive check also cannot declare meaning incapable of affecting any outcome without passing the null-conclusion check. [T-main；T-H1-contract]

Across nine axes, preserve differences between original expressions, action sequences, distributions of positions, and summaries. Aggregation requires added representation rules, heterogeneity, cost/benefit distributions, and J. Different goals at low-safety positions cannot be erased by majority summaries; silence, coerced agreement, and internal competition enter uncertainty and local exclusion zones. Different people may use the same words while referring to different costs and actions. [T-main]

Time windows distinguish short-term slogans, long-term commitments, and intergenerational memories. Outputs may enter events, mobilization for uptake, and normative agendas, but those downstream uses cannot inherit an effect not yet proved. Those claiming representativeness and those allocating resources on that basis have separate recording responsibilities; the interface authorizes neither unified meaning, representation of wishes, nor coordinated action. [T-main]

Appeals permit denial of representativeness, presentation of heterogeneous goals, refusal to be anchored, and review outside the original judgment chain. Authorized rollback must actually revoke naming and its representative/downstream coordination effects, restore heterogeneous-expression status, and retain versions and verification; it cannot compress public opinions into another new slogan. [T-main]

The verifiable original 1990 ADA signing statement publicly invokes liberty, equality, and commitments to administrative implementation. This is sourced expressive material, but it does not itself provide a preselected-outcome effect relative to comparison conditions. The statement alone cannot establish H1 supported or universal public consent. Real historical materials need not be denied significance, but inference ceilings must remain. [P-ADA；T-main]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card: HV03. Interpretation: the short identifier within the cardbook tracks the same interface; it does not indicate that a real-world object has been proved. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card: human_variable:HV03. Interpretation: the namespace prevents naming collisions; references to this ID must still carry object and evidential status. [T-main]
03 | Name (name). Original card: Orientation anchor. Interpretation: the name provides a reading entry point, not an automatic label for particular people, groups, or real structures. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H marks human adaptation; it does not mean all six human clauses are the same kind of fact. R1 effects in this interface require independent H1-instance support; the interface itself carries no empirical truth value. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card: Goals, identities, memories, commitments, fears, or common problems may first be registered as candidate meaning materials; only when H1-instance supports preselected resource-allocation, action-choice, or coordination outcomes may a conditionally effective orientation anchor be registered within that instance’s scope. Interpretation: read this proposition together with the subsequent conditional routes and ceilings; do not extract an unconditional causal or normative conclusion from one sentence. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card: Human structures with intention, coordination, or common problems. Interpretation: scope lists task domains that may be studied, not empirical support for every object within them. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card: Where there are only slogans, interpreter projection, or coerced uniform expression, do not register an R1 conditionally effective orientation anchor; sourced expressive materials, heterogeneous expressions, and coercion risks may still be registered under R0, without inferring a collective will. Interpretation: pausing R1 does not delete expressive evidence. Slogans or forced agreement alone do not register an effective anchor, but sourced materials, heterogeneity, and coercion risks may remain under R0. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card: 1. human_variable:HV01. Interpretation: inferential dependencies provide upstream content needed for the proposition to hold; upstream candidate/support status must pass through unchanged, without automatic upgrading by citation. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card: 1. E2; 2. EVIDENCE; 3. SOURCE. Interpretation: protocol dependencies constrain evidence gathering and expression; completing protocols does not independently prove an empirical proposition true. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: an empty set means only that no such specialization relations are registered, not that evidential responsibility is absent; a nonempty set also does not imply universal validity. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card: 1. route_id=HV03-R0-candidate-anchor; claim_level=candidate_description; when=Goals, identities, memories, commitments, fears, or common problems have traceable expressions and forms of carriage, but no eligible H1-instance exists yet.; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set); additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set); allowed_conclusion=Register candidate meaning materials, heterogeneous expressions, representativeness disputes, and H1 supplementary-evidence needs.; result_ceiling=Candidate expressions of meaning only; do not call them effective orientation anchors or collective will. 2. route_id=HV03-R1-effective-anchor; claim_level=conditional_effect; when=A preregistered H1-instance obtains supported on the uniquely preselected criterion among resource-allocation, action-choice, or coordination outcomes.; additional_inferential_requires=H1-instance; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4; allowed_conclusion=Register a conditionally effective orientation anchor within that instance, outcome family, scale, and window.; result_ceiling=Do not extrapolate to unselected resource, action, or coordination outcomes, or infer genuine consent, unified inner states, or coercively unified meaning. Interpretation: R0 retains traceable meaning expressions and heterogeneous disputes; R1 must uniquely preselect an outcome criterion among resources, actions, and coordination, obtain eligible H1 supported, and add CAUSAL/E4, without switching endpoints afterward. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card: 1. Conditional coordination directions and conflict anchors. Interpretation: coordination directions or conflict anchors may be judged only within the corresponding route’s scope; candidate expressions are not R1 effects and do not automatically have normative justification. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card: 1. A group has a unified inner mind; 2. Shared language equals genuine consent; 3. The goal is justified. Interpretation: these are common boundary violations, not avoided by rewording; inspect actual inference and downstream use, not wording alone. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=aggregation level: individual expressions or actions, subject cases, candidate participant populations, distributions of positions, and aggregation rules; X=spatial scope: relational sites, organizational spaces, digital public spaces, and cross-domain dissemination; T=time span: expression–action windows, commitment cycles, and drift/decoupling lags; O=organizational level: action roles, teams, organizations, institutions, through public-governance ecosystems; C=causal level: expression events, meaning–action interaction mechanisms, meso-level coordination structures, institutional arrangements, and systemic conditions; R=observational resolution: original expressions and actions, event sequences, cases, distributions of positions, coordination indicators, and summaries, with compression loss registered; I=sphere of influence: direct participants, dissenters, indirectly affected people, second-order coordination consequences, cross-domain and intergenerational effects; N=network-topological scope: dissemination of expressions, coordination connections, heterogeneous clusters, and bridging nodes; J=jurisdiction and authorization scope: register authorization separately for anchor naming, adoption of representativeness, and coordination or unification demands; heterogeneous anchors must be retained. Interpretation: register all nine axes individually; particularly, sphere of influence I creates no jurisdictional authority J, and lower observational resolution R requires retention of compression loss. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card: Goals, identities, memories, commitments, fears, or common problems that may alter resource allocation, action choice, or coordination outcomes. Interpretation: this describes the interface’s corresponding object; choosing a lower-threshold descriptive route cannot treat functional meaning in the name as established causation. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card: 1. Bridges from meaning to preselected resource-allocation, action-choice, or coordination outcomes. Interpretation: invariants are comparative responsibilities retained during transfer, not a declaration that variable values remain constant at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions on elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card: 1. Representation rules; 2. Heterogeneity; 3. Cost/benefit distributions; 4. J axis. Interpretation: elevation is not copying and enlarging the original table. Where materials on new populations, interfaces, responsibility positions, and so on are incomplete, restrict conclusions dependent on them. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card: 1. Anchor content, strength, and carrying subjects may change. Interpretation: the same word may change meaning when the object or scale changes; reconstruct correspondence rather than assume the original meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Inapplicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card: 1. Nonhuman systems without capability for intention, meaning, or commitment. Interpretation: inapplicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of human normative, responsibility, and experiential interfaces; they do not deny that other theories can study these objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card: 1. Directly upgrading local expressions into collective will. Interpretation: inference from local to whole requires separate proof; broad impact, a grand name, or formal similarity cannot supply representativeness and authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card: 1. Dispersed; 2. Cohesive; 3. Competing; 4. Rigidified; 5. Decoupled. Interpretation: states are descriptive classifications requiring evidence, not a maturity ladder for scoring people; state changes require windows, grounds, and versions. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card: 1. Resource-allocation differences before/after preregistered meaning expressions appear; 2. Changes in action choices, collaboration completion rates, or conflict patterns; 3. Acceptance, refusal, and alternative formulations of anchors at different positions; 4. Whether outcome differences under comparison conditions exceed predetermined thresholds. Interpretation: observable indications tell us where to seek materials; a single indication’s presence is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card: 1. Resource adjustments; 2. Action sequences; 3. Commitment and exit records; 4. Conflict evidence. Interpretation: resource, action, commitment/exit, and conflict materials may have different uses; applying for H1 requires keeping the preselected outcome family rather than retrospectively seeking the most favorable endpoint among them. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface content (input_dependencies). Original card: 1. Participating positions; 2. Safety of expression; 3. Resource and action data. Interpretation: this states what arrives from upstream and its eligibility; gaps cannot quietly disappear while passing between interfaces. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flow (output_effects). Original card: 1. Generative events; 2. Mobilization for uptake; 3. Normative-choice agendas. Interpretation: variable flow identifies downstream judgments that may depend on this interface; passing references guarantees neither downstream conclusions, actual repair, nor authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Distinguish short-term slogans, long-term commitments, and intergenerational memories. Interpretation: occurrence, observation, execution, and arrival of effects may differ in time; short-term materials cannot automatically certify extensions beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record silence, coerced agreement, and internal heterogeneity. Interpretation: direct uncertainty toward specific materials and positions; an overall confidence score cannot conceal fundamentally uncovered positions. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Different goals at low-safety positions must not be erased by aggregation. Interpretation: exclusion zones limit current inferential coverage, not delete people or facts from the world; unavailability for safety is neither consent nor absence of problems. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Those identifying with the anchor; 2. Dissenters; 3. Those represented; 4. Cost bearers. Interpretation: register directly and indirectly affected parties together; visible members do not represent every cost bearer. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Narratives; 2. Commitments; 3. Shared memories; 4. Institutional goals; 5. Problem definitions. Interpretation: a carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something; its name, completed construction, and arrival of the required function are different evidence. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Those claiming representativeness; 2. Those allocating resources on that basis. Interpretation: identify who proposes, operates, or uses judgments; recording responsibility is not automatically a legal-liability adjudication or new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: An anchor’s existence does not prove it justified. Interpretation: distinguish descriptive, normative, and bridging status according to the card. Established facts do not independently determine value rankings; normative reasons do not automatically prove empirical effects. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card, translated from Chinese: Limit R0 and R1 separately: R0 only describes candidate expressions of meaning; when the corresponding H1-instance supports the selected outcome effect, R1 permits a bounded conditional-anchor explanation, without extrapolating to unselected outcomes. Interpretation: R0 identifies only candidate expressions; R1 is confined to the selected outcome effect. Improved coordination cannot establish improved resources or genuine consent. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card, translated from Chinese: This variable generates only descriptions of candidate anchors, heterogeneous expressions, comparison results, and evidence needs; it does not authorize unifying meanings, representing wishes, or coordinating action. Any real-world adjustment must separately pass C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: The interface itself creates no real-world authority to act; actual actions separately check choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protection, and duration. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Repeated slogans change no resource allocation or action; 2. Uniform expression under high pressure conceals conflicting actual objectives. Interpretation: Counterexamples limit unconditional extrapolation. They may require narrowing the scope or collecting evidence again, without automatically negating all bounded uses. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card, translated from Chinese: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, members may deny representativeness, submit heterogeneous objectives, or refuse to be anchored through safely reachable, anti-retaliation channels, triggering review independent of the original anchor-judgment chain. Interpretation: Appeals must be safely reachable, protected against retaliation, and able to trigger independent review; a channel name alone does not establish power to change an error. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card, translated from Chinese: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, once rollback is authorized, a designated responsible person must actually revoke the anchor designation, remove its representative and downstream coordination effects, and restore the state of heterogeneous expression within the stipulated time, preserving versions and completion verification. Interpretation: Within valid authorization, actually revoke erroneous effects, correct downstream consequences, and verify completion. Changing document wording does not mean rights and resources have been restored to the person concerned. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Fix the object, sources of expression, carrier forms, and observation positions.
R0 registers candidate meanings, heterogeneous expressions, disputes about representation, and evidence needs.
When testing R1, first uniquely preselect one outcome family—resources/action/coordination—and its criteria.
Use qualified H1, CAUSAL, and E4 to judge instance effects, keeping unresolved and null conclusions distinct.
Restrict claims to the selected outcome window; do not infer consent, a common will, or normative justification.
Protect those refusing representation; after authorization, revoke erroneous downstream representative/coordination effects.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: three outcomes cannot be selected for the best result afterward
teachingExamples.text: A constructed study preselects resource allocation alone as its primary outcome. It later observes a resource difference of 0, an action-metric difference of 2, and a coordination-metric difference of 8. The apparent size of coordination's 8 cannot justify renaming the original resource test a successful H1. Coordination material may generate a separately preregistered candidate hypothesis; whether the resource result supports a null effect still requires its dedicated null-conclusion check, and a difference of 0 alone is insufficient.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Numbers, metric scales, and the study are teaching constructions; no formal statistical determination is supplied.
teachingExamples.boundary: Failure to support one primary outcome does not negate every effect of meaning. What is prohibited is changing the primary target after results are known.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: different objectives beneath uniform expression
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional meeting, everyone says “protect the project.” A hopes to keep a job, B hopes to stop a dangerous function on schedule, and C fears retaliation for dissent. Shared wording and heterogeneous interpretations may be registered, without inferring unified inner intentions from identical wording. Nor may C be forced to publicly prove their situation before a safety gap is recognized.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Constructed people and situations; no inference about actual motives.
teachingExamples.boundary: Different interpretations require support from the person concerned or independent material; analysts cannot project actual inner states themselves.

questionAnswers.question: Does a repeatedly occurring slogan constitute an effective anchor?
questionAnswers.answer: It suffices only to register expression under qualified sourcing; R1 requires corresponding H1 support for the preselected outcome.

questionAnswers.question: Does improved coordination establish that an objective is justified?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Effects and normative standing remain separate.
questionAnswers.basis: normative_status and prohibited leaps.

questionAnswers.question: When coerced uniformity is found, should even the expressions go unrecorded?
questionAnswers.answer: Record sourced expressions and coercion risks, but do not register an R1 effective anchor or a common will.

questionAnswers.question: Can another favorable outcome rescue a failed preselected outcome?
questionAnswers.answer: The outcome family cannot be changed after the event; new discoveries retain exploratory status.

A.4.title: A.4 HV04 Generative Node (Complete Interface Card)
A.4.lead: HV04 separates generative conditions, actors, and events. An unidentified actor does not mean an absence of actors has been proved; the fact of generation creates neither justification, complete responsibility, nor continuing authority.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 4034–4117; original site location /theory/appendix-a/a-04#section-a-4. For the current full text, see the theory-v2 source; historical research manuscripts and excerpts remain available for checking in their original downloadable versions.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: “Generation must be separated into generative conditions GC, generative subjects GS, and generative events GE.” GC concerns how conditions and constraints permit new states to form; GS denotes acting subjects with corresponding capabilities, roles, and standing; GE denotes detectable new states or transitions. The three may be connected but cannot replace one another. An event occurring does not mean an actor has been identified, and a visible person does not mean that person created the entire result. [T-main; T-types]

HV04-R0-generation-typing permits separately registering candidate GC/GS/GE and unidentified-actor states, with conclusions stopping at strong typing. No registered inferential dependencies does not mean evidence is unnecessary: EVIDENCE, SOURCE, and specific object material remain required. Successful classification also does not establish a causal generation mechanism among the three. [T-main]

The original card permits emergent generation without an identifiable actor, but “currently unidentified” is not “proved to have no actor.” Observed local interactions and overall changes can be objects of bridging research. A claim about an actorless mechanism additionally requires corresponding channel and comparison evidence; an unknown initiator cannot be concealed behind “natural emergence.” [T-main]

HV04-R1-generation-mechanism requires a preregistered G2-instance identifying an above-threshold effect of GC, GS, or an actorless emergent channel on a specified GE state transition, plus CAUSAL and E4. What is permitted is a candidate generation mechanism and its typing within specified scales, windows, and channels. It does not automatically establish that any technology has intentions, that any crisis wants to change institutions, or that the most visible person bears all responsibility. [T-main; T-G2]

Register nine-axis scales and times for GC, GS, and GE separately: condition accumulation, actor action, event timing, and diffusion delays may differ. Generative subjects, conditions, and events may change with scale. Moving across levels requires new units and populations, representation relations, responsibility types, and external impacts; individual initiation cannot directly establish the intention of an organization as a whole. [T-main]

The fact of generation establishes neither justification nor complete responsibility; having initiated something does not grant an actor permanent continuing authorization. Outputs may establish uptake needs, descriptions of state transitions, and a starting point for a responsibility chain, but a “starting point” is not a final attribution of responsibility. Starting, spreading, or stopping any real-world process requires independent choice and authorization; the interface does not issue orders itself. [T-main]

Those classified as actors may safely challenge attributed intentions, roles, and authorization, with anti-retaliation protection, and request review outside the original typing chain. When rollback is authorized, correct GC/GS/GE types, actually remove erroneous attributions of intention/responsibility and downstream effects, and preserve versions and completion verification. Merely renaming “responsible person” as “generator” while continuing to affect evaluations is insufficient. [T-main]

The SEC's 2013 order on the 2012 Knight incident separately records omissions in code deployment, activation of an old program, and order outputs. This can help record technical conditions, personnel conduct, and event outcomes separately. The technical chain does not make a program an intentional actor, and the order's regulatory findings cannot be substituted in this explanation for a complete responsibility judgment about any individual. [P-KNIGHT]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card, translated from Chinese: HV04. Interpretation: This is the short identifier within the card collection, tracking the same interface; it does not mean a real object has been proved. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card, translated from Chinese: human_variable:HV04. Interpretation: A qualified namespace avoids name collisions; references to this ID must still carry the object and evidence status. [T-main]

03 | Name (name). Original card, translated from Chinese: Generative node. Interpretation: The name provides an entry point for reading, not an automatic label for a particular person, group, or real structure. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card, translated from Chinese: Generation must be separated into generative conditions GC, generative subjects GS, and generative events GE, permitting emergent generation without an identifiable actor. Interpretation: GC/GS/GE are distinct strong types. Emergence without an identifiable actor is permitted, but an unknown-actor state cannot directly be upgraded to proved absence of an actor. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card, translated from Chinese: Formation of new actions, organizations, institutions, or state transitions in human structures. Interpretation: The scope lists task domains that may be examined; it does not mean every object within them has empirical support. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card, translated from Chinese: When conditions are personified, events treated as actors, or actor standing not established on grounds, pause the corresponding actor or typing assertions; R0 may still separately register candidate GC, GS, GE, and unidentified-actor states, without treating unidentified as proved actorless. Interpretation: When personification is erroneous or actor standing insufficient, pause the corresponding assertions. R0's candidate conditions, actors, events, and unidentified states may still remain separately. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card, translated from Chinese: None (empty set). Interpretation: This is explicitly an empty set, with no inferential dependencies registered. It does not waive SOURCE/EVIDENCE protocols or turn R0 typing into causal proof. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. EVIDENCE; 2. SOURCE. Interpretation: Protocol dependencies constrain evidence collection and expression; completing protocols does not independently establish the truth of empirical propositions. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: an empty set means only that no such specialization relations are registered, not that evidential responsibility is absent; a nonempty set also does not imply universal validity. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional-support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. route_id=HV04-R0-generation-typing;; claim_level=descriptive_classification;; when=The required GC, GS, and GE fields can be registered separately, while preserving actorless emergence and unidentified-actor states.;; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set);; additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set);; allowed_conclusion=Separately register candidate generative conditions, candidate generative subjects, and candidate generative events, without substituting them for one another.;; result_ceiling=Strong typing only; the existence of any condition, actor, or event does not establish the other two or a causal generation mechanism.; 2. route_id=HV04-R1-generation-mechanism;; claim_level=mechanism_explanation;; when=A preregistered G2-instance identifies an above-threshold effect of GC, GS, or an actorless emergent channel on a specified GE state transition.;; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register a candidate generation mechanism within the specified scale, window, and channel and its GC, GS, GE typing.;; result_ceiling=Do not personify conditions, infer actors backward from events, or derive justification, responsibility, and authorization from the fact of generation. Interpretation: R0 only classifies. R1 requires preregistered G2 identification of GC, GS, or an actorless channel's effect on specified GE, plus CAUSAL/E4; an event having occurred does not justify inferring an actor backward. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Conditional generative paths; 2. Generation with or without an actor. Interpretation: These are permitted directions of conclusion; which is actually reached, and at what strength, remains bounded by the selected route and material. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Technologies or crises have intentions; 2. Generative subjects automatically possess continuing authorization. Interpretation: These are common boundary crossings that cannot be avoided merely by rephrasing; examine actual inferences and subsequent use, not just wording. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card, translated from Chinese: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=Aggregation level: units of condition exposure, actor action, and generative events, each with its own case population, distribution, and aggregation rules; X=Spatial scope: generation sites, organizational or platform boundaries, diffusion regions, and cross-domain environments; T=Temporal span: condition-accumulation periods, actor-action windows, event times, and diffusion delays; O=Organizational level: action roles, generative teams, organizations, institutions, and governance ecologies; C=Causal level: generative events, actor–condition interaction mechanisms, meso-level generative structures, institutional arrangements, and system conditions; R=Observation resolution: raw conditions, actions, and events; generation sequences, cases, outcome distributions, transition indicators, and summaries, with compression losses registered; I=Range of impact: direct participants in generation, those taking it up, indirectly affected people, second-order consequences, and cross-domain and intergenerational impacts; N=Network-topology scope: condition propagation, actor collaboration, event diffusion, and emergent connections; J=Jurisdiction and authorization scope: separately register authorization for identifying generation, initiating changes, investing resources, and handling diffusion; GC, GS, and GE each register their own scale. Interpretation: In addition to checking all nine axes separately, GC conditions, GS actors, and GE events each need their own scales; one overall scale must not conceal cross-level differences among conditions, actions, and consequences. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card, translated from Chinese: A combination of conditions, actors, and events forming a detectable state transition. Interpretation: This describes the object corresponding to the interface; choosing a low-threshold descriptive route does not permit treating functional meaning in the name as proven causality. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Strong-type separation of GC, GS, and GE. Interpretation: Invariants are comparative responsibilities to preserve during transfer, not a claim that variable values are unchanged at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions for elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. New units and populations; 2. Representation relations; 3. Responsibility types; 4. External impacts. Interpretation: Elevation is not copying and enlarging the original table. When material about new populations, interfaces, responsibility positions, and other items is incomplete, limit conclusions that depend on them. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Generative subjects, conditions, and events may change with scale. Interpretation: A word may change meaning when the object or scale changes; rebuild the correspondence rather than assume the original meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Non-applicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Stable descriptions with no formation of a new state or claim about generation. Interpretation: Non-applicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of interfaces concerning human norms, responsibility, and experience; they do not deny that other theories may study these objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Elevating conditions or events into intentional actors. Interpretation: Inferences from local parts to wholes need separate proof; broad impact, grand names, and formal similarity cannot supply representativeness or authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Latent; 2. Triggered; 3. Formed; 4. Interrupted; 5. Diffusing. Interpretation: States are descriptive classifications requiring evidence, not maturity ladders for scoring people; state changes require windows, grounds, and versions. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Time records of candidate conditions appearing, changing, or being removed; 2. Generative subjects' capabilities, authorization, decisions, and actual actions; 3. Preregistered state transitions before and after generative events; 4. Bridging records between local interactions and overall outcomes in actorless emergence. Interpretation: Observable clues indicate where to find material; a single clue's existence is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Initiation records; 2. Condition windows; 3. Actor actions; 4. Actorless interaction mechanisms. Interpretation: Gather listed evidence according to route and task relevance. Distinguish unknown, not collected, inapplicable, and unavailable under protection; do not compel disclosure merely to fill the table. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface content (input_dependencies). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Orientation anchors; 2. Resource and institutional conditions; 3. Causal contracts. Interpretation: This states what enters from upstream and with what qualifications; gaps must not quietly disappear during transfer between interfaces. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flows (output_effects). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Uptake needs; 2. State transitions; 3. Starting points of responsibility chains. Interpretation: Variable flows indicate which downstream judgments may depend on this interface; passing references does not guarantee downstream conclusions, actual repair, or authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Register accumulated conditions, triggering events, and formation lags. Interpretation: Occurrence, observation, execution, and the arrival of effects may happen at different times; short-term material cannot automatically certify extension beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record joint generation, emergence without an agent, and unidentifiable agents. Interpretation: Locate uncertainty in specific material and positions; do not merely write an overall confidence score that conceals positions never covered at all. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Omitted informal initiators and affected positions. Interpretation: An exclusion zone limits the coverage of the current inference; it does not erase these people or facts from the world. Material unavailable for safety reasons is neither consent nor evidence of no problem. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Initiators; 2. Those taking up the process; 3. Beneficiaries; 4. Affected people. Interpretation: Register both directly and indirectly affected people; visible members do not represent all cost bearers. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Initiators; 2. Procedures; 3. Technical facilities; 4. Relational networks. Interpretation: A carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something. Its name, completed construction, and delivery of the required function require different evidence. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Actual actors; 2. Decision-makers; 3. Authorizers. Interpretation: Specify who proposes a judgment and who operates or uses it; registering responsibility does not automatically constitute adjudication of legal liability or new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: Facts of generation do not establish normative justification or completeness of responsibility. Interpretation: Distinguish descriptive, normative, and bridging status as specified by the card. Established facts do not independently determine value rankings, and normative reasons do not automatically establish empirical effects. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card: Up to the explanatory level when the mechanism chain is complete. Interpretation: A complete mechanism can support the explanatory level; R0 still reaches only candidate classification, and R1 likewise concerns a candidate mechanism for a specified channel. Neither grants responsibility assignments or continuing authorization. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card: This variable generates only candidate classifications of GC, GS, and GE, descriptions of state transitions, and requirements for additional evidence. It does not authorize initiating, spreading, or stopping generative processes; any real-world adjustment must separately pass C12, an explicit runtime N premise, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: The interface itself does not confer real-world authority to act; actual actions require separate checks of choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protection, and validity periods. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card: 1. Technical conditions are incorrectly described as a goal-directed generative subject; 2. An emergent process without a unified initiator is forcibly attributed to one visible person. Interpretation: Use counterexamples to limit unconditional extrapolation. They may require narrowing the scope or obtaining new evidence, but do not automatically invalidate all bounded uses. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, those classified as generative subjects may challenge attributions of intent, role, and authorization through safe, accessible channels protecting against retaliation, and trigger review independent of the original classification or decision chain. Interpretation: Appeals must be safely accessible, protected against retaliation, and capable of triggering independent review; a name alone does not imply authority to change errors. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, when rollback is authorized, the designated responsible person corrects GC, GS, and GE types within the specified time limit, actually removes erroneous attributions of intent or responsibility and their downstream effects, and retains versions and verification of completion. Interpretation: Within valid authorization, actually revoke erroneous effects, correct downstream consequences, and verify completion; changing words in a document does not restore rights and resources to the person concerned. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Starting from a claim about a new state, register GC, GS, GE, and their sources separately.
R0 retains candidate status and unknown agents without personifying conditions.
If seeking a mechanism explanation, preregister the specified state transition and G2 channel comparison.
Check the scale, time window, and cross-level bridging for GC, GS, and GE separately.
Effects, normative justification, responsibility, and authorization must each be established; a generator does not automatically retain authority forever.
Disputed attributions may undergo independent review; after authorized correction, remove downstream effects.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: three kinds of object within one new function
teachingExamples.text: A fictional platform opens a new interface, team A publishes a new service under existing permissions, and users form new exchange activities. The interface capability may be listed as GC, team A as a GS candidate, its actual publishing action as evidence of agent action, and a specified change in exchange state as a GE candidate. If users later combine spontaneously to form another state, not all subsequent developments can be attributed to A's original intent; a new object window and mechanism material are needed.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The platform, team, and events are constructed; no actual launch is involved.
teachingExamples.boundary: Candidate classification does not replace G2 or establish A's responsibility for, or authority over, all subsequent behavior.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: not knowing who does not mean there was no one
teachingExamples.text: Constructed records show that queue rules changed at a particular time, but the initiation log is missing. Register a candidate event and an unknown agent, rather than ‘emergence without an agent has been proved.’ If a recovered log later shows that an authorized role changed the configuration, update the corresponding GS and version. If a mechanism of distributed interactions is found, its bridging and causal evidence also require separate checks.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A fictional record-recovery scenario.
teachingExamples.boundary: Retaining an unknown presupposes neither a hidden operator nor the absence of an agent; both assertions require evidence.

questionAnswers.question: Can a crisis be described as intentional because it triggers change?
questionAnswers.answer: No; it may be a condition or an event, while agent intent requires separate checking.

questionAnswers.question: Does the existence of GC prove that GE will occur?

A.5.title: A.5 HV05 Action-uptake layer (complete interface card)
A.5.lead: HV05 distinguishes uptake, costs, benefits, authority to stop, and six types of responsibility. Its five routes separately address current functions, historical traces, and two intertemporal explanations; none creates an unlimited obligation to bear burdens.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 4118–4207; original-site location /theory/appendix-a/a-05#section-a-5. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; the historical Chinese research manuscript and slices remain downloadable in their original versions for checking.

Short quotation: ‘Capacity for uptake does not become an obligation, and CV does not become RS’ (translated from Chinese). CV is a carrier that actually executes, transmits, maintains, records, cares, or repairs, and may be a person, post, procedure, facility, or institution; RS is a party bearing the relevant type of responsibility. Who acts, who incurs costs, who benefits, who has authority to stop, and who bears which responsibility must be kept separate. A facility's ability to transmit data does not make it a bearer of moral or legal responsibility. [T-main；T-H2]

HV05-R0-carrier-responsibility-split registers CV, cost bearers of the same type, beneficiaries, authority to stop, RS, resources, and capacity under H2, stopping at current classification and gaps. H2 is an operational classification rule, not an empirical causal law. R0 can identify mismatches between tasks and resources, but does not automatically make the most visible executor the principal party responsible for decisions, authorization, benefits, or remedies. [T-main；T-H2]

HV05-R1-functional-carrier-effect requires a qualifying G2 to support the channel effect of specified carrier replacement, interruption, replenishment, or load reduction on a preselected functional outcome, plus CAUSAL/E4. It supports only measured dimensions of function, capacity, delay, or loss. Fewer labor hours for one task does not establish lower overall burdens; improved function does not create an obligation for continued sacrifice or permission to reallocate resources. [T-main；T-G2]

HV05-R2-intertemporal-reproduction requires G2 support for the current channel, plus G3 establishing that historical variables provide a conditional increment for subsequent uptake/reproduction beyond the current representation, again with CAUSAL/E4. This historical increment does not mean merely ‘it happened long ago’ or ‘the old rule remains.’ It means that, with the current representation and other conditions fixed, a historical variable still provides a proportionate increment for the specified subsequent outcome. This does not imply historical fate, irreversibility, or attribution of responsibility. [T-main；T-G3]

HV05-R3-historical-carrier-trace is the H5 trace route. It requires supported status for the uniquely preselected concrete carrier and persistence criterion, plus E4. It supports only persistent traces within that carrier, observable, and window, and may submit a predefined candidate historical variable to G3. Alone, it does not establish future paths, intertemporal reproduction, repair windows, or eligibility for action. An old record that still exists is only a clue to a trace, not a complete historical causal conclusion. [T-main；T-H5]

HV05-R4-carried-reproduction is another intertemporal explanation: G2 already covers the claimed subsequent outcome/window, and §4.5 is used to check current capability, rule, resource, or relational carriers; retention/replenishment over multiple cycles; actual continuity; and discriminating causal material. It does not require an additional G3 increment beyond the current state, but cannot extrapolate long-term results directly from a single functional effect. R2 and R4 are different explanatory routes and must not subsume each other. [T-main；T-G3]

Together the five routes provide precise ceilings: R0 classification; R1 bounded functional effects; R2 historical-increment intertemporal candidates; R3 persistent traces; R4 carrier-transmitted intertemporal candidates. The weaker language of persistence in R3 cannot secure R2/R4 conclusions. Conversely, lack of G3 support does not negate carrier transmission already supported by independent channel evidence. No route creates an unlimited obligation to bear burdens. [T-main]

Register CV and RS separately along the nine axes. Task cycles, maintenance backlogs, schedules, recovery lags, cost flows, alternative paths, and authority to stop each require material. The six types of responsibility concern conduct, decisions, authorization, supervision, benefits, and remedies; they cannot be collapsed into one ‘responsible person.’ If the task asks only whether one task is feasible, collection of every private burden is not mandatory. If overall burden reduction is claimed, management, standby work, substitutes' conditions, and continuity require proportionate examination. [T-main]

Those taking up work with limited permissions, informally, or without the ability to exit belong to an exclusion zone that cannot be ignored. They may challenge tasks, resources, costs, restrictions on stopping, and responsibility assignments, and obtain review outside the original allocation/attribution chain. Authorized rollback must revoke erroneous task-resource or attribution states, actually restore records and task status, and implement authorized remedies. Shifting the burden to another person without a voice cannot be called completed correction. [T-main]

The 2005 three-state Cash and Counseling report separates actual personal assistance, spending plans, counseling, employer tasks, and fiscal tasks. It provides actual program-design material for separating uptake labor from coordination and management, but two pages of the report cannot prove that total burdens vanished or all support arrived. Here it serves only as an R0-style reference for division of work, without claiming formal G2/G3/H5 support. [P-CC]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card: HV05. Interpretation: This is a short identifier within the card collection, used to track the same interface; it does not establish a real-world object. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card: human_variable:HV05. Interpretation: The qualified namespace prevents naming collisions; references to this ID must still carry the object and evidentiary status. [T-main]
03 | Name (name). Original card: Action-uptake layer. Interpretation: The name offers a reading entry point, not an automatic label for specific people, groups, or real structures. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card: The uptake carrier CV for execution, transmission, maintenance, recording, care, and repair must be registered separately from the responsible party RS, cost bearers, beneficiaries, and authority to stop. Interpretation: This proposition must be read together with the conditional routes and ceilings below; an unconditional causal or normative conclusion cannot be extracted from one sentence. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card: Human structures requiring sustained action, maintenance, care, or execution. Interpretation: Scope lists task domains that may be examined; it does not mean every object within that scope has empirical support. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card: An executor with limited permissions is assumed to be the principal responsible party, or capacity for uptake is treated as an obligation. Interpretation: Pausing targets the dependent judgment or adoption. Independently established descriptions may remain, but invalid premises cannot continue to be used. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: Inferential dependencies provide the upstream content needed to establish a proposition. Upstream candidate/supported status must be carried through unchanged; citation does not automatically upgrade it. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. EVIDENCE; 2. SOURCE. Interpretation: Protocol dependencies constrain evidence collection and expression; completing protocols does not independently establish the truth of empirical propositions. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: 1. H2. Interpretation: This card specializes the operational classification rule H2. It helps distinguish CV from RS; correct classification does not confer empirical causal truth. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card: 1. route_id=HV05-R0-carrier-responsibility-split；；claim_level=descriptive_classification；；when=CV, cost bearers of the same type, beneficiaries, authority to stop, RS, resources, and capacity can be registered separately under H2.；；additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set)；；additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set)；；allowed_conclusion=Register current uptake carriers, tasks, costs, capacity, authority to stop, responsibility types, and uptake gaps.；；result_ceiling=Current classification and gap description only; capacity for uptake does not become an obligation, and CV does not become RS.；2. route_id=HV05-R1-functional-carrier-effect；；claim_level=conditional_effect；；when=A qualifying G2-instance shows a channel effect exceeding the threshold for specified carrier replacement, interruption, replenishment, or load reduction on a preselected functional outcome.；；additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance；；additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL、E4；；allowed_conclusion=Register candidate uptake effects of the specified carrier on measured dimensions of function, capacity, delay, or loss.；；result_ceiling=Unmeasured dimensions remain unknown; functional effects must not directly generate responsibility, obligations of sacrifice, or authorization to reallocate resources.；3. route_id=HV05-R2-intertemporal-reproduction；；claim_level=intertemporal_explanation；；when=The current uptake channel has G2-instance support, and a G3-instance shows that its historical variable provides a conditional increment for subsequent uptake or reproduction outcomes.；；additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance、G3-instance；；additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL、E4；；allowed_conclusion=Register historical-increment candidates for intertemporal uptake or reproduction beyond the current state, within the specified window and carrier.；；result_ceiling=No inference of historical fate, irreversibility, responsibility assignment, or an obligation to continue bearing burdens.；4. route_id=HV05-R3-historical-carrier-trace；；claim_level=descriptive_classification；；when=An H5-instance achieves supported status for the uniquely preselected concrete carrier and persistence criterion.；；additional_inferential_requires=H5-instance；；additional_protocol_requires=E4；；allowed_conclusion=Register persistent human traces within the specified carrier, trace observable, and window, and submit a predefined candidate historical variable to a G3-instance.；；result_ceiling=An H5-instance does not establish future path effects, intertemporal reproduction, repair windows, responsibility, or action; these conclusions require evidence under the respective carrier or historical-increment routes, outcome contracts, and normative procedures.；5. route_id=HV05-R4-carried-reproduction；；claim_level=intertemporal_explanation；；when=A qualifying G2-instance supports the specified uptake channel's effect within the claimed subsequent outcome and window, and §4.5 is used to verify current capability, rule, resource, or relational carriers, retention or replenishment over multiple cycles, actual continuity, and discriminating causal material.；；additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance；；additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL、E4；；allowed_conclusion=Register carrier-transmitted candidates for intertemporal uptake or reproduction within the specified carrier, cycles, and outcome.；；result_ceiling=Do not register a historical increment beyond the current state, extrapolate long-term results from a single functional effect, or derive an obligation or authorization to continue bearing burdens from uptake facts. Interpretation: The five routes are individually independent: R0 current classification; R1 G2 bounded function; R2 G2 + G3 historical increment; R3 H5 traces for a unique carrier/persistence criterion; R4 G2 subsequent window + continuity of current carriers across cycles. Conditions and conclusions must not be interchanged. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card: 1. Uptake gaps; 2. Task-resource mismatches; 3. Separation of responsibilities. Interpretation: These are permitted directions for conclusions; which one is actually reached, and at what strength, remains bounded by the selected route and material. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card: 1. The most visible person is the principal responsible party; 2. Ability to bear a burden means an obligation to bear it; 3. Responsibility is assigned solely because a facility or procedure performs a function; organizational responsibility requires separate agent eligibility and specific rules. Interpretation: These are common overreaches that cannot be avoided merely by rephrasing; examine the actual inference and subsequent use, not wording alone. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=aggregation level: individual task or uptake event, carrier case, uptake population, cost and capacity distributions, and aggregation rules; X=spatial scope: worksite, team or organizational boundaries, digital systems, and cross-domain service scope; T=time span: task cycles, maintenance windows, recovery lags, and periods of responsibility; O=organizational level: executing roles, teams, organizations, institutions, through governance ecosystems; C=causal level: execution events, task–resource interaction mechanisms, meso-level uptake structures, institutional responsibility arrangements, and system conditions; R=observational resolution: original task logs, uptake sequences, carrier cases, cost and capacity distributions, performance indicators, and summaries, with compression losses registered; I=impact scope: direct uptake providers, service dependents, indirect beneficiaries or cost-bearing positions, second-order spillovers, cross-domain and intergenerational effects; N=network-topological scope: uptake dependencies, alternative paths, single-point bottlenecks, and cross-domain service networks; J=jurisdiction and authorization scope: register authorization separately for task assignment, stopping, resource adjustment, attribution of responsibility, and remedies; register the scales of CV and RS separately. Interpretation: Register all nine axes individually. In particular, impact scope I does not generate jurisdiction J, and compression losses must remain recorded when observational resolution R decreases. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card: People, positions, procedures, facilities, or institutions that actually execute, transmit, maintain, record, provide care, or repair. Interpretation: This describes the object of the interface. When selecting a low-threshold descriptive route, functional meanings in names must not be treated as established causation. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card: 1. CV is not RS; 2. Register costs and benefits separately; 3. The right to stop. Interpretation: Invariants are comparative responsibilities to preserve during transfer, not a claim that variable values remain unchanged at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions for elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card: 1. Task aggregation; 2. Representation and delegation; 3. Six kinds of responsibility; 4. External costs. Interpretation: Elevation is not copying the original table at a larger size. When added material about populations, interfaces, and responsibility positions is incomplete, limit conclusions depending on it. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card: 1. Uptake carriers and responsible parties may change across levels. Interpretation: The same term may change meaning when the object or scale changes. Reestablish the correspondence rather than assuming the old meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Non-applicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card: 1. Nonhuman processes without requirements for subject action, responsibility, or maintenance. Interpretation: Inapplicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of interfaces for human norms, responsibility, and experience; they do not deny that other theories may study those objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card: 1. Directly equating individual uptake with organizational responsibility. Interpretation: Inferences from a part to the whole need separate evidence. Broad influence, grand names, or formal resemblance cannot supply representativeness or authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card: 1. Sufficient; 2. Fragile; 3. Overloaded; 4. Broken; 5. Replaced. Interpretation: States are descriptive categories requiring evidence, not a maturity ladder for scoring people. State changes need windows, grounds, and versions. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card: 1. Logs of actual task execution, maintenance, recording, and repair; 2. Flows of resources, capacity, time, and costs; 3. Records of stopping rights, replacement arrangements, and uptake transfers; 4. Grounds concerning decisions, authorization, oversight, benefit, and remedies. Interpretation: Observable clues indicate where to seek material. One clue’s presence is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card: 1. Task flows; 2. Working time and resources; 3. Maintenance records; 4. Stopping and refusal records; 5. If the target concerns total burden, separately examine management, standby, replacement-provider conditions, and continuity; individual-task judgments do not require collecting all of these. Interpretation: Evidence for an individual task need not expand without limit. Claims about total burden require the additional checks on management, standby, replacement conditions, and continuity. Evidence strength must be proportionate to the endpoint asked about. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface contents (input_dependencies). Original card: 1. Generative needs 2. Resources 3. Authorization 4. Roles. Interpretation: Resources, roles, authorization, and generative needs are inputs to examine. “Someone can do it” must not be treated as their consent or obligation. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flows (output_effects). Original card: 1. Realization of state transitions 2. Cost distributions 3. Structural load. Interpretation: Variable flows indicate which downstream judgments may depend on this interface. Passing a reference does not guarantee a downstream conclusion, actual repair, or authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Register scheduling, maintenance cycles, backlogs, and recovery lags. Interpretation: Occurrence, observation, execution, and arrival of effects may happen at different times. Short-term material cannot automatically certify what lies beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record hidden labor, informal care, and costs beyond the boundary. Interpretation: Tie uncertainty to specific material and positions; do not write only an overall confidence score that hides positions never covered. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Low-authority, informal, and non-exitable uptake providers. Interpretation: An exclusion zone limits the coverage of current inference; it does not delete these people or facts from the world. Unavailability for safety reasons is neither consent nor absence of problems. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Uptake providers; 2. Beneficiaries; 3. Service recipients; 4. Replacements. Interpretation: Register both directly and indirectly affected people. Visible members do not represent everyone bearing costs. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Personnel; 2. Positions; 3. Procedures; 4. Facilities; 5. Institutions. Interpretation: A carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something. Its name, completion of construction, and delivery of the required function are different evidentiary matters. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Actors responsible for conduct; 2. Decisions; 3. Authorization; 4. Oversight; 5. Benefit; 6. Remedies. Interpretation: Determine the six kinds of responsibility separately from actual rules, facts, and subject eligibility. One person may hold several kinds, but low-authority execution alone cannot establish all responsibility. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: The fact of uptake does not generate an obligation to continue bearing it. Interpretation: Distinguish descriptive, normative, and bridging status according to the card. An established fact does not independently determine value rankings; normative reasons do not automatically prove empirical effects. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card: R0 is limited to typing uptake and responsibility; R1 to the identified carrier-function effect; R3 to persistent traces supported by H5; R4 explains carrier-based reproduction under §4.5 and channel evidence covering subsequent windows; R2 explains historical increments beyond the current representation only with additional G3 support. Material and windows impose their respective limits; no route replaces the others, and none generates an unlimited duty to bear burdens. Interpretation: Guard especially against three substitutions: H5 traces are not G3 historical increments; a one-time G2 function is not cross-period reproduction; and unsupported G3 does not automatically negate independently evidenced R4 carrier transmission. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card: This variable generates only descriptions of CV, RS, costs, capacity, stopping rights, and uptake gaps, along with needs for load reduction, added resources, or redistribution. It does not authorize task adjustment, resource allocation, attribution of responsibility, or protection. Every real adjustment must separately pass C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: The interface itself generates no power to act in reality. Actual actions require separate checks of choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protection, and duration. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card: 1. The most visible low-authority executor is not the party responsible for decisions, authorization, or benefit; 2. An automated facility carries out transmission tasks but cannot bear moral or legal responsibility. Interpretation: Use counterexamples to limit unconditional extrapolation. They may require narrower scope or renewed evidence collection, not automatic rejection of every limited use. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, uptake providers may challenge tasks, resources, costs, restrictions on stopping rights, and attributions of responsibility through safe, accessible channels protected against retaliation, triggering review independent of the original task-assignment or responsibility-attribution chain. Interpretation: Appeals must be safely accessible, free from retaliation, and able to trigger independent review. A name alone does not establish authority to change errors. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, when rollback is authorized, designated responsible persons must revoke erroneous task, resource, or responsibility-attribution states within specified time limits, actually restore previous task and record states, and execute authorized remedies, preserving versions and completion verification. Interpretation: Within valid authority, actually revoke erroneous effects, correct downstream consequences, and verify completion. Editing document text does not mean rights and resources have returned to the person concerned. [T-main]
argumentSteps: First use H2 to separate CV, RS, cost bearers, beneficiaries, and stopping rights.
R0 describes current resources, capacity, and gaps, preserving hidden labor.
R1 uses G2 to examine the specified functional dimension, without turning local improvement into total burden reduction.
R3 uses H5 to examine traces on a uniquely identified carrier; future effects require another route.
Cross-period R2 requires G3 historical increments beyond the current representation; R4 is established through current-carrier continuity across cycles and subsequent channel evidence.
Check responsibility, norms, and authority separately, protecting uptake providers’ appeals and right to stop.
After correction is authorized, actually revoke erroneous tasks and attributions of responsibility, and verify that remedies arrive.

boundaries: Counterexample in the original card: the most visible low-authority executor is not the party responsible for decisions, authorization, or benefit.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: one task decreases while total burden remains undetermined
teachingExamples.text: An artificial care task originally requires 4 hours of execution, 1 hour of management, and 2 hours of standby. A replacement takes over the 4 execution hours, while the original provider still manages and remains on standby. A reduction of 4 execution hours can be recognized. Under a simple common time measure, 3 hours remain for the original provider, not zero. Actual total burden also includes overlapping time, psychological and resource factors, and more; 7 and 3 cannot simply be treated as complete welfare quantities.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All hours are artificial and assumed not to overlap; they only illustrate the difference between task and total endpoints.
teachingExamples.boundary: The remaining 3 hours do not negate the reduction of 4, and continuity requirements must not impose unlimited remaining responsibility on the original provider.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: three historical claims require separate evidence
teachingExamples.text: A fictional institution still preserves old training records: a trace candidate. Currently trained personnel apply their skills to service each period and receive replenishment: a carrier-continuity candidate. Under the same current representation of skills, rules, and resources, different historical paths still improve subsequent prediction or identification: a historical-increment candidate. These respectively require H5, the G2 and carrier-cycle material needed for R4, and the G2/G3 needed for R2. Preserved records alone cannot certify all three.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The institution, material, and comparisons are artificial; there are no formal instance results.
teachingExamples.boundary: “Candidate” is not supported. Increments beyond the current representation and transmission through current carriers neither exclude nor prove one another.

questionAnswers.question: Is the busiest person necessarily chiefly responsible?
questionAnswers.answer: No. CV, costs, and the six kinds of RS require separate checks; visible execution cannot establish responsibility for decisions or authorization.
questionAnswers.basis: H2 and the inferential leaps prohibited by this card.

questionAnswers.question: Can H5-supported traces establish future reproduction?
questionAnswers.answer: No. R3 establishes traces only; cross-period claims need separate evidence through R2 or R4.
questionAnswers.basis: R3 ceiling.

questionAnswers.question: Without G3, does every explanation of uptake across periods fail?
questionAnswers.answer: No. R4 explains carrier transmission through the current carrier, continuity over multiple cycles, and G2 evidence covering subsequent periods; it cannot pose as a G3 increment.
questionAnswers.basis: Difference between R4 and R2.

questionAnswers.question: If help reduces execution hours, can a local outcome be recognized?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes. Recognize it for the specified task and conditions; total-burden questions require additional checks on management, standby, and replacement-provider conditions.
questionAnswers.basis: Item 5 of evidence.
