A.6.title: A.6 HV06 Drive–Uptake Chain (Complete Interface Card)
A.6.lead: HV06 examines direction, generation, uptake, maintenance, and repayment segment by segment. Locally grounded segments, a candidate complete chain, and an effective channel are three different conclusions.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 4208–4293, original-site location /theory/appendix-a/a-06#section-a-6. The current full text is in the theory-v2 source; the historical research draft and excerpts remain downloadable in their original versions.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “One cannot simply multiply the average effects of the edges.” HV06 asks how the chain connects segment by segment from direction and generation through execution and maintenance to repayment. Every segment needs a channel, resources, costs, responsibility, and lag, rather than treating enthusiasm, vision, or commands as evidence that resources have arrived and maintenance has someone to undertake it. [T-main]

HV06-R0-segment-map requires only that inputs, outputs, delays, losses, interruptions, and resource and cost boundaries be observable for at least one chain segment. It permits descriptions of local segments, missing bridges, and cost positions, useful even before a complete chain exists. But one visible segment or a statement that “the drive is strong” cannot establish a complete or effective channel. [T-main]

HV06-R1-complete-chain-composition adds the HV03, HV04, and HV05 interfaces and requires segment-by-segment connections within the same mapping of object, scale, window, and quantities. This is composition of a candidate chain, not causal support for every edge. If upstream meaning expression is only R0, even the complete chain must retain its candidate status; drawing connections cannot automatically upgrade H1. [T-main; T-anchor; T-generation; T-carrier]

On top of a complete candidate chain, HV06-R2-effective-channel requires qualified G2 support for the specified channel, along with same-case correspondence, common support, joint responses, temporal capacity, and terminal outcomes sufficient to support the whole-chain effect in question, plus CAUSAL/E4. Edges from different populations or windows, upstream outputs exceeding downstream capacity, or mutually incompatible success conditions can all prevent individual average edge effects from combining into a whole-chain result. [T-main; T-G2]

A necessary check for “completeness” is alignment of quantities and objects, not a sufficient number of node names. An upstream output may be service places while a downstream input requires qualified personnel at specific times; the two are not equal merely because both are written as headcounts. Temporal order must also allow upstream outputs to arrive when the next segment needs them. Late resources cannot retroactively fill harm that has already occurred. [T-main]

One successful traversal does not establish reproduction across periods, justified goals, complete responsibility, or action authorization. Informal caregivers outside the boundary may bear costs, so the apparent chain keeps operating while draining reserves; subsequent maintenance may also lack continuity. Failure does not automatically mean insufficient willingness, much less that uptake providers should fill the gaps themselves. [T-main]

Register start-up, transmission, maintenance, and repayment lags segment by segment, retaining uncertainty about cross-organizational, low-visibility, and informal positions and alternative channels. Uptake providers and affected people along the chain must be able to challenge resources, costs, and attribution safely, with review outside the original chain’s judgments and decisions. Authorized rollback should revoke whole-chain attribution and downstream effects, restoring node-level descriptions and unresolved status without deleting locally grounded material. [T-main]

GOV.UK retirement guidance separately arranges uptake of needs, notification, redirection, and data protection, helping map distinct task nodes in a candidate chain. The guidance’s existence does not prove that a particular user reached a new service or that subsequent operating budgets are in place. It serves here as an R0/R1-style design comparison; a policy flowchart is not treated as whole-chain G2 support. [P-RETIRE]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card: HV06. Interpretation: This is a short identifier within the card collection, used to track the same interface; it does not mean that a real object has been proven. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card: human_variable:HV06. Interpretation: the namespace prevents naming collisions; references to this ID must still carry object and evidential status. [T-main]
03 | Name (name). Original card: Drive–uptake chain. Interpretation: the name provides a reading entry point, not an automatic label for particular people, groups, or real structures. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card: The chain from orientation and generation through execution, maintenance, and repayment must register channels, resources, costs, responsibilities, and lags segment by segment. Interpretation: read this proposition together with the subsequent conditional routes and ceilings; do not extract an unconditional causal or normative conclusion from one sentence. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card: Human collective action, projects, organizations, and institutional operation. Interpretation: scope lists task domains that may be studied, not empirical support for every object within them. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card: Enthusiasm, visions, or orders substitute for evidence of uptake and repayment. Interpretation: pausing concerns dependent judgment or adoption; independent descriptions may remain, but failed premises cannot continue to be used. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: Inferential dependencies provide the upstream content needed to establish a proposition. Upstream candidate/supported status must be carried through unchanged; citation does not automatically upgrade it. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. EVIDENCE; 2. SOURCE. Interpretation: Protocol dependencies constrain evidence collection and expression; completing protocols does not independently establish the truth of empirical propositions. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: an empty set means only that no such specialization relations are registered, not that evidential responsibility is absent; a nonempty set also does not imply universal validity. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card: 1. route_id=HV06-R0-segment-map; claim_level=descriptive_classification; when=Inputs, outputs, delays, losses, interruptions, resources, costs, and boundaries of at least one chain segment are observable.; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set); additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set); allowed_conclusion=Register local chain segments, missing bridges, lags, losses, interruption points, and cost positions.; result_ceiling=No claim of a complete chain or effective channel from a single segment or language of drive. 2. route_id=HV06-R1-complete-chain-composition; claim_level=descriptive_classification; when=Records for the three interfaces of orientation, generation, and uptake can be connected segment by segment within the same object, scale, window, and mapping of quantities.; additional_inferential_requires=human_variable:HV03, human_variable:HV04, human_variable:HV05; additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set); allowed_conclusion=Register a complete candidate drive–uptake chain and segment-by-segment evidence coverage.; result_ceiling=Candidate chain composition only; complete interface records do not mean each segment has causal efficacy. 3. route_id=HV06-R2-effective-channel; claim_level=mechanism_explanation; when=A complete candidate chain has been composed, an eligible G2-instance supports the specified channel, and same-case correspondence, common support, joint responses, timing, capacity, and terminal outcomes suffice to support the whole-chain effect at issue; average edge effects cannot simply be multiplied.; additional_inferential_requires=human_variable:HV03, human_variable:HV04, human_variable:HV05, G2-instance; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4; allowed_conclusion=Register effective drive–uptake channels and mechanisms of loss and interruption within tested segments and windows.; result_ceiling=One successful traversal cannot imply reproduction across periods, responsibility, justification, or action authorization. Interpretation: R0 covers local segments; R1 connects HV03/04/05 into a candidate chain under the same object, scale, window, and quantity mapping; R2 additionally checks G2, same-case common support, joint responses, timing, capacity, and terminal outcomes. Simply multiplying edge averages is prohibited. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card: 1. Chain bottlenecks; 2. Disconnection between drive and uptake; 3. Hidden repayment. Interpretation: these are permitted directions of conclusion; which is actually reached and with what strength remain limited by the selected route and materials. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card: 1. Strong drive equals sustainability; 2. Attributing failure to insufficient willingness; 3. Uptake providers should fill gaps themselves. Interpretation: these are common boundary violations, not avoided by rewording; inspect actual inference and downstream use, not wording alone. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=aggregation level: individual link events, chain cases, populations of similar chains, input/output distributions, and aggregation rules; X=spatial scope: action sites, project or organizational boundaries, digital collaboration spaces, and cross-domain spillovers; T=time span: initiation, maintenance, interruption, and recovery windows and cycles across periods; O=organizational level: initiating roles, execution teams, organizations, institutions, through governance ecosystems; C=causal level: link events, drive–resource–task interaction mechanisms, meso-level uptake chains, institutional arrangements, and systemic conditions; R=observational resolution: original task/resource records, link sequences, chain cases, loss distributions, performance indicators, and summaries, with compression loss registered; I=sphere of influence: direct initiating and uptake positions, indirect beneficiary or cost positions, second-order spillovers, cross-domain and intergenerational effects; N=network-topological scope: dependency chains, alternative paths, bottlenecks, feedback connections, and cross-domain bridges; J=jurisdiction and authorization scope: register authorization separately for goal adoption, task allocation, resource input, stopping, and experimentation; mark cross-axis positions segment by segment. Interpretation: register all nine axes individually; particularly, sphere of influence I creates no jurisdictional authority J, and lower observational resolution R requires retention of compression loss. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card: A traceable chain turning orientation and generation into sustained action. Interpretation: the traceable whole chain is the object of study; its name does not establish persistence in advance. R0 is local only, R1 candidate composition only, and R2 effects within tested windows only. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card: 1. Chains of orientation, generation, uptake, resources, costs, and responsibility. Interpretation: invariants are comparative responsibilities retained during transfer, not a declaration that variable values remain constant at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions on elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card: 1. Cross-level bridges; 2. Aggregation losses; 3. Responsibility inheritance; 4. Protection floors. Interpretation: elevation is not copying and enlarging the original table. Where materials on new populations, interfaces, responsibility positions, and so on are incomplete, restrict conclusions dependent on them. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card: 1. Nodes, channels, and bottlenecks may change with organizational scale. Interpretation: the same word may change meaning when the object or scale changes; reconstruct correspondence rather than assume the original meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Inapplicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card: 1. Nonhuman processes without intentional drive and human uptake. Interpretation: inapplicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of human normative, responsibility, and experiential interfaces; they do not deny that other theories can study these objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card: 1. Local drive or a single node directly representing the complete chain. Interpretation: inference from local to whole requires separate proof; broad impact, a grand name, or formal similarity cannot supply representativeness and authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card: 1. Connected through; 2. Lagging; 3. Overloaded; 4. Broken; 5. Replaced. Interpretation: states are descriptive classifications requiring evidence, not a maturity ladder for scoring people; state changes require windows, grounds, and versions. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card: 1. Records of anchors becoming tasks, budgets, rules, or schedules; 2. Inputs/outputs, delays, losses, and interruption points of each segment; 3. Changes in uptake providers’ capacity, stopping, and alternative paths; 4. The chain output’s actual contribution to target outcomes. Interpretation: separate tasks, budgets, and schedules from actual terminal contributions. Record delays and capacity for every segment, allowing bridge failures to be found rather than selecting successful endpoints only. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card: 1. Resource flows; 2. Task and maintenance records; 3. Repayment and costs; 4. Lags. Interpretation: obtain listed evidence according to route and task relevance; distinguish unknown, uncollected, inapplicable, and unavailable for protection, without forcing disclosure to fill a table. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface content (input_dependencies). Original card: 1. Orientation anchors; 2. Generative nodes; 3. Uptake layers. Interpretation: orientation, generation, and uptake are interfaces required for complete candidate chains under R1/R2; R0 needs at least one segment only, without fabricating all interfaces to describe a local gap. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flow (output_effects). Original card: 1. Action outcomes; 2. Loads; 3. Feedback and evolutionary traces. Interpretation: variable flow identifies downstream judgments that may depend on this interface; passing references guarantees neither downstream conclusions, actual repair, nor authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Register initiation, transmission, maintenance, and repayment lags segment by segment. Interpretation: occurrence, observation, execution, and arrival of effects may differ in time; short-term materials cannot automatically certify extensions beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record breaks, alternative channels, and repayment outside boundaries. Interpretation: direct uncertainty toward specific materials and positions; an overall confidence score cannot conceal fundamentally uncovered positions. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Informal, low-visibility, and cross-organizational uptake positions. Interpretation: exclusion zones limit current inferential coverage, not delete people or facts from the world; unavailability for safety is neither consent nor absence of problems. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Initiators; 2. Uptake providers; 3. Beneficiaries; 4. Cost bearers. Interpretation: register directly and indirectly affected parties together; visible members do not represent every cost bearer. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Personnel and posts; 2. Procedures; 3. Budgets; 4. Infrastructure. Interpretation: a carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something; its name, completed construction, and arrival of the required function are different evidence. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Those responsible for behavior, decisions, authorization, supervision, and remedies at each node. Interpretation: identify who proposes, operates, or uses judgments; recording responsibility is not automatically a legal-liability adjudication or new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: Chain effectiveness does not prove the goal justified. Interpretation: distinguish descriptive, normative, and bridging status according to the card. Established facts do not independently determine value rankings; normative reasons do not automatically prove empirical effects. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card: Up to explanatory or diagnostic level when evidence for the whole chain is sufficient. Interpretation: proportionate whole-chain materials permit explanation/diagnosis; R0/R1 retain local or candidate ceilings respectively, while one successful traversal under R2 still does not certify reproduction across periods. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card: This variable produces only descriptions of chain connectivity, lags, losses, interruptions, costs, and uptake needs; it authorizes no load reduction, resource adjustment, or experiment. Any real adjustment must separately pass C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: the interface itself creates no real-world authority to impose dispositions; actual actions separately require checking choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protections, and periods. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card: 1. Strong visions and concentrated mobilization lack sustained resources, maintenance, or repayment; 2. An apparently connected chain transfers key costs to uptake providers outside its boundary. Interpretation: counterexamples restrict unconditional extrapolation; they may require narrowing scope or gathering evidence anew, without automatically negating every bounded use. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, uptake or affected positions along the chain may challenge resources, costs, and chain attribution through safely accessible channels protected against retaliation, triggering review independent of the original chain judgment or decision chain. Interpretation: appeals must be safely accessible, free from retaliation, and capable of triggering independent review; a name alone does not mean authority to correct errors exists. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, when rollback is authorized, a designated responsible person must actually revoke whole-chain attribution and its downstream effects within the specified period, restore node-level descriptions and unresolved status, and preserve versions and completion verification. Interpretation: actually cancel erroneous effects within valid authorization, correct downstream uses, and verify completion; changing document wording does not restore rights and resources to the affected person. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Find observable chain segments and separately register inputs/outputs, resources and costs, delays, and boundaries.
R0 retains local facts and missing bridges without first inventing the whole chain.
R1 connects HV03/04/05 under the same object, scale, window, and quantity mapping.
R2 separately checks G2, same-case joint conditions, timing and capacity, and actual terminal outcomes.
Separate a one-time channel effect from persistence, responsibility, justification, and authorization.
If a whole-chain conclusion fails, revoke its overall effect, retain grounded nodes and unresolved status, and protect uptake providers.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two 50% rates do not guarantee 25% for the whole chain
teachingExamples.text: In 100 constructed same-case records, the first 50 succeed at segment one and fail at segment two; the last 50 fail at segment one and succeed at segment two. Each segment has a 50% success rate, but both succeed in 0/100=0% of the same cases, not 50%×50%=25%. This example only shows that marginal success rates cannot be multiplied unconditionally. Success rates are not causal effects either; formal G2 whole-chain judgments additionally require channel comparisons, capacity, timing, and endpoints.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A constructed table of complementary events, with no actual observations or randomized causal study.
teachingExamples.boundary: Does not deny that probabilities can factorize under explicit conditions; it prohibits using disproportionate edge averages as whole-chain effects.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: resources arrive late and no one maintains them
teachingExamples.text: A fictional project needs 10 units of service capacity on Monday, but procurement supplies them only on Friday, and no maintenance budget is registered. Procurement commitments and actual arrival may be recorded separately; Friday’s 10 units cannot be backfilled as Monday’s fulfilled need, nor can one launch imply subsequent maintenance. Care costs outside the boundary during the wait are listed separately, not attributed to weak willingness among uptake providers.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Dates, capacity, and project are constructed.
teachingExamples.boundary: Recording gaps authorizes no procurement, resource reallocation, or demands that others fill them.

A.7.title: A.7 HV07 Feedback write-back (complete interface card)
A.7.lead: HV07 closes receipt, updating, execution, feedback effects, and learning separately; effective write-back does not automatically mean correct correction or comprehensive improvement.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 4294–4381; original site location /theory/appendix-a/a-07#section-a-7. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research drafts and excerpts remain available for checking in their original downloadable versions.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “A single write-back is not called learning, and write-back does not equal correct correction.” HV07 distinguishes whether feedback arrived, fields changed, changes were executed, and whether they were subsequently retained, invoked, and produced task-level effects. Appeals, audits, or feedback count as institutional write-back in this interface only when they change records, rules, resources, roles, responsibilities, memory, or stopping conditions and are actually executed. [T-main；T-H3]

HV07-R0-writeback-classification checks inputs, receipts, versions, execution, taking effect, persistence, and stopping/rollback statuses under D2 and H3, distinguishing not submitted, submitted, accepted, fields changed, executed, persisting, or failed. Where receipt or statements produce no update, what pauses is the assertion that “institutional write-back is established,” not the value of having been safely heard. [T-main；T-D2]

A procedure that reasonably maintains a decision may also have value; every appeal should not be forced to change its outcome merely to raise reversal rates. Separately check response, understanding of evidence, correction of errors, and restoration of resources and rights. Write-back may itself be wrong, increase harm, or become biased through favorable feedback; effectiveness and content justification require separate judgments. [T-main；T-state]

HV07-R1-causal-feedback requires an eligible G2 to show that the return channel changes preselected subsequent states/transitions relative to no return or a blocked return, adding CAUSAL/E4. It registers feedback and write-back effects within specified fields, channels, and windows; a return path’s existence cannot imply long-term repair, correct goals, or expanded authorization. [T-main；T-G2]

HV07-R2-feedback-mediated-learning requires G2 for effective feedback and G3 support that retainable updates provide a historical conditional increment beyond the current representation for the predetermined task across repeated rounds. Its conclusion reaches only a candidate for learning through historical increment within the task, rounds, and window; it cannot claim that the institution as a whole has learned, its value direction is correct, or comprehensive repair is complete. [T-main; T-history]

HV07-R3-carried-learning is another route: effective feedback already has G2, then C3-carried-learning and §4.5 are used to check the current update carrier, retention across rounds, actual invocation, predetermined-task comparison, and causal grounds. An immediate-feedback instance does not automatically cover subsequent outcomes. It supports a candidate for carrier-transmitted learning within the specified carrier, task, and rounds, without obtaining G3/CM-LEARNING-history status; but lack of G3 support does not cancel this independently supported route either. [T-main; T-history; T-learning]

Training, archiving, publication, or one success alone is insufficient to count as learning; general learning, cross-task transfer, and net benefits should also be resolved separately. An update that is saved but never invoked lacks grounds for learning; if an update is invoked but increases the target error rate, record this according to the predetermined-task comparison, rather than declaring improvement because “the system did change.” [T-main]

The nine axes record cross-level feedback paths and resolution loss. Individual cases do not automatically represent the population; non-submission may arise from lack of digital access, safety threats, or protective anonymity. Silence cannot mean consent, and receipt counts cannot establish coverage of all positions. Separate responsibilities of recipients, decision-makers, write-back implementers, and overseers, with status, deadlines, and results open to independent review. [T-main]

When rollback is authorized, revoke erroneous updates and actually restore the corresponding records, rules, resources, roles, or stop conditions, preserving versions and completion verification. The module generates only needs for review/procedural repair; it does not itself change records, close appeals, or execute repairs, and protective needs do not automatically expand power. [T-main]

The Robodebt website explicitly records the report’s publication and corrected-version dates, and lists recommendations on frontline feedback and automated review. Version notices, recommendation texts, institutional implementation, and actual remedies for residents are different materials. This topic reads only the website, without comparing the PDFs or investigating implementation, so correction notices and published recommendations are not described as learning by the entire institution. [P-ROBO]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card, translated: HV07. Explanation: this is a short identifier within the card collection, tracking the same interface; it does not indicate that a real object has been established. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card, translated: human_variable:HV07. Explanation: the qualified namespace prevents name collisions; references to this ID must still carry the object and evidence status. [T-main]

03 | Name (name). Original card, translated: Feedback Write-Back. Explanation: the name provides a reading entry point, not an automatic label for specific people, groups, or real structures. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card, translated: Appeals, audits, and feedback constitute human institutional write-back only when they change records, rules, resources, roles, responsibilities, memory, or stop conditions and the corresponding changes have actually been executed. Explanation: this proposition must be understood together with the conditional routes and ceilings below; unconditional causal or normative conclusions cannot be extracted from one sentence. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card, translated: Human structures with feedback, appeal, audit, or governance procedures. Explanation: the scope lists task domains that may be examined; it does not mean all objects within it have empirical support. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card, translated: When there are only receipts, statements, or publication without a state update, or field changes have not yet actually been executed, pause claims that institutional write-back holds; bounded states such as submitted, accepted, and fields changed remain classified under R0. Explanation: with only receipts, statements, publication, or unexecuted field changes, pause claims of institutional write-back while retaining bounded R0 achievements such as submission and acceptance. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card, translated: 1. D2. Explanation: inferential dependencies supply the upstream content required for a proposition to hold; upstream candidate/supported status must be passed unchanged, and citation does not automatically elevate it. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. EVIDENCE; 2. SOURCE. Interpretation: Protocol dependencies constrain evidence collection and expression; completing protocols does not independently establish the truth of empirical propositions. [T-main]

11 | Qualification/specialization (specializes). Original card, translated: 1. H3. Explanation: H3 is a classification rule for institutional write-back, classifying by the point actually completed; it is not itself evidence of empirical effects, still less a requirement that every valuable appeal change the original decision. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card, translated: 1. route_id=HV07-R0-writeback-classification;; claim_level=descriptive_classification;; when=Input channels, receipts, before-and-after field versions, execution records, effective times, durations, and stop or rollback states can be checked separately.;; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set);; additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set);; allowed_conclusion=Distinguish write-back states of not submitted, submitted, accepted, fields changed, executed, persisting, or no longer effective.;; result_ceiling=Only fields changed and actually executed count as institutional write-back; one write-back does not count as learning, nor does write-back equal correct error correction. The procedural value of a reasoned decision to maintain the decision and other changes that have occurred are retained according to their respective evidence.; 2. route_id=HV07-R1-causal-feedback;; claim_level=mechanism_explanation;; when=A qualified G2-instance shows that an institutional return channel changes a preselected subsequent state or transition relative to absent or blocked return conditions.;; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register effective feedback and institutional write-back effects within the specified fields, channels, and window.;; result_ceiling=The existence of feedback must not imply learning, long-term repair, justification, or expanded authorization.; 3. route_id=HV07-R2-feedback-mediated-learning;; claim_level=intertemporal_explanation;; when=Effective feedback already has G2-instance support, and a G3-instance shows that retainable updates provide a historical conditional increment for the predetermined task across repeated rounds.;; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance, G3-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register a candidate for feedback-mediated learning through historical increment beyond the current state within the specified task, rounds, and window.;; result_ceiling=Must not claim that the institution as a whole has learned, repair is complete, or the value direction is correct.; 4. route_id=HV07-R3-carried-learning;; claim_level=intertemporal_explanation;; when=Effective feedback already has qualified G2-instance support, and C3-carried-learning and §4.5 are used to verify the current update carrier, retention and actual invocation across rounds, predetermined-task comparison, and its causal grounds; an immediate-feedback instance does not automatically cover subsequent task outcomes.;; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register a candidate for carrier-transmitted feedback-mediated learning within the specified update carrier, task, and rounds.;; result_ceiling=Does not obtain CM-LEARNING-history or G3 historical-increment status, does not directly call training, archiving, write-back, or one success learning, and does not claim improvement of the institution as a whole. Explanation: R0 classifies processes; R1 covers G2 return-channel effects; R2 covers G2 + G3 learning through historical increment; R3 covers carrier-based learning through G2 + update-carrier retention and invocation and task comparison. One update must not be directly elevated to learning under any route. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inferences (allowed_inference). Original card, translated: 1. Effective write-back, blocked write-back, and superficial feedback. Explanation: these are permitted directions of conclusion; which is actually reached, and at what strength, remains limited by the selected route and materials. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leaps (prohibited_leap). Original card, translated: 1. A channel guarantees learning; 2. One update equals long-term repair; 3. Silence equals consent. Explanation: these are common overreaches that cannot be avoided merely by rephrasing; check actual inference and subsequent use, not wording alone. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card, translated: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=aggregation level: single feedback items or appeals, write-back cases, feedback populations, acceptance/execution distributions, and aggregation rules; X=spatial scope: submission channels, organizational or platform boundaries, institutional jurisdictions, and cross-domain appeal scope; T=time span: submission, acceptance, field change, execution, persistence, and review lags; O=organizational level: feedback roles, receiving teams, organizations, institutions, through to governance ecosystems; C=causal level: feedback events, write-back interaction mechanisms, mesoscopic procedural structures, institutional rules, and system conditions; R=observation resolution: original feedback, handling sequences, write-back cases, outcome distributions, timeliness indicators, and summaries, recording compression losses; I=influence scope: direct appellants and those taking up their appeals, indirectly affected people, second-order institutional consequences, cross-domain and intergenerational effects; N=network topology scope: feedback channels, receiving nodes, review paths, blockages, and cross-level connections; J=jurisdiction and authorization scope: register authorization separately for acceptance, field modification, execution, stopping, rollback, and remedy; register cross-level paths. Explanation: register all nine axes individually; in particular, influence scope I does not produce jurisdictional permission J, and compression losses must be retained when observation resolution R decreases. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card, translated: Return channels that change subsequent institutional states or transitions. Explanation: this describes the object corresponding to the interface; when choosing a low-threshold descriptive route, the functional meaning in its name cannot be treated as established causation. [T-main]

18 | Scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card, translated: 1. Feedback sources, channels, write-back fields, and subsequent changes. Explanation: invariants are comparative responsibilities to preserve during transfer, not a claim that variable values remain unchanged at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required scale additions (required_scale_additions). Original card, translated: 1. Feedback representativeness; 2. Cross-level write-back paths; 3. Aggregation losses; 4. External review. Explanation: elevation is not copying and enlarging the original table. When materials about new populations, interfaces, responsibility positions, and so on are incomplete, limit conclusions dependent on them. [T-main]

20 | Changing semantics (changing_semantics). Original card, translated: 1. Write-back carriers, lags, and responsible parties may change. Explanation: the same word may change meaning when the object or scale changes; rebuild correspondences rather than assuming the original meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Non-applicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card, translated: 1. Processes without records, rules, resources, roles, or stop conditions. Explanation: non-applicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of human normative, responsibility, and experience interfaces; they do not deny that other theories can study these objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card, translated: 1. Feedback from individual cases directly represents the population’s opinions. Explanation: inference from local to whole needs separate support; broad influence, grand names, or formal similarity cannot supply missing representativeness or authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card, translated: 1. Arrived; 2. Accepted; 3. Written back; 4. Blocked; 5. Distorted. Explanation: states are descriptive classifications requiring evidence, not a maturity ladder for scoring people; state changes require a window, grounds, and version. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card, translated: 1. Proof of submission and acceptance of feedback or appeals; 2. Version differences in records, rules, resources, roles, responsibilities, or stop conditions; 3. Execution records, effective times, and durations of changes; 4. Review, revocation, remedy, and subsequent state changes. Explanation: observable leads indicate where to seek materials; a single lead is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card, translated: 1. Original feedback; 2. Acceptance trail; 3. Field versions; 4. Subsequent rule or resource changes. Explanation: obtain evidence according to route and task relevance; distinguish unknown, uncollected, not applicable, and unavailable for protection, without forcing disclosure to fill the table. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface contents (input_dependencies). Original card, translated: 1. Feedback sources; 2. Safe channels; 3. Responsible persons; 4. Review procedures. Explanation: this specifies what comes from upstream and its qualifications; gaps cannot silently disappear during transfer between interfaces. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flows (output_effects). Original card, translated: 1. Updates to records, rules, resources, roles, responsibilities, memory, or stop conditions. Explanation: the original card lists update types; which field actually changed and was executed, and when it took effect, require versions and external states. Listing seven types does not mean all were updated. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card, translated: Register deadlines for submission, acceptance, decision, execution, and review. Explanation: occurrence, observation, execution, and arrival of effects may happen at different times; short-term materials cannot automatically certify extension beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card, translated: Record undelivered feedback, protective anonymity, and invisible handling. Explanation: tie uncertainty to specific materials and positions; a single overall confidence score must not conceal positions that were never covered. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card, translated: Positions unable to submit safely, facing threats concerning retaliation, or lacking digital access. Explanation: exclusion zones limit the coverage of current inferences; they do not erase these people or facts from the world, and safety-related unavailability does not mean consent or absence of problems. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card, translated: 1. Submitters; 2. Those evaluated; 3. Implementers; 4. Institutional beneficiaries. Explanation: register both directly and indirectly affected people; visible members do not represent everyone bearing costs. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carriers (carrier). Original card, translated: 1. Appeal systems; 2. Audit procedures; 3. Meeting records; 4. Rule repositories; 5. Responsibility chains. Explanation: carriers are the structures or processes actually carrying something; the carrier’s name, completed construction, and delivery of required functions are different evidence. [T-main]

33 | Responsible parties (responsible_subject). Original card, translated: 1. Recipients; 2. Decision-makers; 3. Write-back implementers; 4. Overseers. Explanation: specify who proposes the judgment and who operates or uses it; registering responsibility does not automatically adjudicate legal liability or issue new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card, translated: Assess feedback effectiveness and justification of feedback content separately. Explanation: an effective channel may return erroneous or unjustified content. Whether errors are correctly corrected, people are protected, and overall net benefits arise cannot be inferred directly from the fact of write-back. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card, translated: R0 judges the actual point of completion in the write-back process; R1 judges return-channel effects with corresponding G2 support; R3 judges carrier-based feedback-mediated learning through update retention, invocation across rounds, and task comparison; R2 judges learning through historical increment only with additional G3. One write-back, general learning, transfer, and net benefits are resolved separately. Explanation: completion points, channel effects, carrier-based learning, and learning through historical increment are separate; general learning, transfer, and net benefits do not share a resolution either. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card, translated: This variable generates only descriptions of acceptance, field changes, execution, duration, and write-back gaps, and needs for review or procedural repair; it does not authorize rewriting records or rules, executing repairs, or closing appeals. Any real-world adjustment must separately pass C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O procedures. Explanation: the interface itself produces no real-world authority to act; actual actions require separate checks of choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protections, and time limits. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card, translated: 1. An appeal receives an acknowledgment, but records, rules, resources, and stop conditions are all unchanged; 2. An audit report is published without a responsible person, deadline, or subsequent state update. Explanation: use counterexamples to limit unconditional extrapolation; they may require narrowing scope or collecting evidence again, but do not automatically invalidate every bounded use. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card, translated: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, feedback submitters may request status, deadlines, responsible persons, and write-back results through safely accessible anti-retaliation channels, and trigger review independent of the original acceptance, write-back, or decision chain. Explanation: appeals must be safely accessible, free of retaliation, and able to trigger independent review; a name alone does not mean there is power to correct errors. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card, translated: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, when rollback is authorized, a designated responsible person must revoke erroneous updates within the specified time, actually restore previous states of records, rules, resources, roles, or stop conditions, and preserve versions and completion verification. Explanation: within valid authorization, actually revoke erroneous effects, correct downstream consequences, and verify completion; changing document wording does not mean rights and resources have been restored to the person concerned. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Under R0, check inputs, acceptance, field versions, actual execution, and persistence.
Retain the procedural value of being heard and of a reasoned decision to maintain a decision; do not demand reversal.
R1 uses G2 to compare subsequent states under return and blockage.

Learning requires separate checks of updates across rounds: R2 checks G3 historical increment beyond the current representation, while R3 checks retention and invocation of current carriers and task comparison.
Evaluate general learning, transfer, net benefits, and repair separately.
Protect people who have not entered safely and allow independent review; after authorization, actually roll back erroneous updates.

Can one write-back establish that the institution has learned?
Does R3 automatically obtain G3 status?
Is effective feedback necessarily correct?

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: four states do not share a single completion marker
teachingExamples.text: A constructed appeal is submitted on Monday, accepted on Tuesday, has fields modified on Thursday, and only the following Monday has resource restoration actually executed. Tuesday may be recorded as accepted, not resources restored; Thursday’s field changes also do not establish execution. Even after the corresponding restoration arrives the following Monday, one case does not establish long-term learning by the entire institution or positive net benefits.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The timeline and resource records are fictional.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual restoration and authorization require independent evidence; the bounded value of hearing and acceptance themselves is not denied.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: retained updates must still be invoked and compared
teachingExamples.text: A constructed program saves a correction rule in version v2 but still runs v1 for the next three rounds. Archiving does not prove that v2 produced learning effects. Even if v2 is actually invoked for three later rounds, predefined task comparisons and causal materials remain necessary. Any historical increment beyond the current representation additionally requires G3 testing; invocation counts are not universal proof.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Program versions and rounds are constructed.
teachingExamples.boundary: R3 requires no additional G3, but does require its own retention, invocation, and task comparison; R2 separately bears responsibility for historical increments.

questionAnswers.question: Are appeals that do not change the original decision entirely valueless?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Reasoned maintenance, hearing, and other actual changes remain according to independent evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: R0 inference ceiling.

questionAnswers.question: Can one write-back establish that the institution has learned?
questionAnswers.answer: No; retention and invocation across rounds, task comparisons, and the corresponding routes require separate checks.

questionAnswers.question: Does R3 automatically obtain G3 status?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Carrier-mediated transmission is not a historical increment beyond the current representation.
questionAnswers.basis: R3 ceiling.

questionAnswers.question: Is effective feedback necessarily correct?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Content justification and correct correction are judged separately.
questionAnswers.basis: normative_status。

A.8.title: A.8 HV08 Conditional potential field (complete interface card)
A.8.lead: HV08 separates condition inventories, position/mediation effects, immediate reflexive responses, and carrier-mediated persistence. Environments are not intentional subjects, and conditional effects do not determine every person’s behavior.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 4382–4469; original site location /theory/appendix-a/a-08#section-a-8. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; historical research drafts and excerpts remain available for checking in their original downloadable versions.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “The name ‘potential field’ presupposes no potential function, common unit, or physical conservation.” HV08 conditions may include resources, rules, relationships, power, safety, indicators, platforms, AI mediation, and historical deposits. The name organizes inquiry; it is not a physical-field model, still less an intentional subject called the environment or proof of malice from a power label. [T-main]

HV08-R0-condition-inventory permits candidate conditions, positional heterogeneity, blind spots, competing explanations, and supplementary-evidence needs when conditions can be listed by position, scale, and window but no eligible H4-instance exists yet. An inventory does not prove masking/amplification, behavioral effects, or reflexive effects. Under the same institutional label, different safety and dependency positions may show opposite actions. [T-main]

HV08-R1-position-or-mediation-effect requires H4 to obtain supported on the uniquely preselected success criterion among evidence coverage, safety of expression, or object behavior, adding CAUSAL/E4. It supports masking, amplification, or behavioral-response channels for particular positions, mediators, outcome families, and windows. One cannot retrospectively choose the most favorable of the three families, still less directly infer malice, responsibility, or disposition eligibility from a positional effect. [T-main；T-H4]

HV08-R2-reflexive-response must uniquely preselect a reflexive-response criterion; observation, naming, scoring, or publication must reach the object through an actual channel and obtain H4 supported, adding E3, CAUSAL, and E4. A researcher’s writing a report is not the object’s receiving it; awareness of observation does not automatically prove consequent behavioral change. Channel arrival, response, and competing explanations each require evidence. [T-main；T-H4]

HV08-R3-carried-reflexive-persistence further requires H4 to cover the declared cross-window scope and, under §4.5, checks that the response enters a current carrier, is retained or updated, and has persistent effects, comparing repeated stimulation, ongoing observation, common changes, and other explanations. One immediate response cannot directly become persistent reflexivity; carrier-mediated persistence also gains no eligibility as a G3 historical increment beyond the current representation. [T-main；T-history]

For example, behavioral change one week after scores are published may result from continuing reminders rather than a lasting carrier left by one publication; simultaneous rule changes may also produce common change. A claim of persistent reflexive response requires explicit windows, carriers, and comparisons; elapsed time is not independent evidence. Even if established, it does not permit covert observation, suppression of expression, or expanded authorization in the name of “avoiding reflexivity.” [T-main]

Across nine axes, retain position distributions, cross-domain externalities, the J axis, and different resolutions. Sparse data cannot imply no effects at positions invisible because of low safety, status, or platform barriers; protective indications do not automatically prove particular mechanisms either. Condition accumulation, response, and decay have different lags; collinear conditions and unobservable factors must be explicitly listed as unknowns. [T-main]

Outputs describe candidate condition channels, positional heterogeneity, evidence masking, and risk-reduction needs; they authorize no changes to rules, platforms, resources, evaluations, or dispositions. Different positions may raise mechanism differences, absent signals, and safety impacts and obtain independent review. Authorized rollback must revoke unsupported attributions, remove position labels and their downstream evaluative/dispositional effects, restore unresolved status, and verify completion. [T-main]

The authors’ institutional abstract for Guess et al. 2023 reports a three-month feed study in 2020: usage and exposure changed, while several attitude endpoints did not change significantly. This bounded finding highlights why outcome families cannot be merged; it does not prove every platform’s “potential field” or individual motives. The original journal full text was inaccessible on this occasion; this lesson claims neither complete methodological review nor H4 supported. [P-GUESS]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card: HV08. Interpretation: the short identifier within the cardbook tracks the same interface; it does not indicate that a real-world object has been proved. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card: human_variable:HV08. Interpretation: the namespace prevents naming collisions; references to this ID must still carry object and evidential status. [T-main]

03 | Name (name). Original card: Conditional potential field. Interpretation: the name provides a reading entry point, not an automatic label for particular people, groups, or real structures. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card: Resources, institutions, relationships, power, safety, indicators, platforms, and historical conditions enter a conditional explanation for an outcome family only when they change the corresponding route’s uniquely preselected evidence coverage, safety of expression, object behavior, or reflexive response through detectable mechanisms and obtain corresponding H4-instance support. Interpretation: register the conditional explanation only when the corresponding H4 instance supports the uniquely preselected outcome family; condition names and background narratives supply no causal support. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card: Settings where human action is affected by contexts, institutions, and positions of power. Interpretation: scope lists task domains that may be studied, not empirical support for every object within them. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card: Treating the potential field as a universal background, intentional subject, or moral label. Interpretation: pausing concerns dependent judgment or adoption; independent descriptions may remain, but failed premises cannot continue to be used. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: Inferential dependencies provide the upstream content needed to establish a proposition. Upstream candidate/supported status must be carried through unchanged; citation does not automatically upgrade it. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card: 1. E2; 2. EVIDENCE; 3. SOURCE. Interpretation: protocol dependencies constrain evidence gathering and expression; completing protocols does not independently prove an empirical proposition true. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: an empty set means only that no such specialization relations are registered, not that evidential responsibility is absent; a nonempty set also does not imply universal validity. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card: 1. route_id=HV08-R0-condition-inventory; claim_level=candidate_description; when=Resources, rules, positions, safety, indicators, platforms, AI mediation, or historical deposits can be listed by position, scale, and time window, but no eligible H4-instance exists yet.; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set); additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set); allowed_conclusion=Register candidate conditions, positional heterogeneity, observational blind spots, competing explanations, and supplementary-evidence needs.; result_ceiling=Condition inventories or candidate channels only; do not personify conditions or claim established power, mediation, or reflexive effects. 2. route_id=HV08-R1-position-or-mediation-effect; claim_level=conditional_effect; when=H4-instance obtains supported on the uniquely preselected success criterion among evidence coverage, safety of expression, or object behavior.; additional_inferential_requires=H4-instance; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4; allowed_conclusion=Register masking, amplification, or behavioral-response channels within that instance’s positions, mediators, outcome family, and window.; result_ceiling=Do not extrapolate to unselected outcome families or infer malice, responsibility, or automatic disposition from positional or mediation effects. 3. route_id=HV08-R2-reflexive-response; claim_level=mechanism_explanation; when=H4-instance uniquely preselects a reflexive-response criterion, and observation, naming, scoring, or publication reaches the object through an actual channel and obtains supported.; additional_inferential_requires=H4-instance; additional_protocol_requires=E3, CAUSAL, E4; allowed_conclusion=Register reflexive responses within the specified observation or publication channel and window.; result_ceiling=One response is not persistent reflexivity; it cannot justify hidden observation, suppressed expression, or expanded authorization. 4. route_id=HV08-R3-carried-reflexive-persistence; claim_level=intertemporal_explanation; when=H4-instance obtains supported on the uniquely preselected reflexive-response criterion and within the declared cross-window scope, and §4.5 checks the response’s entry into a current carrier, retention or updating, and persistent effects, comparing repeated stimulation, continuing observation, common changes, and other explanatory materials.; additional_inferential_requires=H4-instance; additional_protocol_requires=E3, CAUSAL, E4; allowed_conclusion=Register persistent reflexive responses within the specified observation or publication channel, current carrier, and window.; result_ceiling=Do not extrapolate persistence from immediate H4 effects, acquire G3 historical-increment eligibility, or justify hidden observation, suppressed expression, or expanded authorization. Interpretation: R0 inventories; R1 preselects one of coverage/safety/behavior; R2 preselects reflexive response with actual channel arrival; R3 additionally requires a current carrier across windows and persistent effects. R2/R3 both add E3; their conclusions cannot cover for covert observation. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card: 1. Conditional opportunities, constraints, masking, and amplification. Interpretation: these are permitted directions of conclusion; which is actually reached and with what strength remain limited by the selected route and materials. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card: 1. Conditions determine individual behavior; 2. A power position proves malice; 3. The environment has intention. Interpretation: these are common boundary violations, not avoided by rewording; inspect actual inference and downstream use, not wording alone. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=aggregation level: individual exposure or evaluation events, position cases, populations subject to conditions, response distributions, and aggregation rules; X=spatial scope: interaction sites, organizational or platform boundaries, public digital spaces, and cross-domain environments; T=time span: windows of exposure accumulation, response, reflexive change, and decay; O=organizational level: action and evaluation roles, teams, organizations, institutions, through governance ecosystems; C=causal level: exposure events, condition–behavior interaction mechanisms, meso-level power structures, institutional rules, and systemic conditions; R=observational resolution: original exposures, expressions, and behaviors, time series, position cases, response distributions, platform indicators, and summaries, with compression loss registered; I=sphere of influence: those directly evaluated, indirectly affected people, second-order reflexive consequences, cross-domain and intergenerational effects; N=network-topological scope: power and information connections, mediating nodes, masked zones, amplification paths, and cross-domain dissemination; J=jurisdiction and authorization scope: register authorization separately for rule configuration, indicator use, public evaluation, human review, and disposition; compare positional heterogeneity. Interpretation: register all nine axes individually; particularly, sphere of influence I creates no jurisdictional authority J, and lower observational resolution R requires retention of compression loss. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card: R0 registers sets of potentially relevant conditions; R1/R2 judge their effects on preselected outcomes from corresponding evidence. The name “potential field” presupposes no potential function, common unit, or physical conservation. Interpretation: the original card explicitly presupposes no physical potential function, common unit, or conservation; different resource, safety, and power indicators cannot be arbitrarily summed into one physical quantity. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card: 1. Mechanism chains from conditions to behavior or evidence. Interpretation: invariants are comparative responsibilities retained during transfer, not a declaration that variable values remain constant at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions on elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card: 1. Position distributions; 2. Conditional heterogeneity; 3. Cross-domain externalities; 4. J axis. Interpretation: elevation is not copying and enlarging the original table. Where materials on new populations, interfaces, responsibility positions, and so on are incomplete, restrict conclusions dependent on them. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card: 1. Key conditions and effect strengths may change with scale. Interpretation: the same word may change meaning when the object or scale changes; reconstruct correspondence rather than assume the original meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Inapplicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card: 1. Nonhuman systems without intentional action, power, or institutional positions. Interpretation: inapplicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of human normative, responsibility, and experiential interfaces; they do not deny that other theories can study these objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card: 1. Directly universalizing local conditions into every subject’s motives. Interpretation: inference from local to whole requires separate proof; broad impact, a grand name, or formal similarity cannot supply representativeness and authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card: 1. Supportive; 2. Constraining; 3. Masking; 4. Amplifying; 5. Mixed. Interpretation: states are descriptive classifications requiring evidence, not a maturity ladder for scoring people; state changes require windows, grounds, and versions. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card: 1. Behavioral differences before/after changes in resources, rules, platforms, or public conditions; 2. Safety of expression, evidence coverage, and absence rates at different positions; 3. Visibility and disposition changes before/after indicators, scores, or AI mediation; 4. Whether candidate-channel effects under comparison conditions exceed predetermined thresholds. Interpretation: observable indications tell us where to seek materials; a single indication’s presence is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card: 1. Resources and rules; 2. Positional differences; 3. Platform or indicator changes; 4. Behavioral responses. Interpretation: obtain listed evidence according to route and task relevance; distinguish unknown, uncollected, inapplicable, and unavailable for protection, without forcing disclosure to fill a table. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface content (input_dependencies). Original card: 1. Boundaries and interfaces; 2. Observation positions; 3. Causal contracts. Interpretation: this states what arrives from upstream and its eligibility; gaps cannot quietly disappear while passing between interfaces. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flow (output_effects). Original card: 1. Feasible paths; 2. Expression and evidence; 3. Generation and destabilization. Interpretation: variable flow identifies downstream judgments that may depend on this interface; passing references guarantees neither downstream conclusions, actual repair, nor authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Register lags in condition accumulation, response, and decay. Interpretation: occurrence, observation, execution, and arrival of effects may differ in time; short-term materials cannot automatically certify extensions beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record unobservable conditions, collinearity, and reflexive changes. Interpretation: collinearity, unobservable conditions, and reflexive changes may supply competing explanations; a “complex potential field” cannot bypass them. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Positions invisible because of safety, status, or platform barriers. Interpretation: exclusion zones limit current inferential coverage, not delete people or facts from the world; unavailability for safety is neither consent nor absence of problems. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Advantaged positions; 2. Low-power positions; 3. Mediators; 4. Those evaluated. Interpretation: register directly and indirectly affected parties together; visible members do not represent every cost bearer. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Institutions; 2. Resource allocation; 3. Platforms; 4. Indicators; 5. Relational networks; 6. Historical deposits. Interpretation: a carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something; its name, completed construction, and arrival of the required function are different evidence. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Rule-makers; 2. Platform operators; 3. Resource allocators; 4. Action decision-makers. Interpretation: identify who proposes, operates, or uses judgments; recording responsibility is not automatically a legal-liability adjudication or new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: Conditional advantages or selection outcomes do not constitute justification. Interpretation: distinguish descriptive, normative, and bridging status according to the card. Established facts do not independently determine value rankings; normative reasons do not automatically prove empirical effects. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card: R0 lists candidate conditions only; R1 and R2 form position or reflexive-response judgments within selected H4 outcomes and windows; R3 additionally requires evidence of current carriers, retention across windows, and persistent effects. Immediate effects do not extrapolate to persistence; established channels generate no conclusions about malice, responsibility, or authorization. Interpretation: immediate positional or reflexive effects are limited to R1/R2 selected outcomes and windows; persistent R3 additionally checks current carriers and cross-window evidence, without automatically acquiring G3 or conclusions about malice or responsibility. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card: This variable produces only descriptions of candidate condition channels, positional heterogeneity, evidence masking, and risk-reduction needs; it authorizes no changes to rules/platforms, resource allocation, evaluation, or disposition of subjects. Any real adjustment must separately pass C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: the interface itself creates no real-world authority to impose dispositions; actual actions separately require checking choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protections, and periods. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card: 1. Different safety and power positions display opposite actions under the same institutional conditions; 2. Replacing actual causal channels with power or platform labels leaves state changes unexplained. Interpretation: counterexamples restrict unconditional extrapolation; they may require narrowing scope or gathering evidence anew, without automatically negating every bounded use. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card, translated from Chinese: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, different positions may submit mechanism differences, signals of absence, and safety effects through safely reachable, anti-retaliation channels, triggering review independent of the original potential-field judgment or decision chain. Interpretation: Appeals must be safely reachable, protected against retaliation, and able to trigger independent review; a channel name alone does not establish power to change an error. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card, translated from Chinese: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, once rollback is authorized, a designated responsible person must actually revoke unsupported potential-field attributions, remove position labels and their downstream evaluation and action effects, and restore unresolved status within the stipulated time, preserving versions and completion verification. Interpretation: Within valid authorization, actually revoke erroneous effects, correct downstream consequences, and verify completion. Changing document wording does not mean rights and resources have been restored to the person concerned. [T-main]
argumentSteps: List conditions and blind spots by position, scale, and window; retain candidates under R0.
Before seeking R1, uniquely preselect evidence coverage, expressive safety, or a behavioral endpoint.
Seeking R2 requires confirming that observation, naming, scoring, or release reached the object, then checking reflexive responses.
Seeking R3 additionally requires checking current carriers, persistence across windows, and competing explanations.
Each route is bounded by its outcome family and window; effects imply neither malicious responsibility nor new authority.
Permit different positions to challenge attributions safely; after authorization, remove labels and downstream action effects.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: arrival, response, and persistence are three different things
teachingExamples.text: A constructed study releases a score on day 1, but verifiable receipt occurs only on day 4. Changes on day 2 cannot be attributed solely from publication to the effect of a score that had reached the object. After a response on day 5, if reminders continue daily, persistence until day 30 still cannot independently establish that one stimulus left a lasting carrier; corresponding cross-window material and competing explanations are needed.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All event dates are fictional, used to check sequence and arrival.
teachingExamples.boundary: No actual behavioral mechanism is established; actual disclosure or observation still requires privacy protection and authority.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: no substitution across outcome families
teachingExamples.text: A constructed preregistration tests only expressive safety. Later, posting volume rises, but safety scales and anti-retaliation material do not support improvement. More posts cannot be directly relabeled as greater safety. The object's behavior can become a separate exploratory topic, preserving distinct families and gaps.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Fictional indicators, with no formal H4 record.
teachingExamples.boundary: Activity volume, expressive safety, coverage, and reflexive responses cannot establish one another; failure to support one item does not imply all conditions are ineffective.

questionAnswers.question: Can the potential field be calculated directly by summing physical energy?
questionAnswers.answer: This interface presupposes no common unit, potential function, or conservation law; a testable model and evidence must be established separately.
questionAnswers.basis: effective_object。

questionAnswers.question: Does a change in the research object's behavior establish reflexivity?
questionAnswers.answer: Channels through which observation, naming, and the like reach the object, plus support for a preselected H4 reflexive response, are required; simultaneous changes alone are insufficient.

questionAnswers.question: Must R3 claim a G3 historical increment?
questionAnswers.answer: It cannot automatically make that claim. It is a route for persistence through current carriers; G3 qualification requires separate proof.
questionAnswers.basis: R3 ceiling.

questionAnswers.question: Does having power establish malice?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Position, mechanism, intention, and responsibility require separate evidence.
questionAnswers.basis: Prohibited leap.
