A.9.title: A.9 HV09 Structural Load (Complete Interface Card)
A.9.lead: Fewer tasks do not mean costs have disappeared, and being able to bear a burden does not mean one ought to. HV09 first examines tasks, capacity, recovery, and specific cost-bearing positions together.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 4470–4557; original site location /theory/appendix-a/a-09#section-a-9. For the current full text, see the theory-v2 source; historical research manuscripts and excerpts remain available for checking in their original downloadable versions.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: “High efficiency or high carrying capacity does not constitute justification.” HV09's object is not abstract entropy but the relation of task and coordination demands to capacity and recovery margins under mappings of specific windows, positions, and types. Tasks, coordination losses, maintenance, capacity, recovery, and cost-bearing positions must be registered together; being able to withstand a burden does not mean one should continue to bear it. [T-main]

HV09-R0-instant-task-capacity provides only same-window descriptions, without requiring G2 or CM-LOAD to hold beforehand. Tasks, margins, backlogs, local gaps, and recovery states may be recorded, but one person's shortfall today cannot independently establish damage, an overload mechanism, or inevitable collapse. Same-window data require consistent units and preservation of the distribution of cost-bearing positions. [T-main]

HV09-R1-overload-mechanism requires complete applicability of CM-LOAD and qualified G2 identification of an above-threshold effect of load, replenishment, load-reduction, or recovery channels on the preselected outcome, with CAUSAL/E4 added. It then permits mechanism candidates bounded by position, type, and window. No channel is generalized into an entropy law for all positions, nor is an obligation created concerning who must reduce load or make sacrifices. [T-main; T-load]

HV09-R2-cumulative-overload requires G3 in addition to G2 and CM-LOAD: historical load must have a conditional increment for subsequent capacity, errors, or recovery beyond the current representation. HV09-R3-carried-cumulative-overload instead checks current damage or capacity carriers, formation, retention or recovery, and discriminating cross-window causal material under §4.5. G2 covers the outcomes in the claimed window, without registering G3 qualification. Neither route holds merely because years of busyness are observed. [T-main; T-history]

Once a momentary gap is resolved, no lasting difference may remain; capacity can also expand alongside demand and absorb it. Accumulation is not necessarily monotonic. H5 traces support only trace candidates and cannot replace later effects. Failure to support the framework's formal route also cannot erase general harms, persistent burdens, or historical causality supported by other independent domain evidence; each remains on its own grounds. [T-main; T-load]

Execution, simultaneous activity, management, standby, and opportunity costs should have separate accounts according to the question. Clock minutes of parallel care and household work overlap and cannot simply be added into a single work-time total. Standby restrictions can be real without every minute being active execution. A transfer across positions can reduce tasks in the original post without reducing costs for households or outsourced positions. Statistical averages can hide critical bottlenecks. [T-main]

States of low load, manageable load, criticality, overload, and recovery require window-specific evidence; they are not character ratings. Absence may be protective and cannot be treated as laziness. Exit and recovery curves, invisible labor, and outsourcing costs should enter uncertainty and exclusion areas. The nine axes particularly preserve load-capacity distributions and different J authorities. [T-main]

This card outputs load-capacity descriptions and needs for load reduction or additional resources; it does not authorize performance-related action, compelled burden-bearing, or task adjustments. Those taking up work should be able to report safely and trigger independent review. Authorized rollback must not only remove erroneous labels but also address performance and responsibility effects, actual tasks and resources, and records, with completion verified. [T-main]

The design for three US states in the 2005 Cash and Counseling report separates tasks of counselors, participants, and fiscal services. It helps identify who may bear management and payment labor; it does not mean this discussion measured total burdens or established a recovery mechanism. Two pages of the previously available original PDF were read; the current official website's 403 status is explicitly retained. [P-CASH]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card, translated from Chinese: HV09. Interpretation: This is the short identifier within the card collection, tracking the same interface; it does not mean a real object has been proved. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card, translated from Chinese: human_variable:HV09. Interpretation: A qualified namespace avoids name collisions; references to this ID must still carry the object and evidence status. [T-main]

03 | Name (name). Original card, translated from Chinese: Structural load. Interpretation: The name provides an entry point for reading, not an automatic label for a particular person, group, or real structure. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card, translated from Chinese: Human structural load must register tasks, coordination losses, maintenance requirements, capacity, recovery margins, and cost-bearing positions together. Interpretation: Read this proposition together with the conditional routes and ceilings below; a single sentence cannot yield an unconditional causal or normative conclusion. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card, translated from Chinese: Human structures under sustained operation, maintenance, care, or high pressure. Interpretation: The scope lists task domains that may be examined; it does not mean every object within them has empirical support. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card, translated from Chinese: Only entropy, vulnerability, or resilience metaphors are used, without tasks, capacity, and recovery mechanisms. Interpretation: Pausing targets judgments or adoption relying on the premise; independently established descriptions may remain, but invalidated premises cannot continue to be used. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: Inferential dependencies provide the upstream content needed to establish a proposition. Upstream candidate/supported status must be carried through unchanged; citation does not automatically upgrade it. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. EVIDENCE; 2. SOURCE. Interpretation: Protocol dependencies constrain evidence collection and expression; completing protocols does not independently establish the truth of empirical propositions. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: an empty set means only that no such specialization relations are registered, not that evidential responsibility is absent; a nonempty set also does not imply universal validity. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional-support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. route_id=HV09-R0-instant-task-capacity;; claim_level=descriptive_classification;; when=Task or coordination demands, capacity, recovery margins, and their distributions are observable within the same window, position, and type mapping.;; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set);; additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set);; allowed_conclusion=Register instantaneous task–capacity relations, margins, backlogs, local gaps, and recovery states.;; result_ceiling=Same-window description only; momentary peaks or gaps do not automatically become overload mechanisms, cumulative damage, or collapse.; 2. route_id=HV09-R1-overload-mechanism;; claim_level=mechanism_explanation;; when=CM-LOAD's applicability conditions are complete and a qualified G2-instance shows an above-threshold effect of load, replenishment, load-reduction, or recovery channels on the preselected outcome.;; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance, CM-LOAD;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register candidate overload or recovery mechanisms within specified positions, types, windows, and channels.;; result_ceiling=Do not generalize into entropy, resilience, or inevitable collapse at every position, or directly generate obligations of load reduction or sacrifice.; 3. route_id=HV09-R2-cumulative-overload;; claim_level=intertemporal_explanation;; when=The overload mechanism already has G2-instance and CM-LOAD support, and a G3-instance shows a conditional increment of historical load for subsequent capacity, errors, or recovery.;; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance, CM-LOAD, G3-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register candidate cumulative damage or delayed recovery of the historical-increment type beyond the current state, within preregistered carriers, windows, and outcomes.;; result_ceiling=Do not infer irreversibility, inevitable collapse, attribution of responsibility, or obligations for named actors to bear burdens.; 4. route_id=HV09-R3-carried-cumulative-overload;; claim_level=intertemporal_explanation;; when=CM-LOAD-carried-cumulative conditions are complete, a qualified G2-instance covers the specified load, replenishment, or recovery channels and claimed cross-window outcomes, and current damage or capacity carriers, cross-window accumulation or recovery, and discriminating causal material are verified under §4.5.;; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance, CM-LOAD;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register candidate carrier-transmitted cumulative damage or delayed recovery within specified carriers, windows, and outcomes.;; result_ceiling=Do not register a G3 historical increment, infer a damage mechanism from a single overload or continuing correlation, or infer irreversibility, inevitable collapse, responsibility, or obligations of sacrifice. Interpretation: R0 is same-window description; R1 is mechanism; R2 is a historical increment beyond the current representation; R3 is accumulation in current carriers. Routes are not severity levels. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Candidate overload, insufficient margins, maintenance gaps, and recovery differences. Interpretation: These are permitted directions of conclusion; which is actually reached, and at what strength, remains bounded by the selected route and material. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Those taking up work should continue bearing it; 2. High load proves devotion; 3. An overloaded actor is an mechanism of destabilization. Interpretation: These are common boundary crossings that cannot be avoided merely by rephrasing; examine actual inferences and subsequent use, not just wording. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card, translated from Chinese: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=Aggregation level: individual task loads, uptake cases, post or group populations, load-capacity distributions, and aggregation rules; X=Spatial scope: work or care sites, organizational boundaries, digital-labor spaces, and cross-domain outsourcing scope; T=Temporal span: momentary peaks, persistent backlogs, recovery delays, and cross-period and intergenerational windows; O=Organizational level: uptake roles, teams, organizations, institutions, and governance ecologies; C=Causal level: task events, task–capacity interaction mechanisms, meso-level bottleneck structures, institutional distribution, and system conditions; R=Observation resolution: raw task and work-time records, load sequences, uptake cases, capacity distributions, delay and error indicators, and summaries, with compression losses registered; I=Range of impact: those directly taking up work, people dependent on services, indirect substitutes, second-order spillovers, and cross-domain and intergenerational costs; N=Network-topology scope: task dependencies, critical bottlenecks, substitute nodes, recovery paths, and cross-domain outsourcing networks; J=Jurisdiction and authorization scope: separately register authorization for task allocation, resource adjustments, stopping, performance-related use, and remedies; preserve load-capacity distributions. Interpretation: Register the nine axes item by item. In particular, range of impact I creates no jurisdictional authority J; when observation resolution R decreases, preserve compression losses. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card, translated from Chinese: The structural relation of task and coordination demands to available capacity and recovery margins within a given window. Interpretation: This describes the object corresponding to the interface; choosing a low-threshold descriptive route does not permit treating functional meaning in the name as proven causality. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Load, capacity, recovery, and cost-bearing positions. Interpretation: Invariants are comparative responsibilities to preserve during transfer, not a claim that variable values are unchanged at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions for elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Load distribution; 2. Concealment through aggregation; 3. Inheritance of responsibility; 4. Intergenerational impacts. Interpretation: Elevation is not copying and enlarging the original table. When material about new populations, interfaces, responsibility positions, and other items is incomplete, limit conclusions that depend on them. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Bottlenecks, capacity, and modes of recovery may change across levels. Interpretation: A word may change meaning when the object or scale changes; rebuild the correspondence rather than assume the original meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Non-applicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Processes without sustained nonequilibrium, maintenance, or human uptake requirements. Interpretation: Non-applicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of interfaces concerning human norms, responsibility, and experience; they do not deny that other theories may study these objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Average load concealing local overload. Interpretation: Inferences from local parts to wholes need separate proof; broad impact, grand names, and formal similarity cannot supply representativeness or authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Low load; 2. Manageable; 3. Critical; 4. Overloaded; 5. Recovering. Interpretation: States are descriptive classifications requiring evidence, not maturity ladders for scoring people; state changes require windows, grounds, and versions. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Task volume per unit time, backlogs, delays, and error rates; 2. Personnel and resource capacity, invisible labor, and availability of substitutes; 3. Stopping, absence, exit, and recovery curves; 4. Distributional differences between average load and critical local uptake positions. Interpretation: Observable clues indicate where to find material; a single clue's existence is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. Task volume; 2. Delays and errors; 3. Personnel and resources; 4. Recovery records; 5. Exit and absence; 6. Distinguish execution, simultaneous activity, management, standby, and opportunity costs according to the objective, explaining overlap, units, and transfers across positions rather than directly adding them into a unified burden; 7. When the task in question depends on uninterrupted periods, separately record how default-contact, standby, and temporary gap-filling responsibilities fragment available continuous blocks, without converting this into hours. Interpretation: Distinguish execution, parallel activity, management, standby, and opportunity costs according to the objective; explain units and overlaps before calculating, without inventing a unified burden quantity. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface content (input_dependencies). Original card: 1. Uptake layer; 2. Drive–uptake chain; 3. Conditional potential field; 4. R0 registers task volume, capacity, backlog, and recovery of the same type, in the same time window and burden-bearing position, without making established G2 a prerequisite for description.; 5. R1 channel effects invoke G2 and CM-LOAD; R3 carrier-based accumulation checks the current state, formation, and cross-window effects under §4.5; R2's additional historical conditional increment is checked separately through G3. H5 traces do not replace subsequent effects or G3 testing.; 6. Lack of formal mechanism support under these routes does not cancel general harm, continuing burdens, or historical causation already supported by independent domain evidence; conclusions are registered separately on their own grounds. Interpretation: Insufficient formal-route support does not negate harm supported by independent domain evidence; H5 traces do not establish delayed recovery or G3. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flows (output_effects). Original card: 1. State updates; 2. Behavior of destabilization; 3. Maintenance and repair needs. Interpretation: Variable flows indicate which downstream judgments may depend on this interface; passing references onward does not ensure downstream conclusions, actual repair, or authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Distinguish immediate peaks, persistent backlogs, recovery lags, and intergenerational costs. Interpretation: Occurrence, observation, execution, and the arrival of effects may happen at different times; short-term material cannot automatically certify extension beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record hidden labor, outsourced costs, and protective absence. Interpretation: Locate uncertainty in specific material and positions; do not merely write an overall confidence score that conceals positions never covered at all. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Informal labor, family care, outsourcing, and uptake positions with low visibility. Interpretation: An exclusion zone limits the coverage of the current inference; it does not erase these people or facts from the world. Material unavailable for safety reasons is neither consent nor evidence of no problem. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Those taking up work; 2. Those dependent on services; 3. Substitutes; 4. Positions receiving cost spillovers. Interpretation: Register both directly and indirectly affected people; visible members do not represent all cost bearers. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Personnel; 2. Posts; 3. Procedures; 4. Facilities; 5. Budgets. Interpretation: A carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something. Its name, completed construction, and delivery of the required function require different evidence. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Task allocators; 2. Resource allocators; 3. Authorizers; 4. Supervisors; 5. Parties responsible for remedies. Interpretation: Specify who proposes a judgment and who operates or uses it; registering responsibility does not automatically constitute adjudication of legal liability or new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: High efficiency or high load-bearing capacity does not constitute normative justification. Interpretation: Distinguish descriptive, normative, and bridging status as specified by the card. Established facts do not independently determine value rankings, and normative reasons do not automatically establish empirical effects. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card: R0 describes tasks, capacity, and recovery within the same window; R1 forms a bounded channel explanation under G2 and CM-LOAD; R3 forms a judgment of cumulative damage or delayed recovery transmitted by current carriers under §4.5; R2 judges historical increments beyond the current representation only with additional G3. Persistent correlation, temporary overload, and overall averages do not replace the corresponding evidence. Interpretation: Keep four ceilings separate: same-window gaps, causal mechanisms, carrier accumulation, and historical conditional increments. Means or persistent correlations cannot justify moving to a higher level. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card: This variable generates only descriptions of load, capacity, recovery, local overload, and needs for load reduction or additional resources. It does not authorize task reductions, resource investment, performance-related action, or forced burden-bearing; any real-world adjustment must separately pass C12, an explicit runtime N premise, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: The interface itself does not confer real-world authority to act; actual actions require separate checks of choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protection, and validity periods. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card: 1. Overall average capacity is sufficient, yet a few crucial uptake positions remain persistently overloaded; 2. Entropy or resilience metaphors are used without identifying tasks, capacity, and recovery channels. Interpretation: Use counterexamples to limit unconditional extrapolation. They may require narrowing the scope or obtaining new evidence, but do not automatically invalidate all bounded uses. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, those taking up work may report hidden labor, overload, and recovery needs through safe, accessible channels protecting against retaliation, and trigger review independent of the original load judgment, performance, or task decision chain. Interpretation: Appeals must be safely accessible, protected against retaliation, and capable of triggering independent review; a name alone does not imply authority to change errors. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, when rollback is authorized, the designated responsible person revokes erroneous load judgments and their performance or responsibility effects within the specified time limit, actually restores task, resource, and record states, and retains versions and verification of completion. Interpretation: Within valid authorization, actually revoke erroneous effects, correct downstream consequences, and verify completion; changing words in a document does not restore rights and resources to the person concerned. [T-main]

Evidence item 7 of the card is added only when the target depends on uninterrupted periods. Record how being the default contact, being on standby, and temporary gap-filling responsibilities divide usable uninterrupted stretches, retaining their lengths and predictability rather than converting them into an hours total. Execution, simultaneous activities, management, standby, and opportunity costs also require units and overlap to be marked; one large table cannot manufacture a unified burden through repeated addition.
argumentSteps: Fix units of the same type, burden-bearing positions, and windows; separate execution, parallel activities, management, standby, and opportunity costs.
R0 lists demand, capacity, margin, and backlog without first claiming damage.
R1 checks CM-LOAD applicability and G2 channel effects.
Cross-window R3 checks carriers, formation, recovery, and comparisons; R2 increments beyond the current representation separately require G3.
Check local positions, outsourcing, families, and protective absences concealed by averages.
Actual adjustments separately require N/J/O and C12; authorized rollback revokes performance and responsibility consequences and actual effects.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an average margin does not resolve a crucial gap
teachingExamples.text: Within a constructed window, post A has 6 hours of tasks of the same type and 4 hours of available capacity, while post B has 2 hours of tasks and 6 hours of capacity. Total tasks are 8 and total capacity 10, leaving an overall margin of 2. A still has a gap of 2, while B has a margin of 4. If qualifications and timing make the posts noninterchangeable, the overall margin cannot fill A's gap.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Task hours can be compared within the same post; noninterchangeable qualifications between the two posts are a fictional condition.
teachingExamples.boundary: This only illustrates an R0 distribution. It does not establish a G2 overload mechanism, damage, or responsibility on A's part.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: parallel activity and standby cannot be double-counted as clock time
teachingExamples.text: A constructed record shows 40 minutes of care work within one hour, alongside 20 minutes of housework that entirely overlaps it. The combined direct activities occupy 40 minutes, not 60. A separate standby constraint lasting the whole hour must be listed separately, rather than added into a single 100-minute clock duration.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The complete overlap and all durations are fictional; the union of the activity sets is 40 minutes.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not establish that housework or standby carries no burden. Other costs need corresponding measures; the union of clock intervals cannot replace experience.

A.10.title: A.10 HV10 Evolutionary phase (complete interface card)
A.10.lead: First check applicability to human collectives, then assess components, prototypes, mechanisms, and exit through six distinct routes; the numbers are neither an obligatory sequence nor a ranking of value.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 4558–4649; original-site location /theory/appendix-a/a-10#section-a-10. See the theory-v2 source for the current full text; the historical Chinese research manuscript and slices remain downloadable in their original versions for checking.

Short quotation: ‘X0 is not an eighth stage’ (translated from Chinese). HV10 applies only to human intentional collectives that are forming or operating. Direction, generation, uptake, and institutionalization are dimensions to examine, not requirements that everything be mature. The numbering cannot be used for individual personalities, purely technical systems, or rankings of species' value; nor does the absence of mature uptake exclude all collectives in formation. [T-main]

HV10-R0-component-applicability requires auditable assessment records for HV03/HV04/HV05/HV07, allowing missing, not_applicable, and unsupported. All four components need not be empirically established, but these statuses must be distinguished. R0 can register applicability, missing components, mixed observations, and needs for further work; component assessments alone cannot complete an S prototype or X0 path. [T-main]

HV10-R1-pattern-phase-match checks the object's K, window, applicability, and the selected prototype's entry conditions, observations, counterexamples, and falsification under §8.2–8.3. Once the specific cross-window criteria are satisfied, register single_dominant, mixed, or parallel; crucial gaps require unknown. It does not impose a prior requirement to obtain two operational intervals or CM-PHASE. Conversely, prototype matching does not automatically establish a phase-threshold pattern. [T-main；T-state]

HV10-R2-causal-transition requires CM-PHASE pattern matching plus G2 preselected state effects through a specified transition channel; R3-path-dependent-phase requires CM-PHASE plus G3 historical conditional increments beyond the current representation; R5-carried-phase-persistence requires CM-PHASE, G2, and the current carriers, cross-window persistence or delayed recovery, and discriminating evidence specified in §4.5. All three routes additionally require CAUSAL/E4. Curve shapes, reversals, and persistent correlations do not directly establish them, and their conditions cannot be borrowed from one another. [T-main；T-phase；T-history]

HV10-R4-orderly-exit-path independently checks X0 entry and completion conditions under §8.5, recording the original K, functions, personnel, relationships, resources, memory, debts, appeals, and continuity. It does not require a minimum S prototype or CM-PHASE; candidate, in progress, partially complete, complete, and unknown must remain distinct. If any affected group, residual obligation, receiving capacity, appeal, or memory safety is unknown, benign completion cannot be recorded. [T-main；T-exit]

One collective may simultaneously exhibit S2 uptake taking shape and S5 accumulation of vulnerabilities; jumps, reversals, splits, mergers, dormancy, and functional transfers are also allowed. mixed and parallel require positive evidence for the corresponding prototypes and positions; lack of material cannot be renamed mixed. If K is redefined, version the change and check identity; until that check is complete, do not connect two sets of object records into a historical path. [T-main；T-state]

The nine axes preserve local phase distributions and differences of scale. An overall label does not represent every subgroup, and an expanded scope of effects does not expand J. Phase is not health, success, or normative justification. Even a reliable judgment does not authorize probing, advancement, merger, exit, or elimination: each still requires N/C12/J/O, rather than authority conferred by a high number. [T-main]

Members may safely challenge phase evidence, linear assumptions, and moralizing uses; independent review must be outside the original decision chain. Authorized rollback revokes labels and downstream decision effects, restores variable-level descriptions and unresolved status, and retains versions. Simply renaming something cannot restore a situation already harmed. [T-main]

The UK GOV.UK guidance on retiring a service separately lists notifying users, continuing needs, new services, and data handling. It helps reveal continuity responsibilities beyond closing a webpage. No material from an actual service retirement is provided here, so it cannot support a claim that an institution has met all X0 completion conditions. [P-RETIRE]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card: HV10. Interpretation: This is a short identifier within the card collection, used to track the same interface; it does not establish a real-world object. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card: human_variable:HV10. Interpretation: The qualified namespace prevents naming collisions; references to this ID must still carry the object and evidentiary status. [T-main]
03 | Name (name). Original card: Evolutionary phase. Interpretation: The name offers a reading entry point, not an automatic label for specific people, groups, or real structures. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card: S0-S6 and X0 apply only to human intentional collectives that are forming or operating; direction, generation, uptake, and institutionalization are dimensions to examine, without requiring all to be mature; jumps between stages, parallelism, mixtures, reversals, splits, mergers, dormancy, absorption, and functional transfers are allowed. Interpretation: This proposition must be read together with the conditional routes and ceilings below; an unconditional causal or normative conclusion cannot be extracted from one sentence. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card: Human intentional collectives meeting the applicability conditions. Interpretation: Scope lists task domains that may be examined; it does not mean every object within that scope has empirical support. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card: When stages are moralized or titles conflict with criteria, pause the corresponding prototype assertions; when applicability conditions are missing, do not make prototype or path conclusions that depend on those conditions, while inapplicability, missing components, and observation needs may still be registered under the complete R0 conditions. Interpretation: Pausing targets the dependent judgment or adoption. Independently established descriptions may remain, but invalid premises cannot continue to be used. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card: 1. human_variable:HV03; 2. human_variable:HV04; 3. human_variable:HV05; 4. human_variable:HV07. Interpretation: HV03/HV04/HV05/HV07 require auditable component records; do not misstate this as requiring all four empirical propositions to hold. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card, translated from Chinese: 1. EVIDENCE; 2. SOURCE. Interpretation: Protocol dependencies constrain evidence collection and expression; completing protocols does not independently establish the truth of empirical propositions. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: an empty set means only that no such specialization relations are registered, not that evidential responsibility is absent; a nonempty set also does not imply universal validity. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card: 1. route_id=HV10-R0-component-applicability;; claim_level=descriptive_classification;; when=HV03, HV04, HV05, and HV07 have auditable assessment records; records may be missing, not_applicable, or unsupported, and empirical establishment of all four components is not required.;; additional_inferential_requires=none (empty set);; additional_protocol_requires=none (empty set);; allowed_conclusion=Register applicability, inapplicability, missing components, mixed states, and needs for continued observation.;; result_ceiling=Component checking alone produces neither an S0-S6 prototype match nor a completed X0 exit-path judgment.; 2. route_id=HV10-R1-pattern-phase-match;; claim_level=descriptive_classification;; when=Complete the checks of applicability, object K, observation window, and the selected prototype’s necessary entry conditions, observations, counterexamples, and falsification conditions under §8.2–8.3; specific criteria needing evidence across windows must meet their requirements, but a second operating interval or a CM-PHASE pattern is not required in advance.;; additional_inferential_requires=none (empty set);; additional_protocol_requires=E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register single, mixed, or parallel prototype configurations of S0-S6; record other descriptive paths separately under their respective conditions in §8.4, and judge X0 as an independent exit path.;; result_ceiling=Limited to description of prototype configurations; does not automatically confer eligibility for a CM-PHASE pattern, causal phase transition, or historical increment. Prototypes are not rankings of health, success, legitimacy, or elimination.; 3. route_id=HV10-R2-causal-transition;; claim_level=mechanism_explanation;; when=CM-PHASE matching holds, and a G2-instance identifies the effect of a specified phase-transition channel on a preselected state change.;; additional_inferential_requires=CM-PHASE, G2-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register a candidate causal phase transition within the specified object, window, and channel.;; result_ceiling=Do not infer a necessary stage sequence, value direction, or authorization for advancement or elimination from a transition mechanism.; 4. route_id=HV10-R3-path-dependent-phase;; claim_level=intertemporal_explanation;; when=CM-PHASE matching holds, and a G3-instance shows a conditional increment from historical phase variables for subsequent states, hysteresis, or regression.;; additional_inferential_requires=CM-PHASE, G3-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register candidates for historical-increment path dependence, hysteresis, or historical phase differences beyond the current state within a preregistered window.;; result_ceiling=Do not call them fate or absolute irreversibility, or automatically prescribe repair, exit, or retirement plans.; 5. route_id=HV10-R4-orderly-exit-path; claim_level=descriptive_classification; when=Check X0 candidate-entry and completion conditions individually under §8.5, separately recording the original object K, functions, personnel, relationships, resources, memory, debts, appeals, and continuity states. No minimum S0-S6 prototype or CM-PHASE match is required first.; additional_inferential_requires=none (empty set); additional_protocol_requires=E4; allowed_conclusion=Register an independent lifecycle-path judgment of X0 as candidate, in progress, partially complete, complete, or unknown.; result_ceiling=If affected groups, legacy obligations, receiving capacity, appeals, or memory safety remain unknown, do not judge completion as benign. X0 is not an eighth stage and generates no authorization to dissolve, transfer, publish archives, or abandon responsibility.; 6. route_id=HV10-R5-carried-phase-persistence;; claim_level=intertemporal_explanation;; when=CM-PHASE pattern conditions hold; evidence of the current carrier, persistence across windows or delayed recovery, and discrimination required for CM-PHASE-carried-persistence is complete; and a qualified G2-instance covers the specified outcome and window.;; additional_inferential_requires=CM-PHASE, G2-instance;; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4;; allowed_conclusion=Register a candidate mechanism of phase persistence or delayed recovery maintained through a current carrier within the same K and specified window.;; result_ceiling=Do not directly treat phase persistence, regression, or curve shape as a mechanism; do not register a G3 historical increment; and do not generate necessary stages, value directions, or real-world action authorization. Interpretation: The six routes—R0 component assessment, R1 prototype description, R2 causal transition, R3 historical increment, R4 independent X0, and R5 current-carrier persistence—each retain their own complete conditions. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card: 1. Conditional state coordinates; 2. Nonlinear paths; 3. Orderly exit X0. Interpretation: These indicate permissible directions of conclusions; the selected route and material still limit which one is reached and its strength. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card: 1. Every system must pass through S0-S6; 2. A higher stage is more legitimate; 3. Dissolution equals failure. Interpretation: These are common overreaches, not problems avoided by rewording. Examine actual inferences and subsequent uses, not vocabulary alone. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=aggregation level: single state events, local group cases, intentional collective populations, phase distributions, and aggregation rules; X=spatial scope: action sites, organizational or institutional boundaries, digital collaboration spaces, and cross-domain evolutionary scope; T=time span: state windows, transition lags, regression, dormancy, hysteresis, and intergenerational cycles; O=organizational level: member roles, teams, organizations, institutions, through governance ecosystems; C=causal level: state events, transition interaction mechanisms, meso-level phase structures, institutionalization processes, and system conditions; R=observational resolution: original state events, transition sequences, local cases, phase distributions, state indicators, and summaries, with compression losses registered; I=impact scope: direct members and uptake providers, those exiting, indirectly affected people, second-order consequences, cross-domain and intergenerational effects; N=network-topological scope: local phase clusters, cross-level connections, splitting and merging, functional transfers, and inheritance paths; J=jurisdiction and authorization scope: register authorization separately for phase naming, adoption of monitoring, probing, advancement, exit, and elimination; retain mixed phases. Interpretation: Register all nine axes individually. In particular, impact scope I does not generate jurisdiction J, and compression losses must remain recorded when observational resolution R decreases. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card: Human intentional collective states in formation or operation; components may be present, forming, missing, or inapplicable, judged according to the prototype’s specific conditions. Interpretation: This describes the object of the interface. When selecting a low-threshold descriptive route, functional meanings in names must not be treated as established causation. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card: 1. Applicability conditions; 2. Phase criteria; 3. Nonlinear paths; 4. X0 is not counted as an eighth stage. Interpretation: Invariants are comparative responsibilities to preserve during transfer, not a claim that variable values remain unchanged at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions for elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card: 1. Local phase distributions; 2. Cross-level transitions; 3. Uptake inheritance; 4. Protection and exit. Interpretation: Elevation is not copying the original table at a larger size. When added material about populations, interfaces, and responsibility positions is incomplete, limit conclusions depending on it. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card: 1. Uptake providers, institutional carriers, and effective objects may change with phase. Interpretation: The same term may change meaning when the object or scale changes. Reestablish the correspondence rather than assuming the old meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Non-applicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card: 1. Populations, purely technical systems, or similar categories without grounds for a human intentional collective; a lack of mature uptake during formation does not by itself justify blanket exclusion. Interpretation: Human prototypes cannot be directly attached to purely technical systems; a forming collective is not categorically excluded merely because mature uptake is missing. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card: 1. A case’s phase directly represents the population; 2. Human stages are transferred into the universal core. Interpretation: Inferences from a part to the whole need separate evidence. Broad influence, grand names, or formal resemblance cannot supply representativeness or authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card: Prototypes: S0, S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6; classification modes: single_dominant, mixed, parallel, unknown; independent path: X0, registered through R4, not listed as an eighth state. Interpretation: There are seven prototypes and four classification modes; X0 is an independent path, not an eighth state. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card: 1. Contemporaneous states of direction, generation, uptake, institutionalization, and feedback variables; 2. Records of repeated phase-criterion matches across observation windows; 3. Trajectories of stage skipping, parallelism, mixture, regression, splitting, merging, and dormancy; 4. Records of functional transfer, responsibility inheritance, and orderly exit in X0. Interpretation: Observable clues indicate where to seek material. One clue’s presence is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card: 1. Phase variables; 2. Transition records; 3. Traces; 4. Uptake and institutional states. Interpretation: Obtain the listed evidence according to route and task relevance. Keep unknown, not collected, not applicable, and unavailable for protective reasons separate; do not force disclosure to fill the table. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface contents (input_dependencies). Original card: 1. Orientation anchors; 2. Generative nodes; 3. Uptake layers; 4. Feedback written back into revision; 5. Structural load; 6. Pattern phases do not require G3; causal transitions separately require CAUSAL. R5 checks persistence or delayed recovery transmitted through current carriers under §4.5; only R3 additionally requires G3 to test an extra historical conditional increment. H5 supports only the corresponding candidate traces. Interpretation: This specifies upstream inputs and their status; gaps must not quietly disappear as references pass between interfaces. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flows (output_effects). Original card: 1. Phase judgments 2. Uptake inheritance 3. Exit and repair needs. Interpretation: Variable flows indicate which downstream judgments may depend on this interface. Passing a reference does not guarantee a downstream conclusion, actual repair, or authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Register phase observation windows, transition lags, regression, and dormancy. Interpretation: Occurrence, observation, execution, and arrival of effects may happen at different times. Short-term material cannot automatically certify what lies beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record mixed phases, splitting, merging, and scale differences. Interpretation: Tie uncertainty to specific material and positions; do not write only an overall confidence score that hides positions never covered. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Local groups and roles not represented by the overall phase. Interpretation: An exclusion zone limits the coverage of current inference; it does not delete these people or facts from the world. Unavailability for safety reasons is neither consent nor absence of problems. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Members; 2. Uptake providers; 3. Dissenters; 4. Those exiting; 5. Successors. Interpretation: Register both directly and indirectly affected people. Visible members do not represent everyone bearing costs. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Collective action; 2. Organizational structures; 3. Institutional records; 4. Shared memory. Interpretation: A carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something. Its name, completion of construction, and delivery of the required function are different evidentiary matters. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Analysts making phase judgments; 2. Decision-makers and authorizers acting on them. Interpretation: State who proposes the judgment and who operates or uses it. Registering responsibility does not automatically adjudicate legal liability or create new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: Phases do not constitute rankings of health, success, or legitimacy. Interpretation: Distinguish descriptive, normative, and bridging status according to the card. An established fact does not independently determine value rankings; normative reasons do not automatically prove empirical effects. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card: Limit each route by its own complete conditions: R0 only classifies component applicability and absence; R1 matches S0-S6 prototypes under §8.2–8.3 without a rigid CM-PHASE requirement; R2 offers a bounded candidate causal phase-transition explanation under CM-PHASE and G2-instance conditions; R3 explains historical conditional increments under CM-PHASE and G3-instance conditions; R4 independently judges X0 path states under §8.5 without presupposing an S0-S6 or CM-PHASE match. R5 judges a mechanism maintained across windows through current carriers using CM-PHASE, G2-instance, and §4.5 evidence. Routes do not supply one another’s missing conditions, and none generates real-world action authorization. Interpretation: R1 does not rigidly require CM-PHASE; R4 does not require a minimum S prototype; R2/R3/R5 follow their own mechanism conditions, with no borrowing of gate satisfaction between routes. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card: Depending on the selected route, this variable generates component applicability, prototype matches, mixed states, bounded explanations of phase mechanisms or historical conditional increments, independent X0 path states, uncertainty, and observation needs. It does not authorize probing, advancement, merging, exit, or elimination. Every real adjustment must separately pass C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: The interface itself generates no power to act in reality. Actual actions require separate checks of choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protection, and duration. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card: 1. The same collective simultaneously exhibits a mixed phase of S2 uptake formation and S5 vulnerability accumulation; 2. Orderly exit X0 preserves functional transfer rather than constituting stage failure. Interpretation: Use counterexamples to limit unconditional extrapolation. They may require narrower scope or renewed evidence collection, not automatic rejection of every limited use. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, members may challenge phase evidence, linear assumptions, and moralizing uses through safe, accessible channels protected against retaliation, triggering review independent of the original phase-judgment or decision chain. Interpretation: Appeals must be safely accessible, free from retaliation, and able to trigger independent review. A name alone does not establish authority to change errors. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, when rollback is authorized, designated responsible persons must revoke phase naming and its downstream decision effects within specified time limits, actually restore variable-level descriptions and unresolved states, and preserve versions and completion verification. Interpretation: Within valid authority, actually revoke erroneous effects, correct downstream consequences, and verify completion. Editing document text does not mean rights and resources have returned to the person concerned. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Assess the four components auditably, distinguishing missing, not applicable, and unsupported.
Freeze K, the nine axes, subsystems, and window; R1 checks prototype entry conditions, counterexamples, and falsification conditions individually.
R2/R3/R5 separately check CM-PHASE and evidence for channels, historical increments, or current carriers.
R4 independently checks X0 entry and seven completion dimensions, without setting a minimum stage.
Retain positive evidence for the positions in mixed/parallel configurations; missing evidence means unknown, not a guessed label.
Classification is a revocable description only. Interventions require separate authorization, and erroneous downstream effects must also be corrected.

questionAnswers.question: Does R0 require all four components to be proven?
questionAnswers.answer: Full empirical establishment is not required, but auditable assessment records are; missing/not_applicable/unsupported are allowed.

questionAnswers.question: Must R1 have two operating intervals?
questionAnswers.answer: Not rigidly. It follows each prototype’s conditions; CM-PHASE is a separate contract.
questionAnswers.basis: R1 and 6.7.

questionAnswers.question: Can exit occur from S0?
questionAnswers.answer: X0 has no minimum S state, but still requires its own entry and completion conditions.

questionAnswers.question: Is a higher phase more legitimate?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Numbering, capability, norms, and action authority must remain separate.
questionAnswers.basis: Prohibited leap.

A.11.title: A.11 HV11 Open-Ended Undertaking Action (Complete Interface Card)
A.11.lead: Retain actual failure and unknown outcomes, and closely examine refusal and exit. Effectiveness is not voluntariness, and sacrifice does not prove love. The ending checks the non-authorization boundaries of all eleven variables together.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 4650–4759, original-site location /theory/appendix-a/a-11#section-a-11. The current full text is in the theory-v2 source; the historical research draft and excerpts remain downloadable in their original versions.

Short quotation translated from Chinese: “It does not diagnose whether someone has love.” HV11 observes only evidenced actions, real costs, direction, voluntariness, alternative explanations, and consequences. It specializes H6/H2 and is constrained by N4; it does not score love by the amount of sacrifice or treat refusal as moral failure. The name must not be used to requisition the actor’s actions in reverse. [T-main]

HV11-R0-action-cost-record may still record candidate undertakings, cost distributions, coercion risks, gaps in stopping rights, and protective needs when action costs are grounded but voluntariness, refusal, or exit are insufficiently supported. What pauses is R1’s naming of open-ended undertaking, not the retention of known costs. Card requirements cannot force actors into refusal or disclosure they cannot safely perform. [T-main]

HV11-R1-voluntary-limited-action requires real action costs and a clear direction, with separate support for voluntariness, genuine refusal, and conditions for exit or negotiation, and checking relevant alternatives such as fear, dependency, interests, and performance. Outcomes are separately recorded as achieved, not achieved, harmful, or unknown. Genuine failed attempts are not erased because they did not succeed, nor does grounded voluntariness disappear because outcomes are unknown. [T-main]

HV11-R2-structural-consequence additionally requires eligible G2 identification of an above-threshold effect through the specified channel on preselected outcomes, plus CAUSAL/E4. Coerced action can also be effective, so R2 cannot backfill R1’s voluntariness; bounded voluntariness is not automatically effective either. The three routes are not a bad-to-good ladder, still less do effects prove love, goodness, justification, or unlimited responsibility. [T-main]

Ethical naming remains constrained by GOV-14’s normative premises; reaching R2 cannot replace them. An action description is also not an individual or group obligation: one person voluntarily contributing once does not mean similar members all consent to ongoing burdens. Representative relations, cost spillovers, genuine exit, and proxy protection must be added separately on elevation. Human voluntariness and meaning diagnoses do not apply to nonhuman systems. [T-main；T-gov]

Observed costs include time, resources, opportunities, and physical and psychological costs, but this interface makes no personality or clinical diagnoses. Separate immediate contributions, ongoing depletion, and recovery lags; beneficiaries, dependents, and alternative uptake providers may all be affected. Retain positions unable to refuse or exit safely or obscured by moral pressure; silence cannot fill in voluntariness. [T-main]

The appendix-wide notes at the end of this lesson must also be read: N in the nine-axis SP means network topology, whereas explicit runtime N means normative premises N1–N5; they differ. Identity belongs to K; relational channels belong to inputs, carriers, or causal contracts; membership positions belong to affected/excluded/observation fields. None can impersonate a scale axis. Expanding A/X/O/I does not expand J. [T-main]

The common table specifies outputs for each of the eleven variables: HV01, candidate domains, boundaries, and supplementary-evidence needs; HV02, boundaries, interfaces, exclusions, and testing needs; HV03, anchors, heterogeneous expression, and comparisons; HV04, GC/GS/GE candidates and transitions; HV05, CV/RS, costs, capacity, stopping rights, and needs for additional resources and redistribution; HV06, connectivity, lags, losses, interruptions, costs, and uptake; HV07, acceptance, fields, execution, persistence, write-back, and procedural repair; HV08, candidate conditions, heterogeneity, masking, and risk reduction; HV09, loads, capacity, recovery, local overload, and load-reduction needs; HV10, components, prototypes, mixtures, bounded mechanisms/historical increments, independent X0, and uncertainty under the selected route; HV11, voluntariness, costs, direction, alternatives, consequences, and needs for stopping and protection. [T-main]

All are descriptions or requirements, not authorization for actual testing, load reduction, additional resources, repair, protection, responsibility attribution, advancement, or exit. Any real adjustment separately requires C12, explicit normative premises, valid J, and O. Even obvious protective needs require checking independently existing authority; this card cannot be an authorization document. Authorized rollback revokes undertaking labels and requirements, actually restores refusal, exit, records, and resource states, and verifies completion. [T-main]

NASA ASRS’s confidentiality page describes voluntary reporting, deidentification, and restricted incentives; the first item on its separate Caveats page explicitly excludes accident or criminal-activity reports from confidentiality and penalty-immunity protections. This is used to examine the distinction between an institution’s description of itself as voluntary and its concrete protective conditions. It does not infer that every reporter can genuinely refuse, characterize them as loving, or claim R1/R2 support under this framework. [P-ASRS；P-ASRS-C]
Field-by-field study of all 39 fields (“Original card” below retains the field’s complete content in translation; “Interpretation” specifies its role and irreplaceable responsibility).

01 | Interface ID (id). Original card: HV11. Interpretation: the short identifier within the cardbook tracks the same interface; it does not indicate that a real-world object has been proved. [T-main]

02 | Qualified ID (qualified_id). Original card: human_variable:HV11. Interpretation: the namespace prevents naming collisions; references to this ID must still carry object and evidential status. [T-main]

03 | Name (name). Original card: Open-ended undertaking action. Interpretation: the name provides a reading entry point, not an automatic label for particular people, groups, or real structures. [T-main]

04 | Claim type (claim_type). Original card: H. Interpretation: H identifies the role of a human-instance/interface proposition; it cannot be upgraded into formal proof or an unconditional law of the world. [T-main]

05 | Contract role (contract_role). Original card: human_variable_interface. Interpretation: this variable-interface contract specifies how to enter analysis; a field’s existence does not mean an empirical instance has been established. [T-main]

06 | Proposition (proposition). Original card: Open-ended undertaking observes only real costs, voluntariness, direction, alternative explanations, and structural consequences; it does not diagnose whether someone has love. Interpretation: read this proposition together with the subsequent conditional routes and ceilings; do not extract an unconditional causal or normative conclusion from one sentence. [T-main]

07 | Scope (scope). Original card: Undertakings in human relationships, organizations, institutions, and public action. Interpretation: scope lists task domains that may be studied, not empirical support for every object within them. [T-main]

08 | Pause condition (pause_condition). Original card: When voluntariness, refusal, or exit cannot be safely confirmed, pause R1’s naming of open-ended undertaking; R0 may still register candidate actions, costs, coercion risks, gaps in stopping rights, and protective needs. Personality and love diagnoses are always prohibited. Interpretation: inability to confirm voluntariness safely pauses R1 naming, while R0 retains costs, coercion risks, and protective needs; diagnosing love is always prohibited. [T-main]

09 | Inferential dependencies (inferential_requires). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: Inferential dependencies provide the upstream content needed to establish a proposition. Upstream candidate/supported status must be carried through unchanged; citation does not automatically upgrade it. [T-main]

10 | Protocol dependencies (protocol_requires). Original card: 1. N4; 2. EVIDENCE; 3. SOURCE. Interpretation: protocol dependencies constrain evidence gathering and expression; completing protocols does not independently prove an empirical proposition true. [T-main]

11 | Qualification / specialization (specializes). Original card: 1. H6; 2. H2. Interpretation: an empty set means only that no such specialization relations are registered, not that evidential responsibility is absent; a nonempty set also does not imply universal validity. [T-main]

12 | Applicable-object references (applies_to). Original card: None (empty set). Interpretation: applicable-object references cannot replace the current object contract; an empty set is explicit registration, not permission to apply to every object. [T-main]

13 | Conditional support routes (conditional_support_routes). Original card: 1. route_id=HV11-R0-action-cost-record; claim_level=normative_boundary; when=Actions and relevant costs are grounded, and known or unknown states of direction, benefits, and consequences can be recorded, but voluntariness, refusal, or exit are insufficiently supported.; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set); additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set); allowed_conclusion=Describe candidate undertaking actions, cost distributions, coercion risks, gaps in stopping rights, and protective needs.; result_ceiling=Do not call this open-ended undertaking, diagnose love or personality, or demand continued undertaking. 2. route_id=HV11-R1-voluntary-limited-action; claim_level=normative_boundary; when=Actions and real costs are grounded, direction is clear, voluntariness, genuine refusal, and conditions for exit or negotiation are separately supported, and relevant alternatives are checked; record outcomes as achieved, not achieved, harmful, or unknown, without making structural success an entry condition.; additional_inferential_requires=None (empty set); additional_protocol_requires=None (empty set); allowed_conclusion=Register descriptions of bounded voluntary undertaking and outcome states; failure or unknown outcomes do not cancel grounded facts of action and voluntariness.; result_ceiling=Action description only; do not elevate individual undertaking into group obligations or authorize requisition, protection, or resource arrangements. 3. route_id=HV11-R2-structural-consequence; claim_level=conditional_effect; when=An eligible G2-instance shows that the action produces an above-threshold effect through the specified channel on preselected structural outcomes.; additional_inferential_requires=G2-instance; additional_protocol_requires=CAUSAL, E4; allowed_conclusion=Register structural consequences of the action within the specified channel, object, and window.; result_ceiling=Structural effects prove neither voluntariness, love, goodness, justification, unlimited responsibility, nor action authorization; R2 effect support cannot supply missing R1 evidence, and coerced action may also have identifiable effects. Interpretation: gather evidence separately for R0 candidate costs, R1 bounded voluntariness, and R2 structural effects; effective coercion cannot supply voluntariness, and genuine failure is not absence of action. [T-main]

14 | Allowed inference (allowed_inference). Original card: 1. Describe bounded undertaking actions and consequences. Interpretation: these are permitted directions of conclusion; which is actually reached and with what strength remain limited by the selected route and materials. [T-main]

15 | Prohibited leap (prohibited_leap). Original card: 1. Diagnosing whether love exists; 2. Sacrifice equals love; 3. Responsibility equals unlimited undertaking; 4. Refusal equals moral failure. Interpretation: these are common boundary violations, not avoided by rewording; inspect actual inference and downstream use, not wording alone. [T-main]

16 | Nine-axis scale profile (scale_profile). Original card: SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>; A=aggregation level: individual undertaking actions, actor cases, relationship or organizational populations, distributions of costs and voluntariness, and aggregation rules; X=spatial scope: relationship and care sites, organizational boundaries, digital public spaces, and cross-domain beneficiary scope; T=time span: immediate action, ongoing undertaking, depletion, recovery, and intergenerational windows; O=organizational level: action roles, relationships or teams, organizations, institutions, through governance ecosystems; C=causal level: undertaking events, action–cost interaction mechanisms, meso-level relational structures, institutional responsibility arrangements, and systemic conditions; R=observational resolution: original actions and costs, undertaking sequences, actor cases, distributions of costs and voluntariness, consequence indicators, and summaries, with compression loss registered; I=sphere of influence: direct actors and beneficiaries, dependents, indirect alternative uptake providers, second-order spillovers, cross-domain and intergenerational effects; N=network-topological scope: dependency and care, beneficiary connections, alternative uptake, exit paths, and cross-domain cost networks; J=jurisdiction and authorization scope: register authorization separately for undertaking requirements, resource use, refusal, stopping, protection, and remedies; retain differences in voluntariness, costs, and exit. Interpretation: register all nine axes individually; particularly, sphere of influence I creates no jurisdictional authority J, and lower observational resolution R requires retention of compression loss. [T-main]

17 | Effective object (effective_object). Original card: Human undertaking arrangements requiring separate examination of actions, costs, direction, voluntariness, refusal conditions, and consequences; judge R0, R1, and R2 under their own conditions, without first filtering actions by structural consequences. Interpretation: this describes the interface’s corresponding object; choosing a lower-threshold descriptive route cannot treat functional meaning in the name as established causation. [T-main]

18 | Cross-scale invariants (scale_invariants). Original card: 1. Costs, voluntariness, direction, alternative explanations, consequences, and stopping rights. Interpretation: invariants are comparative responsibilities retained during transfer, not a declaration that variable values remain constant at every scale. [T-main]

19 | Required additions on elevation (required_scale_additions). Original card: 1. Distribution of voluntariness; 2. Representative relations; 3. Cost spillovers; 4. Genuine exit and proxy protection. Interpretation: elevation is not copying and enlarging the original table. Where materials on new populations, interfaces, responsibility positions, and so on are incomplete, restrict conclusions dependent on them. [T-main]

20 | Semantics changing with scale (changing_semantics). Original card: 1. Forms of undertaking, cost positions, and beneficiaries may change. Interpretation: the same word may change meaning when the object or scale changes; reconstruct correspondence rather than assume the original meaning applies unchanged. [T-main]

21 | Inapplicable objects (non_applicable_objects). Original card: 1. Nonhuman systems without capability for intention, voluntariness, responsibility, or meaning. Interpretation: inapplicability constraints prevent unconditional projection of human normative, responsibility, and experiential interfaces; they do not deny that other theories can study these objects. [T-main]

22 | Forbidden elevation (forbidden_elevation). Original card: 1. Elevating individual undertaking into group obligations; 2. Transferring human undertaking concepts into the nonhuman core. Interpretation: inference from local to whole requires separate proof; broad impact, a grand name, or formal similarity cannot supply representativeness and authorization. [T-main]

23 | State set (state). Original card: 1. Candidate; 2. Voluntary and bounded; 3. Coercion risk; 4. One-sided depletion; 5. Stopping or exit. Interpretation: states are descriptive classifications requiring evidence, not a maturity ladder for scoring people; state changes require windows, grounds, and versions. [T-main]

24 | Observables (observables). Original card: 1. Time, resources, opportunities, and physical and psychological costs invested in action; 2. Whether refusal, exit, stopping, and renegotiation are genuinely available; 3. Action direction, beneficiary positions, and detectable structural consequences; 4. Alternative explanations such as coercion, fear, dependency, interests, and performance. Interpretation: observable indications tell us where to seek materials; a single indication’s presence is not proof of a complete mechanism or causal effect. [T-main]

25 | Evidence requirements (evidence). Original card: 1. Actions and costs; 2. Refusal and exit conditions; 3. Alternative explanations; 4. Benefits and consequences. Interpretation: obtain listed evidence according to route and task relevance; distinguish unknown, uncollected, inapplicable, and unavailable for protection, without forcing disclosure to fill a table. [T-main]

26 | Input dependencies and interface content (input_dependencies). Original card: 1. Orientation anchors; 2. Uptake layers; 3. Conditional potential fields; 4. Power and safety. Interpretation: this states what arrives from upstream and its eligibility; gaps cannot quietly disappear while passing between interfaces. [T-main]

27 | Output effects and variable flow (output_effects). Original card: 1. Cost distributions; 2. Relational and institutional states; 3. Stopping and repair. Interpretation: variable flow identifies downstream judgments that may depend on this interface; passing references guarantees neither downstream conclusions, actual repair, nor authorization. [T-main]

28 | Time window and lag (time_window_and_lag). Original card: Register immediate costs, ongoing undertaking, depletion, and recovery lags. Interpretation: occurrence, observation, execution, and arrival of effects may differ in time; short-term materials cannot automatically certify extensions beyond the window. [T-main]

29 | Uncertainty (uncertainty). Original card: Record dependency, fear, hidden coercion, and safety of expression. Interpretation: direct uncertainty toward specific materials and positions; an overall confidence score cannot conceal fundamentally uncovered positions. [T-main]

30 | Local exclusion zone (local_exclusion_zone). Original card: Positions unable to refuse safely, unable to exit, or obscured by moral pressure. Interpretation: exclusion zones limit current inferential coverage, not delete people or facts from the world; unavailability for safety is neither consent nor absence of problems. [T-main]

31 | Affected positions (affected_positions). Original card: 1. Actors; 2. Beneficiaries; 3. Dependents; 4. Alternative uptake providers. Interpretation: register directly and indirectly affected parties together; visible members do not represent every cost bearer. [T-main]

32 | Uptake carrier (carrier). Original card: 1. Concrete actors; 2. Relational practices; 3. Care or responsibility arrangements. Interpretation: a carrier is the structure or process that actually carries something; its name, completed construction, and arrival of the required function are different evidence. [T-main]

33 | Responsible party (responsible_subject). Original card: 1. Those making demands; 2. Authorizers; 3. Those responsible as beneficiaries; 4. Those responsible for remedies. Interpretation: identify who proposes, operates, or uses judgments; recording responsibility is not automatically a legal-liability adjudication or new authorization. [T-main]

34 | Normative status (normative_status). Original card: Constrained by N4; cannot be commanded or requisitioned. Interpretation: N4 prohibits commanding or requisitioning this ethical designation; independently grounded responsibilities cannot be expanded without limit by this label. [T-main]

35 | Judgment ceiling (judgment_ceiling). Original card: Limited separately under R0/R1/R2: R0 describes only costs, direction, risks, and candidate actions; R1 describes actions in terms of voluntariness, refusal, and exit conditions under corresponding evidence; R2 makes bounded structural-consequence judgments only when corresponding G2 and causal conditions hold. No level may enter personality diagnosis, prove love or goodness, infer undertaking obligations, or generate real authorization. Ethical naming is separately constrained by GOV-14’s normative premises; reaching R2 cannot replace this requirement. Interpretation: no route proves love, personality, goodness, or real authorization; ethical naming additionally requires GOV-14 normative premises. [T-main]

36 | Action ceiling (action_ceiling). Original card: This variable produces only descriptions of voluntariness, real costs, direction, alternative explanations, structural consequences, and needs for stopping and protection; it authorizes no protective measures, undertaking demands, resource requisition, or personality verdicts. Any real adjustment must separately pass C12, explicit runtime N premises, J authorization, and O procedures. Interpretation: the interface itself creates no real-world authority to impose dispositions; actual actions separately require checking choice, C12, explicit N, valid J, O, protections, and periods. [T-main]

37 | Counterexamples (counterexamples). Original card: 1. One-sided sacrifice without the ability to refuse is praised as love or responsibility; 2. An undertaking claim lacks evidence of the claimed action or costs. Genuine failed attempts and unknown outcomes are recorded separately; their action descriptions cannot all be revoked for lacking structural success. Interpretation: counterexamples restrict unconditional extrapolation; they may require narrowing scope or gathering evidence anew, without automatically negating every bounded use. [T-main]

38 | Appeal (appeal). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, actors may refuse representation through safely accessible channels protected against retaliation, explain coercion, costs, alternative explanations, and exit restrictions, and trigger review independent of the original undertaking judgment or demand chain. Interpretation: appeals must be safely accessible, free from retaliation, and capable of triggering independent review; a name alone does not mean authority to correct errors exists. [T-main]

39 | Rollback (rollback). Original card: Under appeal_and_rollback_rule, when rollback is authorized, a designated responsible person must revoke undertaking labels and related demands within the specified period, actually restore refusal, exit, records, and resource states, and preserve versions and completion verification. Interpretation: actually cancel erroneous effects within valid authorization, correct downstream uses, and verify completion; changing document wording does not restore rights and resources to the affected person. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Check action costs and direction; where voluntariness cannot be safely checked, stop R1 naming while retaining R0 risks.
Separately check voluntariness, genuine refusal, exit or negotiation, and alternative explanations.
Record outcomes as achieved/not achieved/harmful/unknown; failure does not delete grounded actions.
R2 structural consequences separately require G2 and CAUSAL/E4; effects cannot fill R1 gaps.
Add representation, distributions, spillovers, and protections across scales; distinguish nine-axis N from normative N.
The eleven variables’ outputs generate requirements only; actual actions separately require C12/N/J/O checks and can be independently corrected.
