D.01.title: D.01 The framework itself, explanatory tasks, and theoretical borrowing
D.01.lead: The same automated reminder system may reduce missed tasks without making appeals usable. Separate the outcomes to be explained first, so we can identify materials needed for technology, institutions, and people’s experiences, and determine what a borrowed theory actually contributes.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 4980–4995; original anchor section-d-01. Short quotation translated from Chinese: “First ask which outcome needs explanation, rather than first selecting the vocabulary one knows best.” The source excerpt for this lesson is separately attached verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and original text are distinct.

D.01 makes the explanatory task itself an object of inquiry. Why equipment fails, how decisions form, who bears consequences, and how people understand experiences are adjacent but distinct questions. Technical mechanisms, institutional authority, and actor experience may correct one another or complete separate local explanations. Register outcomes and tasks before selecting materials and methods, without granting permanent priority to structure, interests, power, psychology, culture, or technology on reputation alone. Main-text §§1.3–1.10 particularly emphasize that knowledge need not first be fully converted into structural variables, and understanding itself can be an endpoint. [source theory-cross]

Theoretical borrowing has at least five statuses: observational heuristics help discover questions; definitions specify word use; testable mechanisms make fallible claims about actual processes; formal inferences hold under explicit mathematical premises; normative choices express what should be protected and how to weigh tradeoffs. They cannot serve as evidence for one another. Defining a relation as feedback does not prove real feedback effective; a mathematical structure’s validity does not prove that real objects meet its assumptions; effective factual causation cannot leap to a duty to adopt. Main-text §§2.2–2.7 specify responsibilities for classification, causation, evidence, analogy, and sources. [source theory-cross]

A formal mapping should specify the relations preserved, distinctions lost, and circumstances that could change the conclusion. The same word in two theories may refer to different objects, variables, or inferential permissions, so word-for-word substitution is invalid. If the source domain concerns conservation of quantities while the target domain borrows only a diagram of “flow,” conservation conclusions cannot be carried over; if a mapping suppresses differences in people’s refusal and rights, its concise representation cannot ground action either. When existing domain methods suffice, checking sources and boundaries is enough; additional circles need not be invented merely to display the framework’s involvement.

The original automatic-reminder example is a teaching example, not a real project already investigated. Fewer missed tasks is a technical task metric; whether appeals can change errors concerns procedural remedy; whether people are respected also requires users’ actual circumstances and expressions. These three outcomes may diverge: real improvement in the first should be retained, deficiencies in the second made explicit, and the third kept unresolved when materials are absent. Calling everything “a better system” conceals differences, while negating all achievements because one item falls short also distorts them.

Historical adoption, mention in a directory, subsequently discovered compatibility, and an analyst’s new connection must be registered separately. Actual adoption of a theory in an original work requires the corresponding text and version; a name in a directory establishes only mention; current compatibility cannot retroactively establish past influence; a connection proposed by a researcher today is new analysis, not a rewritten intellectual history of the author. Versions with the same number remain different identities when they belong to different texts; obtaining A’s original cannot supply B’s still-unverified wording. This concretely implements the source and expression boundaries of §§16.15–16.16 in the map.

Passing procedures, complete files, and closed identifier references support engineering correspondence, not semantic or real-world gain. Files can have perfect formatting while misreading concepts; citations can be authentic without supporting the current inference. First check content and argument, then external facts and effects of use according to purpose; a checking tool’s pass signal must not substitute for theoretical correctness. Conversely, engineering checks do have local value: they can detect omissions and formatting errors, but must be named according to their actual capabilities.

The five answer types are conceptual, textual, formal, domain-empirical, and use-effectiveness answers. Conceptual answers clarify terminology; textual answers interpret originals; formal answers complete conditional derivations; domain-empirical answers support specific relationships in the world; use-effectiveness answers compare whether a method actually improves work. They are not a maturity ladder in which absence of a later type cancels everything earlier; yet obtaining the first four cannot supply the fifth. More materials and clearer writing may help, but effects still need checking in actual tasks.

Value comparisons must fix actual treatment contents, tasks, and proportionate resources, retain sufficiently strong professional methods as comparators, and include nondelivery, misjudgment, waiting, and maintenance burdens. If a new framework answers more tasks or uses more materials, those extra resources should also be reported; not every outcome difference can be attributed solely to the theory. Without comparison, honestly retain conceptual and textual achievements without declaring real-world superiority, equivalence, or uselessness.

The eight topic positions can be understood as follows: 01.01 tracks changes in questions and goals; 01.02 distinguishes concepts, metaphors, mechanisms, and theorems; 01.03 separates documented active choices from historical gaps unseen in the materials; 01.04 prevents one interpretation from suppressing domain questions in advance; 01.05 distinguishes the theory itself, application layers, and tool packaging; 01.06 checks boundaries, object identity, and circle construction; 01.07 allows counterexamples, failures, replacement, and exit; 01.08 checks the relationship between the intellectual framework and its Skill engineering implementation. These numbers are research navigation, not a claim here to have obtained eight full original studies.

The strongest opposing position worries that, without a preset priority of explanations, analysis loses direction. The response is that a mechanism may be given primary importance based on the task and existing evidence, without permanent privilege across tasks. Another objection holds that if domain methods can already answer the question, the framework is useless; the more precise conclusion is that no additional representational layer is needed here. The framework’s boundary checking may be light or may step aside; yielding cannot be interpreted as requiring the theory either to prevail or to fail completely.

D.02.title: D.02 Knowledge, Concepts, Context, and Epistemic Positions
D.02.lead: Understanding someone’s experience, proving a formula, establishing what happened on a particular day, and deciding what is fair cannot be replaced by the same predictive leaderboard. Careful listening and careful verification can proceed together: correcting a date does not cancel someone’s standing to tell their story.
explanation: Original location: Chinese source lines 4996–5011; original anchor section-d-02; short quotation, translated from the Chinese: “Being useful, actionable, consensually accepted, and true are not the same standard.” A verbatim source excerpt for this topic is separately attached in source-slice.md, keeping explanation apart from the original.

This section first distinguishes the burdens of proof of different epistemic activities. Formal derivation must disclose premises and rules; empirical judgment must explain how observations support claims; interpretive research must examine texts, contexts, and competing readings together; normative argument must state reasons and affected positions. Practical and embodied experience may also provide irreplaceable materials about certain circumstances and skills, but cannot automatically answer every causal or normative question. The shared requirement is to make grounds and limits visible, not to reduce all knowledge to prediction scores.

Falsification, paradigms, and research programmes are listed as entry points for criticism at different scales; they should not be combined into a single rule that every counterexample overturns everything. One failed local test may concern auxiliary assumptions, object definitions, measurement, or a broader theory. Examine what the original claim promised, which part the materials touch, and which subsequent judgments depend on it. The possibility of local revision does not mean patches may forever protect the core; when evidence sufficiently touches shared premises, it cannot be dismissed as a small error either.

Changing a question can create valuable new research, but the task change must be public. An original prediction says an indicator will decline, but it does not; later, the question shifts to how people understand that indicator and produces rich interviews. The new interpretive study may hold, but cannot retrospectively turn the old prediction into a hit. Usefulness means assistance for a particular use; actionability means an action plan can be formed from it; consensus means participants reach some agreement; truth concerns whether the corresponding factual proposition holds. The four may be related, but do not define one another.

Language sometimes does more than report facts: under appropriate conditions it constitutes commitments, naming, or granting eligibility. Reports require factual grounds; commitments concern what speakers undertake; granting eligibility involves authorized positions and rules; naming also requires distinguishing an analyst’s introduction of terminology from an actual change in institutional identity. Between uttering a sentence and effectively completing the action, check the speaker’s standing, context, rules, and relevant conditions; literal recognition alone is insufficient.

“I agree” may be a person’s genuine expression, yet still fail to constitute valid authorization under particular pressures, insufficient information, or unmet permission conditions. Understanding the utterance’s meaning and checking institutional conditions are separate tasks; a string cannot directly generate permission. Language mismatch may also stem from translation, terminology, context, or communication-channel differences; it cannot directly diagnose personality or intelligence. Discussing specific language difficulties requires corresponding professional materials and protection, without inferring a personal defect from inability to understand.

Epistemic positions affect access to materials, questions that can be raised, and who is more readily believed. Some people bearing consequences may understand everyday barriers better yet lack opportunities for safe expression and recording. Better listening, translation, and safe entry points can bring previously invisible materials into analysis, but each claim must be verified: excluded people must neither be dismissed a priori nor granted automatic truth privileges for every factual statement. Respecting a subject’s standing and judging factual truth are responsibilities that can be fulfilled together.

Protective non-disclosure can coexist with trustworthy verification. For example, restricted materials may be given to trusted reviewers within a justified scope, while the strength of public conclusions about portions unavailable for public verification is reduced. One must neither require every sensitive detail to be public before acknowledging a problem, nor use protection to waive all verification or expand conclusions without limit. This section connects to §16.6 through safe expression and traceable review, not encouragement of concealment and unchallengeable claims.

Mutual correction among methods must still preserve real differences in theoretical commitments. The influence of position on knowledge production does not imply that objects are entirely fabricated by arbitrary narratives; reasons may enter causal explanation without eliminating the task of understanding meaning. Reliable date records may correct a remembered date, while why the speaker links an experience to a moment and what it means to them remain researchable. Recognizing their standing to tell the story does not guarantee every date is accurate; correcting a date does not establish that all their experience or expression has lost value.

The eight research entries concern the grounds of experience and reasoning, standards of scientific criticism, the relationship between practice and problem-solving, objects and construction, embodiment and lived experience, textual context and understanding, language and concepts in relation to action conditions, and positions and exclusion in knowledge production. This section lists Hume, Descartes, Popper, Kuhn, Lakatos, Peirce, James, Dewey, Husserl, Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Dilthey, Gadamer, Ricoeur, Wittgenstein, Austin, and others as entry points. It does not claim that they agree, or that this text has reconstructed their complete original works. Detailed comparisons of particular authors still require corresponding editions and source texts; a list of names cannot fill an argument.

The strongest objection is that preserving multiple responsibilities for knowledge makes every claim acceptable. The response is that different methods do not mean no standards: criticism should address the actual claim. Empirical facts require material; formal inferences require premises and rules; interpretation requires textual context and competing readings; and normative claims require reasons and affected positions. Another objection accepts only predictable answers, which would unjustifiably erase grounded textual understanding and normative disagreement. Predictive evaluation need not disappear; it simply cannot replace every task.

caseLinks.title: An actual methodological norm: oral history respects narrators while permitting grounded different conclusions

caseNotes.title: An actual methodological norm: oral history respects narrators while permitting grounded different conclusions
caseNotes.text: In the Oral History Association’s 2018 principles, Core Principle 3 explains that memory is shaped by changing personal and social contexts; items 7–9 require attention to power differences, protection from harm, and permission for public use. The final two paragraphs of “Using Oral Sources” in the Statement on Ethics require faithful respect for narrative context while permitting users to reach conclusions different from narrators on accurately cited evidence. Respect, protection, and factual criticism do not exclude one another here.

teachingExamples.title: Expansion of the source’s conditional example: dates may be corrected while experience still deserves to be heard
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a narrator remembers an event on Tuesday, but a reliable original notice and independent records jointly support Wednesday. The date may be corrected to Wednesday while the account of waiting, fear, or ways of understanding remains material about the corresponding experience. A wrong date does not make every experience fictional, and respect for experience does not justify refusing to correct the date.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: changing the question cannot repair an old prediction

D.03.title: D.03 Research Design, Measurement, Causation, and Material Formation
D.03.lead: A table showing a higher approval rate cannot simultaneously tell us whether applying became easier, money actually arrived, and lives improved. The first step in research design is to state which question is being answered, then examine how the material was produced and which other explanations remain compatible with it.
explanation: Source location: Chinese source lines 5012–5027; source anchor section-d-03; short quotation translated from Chinese: “Total effects, specific mediators, joint responses, and reporting mechanisms should be identified separately according to the question asked.” The source excerpt for this topic is separately reproduced verbatim in source-slice.md; explanation and source text are kept separate.

Randomized experiments, natural experiments, observational studies, process tracing, comparative history, oral accounts, and archaeology can each address some identification problems. A method name cannot promise every conclusion. First specify treatment, comparison object, time, outcome, and unit. For example, people invited into a program and people who actually participate are not the same treatment or population. Participants’ before-and-after changes may also reflect self-selection, time trends, and more. Full policy expansion involves capacity and interactions, while a particular individual’s outcome is not directly supplied by a group average. A shared project name does not make these estimands interchangeable.

A total effect may be identified under appropriate assumptions while specific mediators remain unclear. Retain that limited answer about the total effect rather than declaring complete ignorance because every micro-mechanism has not been exhausted. Conversely, describing several mechanisms or establishing local links does not guarantee that they connect within the same cases, population, and window into a complete chain with a net effect. Counteracting channels, different responders, and resource constraints may all change terminal outcomes.

Controlling for the current state may remove a common cause, but may also cut off the historical formation channel under study or introduce selection bias by conditioning on a common outcome. More control variables are therefore not always better. If H affects Y through S and H adds no information conditional on S, separately report H’s total effect on Y and its conditional residual after the specified representation S. In connection with G3, especially do not call a zero conditional residual proof that history never acted; nor does a historical effect automatically pass the historical-increment question.

Measurement should distinguish at least object, observable indicator, construct, and classification rule. The object is the phenomenon to be understood; the indicator is what is actually recorded; the construct is a theoretical expression of a latent attribute; and the classification rule specifies grouping criteria. Multiple indicators reflecting a latent state require examination of how that state affects them and their errors. Components jointly defining an index instead involve content coverage, weights, and composition rules; the same validity argument cannot be imposed mechanically. Test performance, latent capability, resource conditions, and predictive proxies are not equivalent merely because all become numbers.

Trends depend on scale, denominator, measurement method, and sample inclusion. A rising approval rate may mean easier processing or a changed applicant composition. Lower public detection counts may mean less risk, a response preventing events, or a lower detection rate. Indicator improvement may be real progress, real training toward a narrow target, sample selection, or fabrication; several processes may coexist. A shared direction does not decide motives. Good numbers cannot alone establish successful governance, nor does an incentivized indicator directly justify an accusation of manipulation.

The source’s application-process example is a teaching construction. Rising approval rates after simplification may suggest reduced procedural barriers, but livelihood protection also involves actual payments, quality, waiting, and nonapplicants. If barriers exclude nonapplicants, a higher approval rate may increasingly miss difficult circumstances; the denominator and additional outcomes must be specified. Supported local procedural achievements may remain rather than being wholly revoked because more terminal outcomes are unclear.

The absence of dissent in archives has corresponding counterevidentiary force only when relevant dissent should reliably have left records, those records were preserved, and they are accessible. Inability to speak, failure to record, destruction, or records not yet open can all produce silence. Likewise, dates, uses, owners, and actual power associated with archaeological material are different questions. Dating can support temporal location without automatically establishing that an object belonged to a ruler; traces supporting a kind of activity do not simultaneously establish a complete institution. Material formation is part of the inference.

Observed records can be viewed as results of object states passing through collection, response, and reporting processes. If observations are compatible with several generating processes, more records using the same conventions may not resolve identification. New discriminating material is needed, such as independent measurement, collection coverage, or response timing. The simplified calculation below shows indistinguishability only. It is not an estimate of real epidemics, policies, or risks, and supplies no personal health advice.

Positive average effects in both segments do not mean their product equals the whole chain. One must know whether people changed in the first segment are also responders in the second, whether upstream outputs correspond to downstream inputs, and whether timing and shared conditions hold. Body §2.4.2 gives a two-type counterexample, explicitly recalculated in this guide: type 0 changes only in the first segment; type 1 responds only to an externally set mediator. Both segment means are 1/2, yet no one traverses the complete chain.

The nine topic locations correspond to causal mechanisms; research design; cases, processes, and history; statistics and uncertainty; measurement and proxies; incentive-driven changes in indicators; replication and publication selection; archival and oral silence; and archaeological material. These are research entry points, not a claim that one section resolves every methodological debate. The strongest objection is that so many distinctions prevent any conclusion. The response is to retain answers the task actually identifies—such as grounded total effects, local mechanisms, scope boundaries, or specific process knowledge—and stop only additional assertions the material cannot yet support.

caseLinks.title: An actual research record: Snow traced illness addresses and water sources

caseNotes.title: An actual research record: Snow traced illness addresses and water sources
caseNotes.text: In the 1855 second edition, Snow's account of the 1854 London water-supply investigation explains that people who had been moved required tracing to their residence at illness onset. Households often could not directly identify their water company, so bills and chemical tests were combined to check the source. He also records cases whose water supply remained unascertained during the four-week inquiry. This material was not a naturally complete data table; it was formed through address checks, exposure classification, and handling missingness.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, transcript of the original 1855 second edition
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Original printed pp77–80: “In cases where persons had been removed…”; “The inquiry was necessarily…”; the chemical-verification paragraph; final item of “Of these it was ascertained…”
caseNotes.boundary: Only the author's original account of the inquiry is used to illustrate data formation and missingness. It does not establish random assignment, complete mediation, or modern unconfounded identification. The historical inquiry was not replicated, and its chemical values are not cited as current operational advice.

argumentSteps: Register treatment, comparison, timing, outcome, and units, distinguishing invitation, participation, policy, and individual targets.
Examine why the design identifies its target and under which assumptions; evaluate total effects separately from mediation and joint responses.
Explain indicators and constructs, scales and denominators, samples and record-generation processes, and list competing explanations.
For archival silence and material traces, check expected recording, preservation, accessibility, and the specific scope of inference.

When explanations cannot be distinguished, preserve multiple explanations and grounded local answers and plan discriminating material; neither stories nor indicator direction may fill the whole chain.

teachingExamples.title: Expanded teaching example from the source: approval is not provision
teachingExamples.text: Imagine an application approval rate rises after a process is simplified. Judging whether protection improved additionally requires actual payments after approval, service quality, and groups that did not apply; approval cannot simply stand for resources having arrived. With only approval data, limit the claim to changes in approval outcomes; an explanation through procedural barriers still requires evidence of the generating process.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Expanded from the source's teaching example, without actual project data.
teachingExamples.boundary: No causal estimates or subsidy effects are invented.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: multiplying two mean effects fails
teachingExamples.text: Following §2.4.2, let two types s∈{0,1} have equal weight, treatment a∈{0,1}, mediator m(a)=a(1−s), and outcome y(a,m)=sm. For type 0, treatment raises m by 1 but y is always 0; for type 1, a does not affect m, but directly setting m from 0 to 1 raises y by 1. Thus the average a→m effect=1/2 and the average effect of setting m→y=1/2, giving product=1/4. Yet actual y(a,m(a)) is constantly 0 for both types, so the whole-chain effect=0.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All functions and equal weights are explicit formal constructions, with no real-world observations.
teachingExamples.boundary: This only refutes the universal inference of multiplying without joint conditions; it does not deny that independent designs can identify actual total effects.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: the same ten records, three processes
teachingExamples.text: Take 100 opportunities, baseline risk 0.2, detection rate 1, and no prevention, yielding 20 expected records. A lowers risk to 0.1 with everything else unchanged, yielding 10; B retains risk 0.2 but lowers detection to 0.5, also yielding 10; C retains risk 0.2 and detection 1 but prevents half of events through response, again yielding 10. The simplified expectation 100×risk×proportion not prevented×detection rate cannot identify which process occurred from an outcome of 10 alone.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Independent homogeneous opportunities, no false positives, and fixed proportions are teaching assumptions; counts are expectations, not measurements.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual processes may be dependent and more complex; the example estimates no actual risk or medical effect.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: historical effects already incorporated into the current state
teachingExamples.text: Let H be binary, with structural equations S=H and Y=S. Changing H from 0 to 1 changes Y from 0 to 1, so history's total effect is 1; but knowing S completely determines Y, and H adds no predictive information beyond S. A zero conditional increment cannot mean history had no effect, nor can a total effect of 1 automatically count as a positive G3 increment.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Deterministic structural equations solely for teaching, with an explicit intervention meaning and no other paths.
teachingExamples.boundary: Because H and S correspond deterministically, observational data cannot justify claiming that a general real-world direct effect has been identified.

counterexamples.text: H is nonsignificant after controlling for S, so the past did not cause the current outcome.
counterexamples.effect: Distinguish total effects from conditional residuals; controlling for S may block the channel through which history formed the present.

counterexamples.text: Both segment means are positive, so their product must yield a positive whole-chain effect.
counterexamples.effect: Joint responses may not overlap; an explicit functional counterexample yields a zero whole-chain effect.

counterexamples.text: Positive public records have declined, so actual risk must have declined.
counterexamples.effect: Collection, detection, and response processes can produce record changes in the same direction; discriminating material is needed.

questionAnswers.question: Why can a clear total effect coexist with unresolved mediators?
questionAnswers.answer: A design may identify a specified total effect without distinguishing transmission channels. Do not force in a mechanism, but do not withdraw an independently established total effect either.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why is the complete chain zero in the two-segment average-effects example?
questionAnswers.answer: The first segment is effective for type 0 and the second responds for type 1; no type completes both segments.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If records fall from 20 to 10, can we establish that the detection rate stayed unchanged?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Identical numbers are compatible with different generating processes; independent collection and response material is needed.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: When does absence of dissent in an archive have counterevidentiary force?
questionAnswers.answer: When dissent, if present, should reliably have been recorded, the records preserved and accessible, and the relevant generating conditions are supported.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

D.04.title: D.04 Systems, Control, Feedback, Resilience, and Delays
D.04.lead: Knowing the network diagram of a system does not mean knowing its responses; knowing each task can be done separately does not mean all can be completed together. Systems analysis must place observability, reachability, resources, deadlines, and authority within the same actual task.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5028–5043; source anchor section-d-04; brief quotation translated from Chinese: “Investigation, scheduling, and feedback should serve strategies that can actually be executed.” An exact source excerpt is separately attached in source-slice.md; explanation and source text remain separate.

System representation connects stocks, flows, feedback, delays, constraints, and boundaries to specific objects. A stock is an accumulated quantity at a point in time; a flow is inflow or outflow per unit time; feedback is a returning effect influencing subsequent states; a delay is the time a channel or response requires; constraints limit available actions; boundaries specify what the analysis includes. Variables and units must be proportionate to the actual task; drawing arrows alone does not establish a mechanism.

Feedback requires only that a returning influence affect subsequent states; it does not guarantee truthful, timely, or beneficial information. False indicators can cause later misallocation and still constitute a returning effect. Receiving correct feedback without changing subsequent states does not yet establish that the corresponding feedback loop is connected. An organization learning a practice, an emergent pattern appearing, insufficiency of the current representation, and cross-scale causality holding are four different judgments. Unpredictable patterns cannot all be called learning, nor can representation failure automatically be elevated into higher-level causality.

Observability must be relative to the target. Under linear observation O and target L, if every unobservable difference leaves the target unchanged—that is, ker(O)⊆ker(L)—observations identify Lx without reconstructing all states. The public argument is: if Ox=Ox′, then O(x−x′)=0; inclusion gives L(x−x′)=0, hence Lx=Lx′. Conversely, if some v satisfies Ov=0 but Lv≠0, x and x+v have identical observations but different targets, so the observation cannot uniquely identify the target. This result rests on assumptions such as linearity and a specified state domain; real-world mappings still need checking.

The rank of a controllability matrix establishes only a particular reachability property in an ideal model. Actual execution remains constrained by time, input magnitude, resources, lawfulness of actions, and authority. Even if a one-dimensional system's control direction spans its entire state space, a single time step with input bounded by 1 cannot take it from 0 to 2. Rank and qualifications to act operate at different levels; mathematically allowed infinite inputs cannot be treated as actually available resources.

The same network diagram with different response rules can produce different propagation. Nodes may change after one contact, or require multiple neighbors, a specific sequence, or sufficient resources. Delays combined with deadlines, forgetting, and depletion may terminate propagation. In special models with infinite waiting, monotonic accumulation, and no forgetting, finite delays may change only arrival times, not final coverage. Neither result can be generalized into the other; first state the dynamic rules and observation endpoint.

Resilience concerns maintenance or recovery of a relation or function under disturbance, but what is maintained may be an unjust institution. Successful maintenance cannot directly establish justification, nor can restoring the original state be assumed as every person's life goal. People may wish to exit an old structure or change distribution instead of merely restoring it. Function, values, rights, and action choices still need separate explanation.

Stock models help distinguish temporary flow balance from sustainable capacity. A falling backlog may arise from reduced demand, increased capability, changed measurement definitions, or outsourcing; a curve alone cannot distinguish them. Temporarily increasing throughput by overextending personnel does not establish greater long-term capacity either. Short-term overshoot may be compatible with several delays, response strengths, or external disturbances; a single curve cannot directly identify every delay.

When history is sufficiently encoded in the current state, general adaptation and learning may still occur, and carrier-based feedback-mediated learning may hold. Historical-increment learning separately asks whether history adds information or capability beyond the specified current representation. No extra historical increment cannot mean no learning of any kind, and one behavioral change cannot automatically be registered as passing every formal learning contract.

Joint feasibility is stronger than separate feasibility. Two tasks due in the same period, each requiring one unit of capacity, are individually feasible but cannot both be completed when total capacity for that period is one. Add genuinely available capacity or lawfully change timing; the same resource cannot be allocated twice on paper. Furthermore, when identical observations correspond to several states, each state having a correct action does not ensure a shared action is available without knowing the true state. Executable strategies must depend on information actually obtainable.

The twelve topics cover system representation, control and feedback, observer effects, complex adaptation and emergence, network cascades, resilience, historical lock-in, organizational ecology, observational blind spots, intervention capabilities, regulators and internal models, and stocks, delays, and overshoot. Listed figures such as Bertalanffy, Meadows, Wiener, Ashby, Holling, and Arthur provide research navigation, not an assertion that they agree completely or that this section reconstructs all original proofs. The strongest objection is that real-world restrictions render formal analysis useless. Formal analysis can still exclude impossible inferences and clarify conditions needing supplementation; it simply cannot cross its model boundaries to serve as real-world authorization.

distinctions.leftText: A returning effect influences subsequent states.
distinctions.rightText: Truth, timeliness, effects, and learning contracts all require separate checks.

distinctions.leftText: Observations suffice to determine the Lx asked for by the task.
distinctions.rightText: A stronger requirement; target-irrelevant directions may not need observation.

distinctions.leftText: Reachability under the model's input and time assumptions.
distinctions.rightText: Additionally requires bounds, resources, authority, time windows, stopping, and remedy.

distinctions.leftText: Each task individually satisfies resource conditions.
distinctions.rightText: Overall constraints remain satisfied when tasks compete for resources simultaneously.

distinctions.leftText: Maintenance of a function or relation.
distinctions.rightText: Requires normative reasons and the circumstances of affected people; stability cannot establish it.

boundaries: ker(O)⊆ker(L) is a condition for linear target identification; it does not directly encompass arbitrary nonlinear or real-world objects.
Delays leave final coverage unchanged only under explicit conditions such as infinite waiting, monotonic accumulation, and no forgetting.
Stock and overshoot curves cannot independently identify actual channels; resource transfers and overextension need checking.
Each state having a correct action does not imply a shared usable strategy under identical observations.
All mathematical examples in this lesson are conditional constructions; no actual control system was operated or historical spaceflight experiment replicated.

Why can the full-rank example not reach 2 in one step?
Does a declining backlog establish increased capacity?
When does delay leave final coverage unchanged?
Does strong resilience establish that an institution should continue?

caseLinks.title: Actual original test record: Apollo13's emergency filter adaptation faced material and time constraints

caseNotes.title: Actual original test record: Apollo13's emergency filter adaptation faced material and time constraints
caseNotes.text: NASA report CSD-A-1066 explains that the emergency adaptation during Apollo13 had to work, use materials available to the crew, be easy to communicate clearly, and be evaluated early enough to prepare an alternative. The report records unoccupied-chamber tests injecting carbon dioxide to simulate crew metabolism; the second phase determined canister replacement times to reduce electricity consumption from reliance on telemetry for that purpose. This brings actual materials, communicable procedures, deadlines, observation, and power constraints into the same task.

caseNotes.boundary: Only these three body pages were checked, with visual inspection of scans. No claim is made to repeat the tests, review all appendix data, or establish resolution of every spaceflight-system risk; report values are not used to guide actual life-support operations.

argumentSteps: First connect system variables, flow units, boundaries, and response rules to the specific task.
Test whether observations distinguish necessary states for the target; do not demand irrelevant full-state reconstruction.
Check ideal reachability separately from actual deadlines, input bounds, resources, and authority.
Check dynamic rules, delays, and endpoints before explaining propagation, stocks, and resilience; avoid inferring mechanisms from diagrams.
Check joint resource constraints and shared strategies under identical observations; investigation and scheduling should serve actual executability.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: not all states need to be visible
teachingExamples.text: Let x=(x1,x2), observation O=(1,0), and target L=(2,0). The invisible directions are (0,t), all of which leave L unchanged. Observation z=x1 therefore suffices to obtain target 2z, while x2 remains unknown. If the target changes to L′=(0,1), then (0,0) and (0,1) have the same observation but different targets, making identification impossible.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The state space is R²; observation and target are linear and noise-free.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual measurement errors and target definitions require separate checks; the example cannot justify ignoring critical states.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: full rank can still be too late
teachingExamples.text: For one-dimensional dynamics x at the next step=x+u, the control matrix is [1] with rank 1. Starting at 0 with target 2, if only one step is available and |u|≤1, the reachable interval is [−1,1], so 2 is unreachable. If two steps are allowed with u=1 each, reaching 2 is formally possible, but real-world authority and resources are still not established.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A deterministic discrete model without external disturbances, with explicit time steps and magnitude bounds.
teachingExamples.boundary: No actual equipment capability is estimated.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: joint tasks and hidden states
teachingExamples.text: Two tasks with the same deadline each require capacity 1, while total capacity is 1. Each is separately feasible, but their combined need is 2>1. Capacity rising to 2 or a lawful staggering of time windows changes the conditions. Separately, suppose state A succeeds only under action a and state B only under b, but both states have identical observations and a≠b. Without new information, no single action is correct for both.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Action sets and success conditions are teaching constructions; the latter example permits only actions a and b.
teachingExamples.boundary: In reality, safe pausing or investigation may be studied separately, but cannot be assumed without grounds to be costless or always feasible.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: identical connections, different delay outcomes
teachingExamples.text: Suppose there is only one edge A→B. An event leaves A at time 0 and reaches B after delay 2. If B must receive it before time 1, propagation fails; if infinite waiting is allowed and arrival permanently activates B, activation occurs at time 2 and final coverage remains A and B.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Finite positive delays, with no forgetting, depletion, or other edges; the two situations differ only in their deadline conditions.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not assert that all real-world delays affect only speed or necessarily terminate.

counterexamples.text: The feedback returned, so the system must have learned the correct action.
counterexamples.effect: Returning effects, truthfulness, beneficialness, and learning each require evidence.

counterexamples.text: The control matrix has full rank, so there is authority to complete the target action immediately.
counterexamples.effect: Rank provides neither time and resources nor real-world authorization; the amplitude-limited example already refutes this inference.

counterexamples.text: Every state has a correct action, so correct action is possible under any information conditions.
counterexamples.effect: When information cannot distinguish states, the intersection of feasible actions may be empty.

questionAnswers.question: If O=(1,0) cannot see x2, can it calculate 2x1?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes, because the invisible direction does not change the target; reconstructing the irrelevant x2 is unnecessary.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why can the full-rank example not reach 2 in one step?
questionAnswers.answer: The implemented input bound permits an increase or decrease of only 1 in one step; formal coverage of directions does not mean arbitrary magnitudes are available.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does a declining backlog establish increased capacity?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. Changes in demand, outsourcing, or statistical boundaries could also produce it; channel material is needed.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: When does delay leave final coverage unchanged?
questionAnswers.answer: Only when the relevant conditions of the specific model hold, such as unlimited waiting and monotonic accumulation without forgetting, and all necessary arrivals still occur.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Does strong resilience establish that an institution should continue?
questionAnswers.answer: It does not; maintenance of function and normative justification require separate judgments.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

D.05.title: D.05 Information, representation, and borrowing from mathematics and physics
D.05.lead: A table retaining only totals may suffice to answer questions about quantity but not distribution. Abstraction is not uniformly bad; the issue is whether it preserves the distinctions needed for the current question without covertly extending that sufficiency to future dynamics, interventions, or judgments of human value.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5044–5059; source anchor section-d-05; short quotation: ‘Reduced source information need not cause failure of the current task’ (translated from Chinese). The source slice for this topic is attached verbatim in source-slice.md, keeping the explanation separate from the source.

Representations should be evaluated along five separate dimensions: whether source states can be recovered, whether the specified task can be completed, whether computational costs are affordable, whether future dynamics are closed, and whether sufficiency remains after permitted interventions. Lossless recovery of the finest detail is not always required for the current task; a question about totals need not retain every item's identity. But adequacy for one task does not mean adequacy for every future question. When the target changes, time advances, or an intervention alters a channel, distinctions previously merged may matter again.

Let the source domain be X, the representation f:X→Z, and the question q:X→Y. An answer function g satisfying q=g∘f exists if and only if source states with the same representation have the same answer: q is constant on every preimage set of f. Necessity: when f(x)=f(x′), q(x)=g(f(x))=g(f(x′))=q(x′). Sufficiency: for a reachable representation z∈f(X), define g(z) as q(x) for any corresponding x. Constancy on each preimage makes the definition independent of that choice. Only actually reachable representations need definitions here; extending to all of Z additionally requires ordinary set-theoretic premises such as an appropriate nonempty codomain.

This criterion supplies positive conditions under which abstraction works, rather than merely warning of information loss. For example, retaining (a+b) suffices to answer a+b even though a and b cannot be recovered. If the question changes to whether a is greater than b, answers within a preimage may differ and sufficiency fails. After failure, one may add the hidden share that actually affects the target, without endlessly recovering every detail. Additional measurement and maintenance carry financial, privacy, and comprehension burdens; finer representation is not automatically better.

Sufficiency after permitted interventions is an additional question. If the original target is only total stock a+b+c, storing the total suffices. If the task is to report the remaining total after removing the a share, different a values under the same total produce different results. Adding a permits an answer by subtracting a from the total, while the individual details of b and c still need not be recovered. Refinement should thus target the question and permitted operations; one failure of closure does not make every abstraction invalid.

Unit conversion, accounting identities, empirical conversion rates, and value weights have different foundations. Unit conversion restates the same quantity under definitions and unit correspondences; accounting identities check balance within recorded boundaries; empirical conversion rates require corresponding material and may change with conditions; value weights express normative choices. A unit-conversion formula in one domain cannot prove that different people's suffering, attention, and responsibility are precisely commensurable.

Conservation of matter or energy requires correct boundaries and dimensions. Sharing words such as ‘load,’ ‘potential field,’ or ‘entropy’ does not automatically confer conservation laws on social domains. Real technical improvements can eliminate duplicated labor or reduce harm and thereby lower actual costs; they need not be forced into an account where an equal cost must have moved somewhere invisible. Suspected cost transfers require specific bearers and channels, rather than unfalsifiable hidden burdens used to preserve a metaphor.

Gödel's incompleteness and computability results depend on particular formal systems and problem classes; they do not imply that every finite task is undecidable. A finite, complete, accessible table can be checked entry by entry. On general infinite domains, existence of an answer as a mathematical function does not guarantee an algorithm that always halts. An existing algorithm may exceed the budget; an affordable one may still lack data obtainable in time; even with data in hand, a user may operate it incorrectly. These levels require separate verification and cannot all be settled at once by the claim that no information was lost.

Model parsimony cannot be measured only by final parameter counts. How many representations were searched, how parameters were tuned, what resources were spent, and whether the target changed all affect comparison. A final model with just two parameters after extensive hidden searching does not automatically overfit less or cost less than a method with more parameters fixed beforehand. Formal comparisons should preserve the selection process and strong comparators, rather than substitute mathematical or physical prestige for empirical premises in the target domain.

Multiple conversions must preserve the same final question q. If the first step f is already sufficient, the second step h must preserve the distinctions needed for the original answer within the actually reachable intermediate representations f(X), so that a k can satisfy q=k∘h∘f. The first step successfully answering totals and the second successfully answering rankings does not mean their composition can still answer the original total question. Changes in local tasks must be disclosed; correctness on two different local tasks cannot masquerade as sufficiency of the whole chain.

The eight research entry points cover Shannon information theory; compression and recasting; analogies between entropy and social order; borrowing conservation and potential fields; incompleteness and computability; coarse-graining and closure; historical withdrawal of information- or quantum-universe analogies; and model selection and expressive capacity. This section requires preserving the specific assumptions and boundaries of these topics, without claiming from a table of contents that all theories have been adopted or proved. The strongest objection is that any compression is dangerous; the preimage criterion above shows that a lossy representation can be rigorously sufficient for a specified task. The opposite objection—that task sufficiency eliminates further checks—overlooks the independent conditions of algorithms, time, data, and actual use.

distinctions.leftText: All specified details of the original state can be reconstructed.
distinctions.rightText: Only the distinctions needed by q must be retained; other information may be lost.

distinctions.leftText: Mathematically, q factors through the representation.
distinctions.rightText: Algorithms, termination, and other conditions are also required; existence alone does not establish them.

distinctions.leftText: These depend on definitions, dimensions, and accounting boundaries.
distinctions.rightText: These respectively require empirical material or explicit normative reasons.

distinctions.leftText: Enough for the current question.
distinctions.rightText: Subsequent changes and permitted operations also preserve the required distinctions; additional checks are needed.

distinctions.leftText: Fewer parameters or a shorter expression.
distinctions.rightTitle: Parsimony of the entire selection process
distinctions.rightText: Also includes searching, tuning, resources, and target changes.

boundaries: The preimage-constancy criterion initially constructs the answer function on f(X); actual computability and data acquisition require separate checks.
Social burdens do not acquire physical conservation laws through shared terminology; real reductions in cost are possible.
A finite complete table differs from a general infinite problem; incompleteness must not be used to reject every finite judgment.
A multistep conversion cannot change the final question and then claim the whole chain remains sufficient.
The formal teaching examples contain no measured data; this lesson has not converted the encoding of user files or deleted their information.

Why can a total of 10 not answer how much remains after removing a?
Can physical conservation apply directly to a total quantity of suffering?
If the second step answers a new question entirely correctly, has it preserved the old question?

caseLinks.title: A restriction in an actual standard: Unicode compatibility normalization erases some distinctions

caseNotes.title: A restriction in an actual standard: Unicode compatibility normalization erases some distinctions
caseNotes.text: Revision 58 of Unicode UAX15 lists Unicode18.0.0 and August 12, 2026. Section 1.1 explains that compatibility equivalence may preserve visual or semantic distinctions meaningful in particular contexts. Section 1.2 explicitly warns against blindly applying NFKC/NFKD to arbitrary text because they remove formatting distinctions that may affect round-trip conversion and textual semantics. This is an actual encoding standard limiting the uses of a conversion.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Unicode Standard Annex15, fixed Revision58
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Version table; the following two paragraphs on compatibility equivalence in §1.1; Normalization Forms KC and KD must not… and the following paragraph in §1.2
caseNotes.boundary: Only the standard's definitions and usage warnings were checked. This does not claim all normalization is harmful or every semantic task fails, and character conversion is not equated with human information and value.

argumentSteps: Fix the final question q, source domain, representation f, and permitted operations, and separate the five dimensions of sufficiency.
Use constancy of q within each preimage of f to explicitly prove or refute existence of an answer function.
When dynamics or interventions produce a mismatch, add only the distinctions actually needed, and measure privacy, measurement, maintenance, and comprehension costs.
Keep the same final question through multiple conversions, checking subsequent sufficiency on the actually reachable intermediate domain.
Separately check function existence, effective algorithms, budget, timely data, and correct use; do not extrapolate mathematical prestige or conservation terminology into social facts.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: sufficient for totals, insufficient for distribution
teachingExamples.text: On the finite domain X={(1,3),(2,2),(3,1)}, f(a,b)=a+b is always 4. If q=a+b, then g(4)=4 suffices. If q′ asks whether a>b, the three answers are false, false, and true, so they are not constant within the same preimage. No answer function seeing only 4 can therefore be correct for all three.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The finite domain and questions are explicit, with no measurement noise.
teachingExamples.boundary: This finite criterion is not treated as a performance guarantee for every actual compression task.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: add only the needed hidden share
teachingExamples.text: Let the state be x=(a,b,c), with original representation total T=a+b+c. Compare (2,3,5) and (4,1,5), both totaling 10. After the permitted removal of a, the remainders are 8 and 6, so the original representation is insufficient. Adding a gives (T,a), allowing the same answer T−a without separately recovering b and c.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Stocks are nonnegative, the operation removing a is explicitly defined, and there are no other dynamics or costs.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual measurement, permissions, and operational costs are not established by the formal example.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: two steps must preserve the same question
teachingExamples.text: Let X={0,1,2,3}, with final question q asking parity. The first step f(x)=x mod2 suffices. If the second step h maps both 0 and 1 to one symbol, the final representation cannot distinguish parity. h may complete the local task ‘does this belong to the binary set?’ without preserving the original q.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Entirely finite functions that can be exhaustively enumerated.
teachingExamples.boundary: Completing different local tasks cannot restore distinctions between final answers that have already been merged.

counterexamples.text: Once original details are lost, no task can be completed.
counterexamples.effect: When the answer is constant on each preimage, rigorous sufficiency for the specified task remains possible.

counterexamples.text: Social loads exist, so any burden reduction must transfer an equal amount to someone else.
counterexamples.effect: There is no cross-domain conservation proof; technical or process improvements can actually eliminate duplicated costs.

counterexamples.text: An answer function exists, so there is always an algorithm that is timely, inexpensive, and correctly used.
counterexamples.effect: Functions, algorithms, budgets, data, and actual use each have their own conditions.

questionAnswers.question: Why does the sufficiency proof initially define g only on f(X)?
questionAnswers.answer: Only reachable representations correspond to actual source states; no task conditions need be invented for intermediate values that never occur.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Why can a total of 10 not answer how much remains after removing a?
questionAnswers.answer: The same total corresponds to different a values, so the post-operation target is not constant within the preimage; adding a suffices.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can physical conservation apply directly to a total quantity of suffering?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Correct objects, dimensions, boundaries, and bridging are required; shared words cannot establish it.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: If the second step answers a new question entirely correctly, has it preserved the old question?
questionAnswers.answer: Not necessarily. Check whether it still distinguishes different answers to the old q on reachable intermediate representations.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

D.06.title: D.06 Human nature, evolution, habits, and capacity for action
D.06.lead: Someone actually signing a document does not mean they can safely say no; a behavior remaining stable for a long time does not mean it is permanently written into genes. Explaining human action requires separating formation, circumstances, choices, and responsibility, then connecting them according to the evidence.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5060–5075; source anchor section-d-06; short quotation: ‘That constrained people actually act, can safely refuse, give valid consent, and bear a particular responsibility remain four different judgments’ (translated from Chinese). The source slice for this topic is attached verbatim in source-slice.md, keeping the explanation separate from the source.

Current function, historical adaptation, drift, cultural transmission, individual intention, and welfare consequences answer different questions. Behavior beneficial now may have originated under other conditions and acquired this function later. A retained cultural form may involve transmission, constraints, or path continuity rather than endorsement by every member. Welfare consequences concern who benefits or is harmed; individual intention concerns the actor's reasons. Good outcomes cannot establish good intentions retrospectively, nor does historical existence imply that something ought to be retained.

Cooperation may arise from kinship, reciprocity, reputation, partner choice, or institutional constraints. Analysis should specify who can observe behavior, who responds afterward, what benefits and costs are anticipated, and who bears the actual costs. Similar cooperative appearances cannot establish the same mechanism. Without responders or information channels, “reputation” alone cannot explain everything. Several mechanisms may coexist, but their respective material must be specified rather than switching stories arbitrarily to keep the conclusion invulnerable.

Personality differences may appear as conditionally stable tendencies, but slow change does not mean heredity, immutability, or essence. Repeated similar behavior may jointly arise from habit, environmental selection, opportunity, situational cues, and bodily skills. Cross-context records must also examine who entered which situations and whether measurements are comparable. Checking situations first is an investigative order, not a prior verdict that personality has no role. Comparisons of personality, situation, and interaction need proportionate information and evaluation conditions; rich situational material must not be compared with crude personality labels to declare a theoretical victory.

General learning may be supported by practice, performance, and formation processes, for example when skill changes have entered the current state. G3 asks the narrower question of what increment history still provides beyond a specified current representation. Skill learning having occurred can coexist with no observed extra historical increment; failing the narrow contract does not mean no learning occurred. Environmental opportunities and bodily practice also cannot be reduced to an abstract incentive score. Preserve what people can actually do, know, and bear.

Constrained actions may still be decisions made by actors, but that does not make them freely given consent. Separate actual behavior, information at the time, local control, options for refusal, consequences, and attribution of responsibility. The source’s employee signing a record under credible punishment is a teaching example: signing actually occurred, safe refusal may have been unavailable, and valid consent requires separate examination. Designers, supervisors, and beneficiaries may bear different responsibilities along the chains of rules, commands, and benefits. “They chose it themselves” must not erase the control chain; constraint also must not be equated with having no agency whatsoever.

High cost does not automatically establish sincerity, love, or identification. Costs may arise from coercion, misjudgment, lack of alternatives, reputational incentives, or other causes; actual situations and refutable material must be examined. Low-cost goodwill does not lose ordinary value because it fails HV11’s formal contract. Formal outcome registration and ordinary help, care, and meaning are not one ranking of value. High cost must not become a universal credential for judging love or moral status.

The explanatory contributions of situation, personality, and their interaction may overlap. If all shared explanation is first assigned to situation and personality’s residual is then zero, this establishes at most no additional increment under that representation and ordering, not the nonexistence of personality-related variables. Assigning it first to personality and then denying situation is equally mistaken. Explain the distinctions among shared explanation, independent increments, and interaction; do not treat a statistical allocation rule as an ontological conclusion about people.

Behavioral differences caused by a treatment belong to the complete manipulated condition package; they must not be arbitrarily divided into an independent effect of one component. Hurry instructions may simultaneously change available time, expected responsibility, tension, and attention. Even if an experiment finds between-group differences, it does not automatically identify these mediators separately. Answering the effect of one component requires additional design and material. Nor may observed group differences be elevated into fixed personality judgments about any individual.

Neither natural selection nor social selection directly generates an ought. Successful persistence of a form may be an object of causal research, but does not thereby confer normative legitimacy. Institutional reward for a behavior also does not establish that it should be encouraged. Responsibility judgments likewise require explicit normative premises, control capacity, information, and specific consequences; evolutionary stories or the bare fact of a constrained person’s action cannot complete all attribution of responsibility.

The eight topic entries cover, in order, human nature and situationism; selection, adaptation, and drift; cultural evolution and dual inheritance; cooperation mechanisms; personality–situation interaction; freedom, responsibility, and capability; habit, embodiment, and environment; and explanations of action beyond incentives. Names such as Boyd and Richerson indicate research leads, not adoption of the whole of cultural-evolution research as an undifferentiated axiom of human nature. The strongest objection is that emphasizing situations excuses everyone. The response is to allocate responsibility more precisely across capability, information, control, and design chains, rather than replace one extreme with another.

distinctions.rightText: Slow change does not establish this; environment and practice still need consideration.

caseLinks.title: Actual original research: a limited comparison of hurry conditions and helping behavior

caseNotes.title: Actual original research: a limited comparison of hurry conditions and helping behavior
caseNotes.text: The experiment reported by Darley and Batson in 1973 was actually conducted on December 14–16, 1970. The original paper states that 47 people entered the experimental arrangements and that data for 7 were excluded because of procedural contamination or suspicion about the situation, leaving 40 for analysis. Hurry levels were manipulated through different instructions; the authors reported differences in helping responses associated with them. The result is suitable for examining situational conditions, but cannot establish the absence of all personality factors or separately identify pure time pressure.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Darley & Batson, JPSP 27(1), 100–108, scan of the original 1973 publication
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Printed p102, Subjects; p103, Scheduling and footnote 3; pp103–104, Variable 2: Hurry; pp104–105, Overall Helping Behavior
caseNotes.boundary: A small sample of seminary students in a specific situation; footnote 3 discloses an assignment error that increased the moderate-hurry group. This guide does not reestimate statistics, claim universal replication, or adopt unidentified personality essences or single-mediator conclusions.

argumentSteps: Separate a behavior’s current function, historical formation, transmission, intention, and welfare, seeking material for each question.
For cooperation and stable tendencies, specify observation and response channels, opportunities, practice, and selection and measurement across situations.
Separate actual action, safe refusal, valid consent, and responsibility, tracing the different control positions of designers, supervisors, and beneficiaries.
Disclose overlap and increments when comparing personality and situation; do not split condition-package effects into unidentified individual components.
Recognize the potential value of general learning and low-cost goodwill, without deriving normative authorization from evolutionary persistence, cost, or effects.

teachingExamples.title: Expansion of the source’s teaching example: signing under credible punishment
teachingExamples.text: An imagined employee is told that failing to sign a record will lead to credible punishment, then signs personally. The signing behavior can be established; safe refusal and valid consent require separate judgment. The organizational designer who sets the rule, the supervisor who applies pressure, and the beneficiary who receives gains may have different responsibilities. A signature cannot compress the entire control chain into the employee’s sole responsibility.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Follows the source’s teaching example; no real employee or punishment is involved.
teachingExamples.boundary: No legal liability is adjudicated; actual responsibility requires applicable norms and facts.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: overlap does not mean one side is nonexistent
teachingExamples.text: Let four constructed records have situation code S=(0,0,1,1), tendency proxy P=(0,0,1,1), and behavior Y=(0,0,1,1). S alone fits Y perfectly, and adding P provides no further fit gain; using P first and adding S gives the same result. Thus zero increment cannot distinguish which variable has an independent real mechanism, much less establish that the other kind of factor is nonexistent.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The three identical sequences are a formal counterexample, not personality-measurement data or a causal model.
teachingExamples.boundary: No real effects of personality or situation are estimated; real identification needs independent variation, measurement, and appropriate design.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: low-cost goodwill still has value
teachingExamples.text: An imagined coworker brings back a needed document while already going that way. There is no major self-sacrifice, but it does spare the other person one trip. It can be described as ordinary help without first proving high cost or a formal HV11 result. Further claims about changed long-term relationships or institutional feedback would still need corresponding material.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The people and assistance are teaching assumptions.
teachingExamples.boundary: One small act of help does not establish personality essence or repaired long-term relationships.

counterexamples.text: This habit has remained unchanged for years, so it must be hereditary and unchangeable.
counterexamples.effect: Stability alone cannot distinguish mechanisms such as practice, environmental selection, opportunity, and heredity.

counterexamples.text: A personality proxy adds no increment after situation is entered first, so personality is entirely nonexistent.
counterexamples.effect: Allocation of shared explanation depends on representation and ordering; the formal identical-column example refutes that inference.

counterexamples.text: The employee signed personally, so the institutional designer and supervisor no longer have responsibility.
counterexamples.effect: The fact of action does not erase refusal conditions or responsibility across levels of control.

questionAnswers.question: Why does a behavior being useful now not prove that it originated for that function?
questionAnswers.answer: Current consequences and historical formation are different questions; functions may have changed, and other formation processes may exist.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: Can actual action and free consent be respectively true and false?
questionAnswers.answer: Yes. A constrained actor may have local agency without safe refusal conditions; these need separate judgments.
questionAnswers.basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

questionAnswers.question: In the identical-column example, what does no increment from adding P after S establish?
questionAnswers.answer: In that data representation, P adds no fitting information. It does not identify whether personality or situation is nonexistent, or which is causal.

questionAnswers.question: If experimental hurry instructions produce a difference, may it be called a pure time effect directly?
questionAnswers.answer: Not automatically. Instructions may change several conditions simultaneously; individual components or mediators require additional identification.
