D.18.title: D.18 Money, Credit, Finance, and Crises
D.18.lead: An asset-price decline, a demand for additional payment or collateral, and an actual loss are different things. Financial analysis must retain currency, maturity, priority, collateral, and accounting definitions. Statistical comparisons must also check methodology versions to avoid depicting a change of definition as a sudden change in actual burdens.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5258–5273; source anchor section-d-18; short quotation, translated: 'Collateral revaluation, demands for additional payment or collateral, sales, price feedback, and credit contraction must be explained link by link; one price decline cannot fill in the entire chain.' The source passage for this topic is also preserved verbatim in source-slice.md; the explanation is separate from the source.

Financial analysis must specify currency, maturity, priority, collateral, entity, and valuation basis. The same nominal amount carries different risks at different maturities, repayment priorities, and collateral conditions. Insufficient cash flow, impaired net worth, frozen financing, and legal repayment requirements are also different states. The single word 'overload' cannot replace all accounting and contractual relationships.

A loan creates an asset and a corresponding liability, not an equal increase in net wealth. The bank records a loan asset and a deposit liability; the borrower correspondingly has an available deposit and a borrowing obligation. Changes in net worth cannot be assessed from the asset side alone. Writing off a loan asset also does not automatically cancel another entity's deposit unless a separate, explicit transaction or legal arrangement does so. Maintain assets, liabilities, and equity relationships entity by entity, rather than skipping accounts with slogans about money being created or disappearing.

Maturity transformation can support investment and liquidity arrangements, but may also put withdrawals of short-term funding out of step with recovery of long-term assets. A run may involve coordination risk or reflect deteriorating fundamentals; clustered withdrawals alone cannot identify a unique explanation. Keynesian demand and uncertainty, monetary expectations theories, Minsky's financing structures, debt deflation, financial accelerators, and behavioral narratives offer conditional mechanisms. Together they do not establish that every economy must pass through the same crisis cycle.

The source's collateral example requires specifying how the shortfall is made up. If value falls from 100 to 80, loan principal is 60, and the maximum loan-to-value ratio is 70%, the permitted loan balance is 56 and the excess is 4. Restoring the ratio by repaying principal in cash requires repaying 4. If instead only collateral of the same type and under the same haircut conditions is added without repaying principal, the required value is not 4 but 60/0.7−80=40/7. A demand to make up a shortfall is not a realized loss. Whether it is actually triggered and how it is satisfied also depend on the contract and enforcement.

A fire sale is another link. In an independent scenario with no prior repayment, selling collateral for 45 toward a loan of 60 leaves 15 outstanding. This does not automatically equal the creditor's final loss of 15: recourse, other recoveries, costs, and priority still matter. Repaying 4 before selling produces a different balance and later shortfall; different paths cannot be mixed in one account. Price feedback and credit contraction also require observations of additional behavior; a single price decline does not directly establish a complete crisis chain.

Rescue commitments, actual disbursements, risk assumed in advance, and final net costs must be accounted for separately. A commitment may create contingent risk without being money already spent. Actual disbursement also differs from final cost because recoveries, expenses, and unresolved losses may remain. A temporary liquidity bridge may help meet payments due, but does not establish repaired capital, solvency, or a long-term business model. Identify the particular link it addresses.

The aggregate household debt-service ratio does not represent the high-burden tail, nor is it the simple average of each household's ratio. Aggregate payments divided by aggregate income give households with different incomes different implicit weights. Even with the same ratio, essential living expenses, cash buffers, and risk distributions may differ. Measuring vulnerability requires retaining positions and distributions; a stable average cannot erase pressure on particular households.

Contractually required payments, actual payments, changes in balances, and cash pressure are four different objects. An amount due may not yet have been paid; payments may contain different components such as principal, interest, and insurance; balances may also reflect new borrowing, write-offs, or other adjustments. A change in one balance cannot reconstruct every cash flow, and statistical 'scheduled' or 'required payments' must not automatically be translated as amounts actually paid.

The same quarter may have different values under different methods or release payloads. Joining one period under the old method to the next under the new method may create a change absent from a series using a single version. First reconstruct the series under a common method or explain the grounds for bridging, then interpret household burdens and policy contributions. A methodological revision may improve measurement, but is not itself evidence of a sudden change in households' payment behavior.

Different papers on the same rescue program, reanalyses of the same data, and different release versions must retain their connections. They may improve understanding of outcomes or methods, but cannot accumulate independent evidence by article count. The eleven entry points, in order, are money, credit, and debt; banks, maturity, and runs; Keynesian demand and uncertainty; monetarism and rational expectations; Minsky and leverage; bubbles, narratives, and behavior; sovereign and international monetary power; rescue distribution; financial accelerators, collateral, and balance sheets; household DSR; and cash flow, maturity mismatch, and backstops. The strongest objection is that retaining so many accounts obstructs judgment. The response is that only by locating the actual gap can one know what corrections liquidity, capital, and measurement respectively need.

distinctions.leftTitle: Requirement to make up a shortfall
distinctions.leftText: Collateral terms require adjusting the balance or security.
distinctions.rightText: Requires actual transactions, recoveries, and accounting recognition; a difference from a limit cannot directly substitute for it.

distinctions.leftTitle: A loan creates assets and liabilities
distinctions.leftText: Both parties record corresponding entries.
distinctions.rightText: Requires examining net amounts and later changes in real resources; the asset side alone is insufficient.

distinctions.leftText: Helps bridge temporary payment timing.
distinctions.rightTitle: Repair of capital and the business model
distinctions.rightText: Net worth and long-term earning capacity require separate grounds.

distinctions.leftText: Payments required by contract or estimated in statistics.
distinctions.rightText: Cash movements and changes in principal are different records.

distinctions.leftText: Valuations or concepts for the same period are updated.
distinctions.rightText: Requires comparisons over time using the same definitions and corresponding materials, not splicing different versions.

boundaries: This lesson teaches financial relationships and statistical definitions; it does not advise on lending, investment, or rescue decisions.
The statement that 4 must be paid explicitly means cash repayment of principal; the 40/7 required as additional collateral of the same type is calculated separately.
A fire-sale shortfall need not be the final loss; recoveries, costs, priority, and recourse must be considered. Accounts from different paths must not be mixed.
Aggregate DSR is not each household's actual pressure, still less the simple average of household ratios.
All accounts and numerical constructions are hypothetical transactions; no financial products were traded and no personal risk assessment was conducted.

Why is the remaining 15 after a fire sale not necessarily the final loss?
Why does a loan not directly create an equal amount of net wealth?
How should a methodological change connect to explanation of actual mechanisms?

caseLinks.title: An actual publication change: the Federal Reserve's new DSR method in 2024

caseNotes.title: An actual publication change: the Federal Reserve's new DSR method in 2024
caseNotes.text: The Federal Reserve's old release page explicitly states that publication switched to a credit-bureau-data method beginning with the 2024:Q2 release, and that the old DSR series was archived and is no longer updated. Ringo's methodology note, published on 2024-09-04, states that the new method directly uses reported scheduled-payment information and that some mortgage payments include escrowed taxes, fees, and insurance, a different concept from the old method's estimates of principal and interest alone. This is an actual case requiring version and definition checks; it does not mean that a page change caused a sudden change in households' real burdens.
caseNotes.sourceLabel: Federal Reserve archived old DSR release and Daniel Ringo's 2024 FEDS Notes
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Old release page, 'Changes to DSR publication' paragraph (lines 6–7); Ringo's 2024 methodology article, first Estimating paragraph and first four Comparison to the Old DSR paragraphs (lines 16, 24–27)
caseNotes.boundary: This lesson cites no values from the two figures or historical tables and does not re-estimate credit-bureau microdata. The new-method fields are scheduled/required payments, not amounts actually paid. The methodology article identifies its views as staff analysis, not personal financial advice.

argumentSteps: Fix entities, currencies, maturities, priority, collateral, and valuation, and list assets, liabilities, and cash flows separately.
Distinguish liquidity, net worth, financing channels, and legal requirements; a sentence about lending or write-offs cannot skip the corresponding accounts.
After collateral revaluation, calculate limits under the contract and distinguish principal repayment from additional security; account for sales and final losses separately.
Register rescue commitments, disbursements, risks, and costs separately, as well as household averages and tails, and payments due, actual payments, balances, and pressure.
Restore a common method or a defensible bridge; retain dependencies among releases and data. Do not claim an actual discontinuity from a version change.

teachingExamples.title: Developing the source's mathematical example: separate paths for making up a shortfall and a fire sale
teachingExamples.text: With a loan of 60, collateral falling from 100 to 80, and a 70% limit, the permitted balance is 56 and principal repayment requires 4. If only collateral of the same type is added, total required collateral is 600/7, so the addition is 40/7, approximately 5.714. In a separate scenario with no prior principal repayment, a fire-sale price of 45 goes toward a debt of 60, leaving 15. Repaying 4 before selling for 45 leaves 11. These are different paths, and neither shortfall necessarily equals the final credit loss.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Interest and costs are ignored; currency, priority, and collateral haircut are unchanged. Cash repayment and new collateral are two ways of restoring the ratio.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual contractual triggers and recoveries require professional verification; teaching numbers do not provide advice on an actual demand for additional payment or collateral.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: writing off an asset does not automatically erase a deposit
teachingExamples.text: In a closed accounting example, suppose a bank initially has assets of 100, deposit liabilities of 80, and equity of 20. Making a new loan of 60 and recording a deposit of 60 produces assets of 160, liabilities of 140, and equity of 20. A separate loan write-off of 10, with no other transactions, then leaves assets of 150, liabilities of 140, and equity of 10. Deposit liabilities do not automatically fall because an asset is written off.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Simplified bank accounts with no reserve constraints, interbank settlement, interest, taxes, fees, or other business; only accounting relationships are checked.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not claim that banks can lend without limit or that this mechanism explains the entire monetary system.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: an aggregate 20% conceals different tails
teachingExamples.text: Two households each have income of 100. Under arrangement A, payments due are (0,40), giving an aggregate ratio of 40/200=20% and a highest household ratio of 40%. Under arrangement B, payments are (20,20), still giving an aggregate 20% but a highest household ratio of 20%. Equal aggregates do not establish equal distributions; essential expenses and buffers also need checking.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Equal incomes for the two households are assumed solely for easy calculation; these are not actual DSR data.
teachingExamples.boundary: With unequal incomes, the aggregate ratio differs from the simple average of household ratios. This example also sets no personal risk threshold.

teachingExamples.title: Mathematical teaching construction: mixing versions reverses the apparent change
teachingExamples.text: Suppose the old method gives (10,9) for t0 and t1, while the new method gives (12,11) for the same periods, on a percentage-point scale. Both series using a single version decline by 1. Incorrectly joining old t0=10 to new t1=11, however, would produce a reported increase of 1. A version switch is not a real change over time that can be interpreted directly.
teachingExamples.assumptions: All four values are constructed, not actual historical Federal Reserve data.
teachingExamples.boundary: Differences between methods need not be constant. Actual bridging requires an argument; one cannot simply apply an add-2 correction.

counterexamples.text: The collateral limit is short by 4, so the creditor has already certainly lost 4.
counterexamples.effect: This is a requirement to make up the corresponding balance shortfall. Loss requires separate examination of actual transactions and recoveries; the amount of additional security differs as well.

counterexamples.text: A bank writes off a loan, so another person's deposit must automatically disappear.
counterexamples.effect: An asset loss may first be reflected in equity; a deposit reduction needs a separate corresponding event.

counterexamples.text: The old method gives 10 last period and the new method 11 this period, so the actual debt burden rose by 1.
counterexamples.effect: Comparisons using a single version must be restored. In the teaching example each method shows a decline, demonstrating that mixed versions can manufacture a false direction.

questionAnswers.question: Why does repaying 4 of principal not equal adding 4 of collateral?
questionAnswers.answer: Repayment reduces the numerator, while additional collateral increases the denominator; restoring 60/80 to 70% imposes different conditions for each.

questionAnswers.question: Why is the remaining 15 after a fire sale not necessarily the final loss?
questionAnswers.answer: Subsequent recourse, other recoveries, costs, and priority are not yet settled. A residual receivable differs from a final loss.

questionAnswers.question: How should a methodological change connect to explanation of actual mechanisms?
questionAnswers.answer: First construct a series using common definitions or a justified bridge, then explain actual changes with other materials. Do not reverse that order.

D.19.title: D.19 Political Thought, Institutional Visions, and Normative Disagreement
D.19.lead: An institution can remain stable for a long time and still face reasoned normative criticism. A vision may reveal new possibilities without becoming a historical inevitability. Comparisons of political thought must make specific rights, decision-making authority, and transition costs public, without allowing the framework to make political choices for people.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5274–5289; source anchor section-d-19; short quotation, translated: 'Stability, efficiency, and being worth maintaining can truly come apart; normative criticism need not be converted into a prediction of inevitable failure.' The source passage for this topic is also preserved verbatim in source-slice.md; the explanation is separate from the source.

Liberalism, republicanism, democratic thought, conservatism, socialist traditions, anarchism, nationalism, and decolonial critique raise different questions about freedom, equality, order, community, property, and authority. Each label contains internal disputes; one simplified position cannot stand for the whole. Specify which author, period, claim, and mechanism are being compared, rather than having the framework rank entire traditions in advance.

Rules of rights, contestable and removable power, the effectiveness of participation, costs of change and the status quo, control of productive resources, local cooperation, and institutions across regions require separate descriptions. A tradition's focus on one question does not mean that other traditions never address it. A commensurate comparison should not reserve complexity for a favored tradition while reducing opponents to their weakest slogans.

Nominal ownership, shared identity, and local autonomy do not directly establish actual control or distribution. Collective ownership in name may coexist with centralized decisions, while local arrangements may contain irreplaceable control bottlenecks. Trace who can nominate, set agendas, obtain information, vote, implement, remove officeholders, and review. An ownership label or a slogan about community cannot automatically supply everyone's decision-making rights.

One irreplaceable bottleneck can establish significant control; the same party need not monopolize every link. People may freely discuss and vote, for example, while their choices still cannot become reality if one person controls the sole implementation gateway without review. Actual control concerns specific channels. Distributed power cannot be established merely by counting meeting participants or dividing an organization into many small groups.

Visions help propose institutional possibilities not yet realized, and dystopias can reveal risks of control; neither automatically predicts history's endpoint. Conditional inference must state what would happen if particular conditions hold, while observed results need corresponding materials. An illuminating narrative does not make the future known, and an extreme construction used in criticism cannot directly be equated with an empirical verdict on an actual institution.

Specific institutional comparisons must fix objects, periods, and populations, identifying who has which rights, who decides, and who bears transition costs. Maintaining the status quo can also have costs, and reform may bring risks; only one side cannot be examined. For people unable to move or exit, actual positions and consequences particularly need to remain visible. Overall efficiency cannot replace affected people's specific gains, losses, and rights.

The framework's own authorized, applied, and governance states express only its internal commitments; they cannot stand in for external legal effect. Internal permission for a module does not mean that a public action has legal authorization. Nor can the framework force every public decision into a system requiring each individual's unanimous consent. External institutions have their own subject matters, representation, and accountability mechanisms and must be evaluated under their specific rules.

Conversely, an external legal basis does not automatically establish normative justification. Legal effect and being worthy of support are different questions. Comparing political thought can make value conflicts public, but cannot eliminate real disagreements in the name of evidence or procedure. Stability and efficiency also do not provide all the grounds of justification: independent reasons concerning rights or equality remain available even when a criticized arrangement does not quickly fail.

Lawful institutional representation does not require inventing a story that every represented person privately consented. It must still address the matters represented, scope, formation procedure, and accountability. Formal election does not make every action unrestricted or establish that opponents are privately convinced. Do not require impossible individual unanimity at one extreme while expanding representative eligibility into unexamined, unlimited power at the other.

The eight entry points, in order, are liberal lineages including Locke, Mill, Berlin, and Rawls; republicanism and democracy; conservatism including Burke; socialism, Marxism, and social democracy; anarchism, mutual aid, and local autonomy; nationalism, national identity, and fascism; postcolonial and decolonial thought and dependency; and utopia, dystopia, and the end of history. Listing them together does not make them normatively equivalent, much less erase specific oppression or exclusion. The strongest objection worries that refusing an overall ranking amounts to relativism. The response is that explicit reasons concerning rights and protection and specific comparisons remain possible; a general framework simply does not replace all political judgment.

caseLinks.title: An actual historical institutional text: the powers and voting thresholds of representative bodies

caseNotes.title: An actual historical institutional text: the powers and voting thresholds of representative bodies
caseNotes.text: In the U.S. National Archives transcription of the original 1787 Constitution, Article I, Section 1 vests the legislative powers granted in a bicameral Congress; Section 5 provides for each chamber's quorum and rules of proceedings; and Section 7 separately specifies presidential objections and the thresholds for reconsideration by both chambers. These provisions allow representation, quorums, and reconsideration to be examined item by item. They cannot be rewritten as every citizen's private unanimous consent to every decision.

caseNotes.sourceLocator: The page's Note on its status as a transcription of the original; Article I §§1, 5, and 7 (lines 50, 58, 87–91, and 98–102)
caseNotes.boundary: Only the arrangements recorded in the transcription of the original are checked here, without attempting a complete contemporary interpretation of constitutional law. The original includes provisions subsequently amended, as indicated by links on the page. The existence of procedures does not prove the absence of historical exclusion, full realization in practice, or the legitimacy of the system as a whole.

argumentSteps: Compare specific authors, periods, claims, and mechanisms, retaining internal disputes and proportionate comparisons.
List rights, agenda setting, information, voting, implementation, removal, and review separately, distinguishing nominal ownership from actual control.
Fix the object, period, and population; set out both current and transition costs, including those who can exit and those who cannot.
Distinguish inspiration from a vision, conditional inference, and observed outcomes, without predicting an inevitable historical endpoint.
Separate internal authorized/applied status, external legal effect, and normative justification. Hold institutional representatives accountable within their scope without inventing private unanimity.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: control of implementation alone can create a gate
teachingExamples.text: Members of an imaginary association can propose motions, discuss freely, and vote, but only one person can submit the sole executable instruction, and there is no review or alternative if that person refuses. Even with other stages distributed, this irreplaceable implementation gate can block a decision. Assessing the distribution of power requires checking the whole chain; control need not monopolize every stage to count as control.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The association and its powers are entirely fictional and do not allude to any real political organization.
teachingExamples.boundary: The specific degree of control still requires evidence about alternative paths and constraints. No instructions for seizing or circumventing authority are provided.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: stability does not erase normative criticism
teachingExamples.text: Suppose an arrangement persists for a long time at relatively low cost, yet excludes some people from basic positions of participation, violating the principle of equality explicitly defended in this example. One can acknowledge the existing evidence of stability and efficiency while advancing normative criticism, without adding a claim that the arrangement must soon collapse.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Stability, efficiency, and the normative conditions are all stipulated solely to show their logical separability.
teachingExamples.boundary: This identifies no real group and predicts no political change. The normative principle itself still requires public argument.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: internal approval does not equal external authorization
teachingExamples.text: Suppose a research team records an analytical module as authorized and satisfies the internal conditions for applied, then plans to use it to alter another institution's resource allocation. Internal status cannot confer external decision-making power; the actual institution's authority, affected people, and applicable norms must also be checked.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A fictional adoption scenario; no actual allocation has been carried out.
teachingExamples.boundary: External permission does not automatically settle the discussion of legitimacy either.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a representative's scope can coexist with dissent
teachingExamples.text: Suppose an organization elects a representative for its affairs through a valid procedure, while some members vote against the candidate. There is no need to invent private agreement on the part of those members: the representative can perform duties within a defined scope. However, issue-specific authority, removability, and accountability still require explanation; election cannot become unlimited authorization over every aspect of life.
teachingExamples.assumptions: A valid procedure and clearly defined scope are teaching assumptions; no real election is involved.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not judge the legality of any particular system or require opponents to abandon criticism.

counterexamples.text: An arrangement faces normative criticism, so it must collapse in the short term.
counterexamples.effect: Normative judgment and empirical prediction bear separate argumentative burdens; stability does not cancel criticism.

counterexamples.text: Only one stage is controlled and all the others are open, so no important control exists.
counterexamples.effect: An irreplaceable gate can block the whole chain. Check alternatives and review, rather than merely counting open stages.

counterexamples.text: Internal applied status holds, so every public action already has legal permission.
counterexamples.effect: Internal commitments and external legal powers differ; authorization cannot simply cross domains.

D.20.title: D.20 State Capacity, Policy Implementation, and Governance
D.20.lead: Before asking whether governance has capacity, ask for which task, at which stage, for which population, and within what period. Success inside a procedure cannot substitute for coverage of the entire eligible population.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5290–5305, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-20#section-d-20. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘State capacity should be specified in terms of concrete tasks, levels, and organizational resources.’ State formation, fiscal and military mobilization, administrative autonomy, embeddedness, legitimacy, identification, and public services are distinct processes. Strong implementation in one area does not prove strength elsewhere. Nor can observed compliance be attributed solely to identification: dependence, penalties, or routine practices may also be explanations requiring investigation. [T-main]

The policy chain distinguishes at least problem entry onto the agenda, rulemaking, eligibility definition, budget delivery, frontline implementation, notification and application, determination and payment, actual use, and appeal and correction. Completion of one stage may condition the next, but does not substitute for its actual realization; for example, funds reaching an institution do not mean an applicant can use a service. [T-main]

Denominators must be explicit at every stage. Eligible people, notified people, applicants, approved applicants, recipients, and those with sustained usable access each have their own sets and time periods. The approval rate can truly increase while overall receipt coverage remains low. If eligibility is counted by household and receipt by individual, mapping and duplication must be explained; the two counts cannot simply be divided. [T-main]

Frontline discretion can compensate for poorly fitting rules or create exclusion. Examine conflicting tasks, resources, actual choices, and oversight rather than prejudging every workaround as dereliction or innovation. Polycentric governance also means more than opening additional institutions: each must possess real powers, resources, and coordination. If appointments, funding, sampling, implementation, and review all pass through the same controlling gate, the number of institutions does not prove independence. [T-main]

The usefulness of local knowledge does not mean locally powerful people represent tenants, minorities, nonparticipants, and future users. Connections to higher authorities can provide resources and remedies, but can also control objectives and individual cases. Autonomy must specify relative to whom and in which matter: freedom from party control, discretion within administrative rules, and local or user powers to change rules do not lie on the same axis. [T-main]

The random-inspection example in the source is a teaching scenario. More complete records can constitute a local improvement in oversight without proving faster remedies for ordinary applicants. Temporary assistance can also genuinely improve living conditions while long-term fiscal continuity and freedom of choice remain unresolved. Institutional externalities should identify which decision-making calculation omits which costs. An evidenced harm can be described before a final determination of legal liability. [T-main]

Real-world reference: Recommendation 13.1 of Australia's Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme report of July 7, 2023 calls for consultation with frontline staff in designing and implementing new programs; Recommendation 13.2 calls for management to review and respond to their feedback. The additional observation here is that ‘receiving frontline input’ differs from ‘management responding’ within the policy implementation chain. This does not reuse the case as one about legal authorization. Only the recommendation text is checked here; it does not claim that the recommendations were implemented or that applicants received remedies. [P-ROBO]

§§7.3.7–7.3.8 provide interfaces for feedback and the conditional potential field; Parts X–XI trace layers, channels, and events; Part XIV examines normative choice and authorization; and §15.3.5 connects to the institutional module. These connections do not reduce state capacity to a single HV score: specific tasks still require domain evidence. [T-main]

Research navigation: 20.01, state formation and the fiscal-military state (Tilly and others), asks how resource mobilization forms; 20.02, legitimate domination and identification (Weber and others), distinguishes grounds of compliance; 20.03, state capacity, autonomy, and embeddedness (Mann, Evans, Fukuyama, and others), requires specified tasks and relationships; 20.04, street-level bureaucracy (Lipsky), concerns frontline discretion; and 20.05, polycentricity and the commons (Ostrom), concerns real powers and coordination. This lesson explains the book's entry points without claiming to have read these scholars' complete works. [T-main]

20.06, public policy implementation and feedback, connects to the entire policy chain; 20.07, central–local relations, examines scale, resources, and control; 20.08, corruption, capture, and principal–agent relations, asks who appoints, pays, samples, and reviews; 20.09, comparisons of democratic, authoritarian, bureaucratic, and technocratic governance, must hold tasks and populations constant rather than produce overall rankings; and 20.10, governance failure, fragility, and reconstruction, separates functional interruption from subsequent continuation. One failure cannot establish that all state capacities have fallen to zero. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Fix the task, level, target population, and period.
List the state of each policy-chain stage and its actual evidence; do not use upstream success to fill downstream gaps.
Specify denominators, household-to-person mappings, and duration.
Examine frontline discretion and the structure of oversight and control; distinguish nominal polycentricity from actual powers.
Retain local improvements and omitted harms; check effects, legality, and normative choice separately.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: do not mix four different ratios
teachingExamples.text: In an artificial eligible population of 100 people, 40 apply, 30 are approved, and 24 actually receive benefits. The approval rate is 30/40 = 75%; receipt among approved applicants is 24/30 = 80%; receipt among all applicants is 24/40 = 60%; and receipt coverage of the eligible population is 24/100 = 24%. All four fractions are correct, but they answer different questions. Without records for subsequent months, this cannot be called sustained 24% coverage.

D.21.title: D.21 Law, Authorization, Procedure, and Responsibility
D.21.lead: Verify legal texts, application to individual cases, powers, and actual remedies separately. Even a reliable total may be insufficient to support a decision concerning a legally critical time window.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5306–5321, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-21#section-d-21. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Correct arithmetic cannot compensate for a gap in legally critical timing information.’ This section first separates the validity of a legal source, applicability to a case, moral reasons, actual powers, remedial procedures, and realization in lived conditions. Whether a valid rule applies to this person and matter depends on conditions; legal existence does not end normative evaluation, and implementation does not prove its own legality. [T-main]

Natural law, legal positivism, legal realism, and other traditions serve here as research entry points, not as positions compressed into a single answer. Institutional texts supply evidence about rules, but cannot alone prove compliance in practice. Observed unauthorized conduct must still be recorded as fact: its invalidity does not erase the effects it has already produced. [T-main]

Consent, authorization, agency, representation, and standing respectively concern the person's willingness, the source of power, the scope of acting for another, the representative relationship, and procedural status. Some public procedures are not based on private delegation by each individual; that does not mean everyone consents. Nor can personal consent supply public powers that an institution lacks. Record a model's recommendation, actual implementation, and subsequent confirmation separately. [T-main]

Composite procedures can lawfully connect powers; separate verification does not mean procedures can never connect. What matters is that the source, scope, and conditions of authority hold at every node. Chaining several invalid fragments cannot create valid authorization, and authority at one node does not automatically cover later dispositions. [T-main]

Hearing views, respecting procedure, changing evidence, changing a decision, paying compensation, and changing rules may occur at different times. A decision remaining unchanged cannot by itself establish that views went unheard; being heard does not prove that the decision is correct. Relief in an individual case does not establish that every institutional problem has been resolved. [T-main]

Punishment, prevention, compensation, truth, nonviolent coexistence, and forgiveness have different objects and aims; one cannot offset another. T0 prohibits forced reconciliation without rejecting all lawful evidence gathering. Explaining how organizational conditions caused harm does not automatically exempt individuals from responsibility; identifying an individual's error does not erase the roles of upstream design, resources, and management. [T-main]

The source's annual-income teaching example separates the reliability of data from the sufficiency of its transformation. A reliable annual total can still correspond to many short-term income paths. If benefit rules hinge on a short-term window, directly averaging the total introduces an additional assumption. Who must supply further evidence, how absence is handled, and whether enforcement is suspended must follow the specific rules, rather than authorization invented by the model. [T-main]

Historical reference: paragraph [2] of the Federal Court of Australia's June 11, 2021 Prygodicz judgment describes averaging ATO income into fortnights and comparing it with reported income; [5] explains that income may be intermittent and variable. Item 1 of Annexure C explicitly lists the joint conditions under which decisions were invalid, including sole reliance on ATO data without evidence of constant fortnightly income or other supporting evidence. This is not a generalization that ‘all averaging is unlawful.’ [P-FCA]

Paragraph [65] records admissions in the Commonwealth's defence of July 17, 2020; their status must be distinguished from the court's declarations in the annexure. This case is used only to show that reliable aggregate data do not automatically supply missing temporal evidence in an individual case. The judgment is not taken to establish that no party had any real debt, nor that all refunds, freely accepted receipt, or institutional repairs were complete. [P-FCA]

When the error lies in a temporal transformation, correct the inference and derived decisions; reliable source records need not necessarily be deleted. Explanation, correction of source data, notification, changing a decision, compensation, and the person's freely accepted receipt are different endpoints and must be tracked separately. The additional distinction concerns the layer containing the error and whether the correction reaches the actual implementation node. [T-main]

Connect to §§5.5.5 and 5.5.7 for facts and norms, inference and responsibility; §11.3 for knowledge formation; §13.5 for action relationships; Part XIV for responsibility and protection; and §15.2 for closed-loop endpoints. These connections require evidence questions at each layer; a conceptual checklist is not a judicial decision. [T-main]

The eight entry points are: 21.01, the relationship between legal sources and normative evaluation; 21.02, whether the separation of powers and checks actually take effect; 21.03, the distinct statuses of rights, authorization, consent, and representation; 21.04, real entry points to evidence, procedure, and appeal; 21.05, the different aims of punishment, prevention, repair, and transition; 21.06, parallel inquiry into individual and organizational responsibility; 21.07, the application and conflict of multiple rule systems; and 21.08, whether digital decisions can be explained, corrected, and effectively appealed. This explains the navigation without claiming a complete reading of original works across all eight fields. [T-main]

For constitutive questions, first return to §2.4.3: whether a right, office, or decision has the relevant status requires checking applicable rules, valid sources, the acting subject, form, and application to the case. Realization, behavioral responses, and causal effects after that status is established require separate evidence. Legal validity, actual institutional existence, and normative legitimacy remain distinct. Failure to identify an effect cannot directly cancel a valid status, and an existing effect cannot manufacture lawful authorization.
argumentSteps: Identify the rule version, object, time window, and nodes of authority.
Separate original facts, transformation assumptions, and conclusions about the case, preserving reliable components.
Check the respective grounds for personal consent and public authority.
Record hearing, evidence correction, decision changes, compensation, and receipt separately.
Trace upstream conditions and individual actions without letting either exempt the other.

D.22.title: D.22 Class, Identity, Inequality, and Social Exclusion
D.22.lead: Income, wealth, control, and recognition are not the same resource. Group statistics can be true without directly diagnosing a member's circumstances or explaining the causes of differences.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5322–5337, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-22#section-d-22. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘A person's circumstances cannot be diagnosed directly from an identity category.’ Income is a flow over a period, wealth is a stock, and cash buffers affect short-term responses. Control over production and management, eligibility, relationships, and recognition are other resources again. They may correlate or separate; a single label cannot fill in all of a person's opportunities. [T-main]

Class and stratification, stigma and boundaries, intersectionality, elite reproduction, colonial labor, and poverty and mobility provide different entry points. Naming alone does not prove that a group has a common will. Yet labels can have real consequences when they actually enter employers' practices, service rules, or interactions. If a researcher's internal classification never reaches those stages, merely being ‘named’ cannot establish that the same effects were activated. [T-main]

Intersectionality is not the number of identities or the overlap of circles in a diagram. It requires examining how multiple sets of rules jointly exclude particular positions. Statistical interaction is a relationship in a model; institutional intersection concerns how rules act together; lived experience concerns people's situations and meanings. These forms of evidence are connected, but one should not substitute for the other two. [T-main]

Educational mobility must distinguish birth cohorts, applications, admission, graduation, and subsequent opportunities. A few successes do not prove all entry points are open; skill differences alone do not prove fair educational opportunities. Conversely, real selection barriers do not cancel the value of skills someone has acquired. Examining elite control requires tracing access, agendas, resources, and removal, not merely attaching labels based on occupation or qualifications. [T-main]

The welfare example in the source is a teaching construction. Regional mean income among those included in the statistics may genuinely rise, while undocumented people remain outside both statistics and applications, requiring narrower coverage claims. Do not erase observed improvement to emphasize omission, or treat absent people as beneficiaries because the mean improved. The costs of obtaining documentation, travel, time, and care are specific constraints, not verdicts on character or ability. [T-main]

Resources become personal opportunities only with conditions of timing, use, control, and execution. A wealthy household does not mean every member can decide on and use its resources; a firm's assets are not necessarily available to employees. Recognition, redistribution, and participation rights respectively ask whether one is respected, what one receives, and whether one can influence rules. None substitutes for the other two. [T-main]

Specific measurement reference: the U.S. Census Bureau's P60-282, released September 10, 2024, reports 2023 median household income of $80,610 in 2023 dollars, up 4% from 2022. The same page distinguishes changes across groups and explains that the measure is pretax money income excluding in-kind transfers. This is not every American's disposable income or wealth, and it does not identify the causes of group differences. [P-CENSUS]

The agency's accompanying article explains that household categories are defined by the person who owns or rents the home. A ‘median for a household category’ therefore does not assert that every member shares the same identity, resources, powers, or experience. The additional observation in this lesson is the gap between the statistical unit and personal opportunity; the statistical report is not evidence that institutions have become fair. [P-CENSUS-GROUP]

Relative and absolute gaps must be recorded separately. Mathematically, the ratio of the lower to the higher group can move closer to 1 while the monetary difference grows. Whether the aim concerns proportions, absolute shortfalls in living conditions, minimum guarantees, or control must be made public. One cannot select a favorable indicator and declare inequality resolved. [T-main]

Connections in the main text: §2.5 concerns the scope of evidence and inference; §5.5.1 examines aggregation; §9.7 retains material and meaning-related conditions; §§10.5–10.8 examine overlap, power, and continuation across circles; and Part XIV addresses allocation and responsibility. This lesson does not turn these connections into a personal identity scoring tool. [T-main]

The eight research entry points are: 22.01, class, stratification, and the distribution of capital—examine distinct resources; 22.02, status, stigma, and boundaries—trace where labels arrive; 22.03, gender, race, ethnicity, and intersectionality—examine exclusion through interacting rules; 22.04, elite and oligarchic reproduction—examine control and removal; 22.05, colonialism, slavery, and racialized labor—retain specific historical channels rather than group essences; 22.06, poverty, deprivation, and scarcity—list real constraints; 22.07, mobility, education, and inheritance—specify denominators at each stage; and 22.08, recognition, redistribution, and common life—do not substitute normative aims for one another. This is the book's research navigation, not a comprehensive empirical review of these fields. [T-main]
argumentSteps: List flows, stocks, control, eligibility, relationships, and recognition as distinct resources; do not use identity to fill gaps in knowledge.
Trace the channels through which labels actually reach rules or interactions.
Separate the evidential tasks for statistical intersections, interacting institutions, and lived experience.
Check grouping, stages, omitted positions, and individuals' control over resources.
Report both relative and absolute indicators and their normative aims, retaining local improvements and coverage gaps.

D.23.title: D.23 Family, Gender, the Body, Dependence, and Care
D.23.lead: Dependence and autonomy can coexist. Trace care support to who actually decides, who performs the work, and whether the burden is shifted to another household.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5338–5353, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-23#section-d-23. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Dependence and autonomy can coexist.’ Marriage, kinship, co-residence, intimacy, property rights, care, and legal duties are distinct relationships. Relatives need not live together, and co-residents need not be intimate; total household resources do not mean every member can freely use them. Remittances across locations can provide material support, but their amount cannot confirm that daily care has been taken over. [T-main]

Patriarchy, social reproduction, feminist traditions, and work–family research offer different entry points. A single gender essence cannot explain all labor and experience. Examine how rules allocate time, bodily labor, resources, and voice while retaining individual experience and relational meaning; structural analysis must not erase subjects' feelings. [T-main]

Care burdens include not only paid hours but also primary care, simultaneous tasks, planning and coordination, being on call, lost sleep, and future opportunities. Their importance does not mean all durations can be added directly: an hour of supervision may overlap with cooking. On-call constraints must be recorded separately, not disguised as additional clock hours. [T-main]

The dependence of occupational returns on continuous attendance and time flexibility must be examined alongside job design, employer constraints, public support, and discrimination. An observed income gap establishes a descriptive difference, but alone cannot establish natural ability, a unique cause, or fairness. References here to Goldin and others identify research directions; they do not claim a complete review of all their research. [T-main]

Intimate conflict, sustained control, and immediate danger cannot share a single response template. Communication or joint therapy cannot be recommended uniformly, and safe exit need not wait until every ideal resource is available. Continuing limited responsibilities should involve arranging other conditions for taking them over; continued exposure to danger cannot be made a cost the victim must bear. [T-main]

A child's expression, the weight of their views, consent to a particular matter, and final decision-making authority must be separated. First provide support for understanding and expression; temporary inability to express oneself independently cannot justify withholding needed help. Providing support does not automatically confer all powers to decide in the person's place. This is conceptual analysis; actual professional or legal matters still require the relevant procedures. [T-main]

The source's teaching example of an assisted arrangement shows that a person needing daily support can still participate in decisions. Autonomy does not mean complete independence from others, and a helper's ability does not create unlimited obligations. Experiences of the body, sexuality, illness, aging, and disability coexist with institutional barriers; medical treatment, improvements in daily life, and administrative eligibility cannot prove one another. [T-main]

Specific historical arrangement: a 2005 Cash and Counseling report describes programs in Arkansas, New Jersey, and Florida in which counseling, fiscal services, and other support assist participants with spending plans and employer roles. The design distinguishes participation in decisions from support for execution; fully independent execution is not made a conceptual prerequisite for participation in decisions. [P-CASH]

The two specified pages of the original support only the account of arrangements and role division. A spending plan alone cannot establish that every participant can decide freely, and the existence of fiscal support does not imply reduced total burdens for families, grandparents, employees, or counselors. The additional question here is whether roles and support can connect, rather than treating the program's name as certification of every outcome. [P-CASH]

Time saved by one household may come from increased work by another household, grandparents, or paid carers. Preserve both the benefit and the destination of the burden; do not count every transfer as a net reduction. Meaningful work can also involve difficulty refusing. That difficulty needs actual evidence and cannot be inferred solely from family status. [T-main]

Kinship, households, residences, and care networks spanning households have different boundaries. Means from two individually valid populations cannot be combined into records for paired spouses: paired units and a common time basis are required. Connections to §§9.7–9.8 retain conditions and experience; §§10.5–10.8 examine overlapping power and support across circles; and §14.3 and §§15.3.1–15.3.2 trace responsibility and the actual conditions of subjects. [T-main]

The eight entry points are: 23.01, boundaries of marriage and kinship institutions; 23.02, gendered divisions of labor and labor reproduction; 23.03, different feminist questions and evidence; 23.04, distinctions among conflict, control, violence, and safe exit; 23.05, support for expression during development and intergenerational power; 23.06, bodily norms and self-determination; 23.07, support and barriers in illness, aging, and disability; and 23.08, work–family time arrangements and mechanisms of returns. This explains the navigation, not a comprehensive review of all eight fields. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Map kinship, households, support networks, and decision-making powers separately.
Record actual care, simultaneous tasks, on-call demands, and opportunity constraints without double counting.
Check who can decide, who can refuse, and the boundaries of support roles.
Distinguish safety risks from ordinary conflict; do not make continued exposure a condition of continuing responsibility.
Trace work across households, assessing local improvement and total burden separately.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: transfer and net reduction
teachingExamples.text: In a fictional example, household A initially provides 10 hours of care. After a change, A provides 6 hours and household B adds 3. With a consistent measure and no overlapping work, the total falls from 10 to 9: a net reduction of 1 hour. A's four-hour saving cannot all count as a net social reduction. If B instead adds 5 hours, the total is 11: A still saves 4 while the total increases by 1.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Two artificial households, no other work, a common time window, and no double counting of simultaneous tasks.
teachingExamples.boundary: The meaning of the work and harms are not counted; total hours alone cannot determine legitimacy.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: simultaneous tasks cannot be counted twice as clock time
teachingExamples.text: Within an artificial eight-hour care window, two hours also involve cooking. Eight hours of care plus two of cooking make 10 task-hours, but their union in clock time remains eight hours. To describe multitasking intensity, report two simultaneous hours; do not write the union as 10 hours as well.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Cooking is entirely contained within the eight-hour window; the intervals are purely artificial.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not mean simultaneous work is not tiring, or cancel effects on on-call demands and sleep.

D.24.title: D.24 Population, Generations, the Life Course, and Life Across Places
D.24.lead: Separate population totals, composition, life courses, and personal choices. Even a shared version label within a data family does not guarantee synchronized updates across tables.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5354–5369, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-24#section-d-24. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘An identity is not a policy goal.’ Population stocks change through births, deaths, immigration, and emigration. The accounting relationship only shows how quantities connect; it does not decide what population size should be sought, much less authorize assigning reproductive duties over individual bodies. The conditions for having children, not having children, and raising children safely each pose normative questions. [T-main]

Crude rates are affected by population structure. Age-specific rates, period total measures, and actual cohort outcomes are distinct objects. Zero net migration can conceal large inflows and outflows. Nor can an age structure be converted directly into each household's care hours or an institution's fiscal burden; actual support networks and institutional conditions must be added. [T-main]

Age, period, and cohort satisfy age = period − birth cohort. The resulting linear identification problem does not disappear merely by adding observations. Specific stage-related shocks, curvature, or comparisons under additional assumptions can still be studied; an identification limitation must not be rewritten as the impossibility of all life-course research. [T-main]

Early experiences may affect later outcomes through present skills and resources. Controlling for these mediators changes the question being estimated. An insignificant or zero residual historical term does not prove history never mattered. Conversely, the existence of historical effects does not mean the future cannot change. [T-main]

Migration analysis separates legal status, aspirations, practical feasibility, and compulsion; conditions of choice can change during the process. Someone forced to leave may still have choices at the destination or in particular matters, while lacking alternatives at specific stages. One free/forced label cannot fill in every stage. [T-main]

The ILO's explanation of voluntariness requires both free and informed acceptance of work and freedom to leave. A past signature alone therefore cannot prove continuing voluntariness: this is a reasonable limiting inference from the definition. It does not mean that lack of a signed contract or difficult circumstances alone establish forced labor; other elements and conditions of applicability still require checking. [P-ILO]

Members of the same family may separately bear remittance duties, care work, status constraints, and distance constraints. Succession likewise involves distinct transfers of knowledge, office, resources, decision-making powers, and responsibility. Age does not naturally confer authority. A new generation can revise old arrangements; preserving memory does not mean repeating an old way of life. [T-main]

In the source's organizational example, total membership remains unchanged while experienced people leave, newcomers join, and care needs grow. A constant headcount is only one quantitative outcome. It cannot establish complete continuity of knowledge or unchanged burdens; composition, skills, handovers, and support conditions must be recorded. [T-main]

Real versioning case: the UN Population Division's January 19, 2026 interim update to WPP2024 explains that Togo's published census figures had already been adjusted for net undercount, and the Division had applied another adjustment. The correction covers Togo's 1950–2023 estimates and medium-variant population and vital-event counts for 2024–2100. Fertility and mortality rates, other scenarios, other locations, and global and regional aggregates were not changed in tandem. [P-UN]

Recording only WPP2024 therefore does not fix the data's state. Record the specific file, revision identity, download date, country, and scenario. This is a research cross-checking recommendation, not a claim that the UN mandates a universal operating standard. Without recalculating tables cell by cell, do not add unverified global discrepancies. [P-UN]

A population turning point requires distinguishing the first decline, the beginning of a sustained decline, and the year when the sustained-decline criterion is confirmed; natural decrease is separate again. Falling public expenditure does not automatically mean falling need: burdens may shift to households or nonresident supporters. Connect to §§5.5.1 and 5.5.4 for aggregation and identification, §6.12 and §9.2 for history and current conditions, and §10.7 and §15.2.5 for transmission and updating across positions. [T-main]

The eight research entry points are: 24.01, fertility, mortality, and demographic transition; 24.02, age structure and care mechanisms; 24.03, age–period–cohort identification; 24.04, critical periods and cumulative paths; 24.05, migration status, aspirations, and feasibility; 24.06, distinct handovers in inheritance and organizational succession; 24.07, normative boundaries of population policy and reproductive justice; and 24.08, experiences of leaving home, separation, belonging, and life across places. Navigation cannot replace original evidence in each field. [T-main]

Conditions of choice in migration, labor, and life across places can change through the process. A previous contract is evidence about that time. If an arrangement later creates debt, ties housing to it, or establishes dependence on care, remaining in place becomes weaker evidence of continuing voluntariness. For the matter currently at issue, check refusal, negotiation, exit, and limited responsibility separately. Do not equate local agency with complete consent or remove those unable to exit from the factual record.
argumentSteps: First identify quantities, composition, time windows, and statistical objects.
Separate flow identities from normative policy aims.
Check identification assumptions for period, cohort, and age, and the target of controlling for mediators.
Check migration intentions, feasibility, coercion, and powers at each stage.
Record the scope of revisions across tables and trace actual handovers of burdens and knowledge.

D.25.title: D.25 Education, Knowledge Production, Professions, and Lifelong Learning
D.25.lead: What was learned, which qualification was obtained, and which opportunities were gained are different outcomes. Trace corrections to actual downstream decisions and their time windows.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5370–5387, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-25#section-d-25. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘An examination can measure a kind of knowledge without thereby proving fair opportunity.’ Educational aims, accessible learning, actual skills, test interpretation, qualifications, and subsequent opportunities require separate evidence. A test's measurement value cannot close the question of fairness, and unfair opportunity does not imply that nobody genuinely learned anything. [T-main]

Expert instruction can coexist with jointly formulating questions; participation does not require adopting every student suggestion. A reasonable refusal within a curriculum is a specific teaching arrangement, distinct from whether the framework's own GOV-02 is applied. Curriculum choices cannot mechanically be treated as the framework's write-back status, nor can non-adoption prove students never participated. [T-main]

Using qualifications for individual decisions requires individual grounds and proportionate review; checks of group distributions alone cannot replace them. Teacher and expert judgments also need accounts of consistency and uncertainty. ‘Human’ is not an exemption from scrutiny. Both model and human judgments must be checked at the unit of their actual use. [T-main]

Real historical reference: the OSR report of March 2, 2021 reviews awarding grades in 2020. Pages 36–37 describe historical school-level attainment inputs and aggregate equality analysis. Pages 50–52 record checks at subject, school, and other levels, checks of certain anomalies, and dual coding, while noting limited individual-level human review before release. This cannot be simplified into an absence of checks. [P-OSR]

Pages 57–58 of the same report discuss appeal arrangements and scope. Page 58 explicitly notes that even with rapid appeals, university-place decisions had already been made using the initial grades. This supports the problem of misalignment between correction and downstream time windows; it does not prove that no corrections reached admissions, nobody regained opportunities, or all losses were irreversible. [P-OSR]

Reissuing grades therefore does not alone prove restoration of original opportunities and all losses. If a qualification correction reaches admissions conditions in time, it can constitute a real downstream improvement, without establishing that a final job or degree place has been obtained. The additional distinction is which node the correction reaches, when it arrives, and which conditions it actually changes. [T-main]

Support from teaching, families, and organizations works through time and resources. Sending a notice, activating an account, parental attendance, administrative attendance records, and growth in knowledge are distinct. Increased participation may also increase translation, care, and maintenance work. Trace who bears that work rather than automatically calling administrative activity improved learning. [T-main]

Ordinary learning is not denied merely because a G3 conditional historical residual is absent. Carrier-mediated feedback learning and an additional historical increment are each tested under their own contracts; G3 is not a threshold for all learning. In the source's training example, a person gains new skills but has no local job openings: real learning can coexist with non-employment. [T-main]

Knowledge production should trace actual stages: topic selection, budgets, review, practice, drafting, publication, returns, and production, maintenance, proofreading, translation, and communication. Not every study must be forced into the same workflow. Looking only at submitted papers omits people without resources to produce a draft; reanalysis of the same data does not automatically constitute independent replication. [T-main]

Check professional ability, certification, decision-making powers, and public trust separately. Patients' or practitioners' experience can change the importance of a question and the direction of inquiry, but alone cannot establish population-level causation. Open reading, permission to reuse, contribution, joint topic setting, and recognition of labor are also distinct entry points. Public readability does not mean permission for every reuse. [T-main]

Missing citizen-observation records may indicate poor coverage, not the absence of the local objects concerned. Expression and appeal should not require first learning the framework's terminology. Whether existing skills are recognized differs from whether new training is needed. Displaying credentials, recruitment responses, jobs, wages, and net job creation each have separate outcomes. Cumulative establishments, institutions operating in a given year, formal capacity, and actual headcounts cannot be mixed. Failure to complete a course does not erase partial learning. [T-main]

Connect to §1.8, §6.3, Part XIII, §15.3.3, and §16.16 to examine framework uses, learning conditions, expression of knowledge, analysis and action, and specific educational situations. The eight entry points are: 25.01, educational aims and Dewey and others; 25.02, problem setting in critical pedagogy, including Freire; 25.03, cultural capital, hidden curricula, and qualifications; 25.04, coordination among teachers, students, families, and environments; 25.05, selection stages in universities and knowledge production; 25.06, experts, professionalization, and public knowledge; 25.07, distinct permissions in sharing, citizen science, and openness; and 25.08, lifelong learning, skills, and technological change. This does not claim a complete reading of all the named thinkers' original works. [T-main]
argumentSteps: State educational aims and the units of measured outcomes explicitly.
Separate evidence for notification, participation, attendance, skills, qualifications, and opportunities.
Check individual grounds and proportionate review for individual decisions, not just distributions.
Trace corrections node by node, recording arrival times and actual changes in conditions.
Record those who never reach drafting or observation, and the labor of support, preserving the scope of the account.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: an unchanged distribution, reversed individual outcomes
teachingExamples.text: Two fictional people, A and B, have true scores of 90 and 50, incorrectly recorded as 50 and 90. The group mean is 70 in both cases, and the distribution remains {50, 90}. Yet with a purely illustrative admissions threshold of 80, their qualification status is reversed. Matching distributions cannot alone validate individual records.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Two artificial people taking the same test; 80 is a fictional threshold and other conditions are omitted.
teachingExamples.boundary: This does not represent real students in 2020 or prove every model wrong.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: corrections and windows
teachingExamples.text: In an artificial case, a qualification is corrected on day 3 and admissions are locked on day 5. If received and reviewed on day 4, the correction can change eligibility conditions. If it arrives only on day 6, reopening and remedial procedures require separate examination. Even timely receipt does not remove the need for evidence about available places and the final decision.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Fictional dates; actual admissions are not assumed uniformly impossible to reopen.
teachingExamples.boundary: Timing is not a complete judgment of rights and interests, nor does it imply every late correction is worthless.

D.26.title: D.26 Networks, Media, Language, Narrative, and Identification
D.26.lead: Connection, exposure, understanding, belief, and action are not the same event. Independence of factual sources and the number of social supporters also require separate checks.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5388–5403, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-26#section-d-26. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Duplication of the original factual source does not cancel the social coordination that multiple supporters may produce.’ Networks can bring opportunities, language can make experience understandable, narrative can assist mourning and responsibility, and identification can support cooperation. Retain these positive roles while distinguishing connection, actual help, exposure, reading, belief, expression, and action. Risk analysis should not negate all relational value. [T-main]

Weak ties, bridge positions, structural holes, centrality, and actually mobilizable resources have distinct meanings. A node's central position in a graph does not guarantee willingness, authority, or timely ability to help. A topological bridge may transmit a message without meeting an action threshold, resource requirements, or safety conditions. [T-main]

The source's construction of two internally connected three-person groups joined by one cross-group edge distinguishes a single cue from reinforcement by two neighbors. When action requires two distinct neighbors who have already acted, the bridge endpoint may stop after receiving only one source of support; message arrival is not action. The formula 1−(1−p)^n for independent repeated attempts calculates at least one success; it does not automatically become a model of social reinforcement. [T-main]

Multiple nodes can jointly provide support while repeating the same factual source. Multiple people showing up may matter for social coordination; for factual verification, copies from one source cannot count as independent evidence. Retain both dimensions rather than denying support because sources repeat. [T-main]

Silence may reflect risk, privacy, lack of exposure, or lack of interest; it cannot automatically be classified as agreement or opposition. Unverified content, disproven content, and deliberate deception are distinct statuses: uncertainty cannot directly become guilt. Strong group emotions need not be irrational, and real harm does not authorize collective blame of an identity group. [T-main]

Clear boundaries need not mean closure. Identity fusion or costly behavior does not automatically prove free consent. Examine actual conditions for refusal and exit; the extent of sacrifice is not a universal test of genuine willingness. Nor should strong identification alone negate the person's genuine sense of meaning. [T-main]

Translation distinguishes words and sentences, the whole message, the audience's task, and representative powers. Language proficiency does not guarantee listeners' understanding, institutional access, or reliable content; nor does it authorize a translator to make new commitments for the original speaker. Facts learned later cannot be backfilled as knowledge the narrator possessed on the day. [T-main]

Close reading of narratives can explain experiential meaning but cannot replace technical causal analysis. Clear technical causes do not cancel the tasks of memory and literature either: they answer different questions. The same event can receive both a mechanism-based explanation and an expression of experience, without either declaring the other useless. [T-main]

Platform interventions must retain their specific versions: changing a feed, ranking weights, matching, or feedback to authors are different interventions. A fixed recommendation rule can still generate feedback through human responses without retraining every time. Profile changes, private preferences, real opportunities, and long-term harms each require their own evidence; changes in an internal model cannot directly establish changes in a person's essential preferences. [T-main]

Historical research reference: the authors' institutional abstract for Guess et al.'s 2023 paper reports that consenting users were switched to reverse-chronological feeds during the 2020 U.S. election. Usage and exposure changed, while the political attitudes examined over three months did not change significantly. This supports distinguishing outcome levels and time windows; it cannot be read as showing that algorithms never affect attitudes or that long-term effects are zero. [P-GUESS]

The lesson author checked only the abstract on the authors' institutional site; the Science full text returned 403. Randomization details, effect sizes, and statistical power were not filled in on that basis. The additional check here is the match between the intervention's identity and the outcome variable, without extending one intervention's result to all platform mechanisms. Connections to §§5.5.3 and 5.10, §9.7, Parts X–XI, and §§15.3.4 and 15.3.6 trace semantics, relationships, transmission, and actual feedback. [T-main][P-GUESS]

The twelve entry points are: 26.01, weak ties and structural holes—whether resources can be mobilized; 26.02, diffusion thresholds—arrival and reinforcement; 26.03, social identification—boundaries and classification; 26.04, agendas and frames—what becomes visible; 26.05, silence and rumor—uncertainty, error, and intention; 26.06, narrative, memory, and metaphor—meaning and knowledge at the time; 26.07, recommendations and public opinion—specific interventions and feedback; 26.08, translation and migration—tasks and powers; 26.09, language learning and institutions—access; 26.10, uncertainty, identification, and distinctiveness—needs for belonging; 26.11, emotion, fear, and moral panic—evidence and attribution of responsibility; and 26.12, identity fusion and costly experiences—meaning and voluntariness. Named authors serve research navigation, without claiming a complete review of all their theories. [T-main]

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: bridges and thresholds
teachingExamples.text: The graph consists of triangles ABC and DEF with a single bridge C—D. Initially, all of ABC have acted and none of DEF have. Under synchronous monotone updating with threshold 1, D acts in round 1, then E and F in round 2. With threshold 2, D has only one neighbor who has acted, C, while E and F have none; the process thereafter remains permanently at ABC.
teachingExamples.assumptions: An artificial undirected graph with synchronous deterministic thresholds, no spontaneous seeds, and no external input.
teachingExamples.boundary: This illustrates only the specified construction, not that all real bridges are useless or all complex contagions must stop.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: the probability of independent attempts
teachingExamples.text: In an artificial model, each attempt succeeds with p = 1/2 and three attempts are independent. The probability of at least one success is 1−(1/2)^3 = 7/8. If all three share exactly the same source and always succeed or fail together, the probability of at least one success remains 1/2. Do not use 7/8 without checking independence, much less directly call it social reinforcement by three people.
teachingExamples.assumptions: Two distinct models explicitly specify independence or perfect correlation.
teachingExamples.boundary: These are not measured platform success rates.
