D.27.title: D.27 Aesthetics, Art, Literature, Games, and Everyday Culture
D.27.lead: A work's form and experience can address questions of their own. Ownership, custody, interpretation, and community relationships each have their own continuities and changes.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5404–5419, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-27#section-d-27. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘A work's form, rhythm, category, and viewing experience can answer questions of their own.’ Beauty, liking, artistic status, use, popularity, income, reasons for public funding, and social effects differ. A work need not first prove long-term virtue or group coordination to have aesthetic meaning; nor can liking replace all the reasons for public funding. [T-main]

Research into institutional power also has an independent role: materials, skills, evaluation, and distribution affect who can create and be seen. Formal analysis and analysis of production conditions need not exclude each other. Completing one inquiry does not mean another is automatically complete or no longer needed. [T-main]

Check cooperation, conventions, and control in cultural production stage by stage. Critical recognition does not guarantee sales. An institution's liquidation does not mean the end of works, skills, or artistic schools; conversely, surviving works do not prove the original organization is still operating. Continuity must be judged separately for different objects. [T-main]

Literary voice, focalization, characters' judgments, narrative levels, and actual reader responses require separate evidence. A character's view cannot be attributed directly to the author, and a partial perspective does not automatically become an omniscient verdict. Close reading can support an interpretation of meaning; long-term changes in readers' behavior need additional evidence. [T-main]

Science-fiction thought experiments can reveal conditional branches; they are not empirical samples of social mechanisms in the universe. For example, The Three-Body Problem can serve as an entry point for discussing how a setting constrains choices, but fictional events cannot establish inevitable behavior by real groups. [T-main]

Playing can be worthwhile in itself; seriousness and free play can coexist. Artificial difficulty, competition, roles, and rules need not be reduced to final payoffs alone. Consumption can likewise involve practicality, durability, aesthetic pleasure, shared experience, and expressions of status. Multiple meanings can coexist. [T-main]

The source's two-object example holds only the ‘specified function’ equal, while shape and touch produce different experiences. It shows that a particular functional description does not exhaust experience, not that every functional explanation is invalid. Function determining a rating, function being sufficient for beauty, and an aspect possessing functional beauty are three distinct propositions. [T-main]

Fans' love can coexist with maintenance work, commercial control, and internal dissent. An online archive does not mean the original community is active or safe, and continued personal affection does not guarantee continuing member relationships. The meanings of everyday eating, solitude, and care cannot be exhausted by macro indicators, but neither do they require ignoring actual burdens. [T-main]

Discuss heritage ownership, custody, research, display, interpretation, and the right to keep changing one's life separately. Restitution and authorized loans for exhibition can coexist. Preserving streetscapes and memory does not automatically restore former residents' relationships, and the ability to continue changing one's life cannot simply be frozen into preservation as an exhibit. [T-main]

Real-world reference: on October 11, 2022, a Smithsonian-owned publication reported the transfer of ownership of 29 Benin works to Nigeria, with 20 to be returned and 9 to remain at the museum on loan. A change of ownership can coexist with physical retention at the museum; remaining there does not alone negate restitution status. [P-SI]

The report is not a complete loan agreement or a subsequent shipping record. It cannot be written as saying all 20 arrived that day, nor can transferring ownership of 29 works establish complete restoration of interpretive rights, local living relationships, or colonial harms. The additional observation is that different rights and custodial statuses can have different arrangements. [P-SI]

Connections to §§1.8–1.10, §5.10, §9.7, §10.6, and Appendices A.3/A.11 retain distinctions concerning tasks, meaning, experience, relationships, and the boundaries of aims and feedback. The nine entry points are: 27.01, aesthetic experience and judgment; 27.02, production institutions and industry channels; 27.03, narrative ethics and multiple perspectives; 27.04, the processes of games, rituals, and sport, including Huizinga and Caillois; 27.05, fan subcultures, love, and labor; 27.06, multiple uses of consumption, fashion, and taste; 27.07, conditional thought experiments in science fiction; 27.08, everyday life, festivals, food, and bodily experience; and 27.09, memory, museums, and heritage rights. The list does not claim that all original works have been read in full. [T-main]

Gather separate evidence for a work's form, production conditions, and consequences for readers.
Check narrative perspective; do not attribute a character's judgment directly to the author.
Judge continuity separately for works, organizations, skills, communities, and archives.

D.28.title: D.28 Technology, Infrastructure, Platforms, and Artificial Intelligence
D.28.lead: Technical outcomes arise from specific combinations of physical properties, configuration, institutions, and maintenance. Nominal approval, tool requests, and changes in real-world states cannot be conflated.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5420–5435, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-28#section-d-28. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘It is not “half technology and half society.”’ Bandwidth, materials, and interfaces impose independent constraints; default configurations and commercial arrangements can alter reach. A specific outcome requires describing the combination of physical properties, protocols, deployment, institutions, maintenance, and use, rather than replacing mechanisms with a slogan about proportions. [T-main]

Conformity to a written standard, interoperable implementation, shared business semantics, reliability under stress, and human usability are different layers. A message passing through does not prove both sides understand the same business object; working normally does not prove reliability under stress. Maintenance also needs verifiable spare parts, skills, budgets, powers, and continuing labor; it does not arise naturally once equipment is installed. [T-main]

When multiple devices share an upstream power supply or the same defective software, numbers do not guarantee independent redundancy. A comparison of necessity must specify whether it holds constant a product name, binary, configuration, or a complete deployment including training, powers, and maintenance. After changing configuration or training, one cannot say only an abstract institution changed. Substitutes must preserve the task, resources, deadline, and necessary protections. [T-main]

Platform matching and time flexibility can produce real benefits while pricing, eligibility, future opportunities, and appeals remain centrally controlled. The presence of an algorithm cannot directly determine every aspect of workers' legal status; specific rules require separate checking. Benefits do not cancel questions of power, and centralized control does not erase benefits. [T-main]

Judge attribution of AI-generated content, existence of a bibliographic item, metadata, support in the original text, facts about the world, and permission for the intended use separately. Retrieval helps locate material without guaranteeing truth. Internal consistency can reveal contradictions but can also stably repeat the same error. A limited reanalysis or synthetic recalculation may correct one quantity without proving corresponding improvement for actual users. [T-main]

Recommendation, tool request, program execution, external state change, and consequence form five stages. Oversight requires evidence, capacity, time before action, and a manageable workload; a refusal signal must actually reach the executor. The source's example of a user clicking reject after the backend has become irreversible shows why nominal approval is insufficient, not that every backend action is necessarily irreversible. [T-main]

Historical reference: paragraphs 15–22 of the SEC's October 16, 2013 settled administrative order concerning Knight describe a 2012 deployment in which one of eight servers was not updated, there was no review by a second person, and 97 emails were not designed as alerts. Identical product or code names do not guarantee identical deployed states. Sending information also does not mean people understand it and act in time. [P-SEC]

This account follows the findings recorded in the order and preserves its status as a settlement in which the respondent neither admitted nor denied the findings, with exceptions such as jurisdiction. It is not rewritten as a criminal conclusion. The case supports only the deployment-review and alert-to-action chain; it cannot alone explain all losses or establish that any algorithm is inherently unsafe. [P-SEC]

Privacy requires separate checks of collection, inference, reuse, retention, and downstream deletion. Sending an instruction does not prove completion. Actual possession, permitted use, accounting recognition, transaction eligibility, and cross-border eligibility differ. The Ministry of Finance's 2023 text explicitly includes legally owned or controlled data expected to yield benefits but not recognized as assets; item 7 addresses revenue from their sale. Nonrecognition therefore does not directly mean no value in use. [T-main][P-MOF]

That accounting text is not permission for arbitrary use; item 2 also concerns restrictions on rights. It does not imply that all unrecognized data have value, much less that possession or entry in the accounts permits provision to any destination. This explains the boundaries of a historical text; actual rights, privacy, and professional judgments need their respective grounds. [P-MOF]

Trace tasks, independent skills, occupational opportunities, and meaning separately during technological transitions. Tool proficiency or occupational exposure cannot replace long-term outcomes. Before removing old support, check whether substitutes are usable and what interruption would cause. Protective stopping in immediate danger follows the relevant procedures; an ideal substitute cannot be made a reason to insist that danger continue. [T-main]

Connect to Parts X–XI, §§13.8–13.11, §§15.3.3–15.3.5, and §§16.23–16.24 for relationships, knowledge, feedback, and practice. The eight entry points are: 28.01, specific mechanisms of technological determination and social shaping; 28.02, layers of infrastructure, standards, and maintenance; 28.03, technological politics in Winner and STS; 28.04, platform governance and digital labor; 28.05, AI generation and levels of evidence; 28.06, responsibility chains in agents and automation; 28.07, data privacy and digital rights; and 28.08, technological substitution and loss of capability. Navigation does not mean all related original works have been read. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Identify the product version, binary, configuration, and complete deployment conditions.
Test interoperability, semantics, reliability, and actual usability layer by layer.
Specify log evidence for recommendations, requests, execution, states, and consequences separately.
Test whether a refusal signal can reach the executor before the irreversible point.
Check distinct data permissions and deletion endpoints; assess substitution, interruptions, skills, and opportunities.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: shared power and independent redundancy
teachingExamples.text: In an artificial model, one device's failure probability is 0.1. If two devices are fully independent and either can provide service, total failure has probability 0.1 × 0.1 = 0.01. If both depend only on the same power supply, whose failure probability is 0.1, and everything else always works, total failure remains 0.1. Equal device counts do not guarantee equal reliability.

teachingExamples.boundary: These are not safety probabilities or design certification for a real system.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a button without a veto
teachingExamples.text: An artificial task enters an irreversible external stage at second 2, shows approval only at second 3, and receives rejection at second 4. Even if rejection is logged, it is later than the critical threshold. Only if rejection instead arrives at second 1 and actually blocks execution does this task have a prior veto path.

D.29.title: D.29 Cities, Space, Housing, Rural Areas, and Public Accessibility
D.29.lead: City identifiers, geometrical areas, resident cohorts, and actual accessibility are different objects. Record neighborhood improvement separately from outcomes for original households and those who moved away.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5436–5451, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-29#section-d-29. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘After a map becomes connected, actual accessibility still depends on time periods, capacity, costs, admission, assistance needs, and alternative routes.’ The material conditions of urban formation, historical paths, and present agglomeration benefits differ; current benefits cannot provide a complete account of origins. Location, administrative jurisdiction, membership, functional networks, and service areas cannot share one boundary either. [T-main]

Using a common city list at each time point controls only differences between samples at that time. Only a list fixed across all time points yields a fixed statistical cohort. Even with a fixed cohort of identifiers, geometrical boundaries and residents can change. Fixed historical area and fixed current area can serve different indices; denominators must be disclosed. Fixing one element alone does not establish complete comparability. [T-main]

Specific methodological case: pages 34–35 of the UN's December 2025 WUP methodology report use 2025 city identifiers as the baseline and trace cities through overlaps. Nine centers in 2000 within Shanghai's 2025 boundary receive one ID, while Lagos and four centers connected in the 2050 projection retain separate identifiers. Continuity of identifiers is a tracking arrangement, not a claim of constant geometrical boundaries. [P-WUP]

‘No splitting or merging’ in the report's tracking rule does not mean actual urban spaces never split or merge. The 2050 figure is a projection, not completed history. The method seeks to improve comparison; it cannot instead establish that all analysis across time is invalid. The lesson author did not recalculate the grids and does not present a methodological description as independent data validation. [P-WUP]

Network centrality does not directly prove power or welfare. A facility's service area is a spatial representation with assumptions: continuous routes, service hours, bodily conditions, and independent use must be checked. Observe separately the visibility of a facility, lawful entry, affordable continuous access, safe activity, and the ability to change management rules. [T-main]

Everyday contact, staggered use, and local familiarity can support help-seeking and care, but safety, respect, and the ability to remain still require evidence. Local participation may omit tenants, future residents, and users from other districts; a majority of current residents cannot automatically speak for every affected position. [T-main]

Housing and land rights, building rights, tenancy security, mortgages, eligibility to return after redevelopment, and maintenance costs differ. The two specified pages of Roy 2005 criticize equating informality with poverty and note that lawful property title can coexist with violations of land-use rules. A settlement label is therefore insufficient to determine individual poverty or every legal status. The author's analysis of classificatory power does not authorize any particular disposition either. [T-main][P-ROY]

Statistical purposes can legitimately combine categories, but mappings and deduplication must be retained. Rural areas simultaneously support production, nonfarm work, care, and provision across places; they are not merely an earlier, backward urban stage. Roads may expand peripheral markets or intensify competition from central firms. Outcomes cannot be restricted in advance to positives or negatives. [T-main]

Slower relative growth is not absolute decline. The source's example of a redeveloped neighborhood with a higher mean but a different set of residents likewise requires retaining real changes in the current area without substituting them for living outcomes among original households or people who moved away. This does not reject the area indicator; it limits the object it explains. [T-main]

After a disaster, trace building safety and renewed exposure, household services, relationship networks, memory, feasible choices, and remedies separately. Relocation is not necessarily bad, and rebuilding in place is not necessarily good. A visible combination of partial recovery does not automatically prove a feedback trap; examine the looping mechanism further rather than judging by appearance. [T-main]

Connect to §§5.5.1–5.5.3 for aggregation, boundaries, and representation; Part X for relationships and circles; and §§15.3.7–15.3.8 for actual environmental uptake. The additional identification task is whether the object behind the same label has changed, whether improvement reaches the original people, and whether the path is genuinely usable. [T-main]

The eight entry points are: 29.01, different temporal questions about urban formation and agglomeration; 29.02, Lefebvre and Harvey on the production of space and rights; 29.03, Jacobs on local knowledge and diversity; 29.04, housing, land, rent, and segregation; 29.05, rural land institutions and urban–rural multifunctionality; 29.06, regional centers, peripheries, transport, and competition; 29.07, public space, accessibility, and everyday safety; and 29.08, post-disaster demolition, rebuilding, and memory. This explains research entry points without claiming a complete review of all the authors' original works. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Define separate administrative, geometrical, identifier, resident, and service-area boundaries.
Specify the fixed list, area denominator, and time span.
Measure continuous accessibility, not just connectivity on a map.
Separate rights concerning land, buildings, tenancy, return, and maintenance.
Track the area, original residents, those who left, renewed exposure, and remedies together.

D.30.title: D.30 Ecology, Resources, Commons, and Sustainable Living
D.30.lead: Verify material constraints, conditions of access, rights, and recovery endpoints separately. A combination crossing a threshold does not automatically prove statistically significant interaction or recovery of an entire system.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5452–5469, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-30#section-d-30. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Conservation accounting does not provide a unique allocation of value.’ Natural processes, institutions, knowledge, markets, and life connect through specific interfaces. Social choices can change resource use and the distribution of risk, but definitions cannot cancel hydrological and material constraints. Retain domain distinctions among resource systems, units, users, rules in use, and outcomes. [T-main]

Forest cover, species, access to fuel, and household life are not interchangeable. Food stocks, supplies organizations can mobilize, and households' actual access also differ. Pages 433–435 of Sen 1981 distinguish aggregate food availability from the commodity bundles through which individuals can obtain enough food. Aggregate shortages can affect individual hunger, but aggregate quantities alone do not show what each person can obtain. Entitlement sets also relate to initial endowments, exchange or production opportunities, and institutional transfers such as social security. Footnote 5 on page 434 explicitly states that entitlement is used descriptively here, without directly determining which distribution is just. Supply, access, arrival of relief, and nutritional and disease outcomes therefore require separate evidence. [T-main; P-SEN1981]

The exclusion costs and subtractability of common-pool resources are not a legal status of common ownership. Check rights of access, withdrawal, management, exclusion, and alienation separately. Collective organization and engineering support can complement one another, and local rules are not inherently fair. Examine who can participate and who bears costs; the name ‘commons’ cannot supply specific rights. [T-main]

Energy transitions must distinguish continuous fuel flows, construction and in-use stocks, mineral uses, refining quality, and comparable services. Material conservation constrains possibilities without automatically allocating value or responsibility. GDP, material flows, living conditions, care, and ecological outcomes can move in different directions; do not force them into a single overall health score. [T-main]

Water withdrawal, net consumption, evapotranspiration, return flows, recharge, and water levels differ. Area expansion after improved field efficiency can allow local water savings to coexist with higher total net consumption. Better information does not guarantee overall outcomes unless it enters withdrawal constraints and maintenance. Proximity to pollution sources alone does not identify individual health effects either; corresponding exposure and causal evidence are needed. [T-main]

Distribution, recognition, procedure, and remedy in environmental justice each require evidence. Historical contribution, current capacity, future risk, and adaptation needs in climate issues also differ. State measurement, mechanism, scenario, and normative uncertainties separately; no single dimension directly determines compensation shares. [T-main]

Paragraphs 414–415 of the International Court of Justice's July 23, 2025 advisory opinion explain that Article 8 of the Paris Agreement provides cooperative and facilitative support, not a basis for liability and compensation, but does not constitute an express lex specialis excluding general state responsibility. Paragraphs 433–435 distinguish establishing responsibility from the causal showing needed for reparation for particular damage. Multiple causes do not automatically exempt responsibility, but causation cannot be presumed either. [P-ICJ]

These paragraphs do not set an amount that a country owes a person, and scientific findings do not directly confer authority to act. Reparation retains its broader sense of repair and compensation, not only money. Cooperative support, legal responsibility, and claims for particular damage each require their own legal sources, objects, and conditions. A limitation on one mechanism cannot invalidate every other basis. [T-main][P-ICJ]

Actual ecological research reference: Marshall et al.'s 2013 paper manipulates fencing and simulated beaver dams at four sites, measuring willow height and biomass. After ten years, mean height under the combined treatment was 248 cm, exceeding a 2 m threshold; fencing alone gave 160 cm, dams alone 174 cm, and controls 117 cm. The actual manipulation was not randomized wolf reintroduction. [P-MARSHALL]

In Figure 2 and the results, predictive intervals for the interaction effects on both height and biomass cross zero. The combined treatment crossing a threshold therefore cannot alone be called statistically significant synergy. The discussion also acknowledges that dams may alter both water and nutrients, so the effect is not attributed only to water level. A local willow-height target does not equal comprehensive recovery of species, food, water use, and human lives. [P-MARSHALL]

Conservation can simultaneously concern nonhuman individuals, populations, and ecological processes. Scientific knowledge, local knowledge, and legal agency have different qualifications. Successful protection at one position does not automatically offset losses at another. Connections to §2.8, Part V, §6.9, and Parts XII and XIV examine conditions, feedback, aims, responsibility, and disaggregated consequences. [T-main]

The eight entry points are: 30.01, specific social–ecological interfaces; 30.02, rights and governance of commons and common resources; 30.03, flows and stocks in energy and material metabolism; 30.04, access and net consumption in agriculture, food, and water; 30.05, environmental justice and risk distribution; 30.06, climate adaptation and intergenerational responsibility; 30.07, multiple well-being scales in growth and degrowth; and 30.08, conservation, local societies, and nonhuman values. Navigation does not replace all specialist literature and field measurements. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Specify the resource object, actual manipulation, and outcome units.
Distinguish material stocks and flows, household access, nutrition, and living conditions.
Separate powers of access, withdrawal, management, exclusion, and alienation.
List disaggregated outcomes and thresholds before testing interactions and mechanisms.
Separate cooperative support, responsibility, and compensation, preserving gains and losses at different positions.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: crossing a threshold does not mean interaction
teachingExamples.text: The artificial outcome is y = 1 + 0.6A + 0.6B, with A and B each either 0 or 1. The control is 1, each single treatment 1.6, and the combination 2.2. D.31.title: D.31 Risk, Disasters, Public Health, Command, and Recovery
D.31.lead: Warnings must cover the full response time, and recovery claims must specify functions, coverage, and support conditions. Demobilizing command does not mean all aspects of life have recovered.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5470–5485, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-31#section-d-31. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘A function genuinely restored under temporary support is not a false recovery.’ Separate hazards, exposure, vulnerability, observation, acceptance of risk, and action. Social conditions do not erase floods or pathogens, and technical estimates alone do not decide who bears risk. Prevention requires comparing harms of action, proportionality, support, and review. It neither expands powers without limit nor requires complete certainty before limited protection is allowed. [T-main]

Complex coupling, reliable organizational practices, latent defenses, system constraints, and adaptations in ordinary tasks each have explanatory scopes. Do not combine different theories into a universal cause of accidents. A temporary workaround that preserves checks differs from eliminating them. What matters is that protective functions and critical distinctions remain tested, not merely that forms have identical formats; proportionate alternatives need professional grounds. [T-main]

The evidential value of no accidents depends on exposure and observation. A process genuinely established after an accident can coexist with an unknown net safety effect and an unsupported branch of feedback learning. Do not erase the process because its net effect is unproven, or declare safety complete because the process exists. [T-main]

Critical slowing down requires particular conditions concerning dynamics, noise, sampling, and bifurcation. Ordinary fluctuations are not automatically signs of collapse. Warnings must reach endpoints able to understand, mobilize, and act in time. Early issuance alone is insufficient: verification, delivery, understanding, dispatch, and protection taking effect all consume time. [T-main]

No harm after a warning may mean the measures worked. If labels are complete and the target fixed, no event after a warning can still be scored against that target. How much harm action prevented requires a causal comparison. Do not prohibit all prediction scoring to prevent misunderstanding, or fill missing offline monitoring records with zero events. [T-main]

Infection, testing, diagnosis, reporting, and hospitalization have different denominators. Changes in beliefs, attendance for testing, and health outcomes do not establish one another. Medical classification, experience, disease course, benefits, and treatment each bear evidential responsibilities. Shared decision-making can improve knowledge without automatically guaranteeing long-term health. This section provides no individual diagnosis or treatment instructions. [T-main]

Emergency command transfer, coordination closeout, withdrawal of special powers, and recovery of everyday life have different timelines. A real function can depend on temporary electricity or continued support. Evaluations must state the conditions and population actually covered, not automatically substitute all predisaster users. A later new shock need not prove an earlier limited conclusion entirely wrong. [T-main]

Specific institutional reference: page 35 of Maryland's April 2023 ICS guide for active assailant incidents separately lists transfer of command, a briefing checklist, and agency closeout. The briefing covers remaining resources, logistics, and documentation. Closeout requires handing over long-term impacts, recovery needs, and unfinished matters, so organizational withdrawal and subsequent recovery are different objects. [P-ICS]

The guide specifies arrangements for a particular scenario; it is not evidence that any incident has fully recovered. Its complete field procedures are not repurposed here as general instructions for the public. The additional distinction is who takes over unfinished work at withdrawal, rather than attaching an overall ‘recovered’ label to closeout. [P-ICS]

A recovery judgment can acknowledge both local reality and gaps. Some households regaining electricity through temporary power is an actual functional recovery, without proving normal supply is repaired or every predisaster user is covered. Broad claims exceeding the evidence must be narrowed; verified local recovery need not be withdrawn wholesale. [T-main]

Connections to Part VI, §8.6, §12.6, §15.3.8, and §16.13 examine dynamics, observation targets, conditional closed loops, and professional boundaries. Urgent protection and long-term evaluation each require proportionate tasks. A complete retrospective explanation must not become a permanently unattainable precondition for action. [T-main]

The eleven entry points are: 31.01, Beck and others on risk, prevention, and uncertainty; 31.02, Perrow, Weick, and others on complex coupling and reliable organization; 31.03, Vaughan and others on normalization of deviance and silence; 31.04, disaster exposure, vulnerability, and resilience; 31.05, warnings, critical slowing down, and response times; 31.06, public-health trust and denominators; 31.07, medicalization and determinants of mental health; 31.08, layers of investigation, accountability, and collective learning; 31.09, medical institutions, ethics, and shared decisions; 31.10, NIMS/ICS handovers and functional degradation; and 31.11, rescue, repair, reconstruction, and recovery boundaries. Names provide navigation without claiming a full reading of the related original works. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Specify hazards, exposure, observation, and who bears risk.
Distinguish an established process, evidence of learning, and net safety effects.
Compare each stage of warning time with the deadline.
Preserve event labels and offline missingness; distinguish prediction scoring from prevented harm.
Recovery records must specify functions, support, and coverage, with handover arrangements at withdrawal.

caseNotes.text: GitLab's February 10, 2017 postmortem records that after the primary database's data directory was accidentally deleted on January 31, the team discovered that daily `pg_dump` backups had not been generated because of a version mismatch, and error emails had also been rejected. The database was eventually restored from an LVM snapshot manually made for a test environment about six hours earlier; webhooks were restored separately. GitLab.com became available again after about 18 hours, but approximately six hours of database changes after the snapshot were not recovered. ‘A backup process exists,’ ‘this copy is usable,’ ‘the service is available again,’ and ‘all data were recovered’ must be answered separately to make clear what was restored.

D.32.title: D.32 War, Revolution, Empire, Development, and Historical Paths
D.32.lead: Historical explanation retains distinct subjects, mechanisms, and versions. Signature, ratification, legal status, and consequences for life can have different dates.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 5486–5503, original site location /theory/appendix-d/d-32#section-d-32. See the theory-v2 source for the current complete text; the historical research manuscript and excerpts remain available to download and consult in their original edition.

Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘An accurate documentary answer need not wait for an allocation of overall causal shares.’ Identify the state as a legal subject, government, military, organizations, and populations bearing consequences separately. Realist explanations in terms of resources and security, institutionalist explanations in terms of commitments and monitoring, and constructivist explanations of constitutive status can offer different conditional accounts; they cannot be merged into a single unified state will. [T-main]

Defensive intentions, actual security effects, the other side's judgment, future ability to fulfill commitments, and legitimacy differ. Communication can reduce certain informational uncertainties without automatically resolving future incentives and execution constraints. Declared goodwill does not mean the other side's security truly improves, nor does it alone determine legality. [T-main]

Mobilization must distinguish first participation, repeated participation, sustained organization, concessions, transfer of power, and subsequent life. Support without registration, registration without attendance, withdrawal, and continued participation each have positions in the account. Do not turn earlier outcomes into inevitabilities by looking only at winners' retrospective lists, or count repeated attendances as distinct participants. [T-main]

Analysis of empire and decolonization retains separate channels of trade, conquest, cultural exchange, inequality, and dependence. Formal sovereignty, administrative capacity, economic choice, and citizenship do not establish one another. Leaders' histories cannot replace local actors and internal differences. Real industrial effects also do not substitute for living outcomes among workers, carers, and those unable to migrate. [T-main]

The book uses Khaldun's cooperation and ruling coalitions, Toynbee's conditional responses, Tainter's costs of complexity, and Turchin's feedback hypotheses as navigation in historical dynamics. Their distinct questions are retained without combining them into a universal civilizational cycle or claiming a complete reading of all original works. The maintenance costs of model complexity and the organizational costs of actual societies are not the same quantity. [T-main]

Diminishing marginal returns mean only that additional returns become smaller, not that they are negative, net benefits are negative, or collapse is imminent. Preserve separate versions of the original prediction, later models, authors' retrospective assessments, and independent tests. Performance of a revised model cannot be backfilled into the original prediction, and a retrospective assessment cannot be presented as independent validation. [T-main]

Modernization, industrialization, and global connections do not form a single developmental ladder. Peace distinguishes at least cessation of violence, dispute procedures, political arrangements, responsibility, recovery of everyday life, and reconciliation. Group cooperation does not prove individual psychological recovery. Counterfactuals should alter only evidenced nodes and reestimate downstream effects, rather than present an imagined alternative path as known history. [T-main]

Specific documentary case: the chapter in Volume XIII of the U.S. Department of State's FRUS records that the U.S.–German treaty restoring friendly relations was signed in Berlin on August 25, 1921 and entered into force through exchange of ratifications on November 11. For the United States, the state of war had already been declared ended by the joint resolution of July 2. The German government treated entry into force on November 11 as the turning point, and full diplomatic relations resumed on November 16. [P-FRUS]

A bare question of ‘when it ended’ therefore requires first specifying the legal subject and the event at issue. Signature, entry into force, and restoration of diplomatic relations cannot substitute for one another. Documents can clearly answer these timing questions without first resolving causal shares in every social consequence. Dates cannot establish simultaneous recovery of all residents' lives, trauma, or reconciliation either. [T-main][P-FRUS]

Before comparing historical quantities, check the target and common support, then retain remaining disagreements. Total violent deaths and the violence-related component of excess deaths overlap substantially but are not identical; renaming cannot eliminate substantive differences. Intervals from separate studies cannot be joined into a common confidence interval. Assessing completeness, assumptions for correcting underreporting, and adjustment for missing visits are distinct steps. [T-main]

Signature and ratification, funding commitments, receipt, settlement, and consequences for life likewise require separate evidence. Unsupported endpoints remain unknown; a true upstream stage cannot fill them in. Connections to §§2.4–2.7, §8.1, Parts X–XII, Part XIV, and §16.4 examine causal scope, organizational relationships, aims, and responsibility. [T-main]

The eight entry points are: 32.01, three perspectives in international relations; 32.02, distinct judgments about war, security dilemmas, and deterrence; 32.03, multiple stages of revolution, movements, and mobilization; 32.04, empire, colonialism, decolonization, and state building; 32.05, civilizational rise and fall and different hypotheses of historical dynamics; 32.06, multiple outcomes of modernization, industry, and globalization; 32.07, peace negotiations, reconciliation, and postwar order; and 32.08, contingency, individuals, structure, and bounded counterfactuals. Each retains ordinary people and conditions of execution at the endpoint, rather than replacing specific research with grand propositions. [T-main]
argumentSteps: Specify the subject, event, outcome, and time window at issue.
Separate information about intentions, incentives, capacities, and legitimacy.
Track distinct participants and attendances, power outcomes, and ordinary people's lives.
Separate original predictions, revised models, retrospective assessments, and independent tests.
Before comparing quantities, align targets and common support, then record differences that cannot be removed.

references.title: References
references.lead: Twenty references provide traceable entry points. Bibliographic identity, support in particular passages, independent evidence, and real-world use require separate judgments.
explanation: Source correspondence: the references occupy Chinese source lines 5504–5544, anchor part_21. The current source appears on this page. The bundled source-slice.md preserves an excerpt from the historical manuscript, corresponding to source-slices/REFERENCES.md in the original package. This unit contains 20 items, including a working paper, journal and conference papers, legal interpretation, a judgment, official statistical notes, and accounting provisions. The source explicitly states ‘this text cites pages 326–327’ and calls several items ‘specialist model references.’ These qualifications are themselves essential to understanding the section and must not be removed from its presentation.

Central judgment: a bibliography is an entry point back to specific grounds, not a list of authorities guaranteeing the whole book. Readers should be able to answer four questions: exactly which text; which passage the author used; what kind of claim that passage supports; and what is still missing between it and the present judgment. Knowing a title establishes identity, but does not prove that the text has been read. Reading the text does not guarantee that every empirical claim within it is correct.

The book's theoretical concepts stand in comparative relationships to literature from other disciplines, but these relationships are not all of one kind. Some sources delimit case selection and evaluation; some supply formal normative texts; some record how a statistical version was updated; and some provide mathematical models for comparison. Collapsing them all into ‘scientific evidence supports the book’ erases the different responsibilities of proof, explanation, historical fact, norm, and application. A better reading lets each citation do only the work it actually accomplishes.

Connections to the book: §2.7.1 requires preserving material identity and actual reading scope; §2.7.2 warns against counting materials from one source as independent validation; §16.15 discusses checking materials; and §16.24 rejects substituting workflow outputs for methodological value. The references make these principles operational: formal publication of an author's manuscript does not create two studies; translation or reposting of a PDF does not add an independent observation; and correction of a normative text may change logical conditions, so retaining only the most familiar old link is insufficient.

The following 20 items follow the book's order. Each separately records identity, location in the book, actual reading scope, supported content, and remaining gaps. ‘No sentence-level citation explicitly naming the author was located’ describes only the traceable relationship in the current text; it does not judge whether that research influenced the author. Suggested companion reading likewise does not claim the original author made that citation. Actual reading scopes are those recorded in each source entry.

01 | Mahoney & Goertz: The Possibility Principle: Choosing Negative Cases in Comparative Research
Identity: authors' working paper, 2004-01-19.
Location in the Chinese source: references line 5506; §16.4, line 3550.
Reading recorded in the original lesson research: cover, abstract, and the presented portions of the opening introduction, PDF pages 1–4.
Support limit: admission rules for negative cases must consider the actual possibility of the outcome; not every nonoccurrence belongs in the same comparison population.
Remaining gaps: the full 27-page draft was not read, and subsequent case-selection rules were not checked item by item. The published version does not replace the authors' draft specified by the book.
Source: [R01](https://www.compasss.org/wpseries/MahoneyGoertz2004.pdf).

20 | Moore: Gedanken-Experiments on Sequential Machines
Identity: Automata Studies, 1956:129–153.
Location in the Chinese source: line 5544; §4.19, line 1074.
Reading recorded in the original lesson research: original printed pages 143, 145, and 146, visually read page by page.
Support limit: indistinguishable states form equivalence classes; partitions are recursively refined through longer input experiments, with a direct mathematical connection to the finite model in §4.19.
Remaining gaps: the chapter's full preceding definitions and all theorems were not read. In particular, assumptions such as strong connectivity and distinguishability cannot be omitted and then borrowed to declare a unique minimum for all natural systems.
Source: [R20](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~cdm/resources/Moore1956-gedanken-experiments.pdf).

Comparing formal references: Moore's input–output distinguishability, state–action abstraction in SMDPs, preservation of interventions in structural equation models, and macro inference under lossy representations are not four names for the same problem. Mathematical transfer must at least show object sets, mappings, preserved relations, quantifiers, action or intervention sets, and error conditions. Section 4.19 explicitly rests its conclusions on its own finite model and proof. External mathematical literature identifies connections and differences rather than supplying unverified universal optimality. The later papers have not been fully checked formula by formula here; conclusions remain limited to research objects and source roles.

Handling empirical and normative sources: Scheffer and Mansoury can guide distinctions among dynamic signals, feedback, and measurement objects, but simulations or models do not directly prove harm to real people. Montgomery and CRPD return readers to specific legal texts without automatically giving anyone actual powers over a matter. The ILO explanation, Ministry of Finance provisions, and statistical methodology reports also each have their own objects of application. ‘The original is cited correctly’ is only the first step. Applying it to a present case requires additional evidence about jurisdiction, time, object, facts, and authority.

Checking in the reverse direction matters too. Reading only an abstract does not establish that the paper is unreliable, and a link failing to open does not establish that the citation is nonexistent. The specified pages of Sen 1981 support the distinction between conditions of access and aggregate availability; the specified ICJ paragraphs support distinctions among cooperation, responsibility, and causation of specific damage. Neither limited reading completes the whole study or the full legal dispute. A citation's support must track the pages actually read, without expanding a local check into reproduction of the entire work or a guarantee of universal applicability.

This section teaches a static bibliography and evidential responsibilities; it does not require constructing a story of third-order social evolution. Version creation, corrections, and republication have real temporal sequences that can be explained as they occurred. Inferring from the bibliography that an institution will succeed, a person must be harmed, or a policy gains legitimacy lacks sufficient objects and evidence. Complete bibliographic explanation is not complete reproduction of 20 studies. An honest reading scope is more useful than a false claim of ‘complete validation.’

A possible reading order: start with the book's specific assertion, then open the matching version and pages. State the supporting relationship as a limited claim; look for conditions, exceptions, and countervailing explanations in the same passage; only then judge transfer to a new context. If the original passage is temporarily unavailable, identify the missing pages explicitly rather than saying vaguely ‘insufficient material.’ If the relationship is only comparative, retain the comparative question without claiming equivalence. This concluding section reconnects the book to a world of materials that can be checked, disputed, and revised.

boundaries: Actual contrary evidence: WPP's partial update refutes ‘the same product name means every file was updated in tandem’; the CRPD corrigendum refutes ‘an unchanged paragraph number means unchanged words and logic.’
Actual measurement boundary: Mansoury studies preference representations within a simulated system. The phrase ‘preference change’ cannot erase the difference from intrinsic preferences.

Unresolved boundary: this unit has not completed the later historical cases and full formal development in Sen 1981, or the complete ICJ text and all its authorities. Reading specified passages cannot endorse these unfinished tasks.
Conditional counterexample: if a paper has three mirrored PDFs, or a working paper and published version share one experiment, more files do not mean more independent empirical studies.
Partial reading is not rejection of a source; a source's existence is not truth of a claim. Judgment should concern the specific bridging evidence still missing.
Sources relating to law, labor, accounting, and medicine serve textual teaching only in this section. No individual diagnosis, proxy decision, eligibility disposition, or legal action was performed.

caseNotes.title: Actual versioning case: the 2026 partial update to WPP2024
caseNotes.text: On January 19, 2026, the UN Population Division described a correction for Togo involving a duplicate undercount adjustment, explicitly specifying which series were and were not updated. The additional observation here concerns whether tables sharing a product name fall within the same revision scope, not population trends. Forcing revised national population figures to reconcile with unrevised aggregates can mistake version mismatch for a real demographic contradiction. The appropriate response is to label tables, scenarios, periods, and update scopes separately, not independently rewrite values the publisher left unchanged.
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Two-page revision note: revision scope and usage guidance
caseNotes.boundary: The revision note, not all data tables, was read. Togo's population was not recalculated, and no claim is made that the entire original version is invalid.

caseNotes.title: Actual textual case: the 2018 correction to CRPD paragraph 27
caseNotes.text: Paragraph 27 of the 2014 general comment later received an official replacement text. In the corrigendum, the conjunction before the third item is ‘or’; the three items must not still be interpreted under the old ‘and’ as all jointly required. The key change is not a webpage date but a logical connection that changes classification. Reading the corrigendum alongside the original comment prevents a seemingly accurate paragraph number from carrying outdated wording. This example does not establish that any real support arrangement is unlawful; it identifies which text should govern interpretation of that paragraph.
caseNotes.sourceLocator: Paragraph 27 of the 2014 comment; replacement text for paragraph 27 in Corr.1 dated 2018-01-26
caseNotes.boundary: The full comment was not read. The Committee's interpretation alone cannot determine the validity of a particular national arrangement or an individual's powers of agency.

caseNotes.title: Actual bibliographic case: 2017 research republished in 2026
caseNotes.text: The PMLR page gives both the UAI 2017 paper, pages 151–160, and a note that it was republished on October 4, 2026. Preserve both the original research year and the carrier's republication year. Treating the dates as two independent studies and claiming two validations of causal consistency would count the same publication twice. Erasing the republication date would also make the present entry point's version record harder to understand.
caseNotes.sourceLocator: PMLR bibliographic record and BibTeX note
caseNotes.boundary: Full proofs were not read. Republication does not add an experiment or independent study, or turn 2017 research into a new 2026 result.

argumentSteps: Premise 1: every reference has an object, version, location, and use. Different elements may answer different questions.
Premise 2: the book contains both explicit page-specific citations and specialist model references. Citation roles must be determined jointly from the book and source, not inferred from fame.

Inferential connection: first establish the relationship ‘book assertion—specific passage—supported proposition,’ then check the original qualifications and conditions required for transfer. Unread links remain unchecked.
Public conclusion: the 20 items form a bounded network for checking sources, not a universal endorsement of the entire theory, all empirical uses, or real-world dispositions.

Conditions and responsibilities: mathematical claims require matching definitions and proofs; empirical claims require research design and observations; normative claims require authoritative sources and applicable objects; real action also requires authority.

Response to an objection: this does not require reproducing an entire paper whenever it is taught. Reading enough to support the present limited statement is sufficient, but the statement must not exceed that scope.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: three files, one observation
teachingExamples.assumptions: Suppose A is an original research manuscript, B its Chinese translation, and C an unchanged republication of A, with no new sample or independent collection.
teachingExamples.text: There are three files, but grouping by underlying research leaves {A, B, C} as one group. Thus there are three reading entry points, not three independent validations. If D collects an additional sample, first check whether it is genuinely independent and whether it shares critical biases before discussing what it adds. This calculation does not estimate correlations between real studies.
teachingExamples.boundary: A teaching construction, not an accusation of plagiarism, duplicate publication, or quality defects in any reference in the book.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: how conjunctions change a judgment
teachingExamples.assumptions: Let A, B, and C be conditions that can be true or false. Compare Boolean logic only, without substituting anyone's legal eligibility.
teachingExamples.text: When A = true, B = false, and C = false, A and B and C is false, while A or B or C is true. Misreading ‘and’ as ‘or,’ or the reverse, changes the classification of the same factual combination. The actual CRPD corrigendum gives a reason to check conjunctions. This example illustrates logic only and makes no legal determination about any arrangement.
teachingExamples.boundary: Actual provisions include word meanings, context, and scope; three Boolean values alone cannot complete a legal judgment.

counterexamples.text: Actual contrary evidence: WPP's partial update refutes ‘the same product name means every file was updated in tandem’; the CRPD corrigendum refutes ‘an unchanged paragraph number means unchanged words and logic.’
counterexamples.effect: Limits presumptions of identical content based on product names or paragraph numbers.

counterexamples.text: Conditional counterexample: if a paper has three mirrored PDFs, or a working paper and published version share one experiment, more files do not mean more independent empirical studies.
counterexamples.effect: Independence must be traced to the underlying research.

counterexamples.text: Unresolved boundary: this unit has not completed the later historical cases and full formal development of Sen 1981, or the full ICJ text and all its authorities. Limited reading of specified passages does not mean all research is complete or responsibility in a case established.
counterexamples.effect: Limit conclusions to the passages actually read, retaining evidential responsibilities for historical cases, complete works, and specific applications.

questionAnswers.question: A webpage shows 2026 while the paper's bibliographic record says 2017. Should it be relabeled as 2026 research?
questionAnswers.answer: Do not relabel it first. Distinguish original publication, republication in the present carrier, and content revision dates. The Rubenstein item has been checked as 2017 research republished in 2026.

questionAnswers.question: After seeing the abstract of Sen's 1981 paper, can one write ‘pages 433–435 checked paragraph by paragraph’?
questionAnswers.answer: Not from the abstract alone. An abstract and specified full-text pages are different reading scopes. This section's guide to pages 433–435 relies separately on scanned original pages; it still does not imply a full reading of pages 433–464, or replace this QJE paper with the same-year monograph.

questionAnswers.question: If user profiles in a model become increasingly similar, is that enough to prove users' inner preferences were transformed?
questionAnswers.answer: No. First separate system records or representations from independently measured intrinsic preferences. A simulation does not automatically perform real psychological measurement.

questionAnswers.question: If two UN population tables both have 2024 in their names, can their update states be assumed identical?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Check the countries, series, scenarios, periods, and aggregate scope in the actual revision note. Togo's partial update is a counterexample.

questionAnswers.question: If an original-text link fails, can one conclude the author fabricated the reference?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Check official bibliographic records and other lawful entry points, and mark the full text as unobtained. Existence and support for a specific claim are separate judgments.

questionAnswers.question: Do four references on causal or dynamic abstraction already prove every level transition in the book correct?
questionAnswers.answer: No. Compare model classes, mappings, preserved relations, and assumptions, then check the specific proposition. References cannot replace the book's own proofs or empirical evidence.

1.5.3.title: 1.5.3 Reading Scope and Method Use
1.5.3.lead: How much of the source to read must match the judgment being made. Reading only part supports conclusions only about that part. Whether layered reading can replace complete reading requires comparison; equivalence cannot be claimed beforehand.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 141–148, ‘1.5.3 Reading Scope and Method Use.’ Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘Conclusions from partial reading cover only material actually obtained and understood; they do not automatically represent a judgment about the whole book’ (line 143). The lesson is separate from the source text.

This section sits alongside §§1.5.1 and 1.5.2. Those sections determine what work to do and how strong the review should be; this one determines how much source material that requires and how broad a conclusion the reading can support.

The first paragraph links reading scope to judgment. Three kinds of judgment require complete reading: evaluating the book's overall consistency, comparing the entire system, and transferring its common grammar. For conceptual clarification and local applications, one ‘may explore’ organizing reading around common constraints, task-relevant parts, and specifically cited sections. The wording is ‘may explore,’ not ‘has been proved possible’: layered reading may be tried, while its reliability is left to the comparison described in the third paragraph.

Conclusions from partial reading cover only material ‘actually obtained and understood.’ There are two gates: obtaining means actually reading the source; understanding means more than opening it. Unread portions do not mean an absence of objections; they mean this judgment has no information about those portions. The conclusion therefore cannot say ‘the whole book holds…’ or ‘the framework prescribes…’; it can say only ‘within the sections read…’.

The second paragraph specifies the order of layered reading: first retain the common grammar, evidential status, specialized meanings of core terms, nonequivalence relations, and output boundaries; then read the complete sections on which the current task depends. ‘Complete sections’ means more than the single sentence containing a keyword. One way to understand this order is that many terms in the book have specialized meanings and many relationships say ‘does not equal.’ Without these, local passages can easily be misread through everyday meanings.

The same paragraph gives conditions for further reading: cross-chapter references, competing explanations, exceptions, exclusions, or scale transitions require more reading; uncertainty about the dependency scope requires expansion to a continuous part or the whole book. Unclear dependencies point toward reading more, not first concluding from what has already been read. For example, §6.1 requires claims of effects across time to distinguish historical formation, present-carrier transmission, and an additional historical increment under §4.5. Encountering that sentence in §6.1 triggers further reading of §4.5.

Method summaries, indexes, and others' paraphrases help locate material but cannot replace the source conditions being used. On this lesson's interpretation, this site's explanations are also paraphrases, so the rule applies to them: in making a judgment, the explanation helps locate material, while the cited conditions must be checked in the source.

The third paragraph treats whether layered reading can replace complete reading as a question of method use requiring comparison. Hold tasks, materials, model conditions, and evaluation methods fixed, observing four outcomes separately: important misjudgments, effective answers, preservation of unknowns, and reading burden. Because the source requires separate observation, they should not be combined into one score that lets reduced reading burden offset increased important errors.

Acceptable differences must be fixed beforehand, not shifted after seeing results. Section 16.24 makes a parallel requirement when comparing this framework with alternatives: first fix tasks, materials, input cutoff, resources, and evaluation methods; retain sufficiently strong domain methods and accurate source citation as comparators; then separately check errors, omissions, inappropriate abstention, time, disclosure, and maintenance labor. Without an actual comparison, do not claim equivalence has been proved.

Before comparison is complete, experimental applications with explicitly marked scope can proceed, but cannot establish equivalence between the two approaches. Access logs or completion markers do not prove understanding: opening, scrolling to the bottom, and ticking ‘read’ are operational traces. Section 16.16 likewise states that complete reading does not automatically produce understanding or fairness. Complete reading is necessary for some judgments, but does not guarantee understanding.

The strongest objection is that a book with sixteen parts and four appendices makes complete reading a barrier to most people, seemingly contradicting §1.5.2's statement that people cannot be required to learn the entire terminology first. The response is that §1.5.2 prohibits requiring the terminology before acknowledging people's experience or responding to legitimate needs. It governs how people are treated, not how much source material must be read to evaluate the whole book's consistency, compare the entire system, or transfer its common grammar. This section already permits exploration of layered reading for conceptual clarification and local applications, subject to the second paragraph's sequence and further-reading conditions, with honest scope labeling and no presentation of local conclusions as judgments about the whole book. Reading burden is itself one outcome to observe separately when comparing the two approaches.
argumentSteps: Premise: different judgments depend on different scopes of material. Unread material provides no information for the present judgment.

Connection: evaluating the book's overall consistency, comparing the entire system, or transferring its common grammar requires complete reading. Conceptual clarification and local applications may explore reading organized by common constraints, required parts, and specifically cited sections. Cross-chapter references, competing explanations, exceptions, exclusions, or scale transitions require further reading; unclear dependency scope requires expansion to a continuous part or the whole book.
Conclusion: match reading scope to the judgment undertaken, and mark the coverage of local conclusions.
Qualification: equivalence of layered reading remains unresolved until comparison is complete; experimental applications with marked scope may proceed.

Evidential responsibility: tasks, materials, model conditions, evaluation methods, and acceptable differences must be fixed beforehand, with four outcomes observed separately. Access logs and completion markers are not evidence of understanding.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: two scope statements for the same question
teachingExamples.text: Imagine a reader seeking to clarify the difference between ‘the system received feedback’ and ‘the system learned.’ Under layered reading, first retain common grammar, evidential status, specialized meanings of core terms, nonequivalence relations, and output boundaries, then read §§6.2 and 6.3 in full. Section 6.3 states that present-carrier transmission and a historical increment beyond the present representation are branches requiring separate evidence; the historical-increment branch also requires support from a G3-instance. The G3 conditional increment is defined in §4.5. This cross-chapter reference triggers further reading, so §4.5 is then read in full. An appropriate statement is: ‘Within the scope of §§6.2, 6.3, and 4.5 read here, the distinction between feedback arrival and learning is…’. An inappropriate statement is: ‘The whole book's definition of learning is…’.
teachingExamples.assumptions: The reader, task, and reading path are teaching assumptions. The listed sections illustrate a trigger for further reading, not a validated dependency list.
teachingExamples.boundary: This example does not prove that completing this path produces correct understanding or that layered reading matches complete reading on this task.

teachingExamples.title: Teaching construction: a preregistered comparison of reading approaches
teachingExamples.text: Imagine a maintainer comparing layered and complete reading. Beforehand, register the same set of thirty conceptual-clarification tasks, the same source version, model conditions, and scoring instructions. Record important misjudgments, effective answers, correct preservation of ‘unknown,’ and reading time separately. Specify acceptable differences in advance, for example ‘important misjudgments must not exceed the complete-reading group.’ Suppose the layered group takes nearly half as long and produces similar effective answers but two more important misjudgments. Under the prior standard, equivalence cannot be claimed; the standard cannot later become ‘up to three additional errors are acceptable.’ One can honestly report: ‘For these tasks, layered reading reduced burden but increased important misjudgments and failed the prior criterion.’
teachingExamples.assumptions: The task count, outcome numbers, and acceptable differences are fictional, not results of a real comparison.
teachingExamples.boundary: The example's criterion is not a recommended value. Even if a real comparison meets its criterion, the conclusion covers only those tasks, materials, and model conditions, without extending to evaluation of the whole book or other tasks.

questions: Which three kinds of judgment require complete reading in the source?
How far can a partial-reading conclusion extend? What do ‘obtained’ and ‘understood’ each exclude?
Which situations require further reading under a layered approach? How should reading expand when dependencies are unclear?
Why must a comparison fix acceptable differences beforehand and observe four outcomes separately?
What role do this site's explanations have in making a judgment?

questionAnswers.answer: Evaluating the whole book's consistency, comparing the entire system, and transferring its common grammar.

questionAnswers.question: How far can a partial-reading conclusion extend? What do ‘obtained’ and ‘understood’ each exclude?
questionAnswers.answer: Only material actually obtained and understood. ‘Obtained’ excludes not actually reading the source; ‘understood’ excludes merely opening or marking it. Unread portions provide no information for this judgment.

questionAnswers.question: Which situations require further reading under a layered approach? How should reading expand when dependencies are unclear?

questionAnswers.question: Why must a comparison fix acceptable differences beforehand and observe four outcomes separately?
questionAnswers.answer: Setting criteria afterward permits selecting a favorable framing from the results. Observing four outcomes separately reveals whether lower burden comes at the cost of more misjudgments.

questionAnswers.question: What role do this site's explanations have in making a judgment?
questionAnswers.answer: On this lesson's interpretation, explanations are also paraphrases. Like method summaries and indexes, they help locate material in making a judgment but cannot replace source conditions. Return to the source for the conditions used in the judgment.
questionAnswers.basis: §1.5.3, second paragraph.

The difference between layered and complete reading on a specific task requires a comparison preregistered as this section requires. This lesson has not conducted one.

applicability.reason: This section specifies requirements for reading scope and comparisons of reading approaches. The lesson uses teaching constructions only; it has no real comparison to present as a case and adds no figure.

1.5.3.summary: Reading scope follows the judgment: conclusions speak only for the source material actually obtained and understood. Claiming equivalence between approaches first requires a completed comparison with fixed conditions and acceptable differences set beforehand.

6.14.title: 6.14 Search Order for Mechanisms and Paths
6.14.lead: Search order is an order for finding candidates, not a ranking of which is more likely true. Being found first, having complete cards, or following a common search practice cannot promote a candidate into an identified mechanism.
explanation: Chinese source location: lines 1531–1544, ‘6.14 Search Order for Mechanisms and Paths.’ Brief quotation, translated from Chinese: ‘This order is only the working order for finding candidates; it does not mean that a candidate found earlier is more likely to be true’ (Chinese source line 1535). The lesson is separate from the source text.

This section concludes the use of Part VI: §§6.2–6.10 provide conditional mechanisms and their boundaries; §6.11 is the overall gate for mechanism outputs; §§6.12 and 6.13 address multiple clocks and cross-circle relations. This section asks how to find those materials for a specific problem without exceeding their conditions.

The first paragraph specifies two steps: filter potentially applicable mechanisms by object, scale, window, and requested output, then seek paths based on observed differences in state. Defining applicability first avoids taking a phenomenon through every mechanism in search of a matching name.

The same paragraph limits state prototypes: those for human collectives apply only to objects with the corresponding conditions. Actors, technical systems, and natural processes cannot share the same state set merely because their names sound similar. This agrees with §7.5's ‘S0–S6 can serve only as state prototypes for human intentional collectives’ and the state prototypes in §8.3. Two constructed examples: a device being ‘newly assembled’ and a lake ‘beginning eutrophication’ cannot be assigned human-collective prototypes such as S0 merely because the wording seems similar.

The second paragraph lists four types of input material: the object's currently confirmable state; confirmable direct changes after an event; channels, capacity, and clocks able to carry subsequent change; and mechanisms and external disturbances not yet distinguished. Including the last category means making room for competing explanations from the outset of the search.

Candidates have two sources: state-exit conditions suggest path candidates, while observed changes suggest mechanism candidates. Enabling conditions, propagation stages, and minimum evidence are then checked individually. The two sources answer different questions: §8.4 says a path describes ‘how a state configuration or object contract changes.’ On this lesson's interpretation, a mechanism candidate concerns which process might produce the observed change; it remains a candidate until the individual checks are complete.

Order is not probability. A candidate found first is not thereby more likely to be true. The fifth paragraph allows search order to be adjusted based on omissions, misjudgments, and cost of use. These assess search performance; they do not judge which candidate is true in this case. Treating the first match as the default answer is precisely the leap this section excludes.

The third paragraph requires retaining competing candidates that explain the same phenomenon and simple baselines whenever a candidate is used. It names three distinctions: returned signals versus learning (§6.3 requires a return to produce a retainable update that actually enters subsequent tasks); local overload versus temporary demand increases, reduced capacity, and common external causes (the full CM-LOAD conditions in §6.6 determine what counts as local overload); and cross-circle cascades versus synchronous exposure (§6.13 distinguishes one failure triggering the next from a common external cause damaging several locations simultaneously). A search match cannot justify omitting counterexamples or exclusions required by the relevant complete contracts.

The fourth paragraph requires four items for each candidate path: conditions under which it continues to hold, observable changes the mechanism should produce first, contrary signals, and stopping points. Without enabling evidence, a candidate can still organize discriminating observations, but cannot become an identified mechanism. This aligns with §6.11: when items are missing, retain only candidate mechanisms or questions for checking.

An early signal cannot merely restate the outcome in a milder form. In a constructed example, if the expected outcome is markedly longer waits, ‘waiting starts to increase’ is only a mild version of that same outcome, not an early signal of local overload. Temporary demand increases and reduced capacity can also lengthen waits, so it does not distinguish those candidates. Under §12.6, an early signal is an observable change the path's mechanism should produce first. Section 1.2 likewise calls for early and contrary signals that distinguish paths when introducing analysis of specific events. If several paths share the same evidence, repeated citation does not add independent support.

The fifth paragraph permits adjusting search order based on omissions, misjudgments, and cost of use, but requires preserving the original mechanisms' applicability boundaries and comparison with simpler search methods. Convenient searching, complete cards, or several analysts using the same order do not prove a real mechanism exists. Multiple people using the same order may share the same omissions.

The strongest objection asks why prescribe an order if it does not represent probability. On this lesson's interpretation, the order serves searching with fewer omissions and errors at a manageable cost, not ranking truth. Defining applicability first avoids seeking a name for one phenomenon across every mechanism; including undistinguished mechanisms and external disturbances among the inputs preserves space for competitors. This lesson has not compared whether these features actually reduce omissions and errors. The source requires changes to preserve applicability boundaries and face comparison with simpler search methods. Section 16.24 also bars claiming superiority to alternatives without an actual comparison. Inclusion in the framework therefore cannot establish that this order is better.
argumentSteps: Premise: mechanism conditions and applicability boundaries are distributed across Part VI, state prototypes, and the path library. A specific problem requires a procedure for finding candidates.

Connection: first define applicability by object, scale, window, and output. Then start from four types of material, deriving path candidates from exit conditions and mechanism candidates from observed changes, and check enabling conditions, propagation stages, and minimum evidence individually.
Conclusion: search produces candidates and arrangements for discriminating observations, not identified mechanisms.

Qualification: order is not a probability ranking. Retain competitors, simple baselines, counterexamples, and exclusions. Early signals cannot be diminished versions of the outcome, and shared evidence does not accumulate.
Evidential responsibility: adjustments must preserve applicability boundaries and be compared with simpler search methods. Convenience, completeness, and multiple users are not mechanism evidence.
